title: Horizontal picture-theater scroll for a school anniversary
good_for: Anniversary sites for schools or companies that present their history as an interactive experience, with era-based story maps and donation information.

pages.use: Landing page — a numeral loader and a first popup asking about background music, then vertical scroll moves horizontally through an illustrated village from 1925 to 2000, the year counter ticks, people walk, and building buttons open story modals. For anniversary and history experience landings
Commemorative projects — big title, one-line intro, seven staggered two-row photo panels (hover enlarges), three-cell link strip below. For choosing project or program categories by photo panels

A 100-year history — a four-column timeline pinned to the screen (school · affiliated school · sports clubs · campus scenery) turns to the same year in sync with the wheel, and you can jump with year buttons or a 10-year dropdown. For timeline and history pages
News list — four category tabs (.3s rise) and date · category tag · title lines, 12 more per ”More” click. For notice · news lists
Single news item — date, category tag, big title, body, back-to-list button. For announcement detail

notes: Art: instead of the original hand-drawn pieces (hundreds of web-page buildings, people, clouds, mountains), an SVG shape town — each building keeps the original position (vh), height, parallax (200px × −5~7) and z order, while the look is simplified to blocks, roofs and window grids. Colors are --site-* values built from --kf-*, so changing the skin changes the town too

Walking people: the original 32 Lottie figures (hand-drawn period outfits) → 31, rebuilt as our own shape Lottie (30fps · 30-frame walk cycle, 1.2~1.7x speed, random start frame). Distance, speed and direction tables are as in the original, looks differ only by color, skirt, hat and rickshaw

Four object Lotties (tuna, rainbow, paper ball, NEXT 100 YEARS): rebuilt our own data with the same trigger and playback (goToAndPlay(1), playSegments [0,10] and [0,30]). The NEXT 100 YEARS lettering is judged to be drawn inside the original Lottie, so the HTML text fades up over 1s (judgment call)

Background music: the original chains four mp3 tracks per era with Web Audio (bgmPlay when the year counter ends). With no sound files, only the ON/OFF popup and the state of the sound button below (navy↔gray) exist — the sound placeholder files and playback are for the next person

Quiz and game: the original’s 7 Character QUIZ types and fish-farm guessing game overlay (question, answer, explanation, retry) are cut down to two choices in the same modal plus a character card rotateY 90→0 .6s expo.out. Carry the original quiz step values over from CRGVJjz_.js quizAnswer.
Story modal: the original’s 36 content panels → one panel filled with the clicked button’s text and photo label (open/close .6s expo.out · white panel position · close band unchanged)
swiper 4.1.6 and lenis, which the original loads but never calls, are not included (confirmed 0 calls to new Swiper and new Lenis)
The ‹Please view in portrait› notice panel (Portrait) shown when the phone is rotated to landscape was not built

History page below 1024px: the original yd (column switch tabs + year updates via ScrollTrigger) is simplified to window scroll + year position calculation. The 102-year × 4-column timeline data is placeholder generated by a rule
The festival picture was moved from its original spot (162.5vh) to 200vh, overlapping the shopping-street arch (parallax −400 unchanged)

title: Reverse-counting article numbers on a graphic tile checkerboard
good_for: Brand anniversary microsites with a growing article archive or campaign tracker, presented as a retro poster-style magazine list.

pages.use: Anniversary site home — arch wordmark and giant number hero, featured article, category bar, article tile checkerboard. For a brand anniversary or campaign article archive home screen
Commemorative project intro — arch story · project intro · numbered steps · brand intro · old product mosaic. For anniversary project aims and brand history intros
News list — category bar and row list. For commemorative sites·brand announcement lists
People together — category bar and a grid of circular portrait cards. For introducing participants, ambassadors and collaborators
One News item — title and body article with a share row. For notice and press post detail

notes: The logo, the hero arch wordmark and the giant footer wordmark are redrawn as SVG with the same structure (top row with a teapot circle between two words + a big number below) instead of the original art — the text uses TITLE·000 placeholders, and the arch uses a slanted baseline (skewY ±12.5°) instead of the original’s curved lettering.

Illustrations (picnic figures·scenes 01~03·two people on the floor) don’t use the original art but are simple flat figures drawn with shapes — only position·size·color feel are matched (rule: original art files are not used).
The original body and heading typefaces are paid fonts, so Noto Sans KR was used instead, and Anton and Unna for the wordmark. The handwriting slot for ‹(Tea time)› is Caveat (--kf-font-hand).

Graphic tile and illustration colors (yellow · olive · brown · green · purple · sky · orange · light purple · tan · gold leaf) output the original STUDIO color token values from the accent (red) via oklch as they are (shared.css --site-*). When the skin changes they rotate together with the same lightness, chroma ratio and hue spacing — to keep the original colors, the consumer overrides --site-*.

Category pills use per-category URLs like the original (/?category=…) instead of navigating, cards are filtered in place — the category list page has the same form as the first page so it was not built separately. The search box, ”Load more”, share and download are shape only and do nothing (the original uses server search · external share).

The year photo mosaic on about does not copy the original cell layout, but is rebuilt on a 12-column grid with the same types (large cell · vertical cell · vertical year label · red box). Subpage heights are shorter than the original because repeated cells were cut (about 6053→5205, friends 3746→2375).
The phone hero carries over the original layout (logo, wordmark, one line of featured article + progress number) in condensed form, and hides the original phone hero’s left menu text.

Instead of the original modal (a full-screen dialog with its own red band and CLOSE header), the phone menu unfolds only the red panel below the page’s band and header. It opens and closes instantly with no transition, as in the original, and the visible layout (band · CLOSE · links · logo) is the same

title: Illustrator portfolio framed as OS windows and a CRT screen
good_for: Portfolios for illustrators and character artists, including merchandise and event schedule sections.

pages.use: Artist home page — a loader cell that unfolds into a border on entry, four draggable lens windows over the key art plus a 3D mascot, an event schedule row, four work categories on a fixed CRT screen, a work row, a profile and a stack of photo windows. For a character or illustrator artist home.

Work list. A 6-column work grid mixing type filters (slash between words), category filters (pills) and empty cells. Clicking a work opens a work window in place. For lists in portfolios with many works

Single work — a draggable OS-style work window floating over the list (large image · title · tags · info · close · date barcode), pressing the image opens a fullscreen view. For showing work detail as a window over the list
Artist intro — barcode title·intro text·SNS buttons, four lens windows lighting a big dark image, two columns of links·history, works row. For artist profiles
Contact — title and intro text, sticker and dotted X ornaments on the left, name, email and message form on the right with a rounded send button. For commission inquiry forms

notes: Artwork (main character full body, stickers, work thumbnails, CRT category art) is the artist’s work, so it is left as placeholders — in the hero, lens window and profile lens, our own SVG silhouette (a twin-tailed figure) of the same position and size is drawn so the lens effect shows, and the CRT category art is a canvas-drawn placeholder (what it depicts is written in text) fed into the same shader

3D: the two original GLBs (rabbit mascot and character, Draco compressed) were not carried over. They were rebuilt from basic shapes with the same size and silhouette proportions. The rabbit is a flattened ball plus two long ears (same cylinder colliders as the original · mass 10 · restitution .2 · mouse ball radius 80 · push 4e5 · entrance 1s power3.out · exit .8s). The character is a twin-tailed figure built from cylinders, capsules and balls, with three lights as in the original (key .4 · fill .3 · back .3), stepped shading, a black back-face outline, and a .01rad rotation every frame. The shapes themselves are simpler than the original models.

Shaders: grid (noise time×.05 · amplitude .075 · stronger toward the center · edges straightened .02~.12), CRT (RGB .002 · block noise .1 · jitter .002→.25 · 5s-cycle band · tracking line bend .025 · grain .2 · scanline sin(y·800) · green tracking line .005 · vignette) and hologram (fbm 5-octave domain warping · magenta · blue · cyan · metal .7) were rewritten in our own code with the same values. The original block noise is an image file, so a canvas drawing random bars stands in for it

swup: the same swup 4.6.1 + preload·head·fragment plugins as the original. The a11y plugin version inside the bundle could not be identified, so the 5.2.1 already in _vendor was used, and for the fragment plugin 1.1.1, which best matches the bundle strings, was newly added to _vendor (same score as 1.1.0). When opened as a file (file://), swup does not run, so navigation is a normal page load.
The contact form doesn’t submit (the original POSTs to an external form service and then moves to the thanks page). The thank-you page (contact/thanks) wasn’t recorded, so it wasn’t built

The 1:09 window (a small window stacks up to 80 pieces every 0.2 seconds only at that time) was built by the same rules, but the text is placeholder (at_0-00.txt) and the clock is a stopped ”0:00” placeholder text like the original

title: Sky opening followed by sparkling, melting WebGL image transitions
good_for: Anniversary or campaign pages that show many illustrations or photos one after another on a single screen, with archives organized by region or date.

pages.use: One-page commemorative site: an 8s opening where the sky settles down (four big title lines · tagline · poem), a WebGL stage where a full-screen image sparkles at the center and melts into the next every 3s, a left region list that slides along, a drawer opened by a star button for regional collections, and viewer and public-schedule windows. For campaign artwork reveals and gallery hero screens

notes: The 96 images (character illustrations) were reduced to six placeholder canvases of the same ratio (wide screen 2048×1152 · narrow screen 1024×1920) — sky, ground and figure silhouettes painted in skin variable colors, with a label inside saying what each image is. To use the real images, inside .t-view just put it in

The transition shader was rebuilt from measurements with the same numbers (center distance×2 − progress×3 + 1.5, noise ×200, breathing sin(t·.2)·.13/.2, 1.5s power1.inOut, wheel 1.3s). The noise function is our own hash gradient noise, so the sparkle grains do not match the original grain for grain.
The original was written in React (three-fiber) — ported to a plain script using the same three r176
The opening big title uses Outfit 800 text instead of the original lettering graphic (SVG), Elza (paid) was replaced with Outfit
Voice listening (sound button, wav) and the new-post badge were not carried over — the sound file is an original asset, so the spot is left empty
Of the regional groups under the drawer, only part of 5 of the original 8 groups · 96 cells are kept, and the schedule has only 4 rows. They repeat in the same form, so trimming seemed fine
Window (enlarged view / schedule) backdrop and open-close timing: the original c-modal rule was not found, so it was set to a .4s fade by eye — to be re-measured

Drawer region group header, five slots (featured image · overseas · northern region · central region · southern region) — the original uses kanji and kana headings, Korean kept. Drawn in body Noto Sans KR 800 so it matches the bold gothic headings of the original
Drawer person names, 17 characters (.t-ablock__ch .name) — the original uses kana names, Korean kept. latin-slots catches only the final selector .name, but the actual font is the body gothic

The only place changed to English in the font backfill is the footer header (where the original English logo graphic sits). The four large English title lines of the opening and logo, and the list region labels (Global · City …), were carried over from the original English when first built, but because they tie into the opening letter proportions and motion values they were left out of this backfill (text only, Korean slots only) — next time, swap them for ordinary English placeholder copy

title: Cassette loader and airplane-window flow for a travel game promo
good_for: Promotional sites for games, apps, or character content that need news, world-building, character cards with detail pages, video, and social links in one package.

pages.use: Promo first page — cassette countdown loader, Hero slide + lime scoreboard marquee, number-shuffle departure board News, giant marquee boundary, orange About panel (pinned) with airplane window flowing sideways, tilting card carousel (group buttons switch panel color), video over a stack of tickets, SNS card strip, frame Footer

News list — navy left panel + yellow tag buttons (?cat= as a category list), rows with date cell · tag · title | thumbnail image, and the row flips to navy on hover. Slot for a game or service notices board

Worldview / service intro — header with airplane-window rows flowing past, intro text where blacked-out document lines peel away, a tag table that flies in and lands at an angle, and route lines. Spot for the ‹What story is this game?› page

Character detail — on a tilted handheld device screen, intro and stats, a large full-body illustration, outlined English name, thumbnail row of the same group, zoom (ZOOM) and voice buttons, group badge row, SNS card strip. A spot for a single character or product detail

notes: Original subpage 4 (/news/info) is the same form as news list 1 filtered by category, so it was not built separately and uses news.html?cat=Filters the same list by info (the tag button links to that address).

The original-only fonts BRAND Sans Funny and BRAND Sans are paid, so we used the rounded single-line Tilt Neon and the monospace Share Tech Mono — the original font’s ligatures (dlig, like the T tail in INTRODUCTION) are missing. The Korean placeholder falls back to IBM Plex Sans KR.

The eight rows of the original menu drawer are tilted cassette tape images (560~610×130~186), so they were rebuilt at the same positions and angles as lettering plates shaped like tape spines (color band + white label + thickness shadow). The props (3D sticker PNGs) are flat SVG drawings of the same position and size (sun, star, heart, airplane, camera, etc.) and the floating keyframes (7~15s alternate) are unchanged from the original.

The person card, table, SNS card and device are single images in the original (tilted card photos), so they were rebuilt as HTML panels with the same ratio and tilt. The person image in the card is a photo placeholder.

The original ticker sets that day’s temperature and weather from a weather-agency JSON — only date and time are real values, temperature is a 00.0℃ placeholder. The video slot is a same-size 16:9 placeholder instead of an auto-looping video embed, and clicking it opens the video window with the same .3s.
The voice button on the person detail plays an mp3 via buzz in the original — this is a sound-file slot, so only the playing state (lime) turns on for 3 seconds.

Phone (390) follows the original SP layout (side menu hidden, news row folded, window panel on top and text below, card width 92%·adjacent section ±105%). The original SP-only image text (menu pledge text·footer text placed as images) was re-set as live text.
The original common reset’s link colors (default #004986 · hover #5a8fba, instant) were carried over too — links with their own color are overridden by later rules and stay as they are.

The two nickname lines and five intro lines on the detail device screen — in the original these are Kana/Kanji picture text (profile PNG), kept in Korean here. Drawn in IBM Plex Sans KR, the same family as the original IBM Plex Sans JP. This is the spot latin-slots catches by looking only at the final selector span

title: Single-page illustrator portfolio with posters on a clothesline
good_for: One-page portfolios for illustrators and designers, with merchandise or sticker sales information.

pages.use: A one-page artist portfolio — a hero where posters hanging on strings flow endlessly, a rotating ABOUT ring and intro, a band of section names in mixed weights, a 3-column work grid, a row of rounded product photos, a half-and-half sticker sales section, three videos, a walking-people band, a contact form beside an illustration, and a corner ad banner. For the first page of an illustration or goods artist

notes: Illustrations (walking-people strip, guitar player, dot mascot, claw, QR) are redrawn as SVGs in the same position, size and composition, but are simpler than the originals (the five walkers and the guitarist are just a few shapes). Colors are derived in oklch from --kf-accent and --kf-accent-text, so they follow when the skin is changed.

The three embedded videos are placeholder buttons of equal size — pressing one removes the play button and only shows a ”Playing” state with a progress bar filling at 30s (actual playback is the video player’s job)
The card’s libs listed lottie, but it isn’t in the original page code — it was a string in the YouTube player bundle, so it wasn’t built
The contact form does not send (form builder service). The corner ad, like the original, cannot be reopened once closed

At width 834 the original is also the desktop layout (split 820), so the header nav sticks out past the right edge of the screen — left as in the original (fixed header, so document horizontal overflow is 0)

Time (2026-11-17): building took around 90 minutes, but sharing a mini desktop browser seat with other students meant each measurement waited 10~30 minutes for a turn, so the total exceeded 180 minutes

Among the measurement acceptances, one cause could not be isolated: on 1440 the release background transition of the product-sale pill uses the same css as the original (300ms cubic-bezier(.4,.4,0,1)), but the copy snapped at 117ms (same value twice, hover-in passed). Lines where the flowing strip (10s·20s linear, running since the document opens) mixed into the hover measuring window were accepted with the reasons noted.

title: Giant pixel lettering and tilted card stacks for a game agency
good_for: Homepages for game and entertainment companies with service overviews, case study details, and playful 404 or event mini-game pages.

pages.use: Agency home page — giant pixel-type hero, expanding showreel, stacking service panels, client logos and case cards, draggable testimonials, a tilted contact form. For game and entertainment company homes.
Single case detail — two-word case header, swipeable key-points panel, approach paragraph, photo grid, expanding photo, results, next-case card. For portfolio·client work
404 and pixel mini-game — a canvas version where you hit three lime-cell numbers with the mouse to knock them down, with time and remaining-cell bars. For missing-address pages and event play

notes: Of the three recorded subpages, two (one listed in pages.json as about, the other as works) are the same case-detail type, so they were built as a single works.html. The 404 page, whose type is page, is game.html

Fonts: OffBit · OffBit 101 · Neue Power · Nohemi are paid, so bold and thin pixel text is replaced with Jersey 10 (Latin) · Galmuri11 (Korean, OFL), wide titles with Archivo at 125% width, and body with Lexend. Thin pixel text is made with an outline (text-stroke) of the same font, so it differs slightly from the original’s 1-cell stroke

The path shapes of the four hero tails were drawn by us with the same box size, position and zigzag feel instead of copying the original SVG coordinates (100 cells · 100px · .01s spacing · 3s pause · 1s on · 1s off are original values).

The line-art stickers on the testimonial panel (controller · trophy · star) were redrawn at the same position and size but are simpler than the original’s detailed illustrations. The background art behind Contact is also replaced by one large controller outline
The Contact form is a placeholder, so there is no send or recaptcha (tilt 12°·phone 6° → scroll 8°·phone 3°, and 0° on hover or while typing at .6s smooth-2 are the original contactForm values)

The 404 game digit shapes are our own pixel art (three 11×15 grids) instead of the original GLB voxel model. Physics (rapier 2D 0.19.1: gravity -1000 · friction .2283 · bounce .3043 · damping 1 · walls) and mouse path samples (half the cell size, up to 16) are the original values. The record view is a placeholder window
The stair pattern behind the original service panel was not copied by coordinates but drawn as a seeded random staircase with the same cell size and slope
As in the original, “Settings” in the cookie dialog expands two items and closes with “Save”. There is no real cookie handling (localStorage marker only)

404 game page (game.html): the lenis 1.3.11 min build and rapier2d-compat 0.19.1 share the same top-level name (r), so they can’t both load as plain scripts, and lenis was dropped. The original is also a single screen here (h-svh · overflow-hidden), so there’s no difference in scroll feel

The first loader is a reduced approximation of the original — the original has a bordered box with four corner marks that scales 0→1, then grows in 3 steps (desktop 420×420→800×420→1200×600, phone 260×260→300×480→340×700, scaled .4~1.25x to fit the window) over .8s smooth-2 while W·H numbers count along, and in each step the phrase and number (first step 1~49 random, then 100) swap with a −.2s overlap, vanish on the last step, and wait until hero-ready. Ours uses a phrase letter-flip plus a 00→100 count. The original Loader code was only found in the fetched copy after the 150-minute cap was exceeded, so it could not be rebuilt.

Font backfill: the original copy is all English, so every title-font (Archivo 125%) and pixel-font (Jersey 10) slot was replaced with English placeholder text — wordmark Studio, menu, big pixel words (Title Here · Services · Our Work · Start your Project · Client Name · Short Phrase · Big Words · Next Case · five footer words), page names, buttons, tags, name lines, form field labels and loader text. No title-font slot is left in Korean.

Decision: explanatory sentences set in the wide title font (hero · service lead · recommendation sentence · contact lead · works big paragraph · 404 message) were also replaced with English placeholder text, since the original is an English sentence in that font. The README rule ‹body and description sentences are Korean› applies only to sentences in the body font (Lexend), so those (svc-small · small · cookie description · form consent sentence) stay Korean.

Filter categories are short unspaced words like the original (One·Two·Three) — ”Category 1”·”Type 1” wrapped the buttons onto two lines on phones. The first hero line had to be cut to five letters (Title) because Jersey 10 is wider than the original OffBit, to fit the phone width

Moved the data-lines line splitting from DOMContentLoaded to after document.fonts.ready. Once the copy became English, lines were set at the width before Archivo loaded, so the big works paragraph re-wrapped line by line (in Korean the fallback font had the same width, so it never showed).

In the picker panel section images (library-shots are captured with reduce), the hero’s large two lines that split on scroll and the preview sit at the end state (±864px), off-screen — it is reduce handling unrelated to the copy, so it was left as is. thumb is captured without reduce after waiting 7 seconds (at 2.5 seconds the loader and entrance are still in progress)

title: Giant character built from small text that changes per greeting
good_for: One-page company New Year, year-end, or founding greetings with a slogan, per-person single-character messages, and services, contact, and company info.

pages.use: New Year greeting first page — a title that grows after the text rises, a giant single character built from hundreds of small characters, slogan text, a greeting where a screen-fixed mosaic turns into a different character for each person, then after a white curtain fills in: services, video contact, reading, company table, makers, last year’s list, and a big greeting footer. For a company or studio seasonal greeting page.

English edition of the same New Year greeting — same frame with English placeholders, the small Korean subtitle line removed (the mosaic lettering and the large footer greeting are images so they stay). For the second-language edition of a multilingual seasonal page.

notes: Original font Helvetica Now Text (paid) is replaced with Inter, and Japanese Noto Sans JP with the same-family Noto Sans KR

The contact section background video is muted loop playsinline like the original. It plays at 1% visible and stops when it leaves the screen or the tab is hidden. The original video file is not in the archive so its length is unknown, and we use our placeholder video (media/contact.mp4, 16:9 · 8s loop)

Language switch links our two pages (KO → index.html, EN → en.html) instead of the original JA/EN. As in the original, the English version uses the same characters as the Korean version for the mosaic letters, the big letters behind the menu, and the big footer greeting
Reading material, company links and past-year lists have nowhere to go, so they are set to #. The contact form is an outside page in the original too, so it was not built

Font backfill: the spots where the original was Latin (header menu · section name English line · TITLE HERE · Name Here / Role · Service One~Four · Media Name · View more · hero A HAPPY NEW YEAR) were English placeholder text from the start, so nothing was changed.

Index section subtitles, seven slots (q-title__ja — This Year’s Slogan · People’s New Year Greetings · Our Services · More to Read · Company Info · The Makers · Last Year’s Greetings page) — the original uses kana·kanji subtitles, Korean kept

Index slogan: nine Korean lines · five per-person greeting slots · service header copy and four one-line service names · four service descriptions · contact copy · three reading descriptions · one-line explainers (symbol name · (reading) · explanation) — the original was Japanese text, Korean kept. The ko page body uses Noto Sans KR, which is the same family as the original Noto Sans JP. latin-slots is html[lang="en"] This is where the Inter rule on body is read only as the final chunk body, catching even the ko page
Four wire note (wf-note) slots (two each for index and en) — fixed-width notes from wire.css, not site copy, keep Korean

title: Isometric logistics city with a timeline-scale vision section
good_for: Homepages for tech startups, logistics, or manufacturing companies covering mission, staged vision, three services, history, awards, investors, careers, and news.

pages.use: Company home — isometric logistics-city hero, mission accordion, pinned vision steps, three businesses, flowing history band, awards, media, investors, code of conduct, careers. For a tech and logistics startup home in one page
News list — heading at left, dotted row list and more button at right. For company notice and press lists
News item — centered narrow-width title·date·body·four share buttons. For notice·press release article detail

notes: The isometric city in the Hero and Contact is redrawn procedurally with the same composition (a band from bottom left to top right), two-color families and black outlines. Instead of the original’s hand-drawn props (robot arm, ship, truck, conveyor, stair path, wave band) and curved roads, it has only box buildings, stairs, pins, domes and gears. Buildings are denser than the original and there are fewer white roads. The original is a single illustration that cannot be carried over as is, and redrawing at the same density would need the artwork rebuilt.

The four animated embeds inside the artwork were redrawn with the same motion by reading the original Studio embed code: four cubes of the glass-sphere stand + box machine (2.0/1.6/2.3/1.9s · delays -.4/-1/-.2/-.8s · ease-in-out round trip upward by 3/4/2.5/4.5% of the artwork width) and a robot hand + glass box (2.1/1.7s · -.5/-1.1s · 3.2/4%). The artwork shapes are ours, and which cube piece has which tempo may differ from the original. The glass sphere spot in the Contact artwork could not be measured from the original screen, so it sits at the top of the center building.

The pattern behind the company band was redrawn with the same values as the original embed (1440×2400 · phone 840×4800 version stretched to band size, thirteen 45° bands, six of which come in from 300 at the corner over .8s cubic-bezier(.25,.46,.45,.94) · .6/.75s late). The band position is ours. The original is a lazy iframe so the exact trigger time couldn’t be measured, it runs when the band comes within 1250px below the screen (browser lazy iframe distance).

The rounded plate of the logo-cover section was handled as image/background in the original so its values couldn’t be measured — plate height 300·corner radius 120 is raised with a scrub tied to section progress
Of the three recorded subpages, sapporo-open (listed as about in pages.json) and new_lp have the same news detail shape, so they were built as one detail.html

As a Studio site, transitions between pages are SPA routing — it moves straight to the next page without a shade overlay, and that page’s STUDIO entrance (.4s rest → 1.2s ease) serves as the transition. The original starts the entrance late while next-page data loads (first page ~1.2s · news ~.4s), but that wait is due to the network so it was not included

Text splitting was switched to SplitType 0.3.4 (lines, chars · punctuation grouped with the preceding character), the same as the original. The original locks the font on every split character with !important (to prevent Japanese font switching), but since this is placeholder copy it was left out
Slide deck embed (third-party slide service) is a photo placeholder — it is another service’s player, so there is nothing to rebuild of the same behavior
The four share buttons use generic symbols (×·f·+·link) instead of brand shapes
Logo imitates the original digits + hatched silhouette as 「000」 + purple hatch placeholder

title: Drawn grid plane and 3D model morphing into a point cloud
good_for: Product introductions for 3D, spatial, or technology platforms that step through features one at a time, plus a grayscale company site with news and articles.

pages.use: Product landing page — loader number, split title and photo hero (photo cursor distortion, gray clouds), a pinned section where four 3D models turn into point clouds as a feature intro, five category cards, demo video, number row and pulsing rings, two testimonials, FAQ, and a consultation call to action. For platform landings that step through features

Solutions (field) — title and photo header, one large card plus a grid of four small cards, a Dot Cloud panel where symbols fly trailing tails over a gray cloud, and a contact block for other fields. For per-field service lists and business-area overviews.
News list — large title header, one featured post over a full-panel photo, three post cards spanning 4 columns each. For blog and journal first screens
About the company — title with photo header, four principles (2×2 grid), number row, invitation to work together. For company and philosophy pages

One post — title, summary, date and photo header, left body (three subheadings) + right sticky table of contents (reading position marker) and contact box, demo invitation. For blog post · explainer article detail

notes: 3D models: the original loads four glTF models (rocket, VR headset, DNA, test tube rack) with OGL, but the model files were not carried over. They were rebuilt from our basic shapes (cylinder, box, sphere, tube, prism) with the same silhouette proportions, so they have fewer faces and are less detailed than the original. Lighting, grain removal and point-cloud transition values (3,000~22,000 points · .95s · delay .3 · swell .3×radius · settle .7s with .28s) were measured from the original and matched with a newly written shader (model-point-morph). The original’s line (outline) mode is not used by this page, so it was not built.

Photo color grading: the original runs every photo through a grayscale color filter (matrix + 6-step curve), which was left out because the photos are placeholders. The cursor flow distortion (flow-pixel-distort) is applied as is over photo placeholders and the footer wordmark canvas.

Dot cloud board (service.html): the original pushes the trail of the flying mark into a 64×64 viscous flow field to part the clouds below like a stream, but that coupling was not built — the cloud (warp-cloud-trail zoom 2.2) and the mark flight (mark-trail-flight) each use the original values as is. Next person to pick this up: add an external flow injection option (fx:wake) to warp-cloud-trail

Concentric mark (mark-heart-rings): the original draws contour lines at equal distances from the brand outline, but here they are rings stretched outward from the center, so concave symbols are a bit less smooth. The brand mark is our placeholder symbol (not a D shape)

Demo video and Lottie: the original demo video slots keep the same size and the same playback behavior (plays muted on loop when visible, pauses when 200px out of view), but the video files are left empty. The pinned section’s video stage shape (cap-showcase__stage — a panel where videos crossfade in each cell over .5s) is not used by the first page, so it was not built
The language switch (FR/EN) is looks only, with no other language version. The 20 vertical lines behind the original footer wordmark are drawn in the same .9s as the cell-line drawing

Reading (judgment): of the four recorded subpages, Gaussian Splatting, explained was classed as detail by pages.json but is a single news post, so it was built as article.html (type article). The Experiences and Features pages in the home menu were not recorded, so they link to the home page sections (#demo, #framework).

For goods · stationery · tableware brand landings

One product — a product color rail, a separately scrolling photo panel (2-column square grid, click a cell to enlarge) and an info panel (name, star rating, description, specs, cautions, options, quantity, add to cart), plus a color scroll bar. For prop product details

notes: Fonts: Inter instead of the paid original Helvetica Neue, and IBM Plex Sans KR in place of IBM Plex Sans JP for the product name

Logo — the original 4x line logo is brand artwork, so it is swapped for our own mark of thick diagonals, a cross and a thin square outline at the same position and size. The left vertical wordmark is a text placeholder

Photo — there is no original photo, so a canvas placeholder baked in the clothing color (solid fill, faint stains, diagonal lines) is used. The mosaic effect (pixel-develop blocks) runs over this image with the same cell size and spacing as the original
Product video (right of the first slide · detail video slot) uses a same-ratio placeholder and loops <video>(No file) · only a sound button

title: Color ribbons and index-tab folders forming a history timeline
good_for: Founding anniversary pages for companies or organizations, with a history timeline, member comments, archive, and event information.

pages.use: Anniversary one-pager — color ribbon opening, tab-folder timeline, color cards with member comments, character buttons, a dark event-photo section and scattered framed photos. For an n-year anniversary or history archive

notes: The original is a single page (pages: [] in pages.json), so there are no sub-pages. The original’s SP hamburger (#js-hamburger) has only a script and no element on screen, so there is no menu on phone — the copy is the same.

The logo (festival mark), vertical decorative lettering, hero big title and event title are SVG lettering in the original, so they were replaced in the same place and size with text placeholders (logo letters + circled ruby text + smiling arc + stamp) and Black Han Sans · Nanum Myeongjo type.

Event section background photo and face drawings are placeholders (each person is a one-line upper-body SVG, only the circle background color differs per person).

When the skin changes, the five colors turn together, keeping the same lightness, chroma ratio and hue spacing. To keep the original company colors, the consumer overrides --site-ribbon-*

title: White curtain lifting on a three-column hero with a photo column
good_for: Homepages for dental offices, medical practices, and small clinics, with a calm, clean tone for treatment guides and news.

pages.use: Dental home page — a hero where a vertical photo slide and a big photo’s white curtain lift sideways and a vertical-writing greeting settles down, three news lines, treatment intro (two photos + text), a two-doctor photo set with a big vertical title, four treatment boxes, map and hours table, media band, a photo band flowing along the bottom

Clinic About: body 62vw beside a 38vw fixed photo column (crossfades every 6s), page title with vertical-writing curtain reveal, large photo with centered greeting, three principles (photo + vertical English tag), map and timetable, one-line notice, entrance photo. For clinic About and Access pages
News list — category and past posts filter, two-column cards with vertical category tags (logo-slot thumbnail), page numbers. For notice and blog lists
News item — date · category · title, body with bold text mixed in, two external link buttons, four other news cards. For notice detail · a single article

notes: The original motion is jQuery Velocity 1.2.2 — the same beziers (easeInOutQuart .76,0,.24,1 · easeOutQuint .23,1,.32,1 etc.) were ported to GSAP as CustomEase. The open-source parts are the same versions: barba 2.9.7 + @barba/prefetch 2.1.10 (newly added to _vendor, MIT) · slick (Hero vertical photo fade 2s/4s, bottom photo strip 40s linear, subpage photo column 2s/6s) · jQuery 3.6.0. jquery.customSelect (select box styling) is MIT but is not in _vendor, so the same look was built in CSS.

barba 2.9 treats transitions without leave·enter hooks as a full refresh, so empty leave·enter hooks were added (the original init.js also has enter·beforeEnter). Per-page split css·js are loaded from the next page head before navigating

Logos, social icons and title graphics (the hero vertical greeting and the doctor section’s large vertical title are image text in the original) were rebuilt with Mincho vertical-writing text and circle placeholders. The doctor section’s round-window photo only reproduces the same curve ratio with border-radius
The original map is a Google Maps iframe (grayscale filter), so a same-size grayscale placeholder is used. Two media banners are placeholders too

Unbuilt subpages: the recorded ones are About, News, a single News post, and News page 2 — page 2 has the same shape as the News list, so only one was built. Links for Doctor intro, Care guide, By condition, and FAQ point to the matching sections of the built pages

title: Cursor-erased white curtain and a rotating photo ring in monochrome
good_for: Homepages for web and marketing agencies and studios with case studies, services, work lists, company info, and a blog in a black-and-white style.

pages.use: Agency home page — handwritten logo loader, hero where a cursor wipes away a white veil over video, pinned section where a photo ring spins and three cases switch, principles section where the service list pushes up and three photo columns gather into a black veil (cursor photo-fragment trails), cards flying in and stacking, FAQ, light-tube footer

Single service intro — a hero where a small video window expands to fill the screen, result number cards flowing at 33°, a CLICK section (WebGL) where the cursor tail melts into a droplet, step cards stacking over video, and a pinned step section with counting amounts. For marketing and consulting service detail pages.

Work collection — after a number loader, scrolling sends the camera flying through letter and photo panels in 3D depth (including a black stage stretch), followed by a project name list where photos pop up on hover. For portfolio and work list pages.

Company About — a fixed hero of night-city layers moving at different speeds (shooting stars · car lights on the bridge), a 3D staggered photo grid that twists in and straightens out with a band of text crossing it, a video window that opens as scattered words gather, and a fixed section where photos slide up and get cut off as tabs change
Blog post list — 1140 wide 2-column photo cards with two- or three-line titles. For insights and news lists
A single blog post — full-height dark cover with title, 680px body (subheads, lists, figures, numbered links). For long guide articles

notes: Fonts: Maison Neue (paid) → Inter, Apparel Italic (paid) → Instrument Serif italic. Korean uses Pretendard and Gowun Batang. Inter is wider than Maison, so the third line of the principles section uses nowrap to stay on one line.

Videos (hero, service window, card over video, intro video window) show only ”Playing” as a placeholder of the same position and ratio with a slowly flowing pattern (.t7-vid, 8s back and forth). The original video files were not used.

Work page 3D: the original TextGeometry (Maison Neue json) letters are in the same position and size (1px=.066) canvas text board, the photo·video boards are gray boards with name tags (video redrawn as a flowing pattern), and the two handwritten SVG logos were replaced with our signature board. Position·distance blur (50→60)·camera path (z 0→−645)·cursor parallax (±.5, .1)·black stage (z −464~−528) use the original numbers as they are. The sea background board matches only in size calculation (700/300 distance screen cover).

The photo layers of the about hero (sky · clouds · skyline · buildings · street · bridge) were redrawn as our own SVG art — layer position · size · parallax factor · camera hermite curve · shooting stars · car-light lanes use the original values. Sky and light colors are --site-* variables made from the accent hue.

Service CLICK section metaball is a new motion part, metaball-trail-gl, written from scratch with the same numbers (tail 15, smooth-min 7, ray 16, power 7, resolution .5) rather than copying the original shader. The two reflection colours must be mixed in sRGB, not oklab, to get the original brightness (with power 7, .41 vs .29 is a tenfold difference).

The footer light tubes bundle the same threejs-components@0.0.19 TubesCursor as the original into _vendor, and since ES module import is blocked on file://, tubes1.classic.js sits beside it, the same bundle wrapped in an immediately invoked function (body unchanged, only the final export became window.TubesCursor). Tube and light colors are --fx-tube-* and --fx-light-* made from the accent color hue.
The background blobs of the service stats card flow (stats-stage-blobs) are an empty slot because the original CSS has no shape rules, so they were not ported.
The ‹Design & Development› page under Services in the menu was not recorded, so it links to the service page (service.html). Contact goes to the footer (#contact).

Cursor sweep was measured on the Hero, Service CLICK, Work 3D and the four Footer items (all pass). On Work 3D and the Hero, the original photo and video patterns are dense, so the reaction area is narrower than the original (14.7%↔7.2%, 65.6%↔47.5%) — it reacts at the same spot.

title: Bursting fruit opening for a branding agency
good_for: Homepages for small branding or web studios with service lists, work lists, and company introductions.

pages.use: Agency home page — an intro where a big image bursts and settles into four service icons, three-line big title, client logo flow, sketch logo + number tags, screen-wide ABOUT US, showreel (circular progress), work band (arrows), five service rows, orange gradient Why four, review band, awards list, FAQ, and a spreading CTA

About the company — 3D line wordmark, line lettering + four numbers, mission sentence, value accordion advancing every 7.2s (overlapping 8), two co-CEOs, three kinds of clients, 12-cell client logos, testimonials
Services — five service tags floating over a full-width SERVICES, five service rows with descriptions (START A PROJECT opens a contact popup), FAQ
Work list: full-width PROJECTS + six category pills (press to filter), 2-column cards (image · name · two-line intro · tags · VIEW PROJECT), FAQ

notes: Bundle detection found lenis and ScrollTrigger, but the scripts actually loaded are only jQuery and its own main.js (with a Swiper bundle inside). Swiper is used only on a case detail page (more-projects) that we did not build, so this is built without libraries. The work strip and review strip are also library-free scroll-snap with a smooth scrollTo, like the original.

The peach, sculpture, sketch logo and wordmark use our own SVG and canvas at the same position, size and rotation instead of the original art (3D-rendered peach, logo SVG). The sketch logo only draws strokes. The original stroke-to-fill change (fill-opacity) was dropped because the lines are open.
The number 8 on the values panel is text instead of the original 10-layer SVG '8' Follows the same depth and tilt formula with 10 layers (CSS 3D) (depth 3 + 13·(.5 − .5cos), tilt −28 + 8sin, 7.2s)
The showreel is a video slot (.wf-video), so circular progress is faked with a 60-second clock — swap in timeupdate when a real video is added.

Service rows: as in the original, the number rises 8px and fades out, and an icon appears in its place (.2s·.3s). The original’s scroll reaction where the row at the center of the screen turns on by itself (psm-active) is kept as hover only

The help button (the original external chatbot) at the original position (right 20 · bottom 16) was covered by the library toolbar (list · note N) and out of reach, so it was raised to 64px from the bottom
The showreel ring updates at the original video timeupdate tempo (250ms) and delays the first update by ~.39s on replay — switch to timeupdate when a real video is added

title: Alternating cream and coffee sections linked by a milk wave
good_for: Homepages for food and dessert brands that browse products one by one, with store listings, news, and an FAQ.

pages.use: Snack brand home page — crossing-photo hero, milk-wave About, product steps turned by a pin, brand philosophy, stack of overlapping photos, stores, news, online shop band. For food and dessert brand homes
Store list — fixed category index on the left and store cards (photo · address) on the right. For shop and branch guide pages
Single news post — category and date fixed on the left, body on the right (large photo, double-line box, two photos, info box). For new product and event notices
FAQ — left table of contents that follows scroll and a question accordion opened one at a time. For brand or service FAQs

notes: The original 7 products (6 boxed sweets, 1 fresh sweet) are cut to 4 (3 boxed, 1 fresh) — the pin length follows the original rule of product count × 600px, so it is shorter than the original
Original pin length string (+=4200vh·+=3600vh) is read in px by ScrollTrigger so it is carried over as px (600 per product, 1200 per philosophy item, 400 on phone)

The brand philosophy’s 0.8s lock only returns the window scroll, as in the original — while Lenis is gliding only the catch remains and the distance is not consumed, which is the original behavior kept as is

Logo and wordmark (Brand) were swapped for the Brand Name lettering SVG and a newly drawn pinwheel symbol. The hero title is one tspan per letter, so fill-opacity lights it from the left (the original uses opacity on each letter path).

The hero cutout overlaps (transparent PNG layers where the hand and snack cover the title letters) are photos, so they are left as dotted placeholder boxes — position · size are the original values, crossing timing (first scene 0.1s · 1.7s delay) is as is

Paper grain (surface.png), blurred light bloom (top_bokashi) and milk waves (top_wave, footer_bg) are original images, so they were redrawn with SVG turbulence, radial gradients and blur curves — the waves are only a mask shape, so the color follows the skin (--kf-bg).
The original news list has only 2 items so ‹Load more› would be hidden, but to show the feature 6 items are included and expand 4 at a time
The original has no page-transition effect (only the first-visit loading), so none was built. Entering #brand or #products from another page moves to that spot right after the pin is set
Swapped the paid Helvetica Neue LT Pro and FOT-Cezanne for Inter and Gowun Dodum.

title: Rows of spinning discs and a ridgeline-tear transition to detail
good_for: Showcase sites for films, records, exhibitions, or product collections where each item is viewed large and then opened into a detail page.

pages.use: Work collection first page. A row of three discs (wheel, drag or arrows move one step), a work info table at top left, two reviews below, and clicking a disc opens detail. For a film studio or label showroom

Second collection (TV series) — the same disc gallery as the first page with a different list. The slot for the second branch of a two-branch collection like works and series, when paging, the disc recedes and pops back out.

A single work entry: large centered title, cast line, four tables, corners + two buttons between them, a trailer photo revealed by a ridge-line tear with struck-through dialogue words and the trailer curtain on top, synopsis, and the next work’s disc rising from below

notes: The disc front is a canvas-drawn placeholder instead of the original’s circular poster crop (two tone layers mixed from the skin, a figure silhouette circle, title, a cast name band along the edge, three caption lines). For real art, change the films data (label·tone) in index.js or swap A24.discArt to draw an image.

The noise images of the original disc material (grain .59·print texture .35·scratch .36 normal·roughness map), the back radial pattern, the hub grid pattern, and the RectAreaLight top strip were not carried over — it reflects only through MeshPhysicalMaterial with the same values (front clearcoat .8·rough .42·metal .48, back iridescence 1·IOR 1.86·thickness 900, hub transmission .68·IOR 2) and a canvas environment image (PMREM).

Wheel paging carries over only a reduced version of the original’s intensity envelope judgment (τ 550ms · rise 1.2× · tick ratio): a new gesture after a gap of more than 130ms, one more step when pushing at the same intensity for more than 480ms, and one step when 6 or more accumulate per gesture. An extra step on a trackpad inertia tail may happen more often than in the original.

The disc press and push physics during drag (pressDepth .55·pressTilt 1.5·wipePush·wipeSpin·push damping 4.5) and the spin that rotates the disc directly (maxSpinAngle 180·reset 1.2s) were not built — dragging only moves the line position, and on release it settles with friction .89 inertia and then .46s power3.out.
Phone layout: original ct() unreadable, so center disc diameter = Screen width .92, next disc .4x showing slightly at the right edge (gap .58 of screen width)” — approximated that way.

Torn edge: the original is a contour line (marching squares) of a 2D noise field, so small islands break off above the ridge and the ridge is bitten when the cursor passes (cursorBite .5 · drops 28). The copy and its ridge-dissolve part use only a single-line ridge (same peek .19 · reach .4 · wander .13 · center .13 · scale 230 · breath .15) — no islands and no cursor bite.

Trailer curtain: instead of the original YouTube player, a 16:9 placeholder. Only the openings are carried over — band .45s → panel 1.05s → video at .35 mark .5s → control bar at .55 mark .6s — plus the .85s close. Play, rewind and volume bar are static images.

Next work: the original’s roulette (random next-work picker), push physics (pushHold·drain·surge) and the staggered reveal of cast names are left out. Only this is built: over panel progress .3 to .97 the disc rises from tilt −52°·10° to −30°·−30°, and at the end pushing a further 620px with the wheel (disc 1.04x and lifted .1, fill ring at 10fps by the pushed amount) makes it fly off in .7s and moves on to the next work. The word slots (line of dialogue, next title) are fixed placements, not seeded from the title as in the original.

The television list is the same disc gallery in the original, so it uses the same index.css and index.js as works.html. The two details (Title A and Title B) have the same type, so one detail.html serves both.
Fonts: original PP Eiko, PP Neue Montreal and PP Museum are paid, so replaced with Bodoni Moda, Inter Tight and Cormorant Garamond (Korean: Noto Serif KR, Noto Sans KR).

Typeface placeholder text: the original is entirely Latin, so 36 spots for title and label typefaces (Bodoni Moda · Cormorant Garamond) were replaced with English placeholder text (work and series names, table names, medium and review, detail title, button, lines, next work, trailer curtain control line, disc canvas title and edge strip). No title spot was left in Korean. The header menu, list names, director/cast values, synopsis and work title lettering image spots that use the body typeface (Inter Tight) stay Korean — the original is also a body grotesque, so falling back to the Korean counterpart (Noto Sans KR) was judged to be its intended use.

In the disc edge band, English has more characters so letters get tight at the same 1.9π, so repeats were cut from 9 to 6 to keep the letter spacing close to before. Dialogue words were chosen so that on phone (390) the second-line word does not overlap the center Watch Trailer button: a sentence whose first word is two or three letters and whose second word is one letter (Oh, a long way down). A four-letter first word (STAY) went past the right edge on phone.

title: Six shuffling words and a three-way archive view switcher
good_for: One-page archives for game, stage, or album microsites that switch one list between large type, a name list, and a photo grid.

pages.use: One archive page — behind a loading screen, six large monospace words swap cells every 7 seconds and shuffle into place, the top ●▶■ and side dots switch between text, name list and photo grid views (?type=opens directly as list·visual). On a special page for browsing people·episodes together

notes: The original is a single page (pages: [] in pages.json), so there are no sub-pages. In the original, the text, name and photo slots are links to a person detail page (new tab), so href="#" Left as a placeholder.

Typeface: Martian Mono (width axis 75%) instead of the original NB Architekt (paid). Capitals are 6% taller than the original, so large letters are 230px × .943 (--a3-glyph), and labels are 15px × .893 (--a3-label) with 87.5% width to match the glyph cell width — shared.css :root. When changing the typeface in a skin, set these ratios to 1. The glyph cell (133.2px) and line cell (200px) are the original values, so the layout stays the same even if the typeface changes.

VOICE button: the original plays a person’s voice mp3 to the end through buzz, then clears the playing state. There is no audio file, so only a 3-second playing state (orange · press blocked) is kept — when adding sound, replace the index.js voiceTimer spot with the audio end event.
The original reloads the page when crossing 768px to switch the PC/phone version. We switch in place with CSS media and resize (no reload).

The original starts the loading screen after downloading all 26 images (up to 3s) — ours are placeholders, so it starts 30ms after the text finishes unfolding, and the first shuffle of the letter panel is timed to when loading clears, with a part delay of 3.7s.

The 7s-beat retyping of corner labels (per-group random delay 0–.8s, .02/.03s per character) exists only in this site’s shared.js — type-on has no repeat option, so I did not extract it as a part. Whoever adds repeat, jitter (shared per group) and grow (lengthens without taking up space) options to type-on can move it over.

title: Side photo that opens and folds above a staggered work grid
good_for: White-background sites for architecture, interior, and photography studios with work lists, project details, about, and contact pages.

Work list — three-line header and category picker, seven staggered groups (thirteen cards) of portrait and landscape photos with empty cells. For portfolio and case lists

Contact — two-line heading, three columns for address, contact and social, underline input form, wide photo. For contact and booking form pages

notes: The original lightbox opened by clicking a photo in the work detail (site-specific Svelte code) was not built — a to-do for the next person to rewrite the same behavior (photo zoom, paging, close) and carry on
The big text on the About page stands in for the original logo initials (SVG), so three English placeholder letters (STD) are set in the heading typeface — the logo shape was not redrawn.

The original menu’s FAQ page was not captured, so it was not built (link is #)

The white dot cursor was built in site code instead of the dot-cursor-grow part — of the original values (20px, follows .45s power3, over links 80px · opacity .15 over .55s power3.out, −16px offset when small), the opacity and offset are not available as part options. The values are noted in the part’s fx.json source.

title: Rounded panels with flowing lavender noise bands for a finance app
good_for: Product sites for apps, fintech, or developer tools that present several products as individual panels, with company, blog, careers, and article pages.

pages.use: Product home — four rounded panels laid with noise bands (three app phones · dark pro-mode dashboard and market card · cube and horizontally swiping partners · trust icon cards and revenue graph), number cards, FAQ accordion, newsletter signup

About the company — big two-line title, event photo with a description pill following the cursor, two-column history, three number cards (one is two rows tall), fan-shaped holographic value cards, three News items
Blog list — one wide featured post, sliding black pill filter, ten rows with photo left · text right, page numbers, three category cards
Careers — five photos flying in from below and floating, two-column team intro, nine benefit cells, numbered interview-step accordion cards, postings by department

The original’s number wheel (number-flow), live interest gauge inside the phone screen, Rive art and token logos are replaced with placeholder numbers and our own SVG/CSS art — there is no rolling-number motion.
