Sound: in the original, entering turns on background music and effects (hover · scene transition), and a waveform button turns them off. Here there is only an on/off state with breathing waveform bars, and no actual sound.

The Light panel button changes its text to another panel name, like the original, and the loader 'Baking shaders'Spins again from the start, but there is no actual panel transition. Light panel and lab in the menu, legal notice and lab in the footer, and SNS and mail are only placeholders (#).

Our shader paints the same page-transition veil as the original scene post-processing, with the same numbers: progress 0→1 cover 1.1025s sine.out (2.45s × .45), 1→2 reveal 1.3475s sine.inOut (× .55), a threshold mixing the screen diagonal (top left → bottom right) with 3-layer noise (scale 7.3, flowing with progress × .4) at .21, edge .13, brightness +35%, previous screen 9% darker, veil color #262626 (89% background + text color), and text and buttons on screen hidden for .2s during progress 0~1.6. The original refracts the 3D image (.12) at the edge, but we skipped it because the DOM page is under the veil, and the noise is our own, so the cloud pattern differs. The original has no symbol on the veil, so it was removed. The enter door appears only on the first page opened, and after that pages transition by veil (like the original SPA). Adding #enter to the URL skips the enter door (for capture). Pressing enter locks the button like the original and its text fades to 30%, and the loader fades over .9s after .1s and is cleared at 1020ms. The enter button roll uses the original values (.47s · .0187s per letter · power4.out, always upward).

Detail: the original drew text on a 1920-wide canvas and attached it to a 3D panel. The same coordinates (title 64, body 22/32, gaps 44·72, photo 1573, gallery 1134 …) were moved into DOM vertical rows in --d units. The gallery advances every 4 seconds and a bar below fills — in the original, the gallery carousel inside the detail panel shader advances with outside progress values (t.carousel, t.progress), but the place that sets those values is missing from the received bundle pieces (some were lost when unpacking the archive because projects file and folder names collided), so the interval could not be measured.

Leave a spot for the creator’s portrait photo in the big frame in the middle of About 'Reversal' …made it appear at that point — I couldn’t see exactly when and where the original portrait (portraitPane) shows up. Gauge line and label coordinates are values measured on the 1440 screen, converted to vw/vh.

Typeface placeholder notes: the spots where the original used the Latin heading typeface (League Spartan) — the entry door name, entry button, light-version button (pressing gives Full version), scroll hint, work names (the six items in the slide list), next-work button, HUD title, about heading and its changing word, contact heading, detail number, title and the two subheadings — were replaced with English placeholders, and data-label says what belongs in each spot. The entry door name went back to the original values (2·cell/.66 · letter spacing -.07em) after being reduced for Korean. The about heading does not restore the capital-height trim (text-box) that was removed for Korean

Where the body font (Manrope) is used, keep Korean even if the original is Latin: the entrance door what-we-do line, loader status line, menu, ‹Taking on work›, explore work, drag hint, captions, about subtitle, name card, small HUD labels (file name, label 2, origin, residence), contact email, detail close, subtitle, role, shortcuts, next work, tail. The README says to use English only in the Latin title-font slots, and Pretendard, which Manrope falls back to, is a similarly bold gothic, so it was left as is (the menu is in the body font in the original too, so it is included here)

Phone: the original directs small screens to /lite (alternate link). Here the same 3D scene is shown in a portrait layout (wider view · flower top center · small hand), and the menu is a drawer dropping from the top per the original portrait rule.

”Scroll ↓” follows the original formula: it scrolls down to the 38.88% point of the first scene (the arch, i.e. the door face), taking remaining distance ÷ 74.2358vh seconds (1.2~7s) along a quintic curve (6t⁵−15t⁴+10t³). Crystal drag: dragging over 80px goes to the next·previous work (the original drag threshold could not be found in the bundle).

3D scene material colors (stone, moss, leaves, lily petals, sunlight) are scene content so they stay inside the scene, while accent lights (door glow, light inside the crystal, water light, flower light, blue point light) are made by rotating only the hue from the skin’s --kf-accent.

title: Shape-shifting letter loader and color-echo layers for an agency
good_for: Homepages for digital agencies and studios with work lists, case details, services, about, careers, and news, or video-heavy B2B brand sites.

pages.use: Agency home page — loader where wordmark letters change shape as they rise to the header, hero where a small pinned video grows to fill the screen (color echo behind), nine staggered Work cards, testimonial slider · client logo wall, five service cards, four article cards, black footer. For a video-centered agency hero
Work list: a large title rising from the bottom edge of the screen, a monospace uppercase filter, and 4-column and 3-column work cards (service tags rise in turn on hover). For the portfolio list

Services — two-line title, sticky table of contents (the visible item turns darker), and per service a description, detail rows, button and side case card, plus reviews, logo wall and article cards. For showing several services on one page

About the company — long intro paragraph, big lettering panel and story cards, black band with a row of big numbers, client cards, team table (hover a row and a yellow line and photo follow the cursor). For company and team intros

Careers — hero where a yellow header panel peels away and the title rises, four numbered values, a photo strip that flows sideways while pinned, black open-position rows (both ends gather inward on hover). For a careers page
News list — one-line title, monospace filter, text cards alternating square and portrait with long-summary news cards, load more. For blog and news collections

Work detail: a left info column (tags · industry table · visit site) with a large video, a sticky contents list (the summary of the visible section expands), full-width, two-column and split media rows per section, and other work. For introducing a single case.

notes: The original runs on a WordPress theme bundle (gsap 3·ScrollTrigger·SplitText·MorphSVG·Flip·CustomEase, Lenis 1.3.17 inside the bundle, Swiper) — we use the same GSAP plugins (_shared/vendor) and the same Lenis 1.3.17. The bundle does not state the Swiper version, so we used 11.2.10 (fade crossFade·speed 0·controller·navigation are the same settings)

The wordmark loader doesn’t use the original lettering art. The eight letters LOGOTYPE were redrawn as bold shape letters — the starting shape is a rounded bar so MorphSVG morphs bar → letter like the original (the original morphs letter to letter)
The cookie consent bar (plugin), bot verification check and analytics scripts are external widgets, so they were not built

The filter (FacetWP) just hides by tag text instead of server filtering, and only the original’s re-rise of the remaining cards (40px .6s power2.out .1 stagger) is applied. News ‹Load more› is visual only
Customer logos, testimonial company logos and article card images are left as shape and text SVGs and placeholders noting what to insert, instead of original images
Fonts: Messina Sans and Messina Sans Mono (paid) → Geist and Geist Mono. Korean placeholders fall back to the system sans, so the heading line count may differ from the original by about one line

Clients, Contact, service sub-pages (Strategy etc.) and article detail pages were not recorded, so they were not built — menu links lead to the About clients section, the footer contact panel and the service page

Screen compare (compare seven shots at 1440 · first page at 390) matched the original in composition, position and rhythm, with 0 console errors and 0 horizontal overflow (1440·390). Hover·click was checked on the first page at 1440 against the original (full menu · button ▶ jump · card hover).

title: Sections that cover the previous one from above for an embroidered bag shop
good_for: Shops for high-end handcrafted or fashion brands, made-to-order workshops, and photo-rich brand story sites.

pages.use: Brand home page: a hero video with blur-sweep text, a large quote revealed by a mask, two category cards that overlap, descend and grow, a Collection (promo card plus six cards), full-photo sections that cover from above (white box, steps), a city section swept by a white band, a 360° color-change spinner, a three-way split, a history line, a social feed strip, and trust logos. For a photo-led premium brand home.

Brand story — photo hero, a quote with a small photo, split sections alternating photo and text left and right, a text-over-photo section, and a closing quote. For company or workshop intros and history stories
Custom order guide — photo hero, quote, process chapters, text over photo, booking request card (underline input fields). For service pages that take consultations and bookings

Product list — serif category tabs, a count and filter bar stuck under the header line, four-column cards (five photos with arrow paging, sold-out label), right filter drawer, pagination, reservation card. For shopping mall lists

notes: Title font FreightBig Pro is paid, so it was replaced with the closest free high-contrast serif Cormorant Garamond — glyph width is slightly narrower at the same size
Cart, login and currency switch are look only (currency changes text only). Product detail and cart drawer pages were not recorded, so they were not built
Only four of the six sharing sections on the About page were built (same type repeated). The custom order page keeps the recorded type: three sharing sections, one text-over-photo, booking
The original large featured cell in the list (agnes-catalog__feature, 2×2) does not appear on the one recorded page, so it is not included
The placeholder videos media/loop-16x9.mp4 and loop-2x3.mp4 are ffmpeg gradient loops

Font backfill — the original is an English site, so all 63 title-font spots and the header wordmark were replaced with English placeholder text (Korean kept: 0). Header and footer menus, product names and eyebrow text sit in the body font Jost (Korean paired with Pretendard), so they were left in Korean

title: Panels stacking from one corner for a brand and web studio
good_for: Homepages for design and development studios or B2B agencies with case collections and a blog.

pages.use: Studio home page: a big title with only the first line set flush to the left edge, a photo reel that passes through corner circles, client logos, staggered work rows, and white, ink, blue and sky sections stacking as rounded-corner panels. These are About, a letter, a text strip, a service card stack, a check input, a work process where four page marks line up, testimonials, two approach panels and an FAQ. For agency and studio landing pages.
About — one-line big heading and a long letter from the CEO in a single block (center 7 columns). For company intro and CEO message pages
Single service description — back row, four-line big title, dark summary panel, long text with subheads and lists, FAQ. For solution and service detail pages
Work list — staggered case photo list repeating a four-block pattern (7 columns · right 4 columns lower · left 4 columns · right 6 columns lower). For portfolio and case lists
Blog list — one large post first (8 columns) and a three-column post list staggered by lowering only the middle column. For blog and news lists

One case study — back and category row, large name, cover photo, serif summary with three columns for client, role and tools, dark number strip, four stories with pinned subheads and photo pairs, two other works. For Work case detail

notes: Work rows (home) cut from the original 8 rows to 4 (including 2 with quotes), the work list from 34 cells to 8 (a four-cell layout twice), the blog from 12+ posts to 1 large + 9 cells — all layout types kept

The original typeface Ploni is paid, so the free geometric sans Figtree is used, backed by Pretendard and Noto Serif KR for Korean. Bold Korean titles touched line to line, so only the .display line spacing was raised from .94 to 1

The original logo (a pinwheel of four quarter circles) is not used and is replaced by a four-petal symbol rounded outward. The header, page-turn cover, large footer mark and work-process pieces all use the same symbol

The original changes pages with Astro ClientRouter (view transitions) and draws a cover over them. Here it is a real page navigation handed over through sessionStorage, so the cover lifts only on the arriving page, built with the same numbers (.7s/.8s expo.inOut, after .35s shown). There is no cover on the first visit (same as the original).
The AI check input fills in placeholder results (pass · warning · fail) at .14s intervals without a real request. The agent panel’s markdown is also a placeholder
Hebrew (RTL) version · language switching only has a link slot — the script is dir=Built like the original so that rtl flips the circle corner and strip direction
Once chosen, the cookie card does not show again in the same tab (sessionStorage) — the original keeps the same card across page transitions

Subpages are only the five recorded ones (About · one Solution · Work list · Blog · Work detail) — Service, Contact and FAQ list pages have no recordings, so those menu links point to sections of the first page.

Font backfill: the original is an English site, so .display headings (Figtree uppercase), italic serif words, the menu, wordmark, consult and footer titles and big footer name inserted by JS, the example address in the check input, and work detail paragraph titles (serif) were changed to English filler (zero Hangul kept). Sentences set in serif such as .statement, .lead and quotes (first line of the CEO letter, reviews, slogans, check results) are body sentences, so they stay Korean and use the Noto Serif KR pair.

Text length fit — the home hero is set to two lines (six words) like the original, and the solution hero to four lines. Units after home numbers 2–6 are left blank like the original (English units would overflow the cell)

title: Wheel-driven jar carousel and product pages where items fly in to land
good_for: Brand homepages for food, cosmetics, or beverages with few bottled products, including category-banded listings, a table view, and product detail pages.

pages.use: Jam jar carousel first page — a ring of jars turned by wheel or drag, and pressing one makes it fly to the product page and land. For homepages of food and cosmetics brands with only a few products
Product list — opening photo panel head, category cell band with product slider, dark photo panel, small bottle table, closing photo. Bottle and container products live in the brand warehouse
Single product detail — the head where the bottle flying in from home lands, info list, drag-through photo strip, other products. For food and cosmetics product details

notes: The jar body redraws the original cut-out jar photo slot as an SVG glass jar illustration (when inserting a photo, swap out .jar-svg just change it to switch (data-label notes what photo it is). As in the original, the label is wrapped around a three r160 cylinder (height .27~.87 · width .885 · 3° tilt · LatheGeometry 128×16, ambient light .89 · spot .58×5 x −1, roughness .72, 9% of the circumference gap discarded), rotated, and copied onto a 2D canvas for each bottle — the label art is our own drawing: instead of the original label photo, it draws product-colored bands, circles, waves and names on canvas

In the original, pressing the bottle changes the page mid-flight (after .42s) so the product title appears under the bottle. Blocked: the original hands the bottle over through the Nuxt router (site app code) without swapping the document, but in a static multi-page template the flying bottle is cut off when the document changes. So the bottle settles fully over 2s and then moves on to detail.html, the bottle stays exactly where it is, and only the rest appears at .35s.

The product detail page (detail.html) is not in the pages.json recording list, but it is the destination of the home bottle fly-away and the product tiles, so I built it by looking at the original detail page. The title fit (--ph-title-fit) and the drop were ported from the original formulas in simplified form (meta position on tablet and below is simplified)

The 11 loader fruits were redrawn from the original silhouettes as angular single-color polygons (body polygon = Physics bodies, fruit’s own colors are ‹Not Skin›). The original’s 22 pieces, gravity 3.35 and body values are the same, and physics is the same matter-js 0.20.0 as the original. The original keeps a separate vertex table per fruit shape

The original typefaces ivymode and ivystyle-sans are paid fonts from a font service, so Marcellus and Nunito Sans stand in. The substituted Marcellus capitals are wider than the original ivymode, so English titles use short words (Range, Third, etc.) to keep words from breaking mid-word at phone width

The language switch has only look and hover and does not go to other-language pages. Of the menu’s 'Making process'·'Farm Experience'· The secondary link points to a page that wasn’t recorded, so it is set to #
sites pull stalled on a conflict (EEXIST) between the /en file and the /en/dispensa folder, so the archived HAR (desktop·pages) was unpacked separately in /tmp and read

Font backfill: the original is the English edition, so every heading-font (Marcellus) slot was swapped to English placeholder text — wordmark STUDIO/Name (header·footer), four menu items, perimeter slogan, the roll-it-around line, bottle-label product names (Product 01~08, both canvas and SVG), list heads, cover sentence, four category titles, detail product name·category·origin lines, other-products strip title. No heading-font slot is left in Korean. Body-font (Nunito Sans) slots — menu buttons, cursor pill, category pager, table, address — stay in Korean as they are
Judgment: the italic second word under the logo uses --kf-font-script (Gowun Batang first), so even the English Name is drawn in Gowun Batang’s Latin letters — the skin (theme.css) was not touched

title: Tilted video rows and seven pinned scenes for a video production service
good_for: Landing pages for video and ad production, AI or creative services, and B2B services with many case examples.

pages.use: Service one-page landing — a 7s loader, then a hero of a video row tilted 15°, logo marquee, about, What we do (pinned) where a 3×3 photo grid zooms in and passes on, four challenge cards, a showreel with a cross-shaped hole that grows and a case panel that unfolds from the center, TV and phone scene support (pinned), horizontally flowing step cards, FAQ, customers (pinned) where seven photos gather, news, a company section where a curtain lifts, two contact panels, and a video-row footer

Contact — hero with two large full-width English title lines where each letter stands in, left guidance and right underline-input form (select, check, textarea, consent, submit), and a footer with a four-cell line panel

notes: The 11 videos (five tilted rows in the hero · reel · five footer rows) are static placeholder cells — the original plays when visible and pauses when not (iObserver), and picks a short version on Mac PCs · one long row otherwise. On the placeholder cells <video loop muted playsinline> If this is set, the line shift (15°, ±screen width×.15 rem, 3s oi) still applies.

Fonts: Brand Light (paid) → Lexend Giga 300, Brand Display (paid serif) → Bodoni Moda, Noto Sans JP → Noto Sans KR since the slot is Korean. The hero title was an SVG piece in the original (pc and sp, two sets), so it was turned into per-letter spans with flicker-on look: glitch (shift 50) applied.

The scroll lock in the weDo and company scenes is done only with Lenis stop. The original also blocks wheel and keys via x.event.disableEvent and pins the position with window.scrollTo. The stage-by-stage lock conditions (first cell only when scrolling up, middle cell always, last cell only when scrolling down) are kept as in the original.

The reel’s cross-shaped hole uses our cross path as a CSS mask (hole) instead of the original reel_mask.svg = drawn with linear-gradient XOR svg) — the size formula (16rem → 16 × screen height ÷ 3.6rem) is the same as the original.

On phones (767px and below), the original sp scenes (weDo 25·50·75% steps, reel panel unfolding, apply steps) are hooked up the same way, but the sp-only text entrance (reelText·coachMark guide) is not included. The clients·company·flow pinned scenes run on pc only, like the original.

On the original first page, the text-swap hover of the nav menu panel links and the contact menu (conversionMenu, fixed below the phone) was not applied to the menu panel links (they are only visible while the panel is open).

The Contact page follows the main site’s form (three header lines, big title, form, four-cell panel). The big title is the original Splitting chars + chars-in as is (50% below, skew −10°, 8°, rotateX −30° → in place, 1s cubic-bezier(.075,.82,.165,1), .08s stagger). The top line, Brand italic, is the skin’s serif italic, while the bottom line A2Z Faucet (narrow sans-serif, paid) uses the skin’s title font (Lexend Giga — wide type), so the bottom line’s letters are wider than the original. The form does not send (no reCAPTCHA or contact-form-7).
Of the 180 minutes of work, a good 40 were spent waiting for a browser seat (one student per row, taken in turns).

title: Photos that stack and then enlarge for a square-house brand
good_for: Homepages for housing developers, architecture, and interior brands, including opening animations and calm, spacious company introductions.

pages.use: Brand home page — a scroll-locked opening (five photos stack then turn into a color square), a center square that changes color every 2 seconds, black-and-white → color photos and lines flowing with parallax, a square that grows to fill the screen on scroll, a large photo seeping out diagonally, lead text rising line by line, a blue-gray background case study (large photo pinned), an intro photo that changes when you hover the menu, a dotted-cell blog, and a contact square. For brand landing pages with an opening

Case list — a header where empty boxes get drawn, category pills and a region row on a blue-gray panel, a case list alternating a large-cell/small-cell pair with a three-cell row (monochrome → color), pagination, scattered monochrome photos and a story section. For photo-driven work and case lists (the category list /works_cat/subdivision-house has the same form)

About the company — a changing square and quote beside the title, wide photo, story (line-split text, two photos, color square), philosophy, two profiles, dotted overview table, access map. For company and brand intros

Services — hero photo that grows from a square to full screen height on scroll, two imagination cards, quality (tabs, specs, diagram, grade cells), three case cells, collapsible support list, and a closing photo that seeps up from below every 5s. For service, quality and method intro pages
Blog and news list — centered title, category pills and word list, colored square card list alternating one large cell + two small cells / four small cells, page numbers. For blog and news lists

notes: The grid pattern, case section and footer textures were repeating PNG images in the original, so they were redrawn with SVG feTurbulence noise laid over the skin color in overlay and soft-light — the grain is more even than the original.
Hero slogan, intro copy and other spots where the original is SVG lettering are set as Korean text (Noto Serif KR) at the same place and size.
The black-and-white → color photo is a placeholder, so the color cell is filled with a pale gray-blue mix and the B&W cell with gray, so only the change is visible
The original SplitText line splitting does not use the same build but the GSAP SplitText (3.15) in _shared, with the same values (lines · 20% below · .6s sine.out · 60% of screen)
The category case list (/works_cat/subdivision-house) has the same shape (same script and markup) as the case list, so works.html stands in for both
The diagrams in the service quality cells (seismic construction, insulation cross-section) are original artwork, so they are left as picture placeholders (the label says which diagram)
Directions map uses a map placeholder instead of a Google Maps iframe
The phone menu panel is simpler than the original panel (logo, menu, contact link), with only five menu lines — the 1s sine.out float up from 20px below has the same values

title: Horizontal flow with a group photo rushing forward
good_for: Founding anniversary microsites, employee-centered brand campaigns, staff voice collections, and playful history timelines.

pages.use: Anniversary site first page — a fixed Hero where seven panels drift sideways and a running group photo stands in the center, a breathing red ribbon, intro text, an endlessly flowing staff photo gallery (modal), a vertical-writing poem card, CEO message, policy article slider, history entrance, red footer. For anniversary·campaign landing pages

Employee voices — round photo header, for each of four topics three vertical-text poem cards and VIEW ALL (modal where doors open), and ”A Verse from Here” where a new verse lights when the bamboo water-clapper tips. For staff interviews and submission collections

Company history — a rounded photo header, a video spot (modal) above big MOVIE text, and a timeline slot machine where pressing START spins a four-digit reel that stops on a year and opens that year’s story. For history and heritage pages

One news article (company main-site style) — left pinned menu, pink title panel, tag·date, large photo, two photos side by side, subheading·list·quote, video slot, contact box. For press releases and event report posts

notes: The running group photo has two layers, back and front, as in the original (so the ribbon passes between people), but since it is a placeholder the front layer is an empty cell cut as a polygon — put in two real cutouts (full back·people-only front) and the ribbon passes between them like the original.

The photo and sentence positions of the seven hero panels carry over the landscape values from the original css, and each panel’s ribbon curve was redrawn as our own SVG (thickness 56~62, DrawSVG 2s sine.in/out · thickness .7↔1)

The gallery ”CLICK!” marker is text instead of an image, and the bamboo deer-scarer, door modal and slot machine body are our own SVG·CSS shapes (motion values from the original: 2s shake keyframes, door .6s·2.25x, reel 1.3s+.25s·i)
Timeline slot values are placeholder years (0001…0047) and the modal text for each year is a placeholder — the original has ten real years of company history.
Phone (390) comparison was run on the first page only — the phone checks of the three lower pages are left for the next person to continue

title: Single-blue contents notebook where the cursor leaves lens marks
good_for: Research notes, design principle collections, and documentation sites where the chapter and article list is the front page, or experimental text-only personal sites.

pages.use: Home: a left vertical index panel (wordmark, three sections, numbered post list, post count), a center 26-letter alphabet board (only linked letters get a dot), and a cursor lens trail across the whole screen. For the cover of document and notes sites.

Section contents — the contents panel stays as is (marker strip on the current section), with a section symbol, section name and numbered text list centered in the body. For the first screen of a section or category on documentation sites.

notes: Three subpages (Preface, Foundations, UIs) are chapter tables of contents of the same type, so they were built as one page.html. Every chapter link in the contents panel goes to page.html. The single article page (article detail) was not recorded, so it was not built

The original’s 4.2s (6.8s on subpages) blank first screen is WebGPU engine and glyph atlas download time, so it was not carried over — only the changing stretch (533ms) is done as a same-cell gather in .7s
The original #app scrolls with Lenis, but the recorded pages are all one screen (900px), so no scroll panel is set up — whoever builds long-text pages should add lenis.

The original wordmark (Brand logo image) and the top-right symbol (a drawing of four letters joined by dotted lines) were redrawn as our own artwork with the same position, size, and texture (five lowercase English letters in mixed typefaces, an SVG joining the four letters with a dotted curve, a solid line, and a double line). Section symbols are small chevron·corner marks drawn with a shader per section, kept here as a single SVG chevron.
Fonts: Alte Haas Grotesk Bold → Inter Tight 700, Garara (paid experimental serif) → Fraunces variable weight (the three Garara, Garara-0 and Garara-10 faces in the font set → 400·100·900).

title: Round photos slowly drawing near for a neighborhood animal clinic
good_for: Homepages for veterinary, medical, dental, or pharmacy practices that must always show hours and booking buttons, with a friendly tone from hand-drawn people and animals.

pages.use: Clinic home page — Hero with four rounded-corner photos slowly zooming in and changing (vertical text on the right, hours table panel), three-line notice, two treatment rows plus three cards, four feature cards, flowing English band and About, column cards, wavy Contact band, map, white card Footer. For neighborhood clinic or shop homes

Hospital features — four circle-image + large-heading introductions alternate left and right, with an orange-clipped white box between each (check list · dot list · circle list), photo intro row, thick blue-bordered notice box. For service and strengths pages.

News list — dotted category list on the left, on the right photo + category pill · date · title · one-line summary cards (Pick up band on the corner), circle page numbers, Past posts blue-outlined accordion. For notice · column · hiring news lists

A single News item — same left-hand category as the list, pill, date and large title, white table-of-contents box, body with dash-prefixed blue subheadings, ‹Back to list› button with previous/next arrows, and an accordion of past posts. For notice or column detail pages (the same article was also captured as about during recording)

Recruit info — message (photo + text + check box), four numbered-pill appeal points (photo row, benefits box, staff comment speech bubble), left sticky job type list + right per-job duty boxes, white rounded Contact section. For clinic and shop recruit pages

notes: The original people and animal illustrations (png) were redrawn as our own SVG sprites (shared.js — two people, two dogs, two cats, a rabbit, a clipboard) at the same position and size, tied together with paint variables. The poses are not as delicate as the original (kneeling vet, stethoscope) — only silhouette, color placement and size are matched

The original fonts fot-tsukuardgothic (rounded gothic) and pauza (English label) are on a paid font subscription service, so we swapped them for a rounded Korean sans (+ Zen Maru Gothic) and Saira. The distributed css for the rounded Korean sans has no font-display, so we redeclared the same woff2 in theme.css with swap

The original attaches body.loaded to window load, but that site loads fonts after load, so the first paint and load nearly coincide. Ours has a late load because of web fonts, so we attach it two frames after DOMContentLoaded (hero photo·vertical copy·appointment table and the subpage hero appear in the same order and length)
The map (map embed), payment method logos and partner insurance badges are left as placeholder cells

title: Cloud bands, winged line art, and floating child illustrations
good_for: Warm homepages for nurseries, kindergartens, children's schools, and pediatric clinics with education policy, strengths, daily life, and tour inquiries.

pages.use: Nursery school home page — a hero with five fading photos (each with white wings and bird lines drawn like brush strokes) and cloud hills, two vertical strip banners at the right edge, an education policy with three arch photos and a dove thread line, a sky panel with a stipple sun rising and two features (photo and text in a zigzag), a wavy-edge video, a school intro with four round shortcuts, a photo strip bouncing in odd/even rhythm, and two daily life columns. For a children’s institution landing

title: Pixel-art portfolio paged one screen at a time with a feedable creature
good_for: A one-page personal developer or designer portfolio that shows work, about and contact (booking calendar and inquiry form) one screen at a time.

pages.use: A one-screen-at-a-time portfolio — hero with a dot creature you feed · one-line work list · dot-portrait About · schedule/message tabs with calendar · dot-speech footer. For a solo developer or designer one-page intro

notes: The original is a single page (pages: [] in pages.json), so it has no subpages. The original’s work detail (/proyectos/<Name>) is not recorded so it was not built, and list rows are anchored to the same panel.

The original uses a single library, gsap (Astro ClientRouter is a single page so there is no transition) — the copy uses only gsap too. The dot art was rebuilt from the original’s numbers: the crocodile is drawn with PITCH -1.32 tilt plus perspective 1/(K2 6+depth), and normals are rotated along with it to catch light (mouse→floor is solved without perspective in the original too). The portrait’s cell size changes continuously from 7→3.5px by cursor-to-frame distance (distance ratio squared, .12 per frame) and is drawn with an 8×8 Bayer threshold·base brightness .52→.34·blur .68→.9·edge .1, and the button sticks within 8px of the cursor and flips to the opposite side at 6px from the frame edge (enter 1x .35s power3.out · exit .96x .2s power2.out). The city dot field follows the original rules down to 36-cell slots·two families (lifetime 1.37x)·wave .38s·windows 10%·two-cell shadows·B00 brackets·linking two neighbors·cursor cloud (spring .38·tail 2·sway)·N00 tracking box and linking the nearest three. Eye·horse use a 2×2 sample per cell·thresholds .55/.22·reveal after .15s over 1.1s power2.out — the eye has knee .35·contrast around the eye 1.9·whole-image parallax 1.6·two reflected-light letters, the horse has threshold .4·gamma .5·stroke preservation·hover radius 30 cells of scatter (noise blotches·erase .22·shake .6·push 7).

The portrait, eyes and horse are the original’s video, photo and photo-strip sequence rendered as dots and letters, so they are rendered with the same cell size and formula, but with canvas-drawn placeholders instead of the original images (a profile of a face in a hat, almond eyes, 15 frames of a galloping horse with a rider). Each slot’s Photos (portraits are

The booking calendar in the contact panel was originally an external booking widget embedded in the same colors, so a calendar of the same dark tone (date picking only) is drawn directly. The inquiry form is not sent.
The language switch only has motion: the box expands and on selection the wordmark and intro letters unravel (85ms swap, 380ms), and the text itself does not change.

The label typeface Mono RGO Modular is paid, so it was replaced with the angular free mono Share Tech Mono + the Korean Nanum Gothic Coding (the B00 · N00 · distance numbers in the city dot field also use --kf-font-mono). Korean labels look slightly smaller than the original uppercase labels.

Skin: the 15 non-standard variables in theme.css (three dot-pattern greens·ink light·light footer paper·text gray·margin) were moved to --site-* in shared.css :root (values built from the accent·background·--kf-contrast-* with color-mix·oklch(from)), and 60 hard-coded colors were swapped for those variables. The canvas paints with the skin variables received as the sRGB the screen resolves (rgbOf). The black of the mask is read only for alpha, so it is left as not skin.

Font backfill: since the original text is all English, the Instrument Sans heading slots (three intro lines of the band, scroll hint, six work names with their bar duplicates, right-side caption, section titles, four section names of the menu panel) and the mono kickers caught by the check (contacts, channels and local time in the footer and menu) were replaced by English placeholders. The wordmark title is already English. The remaining mono labels, buttons, form text and calendar are body-style, so they stay Korean (the Nanum Gothic Coding · Noto Sans KR pair handles them).

Section images: library-shots --again shoots only the first panel (hero-feed-creature) and stops from the second panel with ”Clipped area is either empty or outside the resulting image” — the panel is off-screen inside a transform track, so scrollTo can’t reach it (the shots folder also had only one hero image from the start). Per-panel checks were shot one at a time by flipping with AC.snap.go (/tmp/lib-brand-netlify-app-type-3).

The wheel scroll in compare.cjs can’t get past the first panel on snap sites (same in the original), so the per-panel comparison was shot separately by advancing one section at a time with the snap:step event (/tmp/lib-name-site-panels-*).

A single column article — tag, date, title, Helpful button and share, header image, TOC box, body with red-dot subheadings (table, quote box, diagram, band banner, reference links), author card, resource info panel, recommended slider, and a pinned ranking sidebar. notes: Construction-line panel: the original is a 974×974 mp4 (13.013s loop), so the same composition, length and repetition were redrawn on canvas (Motion part construct-lines) — from the original’s 390 frames I measured nine lines (the timing and direction at which white lines are drawn and withdrawn over the always-present orange guide lines), eight circles (one orbit lap · diagonal back-and-forth · vertical-axis flip · slipping off at an angle then bouncing into place · drawn angle · opacity) and the radius curves of two groups of concentric circles, and transcribed them into a 0.2s table. The sub-section header image is a single still in the original too (img_sub-mv01), so the still 2.2 was pulled in at zoom 1.42 · at 0.381 0.625 to match the same spot (X crossing · two vertical lines · small circle) — the original’s still is not one frame of the video but a separate drawing of the same construction lines, so a few circles differ

Pattern tiles (keyword band · recommended tiles · menu cards · series band) are redrawn with SVG polygons · arcs · grains, since the original uses two polygon pattern photos (normal · hover). Kept as is — the About section illustration is the slot of the original artwork (1200×1500), so we redrew our own line art in the same 4:5 frame and composition: a line winding in an S from the seed at the bottom to the flower at the top, three oval islands (farm · industrial city · forest and sea), and 60-odd props (house · tractor · water tank · cow · recycling bin · smokestack factory · windmill · building · speech bubble · forest · boat · aquaculture ring · picnic · musician · swing · kite · bicycle · ladder) in the same places as the original. Differences of the ended version (password-protected video slot, pink notice band, gray ”Event ended” button) were not built — the video is hosted externally, so keeping the same playback behavior as a placeholder would require designing a password-entry panel first
SNS icons are drawn in a single text color (follows the skin) instead of the original’s brand colors. The header date uses today’s date like the original

Cards (teardowns/cards) were auto, so this time the seven axes, motion and key scene were filled in

title: Knitting pattern collection with a blobby Lottie hero and hand-labeled photo cards
good_for: A hobby or craft resource collection (patterns, recipes, templates) or a small shop or archive where photo cards help visitors choose a category.

pages.use: Collection home — the first Lottie panel where a blob matte reveals the photo, a white left menu (buttons turn the Swiper panels), method · item · pattern photo cards (vertical labels · popping-out hand drawings), a store banner and a gray News row. For the first screen of a collection of materials chosen by category.
News list — leaf title and wide white rows over a gray grain background, current page in a black box. For notice · update lists
About — bold left-rule subheadings, light body text, gray panel bullet list, hand-drawn corner doodle. For site and maker about pages and usage guides
Step guide — each step has a subheading, a one-line description and a gray header-cell table (inner dotted lines divide the branches). For difficulty, grade and fee tables
News post — leaf title and ‹Back to list› link, thin line under date and large title, short body. For a single notice

notes: The hero Lottie is built by us (hero-lottie.js) instead of using the original JSON. The comp (1200×1200·60fps·160 frames), the blob matte layer’s transform keyframes (opacity 30→36·rotation −47→14→−4→5→−1→0·scale 90→95→97→100·position wobble, down to the curve values) and the photo layer position and scale (59%) are original values. The blob shape is our petal curve (same bounding box 965×751), and the knit-texture photo is a placeholder of the same ratio (1920:1300). It is loaded via animationData instead of a path so it loads even when opened as a file. The original plays a shorter version (mv_light) from the second visit, which was not built (always the first-visit version).

The original motion is framer-motion — only the engine was swapped to GSAP and the curves were carried over using framer’s own formula (easeOut = 1−(1−t)² = power1.out, easeInOut = power1.inOut, backOut = back.out(1.525)). The in-view criterion (useInView threshold .3) maps to ScrollTrigger start ‹30% bottom›

Hand drawings (needle, crochet hook, leaf, nine items, ant) are our own SVG silhouettes in the same place and size instead of the original PNGs. For the ant walk sprite (original 60-frame PNG), shared.js draws a 61-frame strip directly and gives the same 1.3s steps(60) and 100s walk through the sprite-walk-hover part. The hand drawing under the three section titles (heading.png) is a still image in the original too, so it stays static.

The gray grain background (gray.png 300px tile) · black knit-texture footer photo · knitting method band photos (nav_knitting/crochet.png) are photos, so only their places are held with striped textures painted by skin variables (wf-note in the footer). The rough brush edge of the band is replaced with a diagonally cut shape.
The Swiper version isn’t in the bundle, so 8.x was identified by its traits (slideBlankClass · swiper-horizontal, no backface-hidden) and 8.4.7 was used
The walking-ant ”menu...” GIF below the phone menu panel is text only — for the next person to continue: attach the same ant strip (#am-ant) with sprite-walk-hover look: flip
The logo is five handwritten SVG pieces in the original, so five letters (L·O·G·O·!) at the same position and size are used — the .08s stagger per piece (logo-dance .2s) is the original value
All four recorded subpages (News list, About, level, News post) are built. The level page was typed about in the original, but it’s a grade-table page, so it was changed to page

Product list — wide product photo head with product cards and breadcrumbs. For a small brand’s product lineup
News item — press article with hero photo, diagram, table of contents, previous/next. For press release and product news posts
Single product detail — glass-plate product head, contents, point rows, scent photo, FAQ, ingredient table. For cosmetics and household goods details

notes: The five video slots (loading, Hero PC/phone, before-after background, brand video window) use placeholder videos of the same ratio and length (media/*.mp4 — a grid with a passing band, plus text saying which scene) with the same playback behavior, instead of the original videos. The brand video window originally uses an embedded video player (separate PC and phone videos) and the length was not in the recording, so it is a 30-second placeholder using the browser’s default control bar instead of the video player — the behavior is the same: opening plays from the start, closing pauses.

The logo, SNS icons and product strength badges (gold and pink round artwork) were redrawn at the same position and size. The wordmark is Prata text reading Logo, so it is narrower than the original Brand wordmark (height matched).

About the company — over a background where blue and pink vertical-stripe WebGL color fields gather into a single color by half scroll, a big three-line title, two-column Korean/English body, fixed table of contents, four principles, two-column lists of services, awards, media and overview, and recently listened albums. notes: Work detail (/projects/<Name>) was not recorded in the archive so it was not built — the case row is href="#" That’s the idea. The original opens its detail page when clicked.

Txt and Img: as in the original, Txt is the current plate (50% blur) and Img is the link to switch to (underlined). On the Img plate, each case’s thumbnail opens from the left over .8s cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1) (the original th-thumbnail-image-reveal), and the preview and large name are turned off. The original Img plate’s color cover wipe (th-thumbnail-color-wipe) and thumbnail hover video playback were left out.

As in the original, the header line has white text only on Home with mix-blend-mode: exclusion (so it stays readable over the preview image), black for studies and about, and white for contact. Putting z-index on the group (.am-head) creates a stacking context so the blend no longer reaches the background, so it is set per letter.

The about and contact color fields do not port the original shader — they were rewritten as a color-field-gl part with the same values (flow .15 · size 3.5/3.2 · twist 1.2 · lines 3.5/6 · cursor .1 · σ .15 · grain .06 at 12fps · open 1.15s (1−(1−t)^2.2) .64→1 · about gather (progress/.5)²). The contact stripe rotation (90°) may be mirrored from the original — they are horizontal lines, so it looks the same. The original’s iOS status bar color matching is not done.

notes: The big English title font (Melodrama) handles Latin letters only, and Korean placeholders fall to Hahmlet 100. The original font declaration set the glyph range to everything, so Korean fell back to the system sans, and the range was narrowed and redeclared
The leaf-shadow photo behind the hero and guide sections is a photo, so a light-blotch gradient built from skin variables stands in, with a wf-note describing the photo

The hemp-leaf pattern is a single baked png in the original, including how it fades at the corners, so there is no formula — a triangular grid SVG is laid down as a mask and the fade is eyeballed with a radial gradient (0→.4→0, 26%·52%)

The instructor modal uses a single one instead of the original (one modal per instructor), and swaps in only the pressed cell’s name in micromodal onShow — the open/close behavior·options (disableScroll·awaitOpen/CloseAnimation) are the same

The original link-roll hover uses the first-set curve "expo.inout"(lowercase) so GSAP can’t find it and runs the default power1.out — the measured values (delay 2ms · 500ms) have that shape too, so the copy also uses power1.out

In the original, every link’s default text color is #0e7ae0 (--link-color) and turns #46505d on hover — even links whose text is invisible, like logo or photo links. The copy keeps the same rule (a · a:hover), and logos, icons and button arrows get their own color only on the artwork
As in the original, the loader runs only on the first entry from outside — the original decides by referrer, here by sessionStorage (since the referrer is empty on file://)
Subpages found only in the original (instructors, studio, schedule, FAQ, contact, blog) were not recorded so they were not built — menu links point to the nearest page of ours.
Logo, photos and text are all placeholders (the logo is a new drawing of two circles and a diamond ornament, the pricing table, instructor-slot ellipses, stars and arrows were also redrawn)

Font backfill — places that were Latin in the original become English placeholder text: logo letters·drawer/footer menu·two hero lines·big letter band·section names (first page three·pricing·what to bring)·three info window names·instructor names (cell·modal)·buttons (View more·See all·More·Find us)·booking round title·corner words·flowing slogan·copyright line·three subpage big titles·four vertical class names·three vertical pricing table names. Each slot notes in data-label what to put in
index hero one-line intro · section small title · info window small name, subpage small title — the original uses kana titles, Korean kept

Reserve buttons (header, card, footer, phone bar) and three lesson shortcut pills — in the original the Japanese sits inside Jost buttons too, so the Korean text stays (IBM Plex Sans KR takes over after Jost)
Post categories, post titles, price table names, bundle names, period tags, item-to-bring names, modal titles and bios — originals are Japanese, kept in Korean

Body lines left in latin-slots (About paragraph, booking info, Footer address, etc.) are `.an-reserve__loop p`·`.an-ticket__title span` False positive: the checker read a descendant selector as applying to every p and span. notes: The WebGL set (lens grid wall · paint beads · glass cylinder) has our own shaders rewritten with the original numbers (lens [.12,.07,.035,.03] · flow .05 cell/s · inertia .94 · entrance 1.6s expo.out / six palette cells · ripple 1.6s · cloud .35s / radius 2.28 · camera 3.72 · auto .22 slides/s · glass 20%). By the original formula the center slide of the cylinder would be 30% of the screen, so half the view width is multiplied by .73 to match the original measurement (about 41%) — it seems one original layout constant could not be read.

The original preview photos and videos (hover video playback on grid cells and cylinder slides) are left as placeholder boards painted in the skin color. The video-plays-on-hover behavior is missing since there is no video (brightening only).

The site dummy (light board) was built as a scroll scrub deck after measuring, on the original screen, narrower cards stacking up and down behind the front card (.88·.775·.68) — the original code could not be found, so the tempo of the transitions is a guess.

The subscription wall (tilted preview panel), the radius of the demo stage circular slider (card width × bend) and the two circles of the ring ending (panel height .43, inside panel .17) are values measured from the original visuals. The original circular slider code was not in the bundle (the component runtime was loaded separately).

The large dropdown grows a panel below the header row like the original (0→328 in .38s) and the text panel opens at 217px, but the items inside are three placeholders each. The preview images inside the original’s Library mega menu are not included.

The page transition is built from the original (address changes .6s after press, screen changes at about 1.1s) as a background-color curtain that covers at .5s and lifts on the arrival page at .5s — the form of the original transition (curtain or blur) couldn’t be seen on screen, only the timing was matched.

The kit page menu demo replaces the original video slot with our own HTML menu that opens and closes by itself in a loop (same position, size and looping). Fonts: the original aktivGrotesk (paid) → Inter Tight and Inter, Korean uses Pretendard. The original Geist Mono for numbers and labels is the same.
