The photo of a hand holding a phone (cutout) is an SVG placeholder with the same panel ratio (2880×2408) — a gray hand and arm and a black phone body drawn in the same spot as the original (panel center, 18.8×39.9vw on screen). The right-hand panel is the same drawing flipped horizontally. When using a real photo, place a cutout image with the same ratio in the .hm-phone__hand slot.

Four app-screen recording videos (hero 27.5s loop·Programs 3.4s once·loop·Shop once) are placeholder mp4s (media/, line bars flowing upward) in the same portrait ratio (540×1144), with the playback behavior (autoplay·play when in the slot·pause on exit) applied as is. The original program/01·shop/00 videos are broken in the archive, so their length couldn’t be measured and was set at 6s·4s.

The Programs · Shop photo collage (a single original image) was rebuilt as a cell grid — cell size is tied to grid height (cqh) so it shrinks with width like the original image. The Programs five columns by three rows (bottom row of the center column is the phone slot) was re-fitted to the original image, the staggered heights of the four Shop columns are eyeballed.

The first card background (mint-to-blue blurred photo) and the Care first card background (deep purple photo) are replaced with CSS gradients. The long app-screen capture scrolling at half speed (care-card-2) uses the same sticky and scale(.5) structure with a tall vertical placeholder box.

Typeface: Figtree (400 · 500) instead of the original paid typeface, and Noto Sans KR for Korean. Judgment call: the huge section names, first title, three big words and big gradient paragraph keep English placeholders as in the original (Latin title typeface slot), while side text lines, card sentences, FAQ and footer text are Korean. Paragraph line counts match the original section heights by adjusting text length (measured at 16:00, each section before the FAQ is within ±6px, FAQ answer text was lengthened afterwards to match click values).

The get-app buttons, footer links and links inside FAQ answers are #! placeholder links that don’t leave the page. Clicking a link inside an FAQ answer doesn’t toggle the question (the original goes out to an external app store).
Where wire.css border-box and the original content-box differ (FAQ list width · answer column width), it was set back to content-box — otherwise the FAQ text column disappears.
Not shot with theme.css swapped between light and dark skins (lint color 0 · font 0 · out-of-skin variables 0 were confirmed) — a task for the next person to continue.

title: Digital studio with a 3D corridor you walk through by scrolling
good_for: A design and development studio, a product or brand experience agency, or a portfolio led by a 3D showroom.

pages.use: Studio home page: entry loader, a fixed 3D stage (40 portal blades → corridor → platform, figure and arch above the clouds → flying into the logo ring and opening the next section as a circle) with section text switching on in each progress window, plus showreel, work cards, practice accordion (small 3D objects), contact scene and horizon footer
Work list — big title and short intro, one wide card + two offset cards, ending with a ”Still building” inquiry. Slot for portfolio lists

Service — big two-line title and a six-item list. A fixed screen panel on the right wraps around a cylinder from its right edge at each section and the case changes, and in the last section the six panels gather into an open book, ending with a contact section with a light-dot cone door. For service or solution intros

Studio About — two chrome-ribbon 3D heads over a dark field, team intro that flips to portraits lit from the cursor side, work process over sandstorm particles, and a drag-to-flip tech carousel. For company·team intro spots

A single case study — full-bleed cover, fact table and thoughts, dark camera journey with screen panels, light perspective, fixed-width screen strip, three design decisions, phone recording section, prototype open. For Work detail

notes: The 3D corridor models (robot glb · folded observatory · ceramic leaf · plasma membrane) are our own shapes and shaders at the original positions and sizes (40 rounded-rectangle metal blades · corridor frame · two liquid contour membranes · five elliptical stone steps · six-armed arch · capsule mannequin · small leaf ring · logo plate wrapped in three gold rings) — the rule is not to use the original model files, so it stays that way. Camera position · target · fov · progress smoothing (.065s) · entry slide (2.65s) · cursor parallax · section text window · final circle opening keep the original story keys as they are
Hero outer sky and wet ground use our sky shader and dark metal plate instead of the original hero photo (uHero) — it is a photo slot, so left as is

The showreel uses a placeholder + dust-dot canvas instead of the original video. The play button between the letters of ”SH▷WREEL” and the enlarged viewer sit in the same spot. It is a video slot, so left as is

The original liquid-cursor-renderer isn’t in the archive, so only the values (spread .0022 · force formula · mouse only at 761px and up · cell clip-path) were carried over and rebuilt with our own WebGL2 advection·damping shader — there is no pressure solve
The page-transition curtain’s plasma uses two conic-gradient layers rotating at the same 12s·5s and a 3s flicker instead of the original webp. It is an image slot, so left as is

The Solution panel images are not the original case photos or videos but case screens drawn in skin colors (metal rim gradient + 16:9 screen) — they are photo slots, so left as is. The panel’s ”Play preview” video playback is a placeholder, so only the text changes
The About portrait uses a head-and-shoulders distance-field silhouette lit from the cursor side (uPointer) instead of the original relief (depth map bin) — it is a photo slot, so it is kept as is.
The robot greeting and the prototype showroom in the work detail are placeholders (the greeting button only wiggles) — kept as is because it is a product feature (3D showroom app)
The curl-sheet-scroll part gains the original paper-scene form as a paper option (the default stays the earlier form — rule: other people’s parts only get options added)

detail 1440 document height: tables and phone-recording sections were actually built, taking it from 8.94 to 10.63 screens (original 12.85). The remaining gap is because the archive print could not settle whether the original’s eight ”Four Perspectives” screens are stacked vertically or, as in the copy, a fixed horizontal strip

The about skill carousel is built the original way: each cell’s size .78→1, opacity .48→1 and number on/off depend on its distance from the plate center. Mouse drag is 6px, and on release it goes further by speed×180 in 1.05s power3.out. For touch, it settles on the nearest cell .18s after the plate’s own scroll, and the automatic drift stops after the first touch. Phone and tablet drags have the same end value and curve but about 80ms of extra delay, and the tablet length and stagger measure about 100ms shorter (a difference in when the touch-emulated scroll inertia ends).

title: Neighborhood driving school with pressable panel menu and chattering speech bubbles
good_for: A friendly local service site such as a school, lesson studio or clinic with many menu items, cute illustrations and color cards.

pages.use: School first page — photo-fade MV and pressable button menu board, vision statement and colored card group, flowing photo and outlined-text band, randomly floating worry bubbles and town illustration, testimonial slider (press for full-text window), news box, Instagram band, three contact buttons
Features: header title, four promise cards with blue tags (line illustrations), a photo on the left + a list of blue title cards, two color cards. For listing service features and strengths.
About us — three centered pledge lines, a white box intro text, the CEO greeting (photo on left), a blue-tagged company overview table. For company and school introductions
News list — rows of date + one-line title + arrow (letter-spacing widens on hover) with circular page numbers. For notice and news lists
News item — date, large title, body in a white box and white pill previous · list · next. For reading a single notice

notes: On sub-pages, the MENU tab dropping down when it touches the footer’s white panel was fixed by adding ScrollTrigger.refresh after fonts and load, but it could not be re-checked with a capture

Decision: built just one page each — the original /feature as a service type and /news/7004 as an article type (one per type). In the phone-width home page comparison, the color cards (vertical stack), car size, contact header (hidden on phone), Instagram cell 14rem and footer bottom row were fixed to the original values.

title: Project archive on one page viewed through endlessly rolling columns
good_for: A company or studio archive, timeline or anniversary archive, or a portfolio where works are scanned horizontally on one screen.

mood.smooth: Custom lerp (horizontal) + lenis 0.075 inside the expanded column

pages.use: One-page project archive: the title swells and clears from a blue panel loader, vertical columns with number, photo, year and name wind endlessly by wheel or drag, and pressing a column spreads it to the center, followed by a thumbnail photo slider and body text below. The blue strip on the left unfolds into an About panel on interaction.

notes: The original is a single page (pages.json pages: []) — there are no sub pages. The original page transition veil (#transition) is not built since there is no page to go to.

Pillars are 12 instead of the original 21 — for the wrapping seams to stay hidden, the sum of pillar widths just needs to exceed screen width + the widest pillar (2976 at 1440 > 1688). Number, year and name are placeholders, and photo ratios follow the columns on the original hero.

Unlike the original, the loader does not wait until all photos load — it opens the page and starts swelling at 1.1s (swell-title-loader hold 1.1), since there are no photos to load. 1440 matches the original length (3183ms), while 390 is 333ms shorter than the original, noted as accepted in _study/probe.

Fonts: Neue Montreal (paid) → Inter Tight, PP Neue Montreal Mono (paid) → DM Mono, Korean in Noto Sans KR. The swelling loader title and side letters use an English placeholder, Archive, with a width similar to the original BRAND (WORDMARK overflowed the screen at 20vw).

The rest of the large photos and the body text below in the opened pillar are attached from a template when opened and removed after closing, like the original (v-if). Vertical scroll inside the pillar uses the same lenis 1.3.17 as the original, mounted separately on the pillar.

On phone, dragging the thumbnail row works like the original: the panel intercepts touch (touch-action: none) and moves scrollLeft itself. The original’s grid view shortcut (a dev-only 12-column overlay) was not built.

title: Full-width wordmark over swapping renders, styled like an OS desktop
good_for: A small portfolio for a 3D or graphics studio showing product renders and logo work, with a desktop-style first screen where folder icons select clients.

pages.use: One-screen Hero: a screen-wide bold wordmark on top, and a render image in the center that fades off and swaps every 4 seconds over .7s (click for a dark view mode: left and right half press and arrow keys to navigate, name, dots, close). Bottom left a one-line intro, bottom right folder and info icons (on hover a triangle under the name). For a graphic studio Hero

Work list — small wordmark at top center, seven client-colored gradient folder icons in the middle of the screen (white logo and name, triangle on hover), one copyright line below. For client and project selection screens

notes: The center render images (the original’s twenty-six 3D render PNGs: felt ball, chrome symbol, blue initial, app icon, shield badge …) were redrawn as five of our own glossy SVG objects at the same position and cell fit (gradients · blurred fur-texture filter). The colors are oklch values rotated from the accent (blue-gray) hue to the original render colors, so they rotate along when the skin changes. To use real renders, swap the svg inside figure for an img (data-label says which render it is).

The wordmark (original is wide, bold uppercase vector paths) is filled with the English placeholder NAME in Archivo width 125 weight 900, stretched to the panel width with textLength — stroke contrast is slightly lower than the original lettering.

The seven client logos on the work folders (original SVG) are replaced with white single-color symbols of our own (ring · star · wave · orbit · arrow · hexagon · T-circle), and the two-tone gradient colors of the folders are oklch values made by rotating the accent hue up to the original brand colors. On click the original goes to a client detail like /client, but that page wasn’t recorded so it wasn’t built (links are #).
The /info page that the hero Information icon leads to in the original was not recorded either, so it was not built (the link is #info).
The About line is a Korean placeholder because the original is a small uppercase English sentence — on phone the original wraps to two lines, but the placeholder is short so it stays on one line.

title: Furniture collection covered by a geometric shape mosaic
good_for: A special page or serialized landing for a new furniture or living collection, followed by shop product detail pages.

pages.use: Collection home: a loading screen where surrounding pieces float up, a fixed hero where shape cells cover a video, a product header video opening from the center with a stack of five photos and rolling numbers (two products), a 3-column product list, a place strip and a big logo footer. For new product and seasonal collection special landings.
Full product list — big heading and 2-column photo cards (hover: frame .95 · photo 1.15). For the product list section of a collection

Product detail (HQ shopping edition): two-line header · name · big photo · download materials expand · photo cluster rising in · photo cell zoom window · spec table (tabs on phone) · size slider · quote picker · related products · recommended strip · three contacts · fixed right drawer. For furniture and appliance product details

notes: The four videos (Hero background, two product heads, location band) are placeholder boxes of the same position and ratio instead of video files. Playback behavior (background plays after 3.5s loading, heads and location loop automatically) is only approximated by is-playing at the same moment, letting the pattern drift slowly — placeholder video files of the same length are left for the next person to add

The three Lottie sets are animationData we built with the same lottie-web 5.13, the same frame counts (opening 91 · shape 42 · scroll hint 120) and the same curves as the original. The opening has 12 ring pieces in place of the original’s 12 perimeter curve pieces (clockwise from -72°, 5 frames each), and the shape is 180 cells of 8×8 squares, quarter circles and semicircles (fixed seed) — not the exact original piece shapes.

Sound: instead of the original background music (mp3), a 4-second chord WAV made on the spot plays through the same howler 2.2.4 with the same on/off (first press plays with sound, after that a mute toggle)
The logo is a text wordmark (logo | 0000-00 collection) instead of the original SVG. The clip-path wrap and rise values of the Hero and Footer logos are exactly the original’s

Detail (HQ shopping panel): the estimator is cut down to five item rows plus one picker window (the original has seven accordion windows, one per item, plus a real price list and print view). The fabric/material window (fablicmaterialModal) and PDF materials are only expandable-list placeholders. The second recorded detail page has the same type, so one detail.html covers both

The detail-size slider is Swiper 12.1.2, same as the original (1.2 slides·12px → 768 and up 2.5 slides·20px, loop at 4 or more slides). The original also ships jquery.sliderPro, but this page doesn’t use it, so it isn’t included
Page transition: the original has no transition device either, just normal navigation, so it was left as is (collection → detail switches to a different board as in the original)

Detail (main office version) Korean subtitles for the header menu, section titles and contact cells (Products · Get a Quote · Products That Go Well Together …) and the subtitle under the large list title — the original is Japanese (Products · Quick Quote · Compatible Products · All Products), kept in Korean. Noto Sans KR, a gothic match for the title typeface Inter Tight, is loaded as its pair. The detail small line in latin-slots is `.ar-footer small` A false positive from reading the rule as all small, the actual typeface is Noto Sans KR
The detail name line ”Design : designer name” is Latin in the original but is set in the body font (Noto Sans KR) so Korean glyphs don’t drop out, so it was left as is

title: Software studio with a wave hero and terminal-style loader
good_for: A homepage for a development studio or tech agency with services, case studies, founder intro, tech blog with article pages and hiring info.

pages.use: Studio home page — terminal loader (first visit), wave shader hero over video, logo strip and three-principle About, big text band, six services beside a pinned glass orb, work visuals scattered in two columns, testimonials, counting numbers, founder, article cards, social slide strip, FAQ, closing card

Tech blog list — dark page header (path, two-line title, on-this-page contents), white panel with search and topic filter on the left, article rows on the right (image, title, summary, tags, date), pagination
About. Origin story, history cards that change when you click a year, two founder cards, dark band on why the company exists, three beliefs, partner network skill pills
Recruit — no-openings notice, six cards for who we look for, two cards to contact the founder directly. For open-application and talent pool pages
Work with us — struck-through word heading, three counting number cards, four principles, three fitting jobs and four steps, a typing terminal. For how-we-work and pre-quote guidance
Single tech article — header (path, title, date, reading time), body with a sticky table of contents that follows, in-article questions, a strip to slide to more reads

notes: The loader and hero videos are placeholder videos with the same ratio and length (media/intro.mp4 10s square, media/hero.mp4 25s 1280×832 ratio — hand-made purple gradients). Loader progress follows video time/length like the original, falls back to a 10s clock if the video does not run within 2.5s, and in the last 3s the video goes .35→.11 and the background lightens (original [12,0,46]→[37,27,68] approximated by mixing 12% of navy-violet and white)

Water hero: the panel (video and background) is handled by the _fx water-ripple-cover, while the title letter ripple runs one more copy of the same height field in index.js, reads it at 64×36 and feeds it into feDisplacementMap (6px) — because the part doesn’t expose its height field (one extra WebGL context). When the part gets a ‹text ripple css› option, move to it and delete the title ripple in index.js.

Service section glass marbles: the original three.js physical material (clearcoat·ior), shadows, environment baking, 35° camera and 1.5 exposure were rebuilt with the same values. The exact orbit formulas of the two marbles (z axis, color-mix share) could not be read to the end in the original bundle, so they were matched by eye (size, pinkish tint approximated)
The original typeface Neue Montreal is paid, so we used the free Hanken Grotesk, which has a similar feel

The seven cases show only the image, name and field, scattered across two staggered columns like the original — the problem, solution and tech lines in the original DOM were collapsed and not visible, so none were invented

Menu open/close values couldn’t be found in the original bundle (CSS only), so it was built to match the original button curve with a .4s curtain, a .65s cubic-bezier(.76,0,.24,1) panel and links .05s apart

Helper: as in the original, it opens with the bottom-right button (hover 1.05x), and if there is no scroll for 10s it opens by itself and shows a suggestion (cancel = Don’t show again for this tab session = two days). The panel rises in .75s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), with a dark panel in the head · enlarged · close. No real conversation (the original AI reply · lead-capture form), only a placeholder greeting · suggested questions

The cookie bar, search, pagination and contact buttons only have the look and hover feedback — no real consent saving, search server or mail sending (search and topic filters only filter text on screen)
As in the original, the loader shows on whichever page is opened first in this tab (not only the first page)

title: Monochrome company news board with a letter ring rotating behind
good_for: A one-page site for a small company or foundation with a one-line vision, news list and company overview.

pages.use: Company home — two-line vision sentence and Scroll line, 45vw news list of 24 lines on the right, gray-band company overview table, ink-colored footer. A circle of thank-you text letters stays fixed and spins behind every section

notes: In the original, Scroll line keyframes start with a first stop of ”0 {(no percent) so it is invalid — ported as the browser actually renders it: it stands fully drawn for 1s, then shrinks downward over 1s (scroll-cue-line default, the artist’s intended shape is look: grow)

The circle of text behind is an SVG outline drawing in the original, so it was redrawn by wrapping our own text (”thank you” in several languages) with textPath at the same size·position·opacity·speed (200s · 140s at 1024 and below) — the starting angle is not evenly aligned like the original (the phase differs each time it opens)
Logo, social icons and the News/Information English title graphics were replaced with our SVG and Poppins text — the original titles are letter-outline SVGs, so the letter widths differ slightly

I swapped theme.css for a light skin (ink-wash) and a dark skin (blueprint) and captured 1440 and 390 — no original ink-black or gray remains anywhere. The header exclusion uses --site-invert (the opposite extreme of the background brightness), so it inverts on the dark skin too, and the footer uses --kf-contrast-*, so on the dark skin it becomes a light panel

Font backfill — Latin spots (logo LOGOTYPE · News · Information · phone menu News/Contact · Scroll · letter circle) were already English. The logo letter rule `.ab-logo span` Because of this, the checker read every span as the heading typeface — `.ab-logo__word` Changed to a class (text and size unchanged), set the logo aria-label to LOGOTYPE and added data-label

index header menu (News · Contact) · news categories (Notice · Press Release · Media Listings · Event) · two-line hero · latest info · company overview — the original is in kana and kanji (News · Notice · Press Release · People struggling with money…) with a gothic body, so Korean is kept (Pretendard is the match)

title: Cream-toned fertility clinic with glowing wavy lines
good_for: A homepage for a fertility, women's health or specialist clinic with a warm medical tone and subpages for results, columns and recruitment.

pages.use: Clinic home page — a hero where rounded photos set left and right cross-fade, with a wave line drawn and light spreading at each change (vertical copy, inverted badge, timetable), banner Swiper, news row, circle-photo introductions, three strengths rows with changing photos, rising step and case cards, environment and FAQ, oval-photo specialty care, column cards, tangerine-colored recruit band. For hospital and clinic homes

List — cream gradient header, categories on the left with past posts that expand by year, white card rows (on hover a cream panel and orange border switch on in .5s and the text turns orange), and round page number buttons. Used for the News, Work and Results lists (the original’s case list and case category pages share the same form)

Column single — same side menu, a white panel with date, category, title and table of contents, a cost table with yellow-dot subheadings and cream total rows, and previous, next and list buttons. For article or guide detail

Recruit — three round photos and copy, joy of work placed alternately left and right, job intro where the left-attached job pills light up the current job in tangerine, how to apply. For hospital or company recruiting pages

notes: Of the five sub-pages, the case list (casestudy) and the case category (casestudy/treatment) have the same shape as the news list, so they were built as a single news.html — only the header title differs. The case category page that was captured as detail is actually a list
The section-boundary wave graphic (shape image) was also redrawn as an SVG gradient band, and parallax uses the same paroller.js 1.5.0 as the original (factor .1, transform .2s ease-out)
The map is a road drawing (SVG) of the same position and size instead of a map embed
Logo and banner art are image files, so an SVG mark and photo placeholders stand in
The original recruitment application form (tab-switching input form) is a separate form below the recorded recruit page, so it was not built — only the apply button slot is kept
The menu’s other sub-pages (clinic about, facilities, doctors, first visit, FAQ, exams) were not recorded so they are not built — links are left as #

Font backfill — the spots that are Latin in the original (section English titles, CARE/QUALITY/SEMINAR, View All, Recruit/Reserve, logo Clinic Name, footer name, CLINIC NAME) were already English, and measured in the browser, Korean text rendered in Montserrat is 0 on all four pages. The checker `.aa-exit__n span`·`.aa-fbn__t b`·`.aa-fbn__t2 small`·`.aa-tbl tbody th`·`.aa-logo__t b` Font rules ending in a tag selector were applied to every span, b, small and th, catching 82 lines by mistake. They were changed to classes (aa-exit__d, aa-fbn__en, aa-fbn__sub, aa-tbl__t, aa-logo__w) with glyphs and sizes unchanged.

Index hero vertical copy, Korean section subtitles (__jp), buttons, exit notices, news/column categories, recruit job-type pills and subtitles, and article cost table headers — the original is in Japanese (kana and kanji, such as Feel at ease and relaxed… · News · Book your first visit here · Doctor · First-visit fee …), so the Korean is kept. Pairing: body gothic (Zen Kaku Gothic New → Pretendard), logo in Noto Serif KR

title: Portfolio with full-screen video, a single-line list and white menu card
good_for: A designer, film or studio portfolio on a dark site where work videos are the main attraction.

pages.use: Home — project one-line list over a full-screen video (bar auto-advances every 20 seconds · press to switch video), holding turns it into a horizontal tile row (WebGL). For a no-scroll, one-screen portfolio entrance

Work list. A pinned left list of year, name and field, plus a right-hand video box that grows with scroll position while the active row and arrow follow. For the full list of a portfolio with many works
Article list — a grid of uneven-sized article cards over a fixed background (WebGL) that ripples with the cursor, with cards whose frost clears. For journal, news and interview lists

Video collection — full-screen video that switches with each scroll step like changing channels (noise, flashes), year and name on the center line, live card at bottom right. For a collection of showreels, music videos and 3D work
One work — video hero, intro and a period/role table, full-bleed images and video with 3- and 2-column grids, awards, two other works. For case details

notes: Hero tile strip (WebGL, three 0.160): the tile vertex bending (center curl exp(-6x²), edge lay-down, vertical stretch, bulge), the drag and velocity-to-bend formula, center-only color and the grayscale lerp were rewritten in our shader with the original values. For the 2-second enter and exit sequence, only the skeleton of the original 3200 lines was carried over (center tile fills the screen ↔ tile size progress 0 to .78, side tiles .12 to .62, curve cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1)). Not included from the original: video frame handoff (rVFC), the list attaching below the tiles, the description line character roll (spring ω 13) and view-mode memory (localStorage). Blocked: that section of code was not read in full — a task for the next person to continue. When opened via file://, the video is cross-origin so WebGL cannot read it and numbered images go into the tiles instead (open via http to get the video).

Of the six Esc effects, film noise, pixel grid, cursor gradient and infrared are built with the original values (plate size · 7px cells · color · blend). The editing grid lines and the two lens droplets were redrawn with the same intent because the original algorithm wasn’t fully read (line positions, droplet count and speed are guesses). Effect colors are an effect palette, not skin, so they are marked as Not skin.

The ribbon badge on the panel beside the open menu (original scroll-badges — a fluttering water-surface badge drawn with three, swaying with scroll speed) was not built. The hover clip on the side panel’s recent work cards also has only blur and zoom, without frost. Blocked because the badge artwork (SVG) is an original asset and has to be redrawn — a job for the next person.

Scroll collapse (the menu card folds into a single MENU line) was built with the original constants (text .34s · spacing .032 · height power2.inOut · lower row .5s · MENU .16s expo.out · unfold at 1.5x speed). The original’s 2000 lines of edge handling were trimmed: reversing direction mid-fold, the Lenis velocity threshold, and the details of only the lower row folding on phones. Also missing is nav-arrive, where the menu is already pushed aside when arriving from another page.

Pages that were not recorded (Information·Archive·Contact·a single journal post) were not built, so those links stay in place (#). The menu item ”Alter-Ego” is set as ”Showreel” placeholder text for easy reuse
Page transitions in the original also reopen the document (chained via sessionStorage), so it was built the same way — barba and swup are not used

title: Quiet lifestyle brand where photos open through an ink-bleed transition
good_for: A craft, household goods or clothing brand, a local brand that also runs a tea room or shop, or a calm photo-led company intro.

pages.use: Home: first-visit logo curtain, fading hero photo, two photos offset from the intro, a fixed horizontal service band + ink-bleed landscape, a company list (photo on hover), a paper-panel store list, blog cards, and news lines.
Brand intro — a head with three offset photos, two value sections split into text and photos, overlapping fading photos on a paper panel, closing story. The About spot on the home page
What we do — right half photo header, a list of four lines of work running down with text and photos staggered. For business/service intro

Store guide — for each store, left: intro, address, and hours table, right: large photo slider and a row of small images. For branch, store, or gallery guides (recorded as product but it is a store guide so page).
News list — left category column, right side date, category and title one per line, pagination. The original’s per-category news (/news-cat/shop) has the same form, so this one page stands in for it
Blog and case list — left category column, three square photo cards on the right, News row below. The original has no cases, so the card type was filled with the home page blog card

notes: Ink bleed mask: instead of the original mask.webp image, our noise-filter SVG (_fx/soft-mask-reveal look: ink) matches only the size (200%→500%)·position·5s curve — the grain shape of the bleed is different
The paper-grain images (texture · shop-bg) for background, contact band and store band are replaced by noise filter grain
Drawer menu: the original opens and closes with MicroModal — hand-built with the same timing (backdrop 1s · items start .3s late and last .6s · .04s stagger · close .3s)
The anchor-jump smooth-scroll (1s easeInOutCubic) is not included — Lenis moves instead.

The company, catalog, culture and careers pages were not recorded, so the menu links to about.html#company and works.html. That is also why the company page’s horizontal flowing band (splide auto-scroll) is missing.
The blog case list was empty in the original, so it is filled in the shape of first-page blog cards
Category news (/news-cat/shop) has the same Type as the News list, so it was not built separately
Photo slots are grey panels so the hero thumbnail looks empty — the hero photo drifts at 1.3x·−50px so the label is pushed off screen

title: Survey project landing where the digit zero is a pie chart, plus corporate pages
good_for: A project landing that highlights survey results, a corporate lab or campaign page, and the following corporate site with news, business, recruitment, company info and product pages.

pages.use: Research project landing — an opening where a large centered logo (pie chart in the 0 slot) shrinks into a 480px left column, a hero where the pie chart section and photo section swap with a diagonal wipe, stacking declaration sections with a left photo strip, question rows alternating graph↔photo, feature cards and footer. For survey results·research projects·campaign landings

Company news list — blue two-row header (press to open a mega menu), gray title band, left filter for field and year, 40 rows of date · category · title · PDF button, pagination, gray sitemap footer. For press release and IR news lists

Business introduction — a sky photo header, centered intro text, a 3 × 3 photo tile grid with line-art icons (photo scales 1.1× on hover), an ‹Other businesses› box (a dark panel on hover), and a flagship brand ring graphic with a list. For a company with many divisions, as a business guide.

Group recruiting entrance — wide-tracked English title between a 32-cell photo mosaic, group intro and two revenue donuts, flagship company box (new grad·mid-career buttons) and two-column group company cards (underlined title·photo·intro·external link button), large recruiting policy button. Sections float up from 20px below over .7s. For a group recruiting hub

Company info · philosophy — large building photo header, six dark shortcut buttons, group philosophy with an atomic orbit graphic, gray band mission, vision slogan (blue box + two bold lines) with a three-arrow loop, and a bold declaration over a pale cityscape. For corporate philosophy and vision pages

Rental building product intro (another brand’s skin): hero with five buildings of different floor counts and a section-nav strip, serif title cards on a navy stage · giant outlined English text, seismic damping device diagram, maintenance timeline, white card table on gray background (POINT tag), black catalog strip, two plans · cases · model room, fixed vertical button on the right. For architecture and real-estate product detail landing pages.

notes: The five subpages are, in the original too, not the LP (the Studio site) but a parent company corporate site (news, business, careers, company info — four pages) and another brand’s product site (one rental building), so the header, footer and typeface differ. They are built as three shells like the original: the LP uses a left 480px header from index.css + the group common strip footer, the four corporate pages use the blue two-line header (.ak-ch) from shared.css and the sitemap footer (.ak-gfoot.is-full, the same header and footer assembled and shared by all four), and the product page uses its own header, fixed vertical button and lavender sitemap in product.css + the group strip (blue panel). All menu links connect among our six pages.

The original bar chart question (type bar, part of the question line) showed only pie charts on the recorded first page, so it was built as three pie charts — if bars are needed, add them with the same Chart.js options (indexAxis y, stacked, 1200ms easeInOutExpo)

Not built: the cookie consent bar·analytics script on the company pages, and the real photo preload on the product pages — the product page opening curtain (3px progress bar → 1s retract) is imitated by filling evenly in 1.4s instead of by the images

title: Coastal town tourism with handwritten copy and confetti-paper accents
good_for: A regional or seaside tourism site, a municipal or tourism association page with many seasonal events, or a photo-rich travel landing.

pages.use: Tourism landing page — a loader that draws handwritten copy, a photo hero with scattering confetti, four horizontally flowing spots (the back photo peels away, a map route draws itself), seasonal recommendation cards, a flowing row of event cards, a band of large flowing English intro text, a polaroid culture section, an egg-shaped model course slider, ranking cards with a pinned title, a video strip, a seasonal tab slider, a yellow-blotch purpose finder, a handwritten photo strip, a sandy photo footer. For regional tourism landing pages.

Appeal feature: dome photo hero + large English title, four appeals with number boxes (photo and text alternating left and right), three recommended spot cards, and a purpose finder slider. For pages that introduce a region’s or service’s appeal in turn
Seasonal picks — dome photo head, four-slot square photo article cards + page dots, purpose-finder slider. For article and recommended post collection lists
Model course — dome photo header, three-slot course cards with egg-shaped photos on a mint-pattern panel, purpose-finder slider. For travel course · recommended itinerary lists

notes: The original address blocked the headless browser with a security block (WAF) and would not open — the original files unpacked from the archive were served briefly from /tmp only, to measure screens and motion (not copied into the library). So only some of the original photos appear, and the text is Korean translated at archiving time

Handwritten copy, logo and English handwriting (Connecting people) are hand-drawn SVG art in the original, so they are not carried over. Instead we make our own looped strokes that imitate the letter shapes and draw them with the same vivus values (oneByOne 150f · EASE_OUT, map route sync 50f) — swap in the brand handwriting SVG when it is actually used
Confetti (the original decoration SVG art) is replaced by scattered CSS pieces — positions, delays (.3~1.8s), 30px travel and 2s are the original values

The model course slick adds variableWidth to the original options (centerMode·5s·1s·asNavFor) — a judgment call to show several egg-shaped slides, since not all of the original CSS slide width rules could be carried over
The event card row flow uses −50% because the end value of the original @keyframes slider (−25%→, 100s) is cut off in the saved css
The seven header icons are our own SVG shapes (diamond, drop, circle, leaf, zigzag, bar, arch) instead of the original artwork, and the video strip is a video embed placeholder

The vertical wave on the right of the spot panel (wave-vl y −1200 scrub) and the numbers for the spinning circular text in the culture section could not be carried over, so the circular text is guessed at one turn per 40s.

title: Warm neighborhood dental clinic with a dotted path, flying leaf and watercolor trees
good_for: A homepage for a local dental clinic, medical office, herbal clinic or pharmacy with apricot wave bands, orange accents, rounded type, flat people illustrations, doctor intro, recruitment and notices.

pages.use: Dental home page — a left vertical column (logo · notice box · icon menu · phone), a rippling round photo and vertical pledge text, leaves flying along a dotted ring path and rising hearts, two-column about and a photo collection, For first-time visitors (three picture cells), treatment flow (three STEPs), eight icon treatment guides, a notice line, a wide photo band, director’s greeting, map · hours table · calendar, partner banners, and a watercolor-hills footer. Past 1100px a pill-menu header bar drops down

Director and Dental Clinic About — wide photo header cut by waves, pill tabs, director greeting (photo, name, greeting text, dotted career list), clinic tour with six photo cells. For a hospital or shop’s owner greeting and facility intro

Staff and Careers — big orange workplace intro text and a group photo, four Work&Life benefits on a peach panel, a dotted-line daily schedule, three photo slots, a job requirements table and a phone number. For small clinic or shop recruiting pages.
Notice list — under a wavy photo header, a thin-line list of one-line date (orange) · title, plus page numbers. For notice lists
A single news post — orange date, dotted-underline title, a few lines of body, back-to-list button. For notice and news details

notes: The original dotted-path leaves were moved with the same anime.js 3.2.1 motion path (values as is) into the part path-leaf-loop. The path shape is newly drawn following the silhouette of the original dotted loop, and unlike the original, where three leaves share one hidden path, the drawn dotted path itself is used as the path.

The original illustrations (flat people · dentist with a big tooth · watercolor leaves · round/heart trees · leaf-branch background · eight tooth line icons · watercolor hill footer · three-cell first-visit treatment scenes) were redrawn as SVG sprites (shared.js) at the same positions and sizes — silhouettes and color placement match, but details of the original art (expressions, clothing folds, watercolor bleed) are simplified

The hero photo’s wobbling round border uses uneven border-radius instead of the original mask artwork, and the apricot wave strip (bg_wave · fv_bg SVG) approximates similar curves with radial-gradient — curve positions are by eye

/  Map and calendar embeds are replaced with placeholders of the same position and size (the calendar is a panel drawn with month cells and closed-day bands). The three partner banners are placeholders too
The original font Zen Maru Gothic is the same one (fontsource), paired with NanumSquareRound for Hangul

Four recorded sub-pages (notice · head doctor profile · careers · notice article) were built. The careers page is shorter than the original (12839px) — section types were kept (workplace intro · four Work&Life benefits · a day’s schedule · job requirements) while repeated benefits and staff interview cards were trimmed. Pages that were not recorded, such as first-time visitors · treatment guide · FAQ · directions, were not built, and the menu links to the Home tabs and about.

title: Music site entered through a record sleeve door with chrome title, turntable and web sequencer
good_for: A promo page for a record or EP release, a musician or DJ intro, or an interactive experience where visitors play with sound.

pages.use: Album first page — press the record door to enter, then chrome title letters with stair photos, an intro text block for four tracks (hovering a track name shows a preview video), about the makers, vertical video, footnotes and Q&A, footer

Creator About — four large bold text blocks starting about halfway down the screen (each block indented at a different column) · small portrait above the first line · four edge footnotes · vertical performance video

Listen — four track buttons · A/B sides · white record spinning at 33⅓rpm (drag to scratch · flip side) · waveform playback bar, vertical video and track description panel. For album and podcast playback screens
Web sequencer — four songs, twelve control buttons, a 7-row × 16-cell grid, a hands-on page where you tap cells to build a beat and play it back at 145bpm

notes: No audio, video or images are used — the play pill and sequencer sound are seven placeholder synth instruments built fresh in WebAudio (kick · clap · bass · three plucks · pad, 145bpm sixteenth notes), the original track audio and Tone sample kit are not included. For a real track, swap PG.sound in shared.js for an audio element.

Preview above the track name ([data-cue]): I could not confirm what the original cue does (a sound cue or a video preview) — since four videos/home-*.webp exist, I judged it to be a vertical video panel that follows the cursor (.35s on, lerp .15) and built it that way.

Page transition: the original is a Nuxt router transition (site code), so the same behavior was rewritten. Pressing an internal link darkens the body in .3s before navigating, and the new page brightens in .3s. As in the original, the header bar and play pill aren’t raised again on the arriving page, only the body. Sound doesn’t carry over because each page is a new document, so only the on state (sessionStorage p-playing) is passed, and the listening panel spins only when sound was turned on at the entry gate (the original also turns sound on at the gate).

Panel (.js-panel) rise uses values from the original bundle (B3cVYYkG Ec·Cc) — before the reveal, outside the bottom edge of the screen (y = window height - panel top edge) then goes to 0 in 1.4s expo.out with .1 stagger, no opacity. Used by both the listening and sequencer parts (shared.js).

Listening: the original record art front and back (record.webp) and the record sheen are drawn with svg disc and conic gradients, and the waveform uses 60 bars like the original. Only the record spin of 1.8s per turn and the side flip are original values, and the flip length of .72s is a guess from the original constant (vu .72). Changing the track leaves the video slot as is.

Sequencer: the cell layout of the four original patterns can’t be read (encoded string), so only the first pattern was copied from the original screen and the other three are rule-generated placeholders. A ”Share sequence” collapsible panel. No distinct sounds were made for each of the four songs (kits) — selecting a song only changes the pattern.

The phone (390) version could not capture the original phone screen (it sits behind a gate, so scroll capture missed it), so it was built only from the original css phone values (4-column grid, menu button, title low at 48.7svh).

Line rise uses SplitText (mask: lines) with the same values (100% → 0, 1.75s expo.out, stagger .1, within 20% from the bottom of the screen) instead of the original’s own line splitting. An indented first line is moved, after splitting, to a left margin of the same width on the first line box.

Typeface note (2026-11-06): the original text is all Latin (PP Neue Montreal), so the chrome wordmark · sleeve and the label album name (ALBUM NAME) · logo · menu · header album info · section names (● TRACKLIST etc.) · track and credits name lines · buttons · sequencer control buttons and instrument names · footer links were swapped for English placeholders. Sentences such as track descriptions · credits intros · footnotes · Q&A body were kept in Korean (heading typeface = As the body typeface, its pair Noto Sans KR is already loaded).
Two small headings in the index Q&A (next to A: · B: ”Your small heading here”) — the original is a short Latin sentence, but since it is a body-size sentence the Korean is kept.

index track title row (.h-titles): line splitting put two tracks in one line box so the flex gap (2.7rem·1.5rem) had no effect and the two tracks ran together — after switching to English, ‹(00:00)B1› looked stuck together, so the same gap was moved to the margin between tracks.

sequencer 1440: the six album-info lines in the header row overlap the top of the sequencer panel (BPM · Reset loop cells) — same in the Korean version, not caused by text length, so left untouched in this backfill. How the original avoids this spot could not be compared.

The ”Click to enter” text above the door follows the original bundle (D6ZI4dhh) formula as is — each frame it moves .085 (at 60fps) toward the cursor and tilts around the Y·X axes by that frame’s speed×1.6° with perspective(800px) (±32°), and the tilt releases when it stops. The original measurement of ”tilt 18.43° · ratio 3.16” was a value from decomposing the perspective matrix (the resting pose). It is placed 1rem away from the cursor (original translate-x-10).

Door panel pull-out: when the cursor comes within panel width (24rem)×2.5 of the sleeve center, the panel pulls out with smoothstep toward target .25 on a 1.2Hz, damping .85 spring, and the whole door approaches at up to 1.4x and -6° (original bundle Choz-AjC Ye). As in the original, translate and scale are applied to the DOM slot box (.p-gate__slot) and the WebGL panel follows the same values — measured by rAF, the center is 21.13px·1.411x and 195px to the side is 12.15px·1.309x, matching the original (21.13·1.411 / 12.14·1.307). The panel position formula (original V) is tied up with #entry constants, so only the pull distance is an approximation (v^1.68) fitted to two measured points.

title: Furniture workshop intro linked by oxblood-colored curtains
good_for: A homepage for an artisan workshop, furniture maker or interior fit-out company with project portfolio and company and people intro.

pages.use: Workshop home — oxblood greeting loader, hero with video descending in parallax, three-line intro in thin serif, two-column section with staggered photo and text (90% photo · 70/30 photo pair), phrase over a full-bleed photo strip, two work cards. For artisan brand and furniture company homes
Work list — small uppercase label and three-line big sentence header, a two-column grid of 38em-tall photo cards (hover 1.02x). For case study · portfolio lists

Company About — aerial video hero, pledge sentence rising word by word, photo·text two columns, people card swiper (4 cards·free drag), full sample photo, white panel partner name grid. For company and team intro
News list — label · big sentence header, two photo cards with two-line titles and category names (4em gap). For journal · blog lists

A single work — large name and place, a 95% screen-width key photo, headings that rise line by line, two photo-and-text two-column rows, a long quote, a full-bleed photo, a square photo pair, and two random other works excluding the current one. For case studies and project detail pages

notes: Typeface: heading Legquinne VF and body Basis Grotesque Pro (paid) are replaced by Italiana and Inter — the feel of the thin decorative serif differs slightly

Font placeholder text (2026-11-06): the original is all Latin, so the Italiana title spots (big titles · big sentences · section names · people · partners · works · news names), brand name, menu, buttons, card location lines, people categories and job titles, and the footer (address · links · copyright) were swapped for English placeholders. No Korean remains in the title font spots — only the body (Inter) sentences are kept in Korean, and the Nanum Myeongjo pairing in theme.css is left as is
Brand wordmark and AB monogram SVG are not used, a text name and two ring placeholder graphics stand in instead
The original length of the hero video is not in the HAR, so a 10-second loop placeholder is used, and the company aerial video plays once for 4.4 seconds like the original (no loop)

Lottie and swiper were attached to the cards, but lottie was only a site-builder bundle string and is not used on the page, so it was not included. swiper is used only for the people slider on the company page (original 12.2.0 as is).
The Contact, privacy and single news article pages weren’t recorded so they weren’t built — menu 4 points to the footer contact (#ab-contact), and news cards point to #
The original header menu has a desktop dropdown script and CSS but no dropdown in the markup, so it was not built (phone hamburger menu only)

The home page greeting loader holds only the company name for 1.35s, with no swap-in slot like the original (the original script errors while writing into the empty slot, but the time still runs) — the greeting-words-loader part can actually swap greetings via its words option
The original SplitText autoSplit (re-splits lines when the window is resized) is replaced: line-rise splits only once, the first time

So a new page isn’t painted bare before the transition curtain is attached by script, shared.css covers the first screen with body::after (the original puts the curtain in the markup) — if the script doesn’t run, it is lifted after 4s

title: AI browser product site with browser window on sky panel and fine vertical line panels
good_for: A product homepage for an AI tool, browser or productivity app that shows three features through illustration cards and benchmarks, with blog, feature pages, article detail and a dark manifesto page.

pages.use: Product home page — rounded sky-and-cloud panel with header, two-line title, download group and a browser window overhanging the panel, two intro paragraphs, rising app icon grid, three use-case picture cards, tabbed benchmark bars, memory window, password photo card and two vault slots, four privacy cards, blue glow end panel.
Blog list — large heading, four category pills, eight article cards in two columns with 2:1 covers, blue-glow ending panel
Company manifesto — a screen-height black terminal panel with a monospaced manifesto and a dot-character app icon grid, recruiting info and signature (no header or footer)
Single feature intro — big centered title and download, three use-case picture cards, tabbed benchmark bars, and two columns with text on the left and a step-picker menu image on the right

One research article — category path, centered title, cover and author, a fixed dash-style table of contents at the left center of the screen (name shows on hover), and a benchmark table, code block and screenshot inside a 672px body

notes: The original’s title typeface (a custom face) is replaced with Inter Tight — the body typefaces Geist and Geist Mono are the same as the original.

The original use-case graphics (app icon grid · login · message · document) are Rive (.riv) state machines. The original .riv files can’t be used, so the same positions and sizes are drawn in CSS and SVG, and the icons are replaced with a GSAP timeline where, once visible, they rise like a wave from the center (.8s 0.22,1,0.36,1) and a cursor goes to a button and presses it, repeating — the exact scene order and lengths of the original Rive could not be measured.

The first panel’s sky clouds are drawn with CSS gradients and blurred cloud blobs instead of the original image (webp). The screen inside the original browser window is simplified to placeholder tabs, chat and cards.
The three password photo cards, vault screen, article covers and blog covers are photo placeholders (the label says what to put in).
The second and third value groups in the benchmark tab are placeholder ratios (the original uses recharts bars). The pill slide of .3s was guessed from the screen.

The manifesto page’s dotted-letter app icon grid stamps our own shapes onto 4px cells with canvas instead of the original image, and a few cells blink slowly — the icon shapes and blink cycle differ from the original image.
The dash length rule of the article page’s dash-style table of contents couldn’t be read from the original, so it is set proportional to the section name length.
Colors are written in theme.css with lab() like the original (Tailwind v4) — swapping the Skin to hex shows the same colors, and differences only appear when comparing motion.
Page transition opens a static page anew (the original Next.js swaps content in without refetching the document).

title: Monochrome engineer portfolio opened by a data-flow film
good_for: A personal site for a portfolio, technical résumé or notes (writing) collection.

pages.use: Landing page — dot-tunnel loader, then on the first visit a 6.6s data-flow 3D video fills the whole screen and shrinks into the head background, followed by a two-line big title, a four-column row of numbers and company names, and a next-section link. For the hero of personal or team portfolios
Work collection — four-row list of company · project (black band and widened name on hover) and a following preview (structure drawing with drawn lines · three numbers). For career and case lists

About — big title, black-and-white portrait photo that follows the cursor, code-style profile (values decode in), a line diagram where one method splits into three, list of three fields. For personal About · specialties
Field notes list — blinking stream dot, note rows (hover inverts the whole row), outside-article mention rows. For blog·article lists
A single note — long title, side column with topic and reading time, seven numbered sections (as you read down, the number square fills and the heading darkens). For a principle or an article

notes: The Contact (/contact) and Play (/play) pages were not recorded, so they were not built — the header menu item ”Contact” drops down to the footer (external channel link), and the next section after Field Notes and a single note is ”Back to start,” unlike the original (Contact). So of the four next-section cuts (work · about · notes · start), the original’s contact cut (packets run across a dot grid and the camera flies to a faraway new section) and play cut (tiles flip) had their values read but are unused, so they were not built — whoever builds the contact section can add the L·z of page-depth-scene in the same place
The award badge (external awards badge) is replaced by our own round stamp with the same position, size and hover (rotates −10° and scales 1.06×)

The work-preview structure diagrams are redrawn with placeholder text on the same board (800×350, 40px grid, nodes 150×40, center 150×70) in the shapes of the original four (three branches → center → three branches, one with an intermediate step, one converging into one).

Font backfill (judgment): since the original is entirely English, the Archivo 900 title slots (big title·section title·company name·note title·principle title·next section name), the header wordmark·menu (including the phone menu) and the Hero buttons were switched to English placeholder text. Geist Mono eyebrow text (section number·number caption·loader text) and body-weight small titles (field names in About) are body-font slots, so they are left in Korean

title: Sound-reactive 3D experiment with a spinning glyph-dithered hand
good_for: A first screen for an experiment, lab page, exhibition or album intro with a single WebGL scene that spins with sound after an enter click.

pages.use: One-page experiment page: an entry tag follows the cursor, and pressing it opens, with sound, a glyph-dither 3D hand, dust and mouse fluid trails, while a logo, about drawer, title, clock and speed control attach to the four corners.

notes: The original uses three/webgpu + TSL (WebGPU renderer) — with the same three version (0.180), a WebGLRenderer and newly written GLSL reproduce the same values (12px cells · five glyphs · fluid .955/.9 · 5-stage bloom with 6~22 taps · spectral chromatic aberration no. 10 · rate smoothDamp). The WebGPU version is not used because _vendor has no three.webgpu

Instead of the hand model (hand.glb) and dust model (dust.glb), the same size and silhouette proportions are built from basic shapes (cylinder forearm·ellipse palm·four capsule fingers·thumb, ring+bar pin) — finger bending·hand pose are simpler than the original.

The original brightness steps (lumShades) have no value in the bundle, so they were matched by eye to 5 steps and a brightness multiplier of 3.6 — the glyph order (cross → empty square → circle → pink → purple) was also read off the screen
Instead of the original turbulence image, glyph image (icons.png) and hint strip image (slow-hint.png), these were redrawn as value noise, canvas glyphs and a canvas text strip

Instead of the original music (loop.mp3), shared.js synthesizes an 8-second loop (120bpm kick · offbeat hi-hat · low rumble) as WAV and repeats it with the same howler 2.2.4 — kick detection uses the original values (average frequency +7 · .23s interval · lowered along the floor every four frames)

Loading three.cjs as a plain script lets the class AudioContext inside it shadow the browser’s own, which breaks when howler unlocks and recreates the context — load howler before three and Howler.autoUnlock=After turning it off with false, call resume directly on the enter click
The twenty original onomatopoeia that change the title’s last word/document title on each kick were replaced with Korean onomatopoeia placeholders
The original logo image (logo.svg) slot is a text wordmark SVG placeholder of the same width (11rem)

title: Calm dark tech company with sidenote grid and checkered-pattern transitions
good_for: A B2B homepage for a deep-tech or research company with product intro, recruitment and an insights article list.

pages.use: Company home page — small wordmark, 64px title, screen-width parallax video Hero, a problem section where paragraphs light up in turn, a grid-pattern border, a product introduction where screen-height video cards stick, overlap and darken, Contact form. For tech company landing pages

Product introduction — title header attached over a video, 50px overview paragraph, an access section where text and old-plate cards stick one after another under the header bar over thin lines, demo request form. For explaining one product or platform in depth
Careers — sea video header, two-column text on how we work, a left-pinned plate and an openings list by field (apply button), and join-us text. For careers pages and openings lists.

Article list — sidebar category filter, 64px header, 3-column vintage plate thumbnails (on hover the cell pattern lights up one by one) · category dot · title · summary · details, pagination, Contact form. For insight, press and research article lists

notes: The original uses Astro ClientRouter (a swap that fetches the document and replaces it) — the router is a module inside the astro package so it is not bundled separately. The same order (cover with a panel .3s power4.inOut → cell pattern lights from the bottom row → after arriving, turn off the cells and lift the panel) was rebuilt with page navigation + sessionStorage. Difference: the header is not redrawn during the transition
The video uses the same playback as mux-player (auto · muted · loop · cover) with an empty video and a placeholder — the original video is not used
The original cell pattern is random every time it opens — the part (cell-walk-pattern) is also random by the same rule when there is no data-grid, so cell positions differ from the original each time
The site’s gsap curve bundle (P·E·C) was read as Power4·Expo·Circ (judged from the bundle export names and the power4·expo strings in measure)
Footer wordmark, logo A and hero wordmark use our own SVG — pixel-stair symbol + letters
Fonts: FK Aktual and MD Lorien are paid, so Hanken Grotesk and Newsreader are used, and Pretendard and Gowun Batang for Korean
A one-line script (at-arriving) in the head keeps the arriving page from painting once as a bare screen before shared.js — the original doesn’t have this problem because its router swaps the document

Font backfill (judgment call): since the original is entirely in English, the Hanken Grotesk heading slots (.at-h-l·.at-h-m·.at-h-s — from big headings to 50px and 32px large paragraphs), .at-label (section names·menu·categories·form field names·buttons·employment types), text and role-name lines (.at-sub heading), the header line·phone menu·news/contact modals·footer (shared.js), and the wordmark letters were replaced with English placeholder copy. The wordmark uses a word with no descending strokes (Brand), like the original wordmark — Company had its p·y tails cut off under the 250px footer panel

Korean kept in 35 slots (remaining in latin-slots): 18 body serif sentences p.at-body (Newsreader → Korean serif pair, the checker catches them because it reads --kf-font-serif as the Latin heading font), three 18px description sentences .at-sub (hero, careers and product intro text, Pretendard pair), and 14 wireframe notes span.wf-note. All are English in the original, but they are slots where the README says body and description sentences stay Korean.

/  The 366px horizontal overflow at 390 width comes not from text but from the cell-pattern motion part (the i cells of cell-walk-pattern .fx-cwp) drawn at desktop column width — outside this backfill’s scope (text only), so left untouched

title: Vertical-writing inn site with three layered contrast pairs rising in turn
good_for: A homepage for a ryokan, hotel, hot spring, upscale lodging or traditional restaurant where photos lead and vertical serif type sets the mood.

pages.use: Lodge home — brush-stroke logo opening, full-bleed video hero, a pinned section where three contrasting photo pairs rise like windows and overlap (numbers · progress line), three vertical title + photo strips, a room section where a small window photo grows to fill the screen, endless strip of room cards and dish photos, open-air bath photo, building isometric map, news, whole-lodge private booking, social tiles, coastal map, booking bar

About (concept). A photo hero with a vertical title, vertical text over a map illustration, the name’s meaning as text that sticks and follows beside a big square photo, four asymmetric photos for the stubbornness (features), two building intros (text and photo swapped left-right) and a food photo strip. For brand story and space philosophy pages.

Guest room guide — a sea-through-the-window hero, two vertical lines of copy with photos, three bowl cards (blurred photo panels), an interior 3D map of the building, a room index stuck to the left, and a room list with building names + a photo window rising for each room. For room and product list pages

News list — path·title, category stuck to the left, rows of thumbnail (3:2) + date·category + title, sea photo strip. For notice and announcement lists (the category URL /news/category/news has the same type, so it is merged into one)

notes: The original is a site builder’s CSS scroll-linked animation (animation-timeline: view()), so there is no library — the same ranges and keyframes were converted to screen-height units and built with GSAP ScrollTrigger scrub (original % are noted in the pin-pair-stack and pin-grow-photo notes). Values were measured at 1440×900, so on other screen heights they may be off by a few %
