title: Developer tool page with unfolding login cards and install terminal
good_for: Developer tool, API and SaaS landing pages that explain features through many hand-redrawn animated product UI illustrations.

pages.use: Product landing page — three unfolding login cards, customer logos, a three-row feature list, a panel that moves from a terminal install demo to a customization control panel, a 2×2 platform illustration (org switch · connection steps · role permissions · radar), three agent columns, a dark trust band, 8-second testimonial tabs, free-tier numbers that bloom as dots, and two closing cards. For developer tools and SaaS landing pages

notes: The original is a single page (pages: [] in pages.json), so there are no subpages.

The original is animated with React+motion (framer). It is open source but tied to React components, so the same curves, lengths and delays were ported to GSAP and CSS (install line schedule .07 to 2.97s, step names 1.21/2.12/2.97s, tab curtain .52s, agent chat .3/1.1 · 1.1/1.9 · 2.2s, testimonials 8 seconds · .8s · 5px blur, dot numbers 3s inOutQuad · sparkle 10ms/1.8s).

Setup → Decorate handoff: the original keeps the panel pinned and switches by time when the middle of the pinned range is crossed (not tied to scroll). Same approach here with ScrollTrigger pin + threshold play/reverse. The switch duration (.55s outQuint) is a guess, since I only saw frames 900ms apart.

The customizer panel’s language buttons are drawn as language abbreviations (EN·ES…) instead of the original flag images — this avoids flag colors being stamped regardless of the clothing. The four color swatches and the done-check green are ”not clothing”.

Client logos, certification badges and tool logos are our own SVG placeholders of equal size in grayscale. The hero stripe glow uses a repeating gradient with the same spacing (6px) instead of the original stripe image.
Fonts: original Untitled Sans (paid) → Geist. At the same -0.06em letter-spacing Geist runs slightly wider, so large heading lines are 2~4% longer than the original.
On phones (1023px and below), it does not do the fixed jump like the original, and instead adds one more customization status panel in the customization section (duplicating the install panel).
The spring curve used in the original’s pinned skip-over range could not be read (guessed as visualDuration .55 of motion) — worth scrolling on a wide screen yourself and re-measuring the length.

title: Immersive band page orbiting a car on a rainy night street via scroll
good_for: Immersive one-page sites for bands, records and musicians that present songs, videos, bio and contact within a single scene.

pages.use: A one-page band site — a start-door loader (progress wave · press to start), a 3D sedan on a rainy night road circled by scroll (logo on the car front → intro text under purple light → in-car dashboard cassette → intro in front of the forest → open trunk videotape → windshield hologram sticker contact), and scrolling to the end loops back to the start, with a bottom bar showing now playing and a music wave. For album releases and musician introductions

notes: Instead of the original car model (glb), textures (ktx2) and HDRI, this is built from our basic shapes: the body is the side profile (z·y) extruded to width 1.9, wheels are cylinders, and the interior uses boxes, capsules and rings. Silhouette proportions (length 5.9, width 2, height 1.42) and placements (four-eye front headlights, chrome bumper, waist chrome strip, vertical rear taillights, pink trunk interior) match, but the original’s fine body curves, door handles and seat texture are missing.

The original 96-frame camera path is animation baked into the glb so its values can’t be read — I pressed the start button on the original, scrolled down with the wheel, captured each section (/tmp/lib-brand-band-orig-2), re-set position · look-at target · field of view as 17 keys and joined them with Catmull-Rom. Section heights (200 · 200 · 200 · 300 · 400 · 400vh, phone 100 · 100 · 100 · 100 · 400 · 100) · section-to-frame mapping · 30±14 frame slow zone (S curve slow .08) · dot line frames (0 · 30 · 41 · 60 · 80) · section name roll frames (27 · 37 · 53 · 78) · intro text frames (9 · 12→26 · 22→29 / 37 · 40→51 · 51→54) · Lenis (1.7s, 1-(1-t)^5, wheel .7, ±50px clamp) · endless scroll (two copies, rewinds at one copy + 1.5 screens) are the original bundle values as they are

The original’s sound (three tracks, rain, engine sound, HRTF spatial audio) is not included. Music on/off only changes the floor wave (amplitude 10% per frame) and the text, and pressing the dashboard cassette only changes the Now playing track name.
Pressing the trunk videotape opens a video embed panel in the original — in the same spot a 16:9 video placeholder panel is placed (close · Esc · outside click, scroll stops while open).

The sub-routes opened by the original windshield ”BEHIND THE SCENES” sticker (scene descriptions, shader gallery, credits) were not recorded (pages: []), so they were not built — the sticker in the same spot only goes to #link-5.

The original road shader, ground spray and windshield rain refraction were roughly reduced — puddles use a roughness map, the windshield uses a water-drop normal map we painted, rain is lines circling a box around the camera (GPU), and ground spray is absent.

Loader progress does not follow the amount of assets loaded as in the original but fills with 1.35s power3.out (measured: the original mostly fills in the first 0.12s and the button appears at 1.65s). The first 3D draw (shader baking) is deferred until the loader is full so the waves don’t stutter.

The radial mask that cuts the phone panel’s logo and text panel around the logo like the original was not added. The phone cassette pillar, videotape strip and glass pieces are our own panels placed in front of the camera, passing in the same frame range.

The blackletter (ff-brokenscript → UnifrakturCook) slots (section name roll, dot-row heading, phone menu, phone contact title, loading text) and the wide grotesque 800 (owners-xxwide → Archivo 125 width) slots (About heading words, phone album name) are English in the original, so they were kept as English placeholders (Menu 1~5, Contact, Loading, Band Name, Album Name). Black Han Sans is kept only as the pairing for when Korean is put in those slots.

Intro body text and bold words (original owners-wide 200 and 500 body) are kept in Korean, so they fall back from Archivo to Noto Sans KR — narrower than the original. Hangul in small UI text (Inter Thin → Inter 100) uses the system sans — so the loader doesn’t finish late because of a font swap. Canvas text on the 3D pieces (tape cover, cassette label, windshield sticker) is also the body font (sans), so it is kept in Korean too.

3D stage colors are read from the skin (--kf-*·--site-*) when first loaded and painted — swapping theme.css turns the night road into that skin’s colors, but if only the skin changes while it is open, reload to apply it to the stage.
The original only registers ScrollTrigger and computes scene frames directly with rAF — the copy works the same way, so ScrollTrigger is not loaded.

title: One-screen holding company where draggable logo stickers pick the brand
good_for: Holding companies, studios and product families with many brands, using touchable logo mascots on a one-screen home plus blog and careers pages.

pages.use: One-screen first page — four logo stickers floating on a black board (they spring back when dragged and released), pressing lines them up in a row with a brand description panel and left/right buttons on the right, a Lottie wordmark and link row below. For the first screen of a company or product family with several brands

Blog list — back link, large title with a category filter on the right (on click, posts fade out and the remaining posts slide together), and a single-column list of title, author line, summary, and read more. For company News lists
Blog post detail — back link, title and author line, pastel blurred cover image, single-column body, image download and copy-post buttons, icon row. For a single notice or press post.

Careers — a bright careers page handed over from the original careers: a lavender fluid band on top, a heading whose words stand up, five photos that fly in and float, a two-column team intro, nine benefit cells, a numbered accordion of interview steps, job rows by department, a newsletter signup, and a large footer.

notes: The four logo stickers (original brand logo PNGs) were redrawn as our own SVG mascots with the same position·size·thick-outline sticker feel (beret rice cake·petal ring·smiling cloud·sparkle badge). Colors derive the outline·body·shade·face in oklch from one pastel (--c) per sticker.

The Lottie wordmark below is a fresh build of our own lettering BRAND (placeholder, five angular thin-stroke capitals) with the same 1000×270 · 60fps · 120 frames · same curves as the original (the center letter wipes up over frames 5→25 with .756,0→.15,1, the four side letters slide out from behind the center over frames 19→79 with .273,0→0,1). When using the original wordmark artwork, just drop in a Lottie with the same tempo (window.AX_WORDMARK in wordmark.js).

The eight sound effects (press, drag, drop, open, close, next, previous, error) do not use the original wav files — they are newly made as short WebAudio sine-wave sounds for the same uses. The error sound is defined only, since the original does not use it either (there is no inactive brand state).

The recorded careers is another company’s bright page that example.com/careers forwards to. The recruit pieces (header, menu panel, consent card, photo collection, accordion, footer, fbm-flow-band, word-tilt-rise) of library/rounded-panel-fintech-product, already built in our style from the same original, were moved into this site’s Skin. Only this page reconnects --kf-* in body.ar-scope to the stage opposite the background (--kf-contrast-*) to paint it light, and the accent color is made by turning the difference from sticker purple to the original lavender. The original bundle’s own careers (two value columns, benefits, interview steps, department list, black panel) does not open on the original now, so it was not built.

Blog filter category names (Brand One…Studio) and post titles are English placeholders, while summaries and body are text placeholders. The original thirteen posts were cut to eight (repeats of the same pattern).

The post cover image (original PNG 2160×1140 — pastel blurred background with a black symbol in the center) was drawn with a CSS gradient of the same ratio + our petal-ring symbol SVG. The original image slot’s loading shimmer (2s stripes) is left out because the image appears immediately.
The ”Copy logo as SVG” item in the wordmark right-click menu puts the currently drawn Lottie SVG on the clipboard, and ”Get brand assets” just closes the menu since there is no file to download.

In the original, the blog → first page transition takes 2.2s until the first page appears (sticker pops up) (confirmed with --repeat 3 as 268·255·271+2183ms). Subpages pause 200ms while the next page loads and then fade over .2s (original first change 240~270ms), and the first page fades right away over .27s.

The loading shimmer of image slots (avatar · post cover) (::before 2s diagonal stripes, transparent 1s after loading — same values as the original image slot) is a drawn panel, so it becomes Loaded right after the first frame. With real photos, attach it on img load (shared.js).
/  careers phone screen: the benefits cells become a one-line list with icon left and text right, as in the original (390) (the library/rounded-panel-fintech-product version had two columns).

The panel text (Korean placeholder) is drawn once off-screen during an idle moment on the first page, to avoid the font download on first open (index.js). If the real brand text uses a Latin typeface, it can be removed.

title: Interior design firm with spring-pushed photos and gold panels
good_for: Interior, architecture and hospitality design firm sites with large-photo portfolios, expandable services and filterable projects.

pages.use: Company home page — narrow serif title and gold quote, large photo slides pushed by springs (ring-dot buttons, numbers), awards and press, mud-colored panel team intro, partner company card row (slick), full-bleed photo, gold panel work categories (photo swaps on hover), newsletter. For interior and architecture company landing pages
About the company — big photo header, story and four numbers, quote, moss-colored founder section, wishes, names of ideas, people grid (5 columns), client logo grid. For company and team About pages
Services — title and photo on the left, seven expandable list items on the right, sky-blue handwork photo collage, expandable partner companies, golden contact band. For introducing service scope
Work list — pinned category filter on the left (expand · select), three-column vertical photo cards on the right and a large landscape card per row. For project portfolio lists
Newsletter signup — big centered heading and underlined input field, gold panel work categories. For news subscription or short signup pages

notes: All photos are placeholders describing the scene (restaurant, hotel and bar interiors, black-and-white group photo, upper-body portraits). The first-visit loader’s three random photos are also a single placeholder

Typefaces: the original Roslindale Deck Narrow, Roslindale, GT America and GT America Extended are paid, so the closest free ones are used — narrow serif Instrument Serif (Korean Noto Serif KR), light body Inter 300 (Korean Pretendard), wide uppercase label Archivo width 125

about our story, two paragraphs · service intro — the original also sets them as serif h5 paragraphs of about five lines, so Korean is kept (paired with Noto Serif KR)

On phones the button · number row is hidden, as in the original.

Locomotive is 4.1.3 like the original (the library only had 4.1.4, so the npm build was added to _vendor) · slick 1.8.1 · jQuery 3.5.1 are also the same versions. Like the original, once Locomotive starts it pins the page with position: fixed and adds a scroll bar (z 999999).

Work list filtering only goes as far as showing the chosen one of three categories (the original’s CMS-style filter and URL query sync are not built). good_for: Intros for farm-direct and organic food shops, small restaurants and workshops that show big photos while keeping text in a narrow paper column.

For the hero of a small shop or farm-direct homepage
Notice list — section head (title · English tagline · 3:2 photo), vertical CATEGORY label + two categories, date | category · title rows. For news and notice lists

About us — hand-drawn underlined title · bold two lines · text and photos entering alternately from the right and left, a sailboat drawing, a map drawing in a white box over a photo, a flowing photo strip, and owner intros with two round photos. For shop · couple intros

Activities intro — anchor tabs, three Swipers for products·producers (round photo popping out over the panel)·cooking class (fraction number·arrows), customer voices with a pinned picture panel and a growing background (read more fold). For product·service·class intros
Notice detail — date｜category, underlined big title, body paragraphs, previous arrow · back-to-list button, category tabs. For notice · post detail

notes: The navy-line hand-drawn GIFs (sailboat · rowing boat · loading · back to top) were redrawn as SVG at the same ratio and the same 5fps — three waves swap every 200ms and the boat sways at the loop length (3s·9s·6.82s). The delicate lines of the original drawing (window bars · two people) were reduced
The map GIF (36 frames, one turn, 1.35s) was redone in the same order and length with an abstract coastline, regional land, lines drawn from dots and red place-name SVG (plays once when visible)
The hero wavy-edge photo (the original is a PNG with wavy left and right edges) is replaced with an SVG mask of the same shape
Paper-grain tiles (cont_bg01·02·03 photos) are replaced with a fine noise mask + average color (#ece8dd·#e4e4e4·#f2f1eb)
Logo (shop name + boat emblem image) and journal handwritten logo (awalog) are text + simple SVG emblem placeholders — a slot for the actual logo image (data-label)
lazyload@2.0.0-rc.2 only defers image loading (no motion), so it is not included — only the map image’s ”once when visible” was matched using IntersectionObserver.
GSAP uses the _shared build instead of the original 3.10.4. Position of the activity About pin-scrub "500px"(Missing label) is passed through as-is, like the original, and GSAP appends it at the end

Phone panels under 750px carry over only the skeleton (header, menu, footer, Hero, photo strip, section heads) of the vw values in the original smartphone.css — per-section detail spacing relies on desktop values
The 751~1023px tablet version only shifts the column to 100% and hides the left photo
The original journal (awalog) list and post pages were not recorded, so they were not built — the journal link in the menu is a # placeholder

title: Red-panel studio where coins leap onto the headline
good_for: Small design and development studio sites with a playful hero, scattered case studies, service cards, a draggable work board and case detail pages.

pages.use: Studio first page: a hero where the number box unfolds into a red panel (FLIP), the text bounces in from both sides, and then 3D coins pour over the text and pile up, a fixed-sentence section where words rotate like a cylinder to change, four works scattered with parallax as a pink line is drawn, a work list where hovering a row stacks photos in layers, service cards that land with a squash, a contact panel with an ”I need” pill band, and a footer that copies the email

Service About: a first section where choosing a tab rotates a card stack to change the front card (case tiles show a second photo on hover), a pinned section where scrolling lands four how-we-work cards in a fan shape and dragging snaps them back elastically, and a contact panel. For service and working-method pages

Work collection — the whole screen is a dotted board with case cards scattered endlessly in a staggered grid, drag to glide with inertia, move the cursor to an edge and the board flows, zoom with ctrl+wheel or buttons. For a portfolio page that feels like play

A single case — large title with a field, year and role line, wide photo set, next-case panel, More projects list (stacked-photo hover, pink line) and contact panel. For case studies and Work detail pages

notes: The logo is an English placeholder ”studio.” instead of the original wordmark. The letter swap (letters exit toward the direction the cursor was heading .18s power2.in → appear from the opposite side → .5s elastic) is applied to the logo and the hero’s big title letters with the original code as is (AW.charSwap). The end value is the letter width, so the logo is smaller than the original (22px).

Hero coins: instead of the original coin model, a newly turned coin (rim with thickness · dished face · ring pattern) made with three LatheGeometry, using the same physics (matter-js 0.20.0, pre-stacked pile + first 4 coins .32s apart → 3.2s±15%). The RoomEnvironment env map (intensity .45) was replaced with a white fill light (fill 1.6) — coin-drop-physics motion part.

I did not port the original’s ‹path-finding that hops across the letters in turn›. As in the original, parts are thrown once from the top-left at text height. While flying they pass behind the text, and they only collide with it once they drop below the text line (at first, thrown pieces hit the corner of ”REMEMBER.” and piled up in the off-screen wall, so no coins showed in the hero). Since the justified line’s box spans the full panel width, index.js swaps the words for collision boxes. The pieces are bigger than the original (r 50), so the pile lays out in a single row.
Per-row parallax value for the Work scatter section (H = 14·−10·12·−8) are values not found in the original code, estimated from the video recording.
Service card stack: fixed length set to .8 screen per card (the original’s height formula is set after hydration, so it was matched by recording).

The original’s ‹cover FLIP› transition (the cover photo grows into the detail) on clicking a case card was not carried over. All page transitions were unified as sheet-label-page (accent-color sheet plus the destination page name).
The contact page (/contacts) was not recorded so it was not built — the headline get in touch. and the Contacts menu link to the footer (#contact). The cookie consent bar was also left out.

Email copy (on hover the address slides up and Copy to clipboard rises in, on click it goes to the clipboard and shows Copied plus a send-now link) follows the original EmailLink. On touch devices or where there is no clipboard, it is just a mailto link.

After passing the overlay to the first page, the coin 3D setup overlapped with the overlay clearing and made the clearing stutter — like the original whenPageShown, it now waits for ‹fx:sheet-label-page:shown›, fired after sheet-label-page has fully cleared, before appearing (a notification was added to the part).

cursor-sweep first page: the original reaction cells are the title letters flipping as the cursor passes, plus the marks left while writing, where a new coin thrown every 3.2s±15% passes behind the letters from the top left and lands on the pile (confirmed with the cell map). After matching the coin toss to the original path, it passes at y 35% 11.9% ↔ 18.9%, y 60% 17.8% ↔ 16.7% (settle 447 ↔ 448ms).

Not viewed side by side with interact. Phone width was checked only with shot(390, horizontal overflow 0 · errors 0) — the phone menu and work panel dragging are for the next person to check with interact.

title: Award-parody racing game with a warning sign intro and hex arena
good_for: Browser mini games, interactive campaigns and event pages that play an intro sequence and then go straight into one-screen play.

pages.use: Browser racing mini game — loader, warning-sign intro, sound prompt, hexagonal 3D arena, menu and leaderboard, judging gauge, wreck result card, mobile joystick. For interactive campaigns and event games

notes: The game physics is a hand-built arcade physics (forward and back rolling · side slipping · jumping · falling) instead of the original’s Bullet3 (physics.js wasm). Blocked because Bullet3 and ammo are under the zlib license, which is outside the _vendor allow list (MIT · BSD · Apache · ISC · Unlicense), and physics.js is that site’s own build. The car is a primitive-shape car (box · cylinder · capsule driver) rather than the real model. Rival cars, bosses, firing and explosive weapons are absent (the fire and explosion slots are dimmed, like the original’s first state). Boost (Shift) refills for 2 seconds for every 4 likes.

three build is 0.160.0 (npm UMD build/three.min.js) — the original three sits in a single bundle obfuscated with a string array (module.*.js, WebGPU renderer), so REVISION could not be read. three.cjs as a plain <script> Loaded that way, three’s class AudioContext·Audio overwrite global names and break howler, and modules are blocked on file://, so a UMD wrapped in a function is used (three prints one console warning that it will be removed soon — not an error)

Elimination happens not when broken apart as in the original, but when falling out of the arena or into a black hexagonal hole. Instead of the original’s distorted WASTED art, the elimination text is three layers of letters (white · --kf-danger · backing piece) in the same spot and size, slamming in from the right with expo.out over 1s, and the red smoke is drawn as 26 canvas circles

The key art (loader background) and channel banner are left as image slots (.wf-img). The sign-holding character, the sound-prompt face, ranking avatars and medals are redrawn in SVG and CSS gradients to match only the position, size and feel (the originals are 3D renders). The inherent colors of these graphics (skin, eyes, tongue, gold/silver/bronze, avatar colors, browser logos) are marked ”Not Skin” so they stay the same graphic when the Skin changes. The 8 tech logos on the sign are .wf-logo placeholders.

The loader progress has no files to fetch, so it fakes progress in about 3–6 seconds (the original takes about 12 seconds with a real download). The cell formula (√(w·h/200) · cubed distance · opacity .3 expo.out · final scaleY 0→1.1 .5s power3.out random .4s) and the yellow title fill (background-position-x 1.5s power1.out) are the same

Sound is wired with howler 2.2.4 like the original — choosing sound on continues the background track on loop at the original first track volume (.175), with sound effects for picking up likes and for failing, and the sound button at the right of the footer toggles it. The track and effects are not the original files but placeholder sounds made with ffmpeg (media/, track loops at 16s). The original track list (playlist skip) and effect names such as engine and crash sounds are called inside the obfuscated game module and could not be carried over.

Instead of the paid typeface Druk Wide Cy, uses Archivo at width 125 · 900 italic, with Black Han Sans (bold titles) and Noto Sans KR for Korean. Since the original text is all English, titles, section names, menus, buttons, name lines, gauge names and scorecard field names are English placeholders, while only sentences such as warnings, notices, modal body and the one-line contact are in Korean. Archivo is narrower than Druk Wide, so even with the same character count (loader Arcade Title 6·5 chars ↔ original 6·6 chars) titles come out about 20% shorter than the original.

Fixes for text length: on phones (under 767px) the eliminated word (Crashed, 7 letters) overflows the screen at the 80px base size, so only at that width it shrinks to 13vw (the original is an image, so it is scaled to the screen width). The report-card buttons are shortened to Menu · Retry so they do not wrap onto two lines. The modal title follows the text of the button that opened it, and icon buttons use data-title (Share·Settings·Gamepad·Driver·Garage). The aria-label of an icon button stays as the original Korean description

Section images (library-shots --again) capture only the menu and the two arenas — the four intros, elimination and scorecard are initially hidden scenes, so the tool cannot capture them (it has always been so). The intro text was shot with shot --steps 26 in time order and checked for no overflow

Adding #menu · #game · #wasted · #session to the URL skips the intro and jumps straight to that scene (for review and reuse checks, not in the original). Only first-time visitors see the three intros and from the second visit they go directly to the sound prompt (localStorage), same as the original

The phone joystick uses the same nipplejs 0.10.2 as the original (the defaults in the original bundle match this build) with the original settings (static · bottom-left 67px · size 154 · threshold .08 · fadeTime 120 · restOpacity 1 · white 82%). The original’s controller (gamepad) support is missing — blocked: the pad button and axis wiring sits inside the game module (obfuscated), so which button does what could not be read. Going to fullscreen when the phone is rotated to landscape is included exactly as in the original

title: Hospital SaaS page pushing with pure teal bands and orange buttons
good_for: B2B SaaS and business tool sites with case studies, feature lists and news, plus lead-generation landings for document requests and demo sign-ups.

pages.use: Service home page — blue Hero (No.1 ranking band, feature tags, big title, two pill buttons, device graphic, giant B—A letters at the bottom), one flowing customer logo row, photo + panel intro, blue action band, three numbers, a number panel and figure cards straddling the photo strip, testimonial slider, onboarding flow, News, logo grid, final CTA and Footer.
Feature list — six category tabs under the header row, each with a three-column icon feature card set and two orange buttons. For service intros with many items, like features or pricing
Case study list — featured case carousel straddling a blue band (3s tempo), category tags, and a three-column case grid of photo, summary, tag and logo
News list — a notice and event list with tag, date and title rows joined in one white panel below a blue band

One case study — a large photo straddling a blue band with an overlapping title panel, an interview body in Q&A (blue questions, left-bar subheads, photos), a following side column (material request ad, clinic info)

notes: The original was built with STUDIO (a no-code builder) and has no open-source library — appear (.appear), carousel (sd-carousel) and header bar are STUDIO runtime code, so they were not used and were moved into Motion parts with the same values: appear fade-up (y 60 · .6s · .4s later · cubic-bezier(.4,.4,0,1) · opacity only), logo strip marquee (30s per set), testimonial and selected-case advance hold-step-strip (rest 2.4s + advance .6s = Original interval 3000ms, cubic-bezier(.58,.21,.41,.96), pause on hover·arrows — these two were added to the part as options this time).

The device illustrations (admin screens inside laptop · tablet · phone) and award badges don’t use original photos — they were newly drawn as line-art SVG in the skin colors and as round badges. The giant B—A lettering at the bottom is drawn with Oswald letters and bars at the same position and height (225px) instead of the original logo art.

The orange action color has no standard slot in the skin (theme.css), so --site-cta-* in shared.css is derived by rotating the accent oklch (same values as the original #ff7600·#ffb000 and hover #e36900·#eea500). When the skin changes, it follows to the color opposite the accent.

The category tabs of the feature list stick under the header row and follow as in the original, and clicking one jumps to that category (smooth scrolling isn’t in the original either). Feature counts per category and card text are placeholders matching the original item counts.

The category tags in the case-study list have only the look and no filtering behavior (the original navigates to another address). The side column of the case detail sticks beside the body and follows along, like the original (position: sticky).
The event banner floating at the bottom right of the original (150px image, STUDIO _c1/_c2) is not visible in the 1440·390 captures, so it was not built.

On phone (below 840px) there is a white square menu button at top right and a button row stuck to the bottom of the screen (request materials · free demo), as in the original. Tapping the menu opens a blue drawer in .3s — the original drawer shape was guessed because there is no recording.

title: Performing arts department page where a gold oval frame expands into the stage
good_for: University department, arts school and performance group recruitment pages with a long scene-changing scroll covering features, faculty, performances, curriculum, careers and open campus.

pages.use: A one-page department intro. A gold oval frame on a petal-drifting silk background grows and blurs with scroll into the stage video. Two talent profiles have photos that widen to the screen width. A features plate has a photo growing .375→1 with three pinned points. There is a faculty list (hover photo · modal), a performance photo plate approaching from 1→3x, a 9-cell curriculum tab in front of a red curtain, horizontally flowing career cards, a vertical-writing message, and a contact·name curtain over a theater photo. For department and school admissions pages.

notes: The original is a single page (pages: [] in pages.json) — there are no subpages.

The hero’s five baroque frames, gold flower ornaments, silk background, marble floor and rose petals do not use the original artwork but were redrawn. The center oval frame is a thick white rim plus a cluster of gold blossoms in SVG, the four side frames are white double-rim boxes plus chains, the silk is a CSS gradient, and the petals are forty ellipses scattered from a fixed seed (7s · 10s floating and .03x mouse parallax are the original values). The mosaic effect of the photos inside the original frames is the photo itself, so it is not included.

The oval window zoom (diameter 332+.2y, frame scale, background .02, blur .005, vanishes .75s after 2 screens, 10ms throttle) is written in index.js exactly after the original RS() formula, and the same motion is also extracted as the frame-window-zoom part. The site has to compute the frame position from the inner panel layout (design 811·403), so it does not attach the part and uses the same formula directly.

The stage background video (about.mp4, 1920×1080, 30s) is replaced with a dark gradient placeholder video of the same 16:9, 30s, looping, muted, autoplay format (stage-placeholder.mp4, 640×360, 46KB, newly made with ffmpeg). The performance-record modal video uses the same file.

Swiper has no version notation in the original bundle, so classes (swiper-slide-fully-visible = treated as the 11 series) and used swiper@11.2.10. simplebar (modal scroll bar) is not included, and it is left as plain scroll with data-lenis-prevent.

The schedule box (SCHEDULE bracket list) and small photo row inside the feature point panel, and decorations like the yellow circle and blue triangle in the About section, are approximate in placement. The Open Campus and Access sections were built with generic card and map slots because the original print was not examined closely — the next person should compare with the original and refine.

title: Startup design studio with a photo cylinder world and clothesline fabric photos
good_for: Design studio and agency homepages, work-heavy portfolios, services and case detail pages.

pages.use: Studio home page — a 3D world where photo tiles orbit around a cylinder (look around with the cursor, drag, scatter on scroll), with an intro in the center, a ”Book a call” button, a cylinder band of case-study logos, a two-column staggered work list with client quotes, fabric photos pinned on a clothesline, and a pill footer. For studio landing pages with lots of work
Work list — filter pills (with counts) and Surprise me, 4-column 4:3 tiles (on hover the photo changes every .9s). For work and portfolio lists
Services — each service has name, description and customer quote in three columns, three photos below, and a price row at the end. For service and pricing introductions
About — per row: faded name, body and customer quote in three columns, tilted attached main photo, working method and contact list. For a small studio introduction

Case detail — left thumbnail rail (2x and name on hover), right section ruler, fact table, one-liner, large photo, text per section and screen mockups inside a cream panel (switching on as if developing), color swatches, next case. For a single Work page

notes: The original currently has 0 slots for 3D models (GLTF) on the wall, so it loads three without using it — the copy also spins the same wall with CSS 3D without three. The 3 cutout slots are our SVG characters. The octopus 3D model and ASCII build (live-ascii) in the inkbox detail are not in the recorded zinc detail, so they were not built.

The pricing·clients pages were not recorded, so they were not built — nav pricing links to services.html#pricing (the pricing row) and clients links to works.html. ”Book a call” is an external feature in the original that opens an external booking popup, so it only points to #book. Work for the next person to pick up.

The original’s hidden gags (pressing the logo several times → cupcake rain and fireworks, 1999 and 2010 era skins, blueprint mode, theme color meta matching, toast) are not site motion so they were not built.
The work list is cut from the original 36 items to 15 (two staggered columns plus a short comment), the case list to 16 slots, and the detail rail to 16 slots. Shape and order are unchanged.

Page turns use a cross-document View Transition like the original (@view-transition navigation: auto). The old screen fades out upward in .15s, the new screen enters from below in .25s, the nav and bottom pill stay put, and the large detail photo carries over under the name bk-hero in .4s. It runs only in Chrome 126+.

title: Park guide with a forest-green vertical menu and hand-drawn zone map
good_for: Homepages for parks, arboretums, nature facilities and tourist sites, especially facility guides with zone maps and activity programs.

pages.use: Facility first page — Hero where a photo panel and a forest-green vertical menu board interlock · About sidenote · wide photo parallax and island map · vertical fade highlights · hand-drawn zone map accordion · tilted photo course · experience slider · event cards · creature photo strip and detailed illustrations · News strip. For park or tourist facility home pages.
News list — single-line title·date list centered at 860px with circular pagination. For notice and press release lists
A news post — date, large title with a line below, 【subheading】 body, back to list. For closure and operating notices

Facility About — three sections with faint large English titles (Overview, Activities, Operating organization), four 88px numbers, activity rows with number cells, an oval landscape photo. For park and institution About pages

Usage guide: a title column beside the left sticky element and body on the right, a reservation notice, a group of document downloads, a numbered list of rules, and a facility info table. For usage rules and application guide pages.

notes: The hand-drawn area map, island map, botanical illustration and side-panel fern pattern do not copy the original art. They are newly drawn procedural SVG in the same spot, size and texture (blob contours, paths, small facility drawings, compass, fern leaves, fiddleheads). Not as dense as the original illustration.

When a region cell opens, the original shows an enlarged map image drawn separately for each region (top-map-a~e). Since the image is the content, here the same SVG map is scaled 1.7× with that region pulled to the right center, and laid over it with the same motion (.95→1 · opacity .3s).
Weather and temperature in the bottom info bar are filled by the original via a weather API — only today’s date is entered, weather and temperature are placeholders
Original Zen Old Mincho has no Korean glyphs, so it was swapped for Nanum Myeongjo (English labels use the same Source Serif 4, small info uses IBM Plex Sans KR)
The forest-green textured band (the original’s bg-green-texture.jpg photo texture) uses feTurbulence noise layered with soft-light instead, so no image file has to be moved over.

Async loading for the News list ‹Load more›, creature guide filtering (category and season filters), the creature card modal (nature-modal.js), the map facility sheet (spot-sheet.js), and the experience detail and FAQ pages do not appear in the five recorded pages so they were not built

When the pointer is over the creature photo row, the original picks the illustration from the DOM order after Swiper init (if loop reorders the slides, a different creature may show). Here it picks by data-swiper-slide-index (the real slide number) that Swiper sets

Font slot text (2026-11-06): the original is a Japanese site, so the large headings, menu and logo name are Zen Old Mincho kana and kanji, and Latin (Source Serif 4) is only small English such as the English under the menu, English translation paragraphs, View more, Information and the bottom strip. These slots are already English placeholders (Place Name·Event·Map·English subtitle …), so no text was changed. Paired fonts: headings use Nanum Myeongjo (Mincho ↔ original Mincho), and Latin Source Serif 4 is followed by Nanum Myeongjo (serif ↔ Mincho), both loaded in theme.css.
Breadcrumbs (about·news·service·article) — the original is Japanese kana text (Home · What Is the Park), so Korean is kept. It is a Latin typeface slot but is drawn with its pair Nanum Myeongjo

index directions: departure·arrival names (departure 1 · North Gate · South Gate) — the original uses Chinese-character place names (Park North Exit …), so Korean kept. Only the adjacent min stays Latin as in the original
”Zone:” in the index map zone names — original is in kana (Zone:), so Korean kept
wf-note (motion memo for builders, hidden in the artwork) — kept as a Korean memo, not placeholder text. latin-slots catches it because it sits inside a Latin cell, but it is not something to fix

title: Forest bar hotel with a dropping wave logo and a hundred bars lifting off a photo
good_for: Sites for bar- or lounge-centered boutique hotels, ryokan and restaurants, including a home page, time-of-day concept slider, facilities and news list.

pages.use: Hotel first page — loader where 21 bars fall and stand up as a logo, video hero + centered logo, vertical-writing intro, photo slideshow with bar covers peeling away and four overlapping text-panel sections (bar, rooms, hot spring, facilities), four grey-brown news cards, Instagram grid, footer and sister inns

Concept — a wave (WebGL) photo header, vertical-writing About, six full-screen scenes with times 18:00~14:00 (section-snapping scroll, the time fills up by 1 minute), a right-side vertical time scale, and a next-section guide band. For brand story or daily schedule intros.

Bar venue introduction — wavy photo header, vertical-text intro, parallax photo strip, three sections (interior · drinks · food) where two photos slide past in a staggered way, two rows of photo + overlapping text panels, two light cards, opening hours info, next-section strip. For presenting a single venue such as a bar, restaurant or lounge in depth
News list — gray-brown title band, category row, four-column cards (a center cross line on hover), square page numbers. For notice and event lists

notes: Of the four recorded subpages, the fourth (the News category list, event) has the same form as the News list, so it was merged into a single news.html (only is-current in the category row differs). It was caught as detail during recording but is actually a list, so it was corrected to news.

Original Canela (paid) was swapped for Cormorant, and the well-known serif for Noto Serif KR. The logo is a newly drawn bar motif with the same 21 bar heights and baseline proportions as the original + an English placeholder.

The original hero video is a video-site iframe (youtube-player), so it is replaced with a local placeholder video in the same spot with the same cover, muted, looping. The loader reveal that switches between 4.2s/4.7s depending on when playback starts is fixed at 4.7s, since the original value is also set at DOMContentLoaded and ends up 4.7s.

The original TweenMax 2.0.1 belongs to GreenSock’s paid license line, so it is not used. Shared GSAP 3 produces the same curves instead (Circ.easeOut → circ.out, Power3 → power3). PreloadJS 0.4.1 (photo preloading) was left out since it has nothing to do with motion. swiper 4.2.2, jquery.ripples 0.6.3, jquery-scrollify 1.0.21, paroller.js 1.2.0 (a version without the transition option, the same form as the original bundle) and jQuery 3.3.1 are kept at the same versions in _vendor (the original bundle has no version label for ripples, so the last version of the 0.6 line was used).

The ripple effect (jquery.ripples) only runs when a background photo URL is set, so a gray patterned photo (media/ripple.jpg) is used as a placeholder. The original uses separate values for PC (radius 100·perturbance .001) and phone (50·.01), and the copy does the same.

External booking engine, cookie consent, chatbot widget and social media feed are placeholders. The booking panel’s calendar is cut down to three fields: date, guests, room (the panel still rises with the same 0.6s Circ motion).

Motion parts: four newly extracted: photo cover bars 100 (bar-blind-reveal), bar wave loader (wave-bars-loader), slanted rising info strip hover (slant-wipe-hover), and minute-by-minute rising time display (minute-count-up).

title: Single-job company page with bear scenes peeling away one by one
good_for: Character-driven company or service intros, part-time and staff recruitment, and storybook-style campaign landing pages.

pages.use: Company home: after the loader, six pagePiling sections (hero with a four-slot bear, a row of working bears, a desk scene, a big arms-wide bear, a perspective bear crowd) lift away with one wheel tick. Inside the last section, the POINT speech bubble, first-timer slider, questions, interview application, contact and footer scroll. For recruiting and service landings that speak through characters.

Company intro — yellow header·cream intro card·navy band title·POINT 01~03 rows (cream·mint·pink)·three work-style cards·staff reviews (silhouette·speech bubble·round face). For company and brand intros, three-strengths pages
Sign-up · job intro flow — registration guide and a wide apply button, STEP 01~06 rows (speech bubbles · comic panels · enlarge window). For process steps from sign-up to settlement
FAQ — nine yellow card accordion (first question open, navy answers). For a service FAQ page

notes: Bear character art: instead of dozens of original PNG illustrations (working poses · props · comic panels), five SVG bear forms in the same place, size and color scheme (upper body · fist · full body · box · desk scene · arms spread) are reused with only the shirt color changed — props like long materials, vacuum cleaner and helmet are only partly drawn. Drawing more of the original’s varied poses is left for the next person
The comic panels (flow STEP 02·04·06) are placeholders with a bear picture in a 4-panel frame — the user supplies the actual comic content. The enlarged view uses dialog.showModal like the original

The original loader starts hiding from a PIXI.loader.load callback in pixi.js 4.8.2 (an empty load, so immediately), but since it draws nothing on screen, pixi is not loaded and the same timeline is hooked on DOMContentLoaded. TweenMax 2.0.2 is mapped to the same-named GSAP 3 curves (expo.in·expo.out·bounce.out). The #wrapper scale-up (1.1→1) at the end of the original loader does not run because the original has no #wrapper, so it is not included

The original title typeface corporate-logo-ver2 (a paid web-font service) becomes Pretendard 900 + italic, and the body Noto Sans JP becomes Noto Sans KR. Where the original makes big sentences as SVG lettering art (white 10px stroke), we used HTML text + -webkit-text-stroke · paint-order to get the same white outline.

The company info and contact form pages (company · contact) were not recorded, so they were not built — the Company Info menu links to the About page footer (#company), and CONTACT links to the contact band on the same page (the home page jumps to item 6 and then scrolls down to that spot)
The header Request Consultation and booking buttons lead out to an external booking service in the original, so they link to the consultation request band on the same page (#bh-fee)

Section 1 at phone (390) is built like the original with a 2×2 grid plus inner scroll (pp-scrollable), but the cropping position of the bear in each cell and the placement of the big sentence are eyeballed

title: White screen with a centered underline field and pill button for a password gate

pages.use: Password gate single page — underlined password field and shadowed pill button at screen center, fills with neon on hover and turns red when wrong. For a pre-launch shop or private preview lock screen

notes: The original is a single page (pages: [] in pages.json) so it has no sub-pages. It has no menu, footer or loader either, so shared.js wasn’t made.

Copy: the original placeholder text PASSWORD stays Password as the field is used (displays in uppercase), and the button ACCESS was changed to Unlock with the same letter count — both are single Helvetica uppercase words, so they stay in English (data-label).

title: Creative label site with fluid ribbons between masking panels
good_for: Creative labels, social projects and cultural organization sites with project intros, members and activity records.

pages.use: Label home page — a wordmark loader (bars and four photos unfold, then the panel lifts away upward), a cursor fluid gradient (WebGL) seen only as a band between the top and bottom masks, an About section sliding in from the right, project photos that pass over a background with fluid showing through a 21px vertical gap in the center and get twisted and cropped, a wall of shrinking photo columns, a member row (rolls over to a dark ink row depending on which side the pointer enters, click opens a portrait photo cover), and a dark footer. For the home of a culture and society project label

About — over a video pinned to the screen, blur panels of white 70%, black 50% and white 50% pass by: the large mission text and body darken one letter at a time, three overlapping value cards fan out, a roadmap (left pinned title · growing progress line · only the passing year darkens), and activity record cards that stack pinned and shrink to .9x. For organization About and roadmaps

Project list — at the bottom of the Hero, an 80px name row rolls over to a dark View More row depending on the side the hand entered from, and photos pop out and stack on the right panel (on phones and tablets rows are revealed by scrolling and the center photo splits). For Work and case lists
News list — large sticky title on the left, one-line ellipsized title rows on the right (same rolling effect and preview as the list). For news and notice lists

Project detail: a 500px fixed text column on the left (date, title, intro, client, partner, members) and on-site photos floating up and passing on the right, with a Next project band below (inverts on interaction). On phone and tablet only the photos flow, with a bottom bar and button opening a half drawer. For a single case detail.

notes: The fluid shader was not ported from the original but rewritten with the same values (brush 25 · force 10 · decay .98 · stop .85 · phone .7/.8/.95x · 30fps) — instead of the original’s 8-step backtracking advection and area correction it uses one advection plus neighbor averaging, so the swirl grain is softer than the original, and the four-color band pattern is also our own (domain warp + sine bands), so the band shapes differ

The original home page’s member preview panel (.member-preview) never actually shows, because the condition for showing the photo (cursor paused frame) is always false in the same frame as mousemove — the copy did not build it either. The home page’s project-preview panel also has no paired list so it never runs, so the same dead code was removed from the copy

swup: the original visit:start fetches the next section’s html once more to attach section-specific css. The copy omits this because it applies the same css to all sections. Opened via file://, swup cannot run so a normal navigation happens (it runs over http)

Kept as is (original assets → our placeholders in the same spots): menu·loader·about background videos (no playback behavior), project·activity·member photos, value card images (line-shape SVG), loader·header logo image (wordmark SVG). The original loader header h1 holds a logo image, so the letter split becomes an empty group and the two letter in/out segments just take up 1s each with no movement — the copy does the same

The twist-crop start point of project photos was judged as bottom bottom because the original string was cut off (end bottom top · scrub .5 are original). The original effect where the horizontal cover turns into a vertical strip in the Projects section is reproduced by opening a 21px gap in the center of the section background and hiding the horizontal cover meanwhile (no motion at the moment of change)

title: Fashion brand where a line of models unfolds into a carousel
good_for: Fashion and streetwear brand shops, collection landing screens and lookbooks with a floating white gauge box, wide capitals and a manifesto that darkens toward the page end.

pages.use: Brand hero — eleven models drawn with shaders on a WebGL stage stand in a row (an elliptical ring on phones), click to spread them into a carousel, advance with the wheel, and click the center model for the lookbook. Corner cells (header, collection bar, product count bar) and page info. For a collection hero.
Product list — cross-grid cells in 6 columns with cut-out products, 1.3x on hover, two branches (each with a heading). For a shop-wide product or drop list

Lookbook story — photos filling the screen width follow one another with a white-text credits table stuck on top, and a bar below with three products from the photos. For campaign and photo-feature stories
Notice text — long copy such as a size chart or terms in a narrow center column. For size guide, shipping and terms pages

notes: The Hero model in the original is a green-screen video (VideoTexture) keyed out by a chroma-key shader. The video is not carried over — instead, gray person silhouettes drawn with our own shader stand on the same plane (9:16) and the same layout formulas (single row, ring, carousel). The original shader’s .05s jitter every 2s, left edge bleed and blur values are included in the same form, but blur is replaced by edge softening (SDF), and the grain (±.05) is a fixed pattern per person. The in-video motion (walking, turning) is absent — a still silhouette that shakes every frame or changes grain looks more agitated than the original, and the Hero length also came out longer.

The phone oval ring keeps rotating in the original and changes position, so it was set to turn once every 60s — the original rotation speed and curve (the segment curves ov/o_ of getCircleTransform) could not be measured
The cart in the corner cell opens only a single empty-cart line (the original’s e-commerce cart · no checkout). The list rows in the phone menu are just All · Stories · Size guide

In the product list, cutout products, lookbook photos and bar thumbnail videos are all gray placeholders (original images and videos are not carried over). The cross tick marks at product cell corners are drawn with our own lines instead of the original background image

Instead of the original paid typeface, the type is swapped for Saira wide width (wdth 125) — same angular feel, but slightly narrower letters, so the line breaks in the manifesto fall in different places
The value that pulls the first cell up by one screen is measured once on load, so resizing the window across desktop↔phone widths may misalign the first-cell margin of the list (a refresh fixes it)
