title: One-screen portfolio with rolling boxes holding work videos
good_for: Personal portfolios with a small number of works (around five to twelve), combining the first screen and an opened work detail panel on one page.

pages.use: A one-page portfolio — after the loader (number count·name blinking), four-sided video work boxes roll in, one work rolls per wheel notch, and the background changes to the work’s color. There is a left outlined name list and a top-right About panel, and clicking a box zooms in to a work detail panel with photo slots + a fixed text slot (back·next). On phones it rolls on scroll. For a personal portfolio that shows just a few works strongly

notes: The original is a single page (pages: [] in pages.json), so it has no sub-pages. Work detail is a panel overlaying the same page, as in the original.

The four work videos on the box face reuse a single gray screen-recording placeholder, media/work-reel-16x9.mp4, with the same ratio and length (848×480 · 9.33s). Opened over file://, the browser won’t let cross-origin video upload to WebGL, so the part draws a same-shaped scrolling screen placeholder itself, synced to that video’s playback time (play, pause and loop follow the video). Served over http, the video attaches to the face as is. The five photo works are stage-color placeholder faces + labels (hidden by wire annotation N).

The original paid Monument Extended was replaced with Archivo width 125. For Korean: Black Han Sans for bold lists (fake bold turned off — when on, outlines clump thick), Gothic A1 for buttons·labels, Nanum Gothic Coding for monospace. Slots where the original used Monument (work-name list · phone title · detail title and item labels · pill buttons · back/next · coming-soon cover · about labels and link buttons) hold English placeholder text, so this Korean pairing is only used when the skin is changed to put Korean in.

Font backfill — the loader text (loading, name blinking), cursor tag, detail body, phone [View work] and [Visit], and clock cities sit in the monospace (Roboto Mono) slot and are set in Korean rather than the title font even where the original is English. That is why the name the loader blinks is ”Your name here”, while the pill button says ”Your Name”.

Section images — library-shots has 0 for this one (the folder was empty before too). The whole page is one pinned screen, so the section clip goes outside the image to capture and fails with ”Clipped area is either empty or outside”. For the picker image, only thumb.jpg was newly shot.

The nine work colors are --site-c0~8, converted from the original values via the accent color in oklch (identical to the original values in the original skin). Yellow (--site-c7) has 2.7 times the chroma of the accent, so in high-chroma skins it goes out of gamut and gets clipped.
Carried over the original behavior where only on phone Safari the loader shows ”Tap anywhere” and wakes the video on tap — it does not appear in headless Chrome 390 (same as the original).
As in the original, scrolling the wheel past 25 steps ends the color band (50 sheets), leaving only the background color — the original structure is kept as is.

In the cursor backfill, the sixth placeholder text in the list was shortened from ”Client Name 6” to ”Client No. 6”. As in the original, the name button covers the canvas so that spot can’t be box-targeted, and the placeholder was wider (1120px) than the original ”Not in City” (right edge 949px), so on the y60 row the cursor never got over the box and the tag never turned on (reaction cell 0%). After the change it is 944px

title: Forest residential development with shape-shifting photo windows and a tilted 3D map
good_for: Apartment or office sales and real estate development sites with a long first page unfolding location, residences, retail and amenities in sections.

pages.use: Pre-sale first page — opening video and large name after the loader, two photo windows that change shape on a 900vh stage, photo-stage sections where the whole section opens (Location · Residence · Business · Amenities), a tilted 3D map with place pins, a picker list (housing type · building · amenities), a roots section where giant words fly in, a horizontal flight through clouds, installment payment guide, and a newsletter signup footer

Business space About — photo hero and promo video button, gray 900vh stage (two windows change shape and only cross halfway, position notes), gray panel list for choosing a building. For retail and office sales sub-pages.

Investment firm or company profile — photo hero, sand-colored mission section (two organic-mask photos), a 10-screen pinned business list (text and photo widths alternate per business · numbers), navy vision section. For developer or construction company intros

Contact — large title over a half-width photo on the left, a form with three tabs (request · phone · business) and a consent checkbox on the right, a one-screen page without footer. For housing sale consultation requests

notes: sites pull could not fully unpack the original HAR (the /en document collides with the /en/business folder name, EEXIST) — the archived zip was unpacked directly and read. Left as a tool-side fix.
Original sub-pages such as the 3D tour (/3d) and residence list (/residences) were not recorded, so they were not built, and their places in the menu link to the first page’s section anchors.

The hero opening video is a 2.73s gray-flow placeholder video — matched to the length measured on the original: after the loader (2.6s), a 2.7s still, then the name rises. The window videos are placeholder videos of the same lengths (12.46·9.17·7.89s).

3D map: instead of the original map image, the tilt-map-light part draws roads and blocks in skin colors. Board · camera · tilt · cursor light values are the original’s, and pin positions are the original coordinates. As in the original it turns on only at 1121px and above, below that it shows a still map placeholder + keen-slider cards.

The About section’s morph shapes were not ported from the original paths. Rounded polygons with about the same vertex count were redrawn (both start and end shapes). Window size, position and range follow the original values (Home 15×20rem·26.375rem / Business 22.5×30rem·33.188rem, based on 1440 and below).
On phone (below 600px) the About section runs the same stage at 600vh using tablet-style values, instead of the separate 5-screen mobile stage (600vh) the original provides.
The leaf-shadow layer (leafs.webp, multiply .4) is replaced with six blurred circular gradients — the 4s ±5° sway is the same.
The phone type (accordion) of the investor page business list is built simply with a details element (without the original’s .5s height transition and photo slide).

Used Cormorant Garamond in place of the paid PP Editorial Old, with Hahmlet backing it up for Korean. Since the original titles, lists and name lines are all English, every title-font slot (t-hero · t-h1 · t-h2 · t-h3 · t-huge · hero name · footer title and name) was switched to English placeholder text as a font backfill. Hahmlet is only used when a skin swaps in Korean text (earlier, headless capture rendered Korean titles in a gothic face).

Font backfill — there are no slots where the original used kana or kanji headings, so 0 places use Korean in the heading font slot. Slots in the body font (Work Sans) — menu, buttons, small labels, map pin names, body — are kept in Korean rather than the heading font, even where the original was English.

Font backfill — the hero name splitting was changed from chars to chars,words (index.js). Splitting by characters only breaks the English name mid-word at phone width (17vw), like ”PROJECT NA / ME” — the original also wraps words with word-wrap. The rising motion (.05 stagger per character) is unchanged.

Section shots — the investor page business list pin (projects-pin) and the home intro (intro-morph) were shot by library-shots with reduced motion, so three screens and six business names are overlapped in one spot. This is due to the pinned stage structure, and it was the same before the copy was changed.
The original cursor thread canvas blocks phone scrolling with preventDefault on mousemove and touchmove, but the part doesn’t block it and turns off entirely on touch devices.

The three-layer mouse parallax of the root section (quickTo .09 · .06 · .035) was left out at first build because the original did not move at the 1440 measure. But after handing the cursor to the section in the cursor backfill (2026-11-10), sweeping showed the original’s three layers do move (see the cursor reaction line below), so it was attached as the depth-follow part.

Cursor backfill — the three root-section mask photos never showed on 1440 Chrome. gsap.from read its end value from a computed value (”100% auto”) whose form differed from the start value ”0%”, so it stopped at 0% inside the page and at 88.9% on a blank page. Replaced with a fromTo that pins start and end to the same form (”0% auto” → computed value measured per layer) — length 1.5s·delay 2s·stagger .3·power2.inOut unchanged.

title: Scroll storybook moving from faded newspaper to space with swapping caption cards
good_for: One-page scroll stories for commemorations and history, family-friendly explainers and long-form campaigns that pin scenes and swap a caption card at the lower right.

pages.use: A one-page scroll story: newspaper page behind the 05 countdown curtain (words scramble and erase) → mosaic window and dog picker → 3D centrifuge inside the window → hero photo card → clouds and rocket launch → Earth orbit → television and numbers board → parachute landing → big headline newspaper → credits. A left table of contents and a bottom-right commentary card follow the scenes

notes: The original illustrations (four dogs, hand, mosaic window, rocket, earth, television, parachute, photographer, stamp) were redrawn as simple SVG shapes with the same position, size and color feel. The stained-glass mosaic texture and hand-drawn texture are left as slots for the next person to swap in artwork. News and portrait photos are placeholders describing subject, light and composition.

The 3D centrifuge is built from three.js basic shapes — tripod base, column, long arm, dog-carrying drum, weight — instead of the original GLB (kerusel · animated Empty). It spins 3 turns with the scroll, and the camera approaches as well. The original rest movement, where two dogs fall off the arm and come forward, was not carried over.

The play (/game) page opened by the top-left stamp was not recorded, so it was not built — the link is left as #. The top-right stamp button (sound on in the original) has only the shape and hover, no sound.

The numbers beside the television are three each for two animals (two names) like the original — the shake width and interval (±4, 1.2 seconds) and the red threshold are values we set because they were not found in the original bundle.
Phone (390): the index is hidden as in the original and cards fill the bottom. The original’s phone-only model (kerusel-m.glb) and vertical rocket scene are replaced by enlarging the same scene.

Typeface slot copy: the original uses one English-edition font (Praho Pro), so the big titles, chapter names (contents, card tags, card titles), protagonist name, stamp text, newspaper name, last chapter title and credits list were replaced with English placeholders. The first newspaper headline at the original character count (11·12 characters) would overflow the page because Libre Caslon is wider than Praho Pro, so it was cut to 10·10 characters (A headline / set in red). Dates, weekdays, number descriptions, body sentences and measure names (pulse, blood pressure, breathing) are sentences or descriptions, so they stay in Korean

title: Publisher site with a blue-band book carousel and vertical-text category rows
good_for: Company sites with large product catalogs such as publishers, bookstores and textbook companies, with category mega menus, new-release carousels, rankings, reading content and trade materials.

pages.use: Publisher home page — center-aligned book card carousel on a blue band, banner carousel, one-line notice, four reading cards, five genre rows with vertical-writing titles (three books each), eight rankings, and a notice list with category buttons. For a company with many products

Company intro: handwritten slogan, centered body text with eight hand drawings floating up separately and eight books, blue wavy-edged panel with four goal cards (rotating circular text), three yellow policy cards, ruled-notebook name origin, pill links. For company philosophy · greeting pages
Partner (bookstore) guide — a notice box (row list · see more) and two resource link cards. For partner-only guide pages
Reading list — seven category buttons, count and sort, four-column thumbnail card grid (NEW band), Load more. For blog, column and magazine lists
Book list by category — count, filter and sort rows, a four-column grid of cover cards (tags), load more. For product and publication lists
Archive of past issues — cream-colored line lists grouped by year (PDF·table icon·date·title), Load more. For newsletter, press release and download archives

notes: The logo, the header mascot and the twelve hand-drawn About illustrations were redrawn as simple SVGs with the same position, size and feel (ink line + yellow circle + blue beret) — the original is artist illustration with far more expressions and props. Drawing in more is left for the next person.
Search window, filtering and sorting have only shape and open/close (no results). Load more shows a 400ms loading state, then clones and appends the first batch, instead of the original POST ajax
slick 1.9.0 is not on npm, so the cdnjs build (upstream slick master build, MIT) was placed in _vendor/slick-carousel@1.9.0

The original subpage ”Back Issues” was dropped from the sites pull because the bookstore file and the bookstore/ folder share a name, so it was built by reading only the structure from the original URL
Book detail and founding-goal (about/founded) pages were not recorded, so they were not built. The About pill link is only a placeholder

SNS icons are placeholders: white glyphs on a dark ink plate of the skin instead of brand colors (brand colors are content, not skin, so whoever uses them swaps in logos). The gold, silver and bronze rank badges are also colors derived from the accent color

title: Solo studio portfolio with a 3D statue on a dark stage and chrome fist footer
good_for: Portfolios for solo creative directors and studios, with service descriptions and case detail pages for a personal brand.

pages.use: One-person studio home page — golden-ratio line loader · hero with a 3D statue on an unlit stage · AI chat pill · client logos · growing case video · work cards · award logos · contact form. For a creative director portfolio home

Work collection — eight works that change from sketch → wireframe → final inside a frame, an awards row, a draggable photo gallery, solution tabs. For a portfolio list that shows works one screen at a time
Services — three numbers, credentials, tool logos, service accordion and list, contact form, floating button. For introducing a single service such as automation or consulting
About me — portrait hero · childhood · interview video · career cards · number grid · turning point · philosophy · contact. For a story-style intro of a personal brand

Single case detail. A tilted-frame hero video, overview, process photos, problem words, solution, a structure diagram panel, horizontally sliding work details (full-width guide video → title → three steps where a photo window opens and the video plays) and a results list. For web and digital work case intros.

notes: The hero 3D does not use the original photoreal sculpture model files (R3F). Figures and pedestals are built from capsules, lathes and cylinders, with a lathe pawn·king, a knight made from an extruded horse head, and tetrahedron shards (same size·silhouette proportions). There are no faces, cloth folds or texture shaders — only the order and composition match: silhouette → lighting → camera approach → horse shatter. three is 0.185.0, same as the original.

Scene transitions are a virtual scroll ported directly from the original STICKY_CONFIG (step length 200 · phone 260, commit/snap segments · chess segment doors, 500ms pause on the white stage and before everything, wheel ±100×.4 · touch ×3.2, target .035 · progress .04 · max 12, release to default scroll at the end and re-capture at the end when coming back up from below, first segment auto 2s easeInOutQuad). Not ported: belowSceneHold (up to 8s), which blocks the wheel after release until the dark intro below finishes, and the keyboard, manual mode and phone cookie-consent gates — the copy’s dark intro is a scroll scrub like the original cards, so there is no moment when it is done. Next person: turn the intro rows into a timed timeline and preventDefault on wheel until its end

The original draws the menu drawer’s ink and the site-wide cursor with brs-webgpu-layers/layers.js (WebGPU, 98KB, sprite pointer-states.png). The headless browser on this machine has no WebGPU, so the original menu doesn’t open and the cursor isn’t drawn, and the look and values could not be measured (blocked). So the menu is built from the navigation-desktop.js timeline values (ink 0.7s, text x30·scale 1.2→1 back.inOut(3) stagger .02, item gap -0.32s, button x100 0.6s, on close 3x reverse playback), the ink is a clip-path circle spreading from the button position, and the cursor is a DOM dot and ring. The WebGL fluid vortex in the same folder (fluid-vortex-desktop.js) is in the original BRS_FLUID_VORTEX_ENABLED = Turned off with false, so not built. Next person: record the original menu in Chrome with a GPU and move the ink in layers.js to a WebGL version
The side drawers (Solutions · Services · Insights · About) also could not be seen open in the original under the same WebGPU layer condition, so they were built guessing a dark panel on the right

The Work detail ”Work details” was replaced this time with the original brs-hz-slider as it is (1000vh cell, from cell top +400px to the end scrub 1.5, items: ① full-width guide video ② half-width title ③~⑤ photo + 1:1 video/text, each box shifts by its own width, the next photo window opens from a 10%·64px rounded window in the latter half after the previous box, progress circle 283). The ”BRANDING · DEVELOPMENT · DIGITAL ECOSYSTEM” word board in the original second step is video content, so the copy also uses a placeholder video of the same ratio and length (media/detail-step-2.mp4). Item widths are measured once on mount (as in the original) — resizing the window requires a reload to fit
On phones, the original’s tiered mobile menu (submenus · < Back, navigation-mobile.js) was not built, and the desktop menu is stacked into one tier

The chrome fist is also an image (PNG) in the original, so the metallic-gradient four fingers·thumb·forearm and the tattoo lines were redrawn in SVG. Their material colors are marked ‹not skin› so they stay chrome when the skin is swapped (QR black-and-white too). Logos·awards·tool logos are text placeholders

The giant site name text uses the English placeholder ”STUDIO” (Pretendard 900 — the typeface is part of the creator’s chosen skin, so it stays) instead of the original wordmark. 3D material colors (bronze, gold, black horse) are scene materials, so they were not pulled out as skin variables

Typeface placeholders: the original is an English site, so the places that use Cal Sans (big menu text · contact button · drawer item names · contact section title · footer group headings, per-page big titles · section titles · name lines · logo · awards · tool names · tabs · result groups) and the header wordmark (Figtree) were swapped for English placeholders. Lists, descriptions and footer items drawn in the body typeface (Figtree) stay Korean as they are. Where text length caused a misfit: the service hero splits by character and broke as ‹Service Na/me› at phone width, so SplitText was bundled as words,chars (motion is still per character), and the detail hero and the first line of the home page’s fourth section were cut to the original character count (Company · A headline about our work,)

The 73 lines left in latin-slots (10 About career list items, 40 detail difficulty·step·result list items with bold leads, 23 service usage tags) are regex false positives — from other pages’ `.sv-logos li`·`.ix-awards b` The rule was applied to every li·b after looking only at the last chunk (li·b). Measuring the actual rendered typeface gives Figtree + Pretendard, so Korean is kept

title: Template curation site with lying rings and cards passing in waves
good_for: Curated directory sites that collect templates, products or works, and listing services with scores and comparisons.

pages.use: Curation first page — hero with 14 templates spinning in a lying 3D ring, a pinned intro sentence that cards sweep past in a wave, three elastic card rows pushed by the cursor, a giant marquee boundary, a judge stack that fans out following the cursor, a scoring method where words gather, a tool intro with rolling letters, a platform list with popping thumbnails, text lines, a giant question riding a line, FAQ

Tool page — rising header, question panel that slides in from the side with each answer, three-column side-by-side table with name rows attached, what-you-can-make cards, cost band, tool list, things to know · questions. For comparison calculators, quote helpers and price comparison
Post list — large title and category chips, post cards staggered in a three-column checkerboard. For blog, news and archive lists
A single article — breadcrumb, title, author line, hero image, narrow body column (images, lists, subheads), question, grid of more articles to read. For blog or guide article detail

About — a big-word marquee head and a photo strip pushed by the cursor, narrow text columns (who uses it · what it isn’t · how scoring works), and a two-column judges list. For service and editorial team About pages

Product (template) list — category heading, maker toggle, value-expanding filters, and a three-column grid of square cards that show a view button and score line on hover. Product and work category list.

notes: compare/platform-a-vs-platform-b (two-platform comparison detail) has the same type as compare.html (only two columns) so it was not built separately — just cut the table columns to two

Question header (MwgEffect104): the small logo graphic pieces on the original line are dropped and only one block of text flows. The overlap pulled up under the previous section’s “See All” (entry 50%, exit 70%) is replaced only by overlapping the FAQ section by −50vh.
Drifting card section (MwgEffect094): the original pulls up 25% under the previous section’s ‹See All› and pulls the next section 15% to overlap, but the part does not overlap

The template expansion skips the original’s search results and category pill panels and builds only a single pill row (All plus three platforms). The search field changes only its placeholder text and has no results panel

Dot menu: on the original wide screen it is a small list that appears instantly without bouncing (measured, no motion), on phone it is a full-screen panel — the copy does the same, but the social row in the phone panel uses circle placeholders
Platform icons and badges don’t use the original logos — redrawn as squares, circles, triangles and text-ring badges

‹Template› expand open and close curves have the same shape (.29s back.out(2) · close .15s cut off), but the first sample wobbles in each measuring frame, so depending on the page the curve gap can come out at .06~.1

Font backfill: the original is all Latin (Poppins), so the display font slot (--kf-font-display) and the intro sentence h2 were swapped for English placeholder text. Platform names appear only in the title slot as Platform A·B·C (one, two, three in order)

Font backfill decision: the body font (--kf-font-sans) slots keep Korean per the README. These are the header line, dot menu, buttons, card name line, article card title, grading criteria line, footer links and round badge ring text (the badge ring would overflow the circle in English).

Horizontal overflow (126px on phone · 112px on wide screens) comes from a single item, the footer language expansion panel .bw-island — the phone width was already 126px in the copy before the change. It is unrelated to text length, so it was left alone

Footer y90 is accept — the original stops the footer marquee (and the hero ring) when there is no press, wheel, key or scroll for 20 seconds (bundle module 84380), but the copy has no such pause. When measuring the second row, only the original marquee stopped, so the original reaction cell looked larger. This 20 second pause is not a cursor reaction, so it was not added — the hero ring side requires fixing _fx/tilt-wheel-ring, which is left to the next person.

Cursor sweep is measured per section on Home (index) only — About’s photo strip and judge stack and other pages’ footers use the same parts (pan-elastic-strip · cover-flow-follow · drop-badge-trail), so they are not measured separately. The original About page is not in the archive.

title: Forest hot spring inn with vertical serif text and scattering photo collage
good_for: Homepages for ryokan, hot spring lodgings and small hotels, including room guides, craft exhibitions and news lists with a quiet vertical-text feel on a washi texture.

pages.use: Lodging home: logo loader, pinned video Hero (sound button), vertical menu section, and under the pinned header twelve vertical-writing sections (two-column text · two photos · scattering collage · video · guest room photo strip · three photos · hot spring fade panel · three news · two links · scattered photos)

Stay story — hero is a scattering photo collage (each panel ripples and swaps via WebGL), centered vertical title and text, three photos + long text, full-bleed photo + text, room photo strip. For brand and philosophy About

Room list — fixed vertical title and room index on the left, a strip of ten thumbnails that becomes the screen background on hover, and for each room a swipe photo (Next·Prev circle cursor at the edges), a two-language description, collapsible details and a booking button. For room and product line introductions.
News list — sticky vertical title on the left, category filtering, three-column photo news with vertical date · category attached, View More appends more
Single news post — Index link line sticks to the left, date, category and title, body mixing photos and text, prev/next links. For exhibition and event posts

notes: Paper background: the original lays a bg.webp image across the screen. Since it is a photo it is not carried over, and the same texture is redrawn with two layers of SVG feTurbulence noise (fine grain + horizontal fibers) (shared.css --bk-paper)

Photo panel WebGL: the values of the original shader (rotation displacement blend) (−45°·135°·intensity 1·1.5s Power2.easeOut·3s interval·starts after 2s·one renderer per panel) were rewritten in our own shader. The original displacement image disp1.jpg is replaced by a sin-noise canvas, and photos by placeholder canvases painted in the clothing color — to add photos, use TextureLoader at the photo() slot of BK.collage

Video: the hero video and the ”And it spins” section video are placeholder videos made with ffmpeg (no sound). The sound button turns on only one and mutes the other, like the original. The loader waits for six events like the original (loadedmetadata, loadeddata and canplay on both videos) and clears after 6s

Of the sub-pages, dining · hot spring · access · FAQ were not recorded so they were not built — those menu items are #. Guest rooms keep all ten as in the original, but the slide photos are four per room (original seven)

Text: the original Japanese vertical-writing title slot uses Korean vertical writing (same Mincho + Noto Serif KR), and the English parallel paragraph is English placeholder text. Room numbers (Part One…) are rendered as ”Number One…”

Cursor: the original .pointer is normally transparent (0) so it is invisible, stays transparent at 40px over links and buttons (is-mouseon), and becomes an 80 or 60px dark circle only on room thumbnails (View 01…) and navigation spots (Next · Prev) (.6s) — the copy does the same. Like the original, the last position is kept in sessionStorage so the next page picks it up.

title: Coffee academy with yellow hand-drawn mascot and sticker page turns
good_for: Sites for schools, academies, workshops and certification courses, covering course lists, categories, detail pages with schedules and subsidy calculators, about, FAQ and inquiries.

pages.use: Academy home — over the video, a column-wide big heading rising letter by letter, three journey cards whose description panel rises on hover, a tilted number-chip strip, four yellow course cards, a half-and-half CTA, reason cards that tilt and bounce pinned over a photo background, a self-flowing review line, a footer of hills explored with the mouse

Experience and workshop list — dark photo hero with a featured card, one-line intro with a hand drawing, sort row and 4-column photo card grid, half-yellow half-latte impact panel, reviews row, FAQ. For product or class list pages
School about — photo plus large intro title, two yellow panels for mission and declaration, awards and certifications grid, black-and-white instructor photo slider, dark space photo slider, FAQ

Course list by category — sticky left filter (chips·collapsibles) + photo course cards in 2 columns, a yellow title panel and three dark accordion columns on a latte panel, number chip band, FAQ. For category and search result pages.

One course — yellow hero panel (title, period, price, photo), left sticky tabs and summary, overview, flowchart, schedule, subsidy table, target audience, subsidy calculator, FAQ, contact form. For course and product detail pages.

notes: The title typeface Jobclarendon (a paid narrow Clarendon slab) is approximated with the free Roboto Serif, which has a width axis, narrowed to wdth 56, opsz 144, weight 700 (font-variation-settings on .b-display in shared.css). Swap in a typeface without a width axis and it stands wide as is.

Of the 5 recorded subpages, the workshop detail (latte-art-competition) has the same type as the course detail (breadcrumbs · yellow hero panel · pinned tabs · body · contact form), so it was built as a single detail.html. The number chip band · review row found only in the workshop detail can be attached as is from index/list.
Fixed the types attached during recording: category list (course-category) recruit → product, course detail (course) service → detail, workshop list stays product.

The original hand-drawn characters (snail, two-headed person, earth and wolf, reading under an awning) were redrawn as our own SVGs (shared.js ART) in the same position, size and line weight — simpler than the original. The 9 transition stickers are placeholders for logo, text-ellipse, disc and character stickers.

The hero video slot is media/hero.mp4, a placeholder video matching the original background video: 16:9, 21.6s, 30fps loop (autoplay muted loop). It shows warm gray-brown waves, with scene changes at the same 4.9·8.7·12.6·14.6·18.6s as the original, and a median brightness change between frames of 0.0055 (original 0.0038, 75% 0.011). If swapped for a video of the same ratio, the parallax (0→20vh·1→1.05x) still applies as is. Other photo slots are wf-img placeholders.
The original’s scroll flip (tr-scrollflip: a snail badge flying to attach at the bottom right) has no target on the first page, so it does not run in the original either — not built.

The cookie consent window (flowappz) · search results list (finsweet) · Company form protection are operating devices of the original site, so they are not built. The search button only expands an input field, and the form does not submit.

Page transitions are built with barba 2.10.3, using the original code as is — wrapping barba.go, the yellow cover rises with .45s expo.out the instant you press (startCover), and leave and enter are fitted to the remaining slide time (.45 − elapsed). First page · workshop list = Stacking 9 stickers (first .55s, the rest .1 apart back.out, random tilt and size), About · Category · Detail = Page name wipe. If it takes over 0.9s, three-dot loading appears (excluded for the first-page branch). Opened via file://, barba is off and navigation is a normal page load.

The original journey card hover (image disappears, dark panel rises 366px) was measured and ported with a .6s custom curve. No element in the original page uses data-reveal bounce-in, so it was not built.

The phone (390) menu is built as a dark drawer dropping below the header row plus details accordions, instead of the original Webflow collapsible menu — the original phone menu expansion could not be measured.

(To do next) The three motion parts (sticky-tilt-bounce · cursor-pan-scene · hover-slow-marquee) were extracted and passed inspection, but inside the site shared.js runs the same values directly (the parts are not attached) — use the motion parts when mixing and building.

Single product detail — photo gallery (auto-advance, progress bar), retailer card slider, feature tabs, DETAILS list, recommendation slider, a WebGL menu that opens with spreading ripples, and a forest-photo footer. The full version that the special page’s ”See details” leads to

Lottie: 8 nature icons, 9 bath card illustrations and 3 sets of ”Back to top” were redrawn with our own shapes in art.js (same canvas size, 60fps, length and repeat) — the baby and bathtub prop illustrations are simpler than the original. For ”Back to top” the original was measured and the movement (−12,+62), wobble (11°↔−11° .48s) and exit (−15,+61, 11°→−5°) were matched.
Concept video: the original YouTube embed spot is replaced with a same-size 16:9 placeholder box (does not play on click)
OverlayScrollbars: the original bundle shows no version, so the existing 2.16.0 was used (body · inner scroll panel autoHide scroll are the same)

Detail (detail.html): this is the parent site’s layout, but since it is one set it also wears the single theme.css (special mint tone) — white background is matched to --kf-surface, and ink black (#222) to --bd-deep, which is --kf-ink darkened by .74

Detail: the original site’s barba transition has only one original page in this set, so only ”white cover .3s, covers then navigates” was built. The global WebGL background (first-page ingredient droplet refraction shader) does not appear on the product detail, so it was not built

Detail menu WebGL: the original lifts the vertices of a 200-cell plane with three waves and adds sparkle with noise and mask textures — rebuilt with the same formulas (ring height sin(d·33·(1−p))·.01, windows −.5~−.2 and 0~−.1, noise boundary) refracted by gradient in the fragment shader, with the sparkle approximated by angular noise. The background photo is a placeholder drawn on a canvas
Below the detail menu’s recommended slider, the ripple graphic effect and the FAQ accordion (not in this product) were not built

Motion part incident: while making a new part, the existing _fx/char-hop-hover (stop-motion-tilted-cards-community) fx.js·fx.css·demo.html were overwritten — the default type was rebuilt from the fx.json original left in the catalog and the usage on the source site (letters·each·dur·hop), and the botanist style was added as look: smooth. There is no guarantee it matches the original files line by line, so the lead is asked to compare it against the original version in git
The three back-to-top Lottie files don’t use the original JSON — measured time series (idle wobble · exit fall) were converted into keys per frame and redrawn — the mountain shape is our own shape

title: Public volunteer guide with a moving hand-drawn town
good_for: Government or municipal information sites, family and child campaigns, and volunteer or community portals that communicate through friendly illustration.

pages.use: First page — hand-drawn village Lottie Hero with three map shortcuts, an About that flips through like a card stack, topics, a video slider, stair-step map cards, activity and help info strung on a ring binder, notifications, and a banner folding at the bottom right. For a public information or campaign portal home.
Topic list — category and tag chips with free search filter, count and sort, rows of News cards with photos, page numbers. For event and News list pages
Copyright and link notice — white card on a gray panel with subheadings, paragraphs and a numbered list. For long-text pages like terms of use, privacy and site policy

Business intro — two-line title and intro, event card on a yellow wavy board, ‹What is a business?› card and PDF resource row, partner company logo cells, pill-shaped survey card. For introducing one public project, campaign or project

notes: The original 13 Lottie files (town first screen 1700×804 · bench couple · paper plane · cloud · puppy · person picking up trash · parent and child · footer kids) are kept at the same canvas size, 60fps, length (1~6s) and playback style (loops start right away, home_inu_pop plays once at 90% of the screen). The art is replaced with animationData that art.js built from our own shapes (people, mascots, trees, buildings, towers, cars). The hand-drawn line texture and joint-motion precision of the original are lower. Fills are applied by class (f-*), so swapping the skin changes them together

The original still graphics (svg · webp: menu icon · map card figures · activity art · public-materials icon · subpage header art · footer village) were also redrawn with the same art language (art.js one-scene Lottie) and small svgs
The Hero title was a handwriting-style SVG lettering image in the original — swapped for text in the skin’s title fonts (Zen Maru Gothic, Jua)

The sub-page recordings (archived pages/1~3.jpg) were empty because the original redirected to port :10443 and the connection dropped — addresses with a trailing / (/topics/·/copyright/·/child-safety/mimamori-project/) open, so I built from those screens
The long explanation inside the ”What is a map?” dialog (the original introduces three maps at length with photos and text, scrolling via table-of-contents links) was cut down to a three-line list
The Language dropdown shows five lines in .4s on hover like the original, but has no translation behavior. The topic filter also only marks chip selection and does not actually filter
Real original card counts (72 items, multiple events) for the topic list and business pages are cut to 6 and 3, and partner cells to 10
Links to places the original was not recorded — the ”Notices” menu, video card, map card — are left as # — there is no page to compare the transition against the original first link (News)

title: Ad agency site descending into a billboard-box building, with horizontal chrome type and case cubes that tip into a TV
good_for: Outdoor advertising, event and brand campaign company intros with a 3D hero, a horizontal principles section, case cubes, field cylinders and a contact form.

pages.use: Company home — after the loading curtain, descending through a billboard-box 3D and a text wall, a three-principle horizontal pinned section where chrome 3D letters land, full-screen photo, four case cubes (typed descriptions), field cylinder over TV noise, stippled greeting footer. For agency and studio homes.
Contact — two-line greeting that shuffles then settles, field tags, email, two-column input form and red send button (ring on press), same stippled Footer. For quote and project inquiry pages
Page not found — only a one-line notice under the same header row. The original /project was a 404 at recording time and still is, so this screen was built as it is.

notes: The original 3 GLBs (billboard building, five chrome letters) were replaced with our shapes — the building is an upper box of the same proportions (13.6×9.67, dark roof plate) plus a lower letter-wall box with a canvas-drawn poster and letter lines attached, and the chrome letters are swollen tubes shaped as zigzag, ring, arc, mountain and wave (TubeGeometry, physical material clearcoat). The original coordinates, scale (23) and camera path (26→19→3, y -1→-5.5→-370) were kept, but since the inner shape of the original model is unknown, the angle and size at which the letter wall shows were tuned by eye.

The original HDR environment (envmap_3.hdr) is replaced by reflections baked from three bright panels with PMREM, and the original TV noise canvas (three r158) is rewritten as a raw WebGL shader (dark face smear + noise + scanlines + color shift).

The original’s placement of 3D letters between lines (corrections such as 2.1×scale for the model origin) is not used, and letters sit centered in the cell. The large titles are English placeholders (Words·Process·Method, where symbols stand in for W·P·c·M·t), so the blanks (19vw·9.6vw·24vw·8.1vw) keep the original widths.
The menu highlight is fixed to the original cell values (7/63·65/96·155/88px, phone 4/57·55/87·136/79) — it slides to the same spots regardless of the width of the placeholder text ”Menu 1·2·3”.

The 8 loading steps match the asset count like the original, but our scene has no files to download, so each step is set to 48ms (the original is network time for fetching GLB and HDR files). As a result the contact → first page transition length wobbles between 2.9 and 3.8s per run (original 3.25s).
The description typing (TextPlugin) and case names on the case cube are placeholders. The original takes the first 200 characters from case data (prismic).

Phone (below 900px) follows the original branch: stacked vertically without 3D, cube or cylinder, and cases become a four-card list (where the original phone list sits). The building slot is a photo slot growing to 1.13× the width.

The original /project (list) was a 404 both when recorded and now, so there is no list page — that 404 screen was built as notfound.html. Case detail (/projects/<id>, pageMove) are not recorded, so they were not built.
Footer logo: the original is a Korean wordmark (logo.svg, a stroke drawing of the Brand name), Korean kept. It is drawn in Pretendard (same sans-serif, 500), the pair of the title font Inter.

title: Branding agency set with a glass pill menu and a physics ball pile
good_for: Branding and web design studios, and agency portfolios that show work in large paired photos with a hero, work list and services.

pages.use: Agency home page: large indented intro sentence, selected works in pairs (one tile is a physics ball pile), two columns of thinking, four columns of services (drag on phones), results glass band (WebGL), team · client logos · news cards, and a big wordmark in a dark footer
Work list — dark stage with a centered two-line title, work photo cards two per row (tag pills), and a drag-to-swipe testimonial panel. For case lists and portfolio lists.

Service About — large centered intro sentence, two photos plus text, lime panel, four services that change row by row with a sticky photo, reviews panel, two selected works, FAQ accordion. For business and service About sections

notes: At recording time all three pages were set to about, so they were fixed to home, works and service.
Font: instead of the original TWK Lausanne (paid), Inter 300 · 400 — letters are wider than the original, so the footer wordmark is set at 12.6vw rather than 15.2vw.

The work card photo ripple is a rebuild of the original’s projectgl fluid drawing (dispers reveal) with our own shader (ripples around the cursor + color split by scroll speed + uncovering from the bottom) — the original fluid simulation’s sticky tail is missing. One screen-fixed WebGL canvas draws in every [data-fluid] slot.

The result glass strip was built from the original glass-carousel (a strip of photo cards plus glass refraction) as cards on a curved strip plus a refraction and color-split shader at the screen center. The original’s thick glass-body reflections and highlights are missing. The big number over each photo is a +00% placeholder.
The physics ball pile (matter.js 0.20.0) uses the same library as the original and draws 64 smiley balls in our own art. Ball count and radius (5.2% of card width) are values guessed from the screen.

The news card pixel photos are pixel-art files in the original, so a canvas placeholder that resolves from coarse pixels is used (1.2s when visible · again on hover) — add a photo and it resolves the same way.
The original’s About·Approach·Insights subpages and Cal.com booking window were not recorded, so they were not built (the menu links to our own pages).

The menu cell stands only on the current page as in the original (does not follow on hover). The original has no page transition block and the intro exists only on the first page — values match the original intro-data (bar 2.64s → panel 2s power4.inOut → first two cards 2.3s cubix).

The review panel follows its target every frame like the original ReviewsSlider (.1 after release, .28 while dragging, 1.2x the dragged distance), and one panel cell is the original width (772.8 at 1440 plus gap 1.22vw − .758px). The throw inertia prediction is a hand-built approximation, and the number roll uses the original values (out 300ms with 30ms stagger / in 600ms with 130+100ms stagger).

Font backfill: since the original text is entirely Latin letters, English placeholders were swapped in for titles (b-xl, b-lg, b-md), section tags ( … ), menu, buttons, cursor labels, name lines (work name, tag, service name, list items, review name, job title), review quotes, footer title, tags and address. Body and description sentences (b-xs intro, thoughts, descriptions, result descriptions, answers), one-line work intros, FAQ questions and the one-line team label stay in Korean. latin-slots remaining slots 0.

The review quote (b-review__quote) is a pulled quote in the heading font, so it stays in English, written at about 240 characters to match the original quote length (220~300). News post titles are about 50 characters so they fold into two lines like the original.

This site also reads data-label as canvas text in photo slots (the [data-label] of the result glass band in index.js, the [data-fluid] of the fluid panel in shared.js) — slot-description data-label was put only on other titles and tags.

title: Designer portfolio where turning a clock changes the sky behind a case strip
good_for: Art director, designer or photographer portfolios that present a few cases as a single-screen horizontal strip, each linking to a detail page.

pages.use: Home and case list — first appearance where four stacked photos in the center spread into a horizontal band, a case band that loops endlessly by wheel·drag while shrinking, and pressing flies the photo to the detail hero spot. A header clock dial switches the sky (day·dusk·night)

One case — large lowercase title, client and field attached at bottom left with a vertical photo on the right, large intro text, two rows of photo strips stuck to the screen flowing in opposite directions, large-screen photos with numbered name tags, an end cell leading to the next case

notes: The original sets the sky by the current time (9 to 16h daytime off-white #f8f6f2, 21 to 4h night #2c2922·text #c3beb1, 5 and 19h yellow text). The copy blends --fx-night by the same time steps and paints between the skin’s --kf-bg ↔ --kf-contrast-bg, so measure the original and the copy at the same time of day for the colors to match. The in-between step colors (#cec9bb·#a59d8a·#857c6a·#60594c) are approximations mixing the two end colors at .2·.4·.6·.8 (component difference within 10).
The original paper texture (paper_bg_2.jpg repeated at 286px, brightness at night) is redrawn with an SVG noise filter with --fx-bright applied — it has less fibre grain than the original.

The archive and about pages were not recorded in the archived copy (pages.json has only one case detail), so they were not built. Those two slots in the menu panel are left without links (#) — a to-do for the next person.
Video cells (cases four and six) play a 6s looping placeholder video (placeholder-loop.mp4, a gradient we made) at the same ratio, muted.

As in the original, hovering the clock dial enlarges only the matching spot to 6.3rem (plate and hands 5.2rem), and pressing a hand tip turns it toward that time within the same AM/PM, in the direction it flows (.55s after a .15s delay). The sky switches to the new time at .2s, with the background taking .65s ease-out and the text .6s ease-in-out (.2s late) — values matched by measuring the frame curves.

Typeface placeholder note: places where the original title typeface (Neue Haas Unica → Inter Tight) is used — detail large title, large intro text, the Next Work line and next work name, menu panel section names (Works · Archive · About), contact panel greeting, hidden h1 on the first page — were replaced with English placeholders, and data-label notes what to put there.

The two-line name in the header, Menu/Contact, local time, case-name strip, client, field and photo-number labels — 12px uppercase lines like these use the body font in the original too (Helvetica Now → Inter), so they stay as Korean placeholders — not a title font slot, so untouched in this backfill.

title: Renovation company site with a full photo hero and layered rising panels
good_for: Real estate, renovation and architecture company sites covering about, services, project list and detail, news and recruiting in one set.

pages.use: Renovation company Hero — Hero where photos shrink into a card collage, filling copy, business list, sticky strengths panel, big numbers, client logo band, results, News, recruiting band. For a real estate or architecture company home.

Company info — vertical photo header, brand message, CEO greeting, future and vision, company overview table, endlessly flowing photo strip (drag to push), history, related links. For a single company About page
Work list — a row of featured works paged one at a time with arrows (PREV and NEXT pills follow the cursor) and a grid of work cards. For construction and sales case lists.
Business — anchor intro, two business details, big numbers, consultation info, photo pair, recent results, related links. For business area About pages
News list — news rows with photo thumbnails. For a company announcement list
Careers info — hero with three photos rising and curving like paper, message, who we look for, numbers, strengths, benefits, flowing photo band, job accordion. For a company careers page

One project detail — hero photo header, scope of work, photo gallery that swaps in overlay by dragging or tapping small photos, keywords, consultation, other projects. For a construction or interior case detail.

notes: The Hero front wordmark on wide screens (1024 and up) is our shader glass lettering (index.js heroGlass) — a flowing text strip drawn on a canvas is used as an overlay texture, each letter passes its box center and radius as uniforms, and a convex lens (elliptic paraboloid · refractive index 1.5187 · min radius 28 · slope .9 · path min(64, radius×1.15) · gain 2 · show-through .82 · bend fades out 160px from the screen edge) refracts the photo placeholder behind it (background color · diagonal · bottom shade). Approximation: the show-through of the original’s one lighting set (three RectAreaLights) is replaced by one white window fitted to a strip of the original captured while paused (430px right of the light spot · white width ~440px · 40px lower), a faint warm light and a thin rim, and the label text of the photo placeholder behind is not put into the refracted image. Phone (1023 and below) is still a white text strip — the original is glass on phone too, but there is no cursor there, so it is outside this cursor backfill

The insulation structure CG builds our own box-shape room using the original values (camera 33° · (0,.36,14.2)→(0,-.05,0) · fog 13~23 · auto .65rad/s + scroll speed ×.0012 · mouse orbit 12°/7° · model tilt 15°/12° · drag .008 · camera-side wall .1→.025 · white panel canvas .5). The AUTO · INSULATION · RESET buttons of the original standalone iframe version and the insulation highlight (emission .14) aren’t visible in the version embedded in the site, so they were not added

Result tabs, filters and pagination only show a selected state and cards floating up again on press — the cards are placeholders so there is nothing to filter. The original’s lower filter list changing per tab is also reduced to one

The centered photo strip on the business page (original ServiceCarousel — LoopGallery, centered in 62rem slots with 5rem gaps) and the phone-header photo carousel on the careers page (original RecruitKV, splide on phones only) have not been switched to splide yet — 150-minute cap. The company and careers photo strips, the featured results row and the detail photos use splide 4.1.4 like the original.
Fonts: Albert Sans instead of Aeonik (paid), Noto Sans KR instead of the paid gothic and YakuHanJP. Logo is a ”wordmark” text placeholder
The collaboration inquiry page was not recorded so it was not built, and its link is #

title: Branding company with an empty hero, a running logo and a four-column feed
good_for: Design and branding company sites that blend work and news into one feed, especially for firms with several offices.

pages.use: Company home — a blank screen with a small logo in the center that runs when pressed, Feed · Work · News pills below, and + City (pressing it turns the hero into an office drawer: text, photo collage, letter-hand clock, map), a 4-column feed mixing case, article and slide cards, and a 16:9 video strip. For a company home that flows work and news as one stream.

Service list — centered two-line heading, 3-column service cards (photo · name · what it does), eight service rows (name | what it does · small photo | one sentence and a paragraph). For laying out all of a company’s services on one page

A single service — two photos stuck to the left and stacking over each other, four groups of sub-work text on the right, that service’s work row (name + twelve same-height photos) and a show-all pill. For a single service · business detail (the original identité visuelle · production share the same shape)
Single work — left fixed info column (info, credits, category collapses and site pill) and right photo stack (one full photo, two half photos, sound button on video). For case and portfolio detail

notes: Motion engine: the original is Framer (React + Framer Motion runtime, site bundle), so it can’t be pulled out as a library — we moved the same numbers into CSS and our own parts. Header hide .2s cubic-bezier(.44,0,.56,1) and sentence↔logo .6s cubic-bezier(.12,.78,.32,.98) are the bundle values as is, while the Read arrow spring (bounce .1·.55s) and the header sentence’s return when leaving (measured as 1−e^(−t/110ms)) are curves expanded with CSS linear()

The lenis in the card tech field was a string that existed only in the Framer edit bar — the site uses the window default scroll, so the copy also leaves out Lenis and the card was corrected too (framer-motion)

The hero horse logo: the original is an Image Sequence Player cycling picture cuts from a zip — no image files are used, we newly drew 8 SVG animal frames (a run with turning legs and tail) and hung the same behavior (one frame per press, rapid presses advance by the number of presses, the end loops back to the start) with the tap-frame-step part. The original frame count is unknown because the zip is not in the archived text (8 frames is a judgment call)

The office drawer map is an external map widget in the original (zoom in/out, my-location button, orange dot). Only a gray road-pattern placeholder and button shapes are placed at the same position and size (3 columns × 247px), with no drag or zoom. The clock (text-hand-clock) runs on the original code part’s values.

The feed is cut from the original 90-odd cards to 32 representative ones (case, article, coming soon, pin, two social slides, two 16:9 video strips), and the Work and News views to 12 and 8. It flows with grid dense like the original, and the large strip text uses mix-blend-mode: difference.

Card videos use the same playback behavior (load 1200px ahead, loop silently within 200px, pause when out of range), and the content is a gray placeholder video in media/ (16:9 and 1:1, 6 seconds, baked with ffmpeg). The original uses a worker and HLS player, so only the poster stands during measurement, and the loader length difference was recorded under accepted differences.

Among the original subpages, production has the same form as branding, so it was built as a single service-detail.html. À propos · Carrières · Contact · the project list section weren’t recorded so they weren’t built, and the header menu items About · Careers · Contact link to existing sections (service-detail · detail)

Phone city drawer: the original was measured only up to the globe button opening the city list, and with no recording of the phone drawer after tapping a city, we decided to stack text, collage, clock and map vertically and scroll within the first screen

title: Short film site with black-and-white dance footage rising from darkness
good_for: Single-work microsites for short films, performances or exhibitions, video-led one-screen paging intros and video portfolios.

pages.use: Work first page — four sections (intro · backstage · credits · video) on one screen switched by wheel · drag, with a black-and-white background video rising from darkness by brightness threshold. The last section is the main video window. For a special first screen that opens one work in four sections

Work intro. A big title in the center and a 270px scrolling text box, with the background rendering the same video as pixel dots (the cursor makes them bulge). For one long text such as planning intent or a director’s statement

Making-of — four full-bleed photos switched with displacement and noise, a title and text per scene, a making-of film playback panel (seek bar, time, close). For production notes and behind-the-scenes photo slides
Credits — two cast video cards and thirty-one role and name rows lined up in one horizontal strip, each piece following with different inertia. For end credits, participant lists and supporter lists

notes: The video length page (/movies/) exists only in the menu and was not captured in the archive, so it was not built. The Movies menu item opens the fourth section of the home page (index.html#movies, the main video window). The original’s section list, navigation line and rewind panel are left for the next person to pick up

Pixel dot cloud shimmer: the original uses Name simplex noise, but to avoid porting the original shader, a formula with the same frequency and strength was newly written with our own value noise (hash interpolation) — the dot-popping grain is slightly rougher

The brush mask sprite (title painting) is our own 56 frames of brush strokes drawn on canvas instead of the original PNG (56 frames). steps(55) and 1.3s are the same, and the original mask size 5700% is set to 5600% so the frames don’t misalign.
Fonts: harfang-pro·proxima-nova·din-condensed are all paid (Typekit), so replaced with Crimson Pro 300·Figtree·Barlow Condensed. Korean slots use Noto Serif KR·Pretendard
Sound: in place of the original background music we use our own two-note drone (media/ambient.mp3, 20s loop). The sound button pulse (.8s · delays .6/.3/0/.3/.6) is the same
Language buttons (en/ja) have no other language version, so only the look and hover exist

Backstage: the four photos are canvas placeholders drawn with skin variables (still-life ellipse + label), and the displacement pattern is 512px value noise — transition 1.6s quint.inOut · vertical displacement 60 · noise .34 steps(12) · the polygon mask that unfolds from the center point on entry (.1/.2/.3/.3s) are original values. The photos shifting sideways with phone tilt (devicemotion) were not built. The making film shares the first page’s feature placeholder video
Credits: two cast cards use the same placeholder video (media/cast.mp4, 4s). The company logo SVGs (Brand A·Brand B) in the original credits were replaced with the text Company Name

Transition: the original uses Barba 1.0.0 to keep the header·menu·background canvas and swap only the body — the copy uses the same Barba with the same order (old section exits → new section revealed .5s after 1s · center line 1.5s). Opened via file://, Barba·PreloadJS·WebGL video are blocked and it falls back to black and white <video> It stands as a fallback type that applies it directly (open it over http to match the original)

Fixed (found by measuring): batching cursor events into the next frame, the original onArrowEnter where the cursor snaps to the center ring of the arrow over an arrow button, drag move curve (power1.out default), arrow face 25%→100% · text color 50%→100% (.25s · delayed .1s), cursor face color as an fill with alpha, menu stroke count (three per letter) · first delay, text block centered in the lower half, wordmark drag blocked (js-no-drag), widths · heights of hidden sections · text panels · covers as % like the original (display swap), backstage text panel 1.8s blur exit · new panel after 1.2s, transition delay (a zero-length fromTo was calling the end immediately), the page number line disappearing on every transition (GSAP 3 clearProps transformOrigin wipes the whole transform), subtitle letters also entering from 50px to the side along with the title, making-of film start · close (nine UI branches display none after .5s · noise · displacement · cursor restore), GSAP 3 set not killing running tweens (overwrite)

title: University shared space and web magazine with hand-drawn characters perched on lines
good_for: University or department news sites, shared-space guides, and institutional home pages that combine a web magazine with event information.

pages.use: Home — a flowing notice strip and date header, about on the left + a pickup slider inside a half-circle panel on the right (a ring around each dot), two big event cells + four rows, three article cells with vertical section names stuck on and following, faculty activity rows, an arch-window photo strip + online/offline two cells. For a department or space intro home

Web magazine list — big English section name header + left category panel + hashtag strip + two-column article cards + pagination. For blogs, magazines and category lists (a list changed only by category is the same Type)
Event info list — hand-drawn header + left category panel + two-column event cells (flyer, category, ended label, date, time, title, intro) + pagination. For event and seminar schedule lists

One event — category, title, large flyer, date·place·share·apply buttons with two summary cells, two people above a line, body, three presenters (characters holding laptops), info table. For event and seminar detail pages

notes: Gradient blob: the original is a blurred video (mp4, loops 5.3~8.3 seconds) in the same spot — rebuilt with two CSS radial gradients so the colors follow when the skin changes (motion part grad-blob-breathe). It rises 15px and appears in 1.19s when visible and hides when out of view, with play/pause at the original values, but without the video’s fine texture

Hand-drawn characters: the original is 10 transparent GIFs (40ms frames, looping every 3.8~6.6s). We redrew 11 SVGs in the same spot, size and look (black silhouette + white face) and ran eye rolls, blinks, alternating legs and tail with steps (part doodle-idle-loop). Per-GIF details (chin-resting hand movement, newspaper turning, etc.) are reduced to eye and leg motion at the same tempo — to do next: someone draws more and continues.

The original emoji table (flags, book stack, house, etc.) was replaced with same-size monochrome SVG symbols (rule: no emoji). Latin picture-text (ONLINE × OFFLINE · WEB MAGAZINE · EVENT, etc.) uses Be Vietnam Pro bold uppercase placeholder text.
The brand mark (circle, bar and square cluster) and the large footer mark are newly drawn geometric placeholders of the same width and height, not copies of the original logo

Splide: the original options (loop, speed 790, interval 5150, gap 60px, easing cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1), autoplay only while visible, pause on hover or focus) and the dot ring border keyframes are kept as they are. Instead of the original default autoWidth, perPage 1 is used — the slide width equals the slider width, so it looks the same.
The search field only has the open/close look and motion, no real search. instant.page·role=Link prefetching isn’t a motion, so it wasn’t built

Subpages: of the four recorded, the article category list (magazine/category/event-report) has the same type as the web magazine list, so it is kept as a single news.html (only the current item in the category view differs). Single article, faculty activity and facility guide pages were not recorded, so they were not built
The notice bar exists only on the first page (the original has none on subpages either). The date in the header is stamped with today’s date by JS, like the original

title: One-page portfolio with ink-bleed intro text and draggable work windows
good_for: Designer or writer one-page portfolios, personal sites that unfold work lists as windows, and minimal lists with a light or dark theme toggle.

pages.use: Single-page portfolio — an intro paragraph and links (mail copy note) whose text near the cursor smears bold in five layers, a difference-blend crosshair cursor spanning the screen, work cards with three corner tick marks (on hover they invert to ink black with a cursor-side marker) ↔ a one-line list, work windows you drag and resize on click that stack out of each other’s way (fill screen, Esc), and a light and dark skin button. On a personal portfolio’s hero

notes: The original is hand-written code with no library. The ink bleed was newly written in the same way (five text copies + SVG dilate filter + stamp mask) as the part ink-bleed-text. The crosshair and work window use existing parts (look: plain of crosshair-coord-cursor, the ox·oy·fade·bound options of desk-window) with the original values plugged in.
The original body font Name is not a distributed font, so Libre Caslon Text is used instead. Tags use DM Mono like the original
The animated images (gif · mp4) in the work window gallery are all one shared 8:5 placeholder video (media/clip.mp4, 6s loop, baked with ffmpeg)
crosshair-coord-cursor: when line: 0 · dot: 0, gsap.quickTo does not redraw a length-0 tween so the line stayed still — the part was fixed to set it immediately when the length is 0

title: Studio site with pinned sections that close a gap and a halftone footer
good_for: Design studio or agency home pages and B2B service landings that persuade through case studies with result numbers.

pages.use: Studio first page — giant title, a results popup card over a case-photo board alternating every 8 seconds, client logos, a big paragraph on a dark board (text darkens), a pinned Close the Gap section, case rows (hover video board), service hover list, 3-step process videos, FAQ, narrow uppercase CTA, halftone footer. For a results-driven B2B agency landing page.

Studio About — an About drawer slides in from the right over the first page, pushing the page behind back 5% (CEO greeting, vertical video with four floating words, clients, awards, principles). For when an About drawer is needed without changing pages
Work list — giant title and (count), left sticky service filter buttons, three-column vertical cards (tag chips). For a work list filtered by service
Contact — big centered title, booking calendar panel (month view, time picker slot), email copy row, dark FAQ. For contact pages that take call bookings

notes: Sound: the original uses Howler for button press·hover sounds (tap_01~05·select mp3) — the sound files are original assets, so they are not included. The sound button’s icon stroke drawing (.2s/.3s ease-secondary, .05 stagger) and the state change ”sound turns on the first time any button is pressed” were built the same

Booking calendar: the original Contact calendar is an external service (Cal.com) widget — kept as a static placeholder of the same size and shape (month view·time slots), and the date-picking behavior is not built.

Video: the case-row hover video, process-step video and about-drawer portrait video are placeholders with the same position, ratio and play condition (play only while visible), while playing they show only as a background with a flowing light band
Work list cards were cut from the original eight to six (repeated shapes) — the first-page work rows are six like the original (01/06~06/06)
Logo: the original wordmark (with a handwritten O) is not used, the text LOGO is a placeholder — the original logo hover letter change is absent

The WebGL halftone footer is a freshly written shader using the original values (amplitude·flow·press multiplier·4px dots·stickiness·2s reveal), so the pattern shape itself differs from the original (same kind of flowing blobs)
three r160 is the same build as the original (UMD build/three.min.js), so the console shows one warning that build/three.min.js will be removed in r150+ — errors: 0

Font placeholder text: places that used the original heading fonts (Khteka → Inter Tight 700·Animo → Anton) — Hero four-line heading·dark panel large paragraph·GAP·process·closing section giant caps·names of cases/clients/services/steps/awards·FAQ headings·case list·contact big heading·menu (header·footer·phone)·buttons·words in the About drawer·name list·principle names·booking calendar header — were replaced with English placeholders, and data-label notes what to put in each.

Spots kept in Korean: the hero left paragraph, the eight FAQ lines, ”Wondering if we’d be a good fit?”, the case summary, the one-line quote in the last section, and the About drawer greeting paragraph are body and explanatory sentences, so they stay Korean (latin-slots is hooked on because it is a t-h5 class, but the original is also a body-size sentence). The Korean pairing is Pretendard in theme.css (same gothic feel as Inter Tight), which is already loaded. The remaining wf-note (annotations) and sr-only (name of the show-results button) are not content text.

Add lang to the hero, work list, and contact title switched to English="en" Added a fix — the Korean :lang(ko) override (line spacing, width) was applied to English text and made it look looser than the original, so it was reverted to the original English values (line heights .78, .85, .9, widths 12ch, 8ch). For the work list title, ‹Selected Work› pushed (06) out by 81px at 390, so it was matched to the original with long words of 7 letters or fewer (All client work).

title: Neighborhood clinic in a forest village with a cloudy sky and a kingfisher flying in
good_for: Local clinic, internal medicine, pediatric and general practice sites with a beige base, green headings, orange English labels, a sky-gradient section with drifting clouds and a flying bird, an icon menu header, and doctor, service, fee and notice pages.

pages.use: Clinic home page — left column (tree logo, subject line, six icon menu items, booking/phone, opening hours table) and a photo panel with a diagonally cut top edge (slick fade + 10s zoom-in), three notices, an intro text on a cloudy sky with a kingfisher flying in, three features on a thick-bordered panel with swaying leaf branches, a white-panel treatment grid, a directions box, a staggered photo strip (90s), partner hospitals, a footer with hours and map

About the clinic — slanted photo header with tab buttons, three numbered philosophy boxes on a sky-blue section, a numbered-circle feature list, doctor profiles (photo, greeting, credentials, two-column history), payment box, history text and photo. For clinic and hospital About and doctor profile pages

Treatment guide: tab buttons, symptom tag box, and for each department an icon circle, tag, description and list of common conditions, plus a vaccination price table, caption lines beside the photo and an app download button. For clinic department and service pages.
Notice list — cloudy sky header, category and month pickers, dotted-line list of date, category tag and title, round page numbers. For notice lists
News post — green title, date, category, a few paragraphs, previous-post link and list button. For notice and news detail pages

notes: The original uses slick 1.9.0 (a master-branch version number that was never officially released and is not on npm or jsdelivr). The closest official release with the same fade and autoplay behavior, slick-carousel@1.8.1 (already in _vendor), is wired up with the same settings (autoplaySpeed 5000 · speed 700 · cssEase linear · fade · dots). The zoom-in (isZoom 10s linear 1.1x) is attached on beforeChange like the original and removed from the previous slide 700ms later.

The graphics (tree logo · three kingfishers · leaf branch · white cloud · eighteen line icons) do not use the original PNG·SVG but are newly drawn SVGs with the same position, size and feel — fills use Skin variables (--kf-accent · orange is --site-orange made from the accent color), so they change together when the Skin is swapped. The kingfishers and tree are simpler than the original artwork.

The drifting cloud band (original background 1440px repeat-x · 60s linear) was built as the new motion part cloud-band-drift (a cloud-shaped mask filled with the skin color, 500px on phone), and the incoming bird (translateX −150% · 100px bottom margin → 1s/.6s, delay .2s, bobbing for 3s after landing) as the new motion part fly-in-bob. Entrance ([data-animation] opacity 1s, delay .2s) is credited to fade-up, and the Hero fade-approach has its source added to fade-zoom-slides.

The staggered photo strip (six original PNGs with slanted top edges) uses placeholders of the same size and height stagger (padding-top 35~201px), cut diagonally with clip-path, joined in four sets and drifting 25% over 90s — the exact sizes of the second to sixth are approximations measured on screen.

The thick-bordered panel of the features section (original SVG frame fill·stroke 12px) and the slanted top-edge cover of the hero photo (original topVis_mask) are redrawn as new paths of the same shape — the bend points are approximations matched by capture
Fonts: Zen Kaku Gothic New · Roboto Condensed are the same as the original (Google Fonts), Korean placeholders fall back to Noto Sans KR

Subpages built are the four recorded ones (About the clinic, Care guide, News, News article). The Care guide (7897px) repeated department sections, so it was cut to four departments, a vaccination fee table and two lines of introduced services. The About page’s features section dropped two photos and the in-house pharmacy box. Endoscopy, fever outpatient and directions pages weren’t recorded, so the menu links to service.html·index.html#access anchors
The map embed (footer) is a placeholder of the same position and size. The app download buttons are text placeholders

Fixed (found by measuring): the ”View details” arrow was fixed green so it vanished on green panels → now inherits the button text color (original is white → green on hover), the header phone button stays as is on hover, English notice window .5s, phone burger (46px circle · ∓45° crossing · middle line width 0 · .3s) and a single-tier drawer, page numbers as 50px round cells with green hover, post category tag hover

title: Branding agency with giant wide headings and a vertically growing post footer
good_for: Branding and design agency sites, studio portfolios with many cases, big-typography company intros and service pages that show process steps as cards.

pages.use: Agency home — a photo stack opening from the corner between two giant title lines, a black-panel serif About (letter scrub), a photo strip opening like a shutter with a big phrase, four works in three columns that unfold on both sides, a growing post footer

Work list — grid under a giant title (center-aligned swiper loop, bottoms cropped more the farther from center) and a list (hovering a row unfolds a photo strip): a portfolio list that toggles between the two views
About us — black panel with a We are ○○ title, serif manifesto that brightens letter by letter, big claim, team illustration slider, client field tags and three columns of names, office photo

How we work — a reason list that swaps one line every 2s between two-line headings, and four colored step cards that stick on top and stack over each other (description, photo, item list). For service and process About pages

Work detail — the work-colored hero shrinks from 100svh, with a fixed collapsible on the left (Challenge · Strategy …) and a 12-column photo grid on the right, pressing the next-work panel stuck to the bottom covers the screen with a color panel via barba, and the title flies into the next hero

notes: The original fonts PP Neue Corp (ultra-bold wide and narrow), FK Roman Standard and Helvetica Now Text are paid, so we replaced them with Archivo (width axis 125·62, 900), Newsreader and Inter. The Korean placeholder is Pretendard, which has no wide or narrow forms, so title widths differ from the original.

Videos (both sides of the three-column work and list row previews) are placeholders so nothing actually plays — for spots that play only on screen or on hover, only the data flag and expansion are wired up

The lenis and lottie in the original card’s libs are not used by the original now (checked by measuring), so they were not included. barba is loaded only on detail pages as in the original and used only when moving between details (detail.html)
The Contact (/contact) page has no recording in the archive, so the menu item ”Contact” links to the office spot (#contact) on the About page

The original Webflow IX3 (hero, nav drop-down, title words) starts after the document is complete, so the copy also hooks in after load — so the first paint shows the end state, then it returns to the start and animates (same as the original)

Font backfill: since the original text is all English, the wide heading (Archivo 125%), narrow post footer (Archivo 62%) and serif (Newsreader) spots were all replaced with English placeholder text — menu (Works·Approach·About·Contact) · clock cities · two Hero lines and side text · section names · big shutter phrases · step names (Phase One…) · twelve reason list items · 36 client names · sectors (Sector 01…) · work name rows (Project Name 01) · detail titles (Project A·B) · serif manifesto · intro · bio · step descriptions · accordion paragraphs · footer tagline and address · four post-footer sentences. No heading or serif spot is left in Korean

Judgment: the serif explanation sentences (service intro, manifesto, team intro, bio, step description, detail accordion) were also English sentences in that typeface in the original, so they were changed to English. Body font (Inter) spots, namely the footer header (contact, city names), bottom links, person name/title lines, field tags, step item lists and accordion buttons, were kept Korean. The work name line is Inter but was made English together with the English title in the detail page to match (latin-slots also caught it via the a-tag rule .lr-foot__group a)
