Hero bottom line: Archivo 125% is wider than the original typeface, so the original character count (11) overflows both sides at 1440, and it was cut to two words (Set here) to fit the top line’s width. The intro claim heading is lr-center (vertical flex) stacking one word per line, so it keeps three words like the original. The work list heading has one word filling the full width at 390, so it uses two words (All Work)
lang on the post footer heading="en" is attached so the original .75 applies instead of the Korean line height (:lang(ko) .95)

title: Two quiet campgrounds told through photos, with a vertical-text hero and swaying leaf shadows
good_for: Brand home pages for campgrounds, lodging or nature facilities with several sites to choose from, including notices, events, maps, site introductions and a blog.

pages.use: Campsite brand home page: a full-height landscape photo with vertical copy and a notice line, an event card slider, a forest-colored map with travel times by city, two sites (vertical caption photo, feature table, button), a company card, a blog and column slider, a closing story, and a leaf-shadow Footer with a white menu panel.

notes: The original site is under maintenance right now (Product 503 maintenance), and the archived HAR holds only a ”page cannot be displayed” error screen. I read the HTML·CSS (id_ raw) from the 2026-10-03 web archive snapshot to carry over the values, and checked the screens against contact-sheet prints (sheet-1440·390) and the archive view.

The Swiper version could not be confirmed because the bundle is not in the web archive. We use swiper@11.1.14, from the same period (Gatsby 5.13), set up as read from the CSS: slidesPerView auto (slide width from css), 36px gap (at 1352, phone 3.13vw), prev/next buttons, draggable scrollbar. Transition speed 300 is the Swiper default.

I couldn’t see the original JS for the versions where the header bar turns white text (forest-green map, blue closing photo), so data-tone is set on the two versions where the white logo shows in the screen capture="dark" Attach it and pick it the same way as under-tone-button (the board beneath the button’s vertical center).

The typeface Gothic MB101 (DemiBold·Medium·Bold) is a paid TypeSquare font, so it is replaced with Zen Kaku Gothic New (Latin·kana) + Gothic A1 (Hangul), and the Helvetica Neue spots (Menu·date) with Arimo. Strokes are thinner and tracking slightly wider than the original.

The dragonfly logo, map line art, leaf shadows (a blurred leaf photo PNG in the original) and SNS logos were redrawn as our own SVG. The leaves are clumps of ellipses along a branch curve with blur 4px · ink 13% to match the faintness of the original photo.

Placeholder text for the “Important” and “Urgent” tags on notice lines, the campsite feature table (6 cells × 2 rows), and the dotted-line duration text is in Korean, sized close to the original character count. The original’s disabled cells (diagonal-striped td.disable) are not used because they don’t appear on the first page.
The original subpages were not recorded (pages: [] in pages.json, links couldn’t be captured due to maintenance). The per-campsite links on the menu panel are set to #.

The notice rows (3) below the hero follow the teardown print (2026-10-29) — the web archive copy (2026-10-03) had no notice, so the hero photo covers the whole screen. Without notices, remove .news and you get the original look (the hero is flex and the photo takes all the remaining height).

title: Companion-style branding service with particle gradient shapes and a drawn logotype
good_for: One-page design, branding or consulting service landings covering worries, reasons, strengths, people, pricing, cases, questions and contact.

pages.use: One-page service landing: a Hero where a logotype is drawn over ring, pill, diamond and triangle grain-gradient shapes, News, overlapping concern circles, Reasons (photo bleeds out to the left), three staggered strength cards, a semicircle-rounded About band, four staggered people, a Pricing board (consultation card, three flat-rate supports, nine option buttons, four-step flow), a consultation band, six Work cases, FAQ accordion, and a tabbed Contact form. A thick white wave band is drawn across the sections

notes: Subpages were not recorded (archive pages.json is empty). The original also sells itself from a single first page, so only one index.html was built
Category: the auto card said Hospital · Clinic, but it is a branding service for medical and welfare corporations, so both the card and meta were changed to Agency

Hero logotype: the original is four katakana characters hand-drawn with thick strokes (SVG path), so it was not carried over — instead four Korean characters (SVG text, Noto Sans KR 900) are placed in the same spot and diagonal layout. The order and durations are as in the original: outline draw (5s·.25s·1s linear) → .1s later the outline switches off in .4s and the filled letters switch on in 1s, but the glyph outline dash length is a fixed value (1400) rather than the path length, so the drawing speed per letter differs from the original

The five wave bands are not ported from the original paths but redrawn as curves at the same height, position and thickness — the bend shapes differ, but the drawing length and curve (1~2s cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1)) are exactly the original’s

Contact form: the original is a built-in form from an external service, so it is a static form with the same fields (name·pronunciation·email·company·industry·what to build·inquiry) — sending does not work
Checking by swapping in other dark and light skins and capturing was not done — lint is 0 and all shape colors are --site-* (values derived from the accent color). Work for the next person to pick up

title: Recruiting site with apricot discs bleeding into the background and vertical copy
good_for: Recruiting sites, company culture and benefits pages for warm, quietly spoken companies that suit large vertical-writing headlines.

pages.use: Recruiting home page — vertical large copy whose letters settle down from a blur, with an intro text, a company intro with pill photo links · glass cards, a culture section with white blurred circles on a solid panel, five glass-panel job cards → a work environment section where a pinned photo grows as it is revealed from underneath, a new-grad section with a 40s photo flow, and news cards. For recruiting · company landing pages

Company About hub — below the page header (title with a drawn line + breadcrumb), three glass-panel cards with a round photo, title, intro and arrow box. Hovering a card spreads the arrow box. For a table-of-contents page leading to subarticles (CEO message, vision, business)
Culture: intro text + photo, four value cards with coral circle art on a charcoal panel, and two Learn more photo links on a glass band. For code of conduct, values and culture pages.

Work environment — number graphic cards (four graphs of bar·donut·circle size, six icon numbers), work policy·benefits cards (three columns) on a glass strip, and an endlessly sliding, center-aligned office photo slider. For benefits·company-by-numbers pages

Job category detail (Product) — intro text, three role cards, four News cards, job posting list (three-column cards), FAQ accordions by category, sibling links to the same job category. Scrolling down turns on a section list on the left. For a single job category or department detail

notes: Grain surface of the two accented Hero characters (original: Exploration). The original cuts a grain canvas (noise-plate) with a letter-shaped mask SVG and makes it boil. Here the surface is a coral radial gradient cut into the letters, so the grain does not boil (the 1.6s color change timing and length follow the original).
The number graphics·value graphics are image files (charts·illustrations) in the original, so they were redrawn as SVG bars·donuts·circles of the same position and ratio — values are placeholders
The job listing list is a React island in the original (filter, load more). Here only nine static cards and a Load more button — no filtering or loading more.

Swup transitions are enabled only when opened over http (file:// blocks fetch, so it falls back to normal navigation). No transition effect, as in the original: main switches off, turns back on after 100ms over .4s, and the backdrop plate slides to its new spot
Inner parallax on the job photos and culture photos (original js-ParallaxImage) — the photo ratio is unknown, so it was guessed at 118.5% height and −15.6% → 0 and set up as inner-parallax
Scroll restoration after page navigation on the original first page (back to the previous position on popstate) is not implemented

title: Developer portfolio where two interlocking wheels raise the work
good_for: Creative developer or studio portfolios with a single-screen work stage, a draggable about board, an experiments wheel and a rotating-gallery experiment page.

pages.use: Portfolio home page: a wheel of photo cards and a wheel of logo panels turn in mesh, standing a work in the front center slot, while the number, name and tag roll over like a slot machine. A top HUD gauge, pill nav and command panel. For a portfolio Hero that flips through 9~17 works on one screen.

About — drag postcards (stamp portrait, postmark) on a bulletin board, a dashboard (time, location, yearly record cells), a record radio and tag cards, and pressing one grows it to the center and opens a letter dialog. For personal or studio About pages

Experiment list — large name rows tilt and line up around a wheel centered off the left of the screen. Wheel · drag rotates it, the center row lights up and the right preview changes. For experiment · work list pages
Single experiment (rotating gallery) — ten photos stand on a ring and flow, drag to spin with weight, switch to grid view and the cards bounce into cells. For photo set and lookbook detail

notes: The two hero wheels don’t port the original’s print-metaphor shader (ink gloss · chrome rim · holographic plate · paper bend · film grain). Instead, flat three cards and a square plate were rebuilt with the same position, size and spin values (twin-wheel-cards). Wheel radius · neighbor angle · front scale are back-computed from the original screen (card wheel .93 · 60° · 1.9x, plate wheel .79 · 83° · 1.1x), and wheel .0011 · drag .0034 · follow .08 are the bundled PARAMS values. The original’s hand-throw inertia (flick · momentum · vmax) is reduced to release speed × 6 slots.
Work card photos and panel logos are Skin-colored placeholders (card: diagonal X + what the photo is, panel: chrome frame + one letter). Inside the cell · Put it in and that picture gets painted.

Instead of the grain (fibers, creases, stains, wrinkles) of the original paper-gl shader, only a grain canvas plus the cursor-trail halftone (paper-wake-dots — 1/8 resolution trail buffer, radius .085, .94 decay, 6px dots, press ring) were carried over.

The HUD’s visitor count, current track and notification bell, plus other visitors’ cursors and join/leave alerts, are placeholder imitations instead of a live server (presence worker · music service). Values jitter randomly ± every 9 seconds and two cursors drift around. The command panel (⌘K) picks only among four pages.

About: details of the original’s four cards (postcard postmark SVG filter and stamp gloss, the radio’s real playback and tape, the dashboard’s Brand record) are drawn as static placeholders. Dragging is rebuilt with GSAP Draggable (the original’s own code). The luggage tag card, like the original, is not shown on the wide-screen board and only appears in the narrow-screen stack (judgment call).

Lab list: the original wheels-lab bundle is not in the archive (the lab document shares its name with the lab/ folder and won’t unpack), so it was built from a screen capture, with a big name wheel (radius max(900, screen height × 1.35), line gap 10% of screen height) and a preview on the right. The wheel feel uses the same .08 follow as the first page, with only the wheel share increased. The List · Grid view buttons are shape only.

Rotating gallery: follows the original rotating-gallery values (10 cards · 36° · 4° per second flow · weight 8 · perspective 4000 · 5-column grid · Flip back.inOut(2.2)), and the ring radius 180px and card 12rem×1.08 scale down with screen size. The original tuning panel (?tune) for drift, weight, perspective and curve is left out.
The original Astro page transition (ClientRouter veil cover) is left as a regular link navigation.
Fonts: the original Oracle·PP Neue Montreal Mono are paid, so the closest free Geist·Geist Mono are used, with Korean in Noto Sans KR.

Interaction responses were rebuilt with the original CSS values exactly — menu · ⌘K · View project letter roll (second text-shadow layer per letter at 1.4em, translate .4s expo-out, 12.5ms per letter), button background plate .95 (.4s) · press .96 (.2s), ⌘K background .97/.95, skin toggle color .3s · sliding background, logo circle border · background .25s, notification panel (opacity .3s + from .5rem up at .97× with .3s expo-out, close .15s), ⌘K panel (opacity .3s + from .5rem below at .3s), social links .7→1, postcard postmark button (dotted border .2s, pressing makes the record card grow from .3× over .4s). At first it was rolled with the char-roll motion part, but the original uses CSS translate so the measured values differ, so the site was switched to the original method (the char-roll source line is kept since the motion is the same)

Rotating gallery page: built the original lab document frame (round stage panel + top-left description button → the stage shifts 27.5rem in .55s expo-out, the description panel goes from −1rem·.985x to opaque in .4s (after 80ms) and transforms in .5s (after 40ms)). The tuning panel inside the original description panel (Drift·Weight·Depth·Morph·Image controls) is a placeholder holding only a value list.

title: Park barbecue site with wiped flower, mountain and leaf masked photos and bouncing hand-drawn people
good_for: Facility sites for campgrounds, barbecue areas, park cafes or farm experiences that bundle pricing plans, menu, usage guide and directions.

pages.use: Facility home — a hero with three masked photos (flower, mountain, leaf) wiped in at offbeat timing, vertical copy and pop-up hand drawings, a news strip, About, a pricing grid strip with a menu Splide and a side-dish grid, a park map usage guide, access directions, a news Splide that stacks in from the right, FAQ, and a booking grid. For barbecue area and campsite landing pages

News list: a large title and category box, three-column cards joined by 1px lines (vertical category text · photo or empty logo image · date · title), and pagination. For announcement and event News lists and category lists (the original /news/category/information has the same form).

Facility intro — large title with grid-shadow photo and hand drawing, three feature columns with hand drawings attached, divider photo strip flowing with parallax, facility overview table beside a hand drawing. For shop and facility intro pages

Menu and pricing: a header index box, two About photos, a pricing guide over a left grid band with three masked photos, four menus with vertical headers (photo Splide · composition table), an auto-flowing row of masked photos, and three white plates over a grid (single items · drinks · supplies in a 2-column price list). For restaurant menus and price lists.

notes: Photos are gray placeholders (.wf-img) labeled with subject, light and ratio. The original hand drawings (30-odd, people, grill, tulips, car, bike, etc.) are in shared.js’s <symbol> The set of 18 items (four people · two kids · grill · table · tree · tulip · dog · bicycle · cart · car · cup · pot · tent · grass blade · ball) as a bundle <use> combined and redrawn in the same place and size. Surfaces are the skin’s base, mint, pink and sky (--site-sky), so they follow when the skin changes.

The logo is an SVG placeholder (#cb-logo) of ”small park name + three color blobs + spaced English name” in place of the original lettering image, and the footer logo is four waves + English name (#cb-ftlogo). The empty News image uses the same logo.

The flower (four-leaf) · leaf · mountain (trapezoid) masks do not use the original SVG but are newly drawn paths at the same ratios (330:300 · 363:300). The 1px ink outline is a four-direction drop-shadow like the original (the Skin’s --kf-ink).

The park map (585×655) and parking guide (426×240) were redrawn as new SVGs instead of the original images (70 randomly placed trees · 10 numbered spots · deck · P). The map iframe is a placeholder of the same ratio (670:420, 1:1 on phones).
The icon font (icomoon) was replaced with line-icon SVGs in the same places (#i-arrow·i-chev·i-ext·i-up·i-down·i-insta). Splide arrows are thin chevron lines via arrowPath.

The grid base (bg-mesh.svg) is two CSS gradients with the same spacing (24px · 2px lines, horizontal mint at y 11.23 · vertical pink at x 12). The vertical line color #edcee2 is --site-mesh-v = oklch(from --kf-accent-soft l−.036 · h−26.3), sky blue is --site-sky = Built from the skin with oklch(from --kf-accent).

Vertical text, second-line letter delay: the original uses line 3.1s · letters 3.1~3.6s (first line 2.0s · 2.1~2.5s), so each line follows a different rule — the rise-underline-title part uses one rule, line delay + lead .1 + .1×i, so second-line letters come .1s late (3.2~3.7s). It is within tolerance, so it was left as is.

Text is Korean placeholder copy, while spots where the original used a Latin heading typeface (Public Sans), such as section names, menu, reserve button, Page Top and category names, use English placeholders (News·About·Menu·Our Guide·Access·FAQ·Reserve·Notice·Side Menu …). The Japanese gothic (Zen Kaku Gothic New 500) was substituted with Gothic A1 500.

title: Name-origin story page with engraved figures turning away and a flaming ampersand finale
good_for: Agency, consulting or law firm intros that tell how two people or fields came together, using a pinned scroll scene, service list and one-question-at-a-time contact.

pages.use: A one-page agency site: a Hero where a big wordmark shrinks into a header line, a crowd of eight engraved portraits that is pulled in close, then steps back and turns away, a two-person close-up (horizontal grain erased, scattering into dust), a handshake, an ampersand crossing the screen, a flame & and white wordmark on an ink panel, About and service lists (engraved art), a Contact form that advances one question at a time, and an ink Footer. The company About section tells the story behind the name

notes: In the original, the figures, powder kegs, pistol and map are engraving image files (webp) drawn with WebGL2. Here no images are used, and our own silhouettes are drawn on canvas with shading (four 17th-century figures in hats, ruffed collars, capes, breeches, boots and swords, two powder kegs, and a pistol on an unfolded map) using the same shader effects (horizontal engraving lines · per-row sideways-dragged erasing · powder scatter · body turn). Because the silhouettes are simple, the original engraving’s detail in faces and clothing folds is missing. To bring in real engraving images, pass images from the same source (transparent background) in place of figure()·barrels()·pistolMap() in engrave.js.

The original swaps in angle-specific images per person to turn them around (from → final angle in scene-intro.json). Here the same angle values only change the horizontal width (cos) and the darkness of the turned-away back to make them rotate.
In the original the sky (cf-sky) has a cloud print drifting slowly. Here it is a fixed band with the light and shade of the cloud masses drawn in print lines.
The effect where the title forms out of gunpowder dust (is-dusting, original Powder canvas) was replaced with words rising inside a cover — the person’s dust scattering is done with a shader dust.

Timeline length and section order were pinned to the original at 31 sections (unit 1 = Screen height 45%, scrub .5 are the original values). Details inside a section (at which unit the person enters) were matched by eye (guess).

Contact builds the original one-question-at-a-time form (6 steps, options, error text, final thank-you) but does not send. The original’s bot-check widget and second form (dropdown inquiry type) are not included.
Text is Korean placeholder, wordmark, titles and lists are English placeholders with similar character counts to the original (Name & Name etc.).

The cursor and dot progress indicator were rebuilt from the original bundle’s rules and values measured by opening the original. Cursor: a 12px white dot (difference blend) that follows 22% per frame, with its box also at 22% (30% for magnet or large box), 2.67× and ink color over links, and over an ember button a box of button+6 showing the button’s text. Engraved panels get a mouse tilt (6%, max 22px × screen width/1680 × depth). The dot progress indicator sits at the very end of body: 8px dots, the current section a 14×48 bar, a hovered dot becomes a pill of name width×42 (name appears after .12s over .25s), when another dot is hovered the current bar folds to 8px, 12~22px gaps that spread with scroll speed, and a press makes a .46s ripple. The original’s crowd character hover (the touched figure turns to look) was not included.

title: Portfolio whose endless photo column rises from a single point
good_for: Designer or photographer portfolio heroes, small merchandise shops and experimental work collections.

pages.use: Portfolio home page — 12 dots spread in a line, then stand as a photo column stacked alternately vertical and horizontal, spinning endlessly by wheel or drag, with work names 01~12 on both sides darkening from the ones nearest the center plate. List/slide toggle and About panel. For the entrance of a personal portfolio with around ten works

Goods shop — after a loader of a row of small product photos, seven products are scattered randomly on screen, and clicking an empty spot scatters them again (”Click to shuffle” next to the cursor). Phone is a 2-column grid. For a small shop with a few products · limited edition showcase.

Experiments collection — a 20×8 grid of photo and video tiles wraps endlessly in every direction with wheel or drag, and on click the camera flies into that tile and arrows page through neighboring tiles. Phone shows a 2-column list. For gathering short experiments, sketches and video clips on one board

notes: Photos and video are placeholders. The pillar panels and grid panels are gray and ink-black placeholders drawn on a WebGL canvas (labeled with what the photo is), and the playground video slot has a bar at the bottom that fills every 4s and loops (autoplay, repeat). Swapping in the original hi-res texture (2000px after 300ms) was left out because there is no image

Playground layout — the original shuffles 6000 times on every open and lays pieces randomly so the same image never neighbors itself. The part (fly-grid-gl) is a fixed layout that picks by shifting 5 cells per column and 7 per row, so it’s the same each time it opens

Page transition: like the original (Next + next-view-transitions), the document is not reloaded and only the wrapper is swapped, using the same View Transition keyframes (vt-swap-page + page-vt-reveal). Since pages load via fetch, opening from a file usually just follows the link, and only the incoming page body opens upward from the bottom

The shop’s ‹Press to mix› text sits at the top left until the first mouse move (the original also settles its position on the first move). Clicking a product goes to /shop/ in the original<slug> Leads to a product detail page, but it was not recorded, so no link was added

Typeface — original PP Neue Montreal (paid) replaced with Hanken Grotesk 500. Because it is 11px uppercase, glyphs run slightly wider, so right-column names start a few px further in than the original

title: Walk-in 3D workshop behind an entrance door
good_for: Space, studio or workshop introductions, interactive home pages that attach people, work and tools to objects in a room, and recruitment or contact pages.

pages.use: Home page — a cobalt entry gate (wordmark·rotating model·Click to enter) → on click, after a progress count the curtain lifts up and the 3D studio opens. Drag to look around, the hotspots and the bottom pill menu fly the camera to the desk (people)·swing (work)·whiteboard (about)·pegboard (tools)·in front of the TV and open the right info panel

Support and Contact — a big pixel serif heading mixed with picture letters (words rise line by line and the picture grows to open up space), a white-panel support form, and a photo strip that stays pinned and flows sideways, pressing down when swiped fast. Arrives from the home Join / phone booth with a cobalt curtain covering the screen.

notes: The 3D room does not use the original models and textures (2 GLBs · 18 webps). It is built from our basic shapes and canvas patterns (brick · tile · wood grain · pegboard · zebra · striped rug · sky) at the original dimensions (10×12m · walls 4.6 / ridge 5.8m · loft 3m · 16 stairs · desk 3×1.4m · 9 lighting cylinder spots …). Plants and props (phone · teddy bear · microphone · camcorder) are simple shapes with only a similar silhouette, and the original’s baked soft lighting (lightmap) is approximated with hemisphere light + sun + point-light shadows

Room material colors: the --site-* values in shared.css are built as oklch relative colors from --kf-accent-soft, --kf-ink and --kf-accent. The bone color (--kf-bg) has low chroma, so Chrome drops its hue to 0 (powerless hue) and it turns pink, so butter is used as the base instead. Changing the skin shifts the tone of the whole room with it.
The entrance door mock video (44s loop, 512:448) was replaced by our desk, chair and light shapes rotated once in 44s on a three canvas in the same place and size (original video file not used)

Original PP Mondwest (paid pixel serif) → Redaction 35 (OFL, fontsource CDN), Aeonik → Geist. The wordmark is set in title-typeface letters instead of the original SVG logo (logo spot). Korean pairs: Galmuri11 · Pretendard

The transition curtain color is picked at random from a CMS list in the original, but the list isn’t in the archive, so only the first confirmed value (cobalt) is kept — add data-tint names to TINTS in shared.js to grow it

Original viewpoint fitting (the calculation that adjusts fov and viewOffset so the object point cluster avoids the info panel and pill at each close-up) — the overview uses the original formula as is, while close-up is approximated with a half-panel-width viewOffset + a widened fov on narrow screens — object placement in phone close-up comes out larger than the original.

The original TV close-up video play button (.tv-controls) and the detailed panel types that change when whiteboard notes are pressed (measured layouts per builder·whiteboard) are not built, and are grouped into four common panel types (people·work·tools·questions)
The four Join graphic letters (lighting · brace logo mark · wavy line · pixel cursor) are our own SVGs in the same position, size and tilt instead of the original 3D render images

title: Publisher site with flowing photo columns and a turning magazine wheel
good_for: Publishing and media company sites with magazine or brand introductions, company profile, news and policy pages.

pages.use: Company first page — the loader curtain folds up to reveal five flowing photo columns that then fade to gray as the logo is drawn in lines, awning, four magazines stuck to the screen and turning over like a wheel, book line art, production video section. For a company landing with multiple media

About the company — 4% letter band laid behind, hero pinned to the screen where four sentence lines slide left and right (middle line is a logo-shaped video), pledge sentence, company overview table, map. For company and organization intros
News list: month/day diagonal-fraction dates and serif title rows, a preview box follows over a row and the picture splits diagonally, page turning. For notice and news archives
Single news item — fractional date + title header, serif body, prev·next news and list (INDEX) navigation. For a single notice
Policy and terms text — large English header · centered serif title · numbered items (underlined heading + body) · effective date. For privacy, terms of use and ethics policies

notes: imagesLoaded (the original uses it to lift the loader after all images are fetched) is a placeholder with no images so it is not included, the loader is lifted on the load event

The photo columns stack placeholder cells vertically instead of the original background-image strip (background-position loop) and flow them with marquee (axis: y) — the original speed (column height × 72ms) is converted to 14px per second. The color → gray fade is a placeholder, done with a grayscale filter only.

Logos, marks, group logos, magazine covers and the book line drawing were redrawn as our own SVG and placeholders — the original book drawing (a bundle of upright book lines) was replaced with two bundles of five books stacked at an angle, in the same spot and width
The logo-shaped video in the About head is a placeholder video inside our mark + long bar-shaped mask — the original logo SVG mask wasn’t used
The curve of the phone menu curved panel follows the original, which wrote ”Expo0ut” (a typo) and so runs on GSAP’s default curve (power1.out)
The original page transition (a dark curtain rising from the bottom) is only attached to staging-address links, so it never runs on the live site — not built
The magazine panel pinning swaps the original fixed/bottom approach for sticky (same position, same scroll length: three 100vh cells, two 33vh rests, 90vh end)
Map is a placeholder — the original is an embedded map, and the cookie consent window (external widget) was not built either

title: Dark sports gear shop where logo fragments open and swap the screen
good_for: Shops with a few product categories such as rackets, shoes and equipment, featuring a video hero, product cards, feature intro, category list, reviews and newsletter signup.

pages.use: Shop home page — video first screen · emphasis paragraph with words lighting up · three racket cards · photo that grows after a splitting title with picker cards · feature cards beside a pinned video · branch cards · half-and-half intro · review line breaks · Instagram grid · newsletter footer, mega menu and comparison table window
Brand story — after the first photo, three halves alternating mission, belief and promise with photos, reviews, social feed. For company and brand about pages

Product category list — large category name, product count line, 3-column product cells where hovering switches on a photo from another angle, and two other category cards. For shop category and search result lists
Newsletter signup form — big title, thin line, and a signup form on the right half with name, email and consent fields laid out two per row. For newsletter, waitlist and simple signup pages.

notes: The hero background is a Vimeo background video in the original (two versions, landscape and portrait, swapped by screen orientation). In headless mode Vimeo blocks it with ”could not verify connection security”, so it looks empty in the original too. The copy puts placeholder videos of the same ratio in the same spot (placeholder-16x9.mp4 · placeholder-9x16.mp4, 8s loop), with orientation swap, autoplay and loop wired as in the original. The video in the pinned feature section uses the same placeholder.

The logo does not use the original mark but a placeholder mark made of the same four 1:2 pieces (half-ring, bar, left half-circle, right half-circle) — the first open and footer logo motion work per piece, so only the piece count and ratio were matched.
The Instagram grid is an external widget in the original, so only four square cells (three on phone) and a ‹Load more› button are placed in the same spot (pressing it does nothing).

Fonts: Ratch (paid) → Lexend 500 · 400, T-Star Medium (paid, narrow uppercase labels) → Barlow Semi Condensed 500, Korean in Noto Sans KR. 1rem uses the original formula (body size clamp(16px,.1vi+15.6px,18px)) as is.

Taxi swaps only the view (data-taxi-view) and keeps the head css of the first page, so all four page css files (index · about · product · page) are loaded on every page to make the look hold whichever page you enter from. Motion also works like the original app.js: one bundle (shared.js · pages.js) finds the sections on screen and hooks them up. When opened via file://, it covers with the same curtain (.6s sine.inOut) and navigates instead of using Taxi.
The pinned feature section’s progress bar has no fill code in the original app.js (it’s in css or another bundle), so I guessed it fills top to bottom along the right-hand list with scrub (guess).

Swiper (product detail photo slider) and Fancybox (photo enlarge view) are not used in the four built pages, so they were not included. The cart is only an empty cart where a white plate (600px wide · 90%) slides in from the right like the original store platform drawer (the .4s open is a guess), currency is only a small plate (.15s from 8px above), and account has only an outside link spot.
The newsletter signup form (original form plugin) is not sent. Pressing it only turns on a one-line thank-you. The cookie banner version (original cookie plugin) is also just a placeholder.
The emphasis paragraph line height was loosened to 1.12 with Korean placeholder text, then reset to the original 1 when the font backfill made it English.

The comparison table window is a panel that slides in from the right like the original (.6s · width clamp(560px,4vi+544px,640px)) with a .8 dark scrim (.4s, .2s later when closing). The table’s cell layout (six skill rows × three shapes) is also the same as the original.

Font backfill: since all original text is English (brand product lines), every slot for title weight (Lexend 500 · --kf-font-display) and labels (Barlow Semi Condensed · --kf-font-label) was replaced with English placeholder copy — intro line·sale strip·menu·currency·mega menu racket cards·cart title·cookie title and buttons·hero title and intro·tag and the two big emphasis paragraphs·racket cards·two-line split title·picker question and buttons·feature names·category names·half-and-half title·four reviews and names·Instagram header·newsletter prompt and button (including the rolling data-label)·footer categories and legal line·comparison table (header·skill row·racket columns)·product names·form field names. No title or label slot is left in Korean.

Decision: body typeface (Lexend 400 · --kf-font-sans) sentences — cookie notice body·split-half body·mission/thought/promise lists·pick descriptions·feature descriptions·empty cart line·form field hints and consent sentences·comparison table descriptions — are kept in Korean per the README. Only the button name quoted inside the cookie body was aligned to 「Accept All」

title: Text ring loader opening into a round hole, with a rainbow sweeping over pinned copy
good_for: New-graduate and career recruiting home pages for service, travel or aviation companies where people are the face, with three tracks (work, people, environment) plus a recruitment info, news and apply band.

pages.use: Recruiting first page — letter-ring spiral loader (opens through a round hole), hero video with a big title whose letters bounce up one by one and blue wing curves, pinned purpose statement where four photos scatter past (highlighted word gets a rainbow sweep), three sections inside a blue rounded panel with a big Latin band flowing: Work (photo strip), People (interview cards flipping every 3 seconds, numbered), Environment, white job info panel, notice list, boarding-pass-style ENTRY band, deep blue footer. For a recruiting site hero

notes: The three subpages (company overview about · job types jobtypes · staff interview interview) were not built because the archive recorded only a bot-protection human-check screen (pages.json title ”Just a moment…” · height 900), so the original cannot be seen. Headless Chrome and curl both still get a 403 check screen. Menu and footer links connect to sections inside the first page (#works·#interview·#environment·#recruit) — once the subpages are recorded with a human browser, about and recruit can be built next with the same shared.css·shared.js.

The loader spiral text (original SVG letter art) is newly drawn as English placeholder text on an SVG textPath along the same circle, the cloud·island map PNG as blurred ellipses·island strokes in SVG, and the logo symbol as a blue wing curve in SVG. The original logo (italic wordmark art) is an SVG text wordmark placeholder.
The hero video is a gray-gradient placeholder with the same 16:9 · 13.2s loop (media/fv.mp4), and the blue wing strip below the hero (original PNG) is an SVG curve of the same ratio (3024:934).

Vertical section titles follow the original character counts (6·5·6) with ”Knowing the work.” ”Knowing people” ”Knowing the environment.” — in upright vertical Korean each character is 1em, so the character count sets the section height (same as the original height of 343px).

Cookie consent (the vendor’s ”Privacy” button), analytics scripts and the Company check are operational devices, so they were not built. The external application site links for MY PAGE · ENTRY point to #entry.

Splide has no panel marker in the original bundle, so 4.1.4 from _vendor was used (the auto-scroll extension is 0.5.3, same as the original). The original loads ScrollTrigger but never uses it, so it is not included.

title: Luxury car brand site with a scroll-opened video prelude and horizontal history
good_for: Luxury product or brand anniversary sites with a video prelude, gallery, horizontally flowing history, craftsman story and showroom guide.

pages.use: Brand first page: loading and opening video → cocoon illustration hero → first wheel brings in the key video → manifesto where a photo and a Lottie title overlap (lead paragraph over a blurred veil) → video frame that grows while pinned, with a ”Watch video” picker → gallery rows and modal slider where the screen tints as the hand enters → 800vh horizontal history (the partition veil lifts) → horizontal craftsman cards → showroom info over a pinned photo → lineup → footer revealed through a window. Suited to premium product, commemorative and brand sites.

Craftsperson story — header photo and title that open as the cover lifts, prologue, three sections where photo and text swap sides, strip photo, back link. For interview and making-of articles inside a brand site

notes: The recorded sub-page is just the English version (/en) of the same first page, so it was not built separately. Same type. Instead, the craftsperson detail page (/japanpride01/), where the craftsperson story card leads, was built as detail.html from the original HTML, CSS and JS without a recording (opens with the cover on and lifts at 1s, lowered photo, .9x text group, table of contents hidden after 80px). Only one of the four craftsperson detail pages was built. Same type

The opening, key video, CM preview and CM main use gray 16:9 placeholder videos of the same lengths (11.2·6.0·6.0·30s) (media/*.mp4, ffmpeg gradient + temporal noise + name label) hooked to the same playback behavior (skip 3s before the end · play on first wheel · play at screen center). The original videos were not used

Typeface backfill: Declaration Lottie title — the original draws English script One of One (OneofOne_En layer) and one line of Japanese (OneofOne_text_jp layer) on a single board. The Korean stroke ‹Title goes here› was redrawn at the same tempo as nine single-line English strokes of A Big Title (the last letter ends at frame 114). The Japanese second line was absent from the first build, so it was not built this time either

Font backfill: the first showroom link ‹Store list› is Japanese in the original, and the Korean text is kept. All three are English-font (font_en) slots in the original, so ct-en is applied to render them in Lato, and Korean falls back to the Pretendard counterpart in theme.css (a thin sans-serif like Lato).

Font backfill: places the original wrote in uppercase in the HTML (LOADING · SKIP · exhibition name labels · venue info titles · detail back-link TOP) are set in uppercase English, and mixed-case places (history English subtitle · Prologue) in mixed-case English. The gallery modal photo caption (.ct-gm__caption) is body font in the original too, so it stays Korean

The cocoon (mayu) drawing, logo mark, and showroom map were redrawn in SVG (a 54-thread cocoon, an abstract bird emblem, a road map). Photos (manifesto, history, gallery, artisans, showroom, lineup, footer) are placeholders
Gallery thumbnails were cut to 12·8·8·6 per row (original about 17). All six video-choice buttons open the same modal (30s placeholder) — the original has a different modal per quality and length

The cookie consent popup (a consent tool) and analytics tags are external services so they were not built. The EN language button opens the same page at index.html?lang=Reopen in en (the original jumps to another language version)
Menu cell width is set to min-width 118px to match the original uppercase English index (longest line 118px) — so the touch target doesn’t narrow because the Korean placeholders are short

title: Event and community site with flowing green mosaic tiles
good_for: Event, camp and community gathering sites, event intros with many participant faces, and photo-heavy gathering archives.

pages.use: Event home page — the loader strip rises to become the headline, a hero where four stair-stepped participant photos line up under the headline, a large intro text with rounded chips mixed in, a story section where small photos fill a frame, a scene where stickers are stuck on one by one, line-by-line filled philosophy text, three circles and a job list, a pile of posters that drop and stack, a three-day schedule where the date changes, a draggable memory wall, reviews, and a footer full of names. Suited to an event or camp home.

About the group — four-cell hero (group photo, black cell, big title, mosaic), founder story with large text and a pinned photo, two feature cells, a large group photo, a yearly event log (the pinned photo changes at each step), a core member ring, vision and goal statements, and a community photo. For the Us page of a community or group.

Photo gallery — below the header bar, one screen is a foggy endless 3D space with stamp-like photos scattered about. Fly around by drag, wheel, and keys, and click to open one large in the center. For event photo archives and lookbooks

notes: In the original, a GLTF butterfly model emerges from circle 1 and lands on a point set per section — ours reproduces the same size and silhouette with two wings (canvas pattern) plus a capsule body, and is on screen from the start. The koi and frog 3D creatures inside the circle were not built (only the peek window over the circle)

The poster stack uses three to drop paper tilted -29° and bend then flatten, but the paper-stack original’s paper wrinkle and layered shadow math is approximated. The large ring circle at the end is read as a circle expanding into the agenda, as seen in the original frames.

The tile-shatter reaction around the mouse over the hero photo is built with DOM tiles (cells holding photo fragments shift and the background shows through the gaps). The original uses WebGL, where each cell shrinks, scatters and ripples (warp .4, ripple 3). Photo swapping is built: when the 6s progress band fills, the band clears to the right (.75s) and four cells, starting from the lowest, at .24s steps (all at once at 899 and below), grow diagonally to cover the hero with five color plates attached to the bottom right corner plus the new photo (original chande-reveal: head -1→.5 power3.inOut 1.481s, plate gap .1, number decrypts when the first plate fully covers). The band is timed from loader end, or from transition start when entered via a transition, and pauses when the hero is off screen. The new photo changes only the placeholder color. Film grain and dither are not built.
The scroll-speed tilt of the large agenda title is turned off in the original settings, so it is not included. The original cursor character is also turned off
Intro chip: the original draws 6 mouth-shape presets and a signal waveform every frame — we reduced it to a single SVG mouth line that smiles on scroll and five beads that ripple
Gallery: the original stamps have perspective warp (warpScale 6.5), zigzag layout, memo notes and chat back-flip — ours has 5 seeds per cluster, fog, drag inertia, wheel, WASD and press-to-open

Phone and tablet (899 and below) are built with a flowing layout at the same height instead of the original’s absolute layout from the 375 mockup. Section height matches the original formula (375 proportional + screen height), but element positions inside sections are approximate.

Measured in screen pixels, the gallery/about → first page transition runs through the original’s ”stacked cards” transition (2.4s), then the first page’s mosaic field 3s bounce and 6s photo swap, so it lands at 7.8~8s (original --repeat 3: gallery 7799~7866ms, about 7983~8016ms). The rebuild also bounces the field on the original slatPluck curve and adds the photo swap, so it measures the same shape. But the phase of the field’s 3s tempo depends on the time elapsed after the page opens (the original loads late because its photos are heavy), so where the longest pause lands, and thus the split between leaving and entering, differs from run to run. The ”stacked cards” values (shrink 1.2s · exit 1.2s · start after .9s · .15s late) are the original settings as they are

The phone and tablet scroll motion rows (the original’s 375 mockup absolute layout, scrub, fixed length) could not be matched — the phone layout needs to be redone section by section like the original

title: School project intro with a photo band that crawls and then flips away
good_for: One-page landings for school or foundation projects and donation drives, and photo-rich institutional campaigns.

pages.use: A one-page school project intro — hero with handwritten logotype over a photo, manifesto over video, six rows of photo strips that flick one slot every 7 seconds, two shapes, eight photo cards (tap to open a detail sheet from the bottom), video · graduate interview, donation text and donation footer. Vertical tabs on the right edge (MENU · MAKING-OF)

notes: A one-page site whose subpages weren’t recorded — the card ”SEE MORE” detail is built not as a page like the original but as a single sheet rising from the bottom (.ca-sheet inside index.html). The original has 10 sheets with different content per card — only the number and title are swapped in
The Swiper version number isn’t written in the bundle (judged as 11.x from warning messages · loopAddBlankSlides) so _vendor/swiper@11.2.10 was used
Photo strip cell count is 6~12 instead of the original 16~50 — the minimum that keeps the loop unbroken. Strip curve, length, and spacing are as in the original (crawl-snap-flow)
The original sets autoplay: true on the film slider but loads only the Mousewheel module so it never advances by itself — the copy does not advance either
Menu panel and footer background video stitching: the original switches 1s before the clip ends — the clip length is unknown, so we swap with a .4s overlap every 5s.
English all-caps heading text-box: trim-both is left as in the original (in browsers that don’t support it, a bit more space remains above and below)
The slide viewer iframe in OVERVIEW is left as a same-ratio placeholder (external widget)
The heading gothic (MB31, paid) is backed by Pretendard 600 — its glyphs are wider than a Japanese gothic, so some lines may wrap earlier than in the original
The MAKING-OF photo swap is shown by changing the photo slot label to data-label-b (photo taken by a student).

Font backfill: the only place switched to English is the two cells of the second info line in the film slider (.ca-film__info, original form CONCEPT FILM / Long Ver.(09:07)). The other titles and labels were already English in the original.

Font backfill: counted by the font-family computed in the browser, there are 36 spots where Korean text is drawn in Inter — 17 card and interview hover tags (.ca-hover — the original’s Japanese kana and kanji card titles and interview one-liners), 18 interview name lines (company/title and name — the original’s Japanese company names and kanji names), and 1 footer tax-guide link (original Japanese). All keep Korean and fall back from Inter to Pretendard, which matches the character of the original’s bold gothic heading face.

Font backfill: the remaining 173 lines in latin-slots are false hits. They matched only the trailing chunk (p · h2 · span · text · a) of .ca-movie__info p · .ca-cards__en h2 · .ca-side__menu span · .ca-dg text · .ca-menu__foot a and so caught the same tag across the whole document, and they read the fallback of var(--kf-font-hand, var(--kf-font-display)) as a Latin setting. The actual fonts are Pretendard and Nanum Pen Script, and the original is entirely in Japanese (body · titles · menu panel · the school-name line on the 100th anniversary cover). The handwritten logotype, shape handwriting and photo-swap hint are Japanese or katakana handwriting drawings in the original, so they stay as Korean handwriting.

Font backfill: places where the original English was carried over as is at first build (Change Agent Project·Significance·Evidence·Uniqueness·Entrepreneurial mindset education·The Next Century·OG Interviews, etc.) are not Korean slots but were left in during this backfill — next time, swap them for ordinary English placeholder copy.

title: Service company set led by a crow mascot through an overnight story
good_for: Problem-solving, agency or guarantee service sites that dramatize customer hardship, then lead through resolution steps, numbers, reviews, FAQ and consultation booking.

pages.use: Company home page — a big title that unwinds and descends from a symbol (the last letter drops), a hero where a mascot flies holding a phone and collides with a plane, a 9-screen fixed night-sky story (Lottie crow, alternating titles, volume ticks), a 6-card horizontal rail, info tabs, a pile of review videos, numbers that unwind from a symbol, a logo strip, a try-the-calculation box, and a finish where a circle covers the FAQ.

Team — large centered title, two leaders in magenta large cards, two executives in navy cards, five columns of lime team member cards on black (each column slides at a different speed, with mascot cells mixed in), navy closing panel. At the company’s Team · People menu spot

Learning center · resource library — signup for upcoming lecture alerts (lime panel · crow wearing headphones), FAQ with five category tabs (crow on a pink cloud), a band for consulting on remaining questions. For webinar, resource and help pages

title: Sand drawing sound on a vibrating plate, with a science story and a lab behind it
good_for: Science and research explainer sites, interactive explanations that pair a scroll story with a hands-on experiment lab, and exhibition introductions.

pages.use: Story first page: sound-on gate loader (000 counter, three buttons), big title header, seven chapters whose shape and camera change on a fixed 3D plate behind the screen (text box on the left, chapter dots on the right), a frequency chapter with a response-curve needle, closing and lab button. For a science and tech explainer landing

About — long text column on the left (experiments · physics · reference plate table · sand · imitations · makes · accessibility · sources), pinned panel on the right. For project About, methodology and sources pages

Lab — a full-screen plate, current plate readout at bottom left, control panel on the right (shape, ratio, frequency slider, resonance chips, mode m,n, sign, intensity, noise, sprinkle, strike). For hands-on simulator or settings panel screens.

notes: The frequency sweep (250~2600Hz) does not compute a response curve like the original. It blends logarithmically between our sixteen-step mode ladder. Needle, Hz readout and section figure have the same position and motion. The Hz values in captions are placeholder calculations (64·(m²+n²)).

Two recorded subpages: About (about) and Lab (lab) (number 2 in pages.json is the home page itself). The Figures (/modes) page was not recorded so it is not built, and the header link goes to the modes section of the story. The language switch (EN/BG) is look only

The lab panel wires shape, ratio, frequency, resonance chips, mode (m, n, sign), intensity, noise, scatter and tap into the plate, but fields from the original such as the drive pad, material picker, volume and screen recording are not built

The home page gate appears only once per window, as in the original (sessionStorage). The original’s screen after the gate isn’t in the archived captures, so we entered directly via ‹Start without sound›, shot and compared it (/tmp/lib-brand-plate-experiment-vercel-app-orig-1)

The section 「Symmetry and the push point」 does the push position readout (0,0 → .38,.22), camera (detail) and frequency shift like the original, but it leaves out the calculation where pushing off-center wakes the odd modes and half-breaks the pattern’s symmetry — the original reworks the plate shape from the sum of mode amplitudes at the push point (14th-order coefficients). The next person should add push point weighting to plate.js field

Typeface backfill: since the original text is all English, every slot for the heading typeface (Instrument Serif) was replaced with English placeholder text — wordmark Project, two-line hero title, seven section titles (the right-side section dot names use the same text), closing big title, three-line About page title and seven section names. No heading typeface slot is left in Korean. Header menu, labels, buttons and gate text use Geist and Geist Mono (body and label typefaces), so they stay in Korean

Font backfill judgment: the section titles were Korean renderings of the original words, so to avoid copying the original text, the English is left as placeholder text like ”The First Title” and data-label carries ”Your section English title here”. The hero and seventh section titles have their character counts matched so a single word does not wrap alone onto the next line (Big Headline / Goes Here).

notes: The 3D-scanned pottery (13 GLB files · draco) is replaced by ten basic shapes (capsule · bowl · barrel · flat mask · ring) of the same position and size ratio, wearing a glaze-blotch canvas that mixes --kf-accent-soft · --kf-dim · --kf-raised · --kf-ink-soft instead of the scan texture. The original /series uses only even light (ambient 3) and has shadows baked into the scans, but the basic shapes have no baked shadows, so one upper-left light was added. Whoever plugs in real models can remove that light

The physics is the same rapier as the original (zero gravity·movement damping 4·rotation damping 5·friction 10·ball collider .47·mass .6·per-frame position × −.05 drag·cursor kinematic sphere .2·follow .05), but the build is the already-present rapier3d-compat 0.14.0. Single work detail (/series/darumas/<Artwork> — the DRAG cursor that spins a single 3D object · work list thumbnails · video scene ticks) were not recorded, so they were not built. List cards are kept as photo slots, not clickable, like the original

notes: The neighborhood model (baked-texture glb · Draco) is rebuilt from basic shapes with the same layout and silhouette: a long row of 4-story apartments (boxes + floor band·window·balcony shade shaders), 14 end-wall murals (our own mural atlas drawn on canvas), stair towers, 230 trees (trunk + three icosahedrons), 320 people, 26 cars (moving along the road), 12 birds. Night (uNightMode) is a navy tint + window lights + mural kept, and the old-times mode (uModBeforeAfterProgress) has no mural · olive tone · cars hidden, covering only the same branches — the original window-light mask texture and mural AO lighting are not included

The gateway photo (original aerial photo·video) was replaced with one render of our village from above — the same 1.3s frame shrink (frame-shrink-intro)·1.1→1 scale·text sliding in 400px from left and right are original timeline values. Pressing a pin flies the camera in front of the mural over 4s, and the story panel enters 2s later over 1.5s cubic-bezier(.25,1,.5,1) tilted 10°, with the lines and text inside settling in --delay order (original css values). The flight path curve could not be read from the bundle, so power2.inOut is used

Videos (pin previews, story board videos, video collection) are photo placeholders in the same spot and ratio, with only a play button shape — the original video files are not used. Instead of the original main.mp3, we generate and play a very quiet pink-noise wind sound (sound button)

ROUTES unfolds like the original, the pill expanding into a list of three routes, and picking one flies to that route’s first story — the original’s route-following path panel (#path, a horizontal scroll section) is not in the recording so it was not built. Font backfill: the original is all English, and the places using the title font (Brand → League Gothic) are the story panel big title and the next story line below the panel — both replaced with English placeholder text (Story Name·A short teaser line, data-label). The map (overview) · exhibition sheet photos · news photos are gray placeholders. The original about page throws its own script error on open (appendChild of null) — the copy does not.

The pagination current cell and hover background lay a four-color conic-gradient(--site-mosaic-tile) with the same center/cover in place of the original mosaic art (pagenation_active.svg), so as in the original the background color turns transparent and the art slot moves over .5s.

Individual classes like cn-nav-* and cn-fnav-* on menu and footer links are there because, as in the original (NavItem Home·About…), each link needs its own tag so pairs match in hover measurement — they can be removed when extracting for use.
