title: Modular street furniture page with a letter hero and a route-following map
good_for: Single-page introductions for street furniture, modular or assembled products that come in several configurations, with unit tables, spec tabs, example sliders, drawing downloads and an inquiry form.

pages.use: Product single page — Hero with the product name built from linked benches (slabs drop down to reveal the wordmark behind), a map illustration with text flowing along the road, four layouts (photo parallax · isometric drawing), unit table · three points, spec tabs + photo slider, sixteen-slide combination examples slider, flowing text · photo strip, drawing download accordion row, contact form. For modular product / street furniture introductions

notes: The original is a single page — the three subpages in pages.json are DXF drawing download URLs, which just re-render the same first page, so only index.html was built.

Hero bench lettering (the original is lettering made of photos of a real bench shot from above) is redrawn as new SVG in the same position and proportions — wooden seat (three planks), gray hexagonal base, planter, person seen from above. Letter cell widths (26.98/30.06 · 33.6/19.33/22.88/24.17%) and panel fit (1903:1249, margins 236·116 / 100·100 / 20·100) are original values, and letter stroke coordinates were measured on a 1440 screen and carried over.

The story map (benches, trees, building clusters, crowds) and the path are redrawn as our own SVG. The path curve does not use the original path but a new, similarly winding curve, so where the text flows differs slightly from the original. The flow (-20%→100% 30s, SMIL) and the 9s crowd alternation (1.45/4.4/7.4s) use the original values.
The four layout drawings are made not from the original images but with an SVG generator (index.js PLANS) that stands the floor plans (mm) up in isometric — dimensions are 0000 placeholders.

Spec tab cell counts reduced: seat 2 cells (original 2), base 2 cells (original 4), parts 1 cell (original 3). Cell shape, slider, color swatch and dropdown are the same. The 16 combination examples are stamped out by index.js with the same markup.

Lenis 1.2.3 (duration 2) is enabled, as in the original, only on desktops that are not Mac or phone (Chrome·Edge with a Safari UA mixed in) — default scroll on Mac Chrome. The bundle has no Rellax version string, so 1.12.1 with the same API was used (speed -2 default, photo -4, unit photo 4, point photo 2).

The original’s viewport swap (window 1024~1279 makes width=1280, below 375 use width=360) and body min-width 1250px were not carried over — widths 768~1249 are covered by part of the original 1023px rule.
The contact form does not submit (onsubmit false) — reCAPTCHA, address autofill and required-field validation messages were left out.

The wordmark is SVG text with textLength to fill the header width. The DIN-style letters of the original logo are replaced by the free Barlow Semi Condensed, so letter spacing is slightly wider than the original (placeholder PRODUCT TITLE, 13 characters).

title: Monochrome web studio with drawn grid lines and a hero photo that drops into a cell
good_for: Homepages for web production or design companies, work-focused company profiles and black-and-white typeset service pages.

pages.use: Company home page — grid-line logo loader, hero where a full-screen Work collage shrinks into a slot inside the next section’s big copy, service graphic where three circles gather, reason cards that stick in the center and fade out at .6x, staggered Work cards, two column media, DOWNLOAD·CONTACT panel

About us — intro text on a dark ink panel over background video, three values, a CEO message canvas where logo grains gather, company info table, partner list. For the company intro and CEO message sections

Services — four flow circles, two groups of feature cells in a 4-column grid for what we handle, a dark working flow with a sticky left table of contents (photo · description · chips per section), related work cards. For the service and production process guide
Record list — 6-cell grid (4·2·3·3 columns) of cards filtered by category buttons, on hover they darken and the text rises. For record and case lists
Work detail — title, site URL, full-bleed main screen with a VISIT SITE glass circle, info table and overview, five screen captures, three other works. For introducing a single case

notes: Hero work-collection photos · About section background photo · work card photos are placeholders. The About section background video is a dark gradient placeholder video (media/placeholder-loop.mp4, 8 seconds) newly made with ffmpeg, with the same spot and same playback (auto · loop · muted)

The CEO greeting logo particle canvas was newly written in about.js using the original values (1.18s, delay 0~240ms, mouse 56px/12px) but was not extracted as a part. The hidden trick where clicking the signature seven times flips and reveals the original photo was not built.

The material download, contact and privacy sections and the column outlet (an external site) were not recorded, so only links are provided. Categories in the results list only filter within the same section, as in the original (the original refetches via API, with no spinner while fetching)
Service feature cell icons and flow circle arrows are redrawn as gray shape SVGs of the same size instead of the original artwork

title: Online event landing with a tile countdown and a rising 3D object
good_for: One-page landings for online seminars and conferences covering speakers, timetable and sign-up.

pages.use: Event page: a tile countdown opening and a hero with a 3D object rising while spinning, a sponsor logo strip, a vertical-writing intro (pinned and covered by a five-line band), an oval-window speaker carousel (Next/back cursor), a rising dome schedule and stacking session cards, a registration window opening into an oval, FAQ · overview, and a footer revealed from behind (cursor photo trail). For online event · seminar sign-up pages

notes: 3D object: the original is an inflated satin ”festival” glyph model (GLB 5.6MB). The model isn’t carried over — instead an ”inflated brush-stroke symbol” with the same square silhouette, six strokes whose thickness varies along an arc plus two dots, is extruded with ExtrudeGeometry (10 bevel steps). Material values (roughness .82 · clearcoat .24 · sheen .04 · environment .38), rim light, strong contrast curve, light positions, opening rotation (5.5π·−7.25π·3.5π), breathing (7.2s), cursor tilt (.16·.26) and scroll tilt are the original values. The original three RectAreaLights are replaced by directional lights from the same directions — RectAreaLightUniformsLib is not in _vendor. Some strokes look flat, so a more inflated type (larger bevel thickness and step count) is left for the next person to pick up

Date graphics (original SVG lettering) are set in bold Myeongjo serif text, the header stamp logo, footer and the dark brush-lettering graphic behind the hero are newly drawn as three SVG circles and large lettering

Application form: the original is an external Brand form (now a single line ‹Applications closed›). No form is built, only a one-line notice slot — when a form arrives, pull() in index.js re-measures the first field position and recalculates the height that overlaps the ellipse.

Phone: the original phone’s concept→speaker band transition (mobile-concept-transition) and infinite speaker card cloning were not built. The phone speaker plate is only a horizontal scroll-snap plate with 4s auto advance and dot indicators. The mask on the phone speaker stage (the original phone-only image sp/speakers-subtract.svg) was not built, and only a black stage remains. The phone apply Section has no five bands, just an ellipse opening over a sky gradient background (the original phone’s mobile-application-transition band is left for the next person to continue).

Timetable transition: like the original, a proxy copy of the timetable body is scaled to the same ratio as the DOM and laid over it, then swapped for the real body once everything settles. The original’s lazy image load sync is left out since the copy has no images.
Cursor glow · Next/back pills · photo trail only on devices with a pointer (same as the original)

title: Bright, friendly recruiting site for a play-loving local company
good_for: Graduate and mid-career recruiting sites for regional or store-based companies that show their culture through staff voices and key numbers.

pages.use: Recruit landing: a white block sentence plus a hero of flipping pastel blocks, a playful equation, flowing number cards, an employee quote speech-bubble strip, three diagonal two-color cards, a role model slider, a map pin, a secret consultation strip, employee news, a roundtable slider and a tag cloud. For friendly recruiting landings.

Recruit project intro: project purpose, four members (speech bubble + character drawing), the play equation and list the company talks about, a letter from the recruiter, and four pastel bands for the people we seek. For “About our hiring” and recruiter greeting pages.
About — 11-cell number card grid, flowing employee quotes, president message, company overview table, local activity cards. For About inside a recruiting site

Recruit flow — new grad/experienced tabs, job tabs, numbered flow step pills, a job requirements table, an inquiry box. For recruiting process and requirements pages (the experienced side /process/midcareer-sales has the same form)

Posts by tag — tag title header, 2-column staff news cards (rounded shadowed photo, New star badge, orange title, tag, date, excerpt), pagination. For blog and tag listings (store tag lists share the same form)

notes: The hero uses the original TopMv timeline values as they are — four text groups (height and width 0→1s, x 36·0·−36·−72, SplitText letters .1s·.15 gap, return in place 1s after finishing), eight cells rotateY +=360 turn in .6s with a .1 stagger, a 32s loop (1·3·6·8 at 8s, 2·4·5·7 at 16s — on phone 1·4·6·7 / 2·3·5·8) and per-cell scenes at 0·4·16·20s (play props .5→1·y10 .4s with .2 stagger · text 1.4s later with .12 gaps · worker·notes .2s · work text · back color). Front and back colors are the original values. However, the original differs per cell in prop type and person drawing (glove, bat, note, cake, bike, cloud …), so here each cell is grouped as two props, one person and three notes, and the same props are reused on the back scene

The original illustrations (car, coffee cup, tools, bag, lipstick, clock, vase, phone, key, tire, tent, pin, person) were redrawn as simple SVGs in the same position, size and color feel — fewer prop types and less detail than the original

The menu matches the original OverlayService and OverlayUi values and layout — on press a transparent backdrop (.4s cubic-bezier(.25,.8,.25,1), closes when clicking outside) attaches, and 300ms later on the next frame an orange panel descends from 0 to the full page height (1402px at 1440, 1879px on phone — the 31-line vertical tag list sets the height) in .6s power4.out, and the menu content opens .3s later the same way. The right menu’s fourteen items (28px · 2 lines, three sub-items 24px), the left tags (18px · 2 lines), the logo and the vertical title slot are also original css values. The menu button stays as is and is released immediately on close.

The map is abstract polygons plus pins instead of real regional terrain, and in place of the original scenery and shop art, those panels and pin groups drop in with the original values (from 120px above at .9 scale over 1s bounce.out, shops .3s later, the three people from 60px below at 1.2 scale over 1s power4.out)

The original’s pop-outs are only the Home speech bubble (back.out(1.6) .6s), the magnifier (Home and About, x 100% · 90° → .6s power3.out) and the vase (Projects, y30 → 1s power3.out), so the pop-outs the copy had added to each prop were removed. Prop parallax (data-speed) follows the original LenisService formula exactly

Among sub pages, /process/midcareer-sales (mid-career hiring flow) and /tags/shop_… (store tag list) share the same form, so only one process.html and one list.html were built. The original hiring flow tabs are page navigation, so they switch immediately with no transition
Fonts: Source Han Sans → Pretendard, Brandon Grotesque → Josefin Sans, VDL PenLetter → Gaegu. Logo, photos and text are all placeholders

The top and footer letter strips flow at 80s exactly like the original DecorationTitle, after 1s they appear, each letter is painted a random one of five colors (orange, yellow #ffde00, gray #d6d6d6, #bab9b9, white), then switches to another random color in .2s (random order at .02 intervals), repeating endlessly. Section English titles have no motion, as in the original, with only the first letter of each word in orange (the orange bleed the copy had added isn’t in the original, so it was removed)

Font placeholder text — spots for the original Latin title font (Brandon Grotesque → Josefin Sans) are already English in this copy (section English titles, letter band, Entry, Menu/Tag, New badge, numbers, two-line English logo), so no spots were changed to English

Number card units (persons, hundred-million, years, age, ten-thousand, days, times, minutes) — the original sets kanji units (person, hundred-million yen, year, age) separately in the Japanese body font rather than the number font, Korean kept, and only the unit is switched to the body font (--kf-font-sans)
Logo ‹Brand Recruit PJ› · breadcrumbs — the original is a kana logo, kept in Hangul

The 65 lines remaining in latin-slots.py are checker false positives — because it only looks at the last chunk of the selector `.cr-side a`·`.cr-nav__grp h3` catches every a and h3 (and the text inside) as Latin. Re-measured with the fonts computed in the browser, Korean text drawn in a Latin font is 0 (all of it is button, card and body text that was Japanese in the original)

title: Dot-grid brand company site where stacked headings become a table of contents
good_for: Corporate sites for brands and manufacturers covering philosophy, products and recruiting, and photo-rich black-and-white minimal company profiles.

pages.use: Company first page — full-width wordmark over a 7-photo crossfade, section titles and links stack sticky 70px apart to form the site index while center photos overlap each other at screen center, tree-ring halftone footer. For company homes with five or six menu groups

Philosophy / brand intro — four photos over a square 5-column dot grid (a wide photo opening at half width in the center), a large subtitle stuck to the screen center, concept poem, brand intro, vision, five-item value list, symbol video, related pages. For company philosophy and mission pages

Product line intro: three page-head photos, and for each product row a sticky title + a wide product shot + a narrow shot and a two-line title·paragraph (three rows repeated + one photo-only row). For product groups and business intros.
Recruiting — three page-head photos, a message paragraph and photo, a recruiting requirements table of eleven rows (1/3 item·2/3 content) and an apply link. For company recruiting pages

notes: The original typeface TWK Lausanne (paid) is replaced with Inter Tight, and the Japanese body text with Pretendard as Korean placeholder — Korean titles are shorter than the original Latin titles and differ in stroke, so the grotesque feel is weaker
The logo and wordmark come with a newly drawn dotted ring and 'wordmark.' Replaced with text (fit to screen width via textLength) — so the original symbol is not copied

The growth-ring graphic is not a moved copy of the original halftone SVG (256-cell grid, square dots at 80% of the cell). It is redrawn on a canvas with the same cells and the same dot size. Using error diffusion (checkerboard texture), it stamps the radial density profile measured from the original (.33~.58, outer shell .8~.85), the harmonic components of the outline bumps, and the eccentricity where the upper band is darker. The fine wood grain in the original picture is not matched one by one (the difference that remains unless the picture is copied)

The Philosophy page video ‹Symbol and Cycle› uses a 3:2 · 4.9s placeholder video (media/symbol.mp4), the same as the original (3:2 · 4.9s · autoplay muted loop playsinline · parallax inside the frame), with the same playback behavior and the same parallax. Only the original timeline is carried over (0.13~0.93s eleven dotted concentric rings get drawn · 2.07s center symbol · 2.97~3.93s clears away · 4.4s black symbol on white screen). The rings and symbol are our own.

At phone width the Korean placeholder wraps less than the Japanese body, so the philosophy page is about 150px (two lines) shorter than the original. The careers page at 1440 is also one line (about 280px) shorter than the original
The Company overview, Retailers, Lab, News, Contact and Store pages were not recorded, so the menu links are set to #

title: Company home with a wheel-paged video hero and aurora-lit panels
good_for: Homepages for B2B SaaS or climate-tech companies with product lines, company profile and recruiting.

pages.use: Company first page — a hero that blocks the first wheel and steps through video scenes (three dots show the order), white News cards over an aurora panel, a product screen panel switched by a progress bar, sustainability cards, three overlapping recruiting photos. For a company home that shows its worldview through video

News list — aurora category card that sticks along the body, filter buttons, rows of photo · title · date · category, pagination. For press release and notice lists (the Press Releases section with only the category changed has the same form)

Business intro — header with a left table of contents, aurora header board, 3-column product cards (service site · get-materials pill), two support cards, community posts and images. For service pages of companies with multiple product lines

Company About: aurora philosophy panel (mission, vision and values with line highlights that unfold), CEO message, executive cards that open a side panel when pressed, two-column company overview, and swipeable partner organization cards. For company info pages.

Careers — an aurora message panel with five photos flowing in parallax, code of conduct, recruiting materials pager, employee interview slider (page-count bar), hiring and selection flow, benefits, event report, in-house photo loop slider, FAQ accordion, service site band. For a careers page.

notes: The six hero videos (3D city renders) are placeholder gradient videos (media/kv*.mp4) with the same square ratio, the same lengths (3.37/2.33/3.0/2.33/2.67/2.33s) and the same play order (once → loop, second and third scene transitions) — just swap in the real videos. The original alternative-video still image (for devices that cannot play video) was not built

Page transition: the original c-pageTransition gradient is invalid because of calc(0 + …%), so no veil shows on screen and only subpage links are delayed by .5s — the copy also keeps it as measured (slant-sweep-page veil: off). The 20° slanted veil the code intended is extracted as the part’s default. barba and slick are only loaded by the original and never used, so they are not included.

The dark panels on subpages (news category cards, service head panel, philosophy, recruit message) are still gradients or solid colors, as in the original, the moving aurora exists only on the first page’s news and sustainability panels and the footer and phone menu, as in the original. The category card background image (Side.background jpg) is drawn as a CSS gradient with the same texture.

The recorded Press Release section (news/press-release) has the same form as the news list (only the category filter differs), so it was built as the single file news.html. The sustainability section was not recorded, so its menu link goes to the first-page sustainability card.

Content was reduced — company officers 20+ → 6 officers · 6 advisors, the 9 service product cards are kept as they are, 5 recruit staff interviews · 7 FAQ lines · 4 event reports. The advisor ‹one line + photo› row in the officers panel and the external ‹job details› page for recruiting were not built

The language picker (shutto translation) is only a box open/close (jQuery fadeToggle 400ms). It’s an external translation service, so there is no real translation. The cookie consent window (Product), fixed banner (fixBanner) and the contact widget below are external or ads, so they were not built

The community illustrations (ship and flag) were redrawn simply as SVG in the same position and proportion — the original has few props such as people, wind turbines, and clouds. Service product screens and logos are left as photo slots (cutouts)

Font placeholder text — in the spots where the original used degular (→ Figtree), the copy was almost all English already (section titles, page headers, big Hero title, Scroll, News categories, dates, page numbers, Request documents/Contact us, romanized person names, Q/A, © line). Two spots changed to English: the footer back-to-top button (original Back to Top → `Page Top ↑`, degular 600 so the button uses the title typeface), community name inside the community title (original ”All Aboard!” → ”Group Name!”, a title typeface 1.3 times larger than the title)

Korean kept, in the places where the original used a Japanese sans-serif (Noto Sans JP): the small Hero subtitle · header line / mobile menu · in-page table of contents · Mission/Vision sentences · CEO greeting slogan · executive titles/names · buttons · news titles · the careers flow (Mid-career hiring · Selection flow · Apply…) · FAQ questions · the intro title of the business section (the words GHG and ESG carry .deg, but there was no degular rule there, so it was drawn in the Japanese sans-serif). The paired typeface Figtree ↔ Noto Sans KR (geometric sans ↔ sans) is already loaded

The original recruit page’s three section titles (Message · Recruit Slide · Event Report) have no title slot in the copy — since this is a text-only backfill, no structure was added and they were left out (to do next)

The 119 lines left in latin-slots.py are checker false positives — it only looks at the trailing chunk of the selector `.rj__flow li span`·`.nl__links a`·`.zb-title h2` The same rule catches every span, a and h2 (and the text inside) as Latin. Re-measured with the browser’s computed fonts, the Korean text drawn in Figtree is 0 on all five pages

The original subpages are `sites pull` Because of a name conflict (EEXIST) between this news file and folder it could not be extracted, so I checked against the document in _study/archive/wheel-video-aurora-company/pages.har.zip

title: Advertising agency site with an infinity-orbit loader and huge capital lettering
good_for: Advertising and branding agency sites with services, case work and a news blog.

pages.use: Agency home page — an ∞ orbit loader unfolds into full-screen video with a play button that follows the cursor, a trust statement, lists of brands, services and fields, a draggable news strip, four full-height projects (pill labels), giant three lines + 3D spiky star, people-photo GL stack, award pills. For creative company landing pages
Service list — large uppercase text, a left sticky table of contents (visible service in bold) and eight video cards on the right. For a business and services overview page

Single service — a giant name stuck to the bottom over a full-height video, intro text, a group of things we can do (sticky photo stack), a team drag row, a related-projects drag row. For service and department detail pages
News list — featured post at screen height that swaps every 4 seconds (bar), collapsible All posts filter, four-column masonry cards. For blog and press release lists
One work case — giant title, intro, service/field row, photo stack, pill play button video and photo row, related posts, credits. For a portfolio detail (wrongly captured as about during recording)
Single news item — big title and date, author pill on a 3:2 cover photo, 740px centered column body and credits. For blog posts and press release detail.

notes: People photo GL stack: original transition effect (1500ms linear progress, expoOut in the shader, color distance between two images < It starts changing from the one in progress and covers with pow 5, zoom 0) — rewritten with our own shader. Placeholder sections draw a blurred person silhouette (position and brightness differ per section) on the canvas in the skin variable color so the dissolve is visible

News drag row: the original uses Embla v9 (the version with the startSnap option, dragFree). The library has no v9, so we wired embla-carousel 8.6.0 with the same options (dragFree, duration 25 default) — when someone drops an official v9 into _vendor, just swap it in.

The original behavior is included: opening the search or menu overlay shrinks the page to (width-100)/width with 10rem corners (1000ms outExpo), but the content inside the search panel (search-service results · tabs) is only a placeholder grid — it is a search service, not motion

Compare·interact side-by-side checks were viewed visually only on the first-page scroll (1440·390). Subpages were built from the original prints (archived pages/n.jpg, inner panels so only the first screen was captured) and the SSR document structure. The lower parts of subpages (team·project drag rows, brick card ratios, related posts) match in structure but were not checked against the screen

Font placeholder text: the seven slots of the title font (Roboto Condensed) — home hero·play button (including Play/Pause in JS)·huge three lines, project title, service name, service list heading, menu panel title (shared.js) — were French uppercase in the original, so they were replaced with English placeholder text

Font slot note: the menu, footer, news cards and body text (t-h1-1, t-h3-bold etc.) sit in the body font slot (Inter→Pretendard), so Korean is kept. The original also uses its body font (CossetteTexte) there, so the Latin-only heading font rule is judged not to apply.

Font slot note: the service detail hero name is Service (7 chars), shorter than the original (a single 10-character word) — because at 390 phone width t-big wraps to two lines past 12 characters, unlike the original (one line)

title: Restaurant operator site with a swaying shop-curtain motif
good_for: Company sites for groups running several restaurants or bars, combining shop guides with recruiting in a warm, photo-heavy layout.

pages.use: Company home page — hero with three WebGL curtain panels and a vertical-text menu, intro text over a fixed background video, navy store card slider with a flowing food band, photo-collage company intro, background-fixed careers card, curtain-band blog, tilted photo wall recruiting invite. For the brand home of a restaurant company with many stores

Company About — outlined big title, two photos at the left edge with a vertical-title lead, wide photo band, slogan / reasons to exist (photo and text alternating left and right), two columns of thoughts. For company philosophy and CEO message pages

Store guide — a navy list that sticks and follows, lighting up the current store, for each store, a photo reaching the left edge with an overlapping white card·address·map·flowing dish strip. For guiding multiple stores·branches

Careers — header text, photo banner leading to numbered pages, wide photo strip, job requirements table with three tabs, training program cards, invitation to join. For the first page of recruiting info.

Company in numbers — line icons and six big-number cards · age group bars · dotted list of hiring routes · benefits cards · two columns of text and photo. For the recruiting By the Numbers and company overview pages
Blog list — curtain-strip title · underlined category tabs · three-column photo cards · round page numbers. For company blog and news lists

notes: Curtain: switched to curtains.js 8.1.6, the same as the original (_vendor newly added, MIT) — a screen-fixed canvas with a Plane (60×60·watchScroll·drawCheckMargins 0) for each .cc-curtain, with the original vertex formula (top edge hanging·cos wave·z/30·x spread) and lighting formula (.35 shade) rewritten in our own code and attached. Intensity follows a random target per frame, with per-screen-width caps and damping (.5/.004 … .08/4e-4), like the original. The original mouse position is always (0,0), so it was left as is. The cloth image (a photo in the original) is redrawn on canvas: fabric base read from the skin color, weave pattern, uneven hem, logo-spot circle and stamp. The original’s title overlap image (titleSampler) is not included.

The shop card slider is the same Splide as the original (drag free · gap 40 · autoWidth · arrows, destroyed at 767 and below) and the arrows are also made by Splide (filled chevrons) with the original values (41px · background/fill .5s) applied. The food and dish strips are a Splide loop + AutoScroll (speed .5 · .3, does not stop on hover, gaps 30/25/20 · 10). The Splide build inside the original bundle carries no version string, so the latest 4.x (4.1.4) and AutoScroll 0.5.3 were used

Lenis is 1.0.10 (@studio-freight/lenis, lerp .2), same as the original. The package has no LICENSE file, so following the README’s MIT notice I included the MIT text from the same project’s 1.0.18 release. The original bundle’s barba 2.9.7 is unused because the deploy setting (PUBLIC_ENABLE_BARBA) is off, so it is not included. The page transition moves a single curtain by hand like the original (starts after window load).
The big hero copy (SVG letter shapes in the original) fits the original width (1313px) with SVG text via textLength, and on phones vertical writing is done with HTML vertical text standing two lines

The fixed background video is set to autoplay, loop and no sound, as in the original. Its content is our placeholder video (media/bg-loop.mp4, 1280×720, 12-second loop, faint light slowly circling over a dark base) — the original video in the archive is a partial download (no moov) so its length could not be measured, and 12 seconds was used. It stops under reduced-motion settings

The nav swirl mark·brush stroke are painted with a mask + Skin colors (--kf-accent·--kf-ink) instead of colors inside the image. Blog cards·footer logo links turn #46505d right away like the original global rule (a:hover, a:active, a:focus), and the footer logo’s round border sits on the inner mark so the link’s own border color follows the text color

Of the original eight menu items, pages we did not build (Cuisine, Company Info, Notices, Contact) link to the nearest page of ours (Store, About, Blog, Recruitment Guidelines). Company Info, Cuisine, Contact and article detail pages were not recorded in the archive, so they were not built (the article detail thumbnail-sync Splide is therefore absent too)
The original shop info repeats eight entries in the same form — only three are kept, and the list has six slots. The map is a placeholder instead of an iframe
The six number icons (line drawings) of the original number page are simple line icons redrawn at the same size (90px) and stroke weight
The original recording categorized the number page as detail and the shop page as product, but they were corrected to recruit and page according to their content
The five subpages were checked at 1440 and 390 for 0 console errors and 0 horizontal overflow, and motion measurement and interact comparison against the original were done for index only
Logo, photos and text are all placeholders (even the text in the logo circle is COMPANY NAME)

title: Character and regional craft collaboration page with a speech-bubble wordmark and region-colored pinned panels
good_for: Brand landings for character, regional and craft collaboration products, with volume-by-volume product sets and pop-up shop notices on one page.

pages.use: Collaboration project one page — opening curtain where a scattered collage lights up and folds, speech-bubble wordmark Hero and flowing collage panel, three region cards, three product features, product issues (vol.) and product cards passing by with panels painted per region attached, pop-up shop notice, wordmark band Footer. For character and regional collaboration product landing pages

notes: The original is a single page (pages: [] in pages.json), so there are no subpages. Product cards and View Detail are links out to an external online store in the original, so they are changed to same-page anchors.

The card’s tech.libs lists lottie, but the original page does not use Lottie (only an import slot in the STUDIO bundle), so lottie-web is not included. notes: The text band is, like the original, one three r180 plane plus our own shader — band length units .02 per second, wheel speed 5e-5×deltaY per second (±2, damping 12), 5×5 grid (movement×10, radius .22, .965 per frame, push 1 = 3% of the band, nearest cell value), letter spacing .025, zoom .9, colors take the skin values as linear as is (the original also passes srgb-linear so hex values come out unchanged). The original GPGPU grid computation is 5×5, so it is stacked on the CPU with the same formula and passed as a DataTexture.

The colophon and paragraph text are also GL planes in the band scene like the original (desktop, with a mouse). The colophon is baked to canvas per character and the paragraph per line, and they take the same grid displacement at plane uv unit .2. Plane = Fragment box + left/right .12× font size, top/bottom max(0,(font size − box height)/2)+.15× font size · line .3× font size (original values). For the entrance, the plane reads the yPercent of the SplitText fragments (115→0, same length and stagger), so the text rises from below inside the plane — the original’s uv.y += Same shape as (1−reveal). The large About header paragraph is the same. The DOM text stays transparent so reading and selection work as before.

The original stencil logo is not used. Instead ABC is drawn in Archivo 900 (width 125, the skin’s --kf-font-mark) with two thin gaps cut through it to hint at a stencil feel. The About header band reads ABOUT. To change the logo, edit WORD in shared.js and the gap positions in makeGlyph.

The loader has the same values and structure as the original: one GL plane per letter panel, three letters gather from gap 5.5 to .025 in 1s expo.inOut, after .8 they fill for 1.5s from the bottom of the panel with an edge of ±.02 (unfilled areas .15), and at .8+.05i they rotate vertically in 1.5s expo.inOut to become the strip slots.

Library cards are also a GL plane in the band scene like the original (card size 32×32 cells) — by the pull (target minus current, ±1.2, following by .15 each frame) the vertical center bends (x −= sin(v·π)·.12pull·.3, y += sin(v·π)·.06pull·.1, original screen units = screen height/.8284) spreads 10 points in the same direction (max .1). A .1 white frame around the edge. The wheel/list view toggle uses the original _setView at 1s with CustomEase(.6171,.109,0,.9953). Photos use label-drawn placeholder panels as textures.

The footer letter pile uses the same matter-js 0.20.0 and the same numbers as the original (50 letters, 30 on phone, .1s apart, letter = width/20.5 · phone /9, Body = image .9× rectangle with .15 corner chamfer, restitution .7, gravity 1, wall thickness width×10, each frame 1000/60ms, mouse radius 1.5 letters pushes .025×mass×(1−d/R)). Instead of the original’s three letter image PNGs, three Skin-font glyphs are drawn on a canvas.

Of the original’s per-section theme transitions, the page-wide switch driven by scrolling is left out — each section carries its own background. The nav is white text + difference blend as in the original, so it automatically turns black, dark gray or white depending on the background (only this white is a value outside the skin — difference blend needs white to invert the background).

The About page is a bit longer than the original (7558px) because of a difference in line count in the Korean placeholder. The photo in the Usage section wraps the text with shape-outside below the third line.
The meaning of the section-header mark (solid dot + numbered ring) couldn’t be read from the original, so only the shape was carried over.

notes: The 3D world is rebuilt from basic shapes instead of the original glb models (rule: no model files) — it has the character, tent, stall, lantern, campfire, trees, stepping stones, pond, work screen, easel and cabin, but lacks small props like the new bird feeder, kite, clothesline and flags, and the original character’s refined walk animation (only arm and leg swinging).

Physics uses the same rapier kinematic character controller as the original (capsule radius .35 · height 1.8, sliding) so the player cannot pass through props. The original also uses the automatic collision of @react-three/rapier (a cuboid per shape at its own size and orientation), and this copy blocks with the same box for each prop shape. The terrain and path shapes that the original worker (worldShapes.worker) extracts separately are not in this copy (flat things under 25cm tall, leaves and flames can be walked over). Jumping and falling use the existing height formula (ground height + jump velocity) rather than rapier, so you cannot stand on top of objects. You cannot go beyond a 27m radius.

The name letters do not use the original typeface file (typeface.json). Instead, the outline of text drawn on a canvas in the skin’s --kf-font-wordmark (Lilita One, free) was traced and extruded into 3D. Lilita One has no Korean glyphs, so the placeholder is 10 Latin letters, SAMPLENAME — just change WORDMARK in index.js. If the font does not arrive within 2.5s, it is extruded with the skin’s next font.

The original ”View Work” opens an in-world work panel, but here it links to works.html. ”Contact” is a simple contact card instead of the original letter-writing panel. The night ”Resting by the fire” letterbox scene and the sunshine and raindrop decorations that pop when the weather switch is pressed were not built.
The graphics buttons (High, Medium, Low) only change the pixel ratio, grass count and shadows. First-person has no head bob.

The credits button is bottom 22px in the original, but the library’s shared List·Notes button covers that spot, so it was raised to 62px (on phones it stays above the jump button, as in the original).

In the original, the work cards play video in place on hover — this is done by having the video slot (wf-video) appear over the photo slot. The paper dart cursor was drawn anew (it is a cursor image, so its white body and ink outline do not change with the skin).
The original’s flat board shown when WebGL is unavailable (boot-fallback) was not built.

title: Scroll-story agency pinning one screen for a very long stretch to wind through five scenes
good_for: Agencies whose scroll choreography is the product, product reveal microsites and explanatory story pages.

pages.use: Agency home — a hero with a ritual stage lighting up, then a scroll story on a one-screen pinned stage: head parting, hourglass ring, white-world binary rain, falling and snow, ending in applause, closing with a purple eclipse ring and three-way buttons. For landing pages that show off scroll choreography
What we do — brass title · two-line intro · three animated icons, gothic quote and three explanations on a red band. For service and principle intros
Work list — brass title and one-line intro, 16:9 cards whose scene spins on hover, newsletter signup. For case and demo lists
Contact — brass title, call button and one-line email at the center of the letter board (spirit board), newsletter signup. For a playful contact page

notes: All the original illustrations are Rive (.riv) canvases: ritual stage, splitting head, hourglass, falling person, hand, accessibility figure, small icon, scene card. Since a new .riv can’t be authored, they were redrawn with our own SVG (some canvas) and GSAP at the same position, size and timing. Fine motion inside the Rive art (the head’s matryoshka breakup, the person’s arm and leg movement, the fingers in the clap) was reduced to moving and rotating whole chunks.

Stage length and scene timing are the original values as they are — temple fixed 1000px, stage fixed 29560px (header share 3000px, hourglass timeline starts at 80% of the header share), timeline points 1.5 (text rise)·3.6 (green fill)·4.2 (drain)·4.65 (center burst)·5.15~10.15 (white world, binary rain)·11.15 (fall)·13.95 (single word)·26.65 (star field)·27.85 (brass)·31.15 (handwriting)·36.45 (eclipse)·39.45 (end). The eye-opening time (19.95~20.65), the hand-rising length (3.5s) and the clap flash happen inside the original’s Rive, so they are guesses fitted by eye.

The original SVG displacement filters (hourglass static, center warp, fall-in warp — shaking the feTurbulence seed every .14s) were not ported. The center hourglass instead grows to 1.25x over the same 3s power1.in.

The original accessibility settings (turn off all motion · scroll motion → saved to localStorage, then reload) and the Scene Player (a panel that steps through scenes with play · previous · next buttons instead of scrolling) only have the window switch shapes, with no function. Turning motion off is handled only through prefers-reduced-motion (only the final eclipse scene stays).

In the original, one card in the work list (death-scrolls) leads to a detail page (temple-of-doom), but that detail was not recorded so it was not built — the card links to the newsletter signup on the same page. The signup and call buttons do not submit.

Fonts: Girthy (paid, very wide black) → Archivo expanded 125·900 + Korean Black Han Sans, Aesteric (paid gothic display) → Grenze Gotisch (--kf-font-gothic), Satoshi is the same. The hero title is set at 187px so the two English lines match the original width (717·866px on a 1440 screen), and the second-line baseline (442) and the red X (center 800,322) are aligned to the original positions (for Korean: 215px · 500 · 365).

Font backfill — since the original is entirely in English, 28 spots that use the Latin title fonts (Archivo · Grenze Gotisch) (the same headline or window counts once) were replaced with English placeholder text and given data-label: the words above and below the logo (BRAND · STUDIO, four sections), three menu items (the phone drawer uses the title font — on wide screens it is the body font, but since it is the same element they change together), the titles of the guide and motion-settings windows, two big temple title lines and one red Gothic line, five scene titles, the meetup title, three sub-section titles, three service names, the principles section title, three Gothic quotes (two lines each, as in the original), and the News signup title (two lines). Korean kept 0.

Body font (Satoshi → Pretendard) slots stay Korean even where the original is English — header icons, buttons (char-roll), small labels, body paragraphs, Yes, No and Hello on the soul panel (db-small), card scene names, footer. The scene description not visible on screen (h2.d-sr) is also kept Korean. Button aria-label (guide, motion settings) stays as is, since the probe accept notes it in writing.

The 44 lines left in latin-slots.py are matched by the regex `.d-tenet__quote p`·`.d-modal__head h2`·`.d-converge__text h2` …’s trailing chunk p · h2 was a false positive from reading every p · h2 — in headless I checked the computed typeface of every text node containing Korean on four pages at 1440 · 390, and Korean drawn in Archivo · Grenze Gotisch is 0.
The page-turn blood pour effect is applied only on wide screens (1020px and up) as in the original. The phone menu uses the same pour at .85s.

notes: The seventeen isometric illustration Lottie slots keep the same lottie-web as the original (autoplay, loop), the same canvas size, and the same length (e.g. 3.33s·4s·2.4s), but the art is a block Lottie we baked ourselves (media/*.json — a block on a plate floats up and settles, baked with media/lottie_gen.py). So that it shows even when opened via file://, the same JSON is held in media/lotties.js and loaded as animationData, and the marker colors (blue·white·black·gray-blue) are repainted to --kf-* after drawing. The original’s per-scene motion (paper flipping·target·scale etc.) could not be carried over — a task for the next person to bake per-scene JSON like lottie_gen and continue.

The stack’s white panel drawing uses the same ranges as the original MorphSVG·DrawSVG timeline (section 0~20·20~40·40~60·60~80%, scrub) and the same curves (none·power2.out·back.out(2)·back.in(2)·back.out(1.5) at .012 spacing·back.out(1.7)), but the paths are our own panel·five pillars·decor lines·twelve bumps·cube (the original path coordinates are not used). The original pillar labels (vertical text) and updatePillars, which re-joins the pillar lines to the panel shape, were trimmed down.

The hero canvas (dash-chain-flow) follows the original values (1440×842 cover · dash 30/3.75px · .7 cells per second · 6 highlights 1.2s · top and bottom 20% muted). The line shape is twenty-two elliptical arc strands in a ”(” shape instead of the original coordinates.
The maker-side hero canvas (dash-column-rise) follows 3 groups × 14 lines · dash 21/10 · top 40% hidden · draw 2.5s · blue 5%, and leaves out the original’s lift from the center and duplication flow.

The end-panel vertical line (balloon-line-press) presses with the original values (radius 140 · min .4 · follow e^−8dt · light blob 280/110 · e^−6dt), but unlike the original, instead of finding convex segments in the line path, it presses with bars drawn separately for each node.

Big title section block drop and the writing-side cylinder fall use the original fall distances (532·187 / 929·819·199) and curves (power2.in · top bottom → center 40%), but the cylinder is in our own drawing coordinates, so the distance ratio is kept and scaled down by .548.

The logo strip (continuous carousel, where the cell nearest the cursor lifts 1.25em) is hidden (hdn) on the original first page, so it was not built. Not carried over: the tick-arc bump on the writing side (initTickRotation), the text list in the learning row, and the real figures of the token page graph (the graph is a static placeholder of the same shape).
TWK Everett and Everett Mono are paid fonts, so they were replaced with Geist and Geist Mono. Korean placeholder text uses Noto Sans KR, so text widths differ from the original English.

The original button text roll (textStagger, SplitText words · second copy of the text 1.25em below) was attached to the char-roll part by adding a by: word option with the same values (.2s · .02 stagger · 0.65,0,0.35,1).

Section title appear (original initTextReveal — per line yPercent 100 · rotateX −45 · perspective 600 · .937s suiEase .08 stagger · top 85%) was attached by adding a tilt option to the line-rise part. The number panel (original initInfoCount) uses a per-slot number strip roll (.9s power3.out · .04) as site code, and the description text scramble (1.6s from the beginning) is attached with the text-scramble part. Scrambling characters are not painted blue as in the original, and the ones overlapping the option separator ; : was removed from the shuffled characters.

Accordion items inside the maker tab (original global-tab-dd), filter buttons, partner cell flip and last-card arrow swap are built with the original CSS values (.2s·.25s·.4s). Subpages have fewer cells than the original (12 project cells etc.), so the pages are a bit shorter.

pages.use: Single-page event site: black curtain intro, background video inside a white frame (sound button), story section ringed by spirit illustrations, two rows of experience cards that raise a video curtain when pressed, venue, sister-event square cells, organizer intro, credits and contact button. notes: lottie in the card’s tech.libs was a false detection (a video-player bundle). The original is just jQuery 3.5.1 plus hand-written class toggles. Judging that jQuery is not a hands-on-feel library like those in the README list of ones to use the same way (slide, slider, smooth scroll, Lottie, WebGL), it is not included, and the same values were done with GSAP and CSS (anchor move swing 2000ms = sine.inOut 2s, same pattern).

The festival spirit illustrations (four original 3D render pngs — left 324×494 · right 280×540 · bottom 992×384 · phone 670×452) are redrawn as our own shape SVG symbols (stone spirit · lion mask · sun baby · fox-mask spirit · goblin · bird mask · small goblin · crane · giraffe · musician) with the same position, size and silhouette ratio <use> Built with it. Colors are --site-fig-* values rotated from gold. No render texture or fine patterns.

Video: the three original YouTube iframes (hero background muted auto-loop, phone intro video panel, experience video panel) are replaced by placeholders of the same position and size <video> Left as a placeholder (media/loop-16x9.mp4, 16:9 10-second loop). What used to load a different video id per experience card is now the same placeholder replayed from the start, and the video player’s control bar is replaced with the browser’s default controls.

The intro counts on window.onload like the original (index.js sets data-fx at load="logo-blur-loader" …is added) — the original has a lot to download, so load is late (DCL 904ms · load 1951ms at headless 1440) and the sentence inside the curtain appears that much later. Adding the phone photo transition at the intro end (load+4s) and returning to the top is also as in the original.

fade-up: the original fadetext.js checks the line (250px below the screen bottom) only on scroll events, so a block already inside the line on load shows only after one scroll, but the copy (ScrollTrigger) shows it at once. There are no such blocks in the 1440 and 390 hero, so there is no visible difference.
The original main.js bgBlur (adds a class to the phone slider after scrolling past 5px) has no matching CSS rule, so nothing changes on screen — not ported.

Text: the event name·1→10·sister-event logos and wordmarks are replaced with English placeholders (PROJECT·Logo) and our own shape sentences, and the unique series section name is changed to PROJECT SERIES NAME. STORY·CONTENTS·VENUE·ABOUT·CREDITS are section names commonly used on event pages, so they were left as they are. The Japanese body text is replaced with Korean placeholders matched to the original line count (document height at 1440 is the same, 8042, while 390 is 8101 against the original 8176 — a difference in line wrapping of the Korean placeholders).

Swapped theme.css between the dark skin (circuit-board) and the light skin (clay-toy) and captured both to confirm no original gold, black or white remains (the spirit illustration colors also follow the accent color).
The nav item name JAPANESGUE (typo in the original) was set to SERIES.

good_for: Full sites for long-established food, drink or lifestyle brands with product list, product detail, business customers, news and company history.

pages.use: Brand front page — three-video progress bar slider, random swap of four glass cells, scroll-speed product band, old photo loops hanging on strings, journey capsule line, two people-photo bands, two culture spots, bag tunnel quiz, news cards, line-art sustainability section, video before sticky footer and glass footer

Product list — large centered title, five category chips, four-column product grid (hover scale 1.025x, button floats up), See more for each category, spinning quiz badge at bottom right. For stores or makers with dozens of products

Single product — Hero where a package illustration blooms on a black panel · intensity badge · ingredient block · concentric sensory chart (tabs) · slice-panel photo wheel · preparation step cards · related products. For product detail and menu detail slots

Enterprise business intro — video hero · three cards · four-line support · two-layer piece panel (hover) · three pinned machines (number and name roll to change) · slanted-photo partners · News cards. For B2B, wholesale or supply pages
News list — full-bleed featured news slider (small image slots), big title with category chips, three large centered cards, press list rows, story cards. For magazine and press release list spots

Company history book — scattered giant serif hero, oval frame opening to the screen edges, giant year opening each chapter, torn paper spread, pinned year scale, fact slider tabs, polaroid articles, mosaic portraits, quote. Each chapter has its own background color, with the current chapter at bottom right and the table of contents at bottom left. For an old company history or founder story slot.

notes: The original uses Rive (@rive-app/webgl2 2.35.2, MIT) to animate the sound and globe icons and the product detail Hero packaging graphic (product-header-default-intro.riv). The .riv file is an original asset so it cannot be used, and there is no editor to make our own .riv, so the runtime is not shipped. The sound button is an SVG wave (1.2s sway), and the detail Hero is 46 SVG leaves, flowers and fruits blooming from the center outward over 1.2s power3.out, with the same position, size and timing. If we make our own .riv, put the runtime in _vendor at the same spot and swap it in.

The business page type panel·detail sensory profile slice panel are Chart.js donuts in the original (inside the bundle, MIT). Only interaction (slice fills cream·photo 1.1x .3s) and photo rotation (−20°→20°, yPercent 40→−40 scrub) are used, so they were redrawn as SVG slices (DC.pie) — the donut animation (Chart.js default radius expansion) is absent.

Video slots (three in the hero, journey, before footer, machine smoke, detail prep) are placeholder boxes of the same ratio. The hero progress bar length follows the original rule (video length, max 15s) via data-dur=Set to 15 — change it to the real length once the actual video is in.

The original history page has nine sections and is 78,551px tall. Every section type is kept (giant opening year, torn paper spread, year scale, fact flip, polaroid article, mosaic, quote), but the section count is cut to three (about 15,000px). The background color changes between brown, reddish brown, teal, olive and dark brown at .8s per section.

For photos hanging on a rope, the original pins photos on points of two rings, outer and inner, and draws ropes from the ring points to the photos. Our part (rope-hang-photos) hangs the photos like a clothesline by chaining angles from photo to photo so it fits any layout — the sway values (spring 640 · damping .55 · wind amplitude 10~19) and the hand tilt (±6°, .64s/.44s) are the same.
For scroll speed, the original uses Lenis velocity (px per frame). The band part makes the same unit from ScrollTrigger velocity ÷ 60 (playback rate 1 + |v| × .15, max 4.5).

For page transitions the original grows the new page’s first section inside Nuxt from an 80px triangular clipPath at the header logo spot (power2.inOut 1s × timeScale .75). Ours are static pages, so the outgoing page blurs out in .5s and, after navigating, the arrived page’s first section opens with a triangular polygon clip-path of the same values.

Fonts: the original Trade Gothic Bold Condensed (paid) is replaced with Barlow Condensed, and the original-only variable font Season (SERF axis) is replaced with Hanken Grotesk and IBM Plex Sans KR on the sans side, and Newsreader and a Korean serif face on the serif side. Korean narrow caps use Do Hyeon, so they run wider than the original and line counts may differ.

Typeface backfill — the original is an English site, so every Latin typeface slot (Barlow Condensed·Newsreader) was swapped to English placeholder text with data-label added (no Korean left): sixteen narrow uppercase big headings and the small serif words inside them (dc-pair ”pair” → short words like the·of·from·to), section names (Products·Journal Title), product names (seven in the first-section strip·twenty-four in the list·four in the detail), product groups·five categories·ingredients·three steps·origin flavor text, the two-line detail product name and one type line, every about serif slot (three hero words·photo caption·spread title·three fact titles·article title·person name·big quote down to the fourth line·long quote), six phone menu items and the footer’s heading-typeface slots (column heads·six uppercase links·three phone accordions·three contact columns·outbound button·bottom line) — the footer and phone menu are drawn in shared.js so they appear on all six pages. Big headings that wrap onto more lines at phone width (390) because English is longer than Korean (home story·closing, detail taste heading — 210px block width on phone, about big quote·article title, closing headings) were shortened to match the Korean line count. The Hero (loader text·hero scene title·header line) is a body-typeface slot and its text is unchanged, so thumbs were not retaken.

Judgment: the long quote on about (dc-h5, about eight lines) is also English Season serif in the original and drawn with Latin Newsreader in the copy, so it was changed to English placeholder text. The README’s ”body is Korean” applies only to the body typeface slot (Hanken Grotesk → IBM Plex Sans KR), so the header row’s center menu (the probe accepts it by the ”Menu n” text and width), mega menu, dc-m step titles, body, buttons, news cards, record rows and section markers were left in Korean.

/  The 6 lines left in latin-slots.py (two detail rounded certification ring textPath, index journey ring steps 1~4 SVG text) are ones the regex `.dc-logo text` …’s trailing chunk text read as every SVG text is a false positive — the actual typeface is the body Hanken Grotesk (.dt-badge text · .dc-cycle text), and I checked the computed typeface of text runs containing Korean in headless on all six pages at 1440 and 390, finding 0 Korean glyphs rendered in Barlow Condensed · Newsreader.

Product-specific colors in the product band, quiz bags and detail packaging art are made by rotating the accent color wheel in 52° steps (they change along with the skin). To use a fixed color per product like the original, put the color directly in place of the cell’s --n.

A long first-visit loader (holds 5s) and a short return loader (.7s nav · .9s hole expand · 1.1s menu items) are split using the original menu code values — the first-visit record is in sessionStorage (the original uses menu-intro-played in storage).

On the detail page, the picker button beside the product name (original dropdown-btn) has only its hover interaction built (background scales .93 over .45s back · arrow slips upward over .675s quart.inOut) — the product list that opens on click does not exist.

During the first-visit loader the center nav takes no hover, so the nav rising as the curtain lifts does not move pills or sub-panels when it sweeps under a motionless hand. The curtain itself does not block the hand, so the page below (e.g. pressing a first-page scene cell) still responds meanwhile (same as the original).

People · giants · coins do not use the original glb (characters · walk/run animation · giant leg rig · props) — our basic shapes only match the same silhouette proportions. The Hero video is a placeholder video with the same ratio and length as the original — media/mv-pc.mp4 (16:9) and mv-sp.mp4 (9:16) 22.02s (original 60fps, placeholder 30fps). Like the original it uses autoplay, muted, loop and playsinline and calls play after loading, and if autoplay is blocked it plays again on the first touch or press. Layout also follows the original values (PC width 177.78vh, height 56.25vw, centered, phone 100dvh×9/16, minimum 100vw×16/9). With reduced motion set, it stops on the first frame.

Skin: the photo-slot colors (tone-*), map land, sea, olive regions, the gray behind video and the teal bloom are built from oklch relative formulas on --kf-bg and --kf-raised (shared.css --site-*) so the original values come out unchanged in this skin — swap to another skin and they follow with the same brightness ratios and hue spacing. White text over photos and video uses --kf-on-accent, and the cover curtain is 60% and 30% of --site-black, which is --kf-ink lowered all the way to the floor. We captured before and after the skin cleanup at 1440 full page, menu, drawer and map and confirmed the pixels match (at 390 only a few points of text-edge blur differ)

The small subtitles beside section names (.eb-sub, .eb-find__name-sub, ”Subtitle”) stay in Korean. The raster mode, where in a Chrome that supports HTML-in-Canvas the original captures the whole page as a texture, bends it into a barrel shape and maps input coordinates back, is a browser experimental feature so it was left out.

The mouse push of the particle portrait (dash-field-morph) takes only the strength, using the same speed filtering (700px/s·18/5), instead of the original fluid grid (velocity field, pressure solve), and pushes directly within a 120px radius. Portrait and work images are photo slots, so they are left as clothing-color canvas drawings (half-body, waving pose, etc.) — drop in cut-out photos as the data-label says and the strokes stand up with the same values.

To match the original 17 cards to the screen spacing (neighbor card centers ~450px), they were duplicated up to 48 (guess).

The loop flow in list view is a .8s power3 follow. The one-slot advance in gallery view (.8s power3.out) and the skewY -12° tilt are values that could not be read from the original bundle and were matched by eye (guess). The next-work strip’s progress ranges in the detail page (gather 0~.6·name .22~.72·intro .55~.9) read only the original projectNext’s titlePresence (.22~.72), and the rest were fitted by eye on screen. Gallery dots·preview·light pillar use the original values (dots 8/5px .3s power2.out·per section max(320, screen×.8)·light 120px·shade .5)

With text-on-path at startOffset 28%, the oval ring passes inside the lower-right corner of the pill so the start of the text turns into white text on a white pill and disappears — it is a ring-shape issue that sat in the same spot with the Korean placeholder text and is independent of text length, so it was left alone.
