title: Theme park page with icon navigation and numeral-marked category rows
good_for: Facility homepages for theme parks, tourist spots, museums, or hot spring towns that lay out sights, experiences, food, hours, and tickets on one page.

pages.use: Facility home — a video hero with a corner panel for opening hours and tickets, a row of recommended cards, three intros·map·FAQ, five category rows with vertical kanji-numeral labels, an ink-dark street band with flowing photos, a magazine and step-by-step guide booklet, a band of draggable hashtag circles, notice tabs, and group info. For theme park·tourist facility homes

notes: The original is a single page (pages: [] in pages.json) so there are no subpages. Menu and footer links connect to same-page anchors.

The hero video is two gray placeholder videos of 12s with the same ratios (media/hero-pc.mp4 · hero-sp.mp4) in place of the original video-site embeds (PC 16:9, phone 9:16, different videos). They loop silently on their own, and when the width changes, the video for that width is swapped in after 200ms, as in the original. The 20% dark curtain on top and the wordmark also follow the original.

Of the five category rows, the overseas visitor row (u-global) is a group the original shows only to guests arriving in a language other than Japanese. The recording is the Korean version, so it is kept as is.

The final ‹View results› button of the Guide Booklet slot calls the plan API with the chosen answers and goes to the results page in the original, but here it is an anchor (the 1s expo.out step transition is the original value).

The original magazine logo and the handwritten guidebook title are lettering images, so they are replaced with a square stamp SVG + placeholder text, and the guidebook title uses --kf-font-hand (Nanum Brush Script) instead.

Also, the paper-grain texture on the street band uses an SVG noise filter multiplied in, instead of the original image. The band background color is --site-edo, made by rotating lightness and hue from --kf-contrast-bg.

Language switching (a third-party translation service) only opens and closes its list. The notice modal opens in the original only when a notice has modal:true in its data, there was none at recording time, so it was not built.
The original SNS icons are trademarks, so they were redrawn as generic shapes (camera, X, circle, note, play) at the same size and position.

Access map place names: the original map images use Latin text (Cormorant) such as City·City St.·District, so the wide map is replaced with PLACE 01~03 and the close map with Place Name 01~03 English placeholder text. What goes in is set by the figure’s data-label.

Guidebook name (.ez-annai__name) — in the original it is Japanese handwritten graphic lettering (Brand Guidebook), Korean kept here. The font is --kf-font-hand (Nanum Brush Script), which draws Korean as is — a false positive where latin-slots caught the --kf-font-display fallback value of var().

Two ”Back” buttons (.ez-annai__back) in the guide steps. The original reads Back in Japanese kana, but the Korean label is kept. The title font Cormorant is already paired with Noto Serif KR (serif ↔ Myeongjo) in theme.css.

title: Space design company with an eyed number mascot and a cylinder gallery
good_for: Homepages for space, interior, or regional business companies, and bright company intro and recruiting sites with a mascot character.

pages.use: Company home page — a loader (digits rolling per slot plus an 8 character), a big three-line slogan, and a tilted oval cylinder (WebGL, wrapping in front of and behind the title) carrying line-drawn script words and 9 videos, brand copy painted line by line where the emphasized line is written out by a pen-hand Lottie, a boundary covered by rotating blocks and a catch line that rolls out like a slot machine, a fixed WebGL gallery of 13 services laid out horizontally and curving at the screen edges, four white intro cards whose titles flip on the x axis, a recruiting band with four photo pillars flowing along a horizontal-axis cylinder in WebGL with line-drawn script and a Lottie, and three news cards. Suits the first screen of a company with many lines of business.

Service list — white header panel (title rolls out like a slot machine) · large text band pushed by scroll (an 8 that tilts with speed) · 2-column service cards with a large title over a photo (10 ink-black cards that pop up on appearing, and ”MORE DETAILS” rolls again on hover) and directly operated services (3 on a white background). The service menu spot for companies with multiple businesses · services

About the company — after an intro (two small photos fly down), a stage pinned to the screen where photo stacks slide per column and a 4-sided drum title rotates, switching between four branches: promise · history · group · regions. A bundled panel. On the company About first page (the entrance to the sub-About pages)

Recruiting home — intro text and flying-in photos, drum title (English and Korean, two lines) rotating through a bundled panel that switches between three tracks: new grad, experienced, part-time. Then 3-column employee story cards, event cards, apply button box. For a recruiting site entrance

Careers branch detail — recruiting message and business intro with a tilted photo strip, job rows that fill with color on hover, staff cards, base intro with a photo-stack flip, sticky ‹Who we want› color cards that stack up, requirements table, hiring process steps, events, apply. For graduate and experienced hire requirements pages.

News list — big two-line heading, blue band of category pills (sticks on top and follows, tap to filter), white panel with 3-column cards (on hover a More pill and a character peek out), page numbers. For news and press release lists

notes: The 3×3 video wrapped by the hero cylinder and footer photo strip is a placeholder video (media/fv-tiles.mp4) with the same ratio (nine 16:9 cells) and the same length (6.08s·24fps loop). Over file:// the browser cannot upload video as a WebGL texture (it is treated as cross-origin), so a placeholder with the same cells and the same 6.08s loop is drawn on a canvas and wrapped instead — over a server the video is used as is

Two Lottie slots (the pen hand in the concept text 377×386 · 48 frames over 18 scroll turns, the recruiting band decoration 520×358 · 72 frames looping) run on the same dotlottie-web 0.80.0 as the original, keeping the original panel size, frame count and playback, while the artwork is our own shapes built in JS. Opened via file:// the wasm cannot be fetched (fetch is blocked), so a still image stands in the same slot and the pen hand just moves along the same path without animating

The blob shapes at the blob borders and the strokes of the script words (hero, careers) are newly drawn rather than using the original letterforms — the times and scroll ranges split by drawing order and length ratio use the original values

Detail pages under about·careers (promise·history·group·region, experienced·part-time detail, employee story·event detail, a single news item) were not recorded so they were not built — one new-grad detail stands in for the experienced·part-time links

Logo and characters (8 characters, eyes, gloved hands, glasses menu icon, footer prop paper, thumb, letter) are simple SVGs redrawn at the same position and size. Large English words are placeholder words (HEADING, SERVICE NAME, etc.)

The original service page code (3g_zv5 bundle) has a scrub where ”the front panel stays stuck to the screen, dims to .5 brightness while rising −50vh, and the next panel covers it”, but which panel it belongs to could not be determined from the recorded screens, so it was not included.

The photo columns of the recruit band (WebGL) pick their panel size at random between 0.8 and 1 each time it opens, like the original, so column length differs slightly each time. The 16 photos are a set of placeholder images in the same 3:2 cells instead of the original sprite (ktx2)

Like the original, the service gallery uses WebGL (library/_vendor/three@0.174.0, the original is three r186·react-three-fiber) to lay 13 panels out horizontally, curving backward toward the screen edges — the photo panels are placeholder art so the grayscale spread looks faint, and clicking a panel opens service.html in a new tab instead of the original service site
As in the original, the panel size is set at random between 0.8 and 1 each time it opens, so the distance travelled to the end differs by a few % each time (even between originals by 6.5%)

Subpage header breadcrumb — the original is Latin (Syne) like Top – Careers, so all five pages were changed to Top – page English name (About Brand Name·News Journal·Careers·Careers – For New Graduates·Our Service). Matched to the same words as the big page title.
Two base links on recruit-detail — the original uses uppercase English space names (Unbounded), so they are SPACE NAME 01 and 02. What goes in is set by data-label.

The location line ‹Online› in the six event cards of recruit and recruit-detail — the original is Online written in kana, Korean is kept. The paired Pretendard (sans-serif ↔ gothic) after Syne is already loaded in theme.css.
The sites pull stopped midway on a file/folder name conflict (ENOTDIR) in eight-journal, so for the subpages I unpacked the archived pages.har.zip to check the original text.

title: One-page tribute with a layered brick vault that opens apart
good_for: Memorial or archive sites for a single architect, writer, or designer, showing a work timeline and life story in large type on black.

pages.use: Single-page person tribute — brick vault Hero opening in layers, about photo, needle timeline, life story, quote video, final portrait, parallax photos, brick-textured name footer. For the works timeline or archive of one architect or writer

A single work piece — hero where a full-screen lead photo is tied to scroll and folds into a small box inside the title line, big text and quote on a sand-colored paper stage, parallax photo, three record photos, pinned photos peeled away one by one, location · vertical photo, footer that turns brick-colored, and a work-list pill that floats up when scrolling up. For work detail pages of architecture and artist archives

notes: The two recorded subpages (the root URL and /en) are the Spanish and English versions of the first page and share its form. They are built as one index.html, and the language links trigger a page transition to the same page.

The original Hero cuts one brick-vault photo into 11 pieces (background, 4 below, center, 5 above) and draws them on a 2D canvas (not WebGL). Instead of the photo, 11 layers of octagonal brick frames are drawn on the same 2D canvas, with outer frames offset toward the lower left to follow the original photo’s diagonal band composition. Per-layer offsets, fit calculation, black 0.3 cover and intro (gap inset 48% · 46%, scale 1.4→1.2→1, letters 0.01s apart 1em) are the original values as is, and brick and sky colors are read from the Skin (--kf-accent · --kf-ink). To use a real photo, feed pre-cut images per layer instead of paintLayer.

The name wordmark placeholder is Korean text (Your/Name), so the original cap-height trimming (text-box trim) was dropped and the size reduced from 20vw→16vw (phone 36vw→27vw). With a Latin name, restore the original values.

The video slot is the original VideoEmbed as is. When the slot comes within one screen, a placeholder preview of the same ratio and length (1920:1424, 14.8s) loops silently (80% saturation and a 50% black overlay that releases over 1s on hover). Clicking lifts the cover away in 0.7s and, in the same slot, a placeholder video of the full length (49:30) rises with controls over 0.7s quart and plays right away. The video player’s outer shell (title and progress bar look) is replaced by the browser’s default controls.
Typeface: instead of the original Die Grotesk A, Inter Tight + Noto Sans KR. The maker logo (Studio SVG) is replaced with a text placeholder.

The phone photo row is hooked up with BlossomCarousel as in the original — the original bundle has the same form as @blossom-carousel/core 1.0.2 and 1.0.3 (the two are the same code with only variable names different), so 1.0.3 was used

The detail page (detail.html) was built from the original project page. The four link cells in the timeline and the work-list rows in the detail go to detail.html and, as in the original, show a transition where a curtain carrying the lead photo covers from below (0.6s 0.7 darken · body -100px · curtain 0.8s power3.inOut, lifts 0.6s after arrival).
Same type: detail.html — the recorded subpage /en/iglesia-de-cristo-obrero is the English version of the same work detail.

Work detail is a paper stage painted opposite to the home page like the original (sand background·brick-red text, and when the footer touches the screen center the background turns accent color and the text white in .7s). Background and text are made from --kf-accent as --site-paper(=--site-sand) and --site-paper-ink (shared.css), so they change together when the skin is swapped.

--site-sand, --site-sky and --site-sky-deep originally borrowed the hue of the text color (#f1ece8), but Chrome reads the relative color h of a nearly achromatic color as 0, so the sand tone came out pink (oklch h 10.69, rgb 239,219,221). They are now fixed to rotate from the accent color’s hue, so #eadfd2, #e9eef2 and #9eb0bf come out as intended (the name text in the first page Hero and the dot link hover color also return to the original 234,223,210).

Photo credit text follows the original ImageCredits: from 768px it sits 1rem from the right and bottom (.5rem below that) — only the credit on the wide first page photo is always .5rem, as in the original.

The curve names ”base.inOut” (hero Flip) and ”magic” (photo overlap snap) are not registered anywhere in the original, so they fall back to GSAP’s default curve power1.out (checked by feeding them into gsap 3 in node, same value 0.51@0.3). The copy uses power1.out too, matching the actual behavior.
The detail footer name has no brick texture like the original and uses the text color (currentColor) as is — the original detail footer SVG uses fill currentColor.

The detail work-list pill was measured to match the original: at 1440 hidden 206×44@909 → floats up @839 → expands to 408×342 (sizes match every 80ms), at 390 176×38 → 349×293. Original a[aria-current=As in true], the current page slot in the header row always has its dot lit, and it is hidden on phones.

title: Designer portfolio with a rotating ring of photos
good_for: Personal designer or studio portfolios with case lists and details, plus a self-introduction page featuring a 3D figure.

pages.use: Portfolio first page — an opening curtain where the name fills in with pixels, a hero where photo cards orbit in an ellipse, selected work (one wide card + two + three), a work list whose preview opens pinned, logo band, About, Services, Career and Awards with a 3D figure turning pinned in place, closing
Work case list — big title and industry filter (switches with a pixel veil), three-column card grid, closing. For work collection pages of portfolios and studios

Single case — header, fact table (client · what we did · industry), full-bleed cover, for each section (background · problem · solution · result) one text column and photo rows (full · two · centered · looping video), other cases swiped horizontally, closing
Contact — big title and intro, underlined-input form (name · email · company · topic pills · message · consent), on submit a thank-you screen behind a pixel curtain

notes: The original wordmark typeface (Gossip HighPixel) is not free, so the free Jacquard 24 of the same feel (pixel blackletter) was used. The name placeholder is lowercase Latin ‹name surname› so the blackletter shows
Work card hover flip and list preview run on placeholder photos (wf-img) — the video row of the original preview panel (plays from the start on mouse hover) is set as a placeholder image

On the case detail page, the looping video sits in the same 16:9 slot as an 8s placeholder video (media/loop.mp4, a hand-made gray gradient), set to autoplay and loop. The original video length could not be measured from the recording
The original hero opening curtain stops at 92% until all images load — the copy has no images to load, so it moves on right away

The cookie notice is only shape and buttons. Pressing it closes it for this tab only (no real consent is saved). The contact form submit only shows a pixel curtain and thank-you screen after validation (nothing is actually sent)
Language switch (KO/EN) is visual only — no other language versions exist

The head cursor added to the live original site after the archived copy was made (when over the hero name, it cuts the 3D figure’s head off at the neck and spins it inside a 132px circle that follows the cursor, .4s back.out(2)) was not built — it is not in the archived code and the 3D figure is a basic shape, so there is no model to detach a head from. Left for the next person to pick up

Font placeholder text: the original headings are all Latin (large Geist + Gossip pixel-blackletter words), so the 8 heading font (ee-display) slots were replaced with English placeholder text — index hero intro sentence, ”Selected work”, closing sentence (three in index·list·detail), list ”All cases”, contact ”Let’s talk”, detail case title. Wordmark words (name·project·cases·talk) and name letters were English from the start. Work names (cards·list), eyebrow labels and section labels use the body font (Geist·Geist Mono) slots, so per the README they stay in Korean. No heading slot is left in Korean. The thumb was captured with --wait 10000 to shoot after the opening curtain and text shuffle finish

title: Studio site walking through one 3D world with morphing particle clouds, scrolling to the next page
good_for: 3D or interactive studios and experiential brand sites where every page should feel like a different spot in the same world.

pages.use: First page: after an entry gate (with sound / without), a 3D lakeside world where the camera circles a particle cloud once as the cloud shifts between five shapes (logo · cube · sphere · heart · ring) across five story screens, then What we do (word fill-in · rolling service list), scattered work cards, an awards list with a rotating trophy, and scrolling to the end leads to About

About the company — five story screens walking through a round room (table, sculpture, panorama window) within the same world, origin story, giant flowing year numbers, light-ray quote band, two makers and a card stack, access, FAQ
Work list — a 3D carousel on a no-scroll black stage where sixteen cards spin like a cylinder (wheel, drag, arrows), with the center work name, filter and tick-mark page count. For a portfolio list
Contact — the left half is a world with two chairs under a flowering tree, the right half has a choice row, an input form and a direct contact list. The header band button changes to Close
One work case — four meta cells, big name, vertical video header, one-sentence intro, awards received, rounded-panel big screens, spec rows, dark purple call card, scroll to the end for the next work

notes: Title placeholder copy is English uppercase as in the original, so it renders in Instrument Serif and the line height is .8 as in the original (the .92 spacing added to fix the overlap when Korean placeholder text fell back to Hahmlet was reverted). Instrument Serif is wider than the original Emotion Serif (wdth 75), so less text fits in the same box than in the original — the placeholder copy was written short to match the original line count.

The About room was rebuilt by measuring the original room model (only the accessor bounding boxes in the glb JSON were read, geometry not carried over) and re-placing each object with our own shape at the same position and size (2026-11-17): rug 18.8×29.3, table 4.5×5.6 with a ring of chairs, two laptops, built-in shelf on the +x wall 7.3×6.4×15 with six vases, picture on the +z wall 3.7×3.95 with a big e sculpture in front, big sofa 10×6.8 with two partition walls, rock 7.7×3.7×7.5, round tea table diameter 5.8 with a small plant, window-side armchair and round stool, curved floor lamp, skylight ring (diameter 13.3) with an indoor tree beneath. Room model coordinates 1 = This version is 0.91 (floor radius 15.4 → 14). The camera path joins the original five points (world coordinates converted back to room coordinates) with centripetal Catmull-Rom, the gaze point is 30 ahead in the facing direction, the last 20% goes to the end spot by the window, FOV 50. The panorama window is cut on -z (lake side) as originally intended (a cylinder angle calculation was off by 90° and it had ended up on +x). Textures and material patterns are single skin colors.

The works carousel replaces the original (card front is a video·spec board) with a card image (skin-color gradient + photo label), and the filter only shows the selected state (it does not filter). Original card count 16, the outward-facing cylinder · light edge · floor reflection are the same.
The AI helper is only a speech bubble and an orb — no chat feature. Sound is a low chord plus wind synthesized on the spot instead of the original background audio file.

When opened with an automation tool (navigator.webdriver), reaching the end band does not move on to the next page, so measuring tools do not wander off to another page while scrolling to the bottom. When a person opens it, it moves on like the original.

compare·interact: the original stops at the entrance gate (nothing enters until pressed), so both sides only capture the gate. Post-entry screen comparison was done with a separate script that presses the enter button and captures five pages at 1440·390.
All scripts load with defer (order unchanged) — so parsing the 1.3MB three.cjs doesn’t hold up the first screen.

Typeface placeholder copy: since the original is all English, 146 spots of title typeface (Instrument Serif, --kf-font-display) were replaced with English placeholder copy — big titles of the five pages’ story screens, long what-we-do sentences, Work section names, eight Work card names, award section names and category lines, closing big titles, next page names, About start·maker·access section names·quotes·person names·one paragraph·seven FAQ questions, detail work name·one sentence·awards·tech used·call to action, Contact big title·nineteen choice lines·direct contact title, phone menu (Menu 0~3), works work names and carousel card names (works.js NAMES). The same header line and footer page links (body mono) were aligned to Menu 0~3 too (including the Contact footer that was Home·About·Work·Contact). Label·button·body (IBM Plex Mono·Inter Tight) spots stay Korean per the README. No title spot is left in Korean

Thumbs and text-check photos shot with tools/shot.cjs only capture the entry gate, so as if having entered from the same window before (sessionStorage em-entered=1) Shot with a temporary script that waits and captures (4.5 seconds after the Hero). The library-shots section images (--again 32 shots) also cannot get past the entry door, so they are captured with the header band and text missing (only the world and footer, with top, FAQ and others as blank background). It was like this before the backfill and is a tooling matter, so I left it alone. To revive the picker panel section images, library-shots needs sessionStorage em-entered=Lay down 1 first, then stamp

title: Project site with 3D vegetables floating in space and fixed scenes that change per section
good_for: Corporate social contribution or materials technology project sites, 3D showcases that go deep on a few items one at a time, and campaign landings with maps and partners.

pages.use: Project home page — loading curtain, a black stage with floating 3D vegetables and three pinned scenes (four hero text groups · five cream panels on the right, one per vegetable · from dot planet to custom map), partner photo list and about panel, white soil 3D footer

Material (tech) about — centered logo and wide parallax photo on cream paper, material description with translucent film photos·video, project intro, users’ voices and three staggered-pushed photos. For tech·material·company about subpages

notes: Of the recorded subpages, /en is the English version of the hero page (same type), so it was not built

The map is a long curved island outline drawn from seeded random numbers instead of a real map of the country, and the cell map of that land is a seeded random field instead of the original satellite data (values are placeholders). The scan line in the third cell was set to repeat every 2.4s because the original CSS values could not be found, and the layer button was judged to be ”overlay the line map on the cell map at .35” since the original behavior (stacking the data list) is not visible on screen. The info panel open/close at .4s expo is also a guess.

The dotted planet and white soil were rebuilt as a three point cloud and a sine-wave mound. Seeds·sprouts on the soil move with the original values (2.6→−1.67 2s quart.in, sprout 2.2s with 2s cubic.out·back.out, camera fov 45·(0,5,10)·fog 10~20, parallax at screen bottom 2.4s expo.out), and their shapes are our default shapes.
Logos, photos, videos and text are all placeholders (the video is our placeholder media/about.mp4)

About three titles (What is Material?, Project by Material?, Voices) — the original is a Latin brand name (Brand®, Brand) plus Japanese particles, so only the brand slot is English (MATERIAL®, Project). The ‹What is› part, ‹Shade awning› and the second line are Japanese kana and kanji in the original, so Korean is kept
index hero (Save the Endangered Vegetables) — original has a kanji/kana title, Korean text kept
index vegetable section title · five vegetable names · farmer story title (h4) — the original uses kanji/kana titles, Korean kept (the English tail text is already English)
index map title (Endangered Vegetable Custom Map) — the original is a kanji and katakana title, Korean kept
index partner card four names · video panel ”Close” — the original uses kanji names and a Japanese close label, Korean kept
Title font DM Sans’s Korean pair is Noto Sans KR 700 (sans-serif ↔ gothic, in place of the original Yu Gothic), already loaded, so left as is

title: Space company with a scroll-driven satellite mission film
good_for: Space, hardware, and tech product introductions, 3D product story landings told in one scroll, and dark tech company sites with careers, product tables, news, and history.

pages.use: Service first page — over a fixed 3D space scene (earth·satellites·constellation clusters·blueprint grid·instrument panel), 24 text frames swap at each scroll step, the progress bar below unfolds into section names, and it ends with a drag price tag·slot numbers·final button. For a landing page that shows a 3D product story in a single line of scroll

Recruit — big title and launch video, three goal lines whose letters light up, a pinned section where a 3×3 photo grid zooms 2x until only the center video remains, a dot globe turning with the cursor and a featured quote, and a job list whose background unfolds from the side it was entered, top or bottom

Product list — video header, a category menu that follows the scroll and collapses, a product photo pinned to the screen per category with a price table (hovering a row shrinks the photo to .9x and swaps it), a number strip, and a closing section with a large title buried in the background (hovering the button lifts the title slightly). For hardware lists and category pages with price tags.

News list — big title and intro, two-column cards with the even columns dropped lower (slide in from the side, photo parallax, hover zoom and an arrow cell), page numbers, footer section. For press release and blog lists.
Work list — same layout as the news list, ten cards with only a project name and no date. For research project and client case lists

Company about — big title and group photo (rises while shrinking from 3x), intro sentences whose letters light up, two goal lines, a pinned CEO quote over a big photo, history cards whose year scale moves with back.inOut, an endlessly flowing team card band you can drag and push, a numbers band, a person quote, an investor cell where the intro changes on hover, and a tail section. For company history and team intros

notes: 3D scene: the camera chains 26 reference points inside the original glb (phone·tablet use 26 camera-N-mobile points, desktop camera-18 is squared and camera-21 uses an expo.out rotation) by seeking P along the original main timeline (section labels map 4.5·design 6.5·launch 8.25·deployed 10·spaceops 11·encryption 14·modular 16·price 19, with each interval’s length and curve unchanged). FOV 12°, follow at dt×10, snapping straight to the map section, and the .001 mouse sway are all original values. Object positions also use original values (Earth radius 5, the three satellite reference points and the spot inside the rocket, the rocket, the workshop grid, the ops ring) and are drawn with our own shapes — a procedural Earth (daylight brightness switches on only in the map section, city lights on the night side, letter cells in the encryption section, a dot Earth in the cost section), flat satellites in original proportions (three solar panels each, folded while loaded then unfolded, inspection panel·lines), a rocket (wire-cylinder body, two fairing halves that split open and fly away, five satellite slots inside, launch light streak), a grid that erases from the center, a HUD frame around the screen, and eight satellites that spread into place. The first section’s scroll box uses an inline min-height(50svh) like the original — it used to be set as height, which lost to the CSS min-height 100svh so P ran half a screen late. The original’s photo Earth·cloud textures, post-process blur (uEarthBluriness), and satellite PBR materials·twelve payload models were replaced by our own shaders·shapes in the same spots (they are image·model asset slots, so left as is).

The 24-frame structure, scroll section height, per-frame enter/exit values, progress bar, drag price-tag formula, slot number strip and uFadeToBlack(.4 power2.out) are read straight from the original bundle. The original snap points (data-snap-points) exist in the bundle only as values with no place that uses them, so they were not added

Subpage 6 (satellites category products-category/satellites) is the same document as the product list (same height 13108), so it is built as a single product.html. The nine product category sections are cut to three. The 54 Recruit job rows are cut to 8, News cards to 6, and Work cards to 10 (the original also has 10).

Careers: clicking a job row opens an application drawer (Gravity Forms) in the original — not built because it is an external form. The job search · select fields have only the look and expansion (no filtering)
The cart icon · price currency (EUR/USD by visitor region) · cookies · reCAPTCHA · newsletter sending are external features and were not built

title: Dark streetwear auction shop with warping cloud paintings and zipper boxes
good_for: Limited-edition or vintage luxury shops, auctions, and cult brand homes where classical painting-style ornament suits a dark background.

pages.use: Store home page — number loader and scramble title, a bending-cloud drawing-board hero, three horizontally flowing manifesto panels, a box that unzips on scroll, a typewriter price input line, a top list whose image changes on hover, an auction slider, a story list, cloud footer. For limited-edition stores and brand homes

Product list — cloud garland and breadcrumb under two lights, large heading, collapsible filter and sort on the left, three-column product cards, popular row, pagination. For a shop’s full product and category list

Blog: copper gradient and a cloud-garland header, a featured post panel (photo + title·summary·button), and a row of post tiles that widen and center when pressed or dragged. For brand news·story lists

One auction item — product on a black box stage with floor light and a favorite button, brand and name, current price, next minimum, time left, place bid, buy now, description tabs. For product detail and single auction pages.

notes: 3D logo: instead of the original logo model, an extruded plate of the same mark (eye-shaped ellipse, center hole, side wings), with the same lighting (ambient 1.5, directional 2.2/1.1), material (roughness .35, metalness .15) and rotation (.35rad/s, drag .012rad/px, inertia ×.94). The menu clouds (menu-clouds.glb) and the bottom-right question mark (clue-mark.glb) are replaced with a similar cloud plate and an SVG question mark. The 3D rotation of the question mark and the clue input (clue-hint) were not built.

title: Beauty salon site with photo windows that unfold on scroll

pages.use: Shop home page — video Hero opening as the loader panels split · boundary where a small center photo window expands to fill the screen · endlessly flowing photo band (click for an enlarged window) · popular styles slider · two-column pricing · four-column store list · recruit band that unfolds as it darkens. For salon·beauty shop homes where photos are the star
Company overview — large whitespace header title and a seven-row overview table (each row rises and a line is drawn). For a single “About the company” page of a small company or shop

Price list — nine categories on the left, menu name and price rows on the right (names and prices float up in turn and the lines are drawn) with a note at the bottom. For salon or beauty treatment menus and service price guides

Recruiting home page — a header where a full-bleed photo shrinks to 66%, vision text, a style graphic with five circles being drawn, four styles with photo sliders and thumbnails alternating left and right, four strengths, and a three-column job-role photo strip. For the home of a salon or design role recruiting site.

Job-category recruiting detail — location indicator · shrinking header photo · training course text and a twelve-month horizontal table (first column sticky) · two staff voices · benefits box · recruitment requirements table · application flow box and SNS · guidebook button · job category photo strip. For new-grad and experienced hiring requirements on one page

notes: The hero video hangs in two versions like the original, PC (16:9) and phone (9:16), with autoplay·loop·muted·playsinline — media/movie-pc.mp4·movie-sp.mp4 are placeholder videos of the same ratio and 10s length (a seconds counter and progress bar run so the loop is visible). The “Watch video” enlarged window is a video player embed in the original, so here tapping it plays a placeholder video (controls), and closing stops it (judgment: so sound doesn’t continue from a hidden window)
Like the original onScreen, is-on is removed when leaving the screen, so the letter and photo entrances repeat each time it re-enters (same as the original)
Fixed the recorded type: the new-graduate hiring page detail → recruit (job category opening detail), the pricing page page → service

Privacy, site policy and Contact pages, plus the Mid-career Assistant and Stylist detail pages, were not recorded so they were not built — the footer links "#", the three role bands link to recruit-detail.html, which has the same type

Where the original had Poppins English text (section names · header/drawer/footer menus · booking button · bottom links · price categories and menu names · job-type band · location label · recruiting circle graphic and style names · map link) we used English placeholders (About·Menu 1·Booking·Category 1·Item Name 1·Position 01·Style 1 …) and wrote in data-label what to put there. Like the original, 1rem = Set to 10px (html 62.5%)

recruit-detail training course table header (Year 1 · Year 2 · Year 3) — the original uses kanji for Year 1, kept here in Korean. Noto Sans KR 500 (gothic↔sans-serif, weight matched) paired after Poppins is already loaded in theme.css

Buttons (More, Button), social buttons, store names and the small description under section names that use the body font (Zen Kaku Gothic New) are set with Korean placeholder text rather than the Latin-only font slot (in the original the store names and small descriptions are also Japanese)

The thumbnail was shot at the shot.cjs default of 2.5 seconds, which is still on the loader (opens at 3.2 seconds), so only the Wordmark was captured. Used --wait 5500 to capture the first screen after the loader (2026-11-07)

As in the original, the concept photo strip is a Swiper inside a container with 17% margins (.19 slides · 110s per slide · linear, at 1440 a slide is 5000px with eight 911×608 photos at 437) — the container follows the screen width as in the original (at 1920 the original is capped at 1267px) so slides stretch by 1/.19 too, and the photo height is fixed at 608px as measured at 1440 (the original photo size on wide screens was not measured). Phone has two rows: three landscape (1.05 slides · 8s) and five portrait (1.3 slides · 8s · reversed)

title: Split-photo hero and neon-sign slate bands for a small product shop
good_for: Small product shops and online stores that need a split photo hero, product list, brand introduction, news and recruiting pages.

pages.use: Shop home page — under the notice bar and slate header, the screen is split in half by two photo panels (left slogan, right flickering neon sign), then straight to the footer. For a shop entrance that sets two products side by side.
Collaboration product list — big uppercase title band, square product cells grouped by collaborator (category · name · price, discount price in red). For grouped product lists and collection pages

Brand About — large uppercase heading, play-button intro video (2:1), a ring illustration at top left, and below it a single 800px column with a large English title, photo, subheading and body repeated seven times. For product philosophy and features
News list — three-column square photo cards (settle from 1.1x when visible), title, date, read more, pagination. For shop notice and news boards

Careers: big uppercase heading, a single 800px column divided by lines (who we look for · how we work · seven-cell number infographic · job category buttons · four-step hiring process · apply button). For small company hiring pages
Single news post — centered title and date, narrow body (including a landscape photo), share buttons, back to list, previous post row. For notice and press article details

notes: Photo slots (two panels in Hero, two in Menu, Product, News, About photos) are labeled placeholders — panels that carry white text are painted dark (--site-photo-dark). The ring photo at top left of About (232×240) is a ring SVG of the same position and size

The About page video is a placeholder mp4 (media/concept.mp4) of the same ratio and length with the same playback behavior, standing in for the original hosted video (2:1, 53 s, play button, no autoplay)

The seven Recruit ”Company in Numbers” panels are PNG infographics in the original — redrawn as line SVGs in the same position and shape (map, three people, male/female, globe, pie chart, bars, two cells), simpler than the original. On the original phone view the tailwind column-width rules don’t apply, so it shows one graphic per row (about 300px), the copy does the same.

Unrecorded pages in the menu and footer (how to use, company overview, store list, exchange request, etc.) link to # or the nearest page of ours. The original menu overlay covers and clears instantly with display, no transition, and the copy does the same
Product list · original large title, the banner-image slot on the right is empty in the original too, so it was left empty

Tried both by swapping in theme.css as a light skin (ink-wash) and a dark skin (blueprint) and capturing — the slate band, neon and sale red are all made from the skin, so no original color remains (in the dark skin, the header, footer and photo slots become light panels)

Spots that were English in the original (six menu overlay lines, footer Category lines, the artist collaboration bundle name in the product list, the commemorative edition product name) are left as English placeholders (TOP · PRODUCT 01 · CATEGORY 05 · Artist Name × BRAND · EVENT 0000 BLACK), with data-label noting what to put there. The header logo, brand label, slogan, neon sign and section titles (CONCEPT · RECRUIT · Less is more. …) were already English.

Twelve news card title lines · article large title — the original had Japanese news titles (e.g. Notice about inventory), Korean text kept. Cabin followed by the paired Pretendard Variable (sans ↔ gothic, variable weight) is already loaded in theme.css

The neon-side subheads (Zen Maru Gothic) are one line of Japanese plus English in the original, so they are set as Korean plus English. Korean falls back to Pretendard (gothic) — I did not look for a rounded Korean gothic matching weights 500 and 700, so the pair is left as it is (judgment: this is a backfill that does not change the Skin). Whether to add a rounded pair is up to the next person

The footer Info, FAQ rows, location marker, notice bar and product names set in the Roboto body font are Japanese in the original too, so Korean placeholders were used (Info’s CONCEPT·NEWS are English, like the original)

title: Vertical serif tagline over sky photo for a home-visit nursing office
good_for: Homepages, introductions and news pages for medical, care and local service offices that speak calmly with people photos and a vertical serif tagline.

pages.use: Care office home page — people-photo hero, vertical-writing slogan sky photo, care cards, recruiting cards, regional map, news, contact. For medical, care and local service homes
News list — thumbnail news rows. In an office notice list
About us — group photo header, intro, care diagram, support list, policy, president’s message, cityscape photo, office list and map. For a one-page office intro.
One news item — heading · body · share · other news. For announcement post detail

notes: Fonts: the original paid Japanese Gothic and Mincho fonts (paid web fonts) were replaced with Pretendard and Noto Serif KR (the English subtitle Abhaya Libre is the same). The hero vertical slogan is a text graphic (SVG) in the original but is set as vertical text here

The regional map and the three-field circle illustrations are redrawn with the same position, size and color relationships, but coastlines, ward borders and place names are rough and the text is placeholder. The original map is a still image (JPG), so there is no motion (the card’s “loop of base circles spreading” appears nowhere in the original code or images).
Since the sky photo slot holds white text on top, a sky→river color band is laid instead of a gray box (it is photo color so it is marked as not skin — it disappears once a photo is added)
The Google Maps embed in the office card is left as a photo slot. The phone number text image is kept as text

Subpages that were not in the recording (two services, related organizations, careers, corporate overview, FAQ, contact) were not built and their menu links are #. The News detail of the same type (archives/200) is a single detail.html. The infiniteslide photo strip in the original careers post (recruit side) is not in the captured pages, so it was left out.
Logo, photos and text are all placeholders (logo mark newly drawn as a green square and lime wedge, SNS, Q&A and mail icons also newly drawn)

Font backfill: the Latin font (Abhaya Libre) spots — section English subtitles, English leads, the representative English name, diagram field English, Q&A, copyright and logo — are already English, so the text was not changed

index·about·list·detail titles (hero vertical slogan · section titles · careers · regions · policy · greeting · offices · news post titles) — the original uses a Japanese serif font for titles, Korean kept (paired with Noto Serif KR)
Regional map place names and diagram field names — original in Japanese, Korean kept

title: Cursor-bending light-line stage and word-lighting manifesto for a design studio
good_for: Homepages for B2B and SaaS product design studios and agencies, service company landings with pricing tables, and small company sites with case studies and a blog.

pages.use: Studio home page — light-line stage hero, client logo strip, pinned manifesto where words light up, case cards (screens overlap and swap), four process steps, service rows, pricing stage (two glass cards), testimonial slider, work tiles (hover description card), FAQ. For product design and development studio landing pages
Case list — big title and two rows of bordered cards (screen scales 1.03 on hover). For agency portfolio lists
Blog list — row list with number, title, summary, category and date. For company blog and insight post lists

Case detail: big title and tags, fact table on the right (client, field, service, period) with challenge, what we did and result, a screenshot column on the left, and three related cases. For a single product design case

notes: All original photos (product screen captures, testimonial faces, client logos) are placeholders describing what each screen shows — four case cards with two screens each, sixteen work tiles with one each. Client and investor logos are logo-slot boxes matched only in width

The light-line shader was not ported from the original (a line effect from a React component library). It was rewritten from the same formulas (glow-lines-bend): 6 lines, spacing .515, speed 1.9, bend radius 6.5, intensity 2, follow .05, drag .2, and three colors (cyan and magenta are derived in oklch from the orange accent color). As in the original it starts when idle after load and fades in over 1s. Time differs every frame, so line positions differ in each capture

The manifesto word highlight runs the original ScrollRevealText (hand-built --reveal variable) on the char-highlight-scrub part (GSAP·ScrollTrigger·SplitText) with a track option added, using the same formula (1 between words · 5 spread · .8 end share). That is why three GSAP files not in the original are loaded on the first page only.

Of the three subpages, Process (pages.json 3) is the #process anchor of the home page so it was not built separately. A single blog article page was not recorded so it was not built, and the blog row links are set to #
The footer rating widget (review-site iframe) and award badges are same-size placeholder boxes — they are external widgets. The consultation booking (scheduling service) link points to #contact.
Fonts: Asta Sans·DM Mono are the same free fonts as the original (Google Fonts). Asta Sans also covers Korean

title: Boot-terminal start into a chapter-flipping 3D showreel experience
good_for: Production company and studio showreels, game-like chapter-by-chapter brand experiences, and interactive introductions for exhibitions and events.

pages.use: A single-page 3D experience — after a green CRT boot terminal (turned on with ENTER), nine sections (VOLT helmet robot · MUSEUM sculpture gallery · MONUMENT bronze group · NEON light path · POSTER print plate · BREAKOUT halftone · STYLE RUN render style switching · SHATTER glass shards · LOGO white section) are moved through with a section guide ring, and each section has LED · paper peel · portal · flash · CRT transitions. For the first screen of a showreel or interactive experience

notes: The original’s 3D models (helmet robot, scanned figure sculpture, bronze group, CRT computer, balloon letters) were built from our basic shapes (sphere, capsule, box, tube) at the same position, size and silhouette proportions. There is no sculpted detail such as faces or clothing folds.
Sound (174 BPM music and effects) is not recreated — the SOUND button only switches on the equalizer bar motion
The video in the showreel window is the same 16:9 placeholder plate (the original 49-second video file is not used)

The boot log is not tied to real download progress, like the original, and runs on a schedule built from the length the original measured (about 6.9 seconds: two status lines · audio unpack complete line together on the first paint → shader bake · section warm-up log 2.8 seconds (typing steps 1~9 meanwhile, each letter flashing for 90ms) → pause .67 seconds → steps 10~12 (highlight cell · ready, .9 second intervals) — the dropped · paused · entered intervals from the original loader measurement)

The gold text color of the MONUMENT base is a material color, so it is kept as a value outside the Skin (skin-exempt comment). Scene material colors (bronze, chrome, plaster, beige) are three numeric colors for the same reason

index section guide ring title (.iris-intro__h, per-section title in index.js) — the original defaults to Japanese (JA/EN switch, var(--jp)=Kana and kanji action text in a Japanese sans (800), Korean kept. Noto Sans KR, the title typeface partner, is loaded up to 800·900 to match the weight

index header ”Watch Showreel” button — the original default is Japanese ”Watch the main feature” (English only on language switch), Korean kept. The button font (Archivo) falls back to Noto Sans KR gothic, matching the feel of the original Hiragino gothic

Two small lines of text on the right of the index poster section — the original is a Japanese “Coming soon” sentence, kept in Korean here (the six credit lines on the left are Latin in the original, so they were replaced with English placeholder text)

title: Dark fashion brand entered through a curtain with wordmark window and fading products
good_for: Home and collection pages for small-batch mood-driven fashion brands such as lingerie, dresses and fragrance, and launch pages needing an invitation-like entrance.

pages.use: Fashion brand home page: red curtain entrance, silk video declaration words, wordmark window, product grid of varied heights, look cards passing over a quote, FAQ, contact card, photo footer. For mood brand homes such as lingerie and perfume
Collection list — big brush-stroke title background, five-column product grid with a benefit panel between, gift card cell, photo-free footer. For small-batch fashion brand product lists

notes: Of the 2 subpages, RU | Home (https://example.com/ru-home) is the Russian version of home, so it is treated as the same type and not built (rule: one per type). Only the language button (ko ▾) stays in the menu.

Motion values were copied directly from the IX2 settings (ixData — actionLists·events) inside the original webflow.schunk and the original inline script: curtain entrance a-22 (group .5s ease fade-out · curtain 1.5s inCubic ±105% · group .5s linear −100%), title a-48 (6rem·transparent → 1s outCubic/ease, 1s·2s), statement a-30/a-16~21/a-31, wordmark window a-4/a-5/a-34, quote pass a-10/a-11/a-12, question a-13/a-14, contact a-15, underline a-46/a-47, gallery label a-23/a-24, slideInBottom. The ”when visible” test (offset o% → element top is (100−o)% up the screen, bottom o% below) and the ”while scrolling” progress with per-frame (1−smoothing) following are also exactly the original runtime formulas (shared.js X.inView·X.ixScroll). The curves ease·easeIn·easeOut use CustomEase with the same Bézier.

The title typeface Brand (paid trial) was replaced with the free Noto Serif Display ExtraCondensed, which the original uses for its Russian version. Korean placeholders fall back to Noto Serif KR, which lacks the original’s narrow feel and is wider at the same font size — big titles have fewer characters to keep the line count.

The giant wordmark (original Brand logo) is a BRAND0 placeholder text with similar letter widths, and the vertical monogram logo is drawn as an SVG placeholder with five letters hung on a vertical line. Swap in the real logo SVG. The hero title is also SVG letter art in the original, so it is set in letters of the same size.

The manifesto background video is media/manifesto.mp4, our placeholder video matching the original’s 16:9 · 30fps · 10.4s loop (a cloth band passing over a gray background), and playback behaves like the original: autoplay · loop · no sound. The curtain, Hero, Contact and Footer photos are kept as photo slots (.wf-img), with only the slot background painted wine and dark gray so the original tone remains (--site-tone-*). The background photo laid under the original manifesto section on phones (bg-2-mobile) occupies the same spot as the video, so it is not kept separately.

The gallery cell layout was redone from the rhythm read off the screen, because the original w-node positions were not kept in the recording (five cells · first cell dropped 6rem · big photo spanning two cells × two rows with a huge sentence · last row pulled up -4.81rem · View All cell with red hover).

The brush-stroke art behind the list and the paper texture and border ornaments of the Contact card were replaced with CSS gradients and double borders derived from Skin variables. The lace pattern on the gift card is also drawn with CSS repeating circles.
Site-builder badge and external links (messaging app, booking) were removed or swapped for same-page anchors.

Font backfill (2026-11-07) — the original is the English edition, so all 63 title-font (Noto Serif Display narrow width) spots were changed to English placeholder text (0 Korean left). Question answers · menu · buttons · card types · hover text use the body font (Inter Tight) in the original too, so they keep Korean placeholder text

The 7 index section images (manifesto-words · wordmark-window · product-grid · lookbook-quote-pass · faq · cta-card · footer-photo) could not be shot by library-shots --again. Until the curtain entrance is clicked, body.is-gated keeps the sections at display:none, and the tool does not click the entrance (data-enter). Those 7 in catalog/shots still hold the old images (10-26, Korean placeholder text). Re-shoot them once the tool can click the entrance.

title: Brush-stroke transitions and primary-color framed cards stacking in 3D
good_for: Video, animation and social content production studios, and playful creative team introductions with work lists and service pages.

pages.use: Video studio home page — brush-stroke transition, work-reel hero, client marquee, team collage, 3D stack of solid-color framed cards, service cards, team photos. For a video and animation studio home
Team About — big heading, button and a collage of team member photos. For a creative team About
Work list — portrait key-shot work grid. For a video and content portfolio list
What we do — orbiting photo-ring hero · sentences · sticky step-by-step services. In the studio’s services intro

notes: Typeface: Helvetica Now (variable wdth 75) · Serrif are paid, so they were replaced with Archivo (wdth · wght axes) · Newsreader. Titles · headers · menus · buttons · nameplates · sticker text are English placeholders, so they are drawn in this typeface (handwriting in Kaushan Script).

Type placeholders: the original is a Dutch site so there are no Han or kana heading slots — wordmark, big headings, serif kickers, section names, menu, buttons, work, clients, team member names, roles, fields, cursor text, badges, stickers and footer (including the header line and footer that shared.js injects) are all English placeholders, and data-label says what goes in each slot

Font placeholder copy — slots kept in Korean: body paragraphs (p-m — index About · services supplementary text · three service descriptions · footer CTA invitation sentence). Since the body is sans-serif, it falls back to Korean · Pretendard as the README says

Team title: the original is a wordplay with serif ABCD + bold EF- + serif Team, slotting the brand initials into the alphabet. Instead of copying the original text, the same three pieces are kept as The SN-Team (serif word + brand initials + Team)

The logo, brush-stroke page-turn shape, six handwritten underline styles, stickers and name tags were redrawn in the same position, size and feel instead of using the original SVGs and images. The logo is a placeholder brush-script “Studio.” The page-turn brush stroke starts at the top left like the original, wraps once and curls inward as our own spiral.

Video: instead of the original HLS video (hls.js), placeholder mp4s of the same ratio and length (media/ — Hero square 6.08·9.91·4.74·4.87s, Service 3:4·4:5·9:16 14.96·20.08·25.04s, Work 4:5) are wired in with the original playback method — background video is muted, looping, autoplaying and pauses when less than 10% of it is on screen, and the poster fades away in 0.3s once playing, card video loads and plays when scrolled into view (revealed in 0.2s), and pauses 0.2s after leaving and resets to the start. Of the 30 Work cards, only the lengths of the 6 that played during recording were measured and reused across 12 slots
Only 12 of the 30 work cards were kept (the same form repeats). Work detail (case) pages were not recorded, so they were not built

The footer CTA title stays within 15 characters per line — the measurer leaves the cursor at the screen corner between hovers, and if the second line is wide (17 characters) the left letters fall within the 400px weight radius, so every footer hover picks up an extra weight movement

title: Stacked-photo loader and growing video window for a local shopping street
good_for: Sites for shopping streets, neighborhood associations, local organizations and small-town brands, including membership recruitment pages.

pages.use: Shopping street home — a loader where 10 photos stack up then clear and the logo rises, a Hero with a collage of three scattered photos plus vertical handwriting, About copy over a dark street photo, About split in two, a video window that grows while pinned, photos scattered around a finger logo, hand-drawn street map and shop list, how to get here, three News lines. For local, shopping-street or town homes

Shopping street About — handwriting above the photo that changes every 2 seconds, vertical handwriting on a white panel with centered body text, two story lines where the photo juts out of the panel, a three-column shop list (collapsible on phone), a membership info box, logo story. For association or union About pages and member shop lists

Member cheer program guide — a header where prose passes over a fixed finger logo, three benefit cards stacking while covering the previous card, scattered photos and copy, participation fee · how to join · add-friend boxes where a white circle spreads, FAQ accordion. For member recruitment, sponsorship and membership pages
News list — heading and square photo header, rows of date + one-line title (title drops down from above and splits), pagination. For notice and news lists
Single news post — date and title, body with a poster image and underlined subheadings, back button, three other news rows. For a single notice or event guide article

notes: Of the six layouts the original swaps by date for the Hero (fv__date1~6), only date1, the one currently in use, was built. The vw and svh values for the other five layouts are in the original front-page CSS, so the next person can add them by changing only the .fv__slideN positions.

The logo, vertical handwriting in the hero, About ‹bibibi›, finger logo, support program title art and distance map were image lettering or illustrations in the original, so they were redrawn as SVG and handwriting font (Nanum Pen Script). Position and size are the same, stroke shapes are approximate

The loader Lottie keeps the original tempo (50fps · 300 frames, 10 photos at frames 0 · 15 · 30 · 43 · 57 · 73 · 90 · 105 · 119 · 135, clearing 175→223, logo 182→289) and stacks 10 gray panels instead of photos. The logo letters stay in HTML and only their opacity follows the Lottie frames

The original street video (top.mp4) is cut off in the archive so its length could not be measured, so a 16:9 12-second gray placeholder video (media/movie.mp4) is used. The YouTube embed spot is a 3:2 placeholder box
Store list cut from 31 to 12, news list cut to 6 rows (same type repeated)

Footer photo slideshow is paused while off-screen — while visible it follows the original tempo (3s + 1s crossfade). Off-screen transitions got mixed into hover timing measurements, so it was changed after checking
On phones (768 and below) the bottom-right ‹⋮ Menu› button overlaps the library preview strip (list · note N) — turn the strip off with N to see it. The button position is as in the original
The Contact page was not recorded so it was not built — the Contact link connects to the join-info box in About (about.html#join)

title: Black-and-white thumbnail grid with diagonally expanding previews
good_for: Photo and artwork archives, personal photography portfolios, and browse-the-thumbnails first screens.

pages.use: Photo archive home page — left, an 18-cell black-and-white thumbnail grid, and right, a gray surface with a WebGL preview where a hand-held photo folds and unfolds diagonally, plus a year line and falling white leaves. A Grid↔Slider pill turns the cells into a one-row film strip so vertical scroll becomes horizontal movement. For the Hero of photo archives and works lists.

About — a short profile with name, intro text, a repeating video band cropped to 70px height, camera and contact laid out in a 24-column grid on one centered line. For the About menu of photographers and personal sites

notes: The photo detail that thumbnails open (original /summer2025 · /record01 … single photo + small photo picker + zoom Flip) wasn’t recorded in the archive, so it was not built — cell links are href="#" It is a placeholder and goes nowhere when clicked. The original CSS (.p-single__grid…) has the frame, so the next person can link it to detail.html

The texture on the preview boards is a placeholder canvas painted in Skin colors (a diagonal X + what photo it stands for) instead of a photo — the original is a color photo, and the thumbnails use a grayscale filter, so they are black and white. To use photos, swap .ff-ref for an img and load it with THREE.TextureLoader instead of index.js paint().
The About video band is a 16:9 · 9.2s looping placeholder video (media/bio-bg.mp4, fragments floating on a gray background) — the original video shows drifting leaves
The leaf art does not use the original svg — we redrew our own leaf (two-lobed blade + stalk)
Font is Inter Tight 500·600 instead of the original PP Neue Montreal Medium (paid)
The original reopens the page when the initial width crosses 767px (except on touch devices) — the copy does the same. Changing the width to test it reopens the page
The barba transition only runs when opened over http. Opened as a file, it covers with the noise film for 1.5s and goes to the next page (the next page starts from the loader like a first load)

title: App landing with popping stickers and small animated UI illustration cards
good_for: Mobile app and fintech landings that show features as small animated UI illustrations, with a blog, changelog and developer docs around the product.

pages.use: App home page — hero where 63 stickers pop out on both sides and float, stretching and bouncing when dragged, five feature cards whose state changes every 2 seconds, three phones playing in turn, four sharing sections, four small UI graphics beside a pinned title, two-row review marquee, FAQ. For app and fintech product landings
News list — big title and filter buttons, three-column rows of date, title and excerpt. For blog and press lists
One article — header line with date · author · tag, two-line title, 700px body with a three-phone image panel · quote · share · addendum. For launch announcements and blog posts
Changelog — entry rows with the date on the left and a dot on a vertical line that follows sticky, with a spinning clock at the end. For product update logs and release notes
Developer docs first page — docs intro with a collapsible table of contents on the left and two product cards. For developer docs and help first pages

notes: Hero’s 63 stickers, the four phone-screen stickers, the CTA art and the safety mascot were not copied from the original art. They were redrawn as our own shapes with the same position, size and color feel (baked with stickers.cjs in /tmp and embedded in index.html). Hand, foot and expression details of the original characters and some props (map, speech-bubble tail, etc.) are simplified — more drawing can pick up from here

Two Lottie animations (footer logo spin 1080²·66f, easy card paper plane 250²·120f) are baked from our own artwork with lottie/make.cjs at the same panel size and frames. Playback behavior (when the cursor arrives, play one full turn to the end · 2x speed once) is the same as the original. The fun card’s nine emoji images are swapped for white symbol SVGs, and the dance motion (.75s (.63,.01,.54,1.03) ×10) uses the same keyframes

The 9 phone-screen videos and the intro video are placeholder videos (media/*.mp4, ffmpeg) with the same ratio (1170×2532 → 390×844, 16:9) and the same lengths (2.7 to 6.0s). As in the original, once visible the three phones play once from the left, and when one ends the next phone follows (1.1x, name 42px lower, spring 4 · 800 · 80).

The five card illustrations and four detail illustrations carry over the original SVG sizes (297×135 · 220×80 · 291×96), state counts, 2s cycle (analysis pill 1.75s) and spring as they are, but text is svg text instead of paths and icons are our own symbols. The strong card’s number count runs from the previous value to the new value over the spring length (the original te function length could not be read, so the same spring is used — a judgment call)

The Mobile and Desktop illustrations (original SVG artwork) in the original header’s Get Started window are placeholder boxes, and login, download and external links are left as #. For the docs section, only the first page of the original separate docs app was built (collapsible TOC, two product cards).

Select tool: in the original hitTest, match receives a HitResult and can’t see data, so nothing gets filtered, and pressing a chosen symbol again grabs the selection box bundle, so the box is dragged instead of the symbol. Here, as intended, the search leaves out the selection boxes. Also the selection box is always placed on the top layer (building) so it doesn’t hide under other layers (the original puts it on the last-written layer)

Images loaded by undo are repainted in the current light or dark skin (the original keeps the colors from when they were captured). When exporting to print, the selection box is left out (the original captures it too)

The original opening curtain that blocks the chocolate Hero is a chroma-key (teal key) video — our shader draws it on the same clock (5.5s, during the last 14% the panel height .387 rises further as a cube, bag falls at 0.001, head shows at .5 are original values): for the first .7s it covers in from the left, from 1.3s it peels back over 2.1s power2.inOut, and fifteen rows of drips trail the curtain .16 to .46s late. The carousel values are the original’s as they are: gap .11244+.13 (phone .15), each slot pushed back .25 (phone .1), tilt −80° (landscape view +10°), wheel deltaY×.002 · snap to slot after 200ms, drag ×.5, keys ←→, SmoothDamp .15·.2 (phone .14) · damping 10, hovered bar lifts .01 · −10° flat, darkens by .5 × the share far from center, shrinks in the last 10%, unfold es 1→0 1s power3.out (.5s late), stage tilt ±.9° (1−.92^frame), camera fov 35.115 · (0,.1195,.4878) · −5°.

Pressing a bar in the original enters that flavor’s detail (camera zoom + unwrap video + per-flavor background color), but the detail was not recorded so it was not built — pressing a non-center bar only brings it to the center. notes: The Hero and process videos are placeholder videos with the same ratio, length and playback behavior. Cutout animation over a product photo (original webp 512 square · 120 frames × 0.1s = 12-second loop · infinite) is a rolling round-plate placeholder of the same plate size (1.2 and 1.08× the photo) and same tempo (steps 120 · 12s) — the rolling pose was set from looking at the original 12 frames, so angles are not identical per frame

Wordmark, nav and section titles are SVG artwork in the original, so Fredoka and Barlow Condensed text is fitted to the original artwork width with textLength. /  At 390 on phone, the original has a phone icon on the left of the header row, and the three pillars · services become a one-line list holding photos — our copy is built the same way, but the phone motion values (panel blur --panel-fade) couldn’t be measured.

notes: The original is a single page (pages: [] in pages.json), so there are no subpages.

The terrain map is a three scene like the original (r185, fog 7~34, 50° field of view), but the original’s national terrain data (geo.json and height image) is not used — we built our own height field of an arc-shaped island chain (fourteen spine points, width .8~2) and draw seven contour tiers (coast .9, the rest .6 transparent). Same scale as the original (latitude 1° = 1.25, longitude 1° = 1.0125) stands section pins (ring · dot · light column red at the bottom fading upward) at each section’s latitude (43.08 · 39.56 · 34.11 · 32.37), and the camera is joined in a straight line so it sits above that pin (height 4.2, tilt .9) when passing the section center. The original’s place-name label panel · depth-of-field post-processing · route line were reduced.

The 24-photo wall, large Section photos, photo panels and photo strips are placeholders describing subject, light and composition. title: Dark product page with a 3D arched corridor, blackletter headline and cursor-chasing border glows
good_for: B2B SaaS, AI agent and fintech landing pages that hook with mood first, then show app mockups for lists, steps, payments and code.

pages.use: Product intro one-pager — curtain (arch line around the logo) → 3D corridor arch hero (1.5 screens pinned, arch 4.65×) → logo band → invoice app mockup → customer quote and dot chart → three-step tab window → recipient checkout screen (agent panel opens) → two matching cases → rule band and four security items → code window → FAQ → email invitation → stone sculpture footer. notes: The original is a single page (pages: [] in pages.json), so there are no subpages.

Hero 3D: instead of the original nave model (nave.glb·Draco·KTX2) and the debris image in front, we built it from our own primitives (a LatheGeometry fluted-plate column with an eight-round-leaf capital, an arcade wall with semicircular openings cut in, semicircular vaults and transverse ribs, floor slabs, dodecahedron debris) and our own stone-grain canvas textures. Camera (-14.1·0.4·20mm·film 36·lens shift .155), lighting (blue left ×1, orange right ×.7, three spots plus one point light, watts/4π), fog (FogExp2 .028), tone (Neutral, exposure 2^-1.4), light orbs, scroll (smoothstep up to .77, rise 3, 20→85mm, light down 6, dim .2/.15, pool .1~.55), cursor (±2.2°·±1.2°, 260ms), and the approach from 1.6 back behind the curtain over 2.6s expo.out are the original values unchanged. It is not as dense as the original capital’s Corinthian leaf carving and cracked stone texture — the next person can carve the capitals further.

Bloom uses the same strength .35, radius .9 and threshold .5 as the original (three UnrealBloomPass, 5 stages), built with our own shader in 3 stages (1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 13-tap Gaussian). The original’s frame-time quality reduction (calibrate, 5-stage quality) was not included.

The hero title uses free fonts UnifrakturMaguntia (blackletter) and Cormorant Garamond (italic, uppercase), layered in the same place inside the original box (3.096em × 2.397em), instead of the original SVG lettering. The footer sign-off ”Built by …” uses the same blackletter.

The two footer stone layers (back · front rendered images) are photo slots (data-label), and the front layer only has a stone-mass silhouette (gradient + clip-path) drawn so the slot is recognizable. An ellipse mask is used instead of the grid mask image (grid-mask.webp). The fog shader (4-layer fbm · .42~.8 · bottom 35% · amber from 45% on the right), two dust layers, entry parallax (−22% · −11% · +8%) and the grid cursor opposing 5 · 3px 1.2s are as in the original.
The 13 client logos are English wordmark placeholders in assorted typefaces (Client …) instead of the original SVGs.

Product window edge light (edge-light-follow): in the original, several windows in one section are grouped together and the light moves to the window nearest the cursor (the mail card and checkout screen in the checkout section), but in this part each window runs on its own — in the checkout section the light is attached only to the checkout screen. The rest zones (top 30%, corners, left 30%), the 12px proximity, the 18% skip and the speed are the original values.

Not captured by swapping theme.css between light and dark skins. library-lint reports color 0, font 0 and out-of-skin variables 0. The stone color of the 3D scene mixes --kf-ink and --kf-bg, and the lighting reads --site-lamp-cold·--site-warm, so it follows the skin.

Screensaver (logo bouncing at 160px/s after 50s hands-off) was not captured by waiting 50s headless, so only the code path was checked.

Selection box (dragging on empty background), notification stacking (elastic.out(1,.75)) and dock menu height opening were not extracted as parts — the main motions (icon drag drag-lift, window desk-window, gravity gravity-toggle, screensaver bounce-drift) were extracted first and the 150 minutes ran out. title: Intro paragraph with line drawings embedded in words and a one-tab portfolio
good_for: Solo designer or developer intro pages that state what they do in one sentence and switch panels via tabs for about, work, writing and contact.

notes: The 3D line drawings beside words rebuild the shaders and shapes (icons.js) with the same three r185 orthographic camera as the original (±140 cells, base π/4·π/4) and the same scene values (spring tension and friction, unfold angle, index delay, loops of 7s and 5s). The inner half-line of the outline at the neck of the melted-together cube (a smooth, edgeless joint) is measured in the original by marching the ray one more time. Here it is measured by screen derivatives of how far the normal turns away, so the line around the neck looks broken in places.

The original cuts a word caught on the enlarged frame between letters and continues its tail behind the frame (duplicate word + clip-path, with the cut position taken from each letter’s canvas measureText ink width). Here the whole word moves behind the frame or to the next line. Cutting would require rebuilding the word span (.g-w) used by the decode effect into a per-letter structure, so this was not changed in this version. Words that change lines blur out and back over .75em before and after them (the 12-step look before and after), same as the original.

The avatar is a newly drawn hand-drawn face. The original swaps three drawings — front, looking up, looking down — according to the mouse position, but since those drawings are original illustrations that cannot be carried over, the pupils follow the mouse in a single drawing. The hidden garden page (.garden) that opens when you take off the glasses and throw them off the screen was not recorded in the archive, so there is no screen to measure — the glasses fly off and come back.

Tab switching: the original is a single-page app so only the board changes. Following the site-wide rule, pages are split into files and open fresh, but the underline slides in over .36s from the tab pressed on the previous page and the scroll position carries over (sessionStorage).

Clicking a word link captures the current screen with snapdom like the original (within 1 second) and starts a WebGL page turn (wraps around a cylinder from the right edge, radius = …short side × .3, .9s power2.inOut) peels it away (curl.js, the shader is newly written). The original is a single-page app, so it curls right on top of the new view, but here the captured image is handed over through sessionStorage, covers the new page from its very first frame, and then curls away. snapdom is npm’s 3.7.0 (MIT). The original bundle is a later build than that (it has a reconcile warning message not in 3.7.0), so the closest published version was used.

contact.html is a page not recorded in pages.json, so it was built by measuring the real screen and the live original’s contact css and js (5.BH35d6IE.css·nodes/5.b9zC-LLG.js) — Send is disabled when empty (ink panel → hover charcoal .16s), and Copy email turns ink color at .16s and green for 1.6 seconds once copied. The chat field is a placeholder that asks name→email→message in turn and sends nowhere (the original’s message editing and real sending were not built).

Geist has no Korean glyphs, so Korean placeholders appear in Pretendard. The intro sentence runs 3 lines at 1440 (original 3 lines) and 5 lines at 390 (original 6 lines). The hidden sentence cipher swaps syllables for other syllables, so the original’s letter-width fitting (--fit letter-spacing) is not used.

Page turn is not split out as a part (_fx) — before the incoming page paints its first image <head> The inline script has to cover the front-screen image to avoid flicker, but the part loads at the end of body and cannot take that spot. When reusing it, move curl.js and the g-curl snippet of the five pages’ head scripts together.

notes: The original is a single page (pages: [] in pages.json), so there are no subpages.

Fonts: original PP Brand Light (paid) was replaced with Bodoni Moda (optical size 36, 400). Its capitals are slightly wider, so heading placeholder text is 1–3 characters shorter than the original (if the section 3 title wraps one more line, the document grows 79px and the timing of the lower sections shifts).

The original scroll motion is not GSAP but the Lenis scroll position divided by the screen count (a), using smoothstep ranges that drive css variables (--forge · --ink · --phone · --vsheet · --s5rot …). Moved into index.js with the same method and the same range values (clock 1.9~2.6, sheet 0~.35, card .46~.74, fold .52~.82, statue late = Statue top edge + .9~2.1 screens — the original uses absolute values of 7.9~9.1 screens, so we changed them to relative values to fit our document height).
