(The original card width 2.4 gets its height from the texture ratio, so our 1.5-ratio cards looked 1.4× larger. Measured on screen and set width to 1.75.) Of the original card shader’s bend (uBend), blur smear (uSmear, proportional to spin speed) and uFlip (2.15~2.6, which flips cards in the accept section), only the bend is done in geometry. Smear and flip are left out — for the next person to continue with a ShaderMaterial.
The hand response that turns the spiral by drag or wheel (added to the original M angle) is not included — only the self-rotation (.15) plus magnet and tilt.

Statues: the original metal models (glb, six animals) were rebuilt as metal sculptures from basic shapes (sphere, cylinder, cone) of the same size — only the head ornament differs per animal. Lighting (white 20 · blue 24.5, original positions) · exposure .95 · switching (push 5.9 · .26 turn · ×2.3 coming in · ×.2 going out) · idle sway are the original values, while the switch length of 1.1s could not be found in the bundles, so it was tuned by eye.

The vine waveform on the voice sheet (original vineGarden · App canvas) and the final section’s light rays (rays canvas) were redrawn as our own canvas art at the same position · size (the original formulas were not carried over).

The develop shader does not copy the original shader. Customer logos are our shapes + Brand 00 placeholders, no photo, logo or video files are used.

The loader, top band, left band, end screen and phone cover all use the single LETTERS table in shared.js, so to change the logo just replace that table (the module-lens-word part uses the same data-rect shape).

Letter widths differ slightly from the original words, so the moment the box touches may come a little earlier or later — positions are re-measured from the word widths, so changing the words keeps everything aligned.
With prefers-reduced-motion, skip the loader and start from the band, table of contents and text show right away, pinned sections show the final scene, and photo shader and parallax are turned off.

Below 1200px width and on touch screens, only the original-style ”desktop only” veil is shown (a wordmark filling the floor panel, with the lens focus circling the four corners for .7s each). Line rise: the original smart-text lifts a mask (40px→0) and the text (120%→0) separately for each line, both over 2s with cubic-bezier(.6,.14,0,1). The existing part line-rise (single layer, y 120 · 2s · .1 per line) reproduces the same curve and duration, but the second layer where the mask rises 40px on its own is missing. notes: Logo shader: the original Framer Shader ‹Logo Gradient› (shape height map + half-resolution cursor push field + sine turbulence palette) was rewritten from scratch as our WebGL2 shader _fx/logo-flow-gl — values (angle 238·bend 1·outline .8·scale .3·speed .4 melt·turbulence .41/1.25/8·waves 5·push .8·radius .9·remain .28·stretch 1) are the original’s as-is. Shape depth is measured at paste time by 3-4 chamfer distance and spread over 6 cells, the palette is an OKLab linear mix (original LCH), and the turbulence start phase is a fixed value unlike the original’s random seed, so the pattern grain is alike but not identical. The logo is our own rounded two letters (o·n) at the same 105:58 ratio and weight, instead of the original nu.

The canvas cell is 50% wide (70% on phone) and 720:635 as in the original, with the shape sitting inside it via contain. The cell appears as in the original: the hero group fades in with a .5s tween (.44,0,.56,1) after .5s, and the shader layer uses a spring (overshoot .2·.4s → CustomEase baked at damping ratio .8·22.5rad/s).

Sub-page big sentences use per-word opacity springs like the original (stiffness 400 · damping 30 → CustomEase gu-word), with delays in the original DOM order (.1·.3·.35·.4…·.9, images .25/.65). The work detail has no appear effect in the original either.

The interaction curve carries over the Framer curve values stamped in the original css (650ms soft approach · card 400ms slight overshoot) into CSS linear(). The 3.7~4.1px settle-down bounce of the card (10% overshoot) is baked in as a spring with damping ratio .59 and 17rad/s.

Next strip: like the original, when the link is idle the box is 1.02x larger (1469×562), and on hover it goes straight to box size and fades to .6 over a 650ms curve. On the first page the 720 box is cut off at the document end (651).

Guestbook cards stick to the bottom of the screen inside the Next band cell like the original (position: sticky). The original feature of sending and showing messages left while the screen rests needs a server and was not built (the form does not send).

title: 3D portfolio where each wheel turn changes the world around a glowing stone, with the making-of as the loader
good_for: 3D and interactive developer portfolios, single-screen stages that page through projects, and showcases that change mood per project.

pages.use: 3D portfolio hero — stone outline where the making process is the loader · glowing stone whose world changes with each wheel · work list · cylinder title. Interactive showcase that flips through works one by one
About me — a sideways-turned stone scene and an intro panel. For a 3D developer’s About
Single work detail — landscape canvas, hero video variant, paper pieces, title, work info panel, previous/next. For 3D and interactive work intros

notes: The original is a three WebGPU/TSL node shader. Here it was rebuilt as a three r174 WebGL ShaderMaterial. The stone pattern uses value-noise fbm for bands, grain and clouds. Transmission first renders the scene minus the stone into a half-resolution render target, then reads it warped toward the normal at the edges (refraction) and tints it with the stone color. The original’s blue-noise accumulation and post-processing (bloom etc.) are not there yet. Next person: per-frame blue-noise jitter plus blending with the previous frame. Stone, ground, sky and dead trees are all procedural

Water reflection: an upside-down clone of the stone sits under the ground, with the puddle spot opened translucently and ripples added — vertices farther from the surface sway wider horizontally (sin 13·31, time 1.7·2.3) and ripple streaks break up the light. It is not a reflection render target, so only the stone is reflected, not the sky·trees.

The loader spins as in the original — outline .9s, then a .5s pause, then the 2.6s stage (Ee = time/2.6) in front, render-stage windows (wireframe, clay, UV, normal, transmission, final) open, and from 56% a snapshot of the window is held while each 20px cell blends into the final scene by smoothstep (from the center), at blend .4 (75%) the cylinder spins twice in 1.5s (1−(1−x)⁴, appearing in the first .3s), and at .8 (87%) the headband lights up. The wireframe window is an icosahedron mesh with the same silhouette as the stone (a dense stone mesh looks like a gray lump). The title strip above the window isn’t in the held image, so it drops out when blending begins

Cylinder title: the original wraps MSDF text onto a WebGL cylinder. Here, two images around the name (fill and outline) are drawn on a canvas and wrapped onto a three cylinder (radius .75 of screen width · .82 on phone, camera distance 1400 · 700px on phone), and a shader fills only one front slot (±15°), so neighboring names bend along the cylinder. It is canvas text rather than MSDF, so the edges get soft when scaled up very large. The title font Integral CF (paid) is replaced by Archivo Expanded 900 + Korean Black Han Sans, and the body font Neue Montreal by Inter Tight.

Stone opening: in the original, the stone shatters in the same scene, pieces fly, and it unfolds into a video panel. As a multi-page site, on the first page the stone twitches and brightens and then moves on to a pixel curtain, and the detail page picks up with a shard burst (1.6s expo.out) and a stone shape → rectangle unfolding (72-point clip-path interpolation, 1.4s). For About, the original moves the camera within one scene (travelDuration 1.7), but here it is split in two across the pages: the first page covers 60% of the path in 1.08s, and the About page continues the rest from that spot in 1s (power1.out). The original’s stone burst, spinning burst and spin are absent.

Details at detail.html?p=0..5 change the hue, title and prev/next. The two recorded details share the same type so they were built as one. Of the 12 original projects, only the stone and scene values of 6 were carried over

Sound: the original has background music and effects. The original sound files can’t be used and placeholder sound isn’t made yet, so there is only the button shape and the on/off line drawing (starting on, as in the original)
The phone detail is hidden because the original phone screen shows no large title, and the phone intro drops the stones and keeps only text like the original
The 404 page wasn’t recorded, so it wasn’t built
sites pull stopped on an about file/folder name collision (EISDIR), so the original was read directly out of the archived HAR (wheel formula in _nuxt/Cd_dFser.js)

The slow rotation of the stone at rest (t × .06) does not exist in the original (decorRotation 0, spin only on swipe), so it was removed. Mouse parallax (camera .25·.12, stone .18) is not in the original code either (the camera only does openTilt after the stone opens), so it was removed when backfilling the cursor.

Font placeholder copy: title font (Archivo extended 900) slots — cylinder titles (name in shared.js GC.PROJECTS)·large detail titles — are two English lines Work/One…Six as in the original. Original names like CLARTÉ/WORLD·1 MILLION/BLACK run 3–9 characters per line, but Project/Name 01 (7 characters) overlaps the neighboring name on phone (390) by exceeding one cylinder cell (about 167px), so each line was cut to under 5 characters

Font slot text decision: the header name, about menu, work list, close, view site and copy email are English in the original but sit in body-font slots (Neue Montreal → Inter Tight), so even if Korean falls to the Pretendard pair (sans-serif ↔ gothic) the character barely changes — judged to be outside the README ‹places used as title font› and left in Korean
The thumbnail was shot with --wait 9000 on shot.cjs --thumb so the cylinder title is visible after the loader (render-stage window) ends (the default 2.5s lands mid-loader)

good_for: Company anniversary microsites (book release, messages from fifty people, events, office move, new symbol) and ad or design company sites with big English headings and four-column work grids.

pages.use: brand anniversary special page — blue monochrome portrait photo grid KV · commemorative book · folded paper card messages from 50 people · anniversary events and goods · clickable office floor plan · a new symbol assembled from pieces. On the company founding anniversary special
Work list — large heading, work grid, pagination, filter pills and category sheet. For an ad or design company work list
Company info — office photo, intro, overview, address map, organization, client logos, award list, recruiting notice. For a one-page company profile of an ad agency
News list — large title, row list, pagination and filter sheet. For company notice lists
One work in detail — a full-bleed photo that stays behind while its bottom is cut into an ellipse, work info, photos and video, person-in-charge card. For ad and campaign work intros

notes: The brand-anniversary special page and the main site’s sub-pages are designed differently even in the original. The header (logo, vertical menu, weather clock), phone menu, weather panel, cursor and page transition are bundled in shared, and the brand-anniversary page hides the header and shows only a menu button, like the original.

The brand anniversary Interaction responses were matched to the original CSS and formulas. See more (color changes immediately · arrow 1.25× at .25s, on press the photo WAAPI moves 25px up ±15° → 1s power4.out · .1s apart), the office dot (80px button · 15px dot breathing at 1.8s · ring 15→63px at 2.2s, on hover the dot goes 1.8× · breathing .8s), the party stamp tilting to follow the mouse (PartyLogoMouseEffect: X 16° / down 23° · Y 42° · Z 10° · 9% per step, only within about one screen), and the magnetic close on the book band and speech window (MagneticHoverEffect). On hover over the pill filter button, three ink-colored panels rise from below at .7s, as in the original (.08s apart · .2/.4/.7).

Sub-page transitions use the same swup 4.6.1 + preload plugin as the original (preloads visible and hovered links, linkToSelf navigate, back navigation also transitions) and only #swup (body + footer) moves. The curtain uses the same three-curve SVG paths as the original TransitionView — on exit it fills from below at .15s intervals over .85s power3.inOut, and on enter after .1s (0 on phone) the top layer lifts over .65s. Colors rotate through seven sets (--site-wave-N-1·2·3 made by rotating the accent color), mixed in turn. Links to the brand-anniversary page go outside swup (data-no-swup). When opened as a file (file://), fetch is blocked, so instead of swup it moves on 1s after the curtain fills and the new page lifts only the top layer.

The 50-card values were checked in the original settings (WORD_LOAD_MORE_ANIMATION: 1s · .1s stagger · power4.out(.23,1,.32,1) · fold 35° · photo 25px up ±15° random, rotation axis at the lower corner of the tilted side / WORD_MODAL_OPEN_FLIP_ANIMATION: .5s power2.inOut). Of the 14 cards, 4 'See more'Spread it out as (the original starts with 9 · 21 at a time).

The symbol assembly was scrubbed with a newly drawn SVG: a half-circle sun, two arcs, 40 outline→50 fill. The original’s piece count and trajectories could not be carried over (the original piece art could not be measured).
Text logos (drive! and GOODS spots) use Alfa Slab One 'title!'·'ITEMS' Rewritten from scratch (the original is a hand-drawn image file). The original stamp is 'Festival' Text on a semicircle.
The office map was redrawn as a striped floor plan, and clicking any of 7 dots opens a seat window (prev · next). Original map lines and seat layout are matched only in similar form.
The vimeo video on work detail is only a playback bar placeholder — the original is a vimeo player (click to play), so the same player cannot show our video.
Fonts: aktiv-grotesk, Helvetica Neue and two Japanese gothic faces (all paid) → Inter and Noto Sans KR. Font loading has moved to theme.css.

Skin: cleaned up 40 hard-coded colors and 7 variables outside theme.css (five tag colors and two fonts) — the tag colors are --site-cyan, red, yellow, green and pink, rotated with oklch from the accent color (royal blue), and the fonts are --kf-font-ko and --kf-font-letter.

The site cursor was rebuilt with the same structure and formula as the original Cursor. The body re-chases every frame at .8s expo.out, a second point chasing the same way stretches the shape by its distance from the mouse (1 + e/1000 × 2, vertical minimum .5, weak 1.6/.8, strong 4/.1) and rotates in that direction, keeping a 3D matrix at z .001. The inner circle is hidden at 0 (.1s), page number 34/12 (.2s, stuck to the center, difference), work thumbnail 80/12 + Detail text·arrow, contact 160/12 + lightGray + handshake Lottie, next page 0, and outside links hide the circle and show a new-window icon (.2s). During page transitions there is a loading-number circle (56/12 back.out(2)). The brand-anniversary page has no cursor, like the original. Not carried over: the canvas metaballs that melt the circle and element together on outside links·dots (CursorCanvas · WorksDetailBtnMetaball) and the vimeo preview over work thumbnails — only the icon·circle size match.

The brand-anniversary cover is rebuilt like the original book__anniversary with three images (car · person · 50, our own art). They drop in from 35px above over 1.3s cubic-bezier(.86,0,.07,1) (year 0 · person .35 · car .7s delay). They bounce for .9s away from the side the pointer is on (±12° · starting at 8px, halving each time). Once visible, they bounce on their own every 3 seconds (perspective 600px · 1s linear · .6 · 1.2s sequence). As in the original, the More button is a magnetic hover target and the card’s folded corner does not grow on hover.

The subpage css of the main site is loaded all at once like the original (works·about·news·detail.css on all four pages) — swup swaps only #swup, so styles can’t be attached per page. Each page uses a different prefix (co-·nw-·dt-·hs-grid), so they don’t collide.

notes: Uses the same library builds as the original. notes: The cylinder bend of the hero photo strip was rewritten with our own shader (part cylinder-tilt-strip). Putting a WebGL panel in every cell as the original does would exceed 16 including loop clones, and earlier panels would get dropped, so one WebGL panel per strip draws and copies into each cell’s 2D panel. The values (rotateY 25°, depth 150px, scale .07, crop 5%, curvature .75, phone 12°·50·.01·0·.35, brightness .7+.3cos) are the original’s as is.

The central device screens in the original are photos of phones and a laptop showing real app screens — drawn here as line-art frames (two phones and a laptop) with screen placeholders in the same spot (210px from top, 659px wide). The right-hand AI chat side panel · the bottom-left ”See it, touch it” popup · the blue pill ”Download Materials · Demo” button are inserted later by external third-party widgets, so they were left out of the site frame. Work list — large title, per work a name · one-liner · category tag and a 2×2 photo panel, a band of testimonial cards that advance every 5 seconds. For case list pages
Post list — post rows in a narrow column with title, two-line summary, category pill and date. For blog and note lists

Studio About — a long text column (subheads, bold keyword list, past workplaces), three bands of big flowing numbers, a two-row team list. For company and CEO introductions.
Single work (dark section): big three-line title and badge, a left column of app screen photos with sticky text on the right, a testimonial card, related work. For app and product case study details.

notes: Motion engine: the original is built on a React-based site builder with its motion runtime and site bundle, and the same values were moved to CSS and our motion parts. Entrance is .6s cubic-bezier(.6,0,.05,1) (fade-up), service cells are spring-appear with spring bounce .2 · .4s solved to stiffness 466 and damping 34.5, and button text roll and menu panel use a curve unfolded from the spring as CSS linear()
The title typeface FK Raster Roman Compact Smooth is paid, so the closest free option, Instrument Serif, is used — the pixel-edge feel is lost (only the footer wordmark is a pixel SVG)

Work card corner notch (notch-corner-card): the original variant Start X → X (No TR·No BL·Diagonal·None) piece scale 0/1·.6s [.6,0,.05,1] was read from the bundle. The piece closing in 400ms after 90ms when hovering a related Work card was measured, and its curve was moved to linear(). The large Hero panel·Work list·detail related cards have no such hover in the original, so hover: off. The photo corner radius change (8 → 26) between growing Start → X on appearing was not carried over.

The original crypto service section has the same type as product, so it was built as a single service.html. The items inside the header menu panel (Work · Studio) were not recorded from the original panel, so they are three placeholders.
The cookie notice only carries over the look, hover (.6 · .25s) and dismissal (transparent · 10px down · .4s) of the original site-builder cookie component — no real consent saving.

The first page flow follows today’s original (logo strip → full-width stack of work panels → logo grid). The service section that exists only in the archived copy (11-04 DOM) (what we do well + 13 photo/video cells) and the closing panel (cursor photo trail) are sections with code in the original, so they are kept before the logo grid. The archived copy’s Why section (pixel strip) and the sideways work strip (Morphing Ticker) are not in today’s original, so they were dropped.

Interaction responses were measured from the original and matched — menu cell widths (27·79·36·33, 12 apart) fixed at the original positions, menu text color .37s ease-in-out, panel open opacity .18s, ‹Contact› button background 90ms then 400ms (redrawn linear()) · text shifts 27px down (up on release) and returns at .54s (redrawn eleven-point keyframes), cookie button .6·.25s, deep-dive row .7, question open (icon .16s then .4s · lower line slide .42s · answer .16s then .42s). The post list section is left out because the original has no entrance or hover

Hero wordmark in four layers (echo-slice-scroll): measuring the archived copy, the three clones inside Logo Wrapper (filled with the background color) rise straight, following −24 · −48 · −72px during scroll 0 → 229px (above the panel −1 −24 ~ + panel height) (at 40px −4.19 · −8.38 · −12.58 — the copy uses the same values). The wordmark and mark are our block mark + ”Studio” text, not the original logo.

Below the Work section ”Trusted by industry leaders”, the original was not a logo grid but a Framer Slideshow of seven testimonial cards. It was built with spring-edge-slideshow (two cards on wide screens · one on phone · card height 440 · gap 24 · every 5 seconds it moves 468px with spring 200/40/1 · cards outside the panel are .9 scale and transparent · bottom-left arrows 48 with gap 10 · no dragging). The photo panel in the Work row was also corrected to the original’s 2×2 four cells (gap 16 · turns on at 20% visible with .6s cubic-bezier(.12,.23,.5,1)). The ”Previous/Next photo strip per project” noted by the previous student does not exist in the original, and those buttons belonged to this testimonial strip

Service section question open: details is replaced with a button plus a 0-height panel so the answer is already drawn even when closed (opacity 0, no offset), the frame after a press it opens, and the answer, shifted down by its own height in that frame, rises into place over 500ms. Icon and opacity use a 533ms linear() curve redrawn from the original — question-open jank 0 at all three widths

notes: Page transition: the original bundle includes barba but never calls init. The Transition module, when a same-site link is clicked, fades #page out with .6s expo.inOut (after .3s, or after 1s for drawer links) and opens the document fresh. The new document fades in only the first page with .6s power4.out (TransitionEnd → hero text), while subpages stand immediately. The copy is built with the same fade (using barba would be smoother than the original and change the feel)

The ScrollSmoother in the card is only a name inside the bundled ScrollTrigger code and is not used. GSAP uses the _shared build instead of the original 3.11.5

Loader clouds: the original uses three white cloud photos (cloud01~03.png) — we drew white radial-gradient blobs with the same layers and timing (1.5s linear 1.5x · blur, .8s · 1.2s overlap). The logo color change (#cccd88 → navy 1s linear) uses the --intro-tone variable with the same length

Specs: instead of the original ship.svg and specification-bg.svg art, a simple side-view line drawing of a ship (same place, width 1197). Number count 2.5s circ.out and section top edge at screen center are as in the original

The volcano eruption carries over only the flash, glow, three streams, four flying drops and shake from the original’s lava stream mask, droplets, tongues and overlapping blobs. The original’s lava pool and dripping drops are missing (the next person can add them to .hl-burst).

In the loader the original hides the real wordmark until the water drains (wordmark-held) and shows imitation lettering — ours does the same. The loader’s letter position calculation can drift if the font arrives late (it is measured before waiting for font ready).

Menu and footer letter-roll links were first built with the existing char-roll part (CSS transition), but its exit length measured 80ms longer than the original GSAP (.5s power3.out, .022s per letter), so we switched to the GSAP roll in shared.js like the original (plus the other links dimming to .45 and shifting .3em). pages.use: One-screen work stage portfolio — wheel-driven WebGL works · corner HUD · pill menu · view switch (film strip · orbit) · work-open detail · percent loader. For showing 5~10 works large, one at a time

notes: Work photos and videos are WebGL textures, so the placeholder in the DOM is drawn onto a canvas (a pool of light in the work’s base color + X + label) and uploaded. As in the original, the first three works are videos (16:9 27.03s · 4:3 13.47s · 4:3 13.17s, looping, media/work-*.mp4 placeholder videos) with the texture refreshed every frame, and the last two are photos. Inside the [data-works] li ·

The blackletter Y in the center is a shape extruded with three.js from a Y outline we drew (height 1, thickness .1, bevel .0072 in 12 steps), and the reflection is our own shader using the same formula as the original (blend the sky azimuth band above and below at the horizon ±3°, Fresnel F0 .6, grain .12, brightness .45~.85 in the garment’s ink color) — the sky band layout is ours, so the reflection pattern differs from the original. The original glyph outline and environment values were not carried over.

Opening a project uses the original values (move 1.7s power2.inOut · cover zoom 1.95s +.2 · wipe 1.95s +.36 power1.inOut · wave 4.25s power2.out · lift .5s). Our shader produces a wave that lifts the photo row up to 210px and a wipe that covers it diagonally with the cover photo from the bottom right. The formulas the original uses to compute the wave and wipe are not ported, so the wave shape is not identical. The DOM detail covers in .3s after the wipe ends at 2.31s (the meaning of the original show 1.5 could not be read). When opened from orbit, it starts from the rectangle that card occupied on screen.

Film strip (02) follows the original exactly — wheel major-axis value × .556 × .0252 / 10 slots, after stopping .15s later it snaps to the nearest slot at .155, follow .07, bend = 152·H/1080·late(=|.12×late cell×10|, max 3, follows at .07).

The loader percentage is not real download progress but rises from 0 to 100 over 1.4s (it is a placeholder, so there is nothing to download). After that, the 5×5 cells 5s, UI 1.5s expo.out and title 140%→0 are original values.

Like the original, the portrait uses WebGL to overlay two photos and cuts the top photo with an fbm-noise edge only around the mouse (radius 190px, mouse follow .07, radius follow .05) to reveal the bottom photo, and pressing within 6px grows the circle 20x over 2.2s so the two photos swap. The noise formula is our own so the edge pattern differs, and 190px, the original radius unit (dmax 1.8129 GL units) converted to px, is a value matched by capture. The 16-cell grid that turns off at random on first reveal is a DOM grid.

The underlined-word photo pile uses the original values (240ms · spread 50 · from below 50 · tilt 10 · .4s power4.out · after .5s .25s back.in(3) .9), and the photos are placeholder boxes with different ratios and background colors (the original uses black-and-white photos).

The original’s click sound (sound.js) uses audio files that are original assets, so at the same moments (link or button press, work change, work open) and the same volume (.2) we play our own short ”tok” (1.2kHz→600Hz 40ms WebAudio). The sound itself differs from the original. The pill menu text knockout was rebuilt with our own SVG mask (on hover or current page the background and text are emptied, and letter and dot shapes are punched out of the ink-color plate and floated in over .2s).
PP Neue Montreal, Mono and FH Phemister are paid, so they are replaced by Inter Tight 700, JetBrains Mono 500 and Instrument Serif. Korean uses Noto Sans KR 700 and Hahmlet 200.

Font backfill: the original used a single PP Neue Montreal family for both headings and body, so the heading-font spots (the two large intro paragraphs, serif words) and the large spots the regex missed were swapped to English placeholder text. Font backfill: body font slots (name pronunciation note, 44px sentence for ”(method)”, work info cell, corner city line, cursor text, contact note) keep Korean placeholder text per the README

The set( the page used to provide{pan, lift, zoom, ring}) is taken as-is as camera side · up move · lens pull · ring.

Photos use placeholder panels (labels) as textures.

The pill nav and menu use the original component values as they are. After attaching, at 600ms it comes down from 120px above over .6s (expo) and turns on at .3s. When opened, the pill goes 326 → 448px over .45s, the box expands to 528px (446px if screen height is under 620) over .55s after .35s, and the rows rise from 44px below over .75s after 680 + 70i ms. The divider and rows rise 6px over .4s/.5s after 870·930·980·1030ms. In the hamburger, the three horizontal lines clear over .3s after .45·.3·.15s, and the two X lines are drawn after .7·.85s (reversed when closing). The yellow curtain covers the screen from the first paint (in the original the server renders the curtain).

What remains — gold logo pose: ”>」「<” Two-piece ExtrudeGeometry, poses set per scene with scroll interpolation between them plus a 0.1 lerp, splitting apart, drag rotation, and a ”Drag to view” chip. The pose values were tuned by eye. The first page logo journey code could not be found in the saved original bundles (_next/static/chunks): the only place that loads the logo GLB is the footer physics bundle, and the bundle that draws the first page canvas data-logo-experience is not in the archive. Next task: download that bundle again and read the pose table.

The hero logo (crown + vertical brush-script name) is original artwork, so the crown outline and star were redrawn as SVG and the name is left as a text placeholder.

The hero ASCII canvas (letters scatter following the mouse) and the ASCII particles above the menu (.base-ascii) in the original code are either disabled (commented out) or have no element in the original HTML, so they don’t appear on screen and were not built.

The contact form goes through the same front-end checks as the original (empty required fields, email format → red text below the field), confirm and edit steps, but it does not actually send — it only opens the thank-you screen. The original sends through a form plugin REST endpoint and opens an error screen on failure (this is a frame with nowhere to send).

Photo slots use a set (shared.css --site-ph-*) that renders the original photos’ brightness and color tone (navy night sea · stage · neon · black poster · jacket) in oklch from the accent blue, labeled with subject · light · composition. The phone hero photo uses a separate portrait photo in the original (noted in the label).

The original bundle includes swup 4.8.2 + a JS plugin (a transition that fades the body .default out and back in over .5s), but the [page-name] element passed as containers doesn’t exist in the original document and there are no other pages, so the transition never fires. Since nothing visible happens in the original, it isn’t included. To use transitions when adding pages, apply the same .5s fade with _vendor/swup@4.8.2 · swup-js-plugin@3.2.0.

notes: The original ties panels, modals and drawers together with Alpine.js, but it is not a motion library, so we did not use it and wrote the same values in vanilla JS. The board drag, wheel, zoom, minimap and table-of-contents fly-to engine is not copied from the site code but newly built as the _fx/zoom-pan-board part, which the site uses (damping .8s easeOutQuad, zoom ±.2 in .3s, table of contents 1s easeInOutCubic, first position 1649,1215, phone .8x are the original values).

Page transition uses the same swup 4.8.2 + js-plugin 3.2.0 + head-plugin 2.3.1 as the original. The sheet returns to its start position in .6s power2.out and the header and small map fade out in .4s, then the story enters from half the left width in .55s power2.inOut. swup only turns on when opened over http, over file:// it normally just navigates

The hand-drawn illustrations on the panel (building·riverside city·forest and waterside·housing complex) were redrawn as our own line art (SVG lines) to match the original placement and size, so they are simpler and more mechanical than the original. The reveal mask that shows them as they are drawn (1.6s steps(14)) uses the original values

The logo, vertical title, red handwritten memo and ”PLACE OVERVIEW” outline letters were lettering images in the original, so they were rewritten as HTML text (handwriting uses --kf-font-hand Nanum Pen Script). The logo is an isometric panel SVG + text

The doodle loader draws an SVG zigzag with 1.2s steps(12) instead of the original animated art. First visit 3.5s or more, and direct-to-story entries clear right away — exactly the original’s conditions
Only story #1 was recorded, so the five folders, previous and next all go to the single article.html. The original contact page was not recorded
The note panel thumbnail inside the how-to-explore modal is a placeholder (the original 6s intro-map-pan repeating motion uses the same values)

title: Portfolio where one contour-striped 3D object selects the work
good_for: Creative developer and 3D artist portfolios with a one-screen home that picks among three featured works via one object, and hands-on project detail pages.

pages.use: Home — full-screen WebGL stage with a contour-line object, three projects on the left (picking one morphs the object into the next shape), cursor pill over the object, directory drawer (tabs·table·cursor preview). For portfolio heroes where three key works are picked via the object

Work detail (view switch) — intro panel on the left with a year/company/tool scale below, drag to rotate the object in the center, switch between light and dark views with pills on both sides, and the description card at bottom right changes. For work or product details showing one object in two modes

Work detail (play) — auto-playing video in the intro panel, and a play button under an object starts a 20-second balloon-popping game (score board, time left, best record, result). For mini games and experiential campaign details.

Work detail (sound reactive): an autoplay video in the intro panel, three sound pills under the object, pressing one makes the mass pulse to the beat and the lines glow, and the line nearest the cursor thickens. For sound and interaction experiment work details

notes: The original object shader was not copied, it was rewritten from scratch with the same values (spacing .016×4 · thickness .109+.165 · noise .165/.42 · flow .15 · ring breathing .09/.16 · five-digit distance field). Dead branches of the original such as the contour band, emboss and bottom sweep were not built

Instead of the original’s reflector (Reflector · blur 8), the floor draws the object once more as a mirror on the floor plane at .42 opacity and covers it with a semi-transparent background-color panel (.59) — with no blur, the reflection is sharper than the original
The dark view (original electric view) bloom (UnrealBloom .9) is not built, it is approximated only with a teal atmosphere shell (.5) and rainbow lines.

The balloons in the balloon game use our own star-balloon shape (same shader, fill 1) instead of the original glb model — rise speed and count are values estimated from the screen (.9~1.7/s, one every .45~.8s)

The hiss sound uses three WebAudio oscillator branches (slow breath · fine tremble · heavy beat) instead of the original audio — it sounds only when the header sound button is on. The surface ripple formula (sum of three sines ×.15×(1+bass .5)) uses the original’s numbers

The camera drift periods (.19 · .23 · .17 · .13 · .11 rad/s) and the object growing from .86 to 1 over 1.4s expo.out on entrance are values estimated by eye. Only the original numbers (drift amplitude .15 · .08 · .05, tilt .012, gaze .09) were read.

The three detail pages share the same frame (focus mode) in the original, but their interactions differ (view switching · play · sound), so all three were built — judgment: so whoever picks them can choose by interaction

The transition length when returning from detail to the first page differs per object in the original (measured Brand A .58s · Brand B 1.3s · Brand C 1.33s), so it is matched per page with body data-leave — measured while the machine is busy, it wobbles ±20%

The balloon game start was measured from the original and matched. On press the play button drops out right away, .1s later only the intro panel slides left by its own width (360px) (.42s expo out) while the scale below only fades, and the button comes back 1.2s later at the upper right next to the number pad. The original countdown text (countdown-alert) was not built

The product page hero graphic is Rive in the original (@rive-app/canvas 2.49, /riv/ach_hero.riv). The runtime is MIT, but the .riv asset belongs to the original and our .riv can only be built in the Rive editor, so we shot the original at .3s intervals and moved the measured order into GSAP: .6s empty code card → 1.2~1.9s lines typed → 2.1~3s value chips → 3.3s white file card rises from below and overlaps → from 3.9s file lines turn yellow → 5s switches to a transfer status card, steps attach one by one and it stays (the original also stays on the status card). Curves and pixels between scenes are not the same as the canvas. When the next person builds our .riv in the Rive editor, swap in @rive-app/canvas in the same place.

Page transition: the original Astro ClientRouter is an in-framework mechanism that can’t be shipped separately, so shared.js reimplements the same job (internal link → fetch the next document, keep the header row and swap in the rest, load only unseen parts and page scripts, back navigation). Because the original css sets the animation of ::view-transition-old/new(root) to none, the swap is instant, and only the newly entering white sweep film (slideFadeOverlay 1s ease-in-out) plays again. Opened as file:, it can’t fetch pages, so it does a normal navigation. The original transition delay (~420ms) is a server round trip, so the local rebuild is faster.

The payment rail bento ports the original values: 12s per rail, 80ms tick, 600~5000ms typing, transfer card at 41% typed, event 400ms later, editor off at 11.5s, time only passes while visible, click jumps to that rail. The platform loop, which runs separately on the same 12s, has only three pieces built: the balance digit roll (every 1s, only changed digits, .42s ease-out-quint, 16ms per digit), the compliance pill (3.1s needs review → 5.4s attachment pops out → 7.4s recheck → 9.1s pass), and the console switching off at 11.5s. The original cycles four platforms and also changes card art, colors, names, loan table, compliance row icons (one checked every 300ms) and the chart window shift. News list — 3:2 photo on the left, italic date and title laid out above a thin line on the right, paged with round numbers. For press releases, industry news and notice lists
Single news item — black band title · date · short body · external link card (cover photo + summary). For short news posts like press coverage and outside articles

notes: The original logo, five black character poses and symbol strip are not used by rule, so they are new SVGs with the same position, size and feel. The character is simple: a droplet body, eyes and white stripes

The water-drop photos are images with the text baked in in the original, so shared.js draws drop-cutout placeholders and curved text (textPath) from data-q·data-no·data-en. Only four drop shapes are cycled, and the curved text positions are eyeballed approximations (the text is inside the original image, so there is nothing to measure).

The hero round window draws the original GIF (500px black background with white dot pattern, 12 frames, 160ms each, endless) as our own canvas where the dot pattern shimmers at the same tempo — dot placement and brightness flicker are random, so it is not the same picture as the original frames.

The original typefaces area (wide, stretched thin uppercase) and aktiv-grotesk are paid, so they are replaced with Archivo’s wdth 125 axis and TikTok Sans — menu letter width is slightly narrower than the original

The original section names (WONDER·ISSUE·EXPERIMENT) were changed to SERIES·ISSUE·LAB. The lists and details of ISSUE·EXPERIMENT·COLUMN were not recorded, so the menu goes to the matching section on the first page. CONTACT links to a single News page
Repetition was reduced: series list 12 episodes → 6, news 15 items → 8, column six cells → four. All section types are kept

Search has only the curtain and input shape and does not actually search (a slot for the CMS search API). The original photo zoom view (PhotoSwipe) · Contact form · slider-gallery block are not used anywhere in the recorded page body so they were not built
Section head intro line (ik-sec-head__copy) — the original is a Japanese sentence in a serif (BIZ UDMincho), Korean is kept (paired with Noto Serif KR)
Series question title (ik-series__ja) · part pill (ik-pill, original Part 1 · Part 2) — original is Japanese serif, kept in Korean (paired with Noto Serif KR)

Three of the four column names (ik-cols__name) · feature photo caption (ik-feature__cap) — the original is serif Japanese, Korean kept. The second column is English in the original, so Column Name Here

latin-slots.py counts the serif slots above as remaining slots — because it reads the fallback after var(--kf-font-serif, var(--kf-font-display)) in our CSS as a Latin assignment. The actual computed font is BIZ UDMincho→Noto Serif KR, so the number of places where a Latin-only font holds Korean text is 0.

title: Creative studio with a black-and-white photo ring and ASCII work strip
good_for: Digital production and creative studio homepages that show work experimentally, with gallery, about, news, and case studies.

pages.use: Home page — a black-and-white photo ring (WebGL) hero, an English manifesto and code lines that form on scroll, a pinned horizontal work strip rippling in ASCII, an outlined-type mission section, a services list, an agency block, a typewriter-title target card, FAQ, and a drawer footer below. For an experimental studio’s home page

Work gallery — on a single black screen, cards bend around a horizontal ring (WebGL) and move on with wheel, drag or arrow keys. Switching to list view gives a table with a preview that follows the cursor. For portfolio lists with many works

About the company — title rising from blur over a big wordmark pattern, sentence forming letter by letter, company overview table, three principle cards, industry tags, drawer footer. For a single company overview section

News list — a large title swept by an ink bar, a featured item with a magazine cover and two-page spread, black LET'S TALK band and footer, floating consultation button. In the media features and press list
Work detail — big English title, wide 21:9 cover, overview + info cells, desktop and phone screen frames, credits, two other works, LET'S TALK band, one per web case

notes: In the original, each page splits the header, cursor and footer Frame into four (first page, About company = difference header + drawer footer, Work = Black one-screen header, News · Detail = Light translucent header + black footer). The copy is split the same way — shared is shared.css/js (cursor · transition mask · recording clock · drawer), and the light frame is light.css/js, used by both News and Detail. Like the original, the light frame has no cursor or transition mask (body data-plain)

Things turned off in the original weren’t built: the first-page logo particle canvas (#gl) and the center labels c1~c3 are display:none in the original css. The language switch (JA/EN) has only the slot and doesn’t change the text. The two real-site iframes in the detail view are a same-size screen frame + placeholder (no other site is embedded).

The work gallery rebuilds the original’s hand-made WebGL (horizontal-axis ring · 90° flip per cell · speed bend 70/30 · wave 16 · RGB ±.004 · corner 16px) with the same numbers — not yet extracted as a part (the next person can extract it under a name like ring-flip-gallery). The wheel moves one cell at a time with a 340ms lock, drag 520px. = One cell, touch and 820px or below start in list view like the original. Original 21 works cut to 8

Fonts: Helvetica Neue (system) slots use Inter, Noto Sans JP becomes Noto Sans KR (900), and the Japanese serif title in the company overview uses Noto Serif KR. The light frame’s ink (#0a0a0a) is made from the skin ink with only the brightness scaled to .76x.
The note button (wire.js) covered the bottom-right drawer bar and could not be pressed, so on pages with a drawer the note button is moved 70px up (shared.css)
Phone (390): the work page starts in list view like the original. The six header menu items are tight, so on phones the logo is 12px and the gap 10px (the original logo image is narrower).

title: Travel record with giant place names sliding together and one photo each
good_for: Serialized travelogue or field-record archives with big titles and a photo per episode, company in-house media pages, and company story pages with history and philosophy.

pages.use: Travel journal first page: a line-drawn walking figure (attached) with hashtag bands and city-silhouette bands flowing behind it at different speeds as the hero. Then a trip list where each episode has a 120px two-line English place name and subtitle riding over the photo and a circle arrow attached to the photo corner (alternating left and right, color panels laid askew), a wide panel leading to the intro text and company story, and a big-sentence footer. A MENU at bottom right opens the trip list drawer.

A company story — a cover where a hand-drawn blue ring Lottie wraps around two faces (vertical title on the right, contents list, pen drawing), section name bands, header bars attached to each section (STORY 01…), large photos, two-column body text, photo collections, a folding table (work flow), line drawings with big English words, a closing pen drawing, and a next-project panel. For long pages that tell company history, the CEO interview and philosophy in sections

notes: Because the card is auto, the breakdown fields are filled with live-page measurements (computed transition · sticky top · band transform change). As this is a site-builder site, the bundle code is not in the archive, so every figure was measured on the live site

The hand-drawn ring runs our own Lottie (ring.js — 1080²·30fps·136f, draw 0~45f · erase 90~135f, stroke 30·round caps, original trim keyframe curve as is) with the same dotlottie-player 2.7.12 as the original. The stroke color is read by about.js from --kf-accent. It is loaded via script instead of json so it opens from file:// too.

Repetition trimmed: trips 10 rounds → 4 (two-line and one-line place names × alternating left/right — every line form is there), company story 6 sections → 4 (01 photo · two-column text · photo collection, 03 folding table, 05 line drawing · big English word, 06 closing). The original’s section 02 vertical large phrase, section 03 map pin, section 04 three black-panel pill cards, and section 05 tool list · cactus drawing were not built — to do next

The MENU button’s open state is fixed in css so that when the drawer is open and the back panel covers it, it returns to blue like the original (dialog). This removes browser differences in hover releasing late.
The phone (390) travel row was built by guessing from the original phone screen (place name 56px · photo 350:560 · circle 120px). Subpage phone hover comparison was not done

title: Regional telecom recruiting portal with hero video cropped into a round window
good_for: Company recruiting landing pages (opening video, CEO message, role banners) and table- and news-heavy corporate subpages such as about and job requirements.

pages.use: Recruiting portal home page · an opening video loader (circular hole), a street video clipped by a rounded window in the lower band, a diagonal-masked glass ribbon behind big white English, a representative greeting with vertical-writing copy and a rounded photo, recruitment categories with four photo and glass banners, and a street illustration footer where people walk in. For a company recruiting site’s Hero.

Company overview — a 2-column table (company name, executives, location…) where a pale sky-blue title band and a white body panel overlap by 120px going up, plus one management philosophy image. For About company / company info table pages

A single job posting — centered greeting, orange-underlined section title, a table with gray header cells (job type, details, pay, location, days off…), navy apply button. For job posting detail and recruitment guidelines

Corporate home — photo band + white copy, three-tier color banners, sky-blue panel with 3×2 news cards (photo 1.1x on hover), photo banner, notice, three-tier topics, guide booklet, green service button, four-column icon shortcuts, related-site banners. For an official company home and news roundups

notes: The three subpages (company overview · employment for people with disabilities · corporate home) are, in the original, the skin of a corporate site different from the recruiting portal (white header bar · orange underline · navy button), so they were built separately as a body.co branch in shared.css. The header bar and footer differ from the recruiting portal first page (body.rp) — as in the original.

The page in pages.json (the corporate site URL) is the corporate home page, so it was built as page.html (type page). The original’s news cards, topic photos, guide brochures and related-site banners are photo placeholders, and the three color banners and icon shortcuts were redrawn with CSS and SVG.

The opening and main videos are gray placeholder videos with the same ratio and length (media/ — opening 1920:1080 11.7s once · phone 9:19.5, main 1920:1680·750:2040 10s loop). The original main video file is cut off in the archive (no moov) so its length couldn’t be read, and it is set to 10s like the phone version.

The glass ribbon background (two original 3D render PNGs) is redrawn as an SVG of three thick translucent lines, and the footer street art (background + 10 people figures) as flat-shape SVGs at the same cell ratios. The people’s positions, sizes and entrances (.6s opacity · steps(1) 1.6s walk · 5% rise, delayed 2s) are the original values as is.

The mask-txt-vertical of the president’s greeting vertical copy is overridden with mask-size: unset in the original, so the reveal is not actually visible — the copy also applies no mask and keeps only a blue glow inside the letters (5s loop).

Checking by swapping theme.css between light and dark skins and shooting was not done — lint shows 0 colors, 0 fonts, 0 variables outside the skin. The placeholder video (mp4) is gray, so it is independent of the skin.

title: Regional bank set with leaf backdrop and floating vertical menu card
good_for: Bank, insurance, and public institution sites with deep menus and many notices, purpose-based product guides, news lists, and recruiting special pages.

pages.use: Personal customer home — a floating vertical menu card (2- and 3-level expansion), folding leaf background, notice banner, important alert, two login panels, service tiles, illustrated purpose cards, recommended and campaign carousels, three News items, a consultation box. For finance or public-sector homes with deep menus

Business customer home — water-drop photo banner slider, two login groups, platform intro panel, important notice, service strip, icon purpose cards, topic carousel. For the entrance of a business-use service
Corporate and IR info — a large white panel with breadcrumbs, CEO message (photo on left, text on right, signature), and two name + description cards. For About or an IR entrance
Product list — large white panel with two lines of guidance and a two-column grid of name + description cards (nine products). For category product lists
News list — year picker row, long news rows with date, NEW, category tag and PDF marker, and two boxes for phone and web consultation. For press release and notice lists

Careers home (different shell) — grid-pattern header, video hero, serif tagline, black strategy band (large wordmark), people grid, diagonal culture band, two-column about / careers, and black footer. For a recruiting microsite inside a company
Recruiter message. Gray diagonal panel with title + photo header, lime diagonal band, white rounded panel with black-band subheadings and body. For a recruiting message or a leader’s letter

notes: The background arch, leaves and yellow-dotted fruit do not use the original SVG · PNG. They are newly drawn shapes in the same position, size and layer order, so there are no leaf veins or grain. The fold values (100px · 0.3s ease-out · arch −250px · 0.5x from center · leaf top −100 · fruit top 100) are exactly as in the original.

The people illustrations on the purpose cards and notice banner are simple line drawings (SVG) in the same place and size — the original illustration’s expressions and prop count are left for the next person to fill in

The four tabs in the phone menu (Menu·Net banking·Branch ATM·Open account) only change the selected state — the original shows a different panel per tab (login button·branch search·account guide). The Menu tab’s 2-level slide-in (50px from the right·.3s) is built
The chat button is an external widget (bedore), so it is only a look-alike placeholder. Only the fund search dialog was built (the original’s chat, securities and map dialogs share the same shape)

The careers hero video is a 32:15 · 48.4s placeholder video, and the handwritten slogan that is drawn inside the video in the original is overlaid separately as text (Nanum Pen Script) on top of the video. The large Brand wordmark is text instead of the original SVG
Search, internet banking login, and font size cookie saving do not work (look and hover response only). Larger font size goes html 62.5%→75% like the original.

The original typeface (a paid Japanese Gothic system font) is replaced by Pretendard, and the serif on the recruiting layout by Nanum Myeongjo. Swiper 12.2.0, the same as the original, was newly added to _vendor

Font backfill: the Latin-only font Lato spots (recruiting board section names MESSAGE …, THE BANK OF HERE wordmark, ENTRY/MYPAGE buttons, Internship, TOP, copyright line, phone number) were already English and digits — only data-label was added to the two wordmarks. Images were not re-shot since the text did not change.

Font backfill: the Hangul titles of the individual, corporate, enterprise, product and news pages and the recruiting panel are Japanese gothic-style kana·kanji titles in the original, so Hangul is kept (the title font is Pretendard gothic, so the pairing stays the same). The recruiting panel slogan is in a Mincho serif in the original, so it uses Nanum Myeongjo, and the handwritten slogan uses Nanum Pen Script, with Hangul kept.

title: Company intro with a window-to-screen hero and stacking service list
good_for: Regional, cultural, and tourism company homepages, business introductions, and recruiting sites.

pages.use: Company home page: a Hero where a small video window between vertical copy grows to fill the screen, a concentric cycle diagram, a service list that stacks and sticks on top, shops and awards, a dark story slider, partner logos flowing in a mix, News cards and a media row, and a photo-band recruiting section. For culture and tourism company landings.

Philosophy (About the company) — white nav over a full-bleed photo header, two-column mission, five-branch diagram over a photo with a flowing photo strip, two vision focuses (before and after diagram), four values lines, director’s greeting, and company sub-page cards. For company About and Vision pages

Business About — photo header, five-step cycle diagram, business structure diagram, a table of contents sticking to the left + per-service photo, three feature lines, store, flow, case, dark three-pillar photos (Beyond). For business and service detail pages

News list — sticky category list on the left + row cards with date, tag, title and photo (hover underline draws in from the left and erases toward the right), load more. For news and press release lists (category lists /news/category/… share the same shape)

Recruiting site: floating white header bar and blue gradient button, photo columns flowing up and down and big text that clears from blur, a crossing line (Lottie), parallax photos, sideways-pushed member cards and bar, count-up numbers, work environment, and a job-type button grid. For a careers page

notes: The category list (/news/category/media) has the same form as the news list so it was not built separately — clicking a left category in news.html leaves only that category

The recruit section (recruit.html) is a separately designed careers site even in the original, so its header (floating white bar, blue gradient button) and footer differ from the main site — it is built inside that page, not in the shared shared.js. The flow speed of the hero photo columns (STUDIO loop) could not be read from the original bundle, so it is set to 40s and 46s, and only 6 of the 14 member cards

The line crossing the careers section is drawn with lottie-web 5.12.2 svg as two of our own lines instead of the original dotlottie-player (lottie.host JSON) — 1920×880 · 30fps · 176 frames · trim 1→60 frames (cubic-bezier(.249,.002,.043,.992)) · 1.5x repeat are the same as the original. The line color is read from --kf-line

Business section (service.html): of the original’s five services (four brands + planning), shop and cases, only Service One · Shop · Service Two (case) · Produce (flow · two cases) are built, trimmed because they repeat the same pattern. The original’s ”First” section is display:none, so it was not built. The wide-screen What We Do image and the business structure diagram are our own SVG diagrams in the same place and ratio.

Partner logos, award logos and company logos are placeholder text (LOGO) or our own SVGs. Fonts: the original paid gothic (Gothic MB101) slot uses Noto Sans KR, the Japanese mincho (Shippori Mincho B1) slot uses Nanum Myeongjo, and Latin is the same Crimson Pro and Forum as the original

As in the original, the first page header nav appears at .4s only after the whole Hero section has passed (rootMargin 0 0 -100% 0). Subpages add a separate white nav (#fv_header) over the photo header, and the fixed header appears after the photo has passed.

title: Orthodontic clinic with white cards in a screen frame over fixed video
good_for: Clinic, dental, and hospital homepages, appointment-centered specialist practices, and calm medical or beauty service intros.

pages.use: Clinic home page — Hero with big serif copy over a fixed video that fades on scroll · oval photo slide with Play Movie · feature thumbnail row widening into white cards inside a frame · first consultation panel · two shortcuts · news and clinic calendar · directions. For clinic or practice home pages where booking a consultation is the goal
Case list — per category a mint line label and description, 3-column photo cards (number · title strip). For treatment cases, build cases and before/after lists

Clinic About — card with attached inner nav, arched portrait greeting with signature, group photo and two doctors’ bios, six scattered facility photos. For director greeting, medical staff and facility introduction

Treatment guide: a text panel over a dark photo, two-step cards with a swapping description panel, treatment rows with staggered photo and text (expandable More), a FAQ accordion, and optional treatments. For medical specialty and procedure pages

A single case — frame first with no header photo, category·number·title cover, info row that sticks to the left and follows, front/upper jaw/lower jaw tabbed before-and-after comparison, row of three step photos, key points·risk notice, other cases. For case and review details that include before-and-after comparison

notes: Fonts: English headings in Canela Web and body in dnp-shuei-gothic are paid, so they were replaced with Newsreader 300 and Noto Sans KR. Newsreader is wider than Canela, so the two English hero lines have line breaks blocked and letter-spacing tightened by -0.01em.

The original’s treatment calendar is a content widget using FullCalendar (+ calendar events), so a static calendar of the same shape (this month, Thursdays and Sundays marked closed) was drawn in shared.js — previous and next month buttons are for show only.

The Google Map embed and the contact page (booking form with snow-monkey-forms·air-datepicker) were not built — the map is a same-size placeholder, and the booking button links to the home page consultation panel

@barba/prefetch 2.1.10 (prefetching) attached to the original barba has no visual motion, so it was left out. Opened via file://, barba cannot fetch the next page, so it navigates normally with the same curtain values (cover .5s → reveal .5s after .5s)

Judgment: the repeated header, drawer, footer, left and right pillars, two shortcut cells and directions are drawn by shared.js into empty slots (data-slot) — because the original also swaps only the main body and leaves the frame as is

Judgment call: the original’s detailed treatment sections (multiple treatment rows, optional treatment) are cut down to two same-shaped treatment rows and one optional treatment row — every section type is kept

Font backfill: the Newsreader (Latin-only) slots were already all English. Only the hero tagline that transcribed the original English (→ A Big Line, / Set Across Two. · trailing italic kept) and the marquee words (→ Brand Word · two on index, about, list) were swapped for placeholder text with data-label added. On phone (390) the tagline wraps to three lines, while the original wraps to four, so it was left as is

Typeface backfill decision: section names (Concept · Feature · FAQ …), Play Movie, Staff Blog, Pre Diagnosis and the English category names (Open Bite Case …) follow the README’s section names and name-line style, so they stay as they are. Korean headings (h1 · h2 · h3) and the hospital name spots stay Korean because the original uses a kana/kanji gothic there. The paired typeface Noto Sans KR is loaded.

title: Airline campaign story advancing by scroll inside a red frame
good_for: One-page campaign or project stories with two-path entry or support guidance, number counters, and a spinning globe storytelling.

pages.use: A campaign page: a hero where a red frame around the screen opens diagonally and a person, airplane and boarding pass rise, then nine scenes tied to whole-document scroll (story copy·intro·record card·distance counter·dreamer·how to enter·supporter·report book) with a WebGL globe turning behind. For entry-style campaign or project intro landings.

notes: The original URL is blocked for headless browsers by a CDN (Access Denied) and cannot be opened, and the archived copy also had its person sequence photos, copy images (kv_desc) and some script requests blocked with 403 at archive time, so the one-line timeline does not start even in the replay (it stops at the Hero and stays put when scrolling) — so motion after the Hero could not be measured on screen. The scene order (kv → story → about → movie → history → dreamer → entry → supporter → donation → report), the curves (expo.in/expo.out, power2.inOut), the durations (.5~1.5s), the document height of 36000px and scrub 1 are values read from the bundle (index-*.js). The layout inside each scene and the time split per scene were guessed from the DOM, CSS and remaining images and rebuilt (low fidelity)
Subpages: the two recorded ones (/report, /jp/ja) both show Access Denied so they were not built — the report exists only as the last scene of the first page (the book-turn slot)

Hero uses the original values as they are (person -30%, plane 30%,10% 2s, ticket 20% 1s cubic(.19,1,.22,1), frame .2x diagonal open .5s + grow .5s, scroll hint and banner at 2.3s). The copy graphic (kv_desc) is not in the archive, so its spot is left empty

Of the six modals (record map, distance conversion, two entry guides, donation, video, interview), only the interview video and one entry guide use dialog-pop (fade .2s). The original exit .15s cubic(.42,0,1,1) is a single fade length, so .2s is equivalent.

The support button frame color change (-white · -story-entry versions), the donate button, and the back-to-top button are not built. Menu links jump straight to the timeline label position (original links scroll to the same spot)
Phone (390): frame, bottom button bar and hero spacing use the original sm values, while scene contents are simplified into a vertical stack (the record’s report and interview are hidden on phone)

People and photos are placeholder boxes (the label gives subject and composition). The airplane, campaign stamp and boarding pass were redrawn in SVG and HTML at the same position and size. Fonts are Montserrat (same as the original) + Noto Sans KR.

The bottom-right strip banner hides once you leave the Hero — a guess, since the original CSS has .bnr.-hidden (when it is added wasn’t visible because the script is blocked). On phones this banner covers the scene, so
story copy, three lines — the original is an SVG drawing Japanese sentences (txt_lg), Korean kept. Loaded 800·900 on Noto Sans KR, which Montserrat 800 falls back to, to match the weight

Application period label — the original pairs an English name with Japanese, as in Dreamer plus an application-period word, so it is mixed here as Dreamer Application Period, keeping the native-language part
Entry guide button (original: entry terms in Japanese) · guide window body (original Japanese terms text) — Korean kept

The header buttons and the menu’s Dreamer·Supporter·How to entry·Report match the English already used in this page’s section titles (for Dreamer, etc.) — the words are the same as the original, but this was a decision to keep them consistent with the section titles. The original proper names (company, campaign and event names) became COMPANY NAME·CAMPAIGN NAME·SPECIAL EVENT

title: Brand story paging one slide at a time with white wing bands wiping the screen
good_for: Corporate brand stories, vision pages, and one-page campaigns that turn large photos and short sentences like slides, including brand declarations with a single video.

pages.use: Brand story single page — a white fixed header (drop-down menu panel), seven full-photo sections that advance one per wheel tick (white wing bands sweep across as a wipe and text lines rise), a video section, a hope header section, a hope section where photos in an arch window slide sideways, and bottom links with a footer. For brand and vision statement pages

notes: Subpages were not built — all recorded subpages are Access Denied (CDN block) screens, so there is no original to build from. Only one Brand Story section was built in the home style

The original cursor-sweep was measured on an Access Denied screen (0% response), so it can’t serve as the original value. Instead I inspected the original bundle with cursor-scan. Shader uniforms are 0 and the only cursor listeners are two analytics scripts (boomerang), so I concluded that no visual reacts to the cursor.

Loader 1750→867ms: both start the first-section timeline at window load, but the original load is late because of the video embed iframe and remote photos (the duration of the screen change after load is the same)

The white wing band doesn’t use the original PNG. It is redrawn as our S-curve SVG with the same ratio (1436:1856) and the same translucent bands (.4/.48/.8/1) — the curve shape differs slightly from the original

The header drop-down menu panel keeps only the number of columns and the open/close behavior (hover, close, Esc) as in the original, and the link grouping inside is simplified. The video window holds a same-ratio placeholder and does not embed a video site

Judgment: the original header menu starts from the left with 35px gaps in 1270px width (1024~1350 is 94.075vw · 2.59vw), hover turns text red instantly + 3px underline opacity .2s ease, and the pill button background changes with no transition — matched to these values. Site search, like the original, only swaps the icon to × on press and a 365×52 box appears immediately

title: Single VHS TV screen where the cursor flips through channels
good_for: One-screen promos for documentaries, films, albums, or exhibitions, mouse-scrubbed teasers with many trailers and clips, and retro broadcast or videotape campaigns.

pages.use: After the entrance door (logo-morph video centered on a black screen + still noise while loading → ENTER SITE) comes a single TV screen — moving the cursor horizontally switches the channel video every 19 columns of screen width, and a big channel number stands in that column. Top-left horizontal logo, top-right two menus·email field, bottom logo strip·terms link·scrolling single line·timecode·sound button are all drawn on canvas and covered with a VHS shader. On phones it advances every 4 seconds and by swipe, and shows a rotate-to-landscape screen when held upright. For a teaser that skims several videos on one screen

notes: The original is a single page (pages: []). The /terms that the footer terms link goes to and the external shop and ticket links in the menu (Merch·Tickets) were not recorded, so they are same-page anchors.

The original shader is a shader-playground-style fragment shader on shader-doodle (MIT), so the same library is placed in _vendor and the shader was rewritten with the same steps and values (band wobble 15 · 50 · .002, lower transition noise, scanlines 100 lines · 5, RGB overlap .001/.003/.002 ×6 ×.1, brightness .6, pixel scanlines at ½ resolution · .2, 1.5x, brightness band) (part of vhs-tape-gl). The original shrinks non-power-of-two canvases before upload because of texture defaults (repeat · mipmap) and prints warnings, while the part uploads at its own size with clamp-to-edge and linear filtering.

The entry-screen logo-morph video is replaced with a placeholder (media/intro-7x5.mp4 — four white-bar logo shapes at .43s each) of the same ratio and length as the original (700×500 · 1.72s loop). The header horizontal logo, the bottom logo strip and the sound button were images in the original, so they are drawn as canvas-shape placeholders at the same position and ratio (11.7·14.4). The test-screen color bars inside the logo are painted with a single shade from the skin.

Font: the original VCR OSD Mono is free but not on Google Fonts, so the closest pixel monospace font VT323 is used. VT323 has a smaller glyph height at the same size, so original size values are multiplied by --site-glyph(1.25) — if the font changes, fix this multiplier too.

Opened via file://, the video counts as another origin, so the canvas is tainted and the shader can’t upload the texture — only then a moving gray panel of the same ratio stands in for the video, and the entrance logo is drawn as white bars at the same tempo. Served over http, the video shows as is.

The original howler background audio (bgAudio in settings) and channel video sound-on are left out because there are no sound files. The sound button only has its look (two waves when on) and a video muted toggle. The email field does not send, it only shows a THANK YOU notice for 2.5 seconds.

Phone: as in the original, the next channel comes every 4 seconds after entry, and you switch by swiping left or right or tapping the left or right side (hammer pan threshold 10). Held upright, a ROTATE YOUR PHONE HORIZONTAL overlay (DOM) covers the screen. The original phone channel number vertical line (top is header height, bottom is +100) is placed in the same spot.

title: Association site where white cells melt into a green stage and particles form a box

pages.use: Organization home — a hero with background sound video, a pickup bar stuck to the bottom, news and help info in two columns on a rounded panel, a big pledge statement, an activity list whose photos unfold on hover, a material intro on a shader stage (particles → white box), a usage photo grid, member company logos, and an overview
Activity list — 3-column photo cards (name + arrow) with a fixed left side menu and a parallax background page title. For business, program and campaign list spots
Work list — one-line intro and a ”No posts yet” empty state, plus a next-page box. Placeholder for a list page with no posts yet
News list — 14:9 photo text cards in 3 columns (two-line title·date·arrow) and square pagination
Organization intro — below a background of two overlapping circles, six link boxes in 2 columns (title, description, arrow, lightly filled by a coordinate circle on hover). Hub for the About submenu
Single activity — big title with a dot, 2:1 cover image, body text, two-column image + text, two images, and a side menu with the current page marked green. For campaign or event detail pages

notes: The original shaders (white cells and a gray cover that melts away, whirlwind particles, a box that appears as if blazing in) were rewritten without porting code, using the same numbers (cells 15 · phone 10 · ×1.6 at 1920 and above, row delay .5, particles 10k · delay range .2 · size 60→7px, box 4×4×4 · .6→1 · y −2→0, threshold width .06 · edge ×2.5, camera fov 15 (33,25,33) · phone (43,35,43), sun 4 · ambient .8). The gray-melting pattern, which the original takes from a single black-and-white image (uMonochrome), was replaced with 5-octave value noise clouds. The blob shapes are similar but the pattern is not the same.
The box-surface normal map (foam beads) is made by piling 2600 beads on a canvas instead of using the original image. Strength was lowered to fit the original look (gradient ×.35).

The hero and the video behind the footer share the same position and playback behavior (starts muted, sound button, plays only while hero or footer is visible, sound lowers on scroll) with a 12-second white block placeholder video (media/hero-loop.mp4, gray diagonal stripes made with ffmpeg + calm brown noise sound). It is not the original video content.
The original arrow hover curve is written in code as slow(0.1, 0.5, true), but EasePack isn’t loaded, so it runs on GSAP’s default power1.out — matched to what shows on screen, power1.out .25s.
The original Japanese text (logo, member logos, photos) was replaced with placeholders. The 60 member-logo cells are just white boxes with a Member logo label.

Subpage title background (diagonal, white block, two circles) was redrawn as SVG from the original image. Parallax values (image height ×1.15 − box height, top bottom → bottom top) are as in the original.
The Work (works) page is an empty list reading No posts yet in the original too, so it was left as is. If post cards are needed, reuse .nw-list from news.html.
/  index statement sentence (about-statement) — the original is a Japanese title (Circular society and…), so Korean kept. Font IBM Plex Sans pairs with IBM Plex Sans KR (300 · 400 · 600).
index material intro text line (material-cube) — the original is Japanese (about 98% of product volume…), so Hangul is kept.

Hero · the three English pledge lines in the footer and the English tags of the material intro were carried-over original text, so they were replaced with English placeholder text of the same character count (the text to insert is given in data-label).

title: Seasonal event with giant serif title ringed by pastel blobs and hand illustrations

pages.use: Event first page — a % number loader (drifting blobs · splitting droplets · invitation card · Enter Site) and an intro video, then a slider that moves three blob illustration scenes by wheel · drag · arrows. Click and the blob grows to fill the screen into that chapter

Event intro — pastel header section wrapped by illustrations, large serif paragraph with inset pictures, blob picture + text, photo collage, campaign video, six numbers, next-section slider at the end

Installation list — mint head section, circled paragraph, blob scene + text, two curved texts that flow with scroll, and a ten-row name list where hovering changes the photo inside the blob. Spot for a work / project list

One installation page — sand-colored head section, paragraph with embedded images, tilted photo collage, story + photo, three event cards that stick to the screen and stack, photo strip (swiper), and a slider repeating the first section at the end. For Work·place detail pages

notes: Hand-drawn illustrations (coral notes, conch, flowers, aloe, cable car and more) do not use the original art, they are redrawn as simple SVG sprites of ours at the same positions and sizes — there is no dense hand-drawn texture like the original. The cursor parallax (a different depth per layer) is the same

The original blob splits and joins through dot-cluster (dots) physics, but the dot-blob-morph part only does a single lump’s wobble, cursor swell, fill screen (.7s power3.out) and revert (.8s back-blob)
The scene slider tilt (--rotate) is a value the original calculates at runtime, so it was estimated from the screen as p × 8° (shift 11.52vw · 5.44vw, scale-down .31 are original figures)
The page-turn curve mask rewrites the original path formula (center, edge, and bend with power3.inOut 1s, the bend going out and back at half length) as a single quadratic curve of ours.
The intro video, campaign video and menu video circles are placeholder boxes — pressing play only removes the button. The sound bars just bounce silently
The swiper build has no version string in the bundle, so judging by feature traces (loopAddBlankSlides present · swiperElementNodeName absent) it was taken as 11.0.x and swiper@11.0.7 was used
Title face Voyage (paid) is matched with the closest free thin all-caps serif, Italiana, and the label face Gill Sans (paid) with Cabin from the same lineage
In the original the inner panel (#scroll) scrolls, so compare.cjs cannot capture it scrolling down — the original was compared with a separate script that scrolls with the wheel
