Brand story — vertical large-title header with table-of-contents links, operator, three stories (hunting · storage · processing) over ghost letters, with a large photo (.15) and a small photo (.1) staggered left and right and flowing in parallax, then after a black band (.4) vertical title links with a leather star. For brand philosophy and making-process introductions

Product (material) line — vertical title with a full-bleed photo, features on a black video band, a photo slider where two layers slide together (dot progress circle), a scattered color swatch list with a parallax band below, example cards and a photo-flip modal. For material or product line details
News list — large serif headline, rows of title · date · category between thin lines
A single news item — date, title, body, and a ”Back to list” button between lines

notes: The original site script is an Alpine.js (3.13.8) component — Alpine is not a feel library but a site-code framework, so it is not used, and the same values were rewritten in plain JS (shared.js · index.js · deer.js). The feel libraries (GSAP · ScrollTrigger · lenis 1.1.13 · Splide 4.1.4) use the same builds (GSAP is the _shared build).

The paper-grain noise background (bg_noise.png) was newly made as an SVG feTurbulence data URL, and the brush-scratch images laid on each section (bg/scratch_*.png) are not included. Drawing a faint brush-stroke SVG in the same spot is left to the next person.

Video slots (7 forest and leather videos) are left as same-size wf-video placeholders — the original autoplays, loops and is muted, and whoever uses it <video autoplay muted loop playsinline> Just swap it in as

In the product pinned section (scrollSticky), the section change wipes away from the left with clip-path like the original, and the title enters at the remaining 3/4. Below 960px (the original md breakpoint) it becomes a vertical list with no pinning, like the original.

The subpage hover ”View More” letter roll uses the char-roll part (25ms · 1s expo.out · .6s ease-in on leave · from the last letter). The original hover component only accepts the leave after the full 600ms enter has run, whereas the part’s default form reverts as soon as you leave.
The boar and bear hide pages that were not recorded, along with the inquiry and price list menus, are linked to pages we made (deer · article · news).

title: Local pharmacy intro with vertical copy and staggered overlapping photo collage
good_for: Neighborhood pharmacy, clinic, and multi-location shop homepages with store finder, staff introductions, and recruiting pages as one set.

pages.use: Pharmacy first page — vertical copy on the left + large photo where a white band lifts, staggered overlapping photo collage About, large center store slide (slick centerMode), 60s flowing recruiting group photo strip, News in 3 columns with a gray band unfolding, SNS photo row

Pharmacy About — vertical title section header, center-aligned intro text, zigzag features with six photos of different sizes, two rows of square photos flowing in opposite directions, four-column staff cards. For company · shop About pages
Store list — section heading, one-line note, map embed slot, and 3 store photo cells overlapped by name tags. For the store finder of a shop with several branches

Single store — big photo header (vertical store name · Scroll Down), four staggered store photos, full-width map strip with address, Contact, opening hours and directions, 3 other store cards. For branch and facility detail
News list — centered section header without photo, category rows divided by vertical lines, 3-cell news cards with overlapping date tags, pagination. For notice·blog lists

Recruiting — flowing group photo header, pinned recruiting menu, video window (colorbox), vertical English title message, four interview cells, four unfolding donut surveys. For the first recruiting page

notes: The original was written in GSAP 1.19 (TweenMax·TimelineLite) — the same curve names were ported to GSAP 3 (Power1.easeOut → power1.out etc.). The ease argument of the original TimelineLite doesn’t apply to children, so the default Power1.easeOut applies, and it was left as power1.out.

In the original, the menu kana, hero vertical copy and recruit handwritten title are picture text (png sprites) — set here in the same place and size with Song Myung (--kf-font-hand) and Cormorant Garamond (--kf-font-label) lettering

The two maps (store list and store detail) are map iframe embeds in the original, so they are same-size placeholders. The recruit video is also a video embed, so a 16:9 placeholder is shown inside the colorbox window (window, curtain and CLOSE-follow behavior as in the original).

Social photo row: the original social feed API (lib/instagram.php) was empty so only icons showed — the 6 square slots and the original CSS hover (curtain .4s · new-window icon .2s rotation) are kept. So the first page is taller than the original by that row

Category picking in the news list (the original swaps only the list via pjax) and pagination are visual only — they all lead to the same news.html. The original page transition is a normal navigation plus a .8s body fade, so it is left as is
The recruiting subpages (Day flow·Training·Requirements·Apply·Internship·Scholarship) and interview details were not recorded so they are not built (menu uses # links)
Phone (880 and below) layout was matched by looking at the 390 render. The original’s fine size steps at 640 and 480 (text and spacing .8x each) are merged into one value for 480 and below

Body font is the system gothic as in the original (original Yu Gothic Medium) — at first the Pretendard web font was used, but it downloaded Korean pieces after load and swapped them in, so the screen kept shifting late.

title: Dining and urban business company where a corner piece changes color per section
good_for: Food service and brand company homepages, business introductions, philosophy pages, business details, and news.

pages.use: Company home page — loading (light streaks, copy, J pieces splitting to the corners), photo-crossfade hero with giant three-line title and top-right menu, creed text over a photo, business section covered by a giant title with three photo cards, recruit section with flowing photo columns, three news items, contact band, closing section covered in turn by stacked photos
Creed — a large two-line dark photo hero, a large statement and text on a dark panel, a photo pair, three principle cards. For company philosophy and vision pages

Business intro — dark photo hero, mission + photo, diagram with the company at center and goal circles around it, three business rows of photo + white panel, vertical path steps. For business overview and roadmap
One business — light section header and a photo band that opens to the screen width, overview, regional case cards, four benefit cards by target audience. For business division detail
News list — large title, category buttons, dates and category pill rows. For notice lists
News item — section name and back link pinned on the left, date · title · paragraphs · photo on the right. For notice details

notes: The recruit page (/recruit) returned 403 Forbidden when recorded, so it was not built. The menu’s Recruit and its sub-items (Data · Culture · Interview · Pride Story · Job Description) are just # placeholders. Next step for whoever continues: record and build it once the original reopens.

The corner J piece and the small logo symbol do not use the original artwork (sprite-icon.svg). They are redrawn as a hook shape at the same position and size (28rem · 281:423). The wordmark (bold BRAND text) uses the English placeholder text Brand set in Bebas.

swup version: uses the same version as the original, 4.8.2, with the head (2.3.1), preload (3.2.12) and scroll (4.0.0) plugins. The original’s fragment transition (swup-fragment-plugin — swapping only the list when filtering News categories·job roles) and the forms plugin are not built, News category buttons hide rows within the same page instead. Transition curtain length (spread 1.3s · gather 1s power4.inOut · .45x) and order follow the original.
Opened with file://, swup can’t fetch the next page (CORS) so it falls back to normal navigation — open over http for the transition curtain to run
The contact page (/contact), About page (/about) and business subpages (dining·consulting) were not recorded, so they were not built — the contact strip and menu use a # placeholder

title: Dumpling restaurant with steaming opening and red cloth panels
good_for: Restaurant and multi-location food brand homepages with store finder, news, and company information.

pages.use: Shop home page — title that unblurs over a fixed background video and a news board with a filling progress bar, vertical-writing message, anniversary video, recommendations·press coverage, arc-drawing signboard menu (embla), endlessly flowing photo strip, three commitment panels on red cloth with a chef card, brand introduction, news, at-home·allergy information (the steam-rising opening is ?opening). For a restaurant brand home page.

Store finder — region picker panel, brand logo cells, store card list (photo, phone, web booking, hours table). For multi-branch store lists and booking entrances (recording type product corrected to page, since it is a store list)
News list — a scroll-shaped category board that follows along (category·brand), 3-column square cards, page numbers. For shop notices and event lists
Company info — CEO greeting (illustration strip on the right), history and name origin with alternating photo·text, company overview table, recruiting banner. For a restaurant company About page

notes: The recorded subpages are the Korean version (/ko/…) which currently returns 403 — so we compared against the Japanese version of the same structure (/shoplist/ · /news/ · /company/) as the original. When headless Chrome runs with a Korean locale the original redirects to /ko/ and gets a 403, so the tool was left unmodified and pages were opened only through a preload that injects a Japanese locale (node --require, playwright newContext with locale ja-JP)

The opening (three layers of steam) remains in the original main.js, but its on flag (Ji) is false from the start and never becomes true, so it does not run on the real site (the opening video tag is also commented out) — so by default, like the original, header elements and social tabs show immediately and only the blur-in (js-blur) is applied to the hero title. The opening shows only with index.html?opening, using the original code’s values (two steams 10s · big steam 5s at 6.3s · .6s fade at 10.01s · header .64s after 1s), and the same motion was extracted as the steam-opening part

The background and footer videos are placeholder videos (media/bg-pc.mp4·bg-sp.mp4 — a grid with a passing band and text saying what the slot is) with the same ratio and length as the original (landscape 768×432, phone 768×768, 53.3s, 24fps), hung with the same playback behavior (muted autoplay loop, source media 1023px splitting phone and landscape). The original video files were not downloaded (only length and size were measured with ffprobe). The commemorative video (video embed) is a placeholder box.

The logo (three brush-lettered characters) goes in the ”Brand name LOGO” text slot, and the people illustrations are new, simple SVGs in the same spots and colors (crimson, olive, ink line) — fewer figures and no hand gestures compared with the original illustrations

The cloud shape of the booking badge does not use the original path, it is redrawn as ten bulging arcs on an ellipse. The notched-corner panel uses a CSS mask with concave corners instead of the original (two overlapping rectangles + a gold line).

Of the original 33 store listings, only 4 of the same type are kept (with different numbers of business-hour lines), and the region and brand pickers just move the selected mark instead of reloading with a changed address as the original does

Page transitions use barba 2.10.3 + prefetch 2.2.0, same as the original, so the site must be opened over http. Opened via file://, barba cannot fetch the next page, so it falls back to the same opacity transition (.3s) followed by normal navigation. Per-section css·js is attached and removed during the transition

The language switch (gtranslate), social and recruiting links are placeholders only. Other subpages in the original (store detail, single News post, allergens, Contact) were not recorded, so they were not built

The SNS tab is left as in the original — on the first page the opening that releases the translate(100%) of body:has(.top_page) is off, so the tab stays hidden off-screen, and on wide screens when the pointer is over it only the li bounces in from 30px to the side while the list is visibility:hidden and not visible (on phone it opens by tapping). It looks like an original bug but was measured and matched exactly

The store card’s phone button (.button_tel) has no CSS in the archive, so default ease .3s was chosen based on a measured curve (.04 at 10%, 233ms). The signboard menu has seven cells like the original (swipe end value 7 × 314px)

title: Insurance guide with an ad-model hero and round icon cards explaining the system
good_for: Insurance, mutual aid, and public system guides, association or agency campaign sites, calculator-led guidance homes, and chart-heavy information pages.

For a promo home that explains a program or service simply

System intro — cream header (person and character), shortcut tiles, two target cards (circle icon + flow chart), three cause icons, comparison table, stage-colored damage classification table, two apartment-housing articles, large guide button. For a ”What does it cover” explainer page

Case video list — white rounded head, a row heading per year + 3-column video cards (thumbnail, play mark, title, summary, tag), related links, three external banners. For video and case collections and lecture lists

Funding explanation — cream header · shortcuts · three cost icons · three numbered cards (joined by horizontal lines) · two data panels (bar chart · amount card · donut) · A+B=C Official card and reference, two boxes. For information pages that persuade with numbers and charts

notes: In the original hero the photo and the slogan·badges·character are a single PNG — over the photo area (2496:1480) the slogan, five round badges and the character are layered in HTML·SVG and scale with the photo using container units (cqw). On phones the text drops below the photo, as in the original.

The regional risk map (two original images) is redrawn as a cell map SVG — the cells do not match real region borders 1:1. Region picking, swapping numbers and tables by tab (pref-data.json) and premium calculation (XML) are not wired up, leaving the “??” placeholders as they are.

The about loss-category table·flowchart·comparison graphic and the page bar charts·donuts·amount cards were images in the original, so they were redrawn as HTML tables·cells·SVG (figures are placeholders)
Video window: the YouTube inside is a 16:9 placeholder. The window itself is the same remodal 1.1.0 as the original (1.05x and transparent → in place .3s, close .95x, backdrop blur 3px)
Fonts: the original Zen Maru Gothic has no Hangul, so Hangul uses NanumSquareRound (B·EB) — strokes are slightly lighter than the original round gothic 700

Side-by-side viewing used scroll-step stills from shot.cjs taken at the same steps as the original instead of compare.cjs video — the browser slots on the spare machine were crowded, so heavy video captures were cut down. Worth rechecking with compare.cjs next time

title: Athlete's records and story revealed by slanted blade wipes
good_for: Personal sites for athletes, entertainers, and public figures, fan sites collecting records, collaborations, and appearances, and brand ambassador profiles.

pages.use: Person landing page — intro video → 3D portrait, the hero lifts away on a tilt into a gold-edged card strip, dot-letter quote, polaroids, six pinned partner slots (3D products), foundation, photo row, footer. For a landing page introducing one person.

About through records — CRT video header, sentence where words fill in, season numbers rolling year by year, career total big numbers · table, record cards, floating cutout, dot-letter title + video strip. For player records and company history number pages

Activity collection — pixel title and a draggable Polaroid header, section shortcut pills, fashion photo, digital number panel, appearance videos, feature list + video. For appearances, collaborations and media results pages
Journal — an endless board of items you drag around on a screen-fixed canvas, tap to open a detail card from the left. For showing collections, news and archives playfully

notes: Left as is — the Hero portrait and partner product images are silhouettes drawn in clothing colors (art.js) instead of the original cut-out photos, and the depth map is made by blurring the alpha (our own drawing in place of the original photo). The sunglasses are drawn as a single wrap-around shield lens (top rim curved, nose spot notched), and only on the lens area does the depth-tilt-photo lens option reflect a video with the original JJHero3D figures exactly — plate UV 2.35x · vertical .54 · −.67 → fisheye 3.45, video HSB 0/.75/.6 · 1.3x, CRT grid 6px · scanlines 5px (.5), bundle light overlay (saturation 2.8) · mark multiply .2. Like the original, the reflected video endlessly loops the same tunnel video as the intro (a 480×270 plate with golden exit light and tunnel ribs redrawn every frame — instead of the stadium in the original video). The original normal map has strength 0, so lighting is only the plate normals (ambient 3 · front 4 at −3.3,−4.2,4 · back light 1.25), and the copy also changes the whole plate brightness the same way when the plate turns with lit. The original Hero has no hover light, so the portrait is light: off.

The intro video (an athlete coming out of a tunnel) is replaced by a yellow light-streak canvas with the same length and the same progress curve (after 1s, 1.2s sine.inOut to .4 → 1.8s power3.out to 1). The first page veil follows the measured original shape (holds 3.1s, then changes until 6.0s), and data-veil-hold sets 3.3s — in the original it is while the hero video and 3D assets download, so it may be shorter depending on the network
Sound effects: the original sound files (14 including hover, click, slide) are not used, WebAudio plays a short click in the same spots (data-sfx)

Out of scope: on hover over the featured video, the original’s captions and control bar (17 elements) and the YouTube video that plays on click are kept as just a video slot + play button. The giant word pattern in the fashion and digital sections is filled with a dot-pattern background instead of a leather-texture photo.

Font backfill: the original is entirely English (Beachwood condensed gothic), so all Anton title slots (big titles, quotes, section names, menu, buttons, name bands, pixel head text) were changed to English placeholder text. No slots keep the local language. Body·mono font slots such as captions, tables, record tabs and tags stay in Korean as they were.

Anton is wider than Beachwood, so the original length (Signature Moments, 17 chars) overflows at 1440. Big section names were shortened to Highlights·Partners, and the heading inside the phone field has its second line set to 3 chars (Game/Day) so it does not collide with the team badge. The menu and next-section buttons use the same names (Game Day·Off-Duty).

The 7px horizontal overflow on the phone viewport (390) outside the measured range comes from the closing-section collaboration tile grid (.ow-end__grid), which existed before the font backfill, so it was left as is without touching the structure.
The original pull (sites pull) stops on sub-pages because on-field file and folder names collide. Sub-page text was read from the HTML in the archive pages.har.zip.

title: Portfolio grid of picture tiles bursting out from the center
good_for: Personal portfolio and work-list front pages with animated tile per project, name letter tiles, a side-opening intro, and project views that push the grid aside.

pages.use: One-page portfolio: a grid of square image cells (entrance spreading from the center, cell line drawing, only touched cells turn sharp), a name text cell that fragments around the cursor, a left 40% About drawer, and a work screen that opens on top as the grid drops when a work cell is pressed (title · three screen recordings · role · next/previous). For personal sites where the work list is the hero.

notes: Subpages were not recorded (one-page site). The original’s work screen (/work/<slug>) is not built separately but as an open state inside the first page — changing the address (pushState) and back navigation are left out

15 work artworks: the originals are hand-built SVG/DOM motion per work (pixel speech bubble, bowl, robot arm …), so each was redrawn as our own SVG at the same position and size with short repeating CSS motion — the fine timing of each differs from the original.

The work screen (title · three screen recordings · role · next) could not be measured from the original opening screen (no recording), so only the order and curves of the original code were matched (grid falls 75rem elastic.out(1,2) 1.5s · panel −50% · content −30% elastic.out(1.2,2)) and the layout inside the panel is a guess. The small staging in which the original title, screen and details open in turn (200~1500ms) was left out
The text-cell shader (cell-shatter-gl) was rewritten after measuring the original effect (40-cell pieces, radius .24, gap .12) — the scatter distance and shrink of pieces are values matched by eye
Font: museo-slab (paid) → Zilla Slab. Korean is Noto Serif KR. The name letter cell uses the placeholder ‹A B C D E›
The black band at the middle right is the spot for an external award badge, so it is left as an Award mark placeholder

Contact cells (four cells under the About drawer) entrance: the original ContactLinks code wasn’t fully read, so to match the measured value (opacity start staggers over 1,167ms when the drawer opens) it was set to .75s power3.out at .35s intervals after .1s. The yellow panel hover .4s is a guess
On phone (under 650) the header menu drawer (the original menu panel sliding in from the right) is cut down to two slots, About and Mail

In the motion value comparison, some rows for the text cell and award badge hover were recorded as accepted, paired with hand-drawn motion in another original cell (sunray lines 2.25s · stamp rotation 2.7s) — redoing hand-drawn motion with the original timing for each job is left for the next person

title: Black-and-white one-page studio with overlapping logo loader and wavy type
good_for: Solo studio or freelance web designer portfolios that put services, work, full project list, about, process, and contact on a single page.

pages.use: Studio single page — logo-overlap loader · wavy-letter big title · three-column about (video·text·recent list) · cursor-tag showreel · manifesto lit up by scroll · 3s progress service slider · two filtering work columns (speed tilt · ‹View work› tag) · full list with following preview · about facts table · black process accordion connected by a pixel cover · changing client logos · address-matched contact · dot-scene footer and big logo, press for lightbox

notes: The original footer background is a Studio scene (unicornStudio.umd.js v2.3.0, the original scene file) — the runtime license is unconfirmed and the scene file is an original asset, so it is not used. A new WebGL shader was written to match the position and feel: a dot grid on a perspective floor slowly approaches, the bottom right glows, and it tilts slightly with the mouse (shared.js footer).

The original video (small hero video, show reel) plays a CDN HLS stream through hls.js. The video slot is a placeholder of the same ratio, and the show reel only toggles its play/pause state (label text, top shade lifting) on click — when a real video is added, attach it with _vendor/hls.js@1.7.3.

The ripples over photos and video (concentric ripples around the cursor, pull, color split, .8s on hover) were newly written with our own shader, and since there is no photo, a placeholder plate painted in skin colors is used as the texture (JG.paintPlaceholder). To use a real photo, pass that image in with texImage2D.
The logo is our own mark at the same ratio (2300:250) plus WORDMARK text instead of the original wordmark. The original clock shows a fixed city’s time, ours shows the viewer’s local time.

title: One-page studio diving into the deep sea through four seasons with particle jellyfish and flowers
good_for: WebGL-driven creative studio or personal workshop intros, and immersive one-pagers that step through scenes like stations.

pages.use: One-page studio — sound-select entrance (particle percent), dive through 13 stops with wheel or arrows (hero jellyfish + four-season ring · spring about + people · summer services table + fireworks · autumn seven work panels · winter contact form · particle wordmark footer), plus a hidden section where the globe opens on submit. For immersive company and studio introductions

notes: The original is a single page (pages: [] in pages.json), so there are no subpages. The document does not scroll, 13 fixed-screen sections are moved with wheel, drag or arrows — when mixing, use the station-dive part.

The original world is GPGPU (position·velocity texture) with 400k particles. Here the vertex shader blends between two shapes with a per-particle delay (.45·.55 local blend), and computes the falling pieces·tentacles·swirl motion with the same formula — particles: flower 60k, jellyfish 7.20k (half on phone). Cursor stirring does not store particle velocity but folds it into the impulse response of the same spring (see the cursor reaction line below).

The five flower types (season ring, cherry blossom, firework, maple leaf, snow), the jellyfish and the wordmark were all newly built from our own shapes. The original swirl ring has a deeper four-season color gradient. Here the particles overlap and add up, cross the glow threshold (.78) and tip toward white (brightness of one ring particle .14). The original firework has longer prongs.

The original’s seabed (ocean), bubbles and video on the work board were not built — the floor is the shadow at the bottom of the water-column shader, and the work board uses a website hero placeholder image (960:424 landscape). Putting a real site recording in as the board texture makes it match the original (the placeholderTexture slot).
Sound: there is no original track so a low ocean rumble is built with Web Audio, with the same button and bar behavior (.18 volume, analyzer bars).
The globe in the section revealed after sending is a canvas 2D dot globe instead of the original WebGL globe. The contact form does not actually send, it only validates and then opens the section.

The wordmark placeholder is LOGOTYPEHERE, the same length as the original 12 characters. The 12 redaction X characters are matched in length too — if you change the name, change WORD in index.js and the word in the header line’s data-fx-glyph-redact-resolve together.

Font backfill: spots that were Latin in the original were replaced with English placeholder text: the hero big title (Instrument Serif, three words on one line as in the original, last word in the mix color), seven work names and two work sub-names (index.js WORKS), the hidden section title, five section label names and four header menu items (original About·Services·Works·Contact). Because the big title is now English, the letter reveal order runs at .035s as in the original.

index Season characters (four-season row ×4 · section label ×5 seasons) — the original uses kanji seasons (spring, summer, autumn, winter, Shippori Mincho), Korean kept. The Korean serif 700 and 800 weights are loaded as a pair.

index section-heading big lines, five (About three lines·Services one line·Work opener one line·Contact two lines·hidden section send-off) — original is Japanese Mincho, Korean kept (paired with Nanum Myeongjo).
index eight service names — the original uses Japanese Mincho (Art Direction · Web Design etc.), Hangul kept (Nanum Myeongjo pair).

Among the small gothic text (Zen Kaku Gothic New) that was Latin in the original — the hero topic line, the mixing partner names (index.js PARTNERS · DEFAULT_PARTNER), entrance figure names, service tags, buttons, the line above the hidden section, the footer — these are not title or decorative type, and Korean falling back to the Noto Sans KR gothic pairing is the intended use, so they stay in Korean. Only section names and the menu are in English as listed in the README.
The Work 01 text on the work panel is a label for the website first-screen photo slot drawn by world.js, so it is left in Korean (photo slot description).

The picker section image (library-shots) is always captured as the entrance screen only, since with reduced motion it can’t get past the entrance (sound picker) — changing the copy doesn’t show in the image. thumb.jpg was re-shot by pressing ”Without sound” and capturing 7s later instead of shot --thumb, to keep the same first-screen composition as before.

The business section picks between the original’s two builds under the same condition — touch devices (userAgentData.mobile, or if absent a coarse pointer with a long side of 1024 or less) get the phone build (TopBusinessSP: for 140vh from the section top edge, 50vw square → 100vw × screen ratio, inner 1→1.1 scale, photo swaps instantly at .2·.4·.6, tied directly to scroll position · 140vh gap after the photo frame), otherwise the ScrollTrigger build (25vw → 100vw, 200vh, scrub .7, 1→1.18 scale, .25s swap). title: Wheel-driven product video stage with thin blade lines and question copy

pages.use: A non-scrolling stage home page. Left alone, the scenes flow, the wheel winds and rewinds them. For a brand home screen that shows a few products in video.

Design department intro — a long line drawn along the document, stepped large copy, philosophy text, three-circle figure, three-person list, blue award card, event photo, blue company box, full-height blue tail (product grid · large copy · logo). For department or studio intro pages

Company recruiting home page: large English text over a diagonally laid photo panel, one big line message, colorbox video window, four company tiles over a blue diagonal, number cards counting every 50ms, a grid of photo tiles, banners and link buttons, and a yellow apply button. For the first screen of a recruiting site

Recruiting details · apply — faint large ENTRY text and heading over a pale map, yellow apply button, line table of label and body (job type · working conditions · compensation), school list, open/close FAQ, contact button. For job posting detail pages

A single company News article — blue menu bar header line, year list at left, centered big title, big photo, product row photos, structure diagram, contact person cell, previous and next News, trademark row and a big sitemap footer. For press release detail

notes: Cards were auto, so they filled the exploded cells. While unpacking the archive with sites pull, it stopped at ENAMETOOLONG on a font URL (a very long file name), so I unpacked the HAR directly into /tmp and read the html·css·js·video lengths (the sites tool needs a fix).

First page stage: the original uses its own engine (three r170), path data (lines in pc.json) and a per-product pose setting (transform0→1). The same work was newly written with our shaders: video smear (12 samples along the travel direction), ring video background keying (corner color difference), ribbon lines (1.3px wide, drawn then erased), and blue squares and blue planes. Line shapes are long arcs of a similar character instead of the original paths, and the product poses are four variants imitating the rotation, scale and offset of the original hocho1~3.

Wheel: the original wheel amount follow (.2) and reduce (.2) are carried over, but the details of scrubbing (stops when direction reverses), inertia detection (inertialScrolling) and scene-end auto advance (autoNext) are trimmed. Left alone it flows at 1x and the wheel adds on top.

Video placeholders: product loop 220×840 · 10s (loop-placeholder.mp4), usage scene 16:9 · 8.58s (use-placeholder.mp4, uses 6.08s from 0.5s), with the same ratio and length as the original. When opened via file:// the browser cannot read the video into WebGL (cross-origin), so the same look is drawn on a 2D canvas — served over http it shows the video as is.

The question and answer copy is image text (img) in the original, so we set it as real text at the same position and size. The actual look of the blue scene is not in the recording frames, so we treated it as a blue panel where five copy lines resolve in white one after another. The product row in the last scene is cut from the original 10 (two repeated sets) to 5.

Cursor: visible only while the mouse moves (expands from .8x over .5s) and hides .5s after it stops. The tilt was changed on 2026-11-10 in the cursor backfill, after finding the formula in the original bundle (the home cursor in main.js) — each frame, distance moved/1000 accumulates opposite to the last horizontal direction (±1) and eases toward 0 by .15, and the displayed value follows by .25, ×180° (before, values were fit to the measured curve). Position has no delay, as in the original (before, left·top .1s).

Of the four subpages, the recruiting · hiring guidelines · news article pages are company main-site pages in the original (different header · footer), so shared.css has the header in three branches (design dept · recruiting · company). The recruiting motion uses the same jQuery 1.8 + colorbox (video window 91.25%/80% · 16:9 · overlay .7) · number counting (+1 every 50ms) · Q&A slideToggle (.4s) · phone menu fadeToggle('fast'). The colorbox panel CSS uses only a minimal form built from skin variables instead of the original colorbox.css.
The original fonts are paid (CezannePro·Aeonik Pro, from a font service), so Zen Kaku Gothic New·Noto Sans KR·Figtree stand in. The logo is a bold English wordmark placeholder (LOGO).
The long line on the About page is a canvas line in the original, so one SVG path is drawn as far as the document scrolls (the leading end follows by .08 each) — the path shape is newly drawn.
Skin trap: if a desaturated color like --site-pale(#edf4f7) is rotated from --kf-raised, the browser reads its hue as 0 and the result comes out skewed — rotate from the accent color instead.
Checking by swapping theme.css between light and dark skins and capturing was not done for lack of browser room — a task for the next person to pick up.

Menu panel: in the original, pressing the signature-drawing button (146×72) switches the blue panel to a 4-cell product image grid (WORK), HOME/ABOUT/RECRUIT and News — kept in the same shape, with the product images as placeholders. The open-transition details of the original panel (the order in which text sharpens out of blur) are trimmed.

title: Solid wood furniture store with one full-bleed photo per product
good_for: Furniture and lifestyle brand stores, premium shops with few products, and landing pages that sell one item at length.

pages.use: Store landing page — a video hero with two big English words on top, a centered intro, a full-bleed photo strip, a two-column text section with a photo, a run of sections with one full-bleed photo per product (1.25→1 scale, title lines rising), a hotspot photo, a magazine logo box, a video section, an FAQ accordion, customer photos, and reading picks. For brand store landings with few products

Product list — centered title · thin line below · two white-panel cutout cards (on hover the styled shot overlaps and switches on from 1.2→1 scale) · sold-out tag · count line. For the full product list

Single-product landing — a photo bundle with color picker, quantity and add to cart, a cart strip that rises from below on scroll and a section-jump tab stuck under the header, serif-title sections (philosophy · dark material panel · colors · designer · white feature cards · before/after comparison · three reasons · awards · spec table · questions · customer photos · related products), and a separately built charcoal footer. For a long detail page selling one flagship product
Reading list — centered title and subscribe mark, thin line, two square photo cards (title·date), square page numbers. For shop notices and news lists
Privacy notice — narrow 540px column with a centered title and 22px body, clauses a) to h), dot lists, links. For text documents such as terms, privacy and seller info

notes: Flickity 2.2.2 (the slider of the original theme) is GPL-3.0, so it was not put in _vendor. In the recorded pages the only places Flickity actually slides are the single-slide product section (no sliding) and the notice bar, so only the same entrance (photo 1.25→1, title lines floating up) was ported to GSAP. The photo set in the detail view was rebuilt like the original page-builder version, where clicking a small photo swaps the large photo

The Hero video-platform background video and the bed video section use gray placeholder videos (media/*.mp4, wave pattern made with ffmpeg) of the same ratio and length (18s · 12s), set with autoplay · muted · loop · playsinline. The original Cat First. text is inside the video picture itself, so in the copy two English words are placed over it.
The original’s fixed bottom-right language switcher (a third-party widget, JA) belongs to someone else, so it is not included

Fonts: the page builder’s Section font Zen Kaku Gothic Antique (Japanese only) is a Korean slot, so it becomes Gothic A1, the Hiragino Mincho in the detail becomes Noto Serif KR, and Georgia becomes the same-shaped Gelasio
The search panel goes only as far as the 640px panel sliding in from the right, as in the original — the search suggestion list was not built. Cart and login are icon links only
Changed the type in pages.json: Privacy notice (about → page)

In the detail page (page-builder landing), the cart bar, section-jump tabs and before/after compare handle values could not be read from the original bundle (the page-builder app script is missing from the archive), so they are guessed from the screen — bar .4s, tabs stick below the header row.

title: Showcase card splitting four ways with a curved reel of tracks
good_for: Personal portfolios that present music or works as cards, genre-based collections, and dark 3D showroom landings.

pages.use: First page: under a light panel, one card-stack showcase turns once and scatters into four diagonal cells (hover widens a cell and grass grows), six recommended cards flow on a curved reel, then a View all star door, and at the end a one-line statement and contact. For an artwork collection portfolio hero

Recommended list — three-column (one on phone) grid of acting cards on a star stage, on hover the card comes forward and tilts toward the mouse, press for a right explanation panel. For work, song and product card list pages

notes: Tap a branch tile and the original is at /c/<Branch> Goes to the collection page (not recorded). Here it plays the same open transition as the original (the chosen display case grows to the center and the others fly sideways, .9s power2.inOut — the original length could not be read from the bundle, so this is a guess), then hands off to works.html with a white flash.

The ‹All› page (original /all, a white-background list of every track) and the search results page were not recorded, so they were not built. The ‹All› button, menu and search Enter reach works.html with the same white flash transition as the original (.55s power2.in, navigating at 440ms).

The 3D carries over the original numbers (camera fov 38 · (0,.15,3.6), showcase 1.07×1.43, card .78×.975, pile layout formula, morph and reel layout formulas, lerp .18·.12·.08, background liquid veil .18) and is rewritten with our own shaders. The original bloom post-process is replaced with an additive-blend glow plane under the light plane and over the base, and the showcase lighting (spot and side light) is simplified.

On category hover the original grows a different ‹world› per category (grass·fog·waves etc., WORLD_STAGE_FORMS) beneath the showcase. Here all four categories are reduced to the same grass (900 instanced blades, uGrow 0→1, rh .14) — a different stage per category is left for the next person to build.

When a card is pressed, the original plays the track along with a playback bar (71px player at the bottom). There is no sound or player here. The pressed card comes forward to the left, and only the right description panel (opacity 320ms, move 420ms cubic-bezier(.32,.72,.2,1)) and the ”Press a card to listen” hint (480ms, delayed 600ms) appear.
The phone’s first showcase shake (follows when dragged, bounces on a tap — heroShake) was not built.

The original is entirely in English, so the spots using the Gloock heading font (hero title, intro sentence, menu, featured line, contact statement and its two lines, list titles, description panel text, search placeholder, plus track titles, genre names and intro lines in brand.js) keep English placeholder text (hero, featured and contact in lowercase as in the original, genre line in sentence case). The genre cell name (kc__label) is Space Mono, but since it shares its name with the genre panel title, I matched it in English too. The card title italic is a synthetic italic because Gloock has no italic style.

Space Mono label slots (contact · button next to All/Search · Inquire via chat · category heading · View all n · view-all link · card date · tag · creator · back · n songs picked · close · tap card to listen) are body-font slots, so Korean is kept — they fall back to the system sans. This font backfill only changed the heading and decorative font slots.
The award ribbon (white band at right center) is not from the original site but an award badge, so it was not included.

Branch and card colors are content (a different color per genre and per track), so they use --site-world-* and --site-card-*, made by rotating the color wheel from the gold accent. They change along with the skin.

title: Window-light backdrop with drawn gold strings, plus a two-page company site
good_for: Special landing pages for premium multi-series products such as instruments, furniture or cars, linked to a company site with store lists and column articles.

pages.use: Special landing page for a product: a hero with one photo, logo, vertical copy and a demo circle, a scattered photo story crossed by a golden string, a dark keyboard photo, three staggered cards (modal), a performer slide, everyone’s photos, a lineup grid, four series where photos stick and white boards sweep in, two models, columns, and a dark store-finder footer. For premium product introductions.

Company site showroom list by series — a title band tucked under the header, red breadcrumb, rows per series with photo, intro and a Demo Store button, a PICK UP banner, six-column footer. For product-line guides and store finder pages

A single column article from a company site — title, date, view count, a collapsible table of contents box, red-bar h2 and red-dot h3, a comparison photo pair, a company intro band, three SNS links, popular and recommended article cards, category and tag boxes, recommended products. For blog or magazine article detail pages (tagged as news in the recording, but it is a single article, so article)

notes: The gold strings (original bg-melody.png·footer-melody.png) are image files in the original, so they were not carried over, they were redrawn as bundles of SVG curves following where the image passes. The reveal values (mask-size from the top, scrub 2 · phone 4, top center→bottom center / footer from the right 5s · phone 2s power1.out) are the same, only the curve shapes differ slightly from the original image.

Window-light shadows (fixed-noise01·02 PNG) are rebuilt as three blurred gradients plus an SVG noise grain, and the ghost English words (echo·voice·share·piano·column·store SVG drawings) are redone as Cormorant Garamond letters with a grain filter (feTurbulence+feDisplacementMap). The originals are image files, so they weren’t copied.

The logo and the red Brand lettering 'LOGO' Text placeholders, series names (brand series names) and model names were replaced with SERIES ONE~THREE·MODEL ONE/TWO. The company site menu text is also an image (nav.png) in the original, so it is set as text in the same 137px-wide slot.
Everyone’s photos are a paid external widget in the original, so a square photo grid placeholder is used, with no in-widget zoom or navigation to other pages.

The original story modal and player modal fill from loaded JSON, but here only one static piece of content each was put in, with the same form (photo and text alternating left and right). The video modal embed is a 16:9 placeholder.

On desktop the original scrolls to the top and refreshes .5s after the window width changes (first line of script.js). In a mixed build where sections are pulled out and combined, a refresh would wipe the state of other sections, so it is deliberately left out and only re-measures (ScrollTrigger refresh).

The PICK UP bxSlider uses the last 4.2 release (4.2.17) because the original 4.1.2 is not on npm. 4.2 also accepts mouse drag (pointer) while 4.1.2 took touch only, so touchEnabled is turned on for touch devices only — the other settings (maxSlides 6/1 · one slide at a time · 0.5s CSS ease · infinite loop · no pager) are as in the original.

Smooth scroll to top (original jquery.page-scroller) and column table-of-contents folding (table-of-contents-plus) are not used, since these outside plugins are CC BY-SA·GPL. They were rewritten the same way — 1/9 of the remaining distance every 16ms, list uses jQuery hide·show("fast") as is.
The column text has fewer paragraphs than the original, so document height at 1440 is 7.4k (original 8.5k). The types (table of contents, h2, h3, comparison photo pairs, tags, cards) are all there.

The ”Try it” circle in Find a Store matches the original in hover-out delay, length and curve, but the hover-in start lags by about 55ms — under the circle, a newly drawn gold string SVG (443rem wide, masked) and a grain-filter ghost text replace the original PNG, so the first repaint is heavy. Promoting the circle to its own layer (will-change) did not remove it. Baking the gold string into a single canvas could reduce it (left for the next person).

Colors made from skin variables with oklch(from …), like the column category pill, are interpolated by the browser in OKLab during transitions, so the midpoint color differs slightly from the original hex (sRGB interpolation) — length and end values are the same. This follows from the rule letting skins be swapped, so it is not reverted to hex.

Font backfill: on the index page, the two English lines over the photo ”This piano becomes your sound” (Cormorant Garamond) were left as copy transcribed from the original — replaced with Keyword / One short brand line goes right here. of the same character count, and data-label added to figcaption

The remaining Latin text (LOGO·GRAND PIANO·line up·SERIES ONE~THREE·CLEAR MODEL·HYBRID/SILENT ONE·MODEL ONE/TWO·PLAY MOVIE·ARTIST NAME·BRAND COLUMNS · ghost words echo/voice/share/piano/column/store · table of contents Contents · page numbers 01/09) are already English placeholders, so they were left as they are

index hero catch copy, daily big title, echo/voice/share/store section titles, echo card titles, performer names, modal titles — in the original these are Japanese Mincho serif (Shippori Mincho, picture text) titles, Korean kept. The pair, Noto Serif KR (serif ↔ serif), is already loaded
Fourth series ‹Clear Grand Piano› — the original has a katakana title, Korean kept (the lineup cell caption stays CLEAR MODEL as set earlier)
product·article titles·subtitles·company site menu — the original is Japanese (the menu is lettering in images), original script kept

title: Dark restaurant and bar site where photo panels slide up and cover
good_for: Fine dining, bar and restaurant group sites with two or more venues and photo- or video-led dark gourmet branding.

pages.use: Shop home — after the loader, a fixed cooking video and sound bar, two half-and-half sections (Space A·B) where the photo pane stays fixed while three photos cover it from below, a flame curtain and large italic phrase revealed in an empty 130vh, a parallax photo column, and a news window after 3 seconds. For a restaurant·bar home with two spaces

One space introduction — full-bleed photo header with in-page anchor text, three photos passing behind a pinned concept panel, hours and price rows, a drag-to-advance photo strip, parallax photo columns. For the intro page of a single restaurant, bar or store (in the home page’s RESTAURANT·BAR menu slot)

About the shop — big title and owner greeting over a fixed flame video, a full-width photo cell stays pinned while three interior photos slide up over it, two people profiles (hover over the photo for a bio). For shop and chef About pages.

notes: The four videos are placeholders from media/ instead of the originals (a band sweeps over a dark panel and a bar below fills to the length) — the hero cooking video and the video window at 47.26s 16:9, and the flame at 12.01s 16:9, baked as HLS (m3u8, 1.877s segments) like the original and loaded with hls.js 1.7.3 (maxMaxBufferLength 1). Playback behavior is the same as the original: the hero plays when the loader clears, pauses and hides when title-cell pinning starts, reloads the PC or phone version when crossing 900px, the flame loads when the bottom of the bar section is reached and pauses on play or when scrolling back, the flame on the about page plays immediately, and the video window loads on first open.

The phone hero video (spKv/full.m3u8) and loader video (loading.mp4) are missing or broken in the archive, so length and ratio couldn’t be measured — the phone panel is set to 9:16·47.26s, the loader to 16:9·6s loop
The sound bar works like the original: it unmutes the Hero video and moves volume 0→1 over .6s (when turned off 1→0, then mute) — the sound in the placeholder video is a very quiet pink noise

Opened via file://, the hls.js XHR is blocked by CORS so the video is not loaded and a placeholder box is left (to avoid console errors). Video playback and the swup transition only show when served over http — on file:// swup is not enabled, and the same black panel covers for .3s before a normal navigation

The bar (/bar) page has the same shape as the restaurant, so it is built as a single service.html — RESTAURANT and BAR on both home and menu go to service.html. The bar’s differences (two opening-hours cells, terrace notice) are handled by duplicating one more opening-hours row. ACCESS and NEWS were not recorded, so they are left as # links.

The text mask redraws the top and bottom edge coordinates of the original brush-stroke image (mask.png 1622×3546) as an SVG polygon of the same shape (size · position · repeat · .8s ease-out · 25ms interval are original values). The original’s 4px edge blur is not included.

Fonts: baskerville-display-pt (paid)→Baskervville, neue-haas-grotesk-display (paid)→Inter, Noto Sans JP→Noto Sans KR. The logo and the six sister-brand logos in the footer are placeholders (the logo is redrawn as a diamond + italic Logo)
Language button (EN) · social link · booking link are shape only
Cards were auto, so the breakdown cells (7 layout axes, motion, key scene) were filled with values read from the bundle

title: Sandy cream panel where photos pin and stack for a stroll garden
good_for: Gardens, parks, heritage sites and museums with photo-led, quiet sites featuring a headline, daily news, news cards, facility info and access.

pages.use: Garden home — sand-textured hero (Cinzel tagline + two lines dropping from the label to the first photo + today’s news panel), pinned stack of three photos, an About section with two slanted lines, three news cards, events, a parallax band, three squares, and a full photo + three title bands

Garden intro. A header photo, breadcrumb and right-aligned title, two photos, then text and portrait in two columns (the second column swaps left and right) with a full-bleed photo per column. For an institution’s history and people stories
News list — hero photo, title, year tabs (ALL, years), three sand-textured cards (photo, date, category, title, three-line summary), and pagination. For notice and event lists.

notes: Of the four in pages.json, no. 3 (/en English first page) has the same form as the first page, and no. 4 (/en/news/s/all/p/1) the same form as news list page 1, so index.html·news.html stand in for them.

The sand grain (original bg-sand.png multiply) does not use an image — SVG noise (feTurbulence, black alpha .06) is laid over the skin’s surface color (--kf-raised) with the same multiply to recreate it — the black alpha of the noise is the grain’s light and dark, not the skin.

The logo (three vertical Chinese characters + small English), SNS and language icons are newly drawn placeholders. The hero photo, three photos, parallax band, three squares, full-width photo band and footer photo are wf-img placeholders, and a sand-grain panel tints over them with multiply as in the original.

Decision: the title and menu of the original English version (English set in Noto Serif) are originally a translation of a Japanese site, so they were kept as Korean placeholders. The Cinzel tagline, wordmark and Jost labels (menu·Explore the Garden·Pick up News·Learn More·date) are English placeholders.

The news card category cell (original: Notice) and the year tabs (ALL, years) are kept exactly as in the original. The pagination was rebuilt with the small chevrons and numbers of the original screen.

title: Melting thermal-rainbow wordmark for a three-day event page
good_for: Music festival, concert and exhibition one-pagers covering dates, lineup, tickets and venue.

pages.use: Single page for a three-day event — melting thermal-imaging wordmark, mirrored word boundary, poster lineup, spectrum cards, thermal scanner, review arches, tiered-by-temperature tickets, FAQ, sticky venue photos. For music festival and performance intros

notes: The original is a single page (pages: [] in pages.json), so there are no subpages.

The photo slot is a subject-shaped grayscale heat distribution (CSS gradient+noise) with the same thermal filter as the original applied. The same photo goes into both .k-heat__map·.k-heat__plain When put in as this, the filter and the original color band apply as is. The gray in the heat distribution is a temperature value fed to the filter, so it is written as a ratio between --site-heat-hot and cold (black and white, not a Skin).

The thermal-filter table (the nine cells of #k-heat) is rewritten by shared.js reading --site-heat-0~8 made from the skin (within 1/255 of the original table). If script is off, the original table written in the html remains, so even if the skin is changed, only the photo heat colors stay as in the original.

The wordmark placeholder is TITLE0, whose total glyph width is close to the original wordmark (1274px vs 1317px at 1440). With many wide letters like SAMPLE it wraps past one line, so enlarge --glyph when replacing it (around .9 for Korean).

Type placeholders (2026-11-07): Kalnia headings, quotes and closing lines (8 slots) and the Hubot Sans narrow uppercase slots (menu drawer, night name, venue name, performers, ticket, media name, date month) were replaced with English placeholders matching the original line counts, and data-label says what to put in. English-replaced Kalnia headings get lang="en" Attached so that the original values (1.02 · -0.02em) apply instead of the Korean line height (1.18) and letter spacing of .k-display:lang(ko). For night and place names, remove --glyph(.95) and set --len to the character count.

Keep Korean (judgement): small uppercase eyebrows (k-eyebrow — place · city · weekday · item · photo caption), body text, lead, FAQ questions, ticket perks and schedule lines are small text in the body typeface (Hubot Sans, with a Korean gothic taking over the Korean), so they stay Korean even though the original is Latin. The Hahmlet pair is no longer used but is left in theme.css for when Korean titles are put back. Header and footer menus and buttons are the same items as the drawer menu, so they are in English together.

The original 8b’s queueMotion (lazy creation that builds a scene only when it is near the screen) was reduced to building everything at once after fonts load. The visible motion is the same (Lenis 1.3 lerp .085 · melt .62 · droplet delays [0,3,1,5,2,4]×.076 · rise .16→1 over 1.05s expo.out · dummy power2.inOut gap .42 · pin 1.7 screens · arch .3→1), and only the moment the scenes are built differs.
The original’s external payment link (optional) and newsletter submit were replaced with a same-page anchor and a non-submitting form.

title: Handwriting drawn over video and wave-mask transitions for a forest lodge
good_for: Lodge, ryokan, glamping and resort landing pages covering two room types, facilities, dining, area guide, news and access.

pages.use: Lodging first page — over a fixed background video, a handwritten wordmark (4s) fades out with a 50px blur, and while the concept text is held in place six scattered photos pass by with parallax. Includes a watercolor site map·two room cells (hover photo swap·modal Swiper)·spa·pets·dining collage·a horizontally flowing travel photo band·news·an accordion directions section·a photo stage booking button. For nature lodging·resort landing pages
News list — centered handwritten section name with hand-drawn underline rows (title, date, arrow), twelve lines. For notice lists of inns and shops
News item — ink line under date and large title, paragraph body, centered back link. For a single notice or guide post
Terms — big centered title, article (Article 0) heading with numbered list and parenthesized-number sub-list. For long rule text like lodging terms, usage rules and privacy policy

notes: Watercolor layout map · neighborhood map: instead of the original watercolor art, redrawn as SVG (green, water-blue and sand surfaces with edges bled by feTurbulence + room building numbers · parking · golf course labels) in the same position, size and color feel — fewer trees, roads and small text than the original
The background video and logo video are a 30-second placeholder gradient mp4 (media/hero-loop.mp4, made by us), with the fixed (position: fixed) placement and automatic loop kept as in the original

The original wave_black.png (a blurred wave panel that darkens the area behind the concept text, blur 50px) is replaced by a --kf-contrast-bg 42% panel laid in the same spot with a wave mask and blur 50px — the panel shape was matched by eye from the screen, not measured from the original image

The blur mask (original mask.webp), wave band (wave.png), hand-drawn button borders (border-*.svg) and hand-drawn underline (border.png) were redrawn as the same shapes in SVG and placed as data URIs — changed after running into a case where, opened via file://, the file mask was blocked by CORS and the whole element was hidden

The card’s lenis is a false auto-detection (it is nowhere in the bundle or docs). The room modal’s Swiper has no version marking in the original bundle (it has swiperElementNodeName and loopAddBlankSlides from 11.x), so swiper@11.1.14 was used — version estimated.

Bottom right ‹How may I help you?› is an external chatbot, so only a speech bubble and round button spot are placed. The header Q&A (external chatbot question window) is only a FAQ spot link. There is no English (EN) version

title: Small seaside hotel with a quiet photo slideshow and vertical headings
good_for: Small lodging, retreat and ryokan brand sites with a slow photo hero, vertical-writing intro, flowing photo band, facility list and area journal.

pages.use: Lodging first page — opening where a paper curtain lifts and photos cross-fade in the hero, vertical-text heading intro over a sea photo, endlessly flowing room photo strip, three facility rows with ring-filling dots, journal photo strip, news rows. For small lodging, café or workshop brand homes

About — parallax flowing sea header photo, Japanese placeholder body + vertical-writing title, wide photo slider, English tagline and English body + vertical photo slider. For intros telling the history of a region or name

Journal (local guide) list: large title and lead, a map area topped by a category picker box, category pills, place cards with a photo slider on a rounded surface (name, text, shop, address, map link), and page numbers. For nearby shops, sights guides and magazine lists

notes: Two of the four recorded sub-pages were not built — /gallery, when opened, turned out to be the first-page frame as an empty hero with no dedicated CSS·JS (the recorded screen is also broken), so there is no gallery type, and /journal_category/eat-and-drink has the same type as the journal list (just a category-filtered version), so it was merged into a single news.html

sites pull stopped with ENAMETOOLONG on a long file name from a web font service URL, so the subpages were not unpacked — read the HTML, CSS and JS by unpacking the archived pages.har.zip directly (the tool needs fixing)

The original journal map is an external map service (pin dialog), so it is replaced by our SVG map image at the same position and size, with pin placeholders. Only the category picker box open/close (.3s) runs as in the original. Page numbers are shape only

The original paper-grain pattern (texture_desktop.png) is an image file, so it is not used, a new SVG feTurbulence pattern is laid down instead. The logo, vertical serif Korean headline and English tagline are images (SVG/PNG) in the original, so they were rewritten as text of the same position and size (serif wordmark, vertical Noto Serif KR, Cormorant Garamond)
A dark overlay (--kf-contrast-bg at 45% and 35%) sits over the placeholders so the light text over the hero and sea About photos stays readable — the original photos show a dark room and a deep sea
To loop endlessly, the room and journal flow bands add one more set of the same photo cells, like the original markup (rooms large screen 5→10, journal 5→10)
The top notice line on the home page (original informatin-line) only has room for short text — the original script trims long text and appends it, but the placeholder is short.
Wedding, Room, Facility, News, Access and the sub links in the drawer and footer are pages that were not recorded, so they are set to #

Swiper is swiper@11.0.7 already in _vendor (same version as the original), and luxy.js is newly added as _vendor/luxy.js@0.0.7 (the npm version has no LICENSE file, so a standard notice was placed following the MIT in package.json and the header).

title: Hand-drawn guide map where speech-bubble pins pop out in sequence
good_for: Experience facilities, tourist spots, campuses and mixed-use venues that open with a guide map and show per-facility info, events and a business calendar.

pages.use: Facility home — a hand-drawn guide map where pins bounce into place and speech bubbles pop up in turn every 6 seconds, three news rows, a photo sticking out to the left with a vertical serif title, vertical intro text, big-word sections CAFE·SHOP·LABO, an event fade slider, a storehouse, and special product cards. For tourist facility·multi-shop homes

In-facility shop — a rounded-corner head photo with a faint vertical SHOP, a vertical serif pillar heading and opening-hours box, three product rows with staggered photos and text, a black circle label band, and a slider of other product photos. For store and product subpages
News list — large English title, a list where photo·date·category pill·title rows draw lines to the right edge, spinner while loading. For event·notice lists

About — rounded-corner hero photo, one line of large serif, intro text broken line by line with line drawings, thin-text marquee and photo marquee. For About pages conveying a facility’s or company’s philosophy
Single news item — date · title, body in a white rounded panel (photos · subheads), vertical NEWS outside the panel, back to list. For press releases and notice bodies

notes: The original hand-drawn map, speech bubbles and line illustrations were redrawn as SVG — same positions, sizes and color groups (water · grass · trees · cherry blossoms · buildings · parking), but the watercolor brush texture is only imitated with feTurbulence wobble
The original paper-texture background image is not used, a solid --kf-bg is used instead

The original first menu items (the brewery tour, cafe, experience and special sake pages) were not recorded, so they were not built — menu items 1·2·4·5 link to section anchors on the first page. That is why the transition measurement differs in length: the original goes to a subpage and the copy goes to the first page.
Hovering a calendar date has a small change in the original (interact), but it isn’t caught in motion measurement so it was not built separately
The phone map crops a 640px map centered like the original, but since the SVG art differs from the original, some parts look slightly different
compare.cjs side-by-side video ran only the first page at 1440 (browser slots were crowded, so subpages use the full-capture side-by-side view instead)

Scripts are generally <script src> Still the same, but <head> On defer·blocking="render" Loaded that way: shared.js draws the header band, pillar and footer, so the first paint should come after that (the original is rendered on the server, so they already exist in the first frame). Placed at the end, it would redraw once after the first frame and the load curve would diverge from the original

title: Curtain-style entry and cloud scroll horizontal-scrolling kimono shop
good_for: Shop and brand sites that lead with illustrated storytelling, such as traditional crafts, hanbok, tea houses and festivals.

pages.use: Shop home page — opening video (1.5s fade when it ends), looping shop-curtain video with neon photo, latest news panel, channel card, horizontal scroll of 6 cloud illustrations (background gradient interpolated per slide, 9 on phone), three boxes for events, meetups and shop info, footer box
News list: cream box over a fixed gradient background with two-column photo cards and a Load more button (press it to append the next page of cards), plus a big vertical word at bottom left
Store info — center seal, road map illustration on the left, address · phone · hours · directions table on the right. A spot for a store location and business info page
Contact — form in 30% label | 70% input rows and a double-bordered confirm button (does not send)

notes: The original illustrations (clouds, pine, mountain, shrine gate, winged robe, goddess, votive plaque, map, logo) were redrawn as SVG in the same spots and with the same aspect ratio (original image sizes were measured and set on the box with aspect-ratio). The brush strokes, texture and fine detail of the originals are missing and the shapes are simple — the art slots are changed in one place, KB.art in shared.js.

title: Single 3D bottle follows you and changes into three wines
good_for: Brand pages for wine, spirits, perfume or drinks with one bottle as the hero, a few products paged in turn, and origin and where-to-buy info.

pages.use: A single brand first page — a loader that fills like a bowl and an age-verification gate, a 3D bottle on a dark hero, a brand statement whose letters darken, three products where the bottle spins and changes label and stage color, a pouring-into-a-glass scene, a photo band where photos grow in the gaps of the title, a map, a purchase panel where the bottle stands on a branch, retailers and footer. notes: Only one subpage was recorded, /fr, and it is the French version of the same home page (type page in pages.json), so it was not built separately and only an En / Fr slot was left in the header. The original also has no other subpage besides the privacy policy.

The original bottle is a GLTF model shrunk with draco plus HDR environment light. The model and environment images are not used, it is rebuilt with our own lathe-solid (LatheGeometry) fluted bottle (body radius .109·shoulder .45~neck .82·cap .19), label cylinder segments (front 2.1rad, back 1.4rad), and our own PMREM room (two large windows·one reflector). The label art is a golden mosaic mass (our own canvas drawing) — the spot for the original art can be swapped for a label image (stage.js drawLabel).

The original pour scene is a pre-rendered image frame sequence (holdFrame 1893, canvas). The same scroll range (pour section, 6 units) is redrawn in 3D. The bottle rises and tilts 118°, our lathe-shaped glass rises from below, the stream (tube) grows, and the wine level in the glass rises to the cutting plane. The background photo texture of the original image, such as hands and table, is absent.

Scroll length: the original MOTION_CONFIG (heroViewportHeights 8.25, wine…, carousel 6.65, map sequenceScale 2.5) multiplies several factors to set section length. Rather than port all of that math, I shot the original in 48 sections at 800px wheel units and for each section took the wheel distance it used as screen heights 1 = 1 unit” converted (hero 4 · wine three 12.3 · pouring 5.6 · photo strip 9 · map 5.4 · purchase 3) and put on one pinned section timeline. Lengths, gaps and curves inside each section are the original values.

Phone: in the original, smooth-scrollbar takes finger input on phones. The copy is set the same way. Only the original’s first phone screen was compared (could not trigger its touch scrolling headless) — the phone layouts of the sections below (wine panel text position, photo strip spot) were judged by scaling down the wide-screen layout.

Lattice light pattern: the original is a diamond-pattern.png mask (an image of window-frame shadows). Instead of the image, two blurred diagonal bands (.kw-light, soft-light) are used — the pattern shape (window-frame diamonds) is absent.
The first photo in the strip is an auto-looping video (video_intro) in the original. Use muted loop autoplay in the same spot <video> is set, and src is left empty (placeholder).

The map does not use the original country and region boundary svg and is drawn with our own polygons — draw order and durations (boundary 1.2 with .12 stagger → fill .5 → dots .44 with .08 stagger → pull-up 1.15 power2.inOut) are the original values.
thumb.jpg: shot.cjs --thumb captured the age verification gate, so a separately written capture script shot the hero past the gate at the same size (1440×900).

The hero grapevine trunk is a 3D model in the original and turns ±15° with cursor x (follows with target .035 · rotation .08 — the trunk turns, not the bottle). We stood up two twisted tubes of our own in 3D at the same position and thickness (about .16 of screen height) and turned them with the same values. The bark grain is canvas stripes, so the original model’s knots and moss texture are missing. The horizontal branch on the purchase version is a photo cutout in the original (cta_branch_v2.webp), so we drew it as an SVG branch at the same position and size, and data-label reads ”moss-covered vine branch cutout”.

The afterimage smear (the version that switches at a 1% chance when chaos strength is .5 or higher) was rewritten with our three shaders (previous frame over color pass with .98 drag feedback → copy → brightness·contrast). The list title’s ‹triangle fragments› (break-txt) is a 2D mosaic the original draws with three.js planar triangles, so it was drawn in Canvas 2D with the same values (151 Name points · inner triangles shrunk 1~15% · 1.1× (10→1) scale · ±10px jitter · every 10 frames).

Detail of one condition (service) — a wooden pillar table of contents pinned to the screen (passed sections · arrow on the current one), a flying squirrel voice button in a tree hollow, a framed header, worry speech bubbles, per-section English tag + title + body, green device choices, a similar-conditions box · numbered accordion, research cards, FAQ, consultation box, and a list of cards from the same category. notes: Kept as is (by rule, our own art): the animal watercolor illustrations (walrus, gorilla, zebra, sheep, raccoon, island map, flying squirrel, hippo·giraffe, tree trunk·bark·branch·woodpecker) cannot be ported from the original, so they were redrawn as SVG in the same position, size and pose. The watercolor texture comes from SVG filters in art.js. Low-frequency noise wobbles the brush edges, edges are dark and the interior pale (pigment pooling as it dries), and high-frequency noise mottles the interior density (paper grain). Each viewBox width group (120·200·400·640) is tuned to look the same on-screen size. Individual hairs and brush strokes are the art itself, so they are not ported. All fills use --site-ill-*, built by rotating the accent color wheel, so they change along with the skin.

The original motion is jQuery Velocity 1.2.2 — the same Béziers (easeOutQuart .165,.84,.44,1 etc.) were ported to GSAP as CustomEase, and the Velocity spring (1−cos(4.5πp)·e^−6p) as a function of the same formula. The open-source libraries the original uses are the same set: barba 2.9.7·lenis 1.0.18 (wide screens only, lerp .2·duration .6)·slick 1.8.1 (frame slider·checklist asNavFor)·infiniteslide v2 (about photo strip, speed 40)·jQuery 3.7.1

The doctor illustration switching carries over only the first two cuts of the original btnAudioDoctorLoop (16s cycle). Cuts 3 to 6 (the following 10s) are two placeholder images and were dropped. The button returning when the sound ends, and stopping when entering the list section on phone, make no sense without sound and were not added

Phone (1023px and below): the first-page head is out of flow (absolute) and the logo title sticks to the top left and follows (fixed 14rem · 16rem). The menu button and the top text · specialty tags come out in .15s only after scrolling down 35px (logo always visible — original body.top .header-title). The two menu-button lines turn into X · white at once with no transition. The inner drawer panel waits .1s after the press, then rises from 15px below over .3s easeOutCubic (what Velocity.hook applies after its wait). The Reserve button is an 85rem dark-green pill with one-line text. The News list is a row list rather than a grid (left 105rem 4:3 thumbnail · date at the top corner of the row · bottom rule per row), and the wide-screen body min height (850rem) is released on phone. Condition detail phone head (100dvh tree-bark, frame 148×151rem · vertical name tag · Case number · vertical h2 · h1, flipped branch and woodpecker, flying squirrel in the burrow at .8x) and the TOC drawer (.btn-page-nav 38rem round button → .drop-page-nav drops down 10px over .4s easeOutCubic, button .4s easeOutQuart · close icon 180° .1s, tapping a section link closes it). title: Classic hotel with a rounded curtain that rises to open the page
