pages.use: Hotel home — 11s opening with a year roll and old photos flying in, video that swells open from a box, About section where the background turns red, three room cards, restaurant, shop, wedding and banquet cards that stick to the screen and stack, About and News. For heritage inns and long-established brand homes
Shop: big English title header, online shop banner, seven product rows with photo slider, shop info table, shop news rows. For souvenir and sweets product lists of hotels and stores

Hotel About: header photo widening from a strip, a history section where the background turns charcoal with a drag-to-scroll timeline, facility rows, three-column nearby attraction cards, and guest experience cards. For long-established inns and shops.
News list — per group, a serif section name on the left and a date row list on the right, plus a report group of three photo cards. For news · notice · event lists
News item — serif title · date · category, schedule · fee paragraphs, dotted underline links, rounded “Back to list” button. For event info · notice body

notes: The card listed three, swiper and lottie, but reading the original bundle shows three is used only for color interpolation (Color.lerp — opening curtain background ink→paper color, shop card text color) and draws nothing, while swiper ships CSS only and is not used on these five pages. So it is built without WebGL or Swiper, and the color blend reads --kf-ink and --kf-bg and mixes at the same ratio. What looked like a video curved into a dome was not a shader but an SVG clipPath (four quadratic curve edges) — a new dome-clip-reveal Motion part was written with the same formula.

The menu drawer background Lottie (the original grid and bellflower line art, drawn with trim path during the first 1s of 2s) was replaced with two line drawings of ours (menu-a.json grid · menu-b.json wildflowers) on the same build (lottie-web 5.12.2) and with the same timing. Since XHR is blocked on file://, the same content is also carried in menu-lottie.js and used as animationData

The first video is a placeholder (wf-video). Since the original video is a dark forest valley, a 55% ink-black veil is laid over the placeholder so the bright tagline reads. Video playback itself (plays from the start at 8.5s) is absent because it is a placeholder
The original background paper grain (noise_0/1.png) is an image file so it is not used, a new SVG feTurbulence pattern (6%) is laid instead

The bottom-right chat support widget (talkappi — external service, two buttons plus a speech bubble) is not built. The booking window is an external booking engine (Direct In) form, so only its look is placed at the same spot with the same entrance (.25s), with no date calendar or search.

Header menu items 1, 2, 4, 5 (Rooms, Dining, Wedding, Banquet) and their sublinks are unrecorded pages, so they are set to #. The language picker only opens its box as in the original, with no other language versions.

The widening of the sub-page header photo is built as in the original (follows scroll by 10% per frame), and the shop page has no photo as in the original — only pale giant Latin text flows (-no-scroll)

The About photo (right side of the hotel About section) does not fire dome-clip-reveal’s on: scroll detection in this one slot (another IntersectionObserver on the same element does fire, confirmed by measuring), so it is set to on: manual and the [data-reveal-one] detection in shared.js opens it. The values (.25s delay · 1.5s power2.inOut · lag .1) are the same. The cause (absolute placement + staggered transform slot) is for the next person to follow up on.

title: Regional video project set on a map with pins dropping in
good_for: Video or AR projects tied to places, local shop campaigns and brand sites centered on a map-based list of locations.

pages.use: Project home page — a giant wordmark with overlapping photos, photo pieces cut into geometric shapes with scattered pins, intro·place video list·contact divided by flowing large text bands, a blurred map that sticks and follows then gets pinned in a regional map, and a footer listing makers·people

A place video: a large video on top, previous·next, the place name and the two people who made it, their words, a row of round face photos by role (video · sound · place), app · back. For a single case or work detail.

App intro — white wordmark, intro video button, and store badges over a background video pinned behind the screen, three picture cards of uses and three phone-screen video columns on a translucent panel (Swiper slide on phones), makers’ words, a row of faces, and Contact. For app and service intro pages

notes: Day · night skin: chosen by the clock like the original (06:00–17:59 day, otherwise [data-theme=dark]). ?nowstr=Append something like 2130 to see the night type. The night type flips the original nighttime artwork (dark map photo · white wordmark) with the same skin variables, so the map texture and contrast differ from the original night screen.

The background aerial map photo is replaced with a building and street pattern baked on canvas in the skin color (shared.js paintMap, 900px tile · edges wrapped). To use a photo, give .mk-main’s --site-map-tile a url().

The wordmark is an English placeholder set in Comfortaa 700 as SVG text (textLength 1440) fitted to the width, instead of the original logo artwork. The overlap where outlined text remains with multiply over overlapping photos (original title-line-img) is done with a stroke version of the same SVG.

The six video captures cropped into geometric shapes do not use the original mask SVG. They were redrawn with SVG clipPath (mountain, lower semicircle, wedge, figure 8, diamond, quarter circle). The exact ratio of the mountain shape is an approximation matched by visual comparison.

Video-platform videos (6 place videos · the video above the detail · the app intro video) and GIFs · background mp4 · phone screen recordings are placeholders in the same position and ratio. Looping slots have an is-loop stripe flowing to show they are auto-looping videos, and clicking a thumbnail opens a 16:9 window over a black .8 overlay with .5s linear, as in the original (no playback).

Parallax uses the same Rellax as the original (rellax@1.12.1, center: true, breakpoints [576,768,1201], speeds .2·.5) as is. The Rellax version bundled inside the original top.js is unknown, so npm 1.12.1 is used. As a part, a span: on (Rellax style) option was added to center-parallax.

The header’s 1s round trip (the transparent header slides out, then comes back down as a low white-panel header, reversed when back at the top) is made by adding the round: on option to dock-down-header. The original chains transitionend, so fast scrolling can trigger one more round trip, but this part only fixes the state changed during the slide-out and comes down just once.
slide-up (from 100px below, .8s easeOutCubic, hides again once it moves 1.5 screens away) was made by adding an again option to fade-up. jQuery easeOutCubic is the same formula as GSAP power2.out.

Map pins: six, like the original HTML (the CSS leaves room for nine). Clicking a pin scrolls down to that place’s row like the original _goto, over (target y × .5)ms with easeOutCubic. The vertical region-name letters use placeholder glyphs for ‘region name’ drawn as outline strokes instead of the original Chinese characters.

The yellow illustration cards of the three use cards on the app page do not use the original illustrations. Newly drawn SVG illustrations (a door, a building, a phone above clouds) stand in the same spots. As in the original, the card swipe is swiper@7.4.1 only at 768px and below (slidesPerView 1.5 · centered).
The maker logos and SNS icons are trademarks, so they were replaced with English placeholder text and generic share-shaped icons.

title: Black manifesto page with entrance door, folding title and spinning line-art rings
good_for: Brand manifestos, vision statements and campaign pages that open with an entrance door and unfold as a long story told in short lines with animated line art.

pages.use: A single declaration page — entry gate (logo · two-line intro · button) → a large two-line title at screen center that lights up and folds away → per-sentence 1920×1080 line-art Lottie loops (city · speech bubble · starry night · sunset pyramid · headphones · waveform · input icon · concentric ellipses) → an outlined year quote box → closing with store badges · social links · document download. Brand vision and campaign on one page

notes: The original is a single page (pages: [] in pages.json), so there are no subpages. It has no separate menu or footer either, so shared.css holds only three text styles plus sunset and line variables, and there is no shared.js.

The eight line-art plates could not carry over the original Lottie JSON, so they are our own svg line art (one side-profile head reused with only position and size changed, surrounding shapes newly drawn), baked by the lottie-loop-scene part at the same plate size (1920×1080, last 1920×1461) and with the same playback (svg render, 30fps 150-frame loop, autoplay, stops on press). What moves in each scene (line sweep, blink, spreading ring, floating, rotation) was picked from the original layer names and the screen. The timing of each keyframe is not the same.
The original gradient line (gray line fading at both ends) was kept as a solid gray line.
The sunset behind the meditation scene is a single photo in the original — redrawn with orange, magenta and purple radial-gradients derived from the accent color (.m-art--sun).

The two title lines were set as letter graphics (svg) in the original — replaced with the same Roboto letters, set at 152px · 60px (phone 50px two lines · 21px) to match the original letter height. As this is English placeholder copy, letter widths differ slightly from the original
The 1968 year is three outlined numeral images in the original (left 19 · right 68 · phone 1968) — redrawn as svg text with a stroke on Roboto 300 glyphs (00 · 00 · 0000).

The five store badges are official store badge images in the original — replaced with outlined badge placeholders (circle icon + two-line text) of the same widths (175·189·212·212·212px) and height 57px.
In the original CSS, the black gradient bands above and below from :global(#__next:before/after) have a broken selector and don’t show even in the original screen, so they weren’t carried over.

title: Portfolio where work videos flow like liquid along a curved arc
good_for: Portfolios for freelancers, creative developers and small studios where the first screen is the work list and each project opens a photo and video gallery in a single-screen app-like site.

pages.use: Home page and work list · after a number loader, six work video panels spread on a 180° curved arc, and wheel or drag rotates them while the panels pinch at the waist and bend with speed. The lower arc shows ring progress and the title below rolls to change. About at the top right is a half-panel intro. For a personal or studio portfolio Hero.

A single Work (case): the pressed panel covers the screen, and on the brightened panel that Work’s 16:9 screen recordings and captures loop endlessly in a vertical strip. Top left shows three lines (category · role · partners), and the bottom bar holds the gallery progress circle · prev/title/next · close. For Work detail and case pages.

notes: The original is three r185 WebGPU (TSL node materials). This uses the same round’s three (r185, _vendor/three@0.185.0) but rewrites the same formulas with WebGLRenderer and our own GLSL shaders (cylinder wrap · speed waist pinch 1−|v|×.008 · RGB split v×.0022 · light panel width ×.585/.862/.75 · rounded corner 4.5 · dither). The original KTX2 images and Mux video are not used. Each panel draws a canvas placeholder video (30 frames per second) with a flowing light blob.

The loader number counts 0→100 by time, not by real download progress as in the original (it is a placeholder, so there is nothing to download). It is matched to the loader length measured on the original (hero 3.05s, case 3.2~3.27s, 3.1~4.0s depending on network), with hero 1.83s and case 2.45s power1.inOut, set strongly. The roll (.35s expo, per cell), arc draw (1.75s expo) and number exit (.75s, .15 later) are the original values.

The About panel opening carries over the original order — the About text slides left by its own width (.75s expo) and Close comes in, the button width shrinks to the Close width (.15s, .09 late), and since the panel is bright the button text color flips to the background color. Counting the blocks inside the panel from the top, each is k×.025 late (capability list k=10 · Awards list k=Starts from 21 — number of front chunks in the original panel) lines rise, skills draw circles (.75s expo) and dots (back.out 1.7), awards count up and underlines extend, face photos clip 25%→0.
The number of panels in the case gallery is 4~6 per work (original 4~6), and video cells are set to odd cells — in the original the photo and video mix differs per work.

About panel inner scroll is the default vertical scroll instead of the original’s hand-built drag and inertia. Line rise (.75s · .025 stagger), clip open (.75s expo), cover (.75/.5s) and the cursor Close label use the original values. The original’s email-copy sparkle (Physics2D emoji) was left out.

title: Seaside guide group with vertical titles and pinned video

pages.use: Guide group home page — a pinned Hero video (auto-play, loop) with vertical copy, an About with scattered photos over a translucent band, a white panel of members, an About video panel opened by pressing, a regional introduction with vertical titles, a vertical-writing experience list, a lodging band, a route-map access Section, and flowing-photo Contact. A Menu pill appears once the Hero has passed, opening a blurred-panel menu. For an experience and tourism guide home.
Group About — full-bleed photo header · scattered photos and vertical heading About text · video panel · two-column member cards with changing photos. For group and club About pages
Member list — below a full-bleed photo header, two-column member cards (change to another shot on hover). For people, guide or instructor list slots

Area introduction — full photo header, two-underline title with scattered photos, staggered two-column topics (geography, history, specialties, roads), four-column sights cards. For neighborhood and tourist spot pages.

notes: The hero background video and intro video are placeholder videos — the hero uses media/hero.mp4 (16:9) and hero-sp.mp4 (9:16, 760px and below), autoplaying, muted, looping and pinned to the screen like the original, and the intro video (a video embed in the original) plays media/movie.mp4 on click in the same 84:50 panel.

The original vertical copy, the large blurred text of the lodging strip, and the logo are image files, so they were replaced with placeholder vertical text and a newly drawn sun and wave symbol. The access route map and the land silhouette behind the area introduction are also redrawn as simple SVGs in the same place and size.
The original Zen Kaku Gothic New and Zen Old Mincho have no Hangul, so they were swapped for Gothic A1 and Nanum Myeongjo (the English bracket labels use the same Sora).

The original bundle includes Swiper·lottie·slideKvX (horizontal flow), but these four pages’ markup has no element that uses them (.slider-*·lottie·.slideKvX), so they are not included. The experience detail, stay detail and contact form pages were not recorded, so they are not built.

Paging between subpages is a plain page navigation in the original (no transition), so it was left as is. Subpages have no Hero indicator (#addFixed) as in the original, so on wide screens the Menu pill stays hidden (on phones it is always visible).

Placeholder text length was set to match the original underline widths (header menu first line 36px, buttons 187·156px) — the underline is drawn as wide as the text, so shorter text changes the end value.

Font backfill — hero vertical copy, video panel vertical copy, region intro, experience list, lodging band vertical title — the original uses kana and kanji titles (Zen Old Mincho), Korean kept. The companion serif Nanum Myeongjo is already loaded.

Typeface backfill — section titles (members · access · contact · subpage header h1 · area intro underlined title · sights card title) — the original has kanji/kana titles, Korean kept (same serif pairing).
Typeface backfill — header and footer logo text — the original is a Chinese-character logo image, Korean kept. The English line under the logo (Sora) was an English placeholder from the start.

Typeface backfill — bracketed section names · Menu/Close · Contact · member English name line (Sora) were English from the start, so nothing was swapped. Images were not re-shot since the text stayed the same.

Project record list — black stage, left vertical filter (sticks and follows), a photo grid with staggered sizes and pagination. For project and portfolio lists

News list — white stage, vertical categories on the left, three-per-row card grid. For company news and recruiting news lists

Careers — staggered three English lines over a people slider whose four color panels swap, table of contents, message, careers news, feature numbers, numeric donut chart, benefits, photo collection. For a careers site’s hero and About

notes: The logo (M mark·brand letters) doesn’t use the original artwork, it is redrawn as our geometric M (four-color bars) and an English placeholder BRAND. The reveal’s hole shape is also that M (clip-path polygon evenodd). The footer’s line-M zigzag is an SVG line at the same position·ratio as the original

The ”homeImageMaskChange” above the hero video (a scene where four photos change by mask while passing the pledge text) was not built — only text passes over the video. A job for the next person to pick up

The history photo bend was moved to the new part velocity-bend-gl with the same three(r180) and the same values as the original (amplitude .1 · wavelength 0 · bend .01 · strength .07 · Lenis velocity). Since the photos are placeholders, the panel image is also a placeholder drawn on canvas. The original photo-swap displacement shader (texture1→2 displacement) was not included because no place where it is actually used could be found.

The lenis.min.js·splide.min.js builds list helper functions at the top as they are, so the names collide — call Splide first and Lenis later (in reverse order, new Lenis throws ”virtualScroll.on is not a function”). three.cjs is loaded with a window.exports shim.

Fonts: Kozuka Mincho (paid Typekit) is replaced with Noto Serif KR, Reckless Standard XL (paid) with Newsreader, and the logo lettering with Jost. Shippori Mincho is the same free typeface as the original.

title: Desktop that opens after a BIOS boot, with glass object, blackletter title and draggable windows
good_for: Solo developer or designer portfolios that lay out projects, about, awards and tools on a single 'work desk' style first page.

pages.use: A single-screen portfolio — BIOS typing loader (waits for Enter), a glass 3D object in front of a giant blackletter title (drag to rotate · swap object), eight draggable windows on a 20px grid (work list · detail · photos · people mosaic · cipher intro · awards · work strip · tools), a faint live gauge panel, corner cursor with coordinate markers, physics boxes (Space · E). On phones the windows stack in one column.

notes: Only one subpage, /en, was recorded and it is the same screen as the first page (/ → /en), so only one index.html was built.

The 3D models (bust, skull, chess, jellyfish, rose, heart glb) were replaced with our own shapes of the same size (screen height .43) and silhouette ratio (lathe, deformed sphere, knot, extruded heart). Glass uses three r185 MeshPhysicalMaterial (transmission 1, dispersion 3, iridescence .55, thickness instead of drei MeshTransmissionMaterial = Produced with the original thickness/1.8) — no anisotropic blur or time distortion (temporalDistortion .06).

The center title is troika SDF text (Emeritus, paid) in the original, so UnifrakturMaguntia was drawn on a canvas glyph plate. This typeface is wider, so it is squeezed horizontally only to fit within the letter spacing (.72 × size). To keep the blackletter feel, title placeholders are English with the same letter count instead of Korean (WORDMARK 8 letters, HEADLINES 9 letters).

Toolbar icons don’t use the original Lottie file. They load a Lottie we wrote on lottie-web 5.13.0 (60fps · 90 frames, the line draws in and breathes to .82×). The length is the same, the artwork is different.
The sound effects (8 wav files) were replaced with short WebAudio beeps. Off at first, turn on with S or the sound button.

On phone (390) the original could not be captured to the end after Tap (the headless tap went in before the BIOS wait and did not advance). The phone version stacks the windows in a single column with the 3D and physics boxes (first 100) laid behind — the window height of the original 3-column grid is eyeballed.

The spots where the detail and photo windows open when a work is picked (4/4/6/3 · 11/4/12/3) were set by reading only the original code’s opening values (photo clip 1s · .1 gap · .35 delay, closing .45s power2.in). I could not capture the original’s selected state headlessly.

The map and contribution-grid panels of the header chip are an SVG map and a cell-grid placeholder instead of the original data (map tiles·code contributions). The award window expand (5 cells)·about expand (15 lines)·photo expand (3 cells 20 lines) values were measured on the original screen.

title: Tableware brand with slow crossfade hero and pinned landscape window showing seven colors
good_for: Brand sites and online shops for household goods, tableware and materials, with many color variations, material and recycling stories, and a news list.

pages.use: Brand home — a Hero where seven photos cross-fade very slowly, a horizontally dragged lineup, three News rows, a two-column About · Recycling (circulation graphic) row, a wide parallax photo band, a two-column product grid where the next photo fills in on hover, and a color section where a fixed landscape shows through between panels

News list — the whole post (title, date, body, photo) strung together in one narrow column that floats up as it enters the screen, with vertical page numbers on the right. For news collections of brands with many short posts
Product list — filter (stock · price) and sort row, four-column square cutout grid, sold-out tag, pagination below. For the all-products page of shops with many same items in different colors
News post — a wordmark and tag panel on top, below it a left section header and a wide body column (title, date, text, external link). For a single post reached from the News list

notes: Of the four recorded subpages, #3 and #4 are the same news item (listed twice in pages.json as about and detail), so they are built as a single article.html. The product detail (/products/…) was not recorded, so it is not built — the swiper·lottie strings in the original bundle (products.js) belong to that detail page and are not used on home, list or news (no .catsvg).

The original ships smooth-scrollbar.js but never initializes it (no scrollbar-track in the DOM) — the lineup row is just overflow-x horizontal scroll (bar hidden), so the copy leaves it as is. There is no smooth window scroll either.

The recycling loop illustration (a hand-drawn PNG in the original) was redrawn as SVG line art in the same position and size, with a handwriting font (--kf-font-hand: Caveat). The wordmark (a picture logo in the original) uses Lexend Exa lettering fitted to the original widths (220·187·150px).

Link hover follows the original style.css: every a at 768px and up is .8 (.3s), only buttons are 1, and only lineup photos are .5. Product list, page number and filter hover match the original Dawn values (ink rgb(18,18,18) — built from the skin as --site-dawn-ink, 20px underline, arrow 1.07x).
Typeface: Suisse Int'l (paid) → Inter, Japanese body text slot → Noto Sans KR.

title: Recruiting site with opening green letter panels and a box grid
good_for: New-graduate recruiting sites and company hubs with a tabbed first page that mixes job type, people and discussion cards in one grid.

News list — gray board, large gradient English heading, rounded dark bullet and date with title and body rows, carousel of other content. For job notices and announcement collections

Work environment page — mascot hero, big gray panel with a program list, outlined English title and round images, benefits photos in a zigzag, employee speech bubbles. For work policy and benefits pages (fixed to about, since it was captured as works during recording)

Main entry — white panels over a blurred photo wall: hero photo with ENTRY button and deadline, message, recruitment requirements table and selection flow, green event card, collapsible Q&A. For the recruitment requirements page.

A single employee career story: an intro window that pops up on open (with a small spinning globe), a big English title, a person, curved-band text, a route band, image and text sections, and a numbered list on the right. For employee interviews and Work detail (fixed from about to detail, which was mis-detected during recording).

notes: Letter doors: the original hero panel is shaped like the company logo letters (M·B·S·digits). The logo is not carried over — four shapes of our own (V notch · two bumps · S blob · hook) were drawn new, with the same size (267×150), spacing (60), stagger, door handle and door-opening values — part door-tile-wall

Intro: original values exactly (plate .7→10x 5s power3.in, door −90° 3s power1.in after 1s, lime curtain 2s at 3s, one-line text 1s in, 1s hold, 1s out, plate 1s hold then 1s lift). The original seems not to show again after one view, so it was judged to run once per session using sessionStorage

Masonry grid: the original stacks each column separately (wide screen 4 columns of 353 · gap 4), so empty cells appear. On a wide screen the starting column read from the original screen is written (data-col) and the script stacks the heights. Of the original’s sixteen job-profile cards only nine are kept, and the per-tab content (Job·About·Topic·Column) shows the same boxes chosen by data-cat

Art: the original mascot (bear character) and career story illustrations are copyrighted works, so they were redrawn at the same position·size as a gray ball-head, green-body figure and a round mascot face. The diagnosis badge at the bottom right of the hero is a graphic banner, so it is a placeholder

Fonts: the original body font toppan-bunkyu-gothic (paid) is replaced with Noto Sans JP/KR, and roc-grotesk (paid) of View All SEMPAI with Archivo. The English title font Aoboshi One is the same as the original.

Phone panel (375): original is in rem=Zoomed at the same ratio as the window width, but the stone masonry grid is an approximation stacking from the lowest of two columns. Phone menu panel layout is also approximate
Work style page: of the original’s Study, Vacation, Welfare, four facilities and Voice, only three facilities are kept.
News line: built like the original TopNewsWrapper, a roll where on hover the same hidden line above drops down 62px (.6s cubic-bezier(.76,0,.24,1))

Category tabs: in the original measurement, pressing the frame changed the tab background and then the screen scrolled (other element changes were counted as scroll) — after the box is gone, I decided to scroll straight to the grid head (160px from the top)

The line beside the center lime door (original .copy — message text) slides out .5s after the intro ends, over .5s power3.out. The faint reflection strip on the left edge of the original panel (.base-reflect default type) was not ported

title: Investment firm with number-bar loader and section progress sidebar
good_for: Homepages for investment firms, holding companies and research labs that list portfolio companies with metric tables, plus essays and articles.

pages.use: Company home page — a number-bar loader folds into the logo slot, left 1/3 fixed sidebar (3D logo, section progress-line list), declaration hero, repeating Work cases (big title, icon, cover, metrics table, photo and isometric line drawing), a Team row with changing background, Contact form, and a footer logo that rises when you scroll further at the bottom. For investor and portfolio intros
Post collection — sand background, two-line title and icon, post line list where only the hovered line darkens, dot-wave video below with a curtain that lifts. For essay·news lists
A single article — a Back slot and a three-line heading, a narrow text box, a top rule for each section, photo with caption, then a keep-reading list. For essay and press article details

notes: 3D: We don’t use the original GLB (the M monogram, on an external r2 address). We draw our own shapes instead (a square Frame with an empty center plus two blocks, translucent faces plus edge lines) with the same orthographic camera (5,5,5) and the same frame fit (1.8 · 1.35 margin). The sidebar plate makes a half turn on the Hero with scrub 2, and springs when dragged (stiffness 80 · damping 14 · 25°). The Contact window plate is purple translucent with sky-blue edges. It starts at −60° with 2.4s power3.out, then rotates .0045 per frame. The original hero plate uses three r160 and the Contact window plate uses r176, but the API is the same, so one r160 (global THREE) draws both. 3D was not extracted as a part — a task for the next person to continue

Logo: the original Lottie (31 frames) was replaced with our own Lottie (31 frames in which four letters sink down and stand back up). On wide screens the original loader script runs before the Webflow Lottie is registered and can’t find the logo Lottie (below 991 it keeps checking until it finds it), so on desktop the logo doesn’t play — the copy follows that actual behavior (it plays back and forth only at phone width)

The sidebar collapse (the 3D column folds to 0 for the first two screens so the list rises), the team section background change, and the image under the sidebar being revealed in the Contact section are original Webflow interactions (outside the code), so the values could not be read and were built from values measured on screen (scrub · power2.out · 2.4 screens, background .6s ease, clip 1.2s lineEase)

The original case detail modal (.projects-detail-modal — clones a case and pages prev/next) was not built. Cases were cut from three to two, team members from four to two (all section types kept). The phone-width case photo marquee strip (.is-marquee-tracker) was not built because its motion values come from a site-builder interaction

Video: the original webm is on an external CDN (not in the archive), so its length couldn’t be measured. It is replaced by an mp4 placeholder (media/) at the same ratios (wave 1920:300, case 16:9), keeping only the original playback behavior (plays when 5% is on screen, pauses when it leaves, wave autoplays + cover panel 1.2s power2.inOut). The original case video’s ”play button → sound-on main video” switch (initCustomVideo) was not built.

The original’s page-transition blur curtain (.preloader-overlay-fader .4s) doesn’t exist in the original page and never actually runs, so the copy leaves it out too. ?section= Sliding from a sub-section to a first-page area via the URL (scrollToAnchorFromQuery) is not built, and is left as a #section anchor

Font placeholder text: the original is an English site, so every Flecha M (→ Newsreader) heading spot was replaced with English placeholder text — Hero four lines·two case names (Company Name 01 two lines, Company 02 one line — matching the original line count)·team heading three lines (the original has three, so the two-line copy was fixed)·contact heading three lines·contact window heading (shared by three pages)·article collection heading two lines·article heading three lines. Each element notes the text to insert in data-label

Inter (body and label typeface) slots — menu, section list, case row names, tags, metrics, team name lines — were set in Korean: the original is English, but it is not the title typeface, and with Inter followed by the Apple SD Gothic Neo and Noto Sans KR gothic pair, the texture matches, so we judged it fine

title: Vocational school with rounded orange panels overlapping and a center photo zooming to fill the screen
good_for: Homepages for vocational schools, university departments and academies with many courses plus events, news, videos and interviews in an admissions-style site.

pages.use: School home page: an orange hero (a vertical video strip growing in the center · white circle arrow cursor · two large phrases · open campus badge) · a picked-news strip · a photo collection where the center photo grows to fill the screen · rounded-pillar introduction with shortcut cards · principal’s message · number cards · three departments aligned to the left · FIND YOUR DREAM favorite-things chips · an open campus where images float up · an orange group (career support · by visitor type · video strip · news · interviews). For an admissions-style school home

School intro — orange sub-head (flowing outline English) · school guide shortcut panel · INDEX box · three educational philosophy cards · long history rows · two greetings · messages from the school (subheads · three photos). For school or institution intros

School highlights — big photo, five POINT cards on reasons to choose, learning support (counseling and an FAQ accordion), gender ratio bar, commute ranking, residence donut chart, monthly event cards, school info panel below. For feature and school-life About pages
For recruiters — orange band section title · two hiring routes (step numbers) · contact · shortcut band. For an employer hiring guide

News list — category and month picker attached on the left, a list of rows with date band, title and thumbnail, plus View More. For school news and blog lists (category-filtered lists share the same type)
Student works — left category column + three-column works list with department tags + View More. For works and portfolio lists

notes: Lenis showed up in the card libs, but the original html has no lenis class and the bundle has no place that creates Lenis (only the argument a drawer class receives remains), so there is no smooth scroll and the window scrolls natively. Swiper 8.4.7 is also in the bundle, but the first three page slides are the site’s own custom-slider, so the center-grow-strip part reproduces the same lerp(.1), scale and spacing

Fonts: title corporate-logo-ver2 (commercial distribution) → M PLUS 1p 800 (Korean: Gothic A1 800), body ryo-gothic-plusn (paid) → Noto Sans JP (Korean: Noto Sans KR), and English is the same Alexandria as the original.
Subpage 6 (news list filtered by the principal’s message) has the same shape as the news list, so it’s one news.html — the original’s recorded type detail is actually a list.

The phone hero is an approximation with the large copy on top alongside vertical text and the video panel below — the original phone panel details (panel size 1 · gap 0) were matched with the part’s sp values

The Hero color change is included as in the original — each time the video plate turns over, one of five colors (orange, red, green, blue, yellow) different from the current one is picked at random (original vi · html[data-theme-color]), and the background, speech bubble and open campus badge colors change as a pair, after passing 80% of the Hero it returns to orange. Red is a value made from the outfit orange using oklch

Section overlap is built exactly like the original t-sticky-area — under the Department · Find-your-dream panel (z 2, bottom corners 10rem), Open Campus (144.5rem) is stuck to the bottom of the screen (sticky bottom 0), lowered so that only the top 60svh+10rem shows, then rises into place while passing a 150svh blank cell (top bottom → bottom top, scrub), and the white panel at the head of the orange group (Career support · Visitors, z 2 · corners 10rem · padding 10rem) is pulled up 120svh+10rem to cover it. The video section is pulled up over a 250svh blank cell (−250svh) and stays stuck, then rises from 100svh−24rem to 0 from when the blank cell’s head touches the bottom until its center touches. On phones, like the original, Open Campus overlaps 100svh under the panel above, stays stuck at head −6rem and rests for one screen, and the white panel · video section overlap by 6rem each (no scrub)

The three speech bubbles in the principal’s message work like the original: one lights up once the section is in view, then one more every 1.5s (.5 scale · .3s overshoot curve at the offset spot, .1s later, tail .15s after .3s), and when all three are on they turn off together

Built the split-letter hover (original data-hover · js-split) — department names and CTA titles color letter by letter with .4s expo.out from the front (total stagger .1s) in the department color·orange, footer and drawer contact buttons roll three sets of letters (front·back·front) up one character at a time (on enter first set↑ second set↑, on leave second set↑ third set↑), in the visitor row only the hovered row’s letters turn orange (.4s), the rest light gray (.8s), line and arrow .2. Not applied on touch devices, as in the original

Course card class video: media/course.mp4 (square 8s gray placeholder, 7KB) with loop muted playsinline preload as in the original=loaded as metadata, plays when hovered and stops .3s after release (thumbnail uncovers in .5s), at 1024 and below the card plays while it passes between 60% and 50% of the screen

The phone photo collection is, as in the original, two rows (height 12rem · gap 1rem) flowing endlessly in opposite directions over 10s, with the large center photo standing between them. The Hero·video row is dragged to advance below 1024, and the picked News row (original Swiper) at all widths (center-grow-strip swipe·sp-swipe 50 15)

Horizontal overflow (three viewport shapes): the picked News row panel and the SEE … IN THE DATA band extended beyond their sections and overflowed by 60px even at 1440, and on phone the screen shrank by the overflow so the document height came to 4.97 screens. Fixes: overflow hidden on both sections, overflow clip on the student panel graphic, the sub-page three-column grid uses minmax(0, 1fr) with photo cell height auto (the 4:3 cell stretched to height 100% and spread the width to 1663), and the phone footer school name is 2.2rem so it fits on one line. Phone drawer: the tab hung at −6rem outside the scroll panel (overflow auto) and was clipped so it couldn’t be pressed. This is fixed (scrolling is handled by the inner cell), and like the original sp, the tab shape stays the same when open and the cover runs 1s ease. The wireframe tool row (list, annotation) moves up on phone so it doesn’t cover the tab. The footer accordion works like the original acdn-content with .2s ease-out, items in a single column, and a white background circle when open (.5s).

To match the phone page length to the original (13150px), the About shortcut cards are low (photo 16:9 · name one line), and News is one row each with the photo on the left and text on the right, like the original sp

Subpages (three-width comparison): About is filled like the original, with a 40-line history, two greetings (head of school and principal), and three subheadings under “Messages from the school”. Features is filled with a large photo at the top, five POINTs, counseling support, FAQ (three accordions), a donut chart of where students live, a ranking of when they first dreamed, a school pride ranking, eleven months of monthly events, a student works strip, and a school guide panel at the bottom. The step illustrations in the original features (MA intro art · StepUp stairs) and the laptop spec line are bound into photo placeholders and text slots.

notes: The paid English typeface avenir-lt-pro was swapped for Nunito Sans, and Japanese Noto Sans JP for Noto Sans KR of the same family
The logo, map, VI blue panel and floor shape pieces are newly drawn in the same shape language — piece count and layout differ from the original

The menu’s How to use, Article list and Contact pages weren’t recorded, so they weren’t built. How to use links to index.html#h2u, Article to detail.html, and Contact to the contact band in the footer (#contact). The share column position on the article detail differs between the original CSS (.Sidebard flex ratio 68.97%·15.52%) and the recorded screenshot, so we followed values measured from the screenshot (body 54.4vw · share 11.1vw)

The original bundle carries no version strings for Swiper or the swup scroll plugin, so I narrowed each to a version by its feature strings. notes: The original draws with three r184 WebGPU node materials (WebGL only on one older browser version) — the same bend formula (cos · |t|^1.25) was ported to a three@0.184.0 WebGL shader. Instead of the original three-text (3D letters made with a display typeface), the name on the plate is a flat lettering plate, and like the original it inherits the photo plate’s ratio and stretches vertically.

Photos and video are placeholders — the dome · band · about card panels are gray and ink-black placeholders (labeled with what photo it is) drawn on a WebGL canvas, and the video slot loops (autoplay · repeat) with a pale light band passing every 6s and a bar below filling every 4s. The original’s first-frame poster → video swap and preloading of nearby panels were left out as there is no art for them

The photo list (/photo) and booking (/book) pages weren’t recorded, so they were not built. The booking page’s circle-spreading text entrance (BookReveal) is therefore absent too.

Page transition — like the original (a Next single-page app), the document is not reloaded and only the body wrapper is swapped (vt-swap-page, vt: 0), while the clock menu stays outside the wrapper and rotates to the new page item over 1.18s power4.inOut. The new body rises with the original reveal-page-content (.4s ease-out). It loads via fetch, so when opened as a file it usually just follows the link and the menu starts in place

The category filter of the work list assigns categories c0 · c1 · c2 to the placeholders in rotation. The number change on the original detail page (NumberCounter roll) only changes the digits — the roll values could not be read from the recording

Fonts — instead of the original Ceraph Roman · articulat-cf (paid), Cormorant 300 · Albert Sans. For Korean, Noto Serif KR 300 · Noto Sans KR. The logo and tagline are our own drawings at the same spot and size (black blob logo, slanted two-line tagline)

Font placeholders — the slogan, clock menu, categories, filter buttons, work strip names, detail titles, large intro sentences and quotes, where the original used a Latin title font (Ceraph), were swapped for English placeholders. Menu and categories are common words, so the same English words as the original are used, like About · Video · Fashion

Work strip panel names are kept short as First / Last — the part’s text panel is a four-vertex plane, so long ones like Client / Name 01 get buried behind the bent photo panel and the second line disappears (verified with a screenshot)

The category names, enlarged 1.5× in the first-visit intro, touch at neighboring spots behind (MAGAZINE·FASHION) — same words and same position values as the original, so left as is. The thumb is taken at 2.5s after load, so that scene is what gets captured
Header links (mail, social…), prev/next, scroll-down prompt and copyright line are English in the original too, but in this copy they sit in the body font (sans) slot, so Korean is kept

title: Product tour where the camera flies through a single mind map
good_for: Chapter-by-chapter product landings for an app or tool: maker greeting, problem statement, feature cards, hands-on try-out, pricing, questions and promises, plus a content hub and support docs.

pages.use: A single product intro page — a story where the camera flies through a mind map, zooming in on each section · contents card · maker greeting · problem statement · feature cards · try it yourself · pricing · scattered questions · promise. For the landing page of an app or tool
Article hub — hub header, featured article, filterable article library, closing invitation. For product guides and blog lists
Support documents — one document card and home chips. For document pages such as product help and terms

One guide article — colored panel header (path · title · author), sticky table of contents, short-answer box · section text · figures · mid-article call to action · download card · article sample, then further reading and a closing call to action. For product guide · blog post detail

notes: The original static section card (.chapter-content — a map card layout shown only when the script is off) was not built. When the script runs, the original is cinematic at 1100px and up, and sticky vertical reading otherwise (narrow screens · reduced motion), so it never appears on screen.

The app screens inside feature cards, the maker photos and the handwritten note paper are photo placeholders. The original note paper is a cut-out with torn edges, so the photo slot is left rectangular and the torn silhouette is redrawn for each section with clip-path (the shadow is the group’s drop-shadow).

The Try-it panel is a reduced version of the original editor. Node picking, Tab for child, Enter for sibling, Delete, arrow-key movement, text input, drag to move, auto-align, five colors, color picker (the same HSV panel and hue bar as the original react-colorful, drag them or use arrows in 5% steps, saving adds to the palette) and the size bar (12~96, steps of 2) all work. react-colorful is a part that only runs on React, so the same behavior was written by hand. Features beyond the original’s twelve nodes and three levels (undo·attachments) are not in the original panel either
Judgment: the original Get app button (app store link) was changed to a button that jumps to our pricing section (#pricing). Footer and document links connect to our list.html and page.html.

The original subpages (guide hub, guide article, support) are static documents with no motion, so GSAP is not loaded. The original has no page-transition effect either, so navigation is ordinary. ScrollSmoother, written on the card, is only a name reference inside the ScrollTrigger code in the original bundle and is not built (no smooth-wrapper, no create), so it is not used. matter-js ships at 0.20.0, the same as the original.

Korean characters are about twice as wide as Latin ones, so headings had their character counts reduced to match the original line counts. As a result the document height is slightly shorter (1440 first page 51295 vs 52379, Support 1426 vs 1638). The guide hub and guide articles had their Korean character counts increased per block to match the original line counts, matching 1440 hub 10899 vs 10836 and article 7105 vs 7102. Section names (contents and map pills) were written to the text width of the original names — when the pill is enlarged to fit the screen width, the aspect ratio must match so that the pill clip (inset, rounded radius) at the end of the zoom ends up at the same height as the original.
Instead of the original logo mark, a new mark was drawn with four branches spreading from a center square (mark in shared.js).

The figure in the guide article (article.html) (app editor capture) is a photo placeholder. The original’s figure·「View larger」 link opens the image file, so it links to the placeholder’s own spot (#guide-shot), the download buttons (.mindmap·.txt) have no file to download so they go to the download slot·sample slot, and the app store link in the mid-page prompt goes to the pricing section (#pricing).

The guides hub keeps the original’s article-row count per topic (5, 21, 9, 4, 5, 9, total 53). The featured article, article rows and continue-reading links all go to article.html — the original articles share one shape, so the detail is a single page. The background, closing call to action, color panels and dark mode shared by the hub and the article live in one guides.css, as in the original.

title: Architecture office repainting the background color per page, with color-framed work cards and number loader

For an office home page where the work is the star

About the company — big promise sentence on orange background, group photo, representative quote, staggered team grid with blank cells (name accordion), numbered values accordion. For small companies with many team members

notes: The original was built in Webflow (IX2 interactions · Webflow slider · Finsweet · Product filter), so it has no matching open-source library — motion durations, delays and curves were read from the IX2 data (events · actionLists) and ported to GSAP (outQuad=power1.out, outQuart=power3.out, ease=cubic-bezier(.25,.1,.25,1), loader curve .327,.007,.327,.96 is a CustomEase). The filters (work category dropdown, News category) copy only the look and open/close motion of the original filter plugin (dropdown-OPEN/CLOSE: arrow 180° .6s, list scaleY .4s), and filtering just hides items by text category — no original server-side filtering or count display

title: Night-island 3D portfolio where you walk a character through portals
good_for: Developer or creator portfolios presented like a game, with signposts for contact links and stepping-stone portals that switch the project shown on a single-screen 3D world.

pages.use: Walking night-island portfolio — water-drop door entrance · 3D world where you drive a character to find signposts (links) and pads (work portals) · sound · joystick · link notices. For a developer or creator game-style single-screen intro

notes: The original is a single page (pages: [] in pages.json), so there are no subpages.

The island does not use the original glb (island · lantern · character · fish · spiral) and is rebuilt from primitive shapes. Same: camera (fov 40 · tilt -π/8 · offset -3.5/17.4/29.6→0/4/5.5 (phone 7.5) 5s power3.out · follow 1-exp(-5dt) · mouse x ±.5), walking (speed 4, Shift 6, jump 6.548, gravity -29.43, turn 15), the three link sign positions (-4.45/-8.55 etc.), hammer 2 seconds (shrink 4 seconds), sound within distance 17 as min(1/distance,.2), pad light 0→3.56 .2s, portal screen .3s power2.out, sleeping creature Z (5s · .88 · .05→.15). Different: layout and sizes are approximations fitted by eye from captures, houses · trees · well · crystals · forge are simple blocks, and the character is a box-and-cone doll, so it lacks the feel of the original stock Idle · Sprint · JumpRunning animations. The original island glb is compressed with draco · ktx2, so measuring node coordinates needs draco decoding. Next person’s task: decode it, measure node positions and sizes, and fix the layout.

The cloud color inside the droplet (#bbd4fc) is painted as linear 0.116/0.644/4.54, found by inverting ACES. The scene of dropping down through the clouds on entry uses 34 sprite clouds plus sky-blue fog that thickens as the camera-to-character distance goes from 10 to 30. Right after the click in headless interact, the original frame looks farther away and hazier. I judged this a timing lag caused by the original rendering slowly in headless (comparing frames at 0.3·0.7·1·1.5·4s after entry shows the same flow). Only this cloud color is a constant from inverting ACES, so it stays the same when the Skin changes (every other island color is read with MF.color from the relative --site-* colors in shared.css).
The original loader shows the progress of downloading models and textures. With no files to load, it counts 0→100 over 1.2s power1.out while fonts load and the scene is built.

Judgment call: opening index.html?enter for thumbnails and previews skips the door and starts inside the island (not in the original). tools/compare and interact only capture the door screen and the moment right after the click, so the inside of the island was checked against the original separately by walking a key-input path (stairs → link sign Enter → high stairs → platform → portal Enter).

Font backfill: spots that were Latin in the original (Metamorphous) — entrance button Enter · control sign Move · link signs Link 1~3 · project names Project Name 01~03 (shown on the portal note) — were changed to English placeholder text. The original island sign text is baked into textures so the words couldn’t be read — it was treated as Latin since it’s an English site, and the control sign is a single word above arrow keycaps so it is kept as Move.

Kept in Korean: the tab title ‹Your name here› (a document title that fonts don’t catch — latin-slots handles it with the html title font rule) · motion explainer notes (wf-note, explanations for builders) · portal note sentences (‹— Put the address here›, ‹First step on the footing …›, guidance sentences not in the original, so they stay Korean — rendered in a Song-style typeface) · portal photo slot descriptions (--wf-mono).

Sound plays through howler 2.2.4 like the original. Volume (wind .09 · run .4 · step .09 · portal .7 · hammer .5), loop, rate (run 1.1), distance rules (hammer: within 17 min(1/distance,.2), portal: within 13 min(2/distance,.8)) and trigger timing (on entering, run while moving on the ground) are the original values. The sound files (media/) are our own synthesized sounds newly made to the original lengths (wind 176.07s · run 1.25s · hammer 1.30s · step .51s · portal 13.44s). There is no skill island, so no glyph sound. Because three.cjs masks the global AudioContext·Audio names, the howler context is set up directly as window.AudioContext and the HTML5 audio pool is turned off. When opened via file:// the sound files cannot be fetched, so it runs silent (served over http it plays)

The island’s colors (52 in all: grass, rock, trees, roofs, lanterns, characters and more) are set in shared.css as oklch relative colors (--site-*) built from --kf-*, and index.js reads the computed values through MF.color to paint them. The original values come out unchanged in the current skin, and when the skin changes the island colors turn with it

The header cell width (914.3 at 1440×900) could not be fully derived from the original geometry, so it is approximated as content height × 1.3705 — if the window ratio differs a lot it may be off by tens of px. The phone scale was measured at 12.02px at the original 390 and fitted as (width+3)/425.

Video: the original video is not used. An 8s gray placeholder made with ffmpeg (media/clip.mp4, 640×400) is laid over cells in the original ratio (1730·1728·1634 ÷ 1080) with cover. First 3 works, the rest are placeholder entries. The fullscreen button is shape only.

title: Winery set where smoke flips black-and-white pages to reveal color
good_for: Brand introductions and product lists for wineries, distilleries, premium food and drink makers or workshops that show land, hands and time through photos and short verse.

pages.use: Winery home page — vine-stem hero · dot-cloud flight · scattered uppercase title · smoke-driven boundary that flips black and white · cropped-frame photo · floating grapes · three people · next page. For winery, brewery, or workshop brand homes

Product list — bottle photo hero, smoke boundary, three lines of text, name list (on hover the bottle photo follows, on press a description window opens over the smoke), next page. For wine and premium food and drink lineups

notes: The second entry in pages.json (/en) has the same form as the home page, so it was not built separately. The menu’s third item (original Sensibiliser & Contribuer) was not recorded, so it is left as #.

Point cloud flight: the original picks from 312 pre-rendered 16:9 frames (1920×1080 webp) by scroll and cover-fits them via an ogl shader (brightness = opacity, flow-map decay .8 · strength .3 · radius .4 with ×.05 ripple) is loaded here. The shader, cover formula, flow map and 312-frame picking use the same values, and since the original frames cannot be used, the frames are redrawn as dots on a 16:9 frame (1600×900), following the original flow (frame 0 black → frame 30 a few bold stars → up to frame 150 sparse stars → dense dust from frame 190 → frame 220 a close look at grape rows → pulling back to gather two walled vineyard terraces · a field on the left · dot-covered ground, and at frame 280 a road with two wheel tracks) and the last-frame layout (positions read from the grid). The position of each dot differs from the original render (image).

Hero stem: the original lights the branchv6.glb model (with material textures) using ogl. With the same camera (fov 45 · (0,0,1) · intro 3s · scroll z+.1 · y-.2), same lights (directional (0,1,1), a point light following the mouse with lerp .1, intensity 50 · size .1) and same rotation (lerp .05, y -.05 · x -.02), we built our own stem in the model’s place: a curved tube carved with vertical ribs and bumps. The original material textures (color · roughness maps) are inside the model so they were not used, and roughness .62 · metal .35 · darker ribs are values tuned by looking at the original screen.

Smoke: re-implemented in ogl with the same formulas as the original c-shader and c-hover-shader values (7-layer fbm · amplitude .5 · gain .45 · domain warp · smoothstep .1 · progress 1~2 erases from the bottom · opacity noise bleed · overexposure above 1 · flow map .99/.3 · scroll time ×.01/s, hover ×.05/s · long side 1800 · pixel ratio ≤1). The noise function is our own simplex, so the pattern differs (the original also uses a random seed each time it opens). The original flow map keeps stamping the last velocity even when the mouse stops — left as is.

Version check (2026-11-16): ogl is 1.0.11 because the original bundle (Vec2, Branch, etc.) contains code that only exists from 1.0.11 (setDracoManager, isDraco, EXT_texture_webp, KHR_draco_mesh_compression), compared against the original src of npm 1.0.0~1.0.11. swiper has no version string and only the core is bundled. The core has loopedSlidesLimit and changeLanguageDirection (since 8.3.0) and dom7 style ($.attr, removeAttr, removed from 9.0), so it is 8.3.0~8.4.7. Core code is identical across this range (only the a11y and cards modules differ between versions, and the original has neither), so it can’t be narrowed further and the last one, 8.4.7, is used.

SangBleu Sunrise and Sackers Gothic are paid fonts, so they were replaced with Tenor Sans, Hahmlet and Syncopate. Korean placeholders come out in Hahmlet and the system sans, so the thin, wide feel of the original is weaker. For letter headings, Latin placeholders TITLE01, HEADLINE0 and SECTION0 were used to keep the wide letter rhythm.

The wine list has 12 rows, like the original. The detail window is three swipers like the original (vertical loop swipe, speed 1000, parallax photo -30%/opacity .1, text card 50%/.4, year description speed 600, year number 4 slots speed 300), and the bottle photo changes every year over 1s. Text that differs per year is filled in by whoever pulls it out (the placeholder uses the same text).

The original’s isMobile is decided by device (phone/tablet UA, touch-capable Mac), not by width. In that case titles aren’t split but fade in whole over .6s via is-inview (repeating items turn off on exit). Hover shaders, list bottle-photo follow, mouse flow, detail window parallax and the menu’s delayed letter shuffle are turned off. The contrast filter, hard-light cover and white cover (tagline white) are removed, desktop-only parallax (progress-context desktop) is turned off, and the next page gets an 85px bottom margin. The copy uses the same criterion (html.is-mobile) — a narrowed desktop window stays desktop, like the original

index body paragraphs (mw-p-300, two or three paragraphs in the cropped frame photo section and the grape section) — the original is French body copy also set in the heading font Light, but per the README body text uses Korean placeholder copy. The paired Hahmlet 300 (thin serif) is loaded, so Korean is kept

Font backfill decision: Latin placeholders were used only in title font (Tenor Sans) slots — Hero·menu·next page titles (Headline·Collection·Third Page & Subtitle), three scattered uppercase titles, three person names, 12 wine name lines and the detail window name. Small uppercase labels·verses·menu buttons·submenus are body font (Syncopate) slots, so they are treated as outside the latin-slots scope and left in Korean

title: Full-screen WebGL canvas that redraws a new scene with every scroll
good_for: Brand sites for music projects, artists, games and anime that present a world scene by scene and link to ID-card-style character detail pages.

pages.use: Worldview first page: logo-cell loader → video hero with a giant wordmark → a red orb in a pink and orange sky with curved flowing text → giant CREATING THE DAMN NEW WORLD lettering → a red-glowing panel grid with character cells (pop out on hover and lead to detail) → a dot-letter wall with a rotating polyhedron → pill → color band → a large statement flowing sideways → a twisted-letter band footer. For artist and worldview brands.
Character card — torn-paper portrait panel on a reddish background, name tag, intro, color swatch chips, big number, likes, next character (?c=0·1·2). Three originals (Name·Name·Name) merged into one

notes: The original’s DOM is nearly empty, and eleven scene modules (Top3·Ph6·NewWorld2·NewTownText·LogoOverlay·Grid9·TextWallEN9·DreamPill4·TextHorizontal3·JoinUs3·Menu2) draw on a single canvas. Here, things that DOM can do, such as video, text and color bands, are sticky sections, while the red ball, grid, dot text wall, pill and twisted ribbon are split off into the same canvas (three r162, pixel ratio ×.5). Sticky panels create a stacking context, so a background panel (z 1, below the canvas) and a text panel (z 6, above the canvas) are layered together.

The original 3D models (red ball sphere4.glb with PBR texture, curved text plane mp_warp.glb, angel angel_export3.glb, pill mp_dreampill_sep.glb, text wall mp_textwall2.glb) are not used and were rebuilt with our own spheres, cylinder segments, polyhedra and capsules (cylinder + hemisphere). The environment map (px~nz), grid post-processing (GridShader4) and menu curtain shader were reduced to plain lighting, a scanline pulse curtain and a CSS noise gradient respectively. The red ball section’s afterimage distortion post-processing (DistortionPh — strength +.1 per scroll event, ×.9 per frame) is not there yet.
Grid cell hover (z .3 · 1.4x), 3-second pulse (5 → ×.96), tilt .1·sin(.1t), angel rotation (x .005 · y .002) and ball rotation (.001) are the original values.

Section heights (first 4 · red ball 3 · NEW WORLD 3 · grid 6 · text wall 3 · dark 1 · pill 5 · color band 3 · horizontal text 3 · bottom 2 screens — total 33 screens, a bit longer than the original 27900px) and the in-section progress motion (NEW WORLD word speed .6~1.5 · horizontal text flow · pill rotation · grid approach .35~.75) are values matched by screen capture (how: guess).

Videos (hero tenshi.mp4 · city town_bg.mp4) of the same position and size as the <video autoplay loop muted> Left as a placeholder with a gradient and SVG city skyline laid as the background — the original video file is not included.

The three character detail pages (akeloo, aisa, nora) share one shape, so a single detail.html with ?c=0, 1 and 2 change only the name, number and portrait color. The original 3D character model is reduced to a portrait plane with a torn-paper-edge shader. The original loads OrbitControls but comments out the line that creates it, so the character does not react to the cursor or dragging — the earlier plane’s mouse tilt (6% steps) and drag rotation (inertia .92) were not in the original and were removed.

The original loader lifts the black curtain over the logo image slots in steps, one per loaded item (9 slots). Placeholders load fast, so that tempo (from 3.3s, one slot every .2s, the front slot larger) is set as HOLD·RUN in shared.js (changed per page via body data-loader-hold·run·out. Details appear within 1 second like the original). Even after the lift finishes, if the scene material (mpLoader.step, 9 slots) isn’t full, it waits up to 2 seconds.

Fonts: body ltc goudy oldstyle → Sorts Mill Goudy, dnp shuei 4gob → Noto Sans KR 900, wide wordmark → Archivo width 125, narrow giant title → Anton, input mono → IBM Plex Mono (the originals are all paid fonts from a commercial font service).

Menu items use Archivo wide letters instead of the original’s lettering images. The motion uses the original values as they are: items stand up from rotateX(1080°) and transparent with opacity .5s ease-in-out and transform .5s cubic-bezier(.01,.44,.15,.82), one after another at .1s+.05s. The first item (LIVE) scales 1.5 times and goes .5 transparent on hover. Pressing the vertical strip on the right raises a 500px news drawer with translateX(100%→0) .18s ease-in-out, and the strip follows with .2s ease-in-out. The original menu overlay shader (menu_overlay_shader) is reduced to a CSS noise gradient.

notes: The Hero was rebuilt like the original: five picture boards on a three r182 orthographic camera (screen px units). The current board is in front at z 10, the others behind at z 0 and blurred, with a white board with 50px corners at z 5 between them (delayed .55s after the first flip’s .5s, it goes to .6 over .5s). It flips every 5 seconds, the current board with elastic.inOut(.4,1.8) 1.6s (1.28s for the first flip), the others with power3.inOut 1.5s (1.2s), and at the start they spread out from size 0 at the center, making one turn, over 1.6s. The board shader is our own (wave strength .03·frequency 2.5·two turns + blur on flip). Differences from the original: the original stacks four picture layers per School (body plus three parts) and filters blur through two render targets (horizontal and vertical Gaussian), while ours uses one circular blur pass per board. The original’s position data (start, flip, ring, message, map states) could not be read from the bundle, so the flip layout (big board in the center plus four corners), ring (r 190) and scatter (r 430) were set by watching the recording. The original’s first board is random, but we fixed it to the first School so the two can be compared. Without WebGL it follows the same path with DOM images

The original character illustrations (by a professional illustrator) are not used. Simple person-shaped SVGs were drawn in the five school colors (figure in shared.js). The Hero bakes this SVG into a canvas texture (clothing variables are resolved to computed colors at that point). Replace with real illustrations in actual use.

The initial shape of the navy band curve could not be traced to the original path, so it was redrawn with the same node structure as the maximum shape (original values). The swell connects with the same MorphSVG as the original, with share speed/25 (curve under the photo /30) and lerp .1 — the same motion was also extracted as the _fx/speed-swell-edge motion part
The timeline is dragged with Draggable + InertiaPlugin and glides with inertia — the scroll-linked behavior of the original SectionHistory script (19KB, site-specific) is not carried over.

Staff notes swap by overlapping in the same slot, one page at a time, like the original (exit .4s ease-1 · after .2s it settles down 3% and scales .98x, enter after .1s with .5s ease-1 · .6s ease-3). title: Album experience on a 3D evidence board lit by a flashlight
good_for: Public experience pages for albums, films and games, mystery-themed campaigns, and drag-to-explore moodboard archives.

pages.use: A single-page experience — after a percent loader, adult warning consent and sound selection, you drag around a wooden evidence board (three.js) joined by red string while lighting it with a flashlight, pressing a paper zooms in and turns on a description in the right column, and pressing the torn sketch in the center starts a matching game. For immersive landings that release music or works

notes: No sound — the original’s sound effects (paper hover, click, drag wind, flicker), 1-minute track previews and background audio files are original assets, so they are not used. The sound on/off button only toggles its status text. Next person’s to-do: make our own sound effects and hook them to the same spots (hoverIn, interact, drag every 0.35 distance, flicker).

The 3D models use our basic shapes instead of the original glb files — board (plane 16.9×18.8), paper (plane, glb placement values kept as they are), string (9 tube strands between 6 pins), and pins (sphere + cylinder). The original’s string fuzz (alpha strands), knots, paper normal map, wood normal/roughness maps, environment light (env_studio PMREM) and LUT color grading (lut_zed) are not included — lighting uses a hemisphere light plus a spotlight, with intensity tuned to the screen brightness.

Post-processing is not the original (postprocessing library, Zlib) but a single shader of our own. Darkness (.7/focus .99), flashlight mask plate, glow plate, pincushion distortion .05, chromatic aberration .007 (tint .825), exposure 1.075, contrast, saturation, lift, vignette .4/1/.9, grain .125 and dust 30fps were rewritten with the same formulas. The original grain and dust textures and the flashlight pattern image were redrawn on canvas

The original repeating icon videos (loader proof, drag hint, game hint cursor) are replaced by a boiling line that alternates three hand-drawn SVG frames every .125s plus CSS hand movement. The video curtain is a placeholder screen with only a 3:30 time bar running (the original is a hosted video).

The actual screen of the original evidence window couldn’t be captured headless (after dragging, the spot I pressed was an empty panel). The window layout was built from the original code and CSS values (lg 4 columns·14-column offset, title 3rem, description 6.25rem offset, divider 6.5rem/2.5rem, record row 9.75rem name column, letter stagger .025)
Even after the window closes, the camera stays on that paper — like the original unfocusPOI, only z and side push are restored (pressing the center again opens the same paper)

Heading font slots (two loader warning screens, seventeen evidence h2s, hidden headings, three pair names, pair success, board all solved, three canvas paper texts) were replaced with English placeholder text — the original is entirely an English site (Founders Grotesk), so no heading slot stays in Korean. The original text on the canvas papers (wanted flyer, record sheet, recruitment poster) is a glb texture and could not be read, so it was judged only from the site being English.

With the loader warning title at the original 22·21 characters, Schibsted Grotesk is wider than Founders Grotesk and wrapped to three lines at 1440. Cut to 18·17 characters so it matches the original: two lines at 1440, three at 390.

Space before commas and periods looks wide (NOTICE ,) — presumed because font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums carried over from the original CSS makes punctuation fixed-width in the substitute font Schibsted Grotesk (original Founders sits tight, not confirmed). This also existed with the Korean placeholder text, and this backfill only changes text, so it was left as is — to fix it, tabular-nums on the percent line (data-part=Applied only to percent)

Section images (library-shots): the evidence window, game and video curtain are fixed curtains behind the loader, so only the dark background was captured, and evidence-list is a 1px list for reading tools so it cannot be captured — left as is due to tool limits.

title: 3D scroll story flying from Earth into a room of a sail-shaped seaside building
good_for: Long scroll stories that follow a building, place or product from outside to inside in 3D, such as tourism, architecture, museum exhibits or product teardowns, with card text, 3D pins, dimension lines and two visual styles.

pages.use: Story first page (left→right): photo hero → foreword → three Earth sections (center card) → sections about buildings on the sea (left card · pin · handwritten dimensions · see-through foundation · night sail) → lobby · aquarium restaurant · suite (walking) → six-number closing → moments horizontal swipe → map card → credits → review → bottom. For scroll stories introducing places and buildings.

Right-to-left version of the same story (where the original Arabic version sits) — cards on the right, rail, switcher and gauge in mirrored positions, 3D screen push also in the opposite direction. For Arabic and Hebrew versions or when right alignment is needed

notes: 3D: instead of the building, lobby, aquarium restaurant and suite models the original codes by hand (brandAlArab.js·atrium.js·royal-suite.js etc.), these were built fresh from our basic shapes. The sail building is two V-shaped wings (window-stripe texture) + a billowed sail panel + mast + white arch tubes·trusses + a round top disc·viewing block. The island is a droplet-shaped slab·lawn·breakwater blocks·palms, and the sea is our shader (shallow→deep·waves·night). The lobby is a wedge-pattern cylinder + diamond floor + gold spindle columns + fountain, the restaurant is a navy cylindrical room + round tank + circling fish, and the suite is a red-striped room + star-pattern carpet + round bed·canopy·door·stairs. It is not as detailed as the original models (escalators, aquarium walls, the web page on the TV, helicopter, wild animals and coastal city were left out).

Camera blending (holds 25% at start and end · smoothstep), approach, walk and turn types, the dark curtain between spaces (1−|e−.5|×4 · approaches over the first 55% · recedes over the last 35%), camera follow 1−e^(−3.2·dt), the left card section’s screen push min(260, width×.2), the phone’s lower 20% and the center section’s upper 12% are original values. Hero video as in the original <video autoplay loop muted playsinline>It plays with (object-fit cover). The original’s video embed has to carry that channel’s video, so it is a placeholder <video controls>(media/full-1·2.mp4), and the YouTube onStateChange hook (stops while playing, spins again when stopped) does the same job with the video’s play, pause and ended events.

Wordmark (original rainbow-outline PNG) is Comfortaa 300 outline lettering 'wordmark' + redrawn as a mirror image. Placeholder words must have no descending strokes, as in the original, so the mirror image doesn’t overlap (g, p, y make it messy). The small header-row logo is the same type.

Differences: sphere positions are evenly spread points on a sphere instead of icosahedron vertices, size noise is 3D (tempo on the time axis) instead of 4D, and the 15 pattern pieces are shapes newly drawn on canvas, so they differ in feel from the original images (webp pieces)

notes: The hero ring lines do not use the original shader — we wrote our own. The camera, shape and noise values of the six scenes, plus the ring count, flow, scene cycle, cursor swirl and particle roughness values, were measured from the original settings and carried over. The original EffectComposer pass set (warp · distort · grain) is merged into one render target and one shader, and because the noise function differs, the ring wobble has the same feel but is not the same curve. The warp strength is only matched proportionally at .08x since the original formula is unknown.

The rounded outline of the service cycle graphic is produced in the original by clipper (BSL, outside the allowed list) — rebuilt the same closed shape with a 4-unit grid distance transform + contour lines (corners may look slightly jagged at grid units).

The handwritten logo (hero·footer) does not use the original logo — a handwriting font (--kf-font-hand, Caveat Brush) ”logo” text is placed in the same spot at the same width — replace with the brand logo SVG.

The doodle blobs, strata panels, paper planes and thumb character art don’t use the original PNGs — they’re redrawn as line-art SVGs at the same spots and sizes (same seed, so the same shapes every time).

The menu’s Culture, Company and Contact pages were not recorded, so they link to about.html#member, #philosophy and the footer (#contact). The original’s contact form (tabs, input fields) was not built.

The original site moves with CSS transitions and Alpine, without GSAP or smooth scroll — the copy is also built without libraries, using the same transition values (.15s opacity .5 · .2s dot retreat · .3s white surface).
Besides the service branch address pages, the original’s Contact page (tabs, input form), Culture and Company pages were not recorded, so they were not built.
