good_for: A mixer, night event or small festival page driven by one mood, with past event records and organizer intro on one page.

pages.use: Event one-pager — a light-cone stage under a lamp (people figures blur as they approach), brush title and intro, a boundary that darkens like grain, rows of past editions (year, intro, poster, record link), organizer, and a scene where the lights go out at the end. For a mixer or night event intro

notes: The original is a single page (pages is [] in pages.json), so there are no subpages. The archived DOM still holds hidden sections that were only visible during the event period (info, guests, schedule, sponsors, teaser video, sign-up button). They are not visible now, so they were not built. If a pre-event version is needed, add them in the form of the edition-log row and the organizer row.

The original motion is STUDIO’s CSS scroll timeline (animation-timeline: view(), cover range · 35% keyframe). The same formula is moved into parts (zoom-blur-fade-scrub · cone-shut-scrub) that paint directly from the scroll value — GSAP and Lenis are not used (the original has none either).

The original title is brush-lettering artwork, so a Korean placeholder is set in Gasoek One with a rough-edge SVG filter, and the section names (Archive · Organizer) are worn letterpress serif artwork, so IM Fell English with a 0.5px stroke added. Box sizes (148×32 · phone 135×29) match the original artwork.
The five English translation lines of About are English slots in the original too, so they are left as English placeholders (judgment).
The bottom-left platform badge that the site builder attaches is a platform mark, so it was not included.

title: Red sun covered by text, then a golden city fills the screen
good_for: A regional specialty, seafood or farm product brand, municipal promotion site or food brand listing stockists.

pages.use: Brand home: a fixed vertical slogan, a sentence covering a red sun with a three-layer golden city scrub, a scattered photo flow, four fish pinned left over four-color bars, a bead-string seasonal calendar, a harbor map, a stockist guide, News and a banner. For the home page of a regional specialty brand.

Brand About — circular-photo hero with three key points, three numbered sections (photo, yellow sea chart), four fish-type detail blocks (color bar, large illustration, sentence heading), expandable FAQ, dark special-offer band. For product and origin intro pages.

Stocking shops list. Vertical brush-calligraphy header, restaurant and fish shop tabs, rows with photo, name, badge, recommended menu, address, parking, hours and phone, pagination. For retailer and member store guides
News list — circled single-letter vertical head with date and title lines. For short notice lists
Single news item — left vertical-line header (date · title), indented body, back to list. For a single notice post

notes: The original’s brush-calligraphy title, logo, sentence (kanji brush strokes), tuna photo, city illustration, harbor map, calendar and yellow nautical chart are all image files (rule: original images are not used), so they were redrawn as SVG in the same place, size and color — the sentence is an abstract mark of four-color brush strokes on a navy ring, the city is a procedural drawing of box houses scattered over golden hills, and the tuna is a simplified side profile, so details differ from the original images
The vertical brush-lettering title (an image in the original) is replaced with Noto Serif KR 900 vertical text

Store tabs filter within a single page instead of going to other pages as in the original. Store detail, special product and port intro pages weren’t recorded in the archive, so they were not built, and Swiper (.swiper-shop), which the original applies on phones only to those pages, isn’t used either.

Like the original .p-intro, the first-visit loader curtain covers the screen until the loader finishes and blocks taps — so tapping during the loader does not open the menu, same as the original (in original timing tests 06:58 opened and 10:28 was blocked, varying by timing).

title: Illustrated park pops out and transforms into an ancient palace
good_for: A park, shopping complex or tourist spot guide, an illustrated local brand, or a history story told as a scroll.

pages.use: First page — park illustration hero with pop-out pieces and a large handwritten title, news slider, floor map plus shop cards, access, park guide cards, numbered-pin neighborhood map and person cards, contact, and a history scroll teaser behind the footer. For local shopping district or park home pages.

History intro — a long scroll where, over a fixed background with modern park imagery removed and an old palace hall and court figures popping out, photo and text cards flow alternately left and right. For introducing a place’s origins and timeline
News list — big centered title, three-column poster thumbnail grid, page numbers. For event and notice lists

Store list — a floor map on the left that follows as you scroll (the store cell passing by lights up), and per building a row with photo + intro + business hours. For tenant stores in a mall and restaurant guides.
News detail — title, date, one poster, body, back-to-list button. For event notice detail

notes: The original art is a raster hand-drawn sprite (stipple texture) — the same composition (red and blue roads converging in perspective, a shop wing·parking lot on the left, a glass building on the right, a distant castle) was redrawn with SVG shapes, then the big pictures (Hero·boundary·shop·elsewhere·neighborhood map·history) were baked as piece sprites onto the same pixi 8.7.3 canvas as the original. The texture is imitated with a noise filter and has no hand-drawn feel.

The person gestures in the original are skeleton animation from a third-party animation tool. Its runtime requires the editor’s license (not MIT or BSD), so it was not used. Leg sprite swinging (±14°, .32s) and moving left and right stand in for it. Gesture kinds like running, sitting and walking a dog are left for the next person to draw.

Piece entrance uses the original bundle values as they are — per group x mm(10,30)·y um(80,100), per piece x·y mm(5,10)·rotation mm(.3π,.5π)+mm(.01π,.02π) with 2.25s elastic.out(4, 0.75)·power4.out·elastic.out(1, 1), opacity 0.9s expo.out, gap 0.015s. Like the original’s random numbers, mm flips the sign of the start value with 50-50 odds (so pieces also pop in from the left with the opposite tilt). History pieces use the original nF (.75s back.out(8)·y um(10,15)·x mm(3,8)·.06s gap, exit .25s sine.in 20 upward·.025s gap), clouds use aF (3s expo.out·outside 60, exit .5s sine.in), and the five drawer drawing chunks use Wm (y um(30,40)·x mm(13,18)·.05s gap)

In the original the hero switches to a night scene from 7pm to 5am (Dm). The night art is a separate sprite set and layout values from the day version, so it would need redrawing and was not built. The next person can draw one night set and swap it in under the same time condition
The history scroller cut the original 20 cells down to 6 on the history page and 2 on the first page. The modern-to-old switch points (180px and 480px of header cell) are values measured on screen

As in the original, hovering a store makes the person at that store’s spot (13 spots at the original map % positions) pop out with .6s back.out(8) (y um(10,15)·x mm(3,8)·tilt mm(.025π,.05π), opacity .24s expo.out) and fade on release with .25s cubic.out, while the cell turns green and the number turns white in .3s (overlap handling while popping·fading is also as in the original). The floor map image itself does not pop, as in the original.

Interaction responses were rebuilt with the original code values — pill button (hA: the dot bounces twice at half the distance in height up to the third letter, letters squash and stretch, the person steps up in .22s back.out(2), text pushed 10px), menu button (fA: three lines gather into the bottom line bending 6→−2→0, person steps up tilted ±20°, when opened ±30° X, pressing mid-spin finishes at 2x and continues), header·drawer·footer menu letters (dA: sin(16t + index×.35π) height 3px .075s→0 .4s — in the original 5px only on the Japanese screen), slider arrows (c-arrowButton keyframes), TOP button (the person always stands on top, hover 4px). The original person is a sprite image with cycling walking frames (background-position), so the copy’s SVG person stands without frames

Not built: the original’s first-visit machine-translation notice modal (shown when the browser isn’t Japanese and the address has no visited), the AR banner link, the map expand modal, and the interview detail page (interview detail wasn’t recorded). The language button on the history side flips its arrow and opens the list like the original, but it does no translation
Page transitions don’t exist separately because the original uses regular WordPress navigation — as in the original, the body turns on immediately once ready, without a transition (body.is-setuped)
The handwritten font of the hero title is original-only lettering, so rounded Jua with a thin outline added stands in. Logo · footer big text are placeholders (LOGO·garden)

Colors inside the illustrations (sky · road · roof · clothes, 126 colors) are content of the picture like photos, so they are gathered in one place in the shared.js palette as not Skin — the background, accent, logo lime, sky, grass and footer panel that overlap with Skin use --site-* built from --kf-accent·--kf-bg
In pages.json, a news item set as detail is made an article, and the shop list is made a product

Font backfill call: the archived copy is a machine-translated English version (html data-lang=en). The index access facility name is Lexend Latin (Brand) in the archived copy and Noto Sans JP kana in the Japanese version — the picker uses the archived screen and the header logo is also a Latin wordmark, so it was changed to English (Place Name)

Font backfill decision: the article ”BACK” button is a spot that does not exist in the original news detail, but the original button (c-button) uses Lexend Exa Latin (OK·MORE) regardless of language, so it was switched to English

Header menu, one-line intro, drawer and footer menu — the archived (English) version uses Lexend Latin but the Japanese version uses Noto Sans JP Japanese, and the copy also sits in the body font slot (Lexend then Noto Sans KR), so Korean is kept

title: Orange panels with circular photo bursts and giant translucent lettering
good_for: A film festival, festival or exhibition site combining dates, programs, news, access and sponsors on one board.

pages.use: Festival first page — large photo that changes by spreading as a circle from a dot on the right, translucent giant English text and date, theme text, news (large text + slider), three offset link cards, directions, two online cards, sponsor list
News list — gray panel under an orange head, left branch list and photo + white text rows, circle page numbers. For event and organization notice lists
Program list — orange panel with a three-row grid of photo cards, each with a category color dot at the photo corner, English category, title and description. For screening/performance/course lists
Donation info page — white sheet on the original site (orange-banded path, 800px text column, key program box, step-by-step screenshots, contact). For donation, membership and volunteer guide pages

notes: The original English heading typeface Transport is paid, so it was swapped for the free Overpass, which has a similar road-sign feel. Noto Sans JP has no Hangul, so Noto Sans KR covers it.

The big translucent English in the hero (original art lettering mv-title.svg), the theme logo for Treasure Hunt, the film festival emblem and the date lettering were redrawn with HTML text and our own SVG at the same position and size — the handwritten texture of the original logo is missing.

Page transitions use Barba.js v1 like the original, so they only run when opened over http. Opened via file:// it is a normal navigation. Barba swaps only the body (.ni-container), so the three pages each load the css of the home, news and program pages.

The original has more pages — program detail (a panel whose background color changes per category · data-theme), schedule, tickets, directions, news article — but only the recorded subpages (news list · program list · support info · news page 2) were built. News page 2 has the same form as page 1, so it’s reduced to a single news.html. The header items Schedule · Directions · Tickets link to anchors on the home page.

join.html comes from a different site in the original (the film festival’s main site, a white Bootstrap page), so the header, footer and font sizes differ and there is no cursor ring or Barba — built as that different page, as in the original. Body screenshots · QR · video are placeholders.

The phone menu works like the original: the panel stands at .1s and items drop in from -15px at 1s power2.out .06s in sequence. The original’s body lock while the menu is open (saving scroll position) is replaced by simple panel scrolling.
The submenu under the menu in the home site version (join.html) was built with two or three placeholders without knowing the original items (expands in .3s on hover).

title: Paper hearts and town illustrations for a hospital and care group
good_for: A hospital, nursing care, welfare or childcare group, community medical corporation or warm-toned nonprofit site with recruiting info.

pages.use: Group home page — heart-cropped photo and green paper heart opening, two notice lines, concept sentence (mask reveal), one-sheet town illustration (phone: fixed horizontal pan), three keyword hearts (hover speech bubbles), area map, photo strip, division speech-bubble strip · staff interviews · culture, newsletter cards, recruiting strip.

Group intro — facility layout map band, policy structure diagram and policies 01~03, message, regional activity cards, future plans (photo collage · number pills · school list). The ”Get to know us” slot for organizations and groups

Business intro — a region/business pill filter (accordion on phones) and a repeating list of green and yellow pill titles + white panel description and photo + facility link pill. For business guides with many facilities or branches
Newsletter list — a title and mascot speech-bubble head between two diagonals, 4-column square cards on a white paper panel. For blog, internal newsletter and activity news lists.

Division intro (recruiting) — a sticky white side menu that follows (shows the current division), and for each division two photos, a speech-bubble name tag, a long intro and a heart-arrow link row. For job type or department hiring pages
News detail — slim newsletter header, title, date, large photo and body on a white panel, pill button back to the list. For notice, press and event post details

notes: The six Lottie spots (fixed button body walk·head nod, staff interview·About map hug, newsletter pencil heart mascot, recruit band mascot, footer heart mascot) run on the same lottie-web 5.12.2 canvas renderer as the original, but instead of the original JSON, shared.js builds animation data in which our own symbols (leaf mascot·heart mascot) are composed from shape layers. Panel size, 24fps, frame counts (48·24·240), speeds (1.5·.7·.5·1.3·.8·.9), ranges (0→16, 0→12), looping, scroll linkage (plays only while scrolling, stops after 100ms of stillness) and the footer’s 110% line playback follow the original. The in-art motions (walk, nod, hug, pencil scribble) could not be seen in the original art, so they were newly designed within the same length. The canvas build is used by adding lottie_canvas.min.js from the same npm package to the same build folder (_vendor/lottie-web@5.12.2).

The original has many hand-drawn town, map and structure illustrations. The town art, regional map and policy art were redrawn in the same composition as procedural SVG and canvas (sparser than the original), and the colors in the art are also built from the skin variables (--site-*). Individual townsperson motions (the original dash·jump·shake keyframes) differ because the art pieces differ, so only the cloud (9·10·12s) and balloon (12·10s) in-out-quad values were matched to the original.

The hero title is a handwritten SVG in the original — replaced with type of the same position and size. Zen Kaku Gothic New has no Korean glyphs, so Korean falls back to Gothic A1 (slightly sturdier than the original).

The opening plays only on the first visit, as in the original (cookie for 3 days, named nh_top_visited). To see it again, add ?opening after the address. Values are the same (photo heart -100% · 11° · green heart 100% · -5° · sineOut∘sineOut 1.2s → back.out(.8) 1s · title 130%→0 1.2s stagger .04).

On phone, the village picture’s horizontal sweep is pinned with position: sticky instead of the original’s fixed switch. The pin height (picture width/screen width × 100vh), xPercent, start top -20%, end bottom 80% and scrub 1.6 are the same.

Keyword hearts work like the original: on PC they open on hover (the heart mascot rises when hovered after entering the screen), on phones they open and close by tapping — the Close button on the phone bubble and tap-the-backdrop-to-close are omitted (tapping the heart again closes it).
In About Business, the original 15 items were cut to 4: two yellow and two green. The newsletter list has 7 cards, the division overview has 2 divisions.

The facility layout strip in the group About is a horizontal swipe dragged by finger on phones in the original — replaced with overflow-x horizontal scroll (the original also reads scrollLeft with no library).
In the recording the news detail was captured as type detail, but since it is a single news post it was changed to article.
A page-to-page transition effect isn’t in the original (plain navigation), so it was left as is.

Subpage breadcrumbs (about·service·news·recruit·article): in the original, what follows ‹Top› is a Japanese page name, so it stays Korean. The Korean pair Gothic A1 was added to the English font stack (--kf-font-en) so it doesn’t fall back to the system gothic. The other Latin spots (line under the logo · Menu · Scroll · Staff Interview · Topics subtitle · Recruit Information · date · number) are already English, and the big titles are kana or handwriting in the original, so they stay Korean

title: Fixed product photos revealed like windows with calm vertical text
good_for: A traditional confectionery, heritage food or long-established online shop with products, history, news and store info.

pages.use: Shop home page — horizontal menu over an 88px gray band (branch panel opens right away), crossed photos cropped by a large circle and a fan-shaped pattern, featured slider (Swiper), seven flagship products revealed like windows over pinned photos (ScrollTrigger pin), four branches, News, two branches for Stores·About, search field. For a traditional sweets and food online shop landing page

Shop About — full-bleed photo header with fan-mark vertical title, old signboard band, vertical-writing history alternating faded old photos and three-leaf pattern panels, two horizontal paragraphs on a patterned background, vertical-writing pride text, company·store two branches. For the history·heritage About of a long-established shop
News list — vertical title with fan mark, category filter tags, rows of white square thumbnail + date + title + tag, pagination. For closure notice and announcement lists

Store guide — white vertical title over a building photo, map with phone and vertical-text store info, large store architecture photo with description, two-photo description. For offline store and branch pages

notes: The original hero is three photo PNGs with arcs drawn in (cut-out shapes are baked into the photo), so they were cropped with a big circle clip-path at the same place, and the fan-shaped three-leaf pattern background (the original background image) was redrawn as an SVG line pattern — since the cut shapes and pattern are image content, line weight and arc curvature are not exactly the same as the original image.

Vertical-writing titles squash the mincho to 1.1 wide and .9 tall like the original, and Korean uses Nanum Myeongjo and Gothic A1 — since these are Korean placeholders, strokes are heavier than Japanese mincho and glyphs a bit wider in vertical writing
The map is an embedded map (iframe) in the original, so a placeholder box of the same size is used — it is an outside service, so it is not carried over

title: Dark green paper texture with hand-drawn arches, ridgelines and wave panels
good_for: A guesthouse, inn or small cafe lodging presenting rooms, shared spaces, dining and directions with warm illustrations and photos.

pages.use: Lodge home page — new loading for first visit, round text line and two-panel fade photo, intro under a white mountain ridge · three hand-drawn arches, under a wave a pink panel with three rooms (photo ring + small photo row) · amenities table · in-lodge space cells · floor plan, green panel with three columns, access with a map and route map
Column list — round-head photo, category pill row (icons), three-row photo card grid (round category icon · date · title), round page numbers. For shop news and blog lists

Single column article — circular category icon, date, title row, body (highlighter marks, vertical illustration), and a category list attached on the left. The original column/20261030/1109 and cms/column/20250323/338 (parking guide) share the same type, so they are merged into one.
Contact — round header photo on a green background, six white rounded inputs · send confirmation · white button. For small shop contact forms

notes: Swiper 6.3.4, which the original uses, is placed in _vendor/swiper@6.3.4 as the npm build (MIT) so the same version is used. jquery.easing is not bundled because the original only uses swing

The first-visit loading GIF (bird + text, 457×407·5.18s) was redrawn as a line-art SVG bird and text writing at the same tempo (bird-type-loader). The bird shape is a simple line drawing, not identical to the original artwork
The handwritten section-name art (stay|Lodging·Inside the Inn·column·access) and the Hero’s rounded text-line art are rendered in a rounded bold typeface (Jua) — the handwritten feel is faint

The three-arch line drawing, white bird, mountain ridge, waves, facility table icons, floor plan and transit route map were redrawn as new SVG·CSS shapes at the same position and size, but they are simpler than the original hand drawings (the floor plan has fewer rooms)
The map embed (iframe) is a same-size placeholder map SVG, and the contact-form plugin form is a static form in the same cell (no sending)
Column article column/20261030/1109 and cms/column/20250323/338 (parking guide — listed as about in the page list) share the same form, so one article.html was built for both
The category icon drawings (bed, bowl, pin, flag) were made as same-size clip-path shapes

title: Forest video with photo clusters flying in through 3D space
good_for: A project site bundling several villas, lodgings or resorts, nature-focused brand landing pages and per-location brand pages.

pages.use: Project landing page — number loader, forest-video hero, large text flowing over a wave background, concept copy that rises line by line, a photo-bundle slide that flies in 3D (Next/Prev circles), a project map pinned to the screen that fills with dark ink color, an intro to two villas, a news row.
News list — big title with rows of date, villa name, title and pill arrow below, underline appears on hover
A single news post — title and date on the left, image, body and back-to-list on the right

Single villa brand front page (deep moss color) — video Hero, scattered-photo concept section, photo that unfolds from a center strip, three pinned rooms (title in a circle), News · links · scenery strip · beige Footer

One villa’s brand home page (sea navy) — aerial photo hero, scattered-photos concept section, expanding photo, three pinned villas (large serif titles), brown experience band, FAQ · contact links, beige footer

notes: Photos are wf-img placeholders (subject · light · composition label), video is a green gradient mp4 of the same ratio (media/forest.mp4 10s loop) — stands in for the original hero forest video and the villa stream video. The loader background (lawn photo) is also a placeholder

Fonts: minerva-modern (paid) → Marcellus, tt-commons-pro (paid) → Figtree, ten-mincho-text (paid serif) → Noto Serif KR. The project and villa logos (SVG) are a mark box + placeholder text, so they lack the character of the original hand-drawn marks.

Wave background SVG line shapes and the project map (cities, waterways) were not copied from the original art but redrawn at the same position and size. The sine tempo (3e-4·1·3.5·.7·1.3·2.6) and gradient stop math are exactly as in the original waveAnimation.
The Lenis 1.3.x build leaks a one-letter global name (r etc.) that collides with Splide’s global helper — so Lenis is loaded after all libraries (changing the order causes a virtualScroll.on error).

Villa navy and sand brown: since the moss color (accent) has low saturation, the browser sees its hue as 0, so only the hue is set to the original values (237.1·61.3) and lightness·saturation are derived from the accent — navy and brown tints remain even when the skin is swapped.

title: Scattered photo chunks that rotate and unfold on a vocational school site
good_for: A college or school site with many color-coded courses and numerous sub-pages for admissions, open campus and career results.

pages.use: School home page — a KV (course-color background) where six photo blocks circle around scattered positions and the center one expands to fill the screen, a News thumbnail slider and open campus banner, News rows, five Strengths where a left numbered nav lights up (photo slider · number count), five Courses that tint with the course color as you pass and an English marquee rising behind, a feature banner slider, open campus cards filtered by category in a slider, and four SNS color panels. For a school or academy home with multiple departments.

School about (educational philosophy) — two red headband photos, red-bar subheading and body, red band title with three bordered boxes below (philosophy), down arrow, 2×2 trust boxes, two mascot illustrations in a gray box, related-link photo cards. For philosophy and policy intros of schools and institutions.

Job and debut support hub: centered intro and bordered banner, three white cards on the right over a grayscale photo panel (title, big number, several pill buttons), a contact box, two banners and a group of text links. For career and support guide pages leading with result numbers

Feature list — five white cards in rows, each with a left banner photo, number tag, title, description and pill button, plus a contact box, two banners and related links. For feature and campaign post lists

Education program About (corporate project) — rainbow lettered intro, three power circles in a triangle, student and company voices (photo + Q&A), vertical STEP tag process flow, finished works box. For program, course and methodology About pages

Photo gallery — a blurred photo pattern background flows horizontally over 20 seconds, with a big title on a white panel, then color-band tags + a three-column photo grid (brightens on hover). For event and school life photo collections

Single program detail (esports support · results) — red and navy diagonal band header (player photo, red box copy, navy button), navy band title, numbered SUPPORT subheads, pentagon chart record table, two-column event list, blue-bordered senior card, two-column senior cells. For support programs and results detail

notes: The original Swiper 7.4.1 is included as _vendor/swiper@7.4.1 with the same panel and the same options (threshold 20, thumbs·carousel 1/2/3 slides). The original bundle’s onscreen library (adds is-onscreen when entering the viewport) is replaced by IntersectionObserver (threshold 0), and jQuery’s scroll-to-top animate 500ms swing by GSAP ScrollTo .5s sine.inOut.
SplitText, Flip, pixi and lottie detected on the cards are detection noise from the gsap/all bundle and ad scripts, so they were not used (the site code never calls them)
The original KV multiply image veil (texture.png) is redrawn as a round shade that darkens toward the edges, and the cover photo (multiply) of the course section is also newly drawn as a round shade

Recording types were corrected: recruit (debut, employment) is a student career support hub, not hiring, so it became page. service (feature list) is an article list, so it became news. works (company projects) is an education program intro, so it became service

The cards inside the mega menu panel (picture and sub-list layout) are simplified to 4–6 photo cards per menu instead of the original’s detailed layout. The phone menu is a one-level accordion per menu instead of the original’s two-level one

Text blocks and boxes of the sub pages (old CSS area) were built at the same position and ratio from the printouts, the original’s illustration banners and logo art became photo placeholders, and the mascot was redrawn as SVG. Table and text line counts in sub page bodies were cut from the original.

The social feed widgets are fixed placeholder boxes. Clicking a photo gallery cell opens a large colorbox photo window in the original, which was not built (left for the next person — the colorbox library is MIT licensed, so put it in _vendor and hook up the same window).

Font backfill: the Latin heading font (Barlow Condensed) slots — section outline big text (NEWS·POINT·COURSE·OPEN CAMPUS), Section English heads, mega menu English heads, KV course name, sub-page English tails (CONCEPT·SKILL·STEP·Vocational Education etc.), and the footer copyright line — were built as English placeholder text from the start, so no text was changed (images not re-shot). Using computed fonts on the 7 rendered pages × 1440·390, we confirmed 0 Korean glyphs in Barlow. The KV big copy, school name, menu, and Section Japanese heads are kanji/kana in the original, so Korean is kept there. Barlow’s companion Noto Sans KR (400~900) is loaded in theme.css

title: Picture-book hand-drawn river town connecting streams of activity
good_for: A town, municipality, regional council or environmental group introducing its area and projects with illustrated characters, an opening animation and news list.

pages.use: Home page — after a mascot sequence opening on a white veil, four hand-drawn river village scenes cycle with a Swiper fade (progress bar), a big headline and rounded picture-book button, about (photo · village drawing · map), six topic cards, two business blocks with photos, and a village drawing strip. For regional or organization homes

About — header photo cut by waves and hand drawings, long intro text beside a chunky photo, concept explanation and map photo on a white cloud panel, contact band, five people (two large, three small round portraits) and six partner cards. For an organization’s about, people and partners menu

Business (cycle) — header photo, speech-bubble question beside a hill house illustration, four-step circles for what we do (arrows), one case study, two businesses (wave photo band, block photo, pop-out speech bubble). For business and how-we-work intro

News list — header photo and angler illustration, big heading, category pill filters (ALL · #REPORT…), three columns of thick-bordered cards, and ‹Load more› unfolds cards that attach at .1s intervals. For notice and event report lists (the category pages have the same shape, so this is the version filtered by the #report address)

notes: The hand-drawn illustrations are redrawn as our own SVG (ill.js — thick ink lines + flat color fills, colors made from the accent color in oklch as --site-*) in the same position, size and composition, but they are not as dense as the original — four hero scenes (field · waterwheel · sandy beach · cruise ship), a 15-frame mascot sequence (sits riding a fish, sways, then dives in), village strip · footer mountain ridge · map · twelve character props. People and animals are simple shape dolls. This is because the original avif art could not be carried over, and drawing more is left for the next person

The picture-book overlay (original /book/ digital picture book iframe) opens the iframe with the same blue overlay and the same open and close (.45s · .1s delay, close message from inside), but inside is only a one-page picture-book placeholder — the page-turn (bookblock) feature was not built
Swiper’s version string isn’t in the original bundle, so 11.1 or higher was confirmed by a feature string (swiperElementNodeName exists) and swiper@11.2.10 from the library was used
For swapping light and dark skins, the first page was shot with the dark skin (neon-sign) and no original colors were seen remaining

title: Photo strips that slowly stand up on hover for a home builder
good_for: A housing, architecture or interior company site, a portfolio with many project cases, or a calm lifestyle brand.

pages.use: Company first page — a two-column text menu over a video hero, a vertical-writing intro band, four tall photo page-link cells, four work photo strips that slowly stand up on hover, a center-aligned model house slider, three event cards, staggered photo sections, a news list, and two contact panels. For an architecture or housing company landing page with many cases

Concept (company philosophy) — vertical-writing title and body over a video with an ink-colored veil, text blocks and photos floating and sinking in a staggered 12-column grid over a noise-textured background, a large photo, one case strip, page links. For long-form intros like a brand philosophy or a founder’s message.

Column list — two overlapping portrait photos at top right and a large title, tag filter row, row list of date·title·tag·excerpt·square photo, page numbers, find by tag. For blog·column·News lists (the tag-specific list /column/tag/living has the same form)

Project case list — big heading, two rows of tag filters, per house several rows of photo strips that drift on their own and stop when touched, page numbers, search by tag and region. For work and case lists with many photos

Construction case — a 1.732:1 large photo, title and intro, horizontal (12-column) and vertical (8-column) photos alternating with ‹+› to enlarge, two-column text, a building overview table and tags, a related case strip, a regional tour slider, 4 model house cards. For case and work detail pages

notes: Hero · the concept hero video is our placeholder video (placeholder-16x9.mp4, 12 seconds) with a slowly flowing gradient, matching only the same autoplay, loop, and mute.

The vertical text in the About band · concept hero was an image of letters in the original, so it is matched with Korean vertical text (writing-mode: vertical-rl) in the same place · width · line count
The brush-tip artwork at both ends of the button (original image) was redrawn as a half-circle SVG, and the hand-drawn borders of the two header buttons were replaced with a 1px rounded border
The per-tag column list (/column/tag/living) has the same type as the column list (l-archiveColumn), so news.html stands in for it
The original fonts A1 Gothic and A1 Myeongjo are paid fonts from a foundry, so they were swapped for Noto Sans KR 300 and Noto Serif KR (Inter is the same)
The tour slider’s region filter redraws the cells in the copy and mounts Splide anew (the original hides them by class, then rebuilds) — the visible behaviour is the same

title: Vertical navigation and clipped-corner buttons for a mansion restaurant wedding venue
good_for: A wedding hall, restaurant, hotel or studio site centered on the space and consultation booking, with photo-rich about, gallery and blog pages.

pages.use: Shop home page — logo loader where a grid clears away, Hero with logo on top and video below, concept with four scattered photos, ribbon date card (consultation schedule), Instagram band flowing with the mouse, three vertical photos, two white cells overlapping a black-and-white band, pricing cards, gray-band photo services, access·contact footer

Photo gallery by category — sticky side index + a large photo per category (English label alternating left and right) and a thumbnail strip flowing with the mouse, click opens a white enlarged modal (number · dots · prev/next). For wedding hall, restaurant and studio galleries

Blog and news list: category pills and period accordion on the side, featured-post carousel advancing two cards at a time every 5 seconds (circle around the dot fills), thumbnail text rows, page numbers. The yearly list (blog/date/2026) has the same form, so this one section serves for both.

One service or space intro — large English title over a taller-than-screen photo, eight photos of varying sizes in a zigzag, a wide space photo with centered text and spec table, then two cards for other spaces. For multiple same-pattern pages such as wedding, banquet, cooking

notes: Of the original’s four sub pages, blog/date/2026 (captured as detail during recording) is just a by-year filter with the same list form as blog, so they are merged into one news.html.

Logo, Brand wordmark and mark share the same look (thin long strokes, a center node dot, an initial inside a diamond) 'LOGO'·'L' Placeholders were redrawn. The place-name slot is PLACE NAME, the award badge is a red circle badge slot, and the affiliate logo strip is BRAND 01–08 boxes.

The original typeface classico-urw (paid, Optima-style) is swapped for Marcellus, and source-han-serif-japanese for Noto Serif KR of the same family. Korean placeholders are wider than Japanese, so a few lines of the large 44px headings have fewer characters than the original.

The original remembers the first visit with a session cookie, and from the second page on only the white strip lifts without the grid logo loader. Cookies do not work on file://, so the same behavior was achieved with a 30-minute marker in localStorage.

The hero video’s original file (fv.mp4) is not in the archived copy, so its length could not be measured — a 10-second placeholder video of the same 16:9 ratio (media/hero.mp4, a light gray band sweeps across) is hooked up with the same playback behavior as the original (plays at first, stops two frames later to lay down the first scene, then loops silently 2.2s after the loader opens). The video sits on top of the photo-slot fill with multiply, so it changes along with the skin.
The map (map-service iframe) was redrawn as a grayscale street illustration (SVG) — colors derive from skin variables (--site-map-*).

The Saturday blue (#006eaf) and holiday red (#ff6261) in the calendar and the award badge red (#c8102e) carry meaning for dates and prizes, so they were treated as not skin and left in shared.css :root as Not skin.
Gallery thumbnails are cut to 16 per category instead of the original ~50 (the loop length is slide count × 7rem, the original formula as is).

Phone finger drags (Insta·thumbnails·affiliates band, blog recommended carousel) accept only clearly horizontal swipes, as in the original, but use touch-action: pan-y instead of the original touchmove preventDefault — vertical swipes still scroll the page as normal.
Links to unrecorded pages such as the contact form, pair detail, FAQ and review detail were connected to our four pages or the first page anchor.

service Space intro label — the original has the form 「( English name -katakana reading- )」, so it uses English placeholder text 「( space -Space- )」, and only the reading inside the parentheses is set in serif (--kf-font-sans) like the original. The first-page hero, lead, menu group names and breadcrumb page names are Japanese (serif) in the original, so Korean is kept — the paired typeface Noto Serif KR is already loaded

title: Calm online shop for diagnosis-based custom mattresses in navy serif
good_for: An online store for bedding, household or made-to-order goods with home, product list, brand story and news on pale gray and cream.

pages.use: Shop home page — two-photo hero · worry speech bubbles · diagnosis steps · certification board · consultation panel where bubbles light up in turn · features that pin to the screen and change with a progress bar · review cards · parallax photos and a big wordmark · product info table · news · FAQ · flowing photo strip. For a custom product · bedding shop home

Product list — rounded big photo header · gradient circle (WebGL) intro · photo strip where the center cell rises · per-product photo and description · endlessly flowing photo strip (Swiper) · notification sign-up circle. For shops with only a few product categories

Brand story — rounded large photo header, a poem going from blur to sharp and a white wave tube (WebGL), photo strip, a mission with vertical English section name, column cards, gradient notice strip, social strip, two photos. For a single brand About page
News list — large rounded photo header, three-column cards, pagination. For shop news and press lists
News item — date·two-line title·large round image·body·column cards. For a single press·notice article

notes: The original is an e-commerce theme (built on a base theme), so it has no page-transition effect — the copy uses plain navigation too
Between the teardown capture (10/29) and the archive copy (11/10) the first page changed — built to match the archive copy (the current version)
three r152 has only a CommonJS build in _vendor, so photo-cylinder-spin/three-global.js creates window.THREE and loads it
Hero laurel frame, certification badge, handwritten English phrase and speech-bubble shape (clip-path SVG) are replaced by simple lines, text and rounded corners of the same position and size.
The mattress shine effect (shineEffect) in the original About has no script to turn it on, so it does not run in the original either — not built
Brand Instagram strip Swiper values (cell count · gap) couldn’t be found in the original settings so they were matched by eye
Cart, account, search and diagnosis pages were not recorded, so they are left as #

title: Right-to-left unrolling scroll with vertical text lines for an artist collaboration
good_for: A landing page for an artist collaboration product, Japanese-style vertical text feature, limited edition or exhibition catalog-like single page.

pages.use: One-page scroll landing — a stage flowing right→left on a vertical wheel, a Hero with vertical title and diamond-art constellation, an author section (name, tagline, vertical body strip unrolling downward, square art, pink vertical ”Details” button, About panel), order flow, links·share, tail. For a feature that shows multiple authors·products one page at a time.

notes: The original blocks access from outside its home country (403, redirect to an overseas notice page), so the archive only recorded the notice page. Instead, structure and values were read from the 2026-02-18 HTML and JS of a web archive (RtlScroller and velocity values in main-min.js) plus the image files. The layout css (assets/css/base.css) is not in the archive, so in-section layout (band gaps, positions) was inferred from image sizes (hero 1760×800 · artist backdrop 1600×800 · bands 72·28·20×640 · image 640 · button 80×640 · flow 480×640) and the diamond positions (the image’s bounding box).

The original motion is site code built with velocity 1.3.0. Only the engine was swapped to GSAP and the curves were matched with the same formula (ease-in-out = 0.42,0,0.58,1 · ease-out = 0,0,0.58,1 · swing = sine.inOut). The wheel is pushed straight with no curve, like the original
Only five of eleven artist sections were built (same type repeated). The original’s empty campaign section (first-section) was not built

The text strip unrolls to the length of the text instead of 640px like the original (in the original the empty strip extends to 640 even when the text image is shorter — the visible end is the same, only the speed differs slightly). The to option of strip-unroll can also fix it at 640.
The artist image and About panel content (profile text · SNS address) are placeholders. The artist name images in the original list panel were replaced with vertical serif text

title: Character-led portfolio diving into a head, with background colors changing per section
good_for: A personal portfolio or self-introduction told as a journey of thoughts, work and profile, with case studies shown as moving app mockups.

pages.use: Portfolio home page: design tool selection-box intro, dive into a character head with a lid that opens, then greeting, what I make, belief statement, where I live, horizontal work cards and About sections alternate in one 2850vh scroll, then come back out of the head for Contact. For personal portfolios and self-introductions

A single Work case: a working app mockup (3D city map delivery control with a left rail, header row, metrics, card board and detail panel, plus four screens: map, depot, load assignment and auto rules). It opens inside a panel that covers the page from below when a Work card on the home page is clicked. For product and dashboard case details.

notes: The character, auto-rickshaw, palm tree, cup, paper plane, closing section doodle and peeking face in the work section are newly drawn SVGs with the same position, size and motion axes (lid hinge 206,232 · loop 320,232 · wheels 72/272,206 · wrist 110,338), so their look differs from the original. When swapping in another character, also adjust the svgOrigin in index.js to match the axis coordinates to the art.

The paid Mighty Brand in the name wordmark is replaced with Melodrama, the original’s usual fallback, and the paid Exposit in headings and the Hi line with Big Shoulders, the original’s fallback. The name letters run wider than on the original screen (STUDIO NAME wraps the selection box more widely).

There is no background music file — eq-sound-toggle only runs the look and states (invitation wiggle, speech bubble after 2.6s, turns on at first press), and if you give data-fx-eq-sound-toggle a src: the sound ramps up to .45 over 1.4s as in the original.

All six work cards and Contact link 3 open the case page detail.html in a panel. The original uses a different case html per card, and the résumé is a PDF. Only one recorded subpage exists (Product TMS), so the other cases were not built (one of the same shape is enough).
The Nominee ribbon on the right edge (an external award badge) was removed because it is not part of the site design.

Case page: the 3D vehicle, city and depot shapes were rebuilt by stacking our rounded boxes at the same dimensions as the original mockup (semi 12.8, box 8.4, van 5.6, grid 6, depot x+140). The chat panel answers a sent message with one fixed reply after 1.2s. File upload in load assignment is faked (progress bar only).
Case page dark mode: as in the original, when prefers-color-scheme: dark, theme.css [data-theme=app] A dark block catches — the 3D color is re-baked from the Skin.

title: Online bank account-opening landing page with a floating signup button
good_for: A signup landing page for an online bank, fintech or subscription service, with product list and detail, payment info, company info and login.

pages.use: Account-opening LP — apricot→blue-gray hero (curved band, phone, medal), crimson name-change band, three numbered benefit cards, two features and three security points, crimson partner band, review carousel, opening steps·FAQ·start band, icon tab finder, notification, floating opening band·QR panel. For financial and app LPs that take sign-ups
Product·service list — three category shortcut cells, slick banner slider (pause button), per category an icon title + a table of name cells·link rows. For list pages of companies with many products

Company intro: floating rounded header bar (a mega panel unfolds on hover), pink ball hero, greeting panel, big English NEWS row, two white-on-dark-photo panels, Sustainability card, cookie band. For the home page of a corporate info site
Smartphone payment service — left category side menu plus a panel of 2 logo-card columns. For partner services and linked app list pages

Purpose-based account product detail — three usage scenes, three feature cards, two open-account buttons, three screen images, accordion usage steps, deposit and withdrawal table, question links. For a page introducing one product in detail.
Login panel — a login window that floats over a dark overlay when the notice is opened (inputs · navy pill button · help panel). For the login screen in front of a members-only page

notes: The original address (/contents/lp/brand/) goes through two meta refreshes to the bank’s first page (/contents/), so we built the pre-login screen (dngnli_ account-opening LP area) as the first page. The post-login screen (balance card, rate graph, banner slider) is hidden even in the original, so we did not build it.

The About page is a different shape from the bank pages even in the original (floating round header bar, cookie band, white footer), so it was built separately in about.css. The four bank subpages share the header and footer from the same piece.

The review carousel is original in-page code (Carousel class), so the same behavior was rewritten as the new part center-loop-swipe. The floating account-opening bar is hooked on appear-past-scroll (at: 100vh · once · drop-solid, visible from the start at 820px and up), and the collapsible usage guide in the detail uses height-fold (.2s swing).

The product list banner uses the same slick as the original (4s auto · dots · arrows · pause) — the slick inside the original lib.js has its version label erased, so the last version 1.8.1 in _vendor was used (jQuery 2.2.4 is the same version as the original)
The original Swiper 8.4.0 is only used for the debit card review group on the logged-in screen and is absent before login — not included in the copy.
The PC account-opening button opens a QR panel like the original (peach→blue-gray panel, floats up in .3s), and on phones it goes to a link (the original is an app store address).
Hero phone, medal, character, QR and app screen are placeholders of the same position and ratio, and the curved band and pink ball are redrawn as SVG.

title: Flipping card columns and a gray left band for a payment service
good_for: A B2B, payment or SaaS product site with numeric results, pricing tables, onboarding steps and case lists for corporate clients.

pages.use: Product home — pink·sky-blue split-line loader, hero where 18 illustrated cards rise and fall in three columns and flip on click, pinned title + three features, two reasons (image zoom modal), three cases, pricing table, 4-step onboarding order, integration · add-on service · related service cards. For B2B service landing pages.

What sets us apart — gray head band · pie chart results · client logo band · two reason images · three cases · integration logo grid · extra service intro. For competitor comparison and strengths pages

Case study list — intro + logo grid, three selected cases, industry filter attached to a left gray band + two-column case cards on the right (half logo, half photo). For client case and portfolio lists
Press release list — rows with date, title, subtitle and circle arrow, numbered paging, and a pill grid of past news by month. For news, notice and press release lists

Case study detail — logo, company name, big title, tags and a main photo on the right, a three-point box, interview body with question headings and photo captions, publish date. For a single customer interview or case article.

notes: The original illustrations (dozens of SVGs of people, shops, maps and charts) were replaced by 20 newly drawn simple line drawings with the same placement and stroke width. They have less variety in poses and props than the original, and the 18 card fronts reuse the same set. The animated logo that lights up when hovering the header logo (original sprite) is replaced by our logo lines being drawn in 12 steps.

The page transition uses barba 2.10.3, same as the original (same hook order, same basic transition, going to the first page has no transition, just the loader), but it only runs when opened over http. Opened as a file (file://), barba can’t fetch pages, so it draws the same line and actually moves on to the next html.
The case list was cut from about 30 original cards to 8 (repeats trimmed). Industry filter and left pin use the original values as they are

The flowing English text in the request band uses a Montserrat text line instead of the original SVG lettering — cell width (PC 151rem · phone 55.2rem · 44.6rem) · duration (30s · 12s reverse · 10s) · direction are the original values
Pages that were not recorded — SNS share button · contact form · map · FAQ — were not built. The menu’s ‹Menu One · Three · Four · Pricing · Adoption Steps› link to anchors on the first page
Logos, certification marks, photos and text are all placeholders

title: Wheel clock switching skull, mask, filter and X-ray scenes of a wearable device
good_for: A hardware, wearable or medical device product story told in multiple scenes on one immersive wheel-driven screen without document scrolling.

pages.use: Product home page — block skull loader → glowing skull HUD + dot halftone model viewer + big title that melts into place → giant statement behind a mask → dive, hyperspace and filter-layer airflow → X-ray skeleton card → red section with product name group and edition cards → ”/” light-pillar footer. For an immersive landing that explains one 3D product scene by scene.

Brand About — a single ticket with its stub torn off rises, showing the intro paragraph, three gauges (dot level · bar wave · tick ring), four stamp photos and an end-cell curl, then ends with a route-picking game of three (find the hidden module) and the same footer. For product intro pages and event ticket style About

notes: The 3D models (skull, mask, filter canister, skeleton) use our basic shapes (sphere, torus, cylinder, box) instead of the original glb files, matching only position, size, and silhouette proportions. The skull is rounder and simpler than the original, and the skeleton is a spine box plus torus ribs, so the X-ray texture is not as dense as the original anatomical model. To add the models, swap skull(), mask(), and skeleton() in world.js for GLTF, and the post-processing (glow, checker halftone, dot halftone, color split, flash) still applies as is.

The original post-processing is several passes inside the neuroform3d engine. Here one composite shader (world.js COMPOSE) redoes the block · glow + horizontal drag · checker halftone (3px) · dot halftone (viewer) · cream flash — values were tuned by eye (guess) and are not 1:1 with the original shader values.

The original loader has ring · bar · CLICK TO START stages in code, but on the live site (measured headless) it entered right after a block skull for 3.4s — only what was seen is built: block skull → entrance (0.15s skull move · 0.5s head line · 0.8s HUD frame · 1.1s text).

The page-turn tear (0.8s): the original tears the browser’s page-transition image (@view-transition). On file:// that image can’t be obtained, so a background-color panel covering the new page is opened with the same tear curve (center top→bottom, spreading to both sides, 4px red edge).

The original’s lenis@1.1.13 has a structure where the document doesn’t scroll (everything fixed) so nothing moves, so it isn’t loaded. Scroll uses the same clock as the original scroll.js (wheel 700px = p 1, .9s power2.out, finger 1.6x, keys power3.inOut between sections) built, and also extracted as a wheel-clock part.

The dive section length (original STORY.hold, 7) and section positions match the p values measured by rolling the wheel headless (Hero 0 · big text 1~4.3 · dive 4.3~5.3 · hyperspace ~6.2 · filter layer ~9.6 · flash 9.9 · skeleton ~13.6 · red section 13.3~ · footer 20.6).

The large statement fades from the top line down like the original, but the original’s line curl (curlAt .2) and ink-blob entrance are not included. The word pillar in the red section uses one blurred plate instead of the original’s two layers, a sharp plate plus a blurred plate.

The hero title uses Anton instead of PP Formula Condensed Black (paid) — since the letters are wider, the placeholders are one or two characters shorter than the original (Headline Set / Item Name / Series).

The About route game drops the original’s 3D view riding along the route and the minimap. It only goes as far as: pick screen (hover brightens only that route) → route board (background color · hatched road · three of six spots hidden) → green/red cards → DONE mark once all three are found. The secret animation (second line of the checklist) is left empty since the original also marks it as later.

The About footer 3D is a mask in the original (about-3d.js), but here the same skeleton as Home is placed in the light beam. Stamp photos and card photos are wf-img placeholders (label gives subject, light, composition).

Phone (720px and below) is, like the original, just a single gate screen (checker halftone skull rotating at 0.55rad/s, three guide lines, label, contact strip) — the original design file has no phone layout, and neither does the original site.

Cursor interaction is matched to the original engine values — hero crosshair (damping 12/s, confined inside the panel, moved by transform), loader skull (5% per frame, .08·.05 rad), hero skull (follows with damping 40/s — rotation range measured from a sweep drawing is about .6 rad, camera moves .35·.25), viewer model. The original’s hover state over the skull (X-ray showing the inside) is not included

Unfinished: after spending over 180 minutes on one piece, the About entry uses a 1.9s top-down reveal (clip) instead of the original 3D ticket roll (ticket3d.js), and the details of the gauge, stamp and end cell (the original barcode strip, QR and stamp texture) were kept simple.

title: Red wordmark opened by scissors on a one-page studio site
good_for: A small design or web studio or freelance team one-pager covering process, work, pricing bundles and contact in one flow.

pages.use: One-page studio — a loader where scissors cut open a dotted line, a header where a screen-wide wordmark shrinks and attaches as a 140px logo, a growing video, a process panel where a four-corner wheel becomes a circle and rolls, a pinned Work photo panel that unfolds from the corners, a price list flipping up inside an old monitor, a Contact path that shapes follow, and a red Footer revealed from below.

notes: Most original motion is Webflow interaction (IX2) settings, so the same library can’t be used — keyframe positions (%), durations and curves from the settings JSON were ported to GSAP timelines · ScrollTrigger (IX2 smoothing is approximated by scrub .3~.8). The original inline scripts (loader number strip · wheel canvas · pinned work panel with Lenis sync · contact track) were rewritten with the same values.

The wordmark does not use the original lettering. It is drawn with our own geometric LOGOTYPE, eight letters, at the same 6.09:1 ratio (shared.js NL.mark). The loader motion is the same: each letter drops from 300px above (2s · .05 stagger · starting from the center).

End of the price scene (original a-6) — from 80%, when the stage is revealed to have been an old monitor screen — the original uses a monitor photo (retro_ps). Here it is replaced with a CSS-drawn rounded bezel and stand, and the price window shrinking into a small window at bottom left (.36x, 80→86%) was guessed from viewing the original screen.

Desktop windows (team photo · Q&A · reviews) open when an icon is clicked, as in the original, and are dragged by the title bar (Draggable). The original a-57’s 5s size growth was too slow, so it was cut to .5s power2.out.
The barcode on card hover is drawn in the original by Lottie (barcode) from 0 to 100. Here a clip-path stands in, revealing the stripes from the left in the same .5s (no Lottie file).
The phone menu hamburger is CSS where two lines rotate into an X (.45s) instead of the original Lottie (.9s), menu panel open .6s and text .3s (.6 later) are the original a-82 values.
On phones the work list stacks photos vertically instead of the original’s separate swipe slide (clip .9s on change, prev/next buttons, page count) — the next person builds the slide.
The hero video is a placeholder panel of the same position and ratio (a page frame in a dark background sways slowly on a 12s cycle). There is no video file.
PP Editorial New (paid) italic emphasis is covered by Instrument Serif Italic, and Korean by Noto Sans KR · Nanum Myeongjo.

The phone price scene replaces original a-80 (cards flip up one by one, reuse the same spot, and end by retreating to an old phone photo) by pulling the desktop key spot over to the phone’s share and placing three cards in a .62x vertical row — the one-by-one swap layout is left for the next person to pick up.

Font placeholder text: since all the original text is English, every slot for the italic accent font (Instrument Serif Italic) was replaced with English placeholder text — three section-name circles (Process·Pricing·Contact), four process card names, three work name lines, three pricing table names and three back-side abbreviations, one pledge line, cookie question·policy link·three buttons. No italic slots remain in Korean.

Judgment: large headings with italic endings (Hero h1·two big About sentences·Selected Work·the blurred text of the pricing scene·the big Contact question·the cookie question) are, in the original, an English sentence in Vazirmatn plus an italic English tail. Swapping only the tail to English would mix two languages in one line, so they were replaced wholesale with English placeholder text. Body-size sentences (small About text·process one-liner·card descriptions·table descriptions·the sentence after the pledge·Contact description) stay Korean, and only the italic emphasis inside them is swapped to English words. The header menu·phone menu (42px)·word lines·reviews stay Korean, since that is the original usage where the body fonts Vazirmatn·Fira Code fall back to their Korean counterpart (Noto Sans KR)
On one line, Selected Work would slip under the right photo panel at 118px, so it is split into two lines (Selected / Work) like the original.

title: Bento card profile that reshuffles by tab and drags into place
good_for: A developer or designer self-introduction, link collection or profile card page, or a personal home of arranged widgets, with an article and work details.

pages.use: Bento: ten cards, one self-intro page. Pressing a white pill tab (All, About, Projects, Media) moves the cards to that category’s layout and dims the rest, and cards can be dragged around. Cards: intro, map, three works, now-playing track, SNS, post, newsletter, night mode. For personal home pages and link collections.

Single post — close circle at top center, one 648px column with a large rounded serif title · date tag · long paragraphs · figures with captions · lists · footnotes. Hovering the close makes the body sink down, pressing it sinks it and returns to the first page. For a personal blog post or retrospective

Single work — title, one-line intro, external link tag, two-column description (with list), and below it seven draggable captures in the same 4-column grid as the home page. For introducing an app, extension, or side project

notes: The archived pages.json had pages: [] (the first page returned 500, so links couldn’t be followed), but the four subpages (/posts/how-it-started-vs-how-its-going, /projects/wrap·recroot·vouch-for) still open with 200. One post became article.html, and since the three project details share the same type, wrap alone was built as detail.html. On both pages the original has a light theme saved by the server (cookie theme=light) it draws the night panel, and if the copy has never been chosen either, the night panel (data-theme-default=Open with dark) — the first page defaults to a light version.

The capture grid in work detail is the same react-grid-layout board as the original first page (4 columns 280px·gap 16, drag to move), so the same bento-drag-grid part is attached unfiltered (a single all). The original’s seven captures are photo slots describing what to put in.

The grid is wrapped as the part bento-drag-grid, using the same react-grid-layout 1.2.0 (React 17.0.2 UMD) as the original — layout values (columns per width, row height, positions per filter) are the original’s as they are, and cards stay in HTML and are moved into the RGL cells. Which of 1.2.0~1.2.4 the original uses can’t be told from the bundle (styles and attributes are the same), so 1.2.0 is used.

The original framer-motion motions (tab pill · face swap · pulse · map marker · night mode knob · corner button · newsletter shake) are matched in GSAP with the same length and curve (0.85,0,0.3,1 via CustomEase, and those given only a length use the framer default easeInOut=power1.inOut, opacity alone .3s linear, array values .8s). The newsletter success face spring (stiffness 550 · damping 30) is approximated with back.out(1.4) .6s.

The confetti is rewritten with the same physics as the original react-dom-confetti (dom-confetti) settings (up 90° · fan 144° · velocity 23 · 40 pieces · drag .12 · 3 seconds · 2ms stagger · 10px · four colors), so the React build of the library is not bundled.

Art: the faces (memoji) are two simple SVG faces painted in clothing color (normal and masked), the music app logo and SNS logos are a note circle and speech bubble instead of brands, and the logo ”nev” art is rounded serif letters logo with a gradient of three accent colors. Text block entrance curve: the original code has ease "power3.inout"(wrong case) so GSAP does not recognize it and runs the default power1.out — ported as power1.out as seen on screen

The original contact, access, nearby area and chat app pages, plus the contact form plugin, bot-check widget and analytics, were not built because they are outside the recorded scope or are functions

Concept (brand story) — four sections where the text stays fixed at screen center and photos pass over it, the background changes black · brown · white · beige per section, and a left index bar follows. For history or brand story pages

A single report — date · tag · title, a photo set viewed large on click (PhotoSwipe), black-band subheading, two photos · photo + text, video, info table, previous · list · next. For case and review details

notes: Original videos (Hero · About portrait video · pinned forest video · footer video) keep the same place, ratio, autoplay and loop, with only the content swapped for gray gradient placeholder videos (media/loop-*.mp4, 8 seconds, ffmpeg). The original downloads multi-MB videos over the network so the first frame appears late, which makes the first-page loader length and curve and the ”logo → first page” transition longer in the original (2.0~2.5s vs 1.0s) — a difference caused by the small placeholder videos, so it is recorded as accepted.

The actual markup of the affiliated dress shop strip at the very bottom could not be fully read from the archive, so it was built from the screenshot (four logos + caption) — column width and gaps were estimated from the screen (guess)
PLAY MOVIE · the original video window (hero circle · ending video on detail) is a link out to an external video, so only the slot is placed (detail has a 16:9 video slot + play mark)

The detail photo set opens with PhotoSwipe 5.4.1 (library/_vendor/photoswipe@5.4.1, MIT) as in the original, and instead of the original photos, placeholder art in the same ratio is drawn on a canvas (skin variable colors) and paged through.

Center-aligned message, sections of white cards (red underline · pill arrow), snack-tray-shaped person cards on a pink band, speech bubbles popping out from the center, an endless photo row, and a recruiting info band. For the hero of a bright product company’s careers page

New graduate recruiting info — a header with a flowing row of products and a pink location strip, a wide photo and recruiting message, two links going down, a job requirements table (small titles with red borders), two hiring results tables, STEP flow (red bands · chevron arrows), a big red entry button, a contact block, and a question list filtered by fork tabs. About the company: a pinned history strip that turns vertical scroll into horizontal (it appears when the cell enters and ends with a star-shaped panel and nine images popping out), a business intro beside product columns flowing in staggered directions up and down plus two red-bordered boxes, a group structure chart over a dark photo, big numbers on five tilted sheets of paper, a now-and-future·slogan on a red brush-line background, and related info cards. For company about·history·numbers pages.

Job roles intro — six role tabs (red underline), a differently colored panel per role (task list, description, employee card with a pillow-shaped face, photo, department head’s quote in a white box), confetti on both sides of the panel. For role and department intros and job intro pages

notes: Original artwork such as cut-out product photos, characters, speech bubbles and hand drawings is redrawn at the same spot and size as SVG snack bags, boxes, bars, mascots and speech bubbles, while photos of people and landscapes are wf-img slots describing what the photo shows. Pack colours (--site-pack-*) and job panel colours (--job-*) are content colours, so they do not change with the skin
The hero copy line is handwritten image lettering in the original, so it was replaced with Gaegu bold text (--kf-font-hand) at the same size and flow (Swiper 15s · desktop 18s)

The paper speckle on the panel pattern (original noise image) is approximated with a two-layer dot gradient. The cookie-shaped person card background (original biscuit image) uses a rounded-notch mask. The number paper (original kraft paper border-image) uses a color fill and a tilt.
