The photo behind the menu overlay (original bg_menu) and the group section background photo are wf-img slots, and the group diagram is an SVG circle diagram instead of the original image
Timeline strip cell image size is an approximation matched by eye, since the original image’s intrinsic size is not in the CSS

Career stories, employee interview details (employee stories opened in a modal, career line drawing), roundtable, survey, benefits and growth environment pages were not recorded, so they were not built — their cards and menu links go to the same sections on the home page (#people·#environment) or to the job role pages. Entry and external application links go to the new graduate recruitment guidelines (#info)
The recruitment guidelines table and FAQ follow the original row counts (table 9 rows, 15 questions in four groups), and the two hiring record tables were shortened to the same form

The menu button (stamp shape) is a hover where the original swaps two images, so with a same-shape mask only the red panel is shrunk to 94% to thicken the white border. The confetti strip over the phone job panel (original artwork) is approximated with CSS circles and triangles

index hero flowing copy line (.ns-kv__copy, 6 clones) — the original is kana handwriting artwork text, Korean kept. The actual font is the Korean handwriting face Gaegu (--kf-font-hand), so the feel matches, and latin-slots reads the fallback var(--kf-font-display) to size it

Logo characters (.ns-logo__mark b), the Japanese line of the section title (.ns-title__jp) and menu group names are kanji and kana in the original — Korean kept. Section names, card labels and the page-header English line (.ns-title__en · .ns-card__label · .-en) were English from the start, so there was nothing to change

title: Gray mist scene with birds flying across, for a support project site
good_for: Long single pages for corporate support or investment projects, research institutes and foundations, with news and facility subpages.

pages.use: Project home — a hero where two birds fly in and become the logo, news drag slider, manifesto, about diagram · areas · strengths, facility photos, member cards (overlapping windows), two logo cells, Q&A, table, resources, contact · flowing GET IN TOUCH. Move between sections with the fixed left table of contents
News list — thumbnail on the left, title and date on one line each on the right, title underline grows from the right, and a bordered pill ”View more” at the bottom. For press or event news lists
Single news item — bold long title, date · category, underlined link body, ”Back to list” in a fixed left column. For press release · notice detail
Facility About — full-width building photo, intro text, underlined subheading, three-column space photo list. For research facility, office and space guides

notes: The original background mixes two cloud videos, gray and color (shine-color/gray.mp4), with a shader — to avoid using video files, the two layers fed into the same mixing formula (0.5/cos(cos(frame)) − distance×uMotion) are drawn as fbm noise clouds. Cloud shape and flow speed differ from the video.

The logo, title bird and background bird are our own bird drawing (a two-piece path: body feathers + wing bend) instead of the original images (webp, svg). The shader wing fold (rotation.x), flight curve and values follow the original.

The original sub-pages have no Hero English lettering graphic, so fetching the color orbs and the new background image never finishes and only fog shows — the copy also shows no orbs or fresh backgrounds on sub-pages.
The facility photo slot has only one slide in the original too (only a Splide version exists), so it is a single photo without Splide.
The video overlay player is not used and only a video placeholder is kept — only the dark panel lifting effect follows the original.
The mobile global menu and the sub-page fixed ”Back to list” button (t-navigationFixedToList) are placed as a pill below the article (ns-article__btn) instead of in a button slot.

Pill button text (.ns-pill__label — View news list · Facility overview · View resource list · To the Brand website · Back to news list), Q&A button (.ns-qa__btn-label View answer), and the article’s left-side ”Back to list” (.ns-fixnav__back) — the original has kana button text (View the news list · Facility overview · View the resource list · To the Brand website · View answer · To the news list), kept in Korean. Falling back from Montserrat to the Korean sans Noto Sans KR gives the same feel as the original (Montserrat followed by a Japanese sans).

Category next to the News date (.ns-row__cats·.ns-article__cats ‹Category›) — the original inserts CMS category names (news_tax) via JS, so the archived copy has no text. Since the categories are Japanese, like the title prefix 【Startup News】, it was judged to keep the placeholder in Korean

Section names · menu · hero big text · logo letters · tags (.ns-title__label · .ns-menu__label · .ns-mv__line · .ns-logo__type · .ns-tags) were English from the first build, so there was nothing to change

title: Isometric yard art, giant wordmark, lime pickup cards and layered round panels
good_for: Outdoor living brands such as garden, camping or interior that combine magazine content and shopping in one site, including top page, gallery, about, news, case list and careers.

pages.use: Brand home page — loading curtain, a giant wordmark over an isometric yard illustration (shrinks to 164px on scroll), a PICK UP band that loops every 16s, lime pickup cards in a slick carousel, campaign banners, a beige HOT! band with popular posts shaped like n·i·w·a, a tag panel with a hand-drawn illustration that tilts then settles, a dark panel with endless flowing photo rows, tea, and recommended and new products. For a lifestyle brand magazine + shopping landing

Photo collection — a tag picker straddling the top edge of a dark rounded panel, a four-column square photo grid, an enlarged view that opens on click and pages with slick over a blurred overlay (text, product link, tags), and pagination. For lookbook or gallery pages (the original /gallery/page/2 has the same shape)

Brand About — an isometric island floating on water with six drifting clouds, ABOUT outline text, wordmark, copy and a down arrow, then a gray-panel product finder (2×2 products) and a white-panel article finder (2×2 articles) in zigzag. For brand About and service About
Notice list — category picker straddling the top line of a 1px panel with rounded top, rows divided by dotted lines (category pill, date, title, ⊕ icon). For notice and press lists

Case article list — rounded gray panel with two pickers for category and tag, four-column article cards (mint category pill), pagination, tag cloud, and most-read articles on a beige panel. For magazine · case study · blog lists
Careers — pink circle head and a one-line hiring status, empty below with a hand-drawn footer illustration overlapping. For a careers page with no openings

notes: The original graphics (the isometric yard Hero graphic, one of four chosen by cookie, the island graphic, hand-drawn gardener, skateboard kid, bicycle, car and chair, and the loading graphic) are in shared.js’s <symbol> Redrawn in the same spots and composition with groups (four people, two seated people, potted plant, palm, chair, dining table, tent, striped mat, hammock, car, bicycle, skateboard, cactus, dog, flower bed, cloud, lantern) and isometric box calculations. The original’s cookie behavior that picks one of four pictures on each visit was dropped because there is only one picture.
The wordmark (Brand) and initial marks (n/c) are English placeholders ”wordmark” and ”a/b” (Jost 600). The ”🔥HOT!” graphic band was rebuilt as a text band (HOT! + a round dot instead of the flame).

The n·i·w·a letter-shaped masks and vermilion shadow plates on the popular-post photos are redrawn at the same size (282) as rounded-cell shapes (arch notch, narrow cell, two notches, round hole) instead of the original SVG.

Colors: mint #03ffc5 · vermilion #e65a41 · lime shadow #cbd64e come from --kf-accent, and the raised-bed shadow and vertical text cell come from --kf-raised via oklch(from …) (shared.css --site-*). The hand-drawn tree, grass, sky and skin tones are also made from the Skin.

The original init all runs after window load, so the loading curtain (.32s after .48s), the hero sequence (art 1.04s .8s · 13s shrink · card 1.6s · banner 1.84s) and the pickup slick were also set to run after load.

Part name incident: I first built the popular-post bounce part as ‹squash-pop-in› and overwrote the same-named part folder that another student had already made. fx.json was restored as is from the record left in library/catalog/fx.json. fx.js, fx.css and demo.html were rebuilt from the recorded values (flower .6s 1.3x overshoot, leaf .7s horizontal-vertical squash, rootMargin -50% 0px) and from the flower-boyoyon and leaf-boing keyframes in the source site’s shared.css (lint and fx-check 0). They may not match the original files character for character, so that student or the lead should check once. My part was moved to bounce-thumb-pop.
Swapping theme.css for another skin and capturing it was not done — only library-lint was checked: 0 colors, 0 fonts, 0 variables outside the skin.

Phone (390) screens carry the original values (rules under 749) only for the main sections. Hero · popular posts · tags · gallery · products · subpage heads are matched. The phone header row, which uses only a drawer instead of a mega menu, keeps a single MENU like the original. Phone details (about-island position · case card text size) should be compared against the original once more by the next person.

title: Design studio WebGL stage with diagonal pillars piercing the headline
good_for: Design and branding studio homepages with alternating white and black sections and service, program and case detail pages sharing one template.

pages.use: Studio home — large title over slanted pillars (WebGL) on a curved grid floor, client logo strip, showreel shrinking into the title box, number row, dark point-cloud section, band, six Work cells, aurora-mountain Method section, four News cells, testimonial slider, large horizontally pushed line. For agency homes
Work list — black background with large title, 6 case cells in 2 columns, pill tabs by type (tap to open a picker list), 4-column cards, aurora section. For portfolio lists
All services — four service cells (photo + /name + description)·client logo strip·4-column Work·flowing number strip·four aurora-text program cards·aurora section. For service list pages

Service detail — left label, large-title header, overlay photo, approach text, ‘text + list of what you can do + image’ alternating four times, quote, horizontally sliding row with three cases, closing contact, black ‘See more’ card. For service and product detail pages

Program (bundle product) detail — same detail header, aurora big-text cover, ”Right for you when” row table, four steps (aurora glow panel + list), quote, two cases, black ”More programs”. For services and course intros with steps

Single case — detail header · cover video · starting point · fact table (program · industry · stage · market) · problem · two photos · wide photo · quote · result · black dot-cloud ”What changed” numbers and next case. For Work case detail
Careers: large black dot-cloud title, photo strip, five value cards, gray panel with ten ritual cells (photo + /name), expandable open-position rows, closing. For studio culture and careers pages.

notes: The WebGL stages (Hero wire · dark section points · method section aurora) were built in three from the original scene settings (camera fov 60/58/52 · height · distance · turns .35 · mouse .13rad · 26 · grid density 48 · rings 35/150/-84 · wave 290/s · entrance .55s stagger .16 · 900 pillars falling). Redo (2026-11-17): after reading the original engine settings, we added to aurora a water plane (mirror camera reflection once every two frames · ripple .6 · blur .46 · reflectivity .55 · opacity .3 · edge .09/1.6), and to points and aurora the original post-process bloom (threshold .82 · softness .25 · 6 mips, 4 on phones · radius .7 · intensity .85) and vignette (.4/.5) using our own shaders (wire has no bloom, as in the original). Terrain shape is a height map image in the original (an original asset), so we use our own noise ridges and 40k points — left as is under the rule of not using original assets

The logo is, like the original, two dotlottie-web 0.80.0 canvases (normal panel + tail panel, one set per header skin, four in all). Using timings read out of the original .lottie (450×88 · 29.97fps · 205.28 frames, 6.85s loop, the dot pops up at .57s and settles at .4s, word strip 3.5s cubic ease · stops at 3s), our own lottie is built in JS — the letters are image layers drawn in the skin’s title typeface. The link clip (29.44%) opens immediately on hover and closes all at once 300ms after the pointer leaves (0s transition · 300ms delay), and the tail panel appears and goes at .3s. Opened via file:// the wasm can’t be fetched, so the DOM wordmark stays as it is

The program detail (product-discovery) uses the same detail frame as the branding detail (hero workDetail, cover, image_text, quote), so both are bundled in one offer.css and only the section composition differs. The original aurora photos on the step cards (/needs, /scope) are drawn as CSS light panels

The video cards in the dark section (Vimeo background playback) are photo placeholders in the same position and ratio — only the showreel keeps the Play glass cursor and the full-screen expand. The menu drawer was rebuilt from the original code (full-screen translucent panel · right-side clip 1.1s · list 50%→0 .5s · each row staggered 300+75ms over 1s · number/name/one-line description hover · bottom row of mail·(more) list, header button toggles Menu↔Close)

The letter-roll button is written as 1.2s in the original CSS but measures about .6s per letter, so it was matched to .6s (.04s stagger). The button text became English placeholder copy, so the stagger total (letter count × .04s) is now close to the original letter count.

Font backfill (2026-11-08 · 11-17): the original text is all DM Sans Latin, so in addition to 27 heading-font spots, the JS logo and the footer pledge, the second pass also switched sentence-style section titles (t-h2), one-line titles (t-h3), large quotes (t-h2), header menu, drawer menu, footer columns, card name lines (client·person·place names), buttons, chips, picker tabs, and client/award logo slots to English placeholder text. Body sentences, descriptions, small labels (t-lxs·t-lsm), list items, number captions and body-size reviews (t-bmd) stay Korean per the README

The wordmark placeholder text is the two letters ‹sn› (data-label ‹two or three lowercase letters›, original usually ‹/nk›) — the header lottie, the drawer-less DOM fallback and the big footer mark all use the same text.

Recruiting. Spotlight headers MESSAGE, JOB INFO and OFFICE, centered greeting, job descriptions alternating left and right with a character and curved arrow, office photo
Single work — category·title·key visual, one-line intro·synopsis and staff in charge (blue panel on phone), and a cast·staff·organizer panel over a darkened key visual

notes: The original first page’s ON AIR (live now) section and the dot-resolving photo (PixelateAnimeImage) did not appear in the original at recording time (is_exist_featured false), so they were not built — to add them, make a part that peels back three canvas layers (90·110·130px dots) at .25s intervals

The side tickers are a Vue component in the original (vue-dynamic-marquee) that cannot be carried over as a library, so the same behavior (100px per second, entering from outside the right edge, repeating with a 10px gap, pausing on hover) was rebuilt

/  Lottie files are our own drawings with the same pane size · frames · keyframe timing as the original (lottie/make.cjs). The original swaps drawings for the menu · transition icons, so ours also swaps poses every 15 frames

index What We Do, two section titles with dotted words (‹make› · ‹deliver›, in the body lines and the t-big inside the graphic) — the original uses kana and kanji titles (つくる · 届ける), Hangul kept. The dot pairing is already set up with Galmuri (PixelMplus ↔ Hangul dot font)

The original has only two typefaces, a Japanese gothic and a pixel font, so there is no separate Latin-only font slot. English pixel text such as SCROLL · LOADING · MESSAGE · what we do was English from the start.

title: Gray single page with blur-fading glass photos and vertical text paragraphs
good_for: Small maker brands showing glassware, vessels or crafts one object at a time, with philosophy, materials, product list, about and news.

pages.use: One-page small manufacturing brand — left vertical header bar and translucent menu panel, Hero with blur-transition Ken Burns photo slideshow, vertical-writing About with scattered square photos, left-right staggered Ideas and Materials, screen-fixed background band, eight products staggered in two rows, letter-style About us, article list and photo grid, photo Footer

notes: The original is a single page — subpage 1 in pages.json is index.html itself (the same screen), so it was not built separately. Product, article and photo links go out to an external store, a blog and social media in the original, so they were turned into same-page anchors.

jQuery uses 1.12.4 from _vendor (same 1.x) instead of the original 1.11.3. Vegas is the same 2.6.0, placed in _vendor/vegas@2.6.0 (MIT, the package has no LICENSE file, so the MIT wording from the README was moved into LICENSE). jquery.easing·instafeed·snapwidget are not used for visible motion, so they aren’t included.

Scroll reveals (blurTrigger · fadeUpTrigger · fadeInTrigger) were moved into a single blur-focus-in part. The original jQuery rewinds when the element leaves below the screen and turns on again on re-entry, while the part fires only once (judgment call).

The social feed block is a snapwidget iframe in the original, so it is a placeholder in the same 4-column square grid. The note post list is drawn from an RSS feed in the original, so four rows of the same shape were written in advance.

The brand table (diagonally striped panel) and the eight glass drawings were redrawn as our own SVG at the same position and size, and the Hero table lighting up one row group at a time (original 1.5s · 2.1~2.7s 1s ease-in) is reduced to three row groups. The original logo art and photos are not used.

Fonts: Montserrat and Shippori Mincho are the same free fonts, Korean falls back to Noto Serif KR. The paid gothic slot is Noto Sans KR. English section names, menus and product names are English placeholders.

The News list arrow is drawn as three skin-colored gradient layers (shaft · two chevron strokes) instead of the original white PNG, and like the original it shifts background-position by 5px over .5s ease. The product round button chevron is a skin-colored mask (::after).

title: Dotted-grid product site whose background shifts between ink, blue-gray and lavender
good_for: B2B software, cloud and data product sites with feature layers, platform accordion, before/after comparison, customer stories, blog and careers.

Blog list — lilac featured post card, drag slider rows by category, all-posts grid with filters and page numbers, press row. For company blog and News lists

The five 3D layer renders beside the platform accordion are drawn as one SVG isometric layer stack, and only the current item’s layer is painted in the accent color. Pinned · one screen height per item · 1s scroll on name press are as in the original.

Dither photo (dither-duotone-reveal): the original draws a plate per photo on one page-fixed canvas, while the part draws with a single WebGL context and copies to a 2D canvas per photo. Photo slots are filled with grayscale brightness drawings (sphere, star flower, ring, human silhouette) drawn on canvas. Real photos would be stamped with the same stipple.

Blog hero image, card images and article body images are dark product-screen placeholders (the label says what to put in).

The large mobile menu (t3) is English, while the header horizontal menu, footer column names, card titles (t6) and monospaced text are body font slots so they stay Korean.

title: Studio site where the cursor melts a white panel like fluid around a wordmark
good_for: Creative studio and agency portfolios that make a first impression with one large logo.

pages.use: Studio home page: a loader with numbers that turn into objects, a hero where the mouse melts a giant white-panel wordmark like fluid to reveal the video behind, a shrinking showreel, a zigzag work list where WORKS letters cross over, a pinned video that shrinks into a gallery photo, object push, letter scatter, FAQ, and a big wordmark Footer.
Work list — big title and year, the same zigzag cells as the first page (photos opening from a corner · pill cursor). For the full portfolio list

One Work — big name and number, an intro with date and field that sticks and follows, two-column concept, photo groups of full and half cells (opening from the corner), a closing button, and at the very bottom, rolling further fills a line and the title flies to the next work’s slot. For case detail pages.

A single article (a long answer to a frequently asked question) — big question title, short answer and photo, three subheading bodies · quote, a one-sentence quote over a dark photo, FAQ · footer. For blog and Q&A answer articles

About the studio — full-bleed photo hero, who and what, six service cells (pill cursor), how we work, past partners, showreel and awards list, client quotes, team intro, FAQ and footer. For company or studio About pages.

notes: Fluid mask: the original curl and vorticity steps are left out because the original setting has curlStrength 0, so the result is the same. The rest (splat, advection, divergence, 20 pressure iterations, gradient subtract, edge smoothstep) is rewritten with the original values. The letters baked into the plane are placeholder glyphs (Archivo Black) instead of the original logo artwork.

In the loader and object section, the original objects are cut-out 3D object photos (balloon · foil · candy) — redrawn as black-and-white single-color SVG illustrations at the same position and size (data-label says which photo it is). Loader order · spacing (100~500ms sine curve) · number 100→000 · curtain lift use the original values

The showroom video sound switch is built down to the knob and the volume fades (on .35s, 1.4s after leaving the section then down over 1.6s), but the placeholder video has no sound. Instead of the original frame art (cadre), a single faint border line

Page transitions: on http it uses the same Taxi 1.9.1 as the original (old screen fades out in .5s → new screen overlaps and fades in in .5s, and the next work is a flip where the title·number fly over). On file:// the next page cannot be fetched, so it is imitated with the same values (.5s power2.inOut out → navigate → .5s in, and for the flip the title flies over for 1.2s and then navigates).

Work detail has only one recorded page (Utopia), so Next Work points to the same detail.html?w=Cycles by number and only the title · number change. Videos hung over part of the photo slots in the original detail (mp4 address in alt) are kept only as photo placeholders

Phone (991 and below): as in the original, the WORKS text Flip, showreel shrink and gallery pinning are turned off, and wide-screen-only motion is not applied. The original layout of the phone menu panel has no recording, so it was built from the archived DOM (.menu_wrapper: four links, two buttons, one line below)

In the original FAQ, each ”Read more” goes to its own question post, but only one post was recorded, so all of them link to article.html. The original Studio’s ”Services” modal, ”method” and ”awards” pages were not recorded, so they link to the About and article pages.

title: Device-tier entry gate then thousands of posters flowing through a Voronoi lens
good_for: Exploratory landing screens, exhibitions and archives that spread many images across one screen to browse with a cursor and pick one.

pages.use: A single-piece work — two-step entry gate (ellipsized title · device tier · view mode · cell count · Continue), a full-screen grid of small poster cells (only the central fisheye lens keeps original color, the outside is grayscale with ripples, the cursor pushes the grid, wheel up or press opens a large lens and the chosen film panel), a lens name tag, corner buttons and an about dialog. For Hero screens of exhibitions or archives where you browse many images and pick one

notes: The original is a single page (pages: [] in pages.json).

The original voroforce (WebGL2, worker, SharedArrayBuffer, jump flooding) is code unique to that site and the repository has no license, so it was not used. The same numbers (force alpha .2 · damping .7 · grid .8 · push .3, view max 10 · follow .15 · scale 1~1.5, lens .5 · ripple 30/2/.02) were measured and rewritten as our own shader (part voro-tile-field). Cells are one set of 240×150 (30k, 6 thousand cells) repeated endlessly. The original film count picker (10k–100k) only picks and does not change the cell count.
Poster slots are seed-picked color and shape drawings. To use real posters, switch the shader’s poster() to read an image bundle (atlas). The original film materials and posters were not used.

The original view modes (Minimal, Depth, Chaos, Contours) have only the picker, and all draw the same panel. Favorites list, settings panel, light view and the low FPS notice are not built (button spots only).
The original emojis (potato, blank face, arm) were replaced with small SVG icons in the same spots (no-emoji rule).

The original entry gate has two steps (device tier, then view mode and film count). The copy keeps two steps and, after the second Continue, runs about 2.6s of loading (title and keyboard hints), then the gate lifts over .7s, then the large-cell intro (3.2s zoom-out), then the lens in 1s. The intro length was measured by eye from the original recording (16 shots at 0.5s intervals).

The amount the plate is pushed by the cursor (gain .3 world px / screen px) is a judgment value tuned by recording, since the number could not be found in the original. In the original, when the cursor stops the plate stops, and a different film comes under the lens by the distance moved.
On wheel = Picker view (lens 1.9x · cinema panel), wheel down · press · Esc = Going back follows the original recording. Movie titles, years and scores are placeholders picked by cell seed.

title: Photo hero and stacking cards for a dental clinic homepage
good_for: Homepages and treatment detail pages for clinics, dentists and beauty salons with service lists, staff, reviews and booking.

pages.use: Hospital home — photo hero with big title, indented intro sentence, four treatment cards (fill darkly on hover), four Why Us cards stacking on scroll, review grid, medical staff slider, photo closing, three-step booking window. For hospital, clinic or service business homes

A single treatment (service): a dark hero with two circles that twist with the cursor, a vertical photo in the center with three dotted-circle explanations on each side, five step cards, reviews, and a closing. For treatment, procedure and service detail pages.

notes: The original card mentions lottie, but neither of the two pages plays any Lottie (the line on the first screen of the clinic detail is two CSS circle borders plus a cursor parallax script) — Lottie is not included.

Fonts: Neue Haas Grotesk Display (paid) → Inter Tight 500, Neue Montreal (paid) → Inter, and Playfair Display italic is the same free font. Korean pairings are Noto Sans KR · Noto Serif KR. The large sentences in About and Staff are Korean placeholders, so line counts differ slightly from the English original.

The care card expand: description slide down and fold use GSAP height 0↔auto instead of the original jQuery slideDown(350)·slideUp(300) (sine.inOut, same as jQuery swing — down .35s, fold .41s to match the 317ms measured in the original, which shrinks margins too). Of the original twelve cells, the three empty slots (2nd·7th·9th) are left empty.
All photo slots are gray panels with a data-label (subject · light · composition) — the Hero and closing are a full-screen warm portrait close-up slot, like the original.

title: Fluorescent green giant wordmark, marker text and splitting circle stage
good_for: Advertising and marketing agencies, AI and data service companies, and bold single-color B2B sites with case and column collections.

pages.use: Company first page — a compressed wordmark filling the screen with a one-line marker, a black band statement (parallax · marker), a 450vh pinned circle stage (circle → splits into Plan A·B → three rings around a big circle at the screen bottom · dotted outline · flowing background big text), CASE with two case cards, a logo marquee and a big-line link, service cards (stacking on the left · tall cards on the right), two big activity banners and a Splide card row, a 3D laptop free-analysis stage, and a contact band that spreads out on hover. For agency and B2B service landing pages

Service intro — screen-filling giant headline with a ↓ anchor row, black business card (large condensed name, marker sentence), horizontal service card row, two other cards, free trial stage, and a contact band that spreads on hover. For business and service list pages

Case interview list — a giant title and three rows of filter chips for industry, purpose and service, 4-column interview cards on a black panel (photo, client logo, tag), PREV, page numbers, NEXT, a free trial stage, and a contact band that spreads on hover. For a client case list

Column list — giant title and anchor row, three groups (ranking, reading, interviews) in a 4-column card grid (green border), VIEW MORE, free trial stage, a contact band that spreads on interaction. For blog, column or resource listings

Company About — giant title and anchor row, company overview table, executive photo cards (name·title·bio), map and map link, free trial stage, contact band that spreads on hover. For company overview and executive intro

Single Work interview — black band overlapping a giant title holding photo and client logo, share buttons, white article panel (pinned section index on the left, title, tags, three marker highlights, body, video, photos), other Work cards, free trial stage, Contact band that spreads on hover. For client interviews and Work details

notes: The free analysis laptop uses our own shapes with the same silhouette (base 2.8×2.0 · lid 1.65, values matched to the original screen’s measured front edge 640px · top edge 400px · hinge height) and two canvas-drawn dashboards instead of the original OBJ model and photo textures — the model file is an original asset, so it is not used. Camera (fov 45 · z 4.5) · light (ambient 1 · directional .1) · one full turn (1.6s power2.inOut) · 0.8s screen swap are the original values

The wordmark and condensed headings use Anton instead of the paid gazzetta, and English heads use Archivo instead of the paid neue-haas-grotesk-display — letter widths differ, so the wordmark is stretched vertically to fit its box (1400×520) and its strokes are a bit heavier than the original

Case filtering in the original is Finsweet Attributes v2 (fs-list). This build uses a loader that fetches feature modules separately from a CDN at runtime and cannot be bundled as a single _vendor file, so the same rules (OR within a row · AND between rows · All clears that row) were rewritten in sub.js. The vanishing effect length when filtered out could not be measured, so items are hidden immediately
Page numbers, map and video are placeholders only (original: Webflow CMS pagination, map iframe, video iframe). The original cookies, chat widget and analytics are not built

The circle stage phone layout (three rings standing vertically along the left edge of a large circle centered off the right side of the screen) carries over the original phone CSS values, but it could not be measured side by side with the original phone screen — the original phone rem is width/600 (/393 at 480 and below) while this board uses a single /390, so sizes differ near 600 width.

title: Gradient headline wiped in over a gray duplicate for a B2B payment service
good_for: Sales-oriented B2B SaaS, payment and finance service sites with feature blocks, problem-to-solution flows, pricing figures, case studies, news and FAQ.

pages.use: Service home page — wiping large heading, floating laptop and six feature cells, client logo strip, trust-number infographic, three pain points → solution flow diagram, resources panel, How-to-use · About · Pricing sections, adopting-company strip and case-study panel

Service intro — hero image, five line-art cells for what is done, 100% guarantee number panel, two strengths with big numbers, competitor comparison table, four start steps. For the What we do page of an enterprise service

Case list — header image, case-book button, challenge/sales method picker panel (pill tags), three rows of photo cards, pagination. ?tag=Opening with 0-0 leaves the picker panel open, like the original per-task list (case_tag)
News list — letter head with date and category / bold title rows, pagination. For press release and notice lists
FAQ — a + accordion row under each subheading, with a blue button note for current users in the middle. For customer support FAQ

notes: The original moves only through a CMS + jQuery·its own bundle (IntersectionObserver and CSS transition) — no open-source motion libraries (Barba·Lenis·Slick etc.) are used on these pages, so nothing was added to _vendor. Page changes are regular navigation (same as the original).

The original sub-pages split into two editions: service is the new edition (l-header · c-animation-title, once the body edition shows, it fades in .8s after .7s), while case · news · faq are the old edition (pageHeader · interactiveTitle, after document ready the edition fades .3s after .7s, the body rises from 40px below in .8s, and the footer piece enters from 200px below the screen in .35s cubic-bezier(.77,0,.175,1)). body.np-old turns on the old edition motion. They look the same so the header row and footer markup are merged into one.
The original case_tag (case list by challenge) has the same form as the case list so it is not built separately, works.html?tag=<Slot>-<Pill> Shows the selection panel in its open state.

Logos·certification marks·client logos are placeholder text (Service·Client 01·Certification mark), and laptop·office photos are gray boxes stating what to put in. Infographics·worry illustrations·workflow diagrams·document covers·line drawings were redrawn as SVG at the same position·size (the original uses image files).
Fonts: acumin-pro and two paid Japanese gothic fonts are paid, so Archivo + Noto Sans KR backs them up. The title sits in a Japanese slot in the original, so it is set in Korean.
Judgment: the FAQ, whose original type was about, is treated as a page, and case_tag, whose type was detail, as a state of works.

The original first page’s c-side-cta and vertical menu graphics are image files, so they were redrawn in HTML·SVG at the same position and size. Original links (external checkout · login) were redirected to pages within the same site.

title: Forest photo with a white animal silhouette for a wildlife nonprofit
good_for: Nonprofit, foundation and local conservation sites that show a donation request panel on every page.

pages.use: Organization home — logo Lottie loader, hero with 3 photos that change as they approach, center image · English slogan · four scattered photos intro, two white-silhouette cards, speech-bubble donation panel, four-column list of activity reports · news, blue donation band

Organization About — icon title, wide photo, vision text, two photo+text blocks (mirrored), two-way cards, address and officers table in two columns. For the About menu of nonprofits and small companies
News list — category pills (All in yellow) · eight four-column photo cards · yellow circle page numbers and a blue ”Next” pill, donation panel at the end
Job listing list — two listing cards under the title (same four-column cards as News), support panel at the end. For a recruiting menu with few openings
One news item — category band·date on the left, title on the right, wide 4:3 photo with short body·attachment link. Slot for a single press release or notice

notes: The original uses jQuery·TweenMax 1.19 (GSAP 2)·ScrollMagic (loaded but unused). Motion is ported to GSAP 3 from _shared with the same lengths and curves, and jQuery is not used. Lottie uses the same lottie-web@5.1.8 as the original, placed in _vendor.

Loader sheet curve: the original code has ease:"Linear" but TweenMax 1.19 doesn’t recognize that name and runs with the default Power1.easeOut (the measured screen does too), so it was matched to power1.out.

The loader Lottie does not use the original data.json, only the per-layer timing and curves (yellow circle 0~16f, blue circle 16~30f, wings 360° · 720°, yellow piece 49~57f, 30fps 60f) are carried over, and shared.js builds it from our own shapes. Colors read from the Skin (--kf-accent · yellow).

Yellow (--site-yellow) is derived from the accent color via oklch, and so that color transitions blend in sRGB like the original, shared.js expands it to rgb on load and re-inserts it (with an oklch end value the transition would blend in oklab and the curve would drift).

The original illustrations (bear, person, dog above About, white silhouettes on cards, support panel illustration, logo, SNS icons) were redrawn as simple shape SVGs in the same place and size — rougher than the original.
The category pills and page numbers in the news list are look only, with no filter or paging behavior (the original also links to other URLs). Most submenus and secondary menus are # placeholders.
The original has no cursor response (shader, mouse follow) (cursor-scan 0).

title: Open-book stage with illustrated people at work for a company intro
good_for: Small company or studio sites that speak through illustration, with a vertical-text statement, works list, news and contact in four pages.

pages.use: Open-book stage company intro — after a vertical-writing intro the book drops in and a character works in the hero · vertical-writing about · page-turn border · results list · fan-paper services · news · contact. For a small company home told through illustration
About — vertical-writing intro, staff grid, company overview table, contact. For small company pages
Track record list — category button filtering · load more after 12 items · contact. For a broadcast and video track record list
News list — clicking a row opens a white paper detail window over a mustard backdrop. For notices opened straight from the list

notes: Books, figures, notes and props are redrawn as SVG at the same position, size and color, but simpler than the original hand drawings since the original art files could not be used — smooth curves and a thin layer of noise instead of brush marks and paper grain, and figures drawn only as faceless blobs in a few poses.

The original drawing GIF (3 frames × 500ms, same pose with only the lines different) is reproduced at the same tempo by cycling the seed of a noise displacement filter through three values over our whole drawing — the original’s per-frame lines were hand-drawn, so ours is the same drawing wobbled within 3px
The card’s claim of a ”scroll-scrub where the book approaches in perspective” was not there when I measured the original (it only drops in once at load). Built as measured
English section titles, VIEW MORE, hand-drawn circle arrows and ink lines are image files in the original, so they were replaced with Crimson Pro text, CSS lines and new SVG

The Work page has 16 instead of the original 24 (first 12 + 4 via VIEW MORE). Category buttons only filter on screen (the original loads the next batch from a CMS — this is a placeholder with no data to fetch)
The news detail window only carries over the date and title of the pressed row, with body and image as the same placeholder. The original also has the same mustard curtain + white paper + BACK type
The original page transition is just a Nuxt view swap plus appear, so no curtain was added — normal navigation plus the same appear was used
Subpages’ original hovers were not captured separately — the header bar, footer, news row and card links are the same parts as on the first page, so comparison with the first page stands in for them
Logo and service logo (brush-script wordmark) are a redrawn sound-bar plus LOGO, a bold BR+ND serif placeholder

title: Blur clearing over a hero photo and a philosophy text written out twice
good_for: Design and branding firm homepages, quiet photo-led portfolios and type studios that showcase typeface changes.

pages.use: Company home — full first photo that sharpens from blur, philosophy text written twice, five-column vertical photo work grid, three news lines, four inspiration books. For the first screen of a quiet branding company
Work list — category nav underline follows the hand, and a 5-column vertical photo grid adds 20 more cells when it reaches the bottom. For photo-focused work lists

About the company — philosophy text, vision, six numbered values, a row of drag-to-advance WebGL photo panels, four people, what we run ourselves, company overview table, two banners. For company About sections
Services — intro to what we do, two-column work cells with names over photos, price table, arrow-linked work process, two banners. For service·pricing pages
News list — 32 news items with a grid/row view toggle that is remembered, plus page numbers. For news and blog lists
Hiring — three vertical photos overflowing to the screen edge swap in a staggered 5s crossfade, plus three workplace culture items and four works. For hiring and company culture intros

notes: Of the six recorded sub-pages, Branding (projects/category/branding) was not built since it has the same shape as the work list (a grid filtered only by category) — the category nav in works.html stands in for it. Work detail (projects/<Name>, the header photo is a WebGL effect that resolves from black-and-white .3 to color over 2s) and Our Inspirations·Contact·FAQ·Download were not recorded, so they are not built, the menu’s Inspirations goes to the inspiration section on the first page, and the rest are set to #

The original fonts BRAND Serif and BRAND Grotesk are company-only (paid), so EB Garamond and Inter stand in, and Yu Mincho and Yu Gothic are backed by Noto Serif KR and Noto Sans KR. The typeface button (typeset-toggle) switches the site-wide font variables with a single html[data-typesetting], like the original, and remembers the choice in localStorage instead of the original IndexedDB

The About section’s photo plane row passes three.js (r175) planes over an orthographic camera through Swiper (drag handling) like the original — n transparent slides are placed in Swiper to take drag and swipe, and on release the original threshold (.15) is measured directly and slideTo advances the slide (Swiper’s default 30% threshold does not advance at the original’s drag distance). The original’s virtual slides and fade matching (suppressSlideChangeEvent) are not done. The Swiper version could only be narrowed down to 11 or above (loopAddBlankSlides) from the original bundle, so vendor’s 11.2.10 is used

As in the original, the hero photo is picked by rotating through one of four per session (header letter color per photo) and resolves with the gl-unblur-intro shader — the photo draws a placeholder panel (diagonal · label) and uses it as a texture

The Barba transition runs only when opened over http (file:// cannot fetch the next page) — on file:// the same cover turns on in .25s, the document is swapped, and on the new page it turns off in .3s after a .2s delay
The Studio Playlist row links to an external playlist in the original, so only placeholder text is used

About section text length: the original text could not be saved separately (the structure record truncates long text), so it was matched to the line count of the 1440 original (vision three lines · values first item one line, the rest two lines). At 1440 each section sits at the same position as the original (document 5746px), while 390·834 are 1~1.5% shorter (the mobile vision text is a separate _mobile text written by the original, so its line count differs)

At 390 the shared footer is 31px shorter than the original (834 is 20px) — footer CSS values match the original so it seems a difference in trimmed inner line height, but it couldn’t be measured to tell.
Among the measurement checks, one cause was not isolated: only the About cell in the Work list 1440 Footer showed no hover change (the same Footer passed on the other five pages)

title: Flag curtain lifts and yellow stage lights come on for a school band
good_for: Intro sites for performing groups such as clubs, bands, theater and choirs, with about, awards, news, schedule and contact on one page plus news list and article.

pages.use: Group home page — orange paper-flag loading scrim, a fixed performance video behind the screen, intro text over a rough yellow spotlight circle that lights up with scroll plus a rough circle photo that changes every 4 seconds, slanted award records over the flags and a member illustration that changes every 2.5 seconds, two columns for News and performance schedule, marching feet, and a Contact panel that brightens as spotlights from both sides overlap. For performance groups and club homepages
News list — 24 one-line 550px list rows (date, vertical tick, title) under a slanted English section name, a hand-drawn Back to top frame, cross ornaments. For notice and activity news lists
News item — yellow title, one small 5:3 photo, two or three lines of body, a hand-drawn frame ”Back to list”. For short activity news and thank-you posts.

notes: The hero video is a placeholder with the original’s ratio (17:13, phone 7:13), length (13.6s) and 18fps (hero-17x13.mp4, hero-7x13.mp4, a scene of three blurred shapes made with ffmpeg) — the original video is not used.

The loading screen redraws the original one-pass GIF (2.68s hold + 40ms×5 + 120ms), seven frames, as seven SVG flag frames (step-wipe-loader). The way the flag peels away is an approximation traced by eye from the original frames
The Created in Studio badge at the bottom is a platform mark, so it was not built
The news list uses twenty-four rows (same Type repeated) instead of the original’s forty-odd

title: Single-orange video collage with a glancing mountain drawing for a nature park
good_for: Homepages for nature experience facilities, ranches, campsites and farms with video-rich intros, a draggable grounds map, and pricing, access and hours.

pages.use: Facility Hero page: an orange loading curtain, a Hero of three full-bleed videos inside a margin (weather and event cards), a limited-time event panel, three News rows, an About collage floating with two-layer parallax from eighteen looping videos, a mountain drawing with rolling eyes, an orange border panel and a full-bleed closing video. For facility and brand landing pages where video and photos are the stars

Facility About — square image and centered long intro, left pinned table of contents and right vertical name tag, drag-and-zoom canvas grounds map (23 pins → photo window), price box and payment methods, map embed and collapsible directions flowchart, opening days and hours. For facility info and usage info pages
News list — big title header, ten rows of date, title and arrow (the arrow slides in on hover), page numbers. For notice and news lists

Experience·shop section — hero pinned behind the screen where a blob-framed photo changes and grows on scroll to cover the screen, About · round-photo contents list, two staggered cells with two round-framed photos each, three white event cards. For introducing one experience program·store·facility
Single news item — two-line large title and date, body paragraphs indented 210px (70px between), a ‹News list› back button. For notices and event announcement posts

notes: All videos are placeholder clips (media/, with a bright band sweeping past once) with the same aspect ratio and length as the original (measured with ffprobe — hero 2000×1088 8.0·8.09·8.09s, collage 1:1 5s·10s, 670×378·590×354 5s, 16:9 6s, 930×518 10s, 2000×1372 8s, footer 214×120 2.96s). Playback follows the original: the three hero clips swap to the next one each time one ends, and the eighteen collage cells load in sequence — from 1s in, when the first frame of the previous video comes in, the next one is requested.

The background sound button uses howler 2.2.4 with the same .6s grow and shrink as the original and continued listening across sections (sessionStorage), but the sound is our placeholder (media/bgm-placeholder.mp3, 12s of brown noise) and plays as html5 audio so it sounds even when opened via file:// (the original uses Web Audio).

Yard map: the original map image (5312×4722) can’t be used, so our own image of the same size and coordinate system (pin x/1328·y/1180.5) (forest circles, meadow, paths, pond, roofs) is drawn once on a canvas with the same formulas as the original (zoom 50·100·200%, keep center, clamp to edges, pin label size r = 1·.66·.53). The 23 pin positions are as in the original, text and photos in the window are placeholders. Forest, road and water colors are map content so they’re fixed as ”not skin”
The Google map embed, payment method logo group and event notice graphic under Access are placeholder boxes describing what goes in

Menu open/close: the original uses Alpine.js (x-data isOpen) to toggle header.open — it is a plain state change with no interaction feel, so the same class toggle was written directly (drawer .3s·two lines ±30° are the original CSS as is)

The limited-time notice bar (fixed at the top, pushes the fixed header down by its height) and the event panel below the hero are temporary notices the original shows only until 2026-11-02 — kept as notice-bar · campaign-banner slots to match the current original screen, so if unused just delete the two elements and --site-notice-h.

The shop section (activity/shop) is one topic section of the 「What We Have and What We Can Do」 group in the original. It is kept as product, the recorded type, and the other topic sections of the same shape (farm · hot spring …) were not recorded, so they were not built. All the other topic links in the menu lead to this section
Fonts: Sawarabi Gothic has no Korean glyphs, so Korean falls back to a Korean gothic font. Glyphs are not as narrow as in the original, so some lines differ in length

About price values in 6 spots (0,000 won) — the source writes them as a number plus a kanji unit, like ”1,000 yen”, so the Hangul unit stays. Numbers stay in Barlow, and a Gothic font pair is added to --kf-font-latin so the ”won” unit falls to a Gothic face.

Font backfill: spots that were Latin in the original (menu · section names · wordmark · date etc.) were English from the start, so no text was changed (0 English spots). Titles and body were Japanese in the original, so they stay Korean

title: Dark telecom product set with shimmering aurora, immersive and light campaign variants
good_for: Landing pages for telecom, subscription and plan products, video-driven immersive brand sites, and campaign pages with long benefit tables, steps and FAQ.

pages.use: Product home page — aurora behind the screen (WebGL) · big photo hero and center-aligned thumbnail slider · left pinned contents + three sections with a light line under a photo collage and thin English big titles · pricing cards · awards · signup · regional map · collapsible notes · news. For a dark pricing · subscription product home

Brand panel — loader bar → ink-bleed opening → each section scrolls separately (Lenis), and scrolling further at the end melts the background into vertical stripes before the next section. Blur-to-clear text, lineup, product section, story cards. For brand statements and immersive About

Campaign landing (light panel) — top benefits band, perk selection tabs, large banner, product cards, two navy sign-up columns, two-layer tab payment table, other perks slider, numbered steps, regional table, FAQ, notes, sitemap. For perk and pricing campaign pages

notes: The card address (brand.example/mansion/status/) redirects to the home page of Brand fiber (www.brand.example/), so that home page was built as the index

The aurora behind the screen is an aurora-veil part rewritten with our own noise shader from the values of the original aurora-gl (amplitude 1 · center .2 · blur .5 · color band .04/s · half resolution · film 40%) — the noise function differs, so the curtain shape has the same feel but is not the same picture
The hero auto-advance interval couldn’t be read from the original bundle (l-swiper), so it is set to 5 seconds (transition speed 300ms · centered · loop are values that were read)

Brand edition: the section videos (monochrome person, purple silk, lineup orb) reuse one gray placeholder video in the same slot, and the skin’s purple tint is layered over the product sections with CSS. The melt transition blends two scenes like the original, but the scene images are canvas drawings baked per section in the skin color rather than video frames

Campaign page: the original uses an older design system, so it is painted with the opposite stage of the same skin (--kf-contrast-*) plus navy and red (--site-navy · --kf-danger). The large banner, application screen captures and perk card art are placeholders. Only the first tab of the payment table (Single / 39 units or fewer · Brand Fiber H) is filled in, the other tabs are same-shape placeholders

The rainbow glow on the hero apply button (the original looping video aurora-btn.mp4) was replaced with CSS in which a skin-color gradient flows over 6s instead of a video — it is the button background, so a placeholder video would turn the button gray

The original typeface SST (brand-exclusive) is backed by Inter 200 (thin English headings) and Pretendard. The swiper build inside the original bundle could not be isolated, so swiper@12.2.0 from _vendor is used, and Lenis is 1.3.25, the same as the original

Brand page interaction: the liquid cursor (dot lerp .3 · ring 118px · disc .4s · gooey filter 11/26) is the goo-liquid-cursor part. Contents proximity (within 200px left · 48px up and down, line scales .25→1x by smoothstep, nearest name opens instantly) is built in about.js. The original effect that shakes letters word by word into place when the contents and section names change (.p-brand__char) was not built
/  about lineup · product section logos Brand Fiber · Brand Mobile — the original uses kanji · kana tails, Korean kept · title font Inter pairs with Pretendard (gothic)
Total amount in the campaign payment table (such as ”4,530 won (max)”) — the original is number + yen, won kept

title: Hero photo rising through a wavy edge with vertical-text product rows
good_for: Cosmetics and beauty brand homepages, ingredient-heavy product pages and small online shops.

pages.use: Brand home — a 350vh pinned first photo revealed through a WebGL wave boundary, a vertical message that lights up letter by letter, a scattered-photo parallax About, product rows with circles that draw in (vertical one-liners), horizontal expert Q&A cards, review fade, big photo band, horizontal News row, FAQ, flowing photo band. For mood-driven beauty and lifestyle brand landings

Brand and ingredient intro. A question-style head with a circle being drawn, a vertical video card and expert intro, three answers unfolding from question index cards (ingredient chips, diagram), a big photo, four features, two how-to-use steps, a product row, reviews and an FAQ. For intro pages that explain ingredients and technology at length.

Product list — a big English title with a circle being drawn, and below it repeated product rows, each with a vertical photo, name, price, description and a vertical-writing one-liner. For shops with only a few products.

News list — ALL and NEWS filters that stick and follow on the left, rows on the right with a vertical banner beside each title. For announcement and event news lists (tag-filtered lists use this same single page)

notes: The first photo is a fresh rewrite in our own shader of the formulas measured from the original (sine-wave UV wobble · blurred sine edge · u_mix 0→1.2 over 2.2s · wave 2.8s). Instead of a photo, it bakes a placeholder picture drawn on a canvas (bright curtained window · figure mass · wire X · label, fills from Skin variables) into a texture — to use a real photo, replace paintPlaceholder in index.js with an image load.

Wordmark, vertical catch copy and vertical About heading use uppercase BRAND and vertical-writing Korean placeholder text instead of the original SVG letters — they appear with the same values per letter and per line, not per stroke (path)

Recording 4 (News NEWS tag list) has the same type as the news list in 3, so it was not built separately — the left filter in news.html filters by tag within the same page (opens directly with news.html#news). The original reopens the page at /tagged/news

Eleven video slots (About scattered videos 5:6 at 3.6 · 4.32 · 5.96s, Q&A card · answer 13:10 at 5 · 5 · 6s, About video thumbnail 9:16 at 6.88s) use placeholder videos (media/*.mp4) with the same ratio and length as the original, hooked up with the same playback behavior — when half visible, they rise at brightness 1.4 · blur 10px over .8s and play .4s later, and pause when leaving view (the thumbnail plays when visible). The picture inside the video is a placeholder of circling light blobs

In the About page’s expanded answers, the illustrations (two roles·three steps·cell diagram) and the two how-to-use figures are redrawn as simple SVGs in the same spots — fewer props than the original illustrations.

The original body typeface ten-mincho-text (paid) was substituted with Zen Old Mincho, and Korean text with Nanum Myeongjo · Noto Sans KR. The English spots the original set in Lato (hero two lines · menu · section names · buttons · footer) are left as English placeholders so Lato shows as is
Unbuilt pages such as Buying Guide, Contact, Account and Cart link to # (FAQ goes to the first page FAQ)

Vertical catch, vertical About title, big question title and card questions — the original uses kana and kanji titles, Korean kept · the pair for the title font Zen Old Mincho is Nanum Myeongjo (serif)

product.html: the original (/collections/products) couldn’t be fetched during the font backfill because of rate limits, so from the header link ‹Products› in the original and the English class (nu-en-disp) it was judged a Latin title and set as English ‹Products›

title: Portrait window grows into the screen with one color per chapter
good_for: Welcome or commemorative pages for a new conductor, leader or author that cover a person's journey, philosophy and upcoming dates in one long story.

pages.use: A long welcome-story page for a person — a yellow panel whose center portrait window becomes the full screen on the first wheel as the opening section · sky-blue video panel · two-line name that splits apart · story paragraphs · drag-to-advance timeline · two words rushing in from both sides · cutout between quotation marks · accordion list · pink video grid · teal schedule table. For person intro and inauguration commemoration pages.
Organization About article page — big title on a gray header band, 65%-wide value subheadings and body on a white panel, three-column photo tiles. For long intros on culture, values and ethics
Document list — big title and intro text, dark gray bands with season titles and rows of date, title and file size. For performance notes, press releases and archive lists

Performance calendar — yellow notice strip · search field · performance rows per date group (pink line on hover) · small calendar stuck to the right · discount code · collapsible filter. For schedule and booking lists

notes: Eleven video slots (sky-blue panel, story, philosophy, pink grid, accordion list) autoplay, loop and stay muted like the original <video> and its content is media/loop-16x9.mp4 · loop-4x5.mp4 (6-second placeholders of flowing gray gradients, made with ffmpeg) — just swap in your own photos and videos. The original play/pause button (media-chrome) is kept only as a mark at the bottom right.

Typeface: the original title font (Control Compressed) is paid, so Anton is used (Korean pair Black Han Sans). Because the original title is English, Anton title, name and button slots are kept as English placeholders and data-label notes what to put in — the Hero title is also restored to the original size min(18vw, 36cqh). Fit text (FitText) re-measures when the font subset loads late

Among the serif (Newsreader) slots, title and name lines (about subheads, tile titles, calendar performance names, expanding-list subtitles) are in English, while body text, quotes, summaries and description paragraphs are kept in Korean per the README (the Newsreader ↔ Noto Serif KR pair is already loaded). The 47 lines remaining in latin-slots are these paragraphs

Inter (body sans) spots — small section head labels, timeline subheads, header menu, drawer, performance table names, calendar times, places, buttons — fall naturally to the paired Korean sans, so they were left in Korean.

The first page turn uses the original bundle values as they are (on enter .63s stagger · window 1.76s expo.out · portrait 1.76s quint.out, turn 1.2s · 1.4s quint.inOut · 20° · welcome text 1s expo.out after .77s). Instead of the original’s stage/sizer swapping, the portrait stays inside the window and only the plate height (portrait height + 18% of width) grows. The next sky-blue plate still rises overlapping by 40% of the width, same as the original.

The teal section title’s last word rolling up to change every 1.7s is a guess from looking at the original screen (HEAR. FEEL…) (how: guess). The text-cycling values for this section could not be found in the original bundle.

The three subpages (about, list, calendar) use the original main site’s shared frame (baseplate), so they have almost no motion. Only the list row hover, the calendar row pink line and the filter fold were carried over. Actual calendar date calculation and filter behavior are not implemented (looks only).

The menu drawer, search overlay and cookie bar were rebuilt with the same values as the original main site — drawer width 0 → 100vw (max 640) .8s ease-in-out, left bar hover 64 → 74px .25s, circle .25s (the light version on subpages .3s), donate button 0s, cookie bar slides down 57.56px in .48s ease when closed. The search overlay does not actually search.
Icons are drawn as strokes, so the original’s fill color change is captured in the copy as a stroke color change of the same .25s.

title: Video hero with a center band and navy two-tone cards for a clinic
good_for: Homepages, about and treatment pages for skin and beauty clinics, spas, wellness and premium consultation services.

pages.use: Clinic first page: a video hero two screens tall (logo, one line and menu strip pinned at 50% of the screen), a large intro sentence, four benefit cells rotating with a progress line (pinned), navy duotone link cards, philosophy text, a large vertical video that expands with a small fixed photo, a text strip, method cards, and a footer where a pearl video sticks. For consultation-style service landing pages.

About — a one-photo hero with a split title and a small video, intro text and address, a large photo that expands plus a People heading, a person row (name, photo, title, long bio), link cards. For company or medical staff About pages

Treatments page — an intro text with a frosted veil over the video hero, quick links at bottom left, a list attached beside a full-height photo strip (only the current photo’s group is expanded), text that sticks below the photo, and two photos passing over a large gray title. For service and menu listing pages (the original Treatments and Concerns share the same shape)

notes: The Concerns (by worry) page was not built — it has the same form as Treatments (photo hero + blurred-film text, attached list, two photos over a large grey title, philosophy text), so it was merged into the single service.html. The menu’s ”two menu spots” link goes to service.html#list

Logo is the placeholder text ”LO GG O” instead of the original Brand wordmark SVG (ss ligature flipping on the X axis over 1s), and the middle two letters flip with the same curve (cubic-bezier(.1,0,0,1)) and axis (0% 60%).
Fonts: PS Times and Basel Grotesk (paid) → Newsreader 300 and Hanken Grotesk 400, Korean uses Hahmlet 300 and a system gothic

The spots where the original used the English title typeface (PS Times) — tagline·big intro·philosophy·short title·two-line sentence·benefit title·menu drawer items·subpage big title·person title·name·rest screen — are left as English placeholders, with data-label noting what to put in. Big sentences are matched to a similar word count as the original.

The Gothic (Hanken Grotesk) spots — header menu, card labels, small uppercase labels, text strips, treatment list, footer contacts, clock — fell back to the paired Korean gothic, so they are left in Korean.

The idle screen (10 minutes with no interaction → blurred photo and one line, covers in 1s, lifts on press) uses the original values, but I couldn’t wait 10 minutes to confirm it really appears — a task for the next person

title: Full video hero and a flowing staircase of photos for an event site
good_for: Event, festival and conference sites with a single-video first screen, flowing photo introduction and press release room.

pages.use: Event landing — date cell, one big serif line and ticket-buy button over a full-screen looping video, with only a news signup footer and big wordmark below. For event landings that end with a single video

Event intro — ink title box, seven photos sized along a bell curve flow down stairs beneath the big title, right-half info column (per-event text and city row links), two partner logo cells, city photo (parallax) and text. For event and brand introductions

Media room — a page with one press release set up as rows of ‹label 1/4 · content 3/4› (audience, date, photo, release text, contact, materials bundle) in the right 7/12. For media guide and press release pages

notes: The French first page (/fr) has the same form as the first page so it was not built — the ‹EN› slot in the header is that language switch link

Fonts: Baikal SemiBold and Forvm Roman are paid, so replaced with Inter Tight 600 and Forum (Google). Korean is backed by Pretendard and Noto Serif KR, so glyph widths and line counts differ from the original
The hero video is a gray gradient montage placeholder (media/hero.mp4) with the same length, ratio and auto-loop as the original (12 s 1920×1080 loop).
Wordmark, partner logos and city logos are redrawn as placeholder SVGs in the same position and ratio (original logos not used)

Page transition: the original Nuxt single-page app pageTransition is rebuilt with vt-swap-page (swapping the same-document wrapper) + page-vt-reveal (a View Transition with the same curve and length) — when opened as a file (file://) it usually navigates by a normal link. The original transition start delay is the time to fetch the next route over the network, so it wavers between 46~378ms on every open.
The cookie box floats at the bottom right on first visit like the original and remembers the choice in localStorage — the original’s Choose cookies panel was reduced to three items and switches.

Whether the original locks scroll while the phone drawer is open could not be measured, so it is not locked (clip-drop-menu lock: none). Pressing the 30% black scrim behind the drawer closes it (the original has only the scrim)

The first scroll amount → 0, 1s expo.out tween of the About photo stairs did nothing at the start position, so it was removed. Photo placeholders are 7 slots with different content, like the original’s 7 photos
The footer newsletter field only shows name and email inputs when a radio is chosen (the original actually submits to the chosen newsletter form)

Font backfill: the Forum (title serif) slots are all Latin in the original, so they use English placeholder text — hero one-line title · table button, About large sentence · partner button · city logo, footer news picker · links · input field (JS). No Forum slot is left in Korean

index hero one-line title — Forum is narrower than Forvm Roman, so the original character count gives three lines, to get four lines like the original, two more words were added (110 chars, original 97)
Slots using Inter Tight (original Baikal) — header menu, title box, About large title, News subscribe notice and so on — are body font, so Korean stays as is — Pretendard is its pair.

title: Widening photo collage and pinned photo windows for a seaside resort
good_for: Inns, resorts, hotels, glamping and tourism sites with large landscape photos and big English section titles, plus course-meal restaurant pages.

pages.use: Resort home page — a hero with a two-photo fade and a white vertical column on the right, a vertical-writing poem, a photo collage that widens while pinned to the screen, three big English title text sections with pinned photo windows between them, sage panel About cards, news rows with big dates, a footer with a tilting reservation card
News list — header photo strip overflowing to the right edge, large English title, rows with large English month date and title, and pagination. For lodging and shop notice lists
Single news item — date (month, day, year), two-line title, body, signature, dark-ink outlined button, and below it a sage panel with six small intro cards. For a single notice or apology.

Restaurant intro — header photo strip, two-line title·text and a usage info table, big photo gallery navigated by thumbnails, a course card row showing 1.2 cards. For a page detailing one restaurant or facility within a lodging.

notes: All photos are placeholders — the two-panel hero Swiper (fade 3s · 4s autoplay), collage, pinned window, course cards and thumbnail gallery run in the same positions, ratios and libraries as the original, but the images are gray boxes. The brush-script logo is a brush-stroke SVG of the same size, and the section title graphics (NATURE · CUISINE · STAY · ABOUT · NEWS · RESTAURANT · COURSE English lettering) are re-set in the same Cormorant Garamond letters

Swiper version: the bundle has swiperElementNodeName so it is 11.0.6 or later, and it ships together with GSAP 3.12.5, so _vendor/swiper@11.1.14 was used — small differences between 11.0.6 and 11.2 could not be ruled out (estimate)
Lenis: the original loads only lenis.css and has no Lenis script, so smooth scrolling does not run — the copy does not hook it up either

Photo collage pin: the original code has end "+=2000 bottom" but matched to the measured widening speed at 1440×900 (about .86px per 1px of scroll) "+=1770 bottom" was set this way — likely a difference in how the original GSAP 3.12.5 and the shared GSAP 3.15.0 resolve end strings (guess, unconfirmed). Below 1024px the start is also set to top top (original "top +=35% top" — Phones can’t measure it)
The mask where the photo clears away from below (original mask.webp 3s) was rebuilt as a vertical gradient mask of the same shape instead of the mask image
Phone screens were built for wide screens and only breakpoints were matched (reservation bar below · one-line drawer · vertical → horizontal writing) — not checked or measured at 390.

The Bar and Sushi Counter sections (hidden as comments in the restaurant’s original HTML) are not on screen, so they were not built. Room, hot spring and facility pages were not recorded, so links only connect to the first page section

Hero and header photo slots are painted dark like the original photos (sunset, sea, evening interior) — so the white wordmark and opening fade look like the original and sit well. Even when the skin changes, they are mixed from ink-dark

In the original, the News list and single post share the same header bar and drawer as the first page, so they are bundled as shared code (shared.js). Pagination shows only up to ”2” like the original (no real page 2)

title: Striped geometric lettering, stacking timeline and text over a lens-pattern panel
good_for: Company or brand anniversary sites, history pages, and campaigns that fit contests or event news on one page.

pages.use: Commemorative one-page site — striped geometric lettering wordmark, a timeline row that flows stacked together (press for a detail window), a sentence over a lens-pattern panel, lying card stack, questions, News. For company or brand anniversaries and contest campaigns

notes: The original is a single page (pages: [] in pages.json), so there are no subpages. The detail pages (contest · talk) that READ MORE on the cards leads to were not recorded and so were not built, the links point to sections on the same page.

Hero geometric lettering is a video the original pre-rendered (3840×1080·30fps·8s, played once the loader clears, then looped back to 3s at the end so 3→8s repeats). Instead of a placeholder video, it is redrawn on a canvas at the same tempo (3s entrance + 5s loop, matched by sampling original frames every 0.25s) — a call made so the lettering can be rewritten. The swapped-in piece combination is random, so it won’t match original frames.

Geometric glyph placeholders are SAMPLE/TITLE (hero), TITLE·LIST (section title) and SAMPLE TITLE (footer). GLYPHS in the site’s shared.js only has S A M P L E T I O 0, so for any other word attach the stripe-glyphs part, which builds all of A–Z.

The timeline object videos (original: 14 clips, 500×500, 24fps, one 5s loop) are placeholder videos (media/*.mp4) baked at the same spec from our 8 basic-shape models (objects.js) — the 14 slots cycle through the 8. The videos do not change with the skin (colors are baked), so when you swap the skin, re-bake them or replace them with real videos.

The detail window 3D shows our model with three r182 + OrbitControls (damping .05, panning on, zoom off) like the original. The original scene’s environment reflection texture (intensity .1) is an original asset, so it was not included.

The lens-pattern panel texture (original bg_message_light.webp) is a striped-shape panel drawn on a canvas with seeded random numbers. The shader is a single-file three r182 build and uses the original values as they are (bulge 1.4/.66/2.5, lighting 1.18·phong .91, ellipse 1.65, .1~.96, falloff 2.15, center .34·.3, mouse .08).

Fonts: Acumin Pro → Archivo, Aviano Didone → Abril Fatface (narrower than the original), Source Han Serif → Noto Serif KR, Neue Haas/Helvetica → Archivo. The wordmark and logo were replaced with LOGOTYPE text and a dotted-line logo slot.
The background grain moves one SVG noise 11 positions every 100ms to simmer at the same tempo as the original gif (128px, 22 frames, 100ms). One loop is 1.1s, shorter than the original (2.2s).

On phones the [MENU] button sits in the same spot as the shared toolbar (.wf-ui), so z-index is raised to 10001 — it covers part of the toolbar’s right side. The loader is also raised above the menu (10000) (in the original the menu is inside a z 300 layer, so the loader covers it).

The original cookie·analytics scripts and external contact form·social links were changed to same-page anchors. The original’s Astro page transitions (ClientRouter) are not used since there are no sub pages.

title: Mask face with deepening ripple rings and archive photo cards
good_for: Traditional performance, exhibition and cultural project sites, dark event archives and performance record collections.

pages.use: Project first page — a hero where pixi rings spread and a mask silhouette rises, a giant wordmark, a mask photo intro, four performance record cards and two exhibition cards (photo fade + MORE circle), two posters, and a booklet row. For cultural event and performance project landing pages

Project intro — a large English title with lines drawing on both sides, a hero photo overlapping the text with a serif intro, photo and text, a three-column credits list, and a link panel below (four plus one wide). For about and credits pages

Program (performance) intro — tall portrait photo behind the text, serif intro, photo with text, video panel with play button, four ARCHIVE record cards, link panel. For a section introducing a single performance or program

Exhibition intro — same Type as the performance section (header photo spread sideways as a Skin, photo and text flip sides, no video, one of two record cards dimmed as coming soon). For exhibition and event intro sections

notes: Fonts: Trajan Pro 3 (paid) → Cinzel, a paid Japanese serif → Noto Serif KR, Noto Sans CJK JP → Noto Sans KR. Cinzel is slightly wider than Trajan so large English headings run a few % longer

Hero mask silhouette: instead of the original mask image (mask face png), our own pixi shapes draw an egg-shaped face, eyes, mouth holes and a mustache. The ring color is mixed from the Skin, leaning slightly toward the background color rather than the original neutral grays (#555 · #aaa)
The original Japanese titles and section titles were SVG letter graphics — replaced with Korean serif text (the page header English title also uses Cinzel letters instead of graphics)

swiper: the original bundle has no version number, so the version was estimated from the class names (swiper-container, 6 instances) and the last 6.x, 6.8.4, was used. As in the original build, the accessibility module is off

The hero and subpage start delays (.95s · .4s) were measured and matched to how long the original sits blank before the framework wakes up — when attaching the same panel to a different frame, they can be shortened

Unrecorded subpages (what is Brand? · SYMPOSIUM · BOOKLET · performance · exhibition record detail) were not built, and menus · links were connected to existing spots such as about.html#links · index.html#symposium
Video (MOVIE): instead of a YouTube player, a preview placeholder of the same spot and ratio — click it to switch to a playing placeholder
Footer sponsor logos are our single-color SVG marks — the original’s image swap on hover (background image .4s) is not carried over
The phone menu items’ framer spring (.8s) is approximated with power3.out .8s (opacity .3s)

title: Two-way entrance panel and six tilted color cards on a green ground
good_for: Brand sites for local companies and retailers with a split sales/brand entrance, character-led activity intros and six color-coded business areas.

pages.use: Company entrance single screen — logo and today’s date above a two-way split panel (wide photo panel 80% · narrow video panel 20%), on hover the panel widens, blur clears and the name rolls over into English. For a first page where the site splits in two, like sales/brand or individual/business
