One-page brand introduction — shape circle loader, hero with two characters and flying shapes, slogan text under a green hill, six activity cards each in a different color per section (standing tilted), closing with spinning shapes, anniversary banner, news slider, TV video wall between tilted marquee bands, character and careers link panel. Spot for the company’s ”What we do”, social contribution and brand introduction menus

notes: The second branch of the original first page (sales site /dealer) was not recorded, so it was not built — the wide-layout link points to index.html itself. The narrow layout continues to about.html.

Logo, characters (bear, mouse) and six shapes were redrawn as SVG in the same position and size instead of the original image files (planted by shared.js <symbol> group, colors use --site-* variables). The hero bear is drawn separately with arms spread wide (head is 37% of the width).

The loader (orbit-icon-loader) and hero entrance play only on the first visit via localStorage, like the original (names o-intro-played and o-hero-played). To see them again, clear both names in developer tools. The original also has a second form where the character positions swap half and half on each open, using the same Math.random() < moved to .5.
The arrow in the original is a transition (.3s), so on release it rotates back in reverse — added look: glide to arrow-cycle-hover (two transitions, applies at any depth inside the link) and used it.
The original’s right-click and drag blocking (contextmenu · dragstart preventDefault) is not design motion, so it was not carried over.

The News slider is Splide 4.1.4 (_vendor) as in the original. The original uses splide.min.css (theme), but we only paint the arrow buttons in the core css with the original values (42/1366vw·5px·#353535·hover .9).
The TV video wall loads and plays video 200px before it enters the screen, like the original (IntersectionObserver lazy). The screen frame (purple monitor) was redrawn in SVG.
The original TV marquee’s clip-path entrance (tv-slide01·02) is commented out in the original CSS, so it was not ported.

title: Cut-out shadows flying in stepwise over vertical text for a local event
good_for: Local festival, experience expo and tourism event sites, or cultural event pages with a handmade feel from vertical text and paper collage.

pages.use: Event home — leaf-shadow splash, logo over ink text two screens tall, vertical-writing header sentence, pinned program collage, tilted card list, participation info box, video-loop slider, news, area intro, map, route diagram, contact. For local event landing pages.

Event intro — behind a logo hero, landscape photos and photos cut into letter shapes change in turn (pinned +1000%), and in front a vertical-writing headline and body rise and leave one by one. For explaining an event or region’s meaning as scenes
News list — vertical heading with staggered letters, 3-column cards with date and photos staggered and tilted, torn-paper page numbers. For notice and press lists

Experience program list — large red heading with a shadow forest, region and season filter fields, cards in groups of six whose width and tilt rotate, page numbers. Goes on the list of experiences and products to book (fixed from what the recording tagged as page)

One news item — large date at the far right, red title, a torn-paper main image, body text · white line, list button, and three other program cards below. For the notice detail (fixed what was captured as detail during recording)

notes: All the original’s imagery is photos and brush paintings — the ink characters (two gate characters), large red characters, trees, leaves, deer, monkey, rabbit and bear shadows were redrawn with SVG and rough filters (not copied, since they are that site’s artwork), but they fall short of the original’s stamp texture and cut-out delicacy (the leaves are procedural drawings with small leaves attached along a stem)

The Brand button is a lottie-web 5.13 Lottie like the original (945×546 · 24fps · 240-frame loop, restarts from the beginning on hover), but the art is redrawn with our own shapes instead of the original’s two photos. Only the head rotation keyframes and the head/body layer anchor and position values come from the original

The video slider is dragged through with Embla as in the original (loop · classNames is-snapped · tween-scale 0.2× slide count). The Embla version inside the original bundle is unreadable, so the closest v8 release, 8.6.0, is used. Instead of a YouTube embed, a 12-second placeholder video of the same ratio (placeholder-16x9.mp4) plays in place when clicked (the original video length is unknown)

The paper-photo background texture is replaced by two layers of SVG noise, and the torn paper edges by seeded random polygons sized to the element. The bluish tint (.3 .35 .5) of the dark paper noise is baked into the SVG artwork, so it stays when the skin changes.
The program filter is a link to another address in the original. Since this is the same type of page, here only the chosen cell turns into white paper within the same row and the list stays
Cards cut to one set of six for both home and list (original has 12, same type repeated)
Program detail, contact form, and privacy pages were not recorded so they are not built — card links go to the list, the menu’s privacy link goes to #
Text, logos and photos are all placeholders (the logo is a brush-script Logo placeholder), the map is a newly drawn regional outline

title: Corner arcs gather into full-bleed video with vertically sliding video headers
good_for: Calm corporate sites with video and large photos: business and service intros, careers list, news list and articles.

pages.use: Company first page — symbol-piece loader, a video header that covers from below each time it ends (four progress bars), intro paragraph, three News cards, two photo links, a fleet video that opens from half width in the center to full screen, two text-and-photo rows, a dark coordinates row, a closing paragraph

Careers — full-bleed photo header, an open-positions table that switches with sea and land tabs (a dark band follows along the row), a sea/land split photo that slides at 64:36, and a full-bleed video closing. For a careers list section

About the company — video header, three photo and paragraph splits, panorama photo, two staggered photos, full-bleed photo link with ear-like arcs. For company-at-a-glance About sections without a history

Services — service rows split by lines (text and photo alternating), a dark inverted row, a card board converging to the center (photos pushed aside by the space), closing paragraph. For a services or business list section
News list: big title, featured post with a text card over the photo, fixed branch buttons, three-column post cards (red square cursor), Load more. For news and blog lists
A single News post — big centered title and date, prev·next photo flip, left sticky share, body·subheadings·quote that darkens on scroll, three related posts. For press release·blog posts.

notes: Video is a placeholder box with the same position and ratio (original mp4, HLS and Vimeo are not copied). The hero slider’s video length is set per section with data-duration (10 seconds). As in the original, it advances to the next slide 1.2 seconds before the end, and the progress bar fills over that same length. When real video is added, switch this to timeupdate (original syncVideoProgress).

The video-player dialog (play, sound, progress bar) of the Watch Video button was not built — it is an external player product feature. Only the button shape and entrance (1.15s late, pushed up from below) are there.

The loader redraws the original 8-second video (symbol pieces) frame by frame as our own SVG version (small circle → spreads to the corners → eight arrowheads circle around the circle). The wipe-away (2 seconds before the end, 1.2s cubic-bezier(.85,0,.15,1), sheet -100% · background fades) uses original values, while the timing between pieces was matched by eye from the frames (guess). It runs only once per window (sessionStorage) — the original runs every time the first page opens

The phone header symbol uses a GSAP SVG with the same timing instead of the original Lottie (60fps, 241 frames): the plate turns 90° over 2.25s and the four arcs open at 2s, each 5 frames later. The curve is power2.inOut (guess), since the Lottie beziers could not be carried over.
The word-darkening range of the closing paragraph (top 85% → bottom 45%) is a value matched by eye (guess) — the original uses a CSS scroll-timeline variable (--split-text-word-window .16)

The original’s three (fleet-position globe and ship scene) is absent from the six recorded pages, so it is not used. Sections that were not recorded, such as fleet, live position and market, were not built (menu links go to #)
The cookie consent window, the News category topic dropdown and the actual sharing of the share button are look only — external services/features

Font backfill: the display font (--kf-font-display, Albert Sans) slots are all English in the original (TT Commons Pro), so 31 slots use English placeholder text: hero headline, section titles, photo links, news titles and subheads, the recruit split (At Sea·On Land), and service names (Service Name 01…). Original words weren’t carried over, only line counts and character counts were matched. No display font slot is left in Korean
Header menu, drawer menu, job role rows and body use the body font (--kf-font-sans is also Albert Sans) · labels are DM Mono, so Korean stays as is — a system gothic is the match

In the first section, the ‹Headline With / Backstory› cell is narrow so ‹Headline With A› splits into three lines, so A was dropped (two lines like the original). Hidden header slide titles were measured by cloning the visible title and counting lines at 1440·390.

thumb.jpg: shot.cjs --thumb caught the middle of the loader (8 seconds), so the loader was skipped via sessionStorage (ol-loaded) and the shot was taken at the same size and quality after the first section title rose

title: Fixed video with a brush heart and blur panels rising over it
good_for: Corporate homepages for service companies with case list, news list and a light-themed recruiting special page.

pages.use: Company home — over a fixed promo video (sound-on button), slogan section (brush heart swelling on scroll)·services·company photo slider·ten-row News·careers·case slider rise as translucent blur panels. For a service company landing

Company intro — brush heart header that zooms in big as it lights up, with slogan above·three photos flowing at different speeds·non-stop flowing slogan photo band·CEO greeting·vision diagram·core business number diagram·company overview table. In the About menu slot

News list — no header image, a narrow column with a category box picker, rows with date and category pills, and pagination. Category lists (news_category) share the same type, so this one section covers both.
Case list — above a brush heart header: number, two-line title and button | three case panels with body and two photos alternate into a blurred panel. For business areas and case introductions

Careers special site — light gray skin, a flowing strip of employee photos, yellow-orange gradient panels (slogan · CEO greeting) that stay stuck on top while the next panel covers them, a white line heart and apply card that swell with scroll, member cards (press to open a profile window), a benefits grid and an office slider. For a careers page.

notes: The Hero video is a gray gradient placeholder video of the same ratio (landscape 16:9 · portrait 9:16) and length (35s) (media/hero-landscape.mp4 · hero-portrait.mp4, including a silent audio track). As in the original, it checks whether the window is landscape or portrait to choose the version (window resize delayed .25s), and the OFF · ON button toggles mute.

The original’s text images (Japanese serif headline SVG·WebP — slogan, company slogan, case titles, recruiting headline, member/environment/office headers) were replaced with Korean serif lettering of the same position and size. The vision and core business diagrams (five images with embedded text) were redrawn in HTML·SVG with the same composition, and the icons and number panels were simplified.

The original wires the drawer, profile window, sound button and slider with an Alpine.js (3.15) state bundle — it is not a motion library, so it was ported by hand with the same values (x-transition .3s ease-out/ease-in, profile window .3s pause + .6s ease-out). Swiper is the same 12.1 line as the original (_vendor/swiper@12.1.3, the build number is not printed in the original bundle, so it was matched to 12.1, which has the swiper-slides-offset-before variable). ScrollSmoother is GSAP 3.15 from _shared (original 3.11.0).
The flowing photo strip in the careers section replaces the original image strip (one 5252×1440 image with repeat-x) with two same-size placeholders flowing linearly over 60 seconds.

title: Filling circle and changing color panels for a public research institute
good_for: Nonprofit and public research institute or consulting sites that present three services as color panels, with large team pages, careers and report articles.

pages.use: First page: a big centered title, a section where three yellow circles grow with scroll until they cover the screen, four color tiles, three service color panels with the left half pinned (the panel switches when the right-hand pattern arrives), an area list, case cards, a publication push, a quote whose words darken, and a color-changing CTA. For research lab and consulting homepages.

Organization introduction — a hero where a 9-photo grid recedes from 3.2x as the title disappears, two-column about, three models and a circle drawing, four navy values, staff · business map with counting-up numbers, and a client logo wall. For company introductions.
People list — five-column face grid with name search and team filter, plum band under the photo on hover, board grid, pink CTA. For team, expert and speaker lists

Careers — intro header, horizontal pattern Lottie (4s when visible), two pattern+text two-column blocks, four-cell values and benefits, remote work list with employee map and numbers, yellow closing. For a careers page.

Single report or article — back link, tag, title, type/tag row, shortcut buttons, a cover on the right that follows as you scroll with a small news signup, overview, body, contributors, share, and a blue-violet news signup band below. For research report and news article details.

notes: Most of the original motion is the site builder’s IX2, not a library — we read the IX2 data (events·actionLists) and rebuilt the same keyframes and durations with GSAP ScrollTrigger. The builder’s smoothing 50 was carried over as scrub .5 (we could not measure whether it is the same value)

The four Lottie files (logo wheel and three hiring patterns) are not the original JSON. Our own shape Lottie is generated in Python and played with lottie-web 5.12.2. Frame count, fps and length match the original (logo 24fps 96 frames, played up to frame 72 in 3 seconds. Pattern 60fps 240 frames, played once when visible), while shapes and motion order were guessed from stills. Colors are painted on the layer name (cl) with CSS variables
The heading font Neue Haas Grotesk Display is paid, so Inter Tight is used — the letters run a bit wider
The center photo of the circular ring section (original layout488_image) is not visible in the print, so it was not built and only the three circles were
Map (staff·business area) is a placeholder of colored dots on concentric contours and cell shapes instead of a real map — the user supplies the map SVG

The client logo wall was built as a still grid (no motion), like the original. The original number roll (Layout 485 Number), progress bar and history circle (Timeline Circle) were not built because no place using them was found in the five pages built this time
People search and team filtering use a short script that does the same job instead of the original attributes

Footer·menu link underlines are the original’s paid gfluo-pro (btn.8) effect, so they were not used and were rebuilt as child bars with the measured values: the text color goes straight to navy, and the bar takes .15s quad-out on entering and .18s on leaving (a curve fitted to the measured points). Footer service·area cell links are h4 size as in the original. The footer logo is a panel rather than a link to prevent pair misalignment.

title: Village rooftop illustration curtain, rounded menu badge and wiggling hand-drawn icons
good_for: Sites for community-rooted nurseries, small schools and local childcare hubs with village stories, photos, news, features, voices, enrollment info and access.

pages.use: Neighborhood daycare home page — a first-visit village illustration curtain (4s approach · slogan · 2.5s lift), four overlapping round menu badges at the top right with a vertical slogan, a fading-photo hero (8s recede), a vertical-title news list, an about text with wiggling hand-drawn icons, two photo slider features with blue-band lettered titles (staggered left and right) · video, a hand-drawn map, round-face voices (read all), three childcare principles, a yellow-cell enrollment table, a social photo grid, a neighborhood map with icons, contact, and a footer of yellow hills. For a local organization landing

Photo gallery — yellow round name tag on the left with a season·genre menu, photo fade slider inside a water-drop shaped panel (Back/Next · blue band title), two-column 4:3 photo grid (on hover a blue overlay with date·season·genre), reaching the end loads the next batch. For activity albums·portfolio lists

News list — a round name tag on the left with year and category menus, rows of date, title and category pill split by blue dotted lines, and the next rows fade in slowly when you reach the end. For announcement and blog lists.
A single News post — left tag·menu, title·date·category, body and big-sentence graphic, vertically continuing photos, round Back/Next and back to list. For notice·greeting posts.

Single photo gallery entry — yellow name tag · menu on the left, two-line title · date · season · genre, one-line description and body with landscape and portrait photos in sequence, rounded Back/Next. For event · activity record detail

notes: The village illustration on the first-visit curtain (the original fv_mv illustration) was redrawn as a new SVG with the same composition (forest slope, winding road, red tiled roofs, a line of children in blue caps, clouds in the corner) — the original’s hand-drawn texture and detail are not there. The timing (4s at 1.05x, 3.5s chant, 2.5s lift starting at 6.5s, 3-hour cookie skip) is exactly the original, and the same jquery.cookie 1.4.1 is used.
Feature sections: of the original four, only the two where left and right differ (photo left, photo right) are built — cut as repeats of the same type. Three hand-drawn icon sets cut to two.
The Voices section uses three of the original five (so both staggered shapes appear). The photo circle crop is a true circle instead of an irregular one.

The hand-drawn map, neighborhood map, social media banner and daycare study-abroad banner are single images in the original, so they are placeholder photo slots of the same ratio (labelled with what to put in). The nine wiggling icons on the neighborhood map keep the original positions but have no motion applied (original rotate-z, bounceIn_50 etc. — they can be added with the spin and pop types of the doodle-tic part).

The Instagram grid is a Smash Balloon plugin feed in the original, so there are only 12 placeholder cells. Load-on-reach-end for the gallery and news appends the same batch once more instead of the original ajax, showing the same delay and fade (news 2s after 1s, photos 1s after 2s).

The original menu badge, village banner and flower sentence are image PNGs, so they were redrawn as circle and hand-drawn icon SVGs. The badge hover bounceIn is commented out in the original CSS, so it was not applied (only 1.05x .4s easeOutCubic).
Article and detail share the same type (left label, body photo row, round Back/Next), but the two recorded pages are different kinds (news article, photo record), so both were built.

title: Black panel number loader and slanted curtain transitions for a travel app
good_for: One-page intros with a news list for travel or culture guide apps and audio guides where photos lead.

pages.use: App home page — a number loader and a curtain that clears away diagonally, a full-screen video Hero (logo line drawing, red vertical line), four zigzag service blocks on gray panels, a big sentence over a phone photo, four guide photos that recede from the front alternately left and right, a drag-to-flip partner card row with a red bar, a get-the-app Section, a next Section leading to the About panel (ABOUT US), and a guide modal.

News and post list — big English heading, category row with red underline, three-column photo cards (only the photo scales 1.1x on hover), load more, get the app, next section. For when a News page is needed

notes: Inertia scroll: the original uses the site’s own code (FakeScroll · Scroll.sliding — the body sits on a fixed panel and trails along with speed .1 · friction .1), so the same trailing is reproduced with lenis 1.3.27 (lerp .1). The body becomes the window scroll, so ScrollTrigger and sticky work as they are.

Page transition curtain (TransitionCanvas): the original 2d canvas’s four-vertex quad was moved into the quad-wipe-page part (a screen-sized SVG path). Cover .6s · uncover .7s, one leading vertex uses CustomEase(0.438,0,0.481,0.399 · 0.554,0.712,0.616,1) at .9× length, another uses Quart.inOut and arrives later. The uncover after the number loader · same-site links · the ABOUT US plate (left-right, quadratic-curve edge) all use this curtain.

The hero video (original mp4 and canvas playback) is a placeholder in the same spot that cycles four scenes every 5 seconds with a 1s swap (1.1x → 1 settling, logo line drawing, one line of text 100px up, and the red vertical line use the original values).

The #fullImg section is empty at 21px height in the original at 1440 (the image is used only on phones), so the copy also keeps height 0 — if a full-bleed photo band is needed on the phone panel only, give .ot-full a height.

ABOUT US panel: the original loads /top/about and draws the cover, mission, future and location sections plus a member slider (arrows·SVG name drawing). The archive has no such response, so only a cover + two sections (big background English word · two-column body) + close were built — the member slider is left for the next person.
Client card row: rebuilt the original DragAndDrop (inertia) and red bar dragging with our own drag with follow .1. On phones only horizontal swipes are intercepted and vertical swipes go to the page.
App store buttons, phone photo and app icon are placeholders (instead of the original app store badge and app screen photo).
Fonts: Barlow Condensed 700 instead of DIN Next LT Pro Bold Condensed (paid), Noto Sans KR instead of Yu Gothic.
The original hero’s notice modal (free-build notice) appears once after the loader — the copy does the same, on the first page only. The news page has no modal or pinned news row, like the original.

title: CRT-style opening then an endless wall of works for an animation archive
good_for: Archives of animation, picture books, folktales or film with hundreds of works to filter and browse, and brand sites with opening sequences.

pages.use: Home page — sound-on door, CRT-style logo, typed text lines, sky and dragon, circular video button opening, then a draggable endless grid of work cards with a bottom filter bar and a work detail overlay. For the first screen of an archive with many works

Works list — round thumbnail · title · tag | three plot lines, one per line, flips to a white sheet on hover, pagination. Spot for the ”ALL LIST” view on the first page (the original is the same address’s ?view=list)

About — hero with sky, clouds and a dragon, white rounded cards (bold title, one handwritten line, two-column bilingual body), a screen-fixed circular band tinted by sunset (description per group). For brand and series introductions
News list — sky background with rows of a 194×116 thumbnail | title, body and related link, a pill button back to the first page, and a grassy footer. For notice and press lists
Company overview — item | content table (company name · business · address · contact) inside a white rounded card on a sky background. For operator intro and company info

notes: The original artwork (brush-script logo · cloud animation · dragon bitmap · meadow · silhouette animation) is not used and is redrawn fresh in SVG and canvas. The logo is a Nanum Brush Script text placeholder, and the dragon segments (head 243×117 · body 136.8×67.2 · eye · legs · tail 193.2×162) are vector drawings with the same box sizes and attachment points, so they are simpler than the original art style. The hidden rail the dragon travels (1920 square, screen width + 200rem) uses the original orbit values as is, and the speed 220 · spacing 96 (phone 45) · scale 1.15 · segment order · flipping only off-screen are also the same.

The original clouds are a 20-frame 10fps (2-second loop) animated image, so peak sizes and swirl positions are redrawn at the same tempo — the shape in each section differs from the original image. The footer silhouette row also redraws leg and body bobbing at the tempo of the original 6-frame 11.99fps walking animation.

The original uses the same URL for the first page list view ?view=The hand-off to list uses swup, but here it is split out into a separate list.html (the transition is the same swup 4.8.2 + JS plugin, while the filter bar and sound button stay outside the transition). Opened as file:, swup cannot fetch the page, so it navigates normally after the .5s exit.

The filter panel’s Apply puts the tags chosen in the original into the URL and the server filters to show the list — here the chosen name goes to list.html?tag= passed along as a parameter and laid out in the header as pills with a clear button, but the placeholder works have no category data so the list itself is not filtered.

Work detail overlay content, the source is WP REST (/wp-json/wp/v2/works/<id>) fills it in — here the tapped card’s title, English title and tag are copied in (open/close values are as in the original).
The Contact (CONTACT) page was not recorded so it was not built, menu 4 links to the Contact row (#contact) of the company page table.

Video and sound are placeholders with the same spots and the same playback behavior. One opening video (media/opening.mp4, plays and loops when Sound on is pressed), a card hover video (media/work.mp4, plays from the start and pauses on leave), and six sounds (media/sounds/*.mp3, tones made with ffmpeg: bgm and under-page loop at 16s, crossfade at .5s between the first page and subpages, pop at volume 3).

title: Dragged handwriting ribbon trailing the cursor for a branding agency
good_for: Branding and design studio homepages that chain philosophy, process, works, members, writing, news and contact into one long page, plus work list and detail.

pages.use: Studio home page — background video revealed from the center with a handwritten ribbon (WebGL) over it, philosophy, an intro with photos sticking out, a work-method video where a small window grows into the full screen, three services as line shapes being drawn, work cards (fog hover), members, articles, news, and a section-navigation menu at bottom right. For a branding company home that states its philosophy at length.
Work list — large centered English title above two rows of half-width work cards, a fixed pill at bottom center opens a category panel to filter. For portfolio lists

Work detail — centered title, full-screen cover photo with a pinned detail box over it, two overview and insight sheets, photo pair, green retrospective panel and credits, previous and next work cards. For a single case page
Visual — under a large English title, ten photos staggered across cells, each with its own parallax, the last one filling the screen. For mood boards and brand-world galleries

notes: The English title typeface is the site’s own custom font, so the free Italiana stands in for it — a similar thin high-contrast caps feel but slightly narrower

The four videos (hero background, how we work, footer) use a canvas of flowing clothing-color blobs (shared.js OD.fakeVideo) with the same placement and playback (loops when visible, the hero plays at 1.72s). To swap in real video, for the hero panel you only need to change CanvasTexture to VideoTexture.

The stroke shapes of the handwriting ribbon do not use the original stroke-data.json (brand handwriting) and were newly drawn as three trochoid cursive scripts. Wave (.04·4.6), drag (1.6·.05·radius 1·follow .08), wandering dots (±.6, 3s), drawing (2.8s power2.out after 1s) and vanishing band (.35) are the original values
Amount the ribbon leans toward the cursor is the original rx {1.2, .6} Read as degrees ×5 (estimated) — cursor-sweep reaction size is about the same as the original

The color cover order for each section of the background panel (green at About, background color at How we work) was decided by looking at the original’s 390 capture — I couldn’t finish reading the original setCover call order
Showing the photo blurred first (lqip .6s) is just a placeholder, so it was not built

The contact form only checks for empty fields and email-shaped input and does not send (placeholder status sentence). The original detail’s ”Work process” and ”Full-bleed photo” sections are not in the recorded detail, so they were not made up. The list ”Load more (10 at a time)” was dropped since there are only 8 cards
The lenis version couldn’t be read from the original bundle so 1.3.27 is used (options lerp .1 · wheelMultiplier .9 are the same)
The placeholder video is painted in a bright mid tone like the original video — if dark, the change revealing the Hero is small and the opening effect is not visible

title: Scattered rainbow petals for a building festival with striped logo project set
good_for: Opening festivals for buildings and commercial facilities with talks, workshops, exhibits and food over several days, followed by local collaboration projects and interview series.

pages.use: Festival one-pager — hero with rainbow petals on a grainy textured background, ended-event notice + photo strip, program contents, lecture cards with notched corners (fixed description), special talk, exhibit and experience cards on a slate-blue panel, photo exhibition, ink-black shop events, gifts, date-tab timetable, floor guide slider, access, striped logo section. For introducing multi-day events

Project collection first page — striped logo Lottie, opening text over a black-and-white photo, and with the left striped pillar attached, three projects laid out (big picture · title · selected text · interview). For business or series collection intros
Collaboration project post list — dark photo slide hero with white box title · OVERVIEW · latest post, below a two-column post list (rotating aurora frame). For case studies and series lists
Interview series list. Photo slide first screen, half-ink half-white photo strip and a striped strip, three-column people list, radio panel. For people interviews and local stories lists

A single collaboration post — location line, title + vertical line, large photo, aurora-bordered overview panel (OUTLINE · BACKGROUND), tap-to-expand progress log, closing note, four related-post slots. For case and project detail pages

notes: The sites pull half-failed due to a path conflict (project is both a file and a folder), so the sub-page HTML (project·xto1/11) was read directly from the archived pages.har.zip.

The original hero wordmark, petals and photos are all image files. The wordmark is redrawn as a wide geometric font (Unbounded) with a subtle gloss gradient, the petal shapes as SVG (gradient + turbulence displacement texture), and the festival background texture (bg.png 250px) as a canvas tile that shared.js bakes in the skin’s text color. The petal shape is not identical to the original (same boomerang V shape, same position and size).

The striped project logo Lottie (one_brand_project_kv.json) is not copied. With the same structure (60fps 62 frames · bar thickness 11.4 · gap 22.5 · 1-frame stagger · 30-frame growth curve .109,0→.047,1 · 20 frames from above photo slot 130 · letters 15-frame drop .136,0→.236,1), shared.js bakes it on the spot in the skin colors and passes it to lottie-web 5.10.2. Wordmark letters are laid out as HTML so they can be swapped to the skin font, and move following the Lottie frame number. The phone version (original _sp.json) is our own vertically stacked structure.
The original timetable and floor guide are image files, so the timetable was redrawn as a grid of color bars by floor and place, and the guide as a room-and-corridor SVG (content is placeholder).

Repeating lecture and experience cards are cut from the original four and seven to two and three (all section types kept). The speaker profile window Swiper is applied only on wide windows like the original — on phones the original is also a stacked list, so the prev/next buttons do not move even when pressed.
The original subpage’s actual post body (the expanded progress log) is long, so it is cut down to three paragraphs.

title: Strip of works pulled along by scrolling for a branding studio
good_for: Branding and design studio homepages, case-focused portfolios and journal (blog) article pages.

pages.use: Studio home page — loader, 120px title, a square work strip dragged along by page scroll (and by hand), white-strip intro, five 16:9 work cards (rise-in, yellow hover), logo marquee, problem·answer·proof pill tabs, 4-slide journal swiper. For an agency landing page that leads with work

A single journal post: cover image at 70% width on a beige panel, pink category pill and date, 62px title, narrow body column and a closing column that repeats once more, back and author line. For blog and insight post details

notes: In the original, the white intro block sticky + 100vh spacing + -100vh does not stick even in the original because of page-wrapper’s overflow:hidden — so it is simply stacked as it appears
The original work strip is Draggable inertia:true but InertiaPlugin is not loaded, so there is no inertia — same here, with no inertia, and it can be turned on with the part’s inertia option
The original strip jumps once on the next scroll after being stopped (it uses lastX as the reference) — fixed so it resumes following from where it stopped

Logos, work GIFs, certification marks and client logos are done with our SVG symbols and placeholders — the loader’s logo motion is redrawn as a repeat of same-size symbols rising in turn in the same spot
The contact button ring carries over the site builder’s smoothing 80 as lag .8s (matched by eye)
Fonts: NT Brand·Awesome Serif Italic ExtraTall are paid, so replaced with Inter Tight·Instrument Serif italic, and for the Korean italic serif slot, Gowun Batang (italic synthesized)

The menu drawer’s open shape failed to be captured on the original because the capture hit the hidden .menu element, and the browser slot queue was long so it couldn’t be retaken — built instead with a CSS grid (2.25fr .25fr 2fr·8rem yellow links·numbers) and IX values (open .7s·close .5s). The next person should press MENU (.nav-bar .menu) with interact and compare
The three Webflow IX2 cursor images (cursor-image 1~3) were not built because no elements on the first page use them

The original cursor moves one step (.4) immediately on an event and then follows .4 per frame — put into the part as is. It does not grow on ordinary links, only on buttons, tabs, journal cards and the contact button, at 50px (where the original IX is attached)

Font backfill — the original is all Latin, so every slot for title and decorative fonts (Inter Tight titles, Instrument Serif italics) was swapped to English placeholders, with no slot left for Korean. Also changed the text JS inserts: menu button, menu drawer, Footer menu, cookie button, certification mark, and Contact ring
Body-font spots (cursor ”View work” · social pills · cookie notice · newsletter · case descriptions) were left in Korean per the README

title: Cream background with monospace capitals and script-style buttons
good_for: Small agency sites for branding and design studios with work portfolio, services and a journal.

pages.use: Studio home page — flowing booking strip, three-column small-text hero with a work photo row that flows in reverse and speeds up on scroll, 3-column work card grid, four things we do, video studio, drag-and-throw testimonial card stack, big case image, contact with flowing hand-drawn objects. For calm cream-toned agency landing pages
Work list — three-line title with service·industry filters (cards remain when picked)·clear, and a 3-column card grid with varied photo ratios. For portfolio lists

Service — header with a huge script word and a rotating sun illustration over a faint engraved landscape, service name line joined by slashes, four services (description, detail items + two photos), contact with flowing hand drawings. For service and capability intros
Journal — header with name, hand-drawn line art and intro, then a 4-column list of square photo, bold title and first paragraph. For blog or journal lists

notes: The fourth recorded page (portfolio/brand-site) was not titled Page not found as in the original. Work detail, case detail and one journal post were not recorded, so they don’t exist. Card links are #

The original photos, videos and hand drawings (illustration objects, hand holding a star, sun, ray-of-light sentences, copperplate engraving texture) were not used — photos are placeholders describing subject, light and composition, and hand drawings were redrawn as our own SVGs of the same size and texture (house, door, lamp, plant pot, sun, blob, tree, bottle, person, journal hand, service sun, footer rays). The original objects have more colors (brown, orange, pink) — ours are painted with only the five skin variable branches

The marquee rows use the same Reeller 0.1.2 as the original (_vendor/reeller@0.1.2 newly added, MIT) and the original’s Brand settings as they are (band 5s · pause, work row 35s reverse · ScrollerPlugin multiplier .5 expo · 3/35 when a hand is on it, object row 15s reverse · ScrollerPlugin). The dot cursor is the same mouse-follower 1.1.2 (speed .55 · expo.out · stickDelta .15) — the original plugin puts tilt 0 on the text "0" Handed over so that only the rotation turns on, matched exactly. Lenis is the same 1.1.5 file as the original bundle (duration 1.8)

Video studio: it’s a placeholder so there’s no video — only the shapes of the play, sound and fullscreen buttons, plus the progress bar and fullscreen button that light up in .2s on hover, match the original

Titles, headers, menu, FAQ, card text — all of it. The original uses Chinese-character/kana titles, Korean is kept. Zen Kaku Gothic New has no Korean glyphs so it falls back to Noto Sans KR, both are gothics on the same weight axis, so they match in feel

Eight name lines on home user cards (#00s · Name 01) — the original has kana tags and names like #50s Man · Mr. Name (only one Latin nickname), Korean kept. Purchase page plan names (Product name 00-pack bundle) — the original Brand 4-pack set is a Japanese line with only the brand name in Latin, so Korean kept

In the phone (390) Hero capture, the three-line slogan (.v-kv__voice) inside the block and the intro text (.v-kv__intro) look overlapped. The changed copy is 9·11·5 characters, the same as the carried-over original English, so it isn’t caused by text length. It is a layout issue where the intro turns on early in the Hero on phones. The section image (index__hero-kv) also captures, at 1440, a moment where the intro overlaps above the heading (the Hero thumb is clean). Left as is, since it is out of scope of the font backfill (text only).

title: Single-object shop with a line-drawn spinning vase and a round-hole loader
good_for: Shop or brand sites that tell the story of one product launch, with a loader, product story, size picker, collection and product detail.

pages.use: First page for a single product — round-hole loader, a dark first photo with a shrinking header title, a large title with rising letters and a photo train, a pinned section where a top-down dot stands up as a vase and spins, an aerial photo ring, a size picker card, a tabletop scene, a collection (hand-print water), flower arrangement, and a big wordmark footer. For product launch and product intro landings.
Brand introduction — on one dark screen, an index menu, four intro paragraphs, a one-line pledge, a flower cover and an item list. For About pages of small brands

Product detail — name, picker and small image on the left, vertical photo column in the center, price, description, line-dimension drawing, accordion rows and a pinned add-to-cart button on the right. For a single product detail

notes: The recorded sub page store (/store) has the same document and same title (same type) as the home page, so it was not built separately and is replaced by index.html#store (size picker cards)

The original line-art vase and table scene flips pre-baked SVG line frames from a 3D model (vase-spin·turn·toiso·tophoto assets), so we did not use it and instead built a new part (tube-wire-turn) that computes a cylinder by orthographic projection and draws the same sequence — the wavy base line below, the dimension lines, and the line-drawing-to-photo scene (tophoto) could not be carried over

For the photo ring (gallery), the original bundle’s smear, wash shader and ruler were not read, only a CSS 3D orbit around a tilted circle and the number/description swap (.35s power2.in → .8s otto, original values) were built. Ring radius and rotation amount are guessed from the screen.

In the original the loader cover is a picture where petals open on a canvas (mark), but we kept our flower SVG as is and moved over only the hole opening (2.3s power3.inOut), the text-line drop (.55s) and the first photo settling (2.4s otto) using the original numbers
The cart drawer and checkout screens (cart · co__) are not recorded pages, so they were not built
The original font OTF APR15 is exclusive to that site, so it is replaced with Marcellus (a capital serif with flared stroke ends) and paired with a Korean serif for Hangul

The hero’s “flowers show through the photo only where the hand passes” is built as water-trail-gl look: reveal. Since the photo is a placeholder, it now shows as a bright glow, and .hero__reveal (same-composition flower photo) — if you drop it in, that photo shows through. Showing only the flower area through the original flower-mask could not be ported

title: Renovation workshop where vertical scroll pushes five green panels sideways
good_for: One-page sites for small construction, renovation or craft companies with only services, company overview and a contact form.

pages.use: One-page company intro — behind the first-visit curtain, two photo cells crossfade. Vertical scroll pushes five horizontal screens (hero, services, company, opening photo window, contact), with scattered photo pieces, speech bubble wave lines and tool drawings. A narrow portrait window opens to fill the screen and then the contact form floats up. Stacks vertically on phone.

notes: The speech-bubble wavy lines and tool drawings (drill, tools) are redrawn as SVG of the same position and size instead of the original PNG. The paper-grain background (back.png) is swapped for a fine pattern made in Skin colors
The contact form is a static form that does not send, instead of Contact Form 7 (the send button is a round text button)
The paid brandon-grotesque was replaced with Josefin Sans, and the Japanese Zen Kaku Gothic New with Pretendard
The original first-visit curtain shows only once via sessionStorage — the copy does the same, so opening it a second time shows no curtain

title: Studio workspace on a draggable, flyable marker-shaped 3D terrain
good_for: Portfolios for game, audio and video studios, brand first screens that enter a 3D scene, and immersive sites with a sound-on entry gate.

pages.use: Home — a door to enter with sound on/off, a misty 3D terrain with water flowing between marker-shaped ridges (wheel to move forward/back·drag to orbit·click a light marker to fly in and attach, and work labels bloom like clouds). For immersive brand·portfolio heroes

Work list — rows of serif name · year · client · reel button, and behind the hovered row that work’s photo spreads with brush-stroke edges, while reel opens a video overlay. For work and case list pages

Studio About — the stage is reflected on the left, and on the dark right panel a large intro, four services, facility photos, two promises and an expandable spec list. For company and studio About pages
Contact — greeting title, one paragraph and big email address (grain underline) on the right panel, two contact buttons fixed at the bottom. For short contact pages

Work detail — hero photo blooming out to brush-stroke edges, with title, serif intro, and year / client / role rising over it, then a two-column role block, video, and a blob-shaped photo leading to the next work. For a single case study page

notes: The 3D terrain is rebuilt with a distance field of our mark (three broken rings + a diamond) and value noise instead of the original model, height field and textures. Ridges·water·fog layers·flame mark·trees·distant mountains sit in the same places, but the original’s photo-like rock grain, water refraction, color correction (color-correction LUT) and post-process bloom are absent

The original camera path (the first-scene flight built with Theatre.js) could not be read from the values inside the bundle, so it was matched by eye. It descends from a top-down marker to an angled viewpoint in 4.2s power2.inOut
After a marker click, the original’s light beam and flame burst (several charge, burst and beam proxies) is reduced to just the flame growing (.6s power2.out) and the camera approach
No sound — Enter with sound · the sound button only changes its state indicator (off↔on, wave line)
Other pages’ background replaces the original’s distant blurred view of the same 3D stage with a single shader fog layer (stage not continued — relaunched per page)

The original is a single-page app, so the stage remains after a transition — here the panel is withdrawn at .5s and raised on the next page .2s later at .8s. Once you have entered, the gate is skipped via sessionStorage

The button grain border and cloud sprite were baked on the spot with an SVG noise filter and value noise instead of the original images (grain.webp, spritesheet.webp). The pattern differs, but the frame count (60) and paging length are the same
The Technical specifications button — the original opens a panel that could not be recorded, so it is built as a spec bundle blooming like a cloud below the same panel (judgment call)
The brush grain of the photo behind work rows and the detail head photo is shader noise instead of the original brush texture — the edge scatter values were tuned by eye
The screen grain is a still image, not shimmering through scene post-processing as in the original — the measuring tool could not tell the door (loader) motion from the grain and stopped

Font backfill — the original is entirely Latin, so every title typeface (Newsreader) slot was replaced with English placeholder text, and no slot keeps Hangul. The wordmark injected by JS (header, door), the menu names (header, menu panel) and the index.js PROJECTS work names were changed too.

Body font (Figtree) spots — buttons (Enter with sound · Browse work · Back to start · Menu · Reel), eyebrow text, client names, role in the detail meta, copyright line — were left in Korean per the README. Only the wordmark is in the body font but it is logo lettering so it stays English (judgment)

Thumbnail: shot.cjs --thumb stops at the door screen, and entering with ?no-loader makes index.js listen for ow:ready late, so the first title (.hero-tag is-on) never turns on — so after pressing the door’s ”Enter silently” and letting the first scene settle, the shot was taken under the same conditions (1440×900 · jpeg 72)

Section images: library-shots shoots the gate cell first and sets it back to visible, so all later cell images get covered by the gate screen. This is a tool-side issue, so I left it alone. The tool should restore visibility after shooting a cell, or shoot the gate last.

In Detail 390, the role-columns block sits flush against the screen edge with no left margin — Korean body text behaves the same, so it is an existing layout unrelated to text length and was left as is

Sub-pages have only a fog backdrop behind the door instead of terrain, so cutting a hole shows nothing — the original is a single-page app, so the same terrain sits behind the door on every page. The overlay shader draws the marker terrain seen from above (fog color + brighter marker ridges) directly and shines it under the hole (judgment call).

The original tail-flow noise is a gray perlin image (512, mean .503 · deviation .074) tiled 4·8·16 times on screen — instead of the image, our own value-noise shader gives the same mean, deviation and grain count. When the door curtain stands, the SVG mark uses visibility:hidden, giving up only its position and fade, and the curtain draws the same two-layer outline. Without WebGL2 or a half-precision render target, the old CSS door is used with no curtain

title: Brand agency alternating black and cream stages with large caps and italic serif
good_for: Branding and advertising agency homepages, portfolios that flip through case studies like scenes, and company sites with services and a blog.

pages.use: Agency home page — an 8.8s intro (skippable) where ten photo columns open and gather while the logo strokes draw and the door closes and opens, a cream first section with a spinning asterisk and city names rolling by (they stick together, then the asterisk grows into darkness), three statement lines over a black-and-white photo that tilts toward the cursor, a regional intro, a company video where a folded screen unfolds, a pinned statement stage, a cream dictionary definition with a media logo marquee, three cream question scenes, a project stage that covers upward as the background color changes, a four-line work wall where hovering a name makes a work-photo polaroid follow the cursor, a hollow-letter specialty line, a rolling list of client names, a text line, contact over video, and a cream footer

Post list — cream header (big uppercase + italic, a star spinning between two lines), sticky glass toolbar (category chips · contents button · grid/list view), 12-column grid of black cards (first post spans 8 columns horizontally · on hover the photo brightens, the cover lifts, the top line draws and the arrow circle grows). For blog and news lists.

Service branch intro. A black head with a spinning star and five numbers, a bracketed title and description, hollow-letter specialty lines (marquee on hover), a centered italic statement, a related-work stage, two columns of what you get, and a black question accordion. For service details such as branding and advertising.
Terms and legal notice — dark background, narrow column of long text (clause headings, lists). For terms of use and privacy policy
A single article — dark photo column pinned to the left, cream body on the right (black comparison box, checklist, questions, author card, more reads). For long blog posts and guides

notes: Font: the original’s elza-condensed·ivypresto-display are paid fonts (Typekit), so they were replaced with the closest free ones, Anton·Instrument Serif — the original body is also an italic display serif, so --kf-font-sans is set to a serif.
Project stage: the original has a snap that glues to the panel via lenis scrollTo (.5s) between sections, but the part uses only scrub .6 with no snap
Company video and contact background video use same-position, same-ratio placeholders (play button shown), the sound-on button does nothing
The original hero photo’s film grain (SVG noise) is left out, only a dark overlay is kept

Declaration section: left out the original’s number of steps (sentence groups) and the per-word delay that changes with scroll speed (velocity). Only carried over steps × 100% · scrub 1 · words below 24% fade from transparent .12 → .4 with power3.out (.04 stagger)

In the hero’s Agency + word definition, the brackets, asterisk and logo are redrawn as SVG instead of the original image files. The trailing letter (trailLetter) cell left in the original CSS is not drawn by the current bundle’s CustomCursor (only dot and ring), so the copy omits it too — the 104px Scroll ring changes the cursor over [data-scrollable] panels like the original

Intro: ported the original IntroAnimation timetable (cells 0.1s · gather·stroke 2.3s · fill·label 4.8s · door 6.3s · reveal 7.2s · blur 8.3s · end 8.8s, skip jumps straight to the door from wherever it is). Left out the per-third-cell cellFlip and the logo slash drawing (film grain kept). Since the logo is a placeholder bar, the stroke drawing uses the bar outline.

Cursor carries over the original CustomCursor formula as is (dot follows at speed .15, B=min(.04×speed,.6) · ring 1−e^(−dt/70) · judged every 3 frames). After judging, the ring change is delayed by 12ms instead of the original React re-render (average measured across three pages)

Page transition: the original PageTransition (an ink-dark curtain drops in .54s to cover, then lifts in .52s on the new page, cubic-bezier(.87,0,.13,1)) is chained with a sessionStorage flag because the copy is multi-page. Even the film grain on the curtain (grain .14, 1.6s 6-step jitter) is carried over. A first page reached from within the site has no intro and only the curtain lifts, like the original

Font placeholder copy: the original is French (all Latin), so no slots remain in Korean — all Anton uppercase slots, plus the big titles·name lines set in Instrument Serif, which doubles as the body font (question scene·project names·work collection·partners·newsletter·big contact sentence·italic asides·menu tags), are in English. Body sentences such as the intro paragraph·second step of the manifesto·definitions·project descriptions·article summaries·answers·author bios stay Korean (backed by Pretendard)

Pin order: the company video and project stage part pins are attached by fx-core on DOMContentLoaded, so they were created after the index.js pins and the later sections’ starts were measured earlier by the two pin lengths (1260+3600px). The third question scene stuck at the work wall position and covered the wall. On DOMContentLoaded, ScrollTrigger.sort in document order + refresh. Motion values are unchanged

title: Home nursing company with hundreds of 3D fragments gathering into a ring
good_for: Home nursing, care and medical company sites with a big message-first company intro and a recruiting entrance.

pages.use: Company first page — loading bar and piece logo, then hundreds of silhouette pieces burst and form a 3D ring wrapping one big phrase (mouse ripple, press, scatter on scroll), a message section with big English laid beneath, an orange business section and a building line drawing drawn by scroll, parallax photo recruiting and interview rows (alternating left and right), news, a flowing photo band, contact, bottom menu. For care and medical company landings

notes: The original subpages were not recorded in the archive (pages: []), so only the first page was built

The original sprite png pieces and hand-placed coordinates are not used — our 17 silhouettes are drawn on canvas and laid out in a jittered grid (spacing 70, center ellipse 430×225), so piece shapes and density differ slightly from the original. At phone width only six per row remain, scaled .72×.

The scroll distance over which the pieces fully scatter is shorter than the original’s because the original measures the business section position while loading — seeing it vanish within 2 screens in the 390 capture, it is set to above the message section + half a screen
The original has four interviews, but they share the same form, so only two (right box · left box) are kept. The original interview text and numbers were image text

The photo strip flow is built into the site exactly as the original formula (.00025 + extra, extra ×.96, +.0002 per scroll up to a max of .003), and as a part it is marquee(dir: right; only added a source to speed: 67)

In a headless comparison the original menu panel (full-screen orange) couldn’t be captured open because the button is off-screen (140px below the bottom on phone) — built from the original css (logo 50% · two-column list · underline .2s)

title: Circus-style music festival set with a pleated theater curtain rising and falling
good_for: Multi-page event sites for music festivals, performances and theme parks covering lineup, areas, tickets and FAQ.

pages.use: Festival front page — an eye loader, a video hero covered by a pleated curtain that moves on to the fifty-year section (hat, gold coin), a bulb-frame performer wall (each row sags), video sections that open and cover the curtain, a folded accordion zone ticket band, cream ticket cards, News cards, and a gold-foil wordmark footer.
Cast list. A strip of lead cast cards flowing in waves (drag to push) and a four-column bulb-frame wall filtered by date pills. For participant lists of performances, festivals and exhibitions

FAQ — row of category photo cards, a pill strip that follows the groups read while pinned at the bottom of the screen, eight groups of open/close question rows, ticket card below. For event and service guide pages
Participant recruitment — big title with long centered intro text (paragraphs, subheadings, steps) and one apply button. For open call, application and volunteer recruitment posts

notes: The eye loader’s image sequence (78 frames at 45fps) was replaced by opening an SVG eyelid in 78 steps. The iris hole (exponential scale-up, outer 30% bleed, video .5→1x) uses the original values as they are.

The hat, wheel face and gold coin in the 50-year section are slots for 3D-rendered images in the original, so they are drawn in SVG at the same position and size. The exact range of the original scroll effect (hat floating up) could not be measured, so it is approximated (hat 35%→−95% scrub, 3s float).

The section ticket strip carries over the original fold formula (lean 3° · fold 14° · 3 waves · perspective 2.5x · springs 1Hz/.5, 1.2Hz/.55) but drops the inertia throw on release (InertiaPlugin, resistance 120rem). Instead, dragging past 15% moves one sheet in .8s main. The pill-gap bounce when the number changes is also removed.

Performer card bulbs are drawn with the color brightness of CSS bulbs, twelve × two rows (bulb-frame-lights), instead of the original’s lit bulb illustration + mask. Wave, warm-up and flicker values are the same as the original.

Section background color bleed (section-fade: the next section’s color bleeds in smoothly over .5s) is fixed to a gradient background per section, and only the cast section’s pink → indigo is moved by scrub.
On the Cast page, the By-area view (area card groups) only changes the pill while the wall stays the same. Date filtering is built.
The FAQ chat button, newsletter popup, cookie box and ticket shop links are non-functional placeholders.

barba transition blocks same-page anchors. The copy’s transition timing (261+1000ms) was set differently from the original (2371+4800ms, including a .8s wait for image decode) — the original waits until all images on the pre-transition screen are decoded.
Title Recoleta (paid) is covered by Fraunces SOFT 100, and Korean by Hahmlet 700 — line height is slightly larger than the original.

Font note: the original was Dutch and English (all Latin), so there are no Korean-kept spots. Fraunces headings, FAQ group names, news titles, and the menu, footer links, performers, sections and table names drawn by JS are all English. Performer names are the short ‹Artist 01›. ‹Artist Name 01› widened the card column because the name plate couldn’t shrink, and it overflowed by 28px at 390 width. Header buttons (menu, ticket), date pills, the FAQ group pill strip and button text use the body font (Onest), so they stay Korean

Cursor backfill fix (2026-11-12): hovering over gradient titles (pp-grad-pink, pp-grad-dark) made the letters split by char-squash-hover drop out of the h2 background-clip:text mask, so the whole title vanished (GPU-composited browsers). As in the original, each split letter now paints its own height’s share of the full-title gradient (shared.css, shared.js gradChars).

title: Motion designer portfolio with work panels circling a 3D spiral
good_for: Portfolios for motion, 3D and sound designers, personal collections of around ten works, and experimental first pages with a sound or intro gate.

pages.use: Home page: a Lottie greeting loader, then an ”Enter with/without sound” gate, and a three.js spiral where 18 work panels turn by wheel·drag (hover shows the title in a pill below). It switches between the spiral and a big-title list (the list uses cursor thumbnails), plus a menu pill drawer, a showreel badge and a sound button. For a portfolio home with few works.

About — an intro sentence pinned to the screen for 500vh lights up word by word and icons pop out in between, a strip of work thumbnails in four heights (40s), a sticker trail over large social links, a one-line credit. For personal intro · contact pages

notes: Project detail (/projects/…) was not recorded so it was not built — clicking a spiral panel or list row scatters the panels as in the original (four at a time at 30ms) and spreads them out again after .9s, and list links point to an anchor (#work-n). Whoever builds the detail page can connect a transition to this click.

Sound: the original sound effect and ambient files (.ogg) are not used. With the same howler.js 2.2.4, short sounds with the same names and volumes (hover 1·click .5·ambient .3 looped …) are baked on the fly into WAV and played. In environments with no sound device (headless), only the sound quietly turns off

Lottie: the original logo and loader are a Lottie with 3D-rendered PNGs (five faces · 75×75 · 25fps), so image files can’t be used, a shape Lottie with the same canvas size, fps and length is generated on the fly in skin variable colors. Loader text (hey!·I'm …) is HTML text placed to match the frame instead of a Lottie text layer
Fonts: Indivisible (paid Typekit) → Inter Tight. Korean placeholder in Pretendard

title: Arena introduction with a draggable 3D blueprint over a line grid
good_for: Overview pages for arenas, venues, gyms and facilities, and homepages for public architecture projects.

pages.use: Facility first page — number-strip loader, hero with title, video and news widget, draggable rotating 3D building complex, dark red-lit band, neon court teaser, news slider, number-cell marquee, photo grid

Facility About — fixed photo on the left + long text on the right (subheads, chip lists), two rows of large-type marquee, a location box, space guide + event Contact form, and a fixed wide photo strip. For facility or building About and venue rental Contact pages
News list — fixed photo on the left, intro column on the right and news rows split by lines (label · date · title · details). For notice and press lists
News item — narrow center column (label · date · lead · big title · body · prev/next) followed by a fixed horizontal photo strip. For notice · press detail

notes: The 3D complex uses our own boxes, cylinders and icosahedrons instead of the original glb models to stand up the same silhouette proportions (wide low stadium, tall tower, oval arena, low houses, trees), with white faces + gray lines (EdgesGeometry) and fog for the same blueprint tone. The original’s per-floor interior view (Piano Terra·-1·-2 with activity buttons, the phone’s floor menu) is cut down to a single-spot move ”Go inside” (1.4s lerpLookAt) and one description card — the floor menu is left for the next person to pick up
The position-move curve was not found in the original’s Vd.default bundle, so power3.inOut 1.4s is used (judgment)
Hero video and teaser video are placeholders. For the neon court video in the teaser, our SVG court is substituted, playing in the same spot with the same loop as a 9s tilt loop + line flicker.
The dark band with a red glow is a photo slot, but to keep the tone it is filled with a gradient made from skin variables (labeled)
Typeface: original APK Systema (paid stencil monospace) → Share Tech Mono, APK Narrative → Inter Tight. No stencil breaks.
The fixed horizontal band in about uses 6 photos instead of the original 9 — the band is shorter, so document height goes from the original 20613 to about 14000
Language switch (IT/EN) is shape only

title: Furniture series page where a curtain logo becomes the hero title and shrinks to a header logo
good_for: Single-page introductions of a product series such as furniture, lighting or objects, with concept, photo panels, prices, spec tables, drawings, designers and outbound links.

pages.use: A single product page: a wordmark rising from a ring loader overlaps the hero title and shrinks into the header logo on scroll, a parallax first photo, concept text with two photos, half-press photo panels (a large panel, plus a normal panel with a side panel), a detail table with three products and attached drawings, a designer section, a diagonal-arrow link row, and a full-height footer where the letters rise by depth.

notes: The recorded subpage /en has the same type as home (same Nuxt page, text only in English), so it was not built separately — the header language link (EN) is left as a placeholder.

The original does not scroll the window but moves the inner panel of .l-wrapper (overflow hidden) with its own smooth scroll (Garden Eight smooth, ease .1). It is site-specific code, so it is not used, and a Lenis with the same damping (lerp .1) was built on window scroll instead. So if you capture the original with window-scroll tools like shot or compare, only the first screen appears: the original is captured by scrolling with wheel events (/tmp/lib-paradox-series-com-fix/inner-shot.cjs, WHEEL=1) compared side by side with the copy at the same step.

The hero wordmark shrink adds at: flow to logo-dock-scrub (stays in place in document flow, scales from the top-left origin, end distance = Wordmark top − header logo top) was received, and the footer bottom wordmark received scrub-chars-rise with the fan (n×25%) and trigger options added.

The product photo plate is the original site’s own slider, so the same behavior was rebuilt as a new tap-wipe-slider part (clip polygon .75 power1.out + x 50%→0 power2.out, number .25 twice, Prev·Next label cursor height .25s). The original’s swiped-left/right (touch swipe) is replaced by a horizontal swipe of more than 40px.

The floor plan beside the detail table is our own line drawing in the same cell (square · thin lines · dimensions) instead of the original line art. The blurred preview image of lazy loading was dropped, and only the fade-in at 1s cubic-bezier(.104,.204,.492,1) when the photo slot enters the screen was carried over.
Fonts: neue-haas-grotesk-text (paid) → Inter, Japanese detail table → Noto Sans KR. Font sizes carry over the original clamp(min, value ÷ 1512 × 100vw, max) as is.

The original’s custom scrollbar (20px strip on the right, a 5px bar that goes to half width in .2s while moving, fades out over .35s starting .35s after stopping, strip hover at full width, click makes the strip the full screen width and glides to that spot) was rebuilt as the edge-scrollbar part (api: rides Lenis damping via pxLenis). The browser scrollbar is hidden.

The 1.15s blank curtain before the loader starts is the measured tempo while the app wakes up in the original, so it was moved to the ring-logo-loader delay, as in the original, the photo slot turns on only after the curtain lifts.

title: Video production company with video seen through a wordmark hole and vertical strip services
good_for: Homepages for video and ad production companies and creative studios, with director and writer rosters and profiles.

pages.use: Studio first page — 15-variant logo loader, video hero seen through a wordmark cutout in a white band, services as three unfolding vertical strips, director name line, five featured works, teal ribbon, three principles, scattered instant photos, news, drag testimonial slider, sticker contact band
Director roster — four large name rows and a video preview card that follows the cursor. For lists of directors, writers and affiliated artists
Work list — a video header that changes every 10s with a play bar, big title, list/grid toggle, 3-column work rows, sticky contact. For portfolio and case lists

About the company — hero with photo tail, a pledge that brightens line by line, two photos, four principles, ten-cell horizontally pinned scroll (philosophy·method·perspective·closing contact). For studio About and ways of working

Single director profile — red header (name · title · local time), four-cell intro, zigzag works and video window, drag-to-move photo board, FAQ accordion, collaboration inquiry, other directors. For person · creator detail pages

notes: The original’s logo, wordmark, stickers, horse illustration and “PURSUIT” illustration are original artwork, so they were not copied — they were redrawn as our own shapes (star mark, rounded band, oval badge, handwritten “Brand logo”) in the same place, size and feel. Concrete drawings like the horse silhouette were swapped for a star.
The hero wordmark is cut out with an SVG mask text (WORDMARK, screen width via textLength) instead of the original SVG artwork — changing the font changes the hole shape too
All video slots are wf-video placeholders (same position, ratio, and loop label) — no actual placeholder video files are included

The data-parallax (hero video) and data-reveal-group (service title) attributes in the original HTML have no script attaching them even in the original, so they do not move — the copy also leaves them static (as in the original)

The grid view of the work list, the other-director preview on the director detail, and the title spots in About horizontal cells 6 and 7 could not be measured from the recording, so they were matched by eye

The video window on director detail builds only the same opening (.3s .9→1x · backdrop delayed .2s · close button 2vw), with the player left as a placeholder — the original uses the video host’s Player API.
The red word change in the director’s detailed intro (#animated-word .3s fade out·in) — I couldn’t find the interval script in the archive, so I set it to 2.4s
The right photo change in the question accordion (scale 1 at is-active) could not be traced to the original script, so it is tied to hover·open and set to 1.1→1x over .6s

In the original, the button and menu letter-roll CSS (data-button-animate-chars) does not actually move because there is no script that splits the letters — the copy also changes only the background color (.4s) without a roll

notes: The original is a single page (pages: [] in pages.json), so there are no subpages.

Thin letters are hairline-thick and only half cover a pixel, so they eroded earlier than in the original — a .6px stroke around the text plate fills them past one pixel. Depth .58 is the upper limit at which everything is submerged at water stain 1 (.28) (original image .51).
The site uses three r159 (three.min.js), same as the original, so one r150+ deprecated warning line remains in the console. The part demo (tide-glyphs/demo.html) uses the warning-free r184 cjs build.

title: Chapter-pinned essay walking from cave-wall shadows out into sunlight
good_for: Interactive essays or campaign single pages that unfold a one-line idea, manifesto or brand philosophy chapter by chapter, flipping tone from dark to light.

pages.use: Section-pinned interactive essay — cave wall canvas stage, hidden question inside a cursor circle, scattering letters, horizontally flowing portraits, press-to-think circle button, sunlight quote, epilogue, section index and reading panel. For a manifesto or brand philosophy page

notes: The original is a single page (pages: [] in pages.json), so there are no subpages.

The back stage is a three (0.161.0) 3D scene like the original: camera fov 35 at (0, .3, 9), approaching 1.8 in the wall section, then retreating 16 and orbiting half a turn in rise/sun section 5. It has a bent rock-grain wall (52×32, z −6) with statue silhouette shadows shot by a fire camera (fov 62), wall words and a cursor torch, a particle statue (60k · touch 2.20k points, breathing, cursor push-away, swirl scatter, hold gather, answer burst), a cave entrance and light beams behind, plus bloom, color shift, tone and vignette post-processing, all rewritten with the original’s formulas and values. Instead of the original model (glb), the statue is a seated figure of ours built from seventeen capsules and spheres, so it has no muscle grain and only matches the silhouette proportions. Noise is our own value noise instead of the original simplex, so rock grain and breathing grain are a bit smoother. Bloom is a three-step blur instead of the original mipmap bloom.

The portrait page is a WebGL plane that follows its DOM slot like the original (two sepia tones → hover original tone · cursor ripple · color shift, revealed from the bottom with jagged light streaks within 90% of the screen, bends with scroll speed, swells when flying to the reading page). It is a placeholder with a figure outline, light and label text drawn on a canvas instead of a photo, so hover shows no original photo color. When moving to the reading page the original has a swap where the previous page ripples away (uOpacity), but here only the opacity swap of the DOM wing panel is followed.

The original’s Questions section shows 7 question-and-answer pairs, and 7 long person bios (three paragraphs, three thoughts, two quotes). These were cut down to 3 placeholder pairs and one reading panel that takes only the name from the card text (name, previous and next change per card).

The original fonts IM Fell English and EB Garamond have no Korean glyphs, so Korean body text falls back to a Korean serif pairing, and the title font slot uses an English placeholder face (see font backfill below). The wordmark placeholder is Title (5 letters), shorter than the original 6-letter wordmark, so it is slightly narrower at the same 23vw. Wall words use the title font instead of the original Instrument Serif.

Scattering word (original: everything) is 'Placeholder' As a placeholder, scattered in a single row like the original. Wall-shadow words and meta words match the number of hidden questions 'Word n' Generated automatically (words in index.js·stage.js).

Judgment call: the original nav Sound button only shows in browsers that support sound, and the copy also hides it when there is no AudioContext. With reduced motion, pinning and scrub are released and sections stack in order (the original only reduces via lerp 1 and shorter durations). If WebGL cannot be created, only the text and the light value (--light) run, with no stage.

Font backfill — the original is an English site, so 39 spots for the IM Fell English heading font were replaced with English placeholder text (Korean kept 0): five hidden questions, shadow words (down to Word n in JS), two scene sentences, big scattering words, a big quote, the rising title, seven person names (aria-label too), the closing sentence, the big question (three question-answer pairs in JS and the direct-ask input example too), the sunlight quote, the back-to-top button (also the transition curtain data-title), the maker name, six table-of-contents section names (data-title — read by the transition curtain’s big text and the nav center line), the reading panel name, the representative quote, prev/next names, and the entrance gate words and button. The Hero eyebrow section name was matched to the same text (Part One — ‹Part n›, eyebrow, body, note, responder and welcome lines are EB Garamond body font spots, so they stay Korean). The closing sentence has its word count adjusted to stay at 9 lines as in the Korean version.

The 3 lines left in latin-slots (the three body paragraphs of the reading panel) are `.ph-reader__bio p:first-child::first-letter` This is a false positive where the checker read the drop-cap rule as applying to every p — paragraphs are placeholders for the EB Garamond body, so they are kept in Korean, and only the first paragraph’s single drop cap is drawn in the heading font pairing (a Korean serif).

Two-line person name is `Person
Name 0n` With
A blank is left at the front — the reader panel name and the previous/next names read h3.textContent, so without the blank it is joined as PersonName.

title: Endless photo card grid whose gaps open on drag, with an aperture shutter
good_for: First pages for photo diaries, work collections and archives where dozens of same-shaped images are dragged around and clicked open on one screen.

pages.use: Photo archive hero — after an intro where piles of photo cards stack up and then scatter, an endless full-screen WebGL card grid flows by (drag · inertia · speed gaps · tunnel warp · card hover 1.07). Pressing a card enlarges it to the screen center and an aperture shutter closes as it moves on. For homes that show dozens of photos or works on one screen

notes: The original was recorded as only one page (pages: [] in pages.json). Tapping a card sends the original to a /photo#… detail page, but that page does not exist, so after the shutter closes it goes to the same home (index.html?photo=NN) swaps pages with swup — on arrival only the grid shows, with no intro (same path as the original re-running skipIntro after the transition). When you build a detail page, just change the card’s data-href.

The grid shader and iris blades do not use the original code — they were rewritten from measured values (_fx/card-tunnel-grid · _fx/iris-shutter). The blade shape is drawn with six tangents to the circle, so the hexagonal hole is neater than the original (blades slanting out from a point at radius 50) — the color is the same, so the seams between blades are invisible in both.

The 25 photo cards do not use the original images (png with photo and small top and bottom text baked onto a white panel), they are placeholder cards painted on canvas in the same form (white panel · 86.7% photo area · 3:2, 2:3, 1:1 ratios · label of what the photo is). To use real photos
  • Instead Add it and the part fills the cell with that photo.

About: on the left a screen-height fixed portrait (WebGL that ripples around the cursor), on the right intro sentences, contacts and two history lists. Scrolling further at the end fills the screen with a splash and moves to the first page. For solo artist About pages.
