What photo each cell holds is in the data-label of .wf-img inside .py-img.
Instead of the original noise image, four layers of value noise are baked onto a canvas — the grain of the bleeding edges differs slightly
Instead of the original EffectComposer (RenderPass+ShaderPass), one render target and one screen quad run the same post-processing shader — the results and values are the same

In the original, pressing a photo panel navigates to a category page (a horizontal list such as /lifestyle), but that page was not recorded and was not built. Pressing a panel does not navigate, and the category name links are also disabled (href=#)

Project list — a big title blurring into soft circles and 3-column square photo cards (blur per section · hover zoom), with 3-column services below. A spot for work · collaboration · product planning lists

A single project (collaboration product) — a two-photo story pin, three pinned photos that cross-fade with fixed text, text · photo · photo strip, three screen-height photos with a pinned spec (dimension table · tags · cautions), a slider of other works, and a sales box at the bottom right. notes: The originals are graphic logos (art deco wordmark, arch monogram, sub-brand logo). The original alpha was measured: 1:1 circle · solid center of 20% diameter · radius .1→.5 going 255→0 on the same curve. Size values 0→300% (hero 5 seconds) · 250% (story pin) · 350/400% (scroll) are the same.

index hero intro, story pin vertical text, ellipse intro, service branch names, detail header intro — the original is Japanese (kanji and kana) text, so Korean is kept. Pairs are already loaded: gothic → Noto Sans KR, serif → Gowun Batang.

Case list search, keywords, page numbers only look like controls and do not filter (only the first page is recorded)

The Japanese subtitles under the about · service · works · news section titles (pc-sub__ja) and the index service · work subtitles (pc-ja) — the original is in Japanese (About Us · What We Can Do · Projects We Have Worked On · Newsletter), Korean kept
Name column of the about company table items (Company name·Founded·CEO …) — the original is Japanese, Hangul kept

Three institution-name lines below the index hero — the original uses a kana subtitle, Hangul kept. Noto Sans KR (sans-serif ↔ gothic) as the pair after Montserrat is already loaded

title: Studio entered through a 3D window over line-drawing paper
good_for: Digital agency and 3D studio homepages where a first-screen portal leads into intro and work in a WebGL set, with a draggable curved work carousel.

pages.use: Studio home page — a number-cell loader folds into a center window, and only inside the window on pencil-line paper are raw 3D objects visible. Scroll once and the camera looks down on the Work carousel below, the window name rolls from About to Work, and clicking the window opens that page

Studio About — a big intro sentence on a black 3D stage, large ”How we work” text where objects bounce and fall, four pinned services with drag-to-rotate 3D models, a horizontally flowing photo story, two columns for awards and clients, and a progress bar that carries on to Work when you scroll further at the bottom
Work list — full-screen curved WebGL carousel moved by drag or wheel (10 panels, slowly drifts on its own, mouse parallax), center work name at bottom left, ten-cell tick scale below
Contact — stage of items floating over pencil-lined paper, with email and phone lines set large, office address and social links at bottom right

notes: The original GLB models (keycap, hand, headphones, balloon dog) are replaced with our basic shapes (extruded rounded rectangle, capsule, torus, cylinder) of the same size and silhouette ratio — the pencil-line texture is simpler than the original, and face directions use smooth normals so round bodies get no hatching (the original uses flat shading on a dense model).

Opened via file://, barba can’t fetch neighboring pages, so it plays the same transition (window open · camera · fold · motion blur), then moves the address, and the new page starts in the state where the transition has finished (objects are placed anew). Opened over http(s), barba 2.10.3 keeps the canvas as is and swaps only the box.
On phones (coarse pointer), tilt-sensor physics, the hero virtual scroll and center-panel name picking were not carried over — the phone follows the original only up to 10 objects · no push-away.
The original’s cookie banner and analytics scripts were not carried over.

Work panel photos and videos are canvas panels describing subject, light and composition — the original’s video panel playback (only the center three play) was not hooked up since the placeholders are drawings

Typeface placeholder note: the original site is entirely in Italian Google Sans Flex, so the slogan, large About title, large Approach sentence (including the three chips), service names, detail items, award and client name rows, work names (including placeholders in pages.js and shared.js), contact questions, menu, buttons, cursor text and portal names were replaced with English placeholder text. latin-slots only caught the 8 portal name slots, and the rest were found by taking page screenshots and checking by eye. There are no title slots that were Chinese characters or kana in the original.

Body and description slots (two hero intro lines, work intro, about lead, service description, one-line work description, four company info lines on the contact page) are Latin in the original too, but Korean is kept per the README

Reveal-text splits lines by measuring letter widths. Measured before the web font Google Sans Flex arrives, the split used fallback font widths, so in the About big title changed to English, single words (make·three) dropped to the next line — a problem hidden in Korean because the system sans was used. Before splitting lines, we now check whether that text’s font has fully arrived (document.fonts.check), and if not, split after it is loaded — only shared.js initReveal was changed. If the font is already there, order and timing stay the same
The awards row wraps to two lines on phone (390) — sized for the original text length (43~63 chars), so the original wraps too

title: One-page scroll story descending with a sinking bottle
good_for: Campaign, environmental message and data storytelling single pages, and feature pages that show numbers and photos in order over a long scroll.

pages.use: One-page scroll story — on a stage stuck to the screen a bottle spins and sinks for 10 screens, followed by glass number cards, a depth-counting number, a white section that opens through a bottle-shaped hole (four steps), a big sentence that blurs while fish and a whale cross, a split screen, three lines of animal stats, stacking photo cards, a plate sentence with a growing circle (letters fill in one by one), a closing photo that opens as a circle, and a glass-panel footer. For a campaign or feature on one page

notes: This is a photo-driven site — the sea, bottle and animal photos and cutouts (bottle, fish, whale) are all placeholders, and the bottle is drawn as a same-ratio silhouette (SVG). The bottle-shaped hole is also our same-ratio silhouette instead of the original bottle image

Matched by eye because they could not be read: the range where the three hero background layers scale up (data-scale-up, set to 1 to 1.7x over 0 to 300vh), the range where the bottom text and menu button recede (data-scroll-anim=bottom-texts·menu — fade out over 0~50vh and move −50vh together with the title), data-scroll-speed on the animal cards=0.7 (a slowly-following value — not included). These three belong to the original’s hidden embed script, so the archived DOM had no code

Scrub lag (original smoothing 0.3~2 — some scenes follow the scroll 0.3~2 seconds late) is added only for the end section’s circle hole (0.2s), and the rest is left to Lenis smoothness alone. The next person can split this out by per-scene scrub values.

The sudden jump between bottle keyframes (the original setting breaks and resumes the width from 71→64 and 56→51 at 9%, 19% and 29%) was stitched together — treated as a mistake in the original setting and smoothed out

The whale section’s text color inversion (dark ink text visible only where the bottle photo covers it, clip sync) and the original SVG mask (cutting the photo in letter shapes) were not built, a single white text passes through instead

Menu overlay: only the structure was carried over, where pressing an item switches to its detail view and Back returns. The original’s per-item text motion (data-menu-text) is a builder script and couldn’t be read.

For construction and installation case details

notes: In the original, clicking a cover goes to that year’s contents page (not recorded), but our replica has only three subpages, so the six covers are linked in rotation to article, experience article and case. The transition curtain (1.5x zoom → a panel in that year’s color covers the screen while the background drifts sideways → on the next page it shrinks into the masthead slot in 1 second and lifts away in 3 seconds) uses the original values

Instead of the original cover illustration (an image file, so not carried over), the cover and transition curtain backgrounds were redrawn as SVG with a different pattern each year (flowers, color blocks, white doodles, plant pots, circles, buildings). It has fewer props than the original

The article header title (in the original, a hand-lettered image) is set in bold text, and the handwritten title is written by 31 mask strokes passing over Gaegu text at .07s intervals (in the original, stroke masks of the lettering image)

The original cookie consent window and analytics were not built

Scroll effects and first visuals on sub-pages are hooked after load, like the original

notes: From the end of 2026-10 the original site has shown ”Under maintenance” (503), so the archived copy (recorded 2026-11-09) was a blank page. Because of that, the subpages were not recorded (pages.json is empty) and only the first page was built. Original screens, code and motion values were measured and compared using the Web Archive 2026-07-11 snapshot (timestamp 20260711205340) as the source address. The poster background is a grid of color blocks in the same cells (147×213.8, five rows making 1069px) instead of an image

title: Pharma company site with growing diamond windows and glass shapes
good_for: Corporate homepages, business overviews and careers pages for technical or manufacturing companies that want weighty pinned-scroll staging.

pages.use: Company home — glass bubble shader hero · scroll video in a growing diamond window and number row · pinned section where the We know title sits on a paragraph · four key pillars with rings being drawn · glass circle/square split · lifecycle numbered rows · pipeline table · team · news cards · join · contact · bottle reveal · footer

About the company — dark header with bubble band · pinned journey section where the center text changes as four photos come in · purpose · people grid · horizontally flowing history band · glass square numbered row (work attitude) · contact

Careers — header with glass capsules drifting at different speeds, intro text that rises along with them, glass-square attitude rows, horizontal people strip, team photo, and pinned apply steps with a vial in a turning circle
What we do — a head where the attached video halves and shapes are revealed · how we work · three overlapping branch cards where the front card shrinks and blurs · glass-crack contact

notes: The original hero is a scene editor (Studio) image, so it was redrawn with our WebGL shader (thin glowing rims and spectral dispersion on two big bubbles). Bubble positions and sizes are measured from the original 1440×900 settled screen (upper bubble bottom edge 78%, lower bubble top edge 64%), and the rim glow is brighter than the original. The About band and Contact window pass different position values to the same shader

The original glass (glass-*.js) is a WebGL2 bundle specific to that site, so we wrote our own shader with the same values (refraction 1.45, dispersion .06, fresnel .35, bevel 26/5.7, tilt .28/.4). Like the original it refracts the text and video behind it, but on file:// drawing a video panel taints the canvas, so only the background color is refracted.

The four scroll-scrubbed videos (diamond window 15s · spiral 10s · journey 12.7s · what we do 11s) and the bottle reveal video are placeholder videos with the same ratio and length. The 16 bottle-cap renders are 16 of our own medicine bottles drawn with canvas
The We know vial blur is produced by video compositing in the original, so it was matched on screen to clear from 24px → 0 between .22→.55 (rotation · appearance .22 are original values)

The About journey section matches pencil-like details of the original (unicorn band width, order the four photos enter) by eye — fixed 2.5 screens, scrub 1.2, text change .8s expo.out, diamond -180°→0 1s are original values
The careers page open positions list (CMS grid) and the What We Do page partner globe (globe-v1.js) were not built — the globe is a WebGL bundle exclusive to that site

// Opened via file:/ , Barba can’t read the next document, so it plays the same push · darkening (1.2s parallax curve), and after swapping documents the new page rises over from 100vh below — over http, Barba works as is

_study/probe/growing-diamond-window-pharma/-1440 is an original record measured without a page name because of a shell word-splitting mistake — it is outside /tmp so it was not deleted. It does not show up in the gate lines

The hero bubble shader is a still image (cursor-sweep original response 0% · gate 0). The original scene does not react to the cursor, but a few seconds after appearing the lower bubble slowly moves up and down, changing the lens size (transition film 1.6~3.1s, first-load film 8~13s). If needed, drive u_c2 with time. On the first page after a transition, as in the original, the heading rises and the scene appears .25s later

title: Street festival page with toy-city scenery, character crowds and a UFO parade
good_for: Month-long multi-venue street festivals, cultural events or pop-up collections that need categorized event cards, schedules, maps and campaigns on one page.

pages.use: A street festival single page — an opening screen where a three-tier logo bounces up, a key visual with 16 characters each moving on its own, an About letter board in category colors, a row of tilted UFOs, event cards filtered by category pills (click for a large image modal), a giant logo marquee divider, a drag-to-flip schedule, a map with place chips, pins and a panel, a thumbnail campaign slider, a logo list, and a footer with a UFO fleet sky. A fixed left menu and a favorites list follow along

notes: The original is a single page (pages: [] in pages.json), so there are no subpages. Event details are in a modal (.l-program_modal) that opens when a card is clicked, as in the original.

The original’s 3D-rendered character, UFO, city and cloudy sky were redrawn as SVG (specular radial-gradient) in the same position, size and tone — the original is not WebGL either but pre-rendered images (webp), so there is no 3D scene. Depth and texture are flatter than the original. Rows of artwork-native colors carry ”Not skin” (the character stays the same when the skin changes, and disappears when an image is inserted).

The logo and section titles are hand-drawn SVG lettering in the original, so Unbounded 800 stands in. At the same letter height it runs about 15% wider than the original (LOGO IS HERE 525px vs POP IS YOU 447px). The flower-shaped O in the original logo was redrawn as a new SVG shape (#c-flower).
Event cards were cut from the original 20 to 12 (one giant logo break after six) — document height 1440 at about 8600px versus 10610px.

The original map is a web map service (gmp-map) with pins on top, so a street map was drawn as SVG. Dragging, +/− zoom, pin and chip selection and panel list changes are the same, but there are no real map tiles. As in the original, the image cursor is hidden over the map.

The language drawer only changes the label when picked, the text stays the same (the original swaps text in five languages — that is content, so it was not carried over). The hero clock shows the event city’s local time like the original (Intl, data-tz default Asia/Tokyo) — when using a different city <time> Only change its data-tz.

Swiper version: the original bundle shows no version, so I picked one by fingerprint. It has snapToSlideEdge and lazyPreloaderManaged, which 12.0.3 lacks, and navigation has arrowSvg, so it is 12.1 or later. 12.1.2 and 12.2.0 share the same core (only the a11y module differs, and the original does not ship a11y), so I use the 12.1.2 already in place. As in the original, swiper css is not included.

The original LP’s neon artwork (title plates, benefit illustrations, scene illustrations, mascot, back-to-top wing) is all static images, so we redrew it as SVG line art in the same position, color and weight. The hero video slot hangs a placeholder video of the same 16:9·60 seconds (media/kv-movie.mp4, silent audio track) in place of the original YouTube video (60 seconds), with the same behavior. The LP column is written as 375px and below 500px it fits the screen width with zoom (the original converts the same dimensions to vw — same ratio, only text rendering rounding differs).

Device search on product does not call the server list — 'Search'Pressing it shows six placeholder result lines immediately like the original, and only the .3s swing scroll 40px above them is the same (the original filters the cells by manufacturer using the chosen OS, carrier and manufacturer. The rule that hides the main site header bar when scrolling down (past 2/3 of the screen and heading down, top .2s ease-in-out) is exactly the original _header.js. The original writes the value to window.scrollY instead of a local variable and uses it as the previous position, so even with the same rule the comparison captures showed product not hiding and service hiding — we could not confirm which one is intended.

libs: lenis@1.0.33 (@studio-freight/lenis — same version as the original, duration 1.2 · expo-style easing)
webgl (the bloom plate is a hand-written shader — the original uses the UnrealBloomPass from the three example)

pages.use: Walk-in 3D house portfolio — scrolling becomes steps: arched door → living room → gallery → water garden → desk room, with wall lettering, a monitor and framed work, and a contact card. For 3D·spatial creators and showroom-style one-page introductions

notes: The original four rooms are baked GLB (38MB) and lightmaps. Since the rule is not to use model or texture files, they were rebuilt from basic shapes plus canvas drawings in the same composition, prop layout and colors — realistic shadows, reflections, wood grain, cloud texture, stair marble reflections, and prop counts (books, plants, waterside trees) are fewer and simpler than the original. The wooden figure is also a capsule and sphere doll instead of the original character model.

The camera path doesn’t use the original GLB camera clip. It joins 24 keyframe positions, matched by sampling the original in 16 divisions, with Catmull-Rom (index.js KEYS). The original clip values are tied to the original model’s coordinate system, so placing them as is on a room newly built from basic shapes throws the composition off. To match it, the room would have to be rebuilt in the original coordinates. Position versus progress is matched, but the original’s subtle head sway and curves differ.

The white curtain when pressing a name (original menu-transition: 2.5s ease-in-out, rises 0→33% to cover, stays until 66%, then leaves) was built with the original css values. The original script is obfuscated, so the moment it jumps to the first position could not be read, and the jump happens at the covered moment (the 1/3 point). The nav menu jumps in one go to the scroll positions Work 51.35% · About 16.04% · Contact 100%, like the original (measured).

On wide screens (over 960px) the monitor screen uses a video texture, as in the original (media/screen.mp4 — a placeholder video of the same 16:10 ratio, looping 9s, played directly with play()), on phones it is a still image. Opened via file://, WebGL cannot read the video because it is cross-origin, so the same 9s loop (the frame changes every 3 seconds) is drawn on a canvas instead.
neulis-sans (paid) was replaced by Montserrat, and Korean text by Noto Sans KR. Contact card icons are link · code · business card · mail shaped SVGs instead of the original SNS logos.

Font backfill: since the original text is all English, every Jost·Montserrat spot was swapped for English placeholder text — loader text·header pill (name·three menu items·Menu)·phone menu (name·Close·four section names·copyright line)·Hero greeting pill·two-line title·three intro lines·3D wall text (living room keyword·two-line phrase, three disc keywords, three exhibition wall keywords, water garden’s four vertical words·three small keywords, book title)·contact card label·title·copyright line. No title font spots are left in Korean

Judgment: the three hero intro lines are explanatory sentences, but since the original sets them as English sentences in the title typeface (Jost), they were swapped for English filler (same call as the backfills elsewhere). Monitor thumbnail cell labels (text drawn on a canvas from data-label) are photo caption labels, so they were left in Korean.

Work list — giant two-line title, categories and view toggle, video cards in one full-width cell + two half cells, fullscreen player view. For video portfolio lists

Company · team intro — one pinned stage: giant title with video showing through · horizontally flowing white half-and-half cells · efficiency panel and testimonial · magenta team panel (click to enlarge). For production company intros
Client logo wall — endlessly continuing, convexly curved logo cells (drag, wheel zoom) · click for a client drawer. For client and partner list pages

notes: The fonts are paid (Neue Haas Grotesk Display Bold · PP Eiko Light Italic), so they were substituted with Inter Tight 800 · Cormorant Garamond 300 Italic. Big titles, menu and name lines are English placeholders, so the original’s narrow, dense all-caps flavor survives, but paragraphs set in Korean fall back to Pretendard.

Font backfill — the original uses a single Latin typeface site-wide (Neue Haas Display Bold + Eiko italic), so besides the 10 italic emphasis spots the regex check caught (the heading-font variable only applies to italic serif), I found by eye and changed to English the large headings, menus, buttons, bracket tags, work/brand/client/team name lines, logo-slot text and cursor text that are set in Inter Tight. Paragraphs, descriptions and list sentences (value, promise, efficiency lines, reviews, address) stay Korean per the README — a judgment call

All videos are 16:9 placeholder videos in the same spot (media/*.mp4), timed to the lengths measured on the original — Home showreel 5.04 · 5.38 · 6.01 · 5.05s (no loop, next work starts .9s before the end), work list 5~6s (plays and loops only within 100px inside the screen), full-screen loop, About 10.03 · 8s, Footer 9.53 · 10.07s. Only the black-and-white videos in the Home brand list could not be timed because the original loads them late (never loaded during measurement) — the four showreel videos are reused, and the progress bar and auto-advance follow those video lengths.

The hero transition (a square window spreading from the center in .9s cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1), scene 2→1×, purple, lemon and mint color matrix) uses the original values as is. The original applies a filter to the whole stage with an feFlood mask sized to the window, while here the filter is applied to the single opening window (the visible result is the same)

Intro 'Letter hole' The screen draws sentence words on a canvas at the same position and typeface as the original and cuts them out (English placeholder text, so the hole thickness matches the original too). From the second visit in the same tab, like the original, it skips the intro and opens with a magenta band transition (sessionStorage).

Phone (≤991) home uses the original’s 'Only the panel movement is tied to scroll, text plays when the panel enters'…was followed, but the original’s in-screen baseline (.9) and revert-threshold calculation were reduced to 20%·50% scroll-progress thresholds — the next person should port the original index script’s entryLine · hysteresis formula.

The About page’s single-stage timeline (original scrub .45, document height 30481px) was rebuilt with the same length, panel order and easings, but the original’s fine devices — a different square rotation per cell (180°), the surfing cell height calculation, the two-tier overlapping wait of the title under the gray panel, and the team card travel-distance calculation — are approximations. Not all of the discriminant expressions in the original About script (about 49KB) were ported — the next person should continue porting the per-panel at and distance expressions from the big timeline script in about-us.

Of the About hero 'Press and hold' The magnifier was built with the original on-hold-rectangle numbers (2026-11-11) — a 280×180 window follows the cursor with x .46s and y .56s power3.out and stays confined inside the plate, and on press the 28px cursor frame widens to window size over .4s power2.out (press 1.08× in .18s → back.out(1.4) in .36s) and switches to a white frame. Inside is a black and white (contrast 1.65) version of the hero video redrawn coarsely in 4px cells (70×45) plus a pink 72% multiply and a 6px halftone dot 52%, with the group of center squares rotating -22°→8°→-2°→0°. On release it folds back to the cursor in .4s power3.inOut. The original also shows the magnifier at length 0 under reduced motion, but per the README it is turned off under reduced motion and on phones (≤767 and touch), and the ”Click & Hold” hint text is not added either — a judgment call. The window interior is darker than the original because the gray placeholder video goes through contrast 1.65 and the pink multiply (in the original a bright sky shows through as pink).

Pressing a card in the Work list takes the original to a Work detail page, but details were not recorded, so here the same work 'Fullscreen' Opens in view mode. The full screen loops the chosen work video like the original, the progress bar and scene cells follow the video position, and pressing a scene cell moves it to center that cell. The original hover strip that paints up to the mouse position over the progress bar (work__full-screen__selected__timeline-hover — gives left·width·opacity from the end of the current spot to cursor x) was not built: no rule for this class exists in the original css bundle or the page inline css, so it is an empty div with no height or background and not visible on screen (confirmed during the 2026-11-11 cursor backfill).

The client logo wall is rebuilt with our own shader on the same three 0.165.0 instanced plane as the original (10×6 cells, bend .4 · phone .55, camera z 5.5↔2.5, cursor dome .15 · 1.5 cells, logo parallax · .85x while dragging · row intro, 125-cell halftone). Only the logo art is our own shapes and lettering placeholders (12 kinds), and the original’s per-logo visual corrections (enlarge and overlap fixes for two of the logos) were dropped because those logos are absent.

The [Director] and [Location] in the menu — because the original page was not recorded '#' Left as a no-op (pressing stays in place with no transition). The language switch is dimmed and blocked, like the original.

The logo uses two lines at the same position and size (152×42) instead of the original wordmark 'LOGO° / STUDIO' A placeholder, and the original per-letter wave (-3.8px·-5°, x-proportional delay .3s) is applied as is.

Header and cursor were re-tuned to the original values — the cross cursor is always visible (the original has no rule hiding it), snaps on at the next frame, and only the text trails behind by 10% steps. The transition band and cursor come before the header in DOM order. [Work] is an expand button marked ‹#› like the original (the current-page marker is the first line of the expanded menu). Header links keep the original English text widths (49·78·61·78·53·38·84px) as minimum widths so positions and gaps match the original. The original that stretches to wrap small links 'hold-morph' was not built — someone else should carry over the is-hold-morphing step values from the original cursor script.

notes: Showreel (2026-11-18 redo, reel.js) — built ShowreelHoverPreview·VideoPreview·VideoPlayerModal·HeroMobile with the same numbers. Hero preview: video A (colorful) and B (showreel scenes) are blended by our shader along a noise boundary (feather .18, cross .3, flow warp .32, cursor pull exp(−4d)×.12, color split .033, hue .5, still keeps .22 even at mix 1). On play button hover the mix goes to .92 over 1.4s power2.out (power2.in on release), follow .18 per frame, cursor .12, plate 1.05x (.6s/.5s power3.out). On press it bursts (.07s power3.out rise, .9s power3.in fall, ×1.05, scanlines .002). When the video grows on scroll, the main film (4.5~63s) is revealed along the same boundary (5s sine.inOut back when the window closes). On press a black cover 1.2s power2.in → at 1.45s it jumps to the end of the Hero → from 1.7s it uncovers over 1s power2.out. Window: wrapper Flip 1s power3.inOut fills the screen, main film is video.js 8.23.4 (_vendor, Apache-2.0, same version as the original), volume .4, control buttons .5s power3.out, time text 1.5s roll, progress bar (hover line, press jumps to that spot), end screen (controls .35s power3.in stagger .06, progress line .7s power3.inOut wipe, title 1.1s roll, two buttons .6s back.out(1.6)), the menu button becomes a ”Close” button (.8s roll after .9s), Esc closes, close uses Flip .7s power3.out. The menu panel video (dot pattern, cross, play button) opens the same window. Videos are our placeholders (reel-preview-a·b 8s loops, reel 67s — baked with ffmpeg). Judgment: the original shader code was not copied, only the numbers — the noise function and hue rotation (YIQ plane) are our own, so the texture differs slightly. The same preview was also extracted as the _fx/reel-morph-preview part (bare WebGL).

Loader (2026-11-18): original Loader — a 48px logo over fog cycles through 15 frames at 12fps. At the end of a loop, if resources (load, fonts, Hero preview video, max 4s) have all arrived, after .3s it shrinks over .5s power3.out and clears at .3s → then the page entrance runs and the fog rises over 2s. On desktop, a “Click to enable sound” cursor (six lines rising and falling .4 to .8s inside a 48px circle) appears at 75% height in .2s power2.in and follows the cursor at .3s power3. On phone the first page shrinks after 1.6s. The 15 logo frames are our logo spun as if breathing (instead of the original logo Lottie)

The WebGL bulge on Work card photos (bulge-image-scene) was added with a three shader only to the About team photos and the Work list (radius .95 · strength .7 · .65s/.8s). The home-page Work cards only have a glow around the panel (canvas bleed) and a 1.012x hover.

Background 48px → panel (75% of screen, min 560) 1s expo.inOut, logo 4·10·.72x → 16·16·1x 1.1s, MENU→CLOSE roll 1s, icon 45°, clip inside the panel bottom→top 1s, name erased .3s (+.3), first page plus four menu rows .5s with .07 stagger from the end (+.4), lines 1s power2.inOut (+.1), Let’s talk clip .7s (+.5), closing runs in reverse. The logo plays the same 15-frame flip as the loader at 1.25x (1s), forward and back. The Hero follows HeroMobile: a full-bleed main video plays silently (dot pattern), and tapping anywhere restarts it from the beginning with sound .4. The pill’s logo and name are erased .5s (gap .1), button width 42 · radius 21 .8s power4.inOut, icon 45°, play button .5s to 0x, dot pattern 1s; Pressing again or scrolling down more than 20% of the screen reverses it. Company overview — mission statement, three photos of different sizes (parallax), overview table, number-box results, history rows. For About and Overview

notes: The original card’s libs listed lenis, but it isn’t in the bundle and only ScrollSmoother (smooth 1.5, effects, normalizeScroll) is used. Hooked up the same thing with the ScrollSmoother from _shared/vendor.

Light refraction video (light.mp4) and section-head icon video (icon.mp4) are same-length looping placeholder videos made with ffmpeg gradients (media/)
Company intro material (embedded Google Slides) is drawn only as slide-shaped slots of the same size — there is no real document viewer
The light photo on the keyword card band (three rotated) was redrawn as a gradient rainbow band — that line is marked ‹Not Skin›

The first image-transition curtain (soft-edge-page) lifts as soon as it attaches with on: ready, because the skin’s web fonts (Inter, Noto Sans KR) arrive late and waiting for font readiness would keep the curtain up longer than the original. title: Studio paragraph where words get painted by scroll and images wake between lines
good_for: Intros for small studios, agencies and solo producers that explain what they do in one long paragraph and keep work in a bottom-pill overlay.

pages.use: Studio first page — one big paragraph painted word by word on scroll, while an app icon pile, team faces, reel thumbnails, seven transforming field words, product pieces, score badges, a calendar and hand stickers wake up in turn between the text lines. A bottom pill opens the work video overlay (client description cell).

A single hiring post: below four paragraphs of job text, three tilted illustration cards where work images are dragged and dropped or clicked to upload, and a bottom pill that leads into name and email steps. Sits at the top right ”Hiring” pill spot of the first page

notes: Every illustration cell in the original is a Rive (.riv) state machine: seven category words (design, engineering, branding, copywriting, video, 3d, interaction), product, score, calendar and finger, three hiring cards (application.riv), and four overlay gesture icons (gestures.riv). The Rive runtime is MIT, but .riv art can only be built in the Rive editor and the original .riv files cannot be used. So they were redrawn in the same place and size (canvas 148×64, 221×64, 190×64, 216×80, 112×64, 400×493, 300×80, 120×100, 100×120, 200×171, 80×80) with our own SVG, CSS, canvas 2D and GSAP timelines. They turn on at the same moment as the original (Active turns on when the cell is painted, and rewinds at double speed when it goes off).

The inner detail order of Rive (the order in which letters turn into outlines, teal cursor speed, when the chrome letters are stamped, dust eraser and handwriting length, when the selection box size pill turns on and off) is a guess matched by eye from captures of the original at 0·150·300·500·800·1200·1800·3000ms. The chrome letters and handwriting use Inter 800 gradient and Caveat 700 for the same feel instead of the original artwork.

3D word: the original 3d.riv takes the cursor over a wide area and tilts the thickness direction (cursor on the left, thickness slants down-left). Our canvas tilts the thickness away from the cursor, from the center of the panel, and follows by .12 each frame — the tilt amount and speed are guesses matched against two original images.

Videos (reel thumbnail at the end of the first paragraph, overlay show reel and work recording) are placeholders (wf-video) in the same spot and ratio. Once painted, the reel shows it is playing only by the progress bar below (6s loop), and the overlay video stands still.

The overlay work was cut down from the original 32 videos and 8 clients to a showreel + seven videos from three clients (one row spans two cells). Pill widths reuse the original item widths (220·190·200·180…) with placeholder titles only. The review line in the client description cell appears only on the second client. Original address ?work=open uses pushState, we use replaceState.

The paragraph cell count matches the original at 116 cells (words·pictures·gaps·12 trailing blanks), so the painted progress is the same. Because the Korean placeholder has a different word count, the picture cell indices differ from the original by ±1 (team 5·reel 20·field 28~36·product 69 (original 70)·score 85 (86)·calendar 92 (93)·hand 103 (104)). As in the original, the pill rises when cell 20 lights up.

framer-motion springs are solved with the same formula (findSpring: damping ratio 1−bounce, end-of-length wobble .001) and used as GSAP curve functions (shared.js rbMotion). Default transform spring is stiffness 500 · damping 25.

Recruit page: the original uploads an image to a server and sends it through three fields of name, email and link. Ours shows the image only within this screen (sent nowhere) and is cut down to name → email → send (only the text changes) — the link field was dropped.

The logo does not use the original mark. It is drawn as our own mark — a rounded square with a round hole — plus a lowercase wordmark placeholder. The app icons in the first-sentence card stack are color tiles rotated from the accent color + our mark.

Font backfill — where a Latin font (Cormorant Garamond · Fira Sans Condensed) is the first font, the text was already English when first built (logo · Our Vision · Name Surname · Service 01 · product · Join Us, etc.), so nothing was changed

Serif slots on all pages (small title under a section·big serif phrase·name line·service·job title·FAQ question·button·Korean menu line) — the original uses a Japanese serif with text led by kana·kanji, like ‹Results are the real strength.› and ‹SEO Marketing›, Korean kept (paired with Noto Serif KR 400–700)

The 171 lines remaining in latin-slots are all the serif slots above — the checker reads even the display in the fallback variable var(--kf-font-mincho, var(--kf-font-display)) inside the font value as Latin. Run with a copy fixed to look only at the first variable and it gives 0

pages.use: Recruit landing page — a hero with a screen-wide headline over people photos that curl up diagonally and swap every 5 seconds (three lines of white-strip voice copy), a manifesto whose curtain lifts line by line, chevron section titles over four mask-card Teams and a ring slider of people cards (click opens an interview window), a showreel video, a diagonally cut workplace photo, three recruiting info cells, two slanted apply buttons and a floating yellow Entry. People list: a header with a wide photo strip of people standing and flowing to the right, table-of-contents anchors, mask-card four teams and eleven people (click to open an interview window), four blog feature article cards. For a recruiting site’s ”Get to know our people” · employee introduction lists

Work intro — eight service photo tiles, four color-bordered circles (challenges solved), a work flow of four step boxes with job-colored arrow lines, four collapsible job-type lists, and four numbered strength boxes. For business and job intro pages

About the company — CEO greeting (photo + text), number boxes (donut, ranking, big number, bar), a three-branch icon policy accordion and three must-know photo cards, a workplace photo fade auto slider, purpose statement, company overview table, sustainability banner. For About and company-by-numbers pages

One team interview — a screen-fixed field photo blurs tied to scroll while a white article column rises from 76vh below, with a quoted title · heading · member intro · face-circle conversation · four people who joined · back link. For interview and case detail articles

notes: swup swaps only #hk-swap, so instead of per-page css and js, every page loads one set of pages.css · pages.js (the original also has one styles.css · bundle.js). Motion that differs per page is attached with HK.page(name) and removed on navigation. The header bar, menu, first-visit cover and transition cover stay outside the swapped area (the original replaces all of #wrap).

Hero tagline (the original is three bold handwritten-style SVG graphics) is set as three pieces of text in the decorative face Black Han Sans (--kf-font-catch), and of the original 11 people photos only 5 are kept (same shuffle, same tempo).

The person interview window (modal) has the same form for every person, so it is built once on first open from a single template and only the job title and name are moved over from the card. The original window’s ‹Favorite things› group and career timeline cells are not included.

The showreel (the original is a muted looping video embed) is only a 16:9 placeholder video box — no playback, no modal. The blog feature article cards (the original loads them from a CMS API) are four static ones.

Know the company: the original graph images (avif), seven case icons, pickup text and some office detail links were trimmed. Number boxes are redrawn as donut (SVG stroke), bar (css) and big number, and the three drafting icons are newly drawn as line SVGs.

The original recruit pages (under /recruit/: who we seek · job types · application guidelines) were not recorded, so they were not built — the menu’s Recruit Info links to #recruit on the home page. Only one interview detail was built, in the recorded interview01 shape.
The logo (Brand joined lettering) is a BRANDNAME English wordmark placeholder, and the round tag at the card’s top right (the original is an artwork of the join year) is a ”00 JOIN” text tag.
The four person-card masks (wave · diamond · rounded square · circle) were redrawn with our own SVG paths in the same 270:250 cells as the original.

The company About page is shorter than the original (about 9800px tall) — only one set each of the number boxes and the drafting-icon row is used. Reveal is not applied to the human-written text cards or the must-know card group, as in the original (the original draws them in via API, so it has no reveal).

title: Graduate recruiting site with flying-stroke headline and a red wedge covering the screen
good_for: Graduate and mid-career recruiting sites led by staff interviews and project stories, or campaigns using black-and-white photos with a single accent color.

pages.use: Careers first page — a Lottie big title where strokes fly in and settle one by one (scroll lock) and a fixed stage where a red wedge covers the screen on scroll, white text lines, a people-card drag slider, case rows, business·HR cards, a CEO message band. For recruiting and brand first screens that push a single accent color

Employee interview list — keyword · category filter sticky on the right (tab panel on phones), headcount, four-column person cards (triangle unfolds on hover). For lists filtering people · cases by condition
Project story list — big serif title row + number, name and description on the right + cut-out photo at bottom center with a triangle that unfolds when visible, READ button. For case and story lists

Project story — a hero with a map-pattern background that slides (triangle unfolds), four members, a timeline with popping dots, a fixed left table of contents (current section red, click to jump) with long body text, a full-bleed photo band and the next Work. For Work detail and long-form articles

One employee interview — header text (tagline · keywords · name) over a dark hero sticks to the left and follows, turning black once past the hero, right-hand Q&A body with parallax photos, four other interviews. For interview and people detail pages

notes: The big Hero title is a Lottie re-baked from the original Lottie (60fps, 145 frames). It keeps the original frame slots and curves (each stroke tilts 40° and settles with 0.7473× decay, straight strokes unfold over 17 frames, the wedge grows over frames 99~115 and rotates -88°→10°→-1°→4°→2° over frames 107~143), and only the glyphs are replaced with our placeholder (Noto Sans KR Black strokes) (lottie/make.py → hero.js). Unlike the original’s brush strokes drawn one by one, the units are font outlines (holes attach to the outer stroke), so stroke count and shapes differ

The scroll effect where a wedge covers the screen runs with the wedge-flood-scroll part using the same values (cover width 7365px · top end -1140px · center -100px · 8° · power2.inOut within progress .25 · stage height × .3). Unlike the original, the wedge path is not lifted out of the Lottie — an svg wedge in the same position and shape as the Lottie end shape is placed in advance and swapped in when the Lottie finishes (is-build)

The people slider is the original site’s own code (not a library), so it was rebuilt with the same values: 270px per slot · .4s cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1) · 10px drag · .35 end resistance · .15 slot flick threshold · .4px/ms fling · buttons move by the number of slots visible on screen

The menu pages for CEO·HR MESSAGE·Business Areas·Job Guide·Benefits·Recruiting Info·Q&A were not recorded, so they were not built — they link to the matching sections of the first page (#ceo·#hr·#business·#info). MYPAGE·INTERNSHIP·Apply buttons belong to outside services, so they are placeholders only (#)

The people list filter filters by the cards’ data- values instead of the original data (JSON), and the URL query (?keyword=) is not used. The phone tap panel (scaleY .3s power3.out / on close .2s later .3s power2.out) uses the original values

Diagram-like graphics (case detail PROJECT FLOW timeline) were rebuilt with the original CSS values (line .4s back · dot .2× .6s · text 4px), but the timeline items were cut to 6. The case detail body sections · photos were condensed from dozens of original paragraphs into four sections

In the interview detail, the header text (tagline · keywords · name) sticks to the left and follows like the original, and turns white (is-invert) only over the dark hero, but the original’s per-section big photo pinning (the photo transition of section-content-main is-enter) is done only with photo strip parallax (--kk-progress) — to be continued by the next person
Skin: Gotham (paid) → Montserrat, ten-mincho-antique (paid) → Noto Serif KR 300, Yu Gothic → Noto Sans KR. One red #e60012 as --kf-accent

Font backfill: the Latin slots in the original (logo COMPANY·RECRUITING·section names PEOPLE·PROJECT STORY·READ·MORE PEOPLE·PROJECT MEMBERS·FLOW·INDEX·PICK-UP INTERVIEW·menu TOP·CEO MESSAGE and so on) were English from the start, so nothing was changed there. All 225 latin-slots lines are original kanji·kana slots below — the heading font --kf-font-display falls from Montserrat to Noto Serif KR 300 (the serif counterpart of ten-mincho-antique), so the texture matches.
index Hero text line (kk-hero__line) · Lottie large title — the original uses kana and kanji titles, Hangul kept
PEOPLE section head title (small particle-style kk-head__title · kk-phero__lead) · description (index · list) — original uses a Japanese title, Korean kept
Person card two-line title (kk-person__title — index · list · article) — the original uses a kana title, Korean kept

Case title and name (kk-story__title·__name — index·works·detail) — the original has kana and kanji titles, Korean kept. Name lines like ‹Brand Line› and ‹Series Name› are kana lines mixed with Latin brand words, so they are kept as Korean name slots.
Section headers and card leads and descriptions for Business, Job type, CEO and HR (kk-head · kk-card · kk-ceo — index) — original uses Chinese characters and kana, Hangul kept
People list filter keywords, categories, buttons, people-count unit and empty-result message (list) — the original uses kana and kanji, Hangul kept

Interview detail tagline·section title h4(article) — the original uses kana titles, keep the Korean text

notes: Only the 3 recorded subpages (about·business·future) were built — the header menu items Work Environment·New Grads·Engineers·Events·Media·FAQ·Open Positions·Casual Interview have no recording, so their links are left as #. business is type service so it is service.html, and future is vision and a CEO message so it is vision.html (type page)

Dither band: not a port of the original Dithering.js (2D canvas · 8×8 Bayer · 3px, 2px under 767 · multiplied by dpr · reveal 800ms easeInOut cubic) but a newly written part, dither-band-reveal, using the same formulas. The color sets (primary-heading · primary-body · secondary-heading · primary-sp-footer · tertiary-01 · 02) are kept in shared.css .sh-band--* with --site-* values derived from the accent color in oklch

Text painting (text-color-reveal 140°·85%→50%·soft .12·does not revert) was pulled as slant-ink-scrub, the Challenge Capital number wipe (capital-reveal .8s in-out · delayed .25s · long Bayer ramp mask the width of the child) as dither-mask-wipe, and button·hamburger·arrow·+ cell hover (64-cell Bayer ramp mask .35s) as dither-ramp-hover, all attached as they are.

Page transitions: the same swup 4.10 as the original, with the a11y, preload (hover and visible links), scroll (betweenPages false), body-class and head plugins, containers #swup and animationSelector false (no transition effect). The subpage header band works like the original TransitionReveal: .8s on first open, and length 0 in a Section arrived at by navigation. Opened via file://, swup cannot fetch the next page, so it does a normal navigation

The company intro deck (slide-deck iframe) only has a dither strip cover in the same 16:9 slot. There is no external player UI like slide-advance buttons or fullscreen. Event·media card photos (external CMS banners) are placeholders labeled only with what the picture shows.

Spots that speak through pictures — three value icons·human capital report cover (spreading brush strokes)·social issue bar chart·city illustration·SaaS∞AI loop diagram·product screen mockups on the business cards are newly drawn as SVG·dither bands in the same place·size·color feel, but simpler than the original (fewer people silhouettes·arrows)

Phone (390): hero, ISSUE and entry use -sp line groups split into finer lines like the original, and the Challenge Capital stair-step band becomes four groups. The phone menu opens the same dialog by height, like the original

notes: Hand-drawn lines play with lottie-web 5.13.0 (svg) like the original. The three in the hero play once from the start on every Swiper realIndexChange, and the three scattered photos and one large photo loop for 5s from the 20% line at the bottom of the screen. Comp size (456²·280×185·782×566·804×557·1520×800), 30fps, 150 frames, stroke width 2, nine draw/erase windows and the curve (.55,.06→.36,1) were measured from the original JSON. The stroke shapes (three accent lines, two cheek wrinkles, head outline) and positions are ours (COMP in lines.js), because the photos are placeholders and there is no spot for a person’s head. When photos are added, only the COMP positions need to be moved to fit the person.

The background ring doesn’t use the original circle.svg. On the same 778×746 board, ten rounded triangles are redrawn at 36° steps with outer radius 373, base 190, height 76 and group opacity .8. The fine texture (pattern.png 200px gray specks 0 to 77, 43% of them 0, screen blend on 100u cells) is also freshly scattered on a seeded random canvas with the same distribution. The hand-drawn circles on section titles (line_*.svg) are newly drawn as single-stroke ellipses.
The One-page Summary band is a single picture with the text baked in in the original (2080×862), so it is rebuilt at the same ratio as a beige text cell on the left plus a photo slot on the right

title: Scroll-scrubbed video turns into a 3D bee landing on a flower under glass
good_for: A solo creative developer or studio portfolio that proves skill with one video-to-3D scene, a few short text blocks and one contact button.

pages.use: One-page portfolio — firefly loader, big lowercase title under a glass film pressed by the cursor, a 460vh stage where scroll-wound video shrinks into a window and a 3D bee flies out to land on a flower, closing text where seven blocks form and scatter word by word, floating contact button. For solo developers and small studios

notes: The original is a single page (pages: [] in pages.json), so there are no subpages.

The 3D stage was rebuilt as a single three(r180) scene like the original — the original bee and flower models (glb) and the drei transmission material are not used. The flower branch is our own shape, merged into four materials from a stem plus sixteen blossoms (five petals, ten stamens, a pistil), and the bee is our own shape with a striped abdomen, thorax, head, antennae, legs, and four wings. The wind sway values (gust·breathe·shiver·landing push), video plate size and window-to-stem (rack), bee flight curves (sx·sy·w·z·yaw·pitch·roll), perch spot (perch normal·direction·lift .16·rel .19), wing flap 7.5Hz ±1.18, shake 8°·3.4Hz·damping 6.5, and the four light plates plus the lighting that follows the video’s average color are the original values as they are.

The glass film is our own shader instead of drei MeshTransmissionMaterial — it first draws the scene behind into a half-precision buffer, then the film (a 44×44 spring panel) bends it by the normal (refractive index 1.34) to show it through, splits red and blue (.04) and blurs with 9 circular samples according to roughness. The thickness·roughness·spectral·blur values, the changes with press and speed, and the clearing when the bee flies away (.56→.88) are the original values. The original material’s temporal distortion (temporalDistortion) is replaced by a sin pattern.

The video is a placeholder with the same ratio, length and playback behavior (media/film.mp4, 960×450=2.13:1, 25fps, 5.68s, 6 keyframes apart — original 1600×750 at the same interval). The blue sky, the white flowers, and a bee dot that flies up from a flower, passes (12.4%, 90.2%) at 5.04s and drops down are aligned to the bee’s spot in the original video, so the handoff to the 3D bee is seamless. As in the original, the whole file is fetched (fetch→blob) and currentTime is scrubbed by scroll. When opened as a file (file://), the video can’t be uploaded as a canvas texture, so the same scene is drawn on a 2D canvas instead (the tools compare·interact·shot look at this version).

Typeface: the original paid typeface was matched by measuring glyph width and x-height, landing on Urbanist 300 (same x-height .50, line width +1~6%). The spacing correction values before and after the substitute glyphs were made for the original font, so they are not used.

Text: headings and closing text sit in the Latin heading typeface slot as in the original, so they are English placeholders (matching word and line counts), and data-label says what to put in. The intro pill, guide lines and the line under the loader are in Korean.
The Brand ‹Nominee› strip at the middle right of the original is an external badge, so it is not included.

Trimmed from the original: the idle flight where a bee occasionally takes a short flight alone and returns while resting, and the leg steps when walking in the closing section. Only the walking spot per block, facing direction, hovering at the 4th and 5th blocks, and occasional wing shaking remain.
With reduced motion, as in the original: first section 110vh, video .36s slot, the bee stays perched on the flower, and the closing text lines up with no stagger.

title: Ink brushstrokes painting behind the screen for a venue reopening event

pages.use: Event first page — behind the opening notice curtain, a vertical-copy hero where 4 brush strokes are drawn behind the screen, then About, a pickup horizontal band, a 3-column event grid, a News list, a weekly calendar, a brush tagline, and access with map. For the hero of an opening or renovation event
Organization About — two center text blocks, brush-stroke tagline, text/photo two-column layout with three main programs, participating artist row, credits table. For the About menu slot

Single event — category · title · tags · key visual, overview table, bold question, body, gray box (timeline · access · good to know · project), performers row. For talk, workshop and exhibition detail pages.

notes: Of the three recorded subpages, /en has the same shape as the home page (English version), so it was not built separately. The event detail page was recorded as product, but since it is a single event it was changed to detail.

Brush paths and ink patterns don’t use the original SVGs (strokes/ and ink-svg-*) and are redrawn. Paths follow our knot, arch, leaf and T shapes, and the ink bakes six brush-grain bands, hue-rotated from the accent color, onto a canvas. Position (screen %), size (relative to the short side), stroke width, 3s curve, .15+.1s stagger, logo turning on at 80% and the tagline ‹when the section top touches the top of the screen› keep the original values exactly (ink-rope-draw).

Left out from the original drawing board: select mode (pick up and move drawn strokes), Ink making (tracing a camera or photo into vectors with OpenCV), export, undo, and localStorage saving of drawn strokes. Only Draw, Ink (pick one of six inks), Clear and drag-to-draw (50px threshold, stroke width 4% of point spacing, 2px 50% preview line, drawn over 1s) match the original.

Vertical-writing copy · body copy · opening notice text are hand-drawn glyph artwork (SVG) in the original, so they were re-set as text (Noto Sans KR vertical writing + rotated English in Space Mono). The Brand pixel wordmark is our block-letter LOGO SVG, and the four-line footer wordmark is Space Mono bold.

The maps (two map iframes), external news links, the app link and the cookie policy link were replaced with placeholders and same-page anchors. The cookie bar is saved to localStorage when pressed and does not show again.
The original video (.mov) of the first event card is replaced with a 6s gray placeholder video (media/weather.mp4) with the same 16:9, autoplay and loop.
The event row below the calendar is empty in the original too, since there is no event that day — clicking a date cell only turns it black and the row stays empty.

Store guide — region headers with lines filtered by region tabs, and two-column store cards (photo, address, map, hours, reserve button). For the branch list of a shop with several locations

notes: The original photo band uses Flickity (GPLv3 — not a license we can use), so the same physics (same integration order as Flickity, default attraction .025 · friction .28) was rewritten as a new part, attract-carousel. The article band advances by a group of the slots on screen + buttons that loop around (wrap: the end panel’s slots are moved over so only one panel moves). The drag’s wrapAround (being pulled on past the last slot) is missing, so it stops at both ends — for the next person to continue

Of the 5 recorded subpages, 4 (case post) and 5 (event post) share the same news-article type, so both are built as a single article.html (following 4, which has the photo strip). When there is just one photo, as in 5, the strip holds only one cell.

The Vimeo video on the home page is only a dark curtain and a play button in the same 16:9 slot. Clicking lifts the curtain and button in .3s but there is no real playback. The still motion video slot is also a placeholder (wf-video).
Among the original drawers, cart·subscribe·contact·account rely on external forms (Brand·reCAPTCHA) and order features, so only our own input fields sit in the same spot with the same slide
Header hiding is the hide-on-scroll part as is, so the header reappears when you reach the very bottom — in the original it stays hidden even at the bottom
Language switch (EN·DE) is a placeholder only — no other language versions exist
Font: Figtree instead of the original Messina Sans (paid). The big wordmark and logo art do not use the original art but a ‹Logo› text placeholder

For shop, hotel and company About pages.

Menu — a mirrored cover, a fixed text panel that switches between cooking principles, drinks, chef and sommelier profiles, three vertical galleries for lunch, dinner and afternoon tea (with booking button), an opening-info table, a scene gallery. For restaurant menus and course intros
Notice list — large English title and category pills, a staggered layout of one large news item and two small ones, the rest a one-line list with photos. For shop and brand news lists

A single notice — on the left the date, category and title (stuck to the top of the screen) and a back-to-list button (stuck to the bottom), on the right a cropped photo, two large paragraphs, body text and links. For a single News or Event post

notes: The original logos (brand wordmark, diamond N, Japanese logo) were redrawn as a line-art LOGO of the same weight and proportion, plus a diamond L. The star-rating badge became a crimson plate with AWARD lettering, and the eight related brand logos became English lettering slots.

The original news category pills link to per-category list pages, but since only one list was recorded, filtering happens within the same page.

The Banquet (/party), Contact (/contact), Wedding (external site) and Reservation (external) pages were not recorded, so they were not built — the menu and floating button link to the Banquet intro on the first page and to the footer Contact and Wedding spots.

Brand concept — full-screen photo hero with large serif section name, text and two photos staggered, before/after technique, sustainability text and photo. For brand story and philosophy intros

The gray-green background uses three blurred white lights as a still image, like the original poster, and the fragrance section and gallery use video slots of the same size (wf-video). Once real videos are added, they are set to autoplay and loop like the original (play after canplay, fall back to the poster on failure). Instead of the original’s seven SVGs (six letters + a round mark), the logo splits Bodoni Moda letters into cells and attaches a newly drawn round-mark SVG as one cell (the spread values are the same). title: Spinning photo sphere on a professional recruiting agency site
good_for: A recruiting or headhunting agency site with job listings, job detail pages with application forms, and a fixed left side navigation.

pages.use: Agency home page — after the loader, a hero with a 3D sphere of 200 spinning photos, a vision paragraph revealed from gray to black, rainbow glass beads in the black section (scene changes per paragraph) with number cards, job category chips, a six-step flow with vertical-writing titles, market report cards, and customer interviews. For the landing page of a company whose service connects people

About the company — big slogan on the left and a whole rotating photo sphere on the right, black section with vision, three mission boxes, 7 value accordions, CEO greeting card, company overview table, office photos, map and address. For company about and vision pages

Job listings — dark photo header band, narrowing panel (keyword, industry, occupation, region chips), two-column job cards (tag, title, workplace, posted date), pagination, rainbow arc glow consultation strip. For job and recruitment listings.
News and column list — photo header band, category pill tabs (click to filter), 2-column photo cards (title · category chip · date), pagination. For news, blog and interview article lists
Rules and terms document — breadcrumbs, large title, numbered subheadings with dot lists, gray header table, footnotes. For long documents such as operating rules, terms of use, and privacy policies

Single job posting — tag, two-line title, conditions table box, company overview · duties · requirements · extra info with dot + line subheadings, apply bar stuck to the bottom of the screen while reading the body, application form with required · optional marks (select box · radio · file). For job detail · apply pages

notes: The photo sphere uses the original settings (radius 5 · fov 45 · camera z7 · 200 photos · entry 280° 4.7s · fog 3.2s · moves aside during 2000px of scroll · Y half turn) and velocity warping (velocityDeformation: distance −0.6 · front-edge influence .4 · center influence 2.4, strength = …the larger of the entry-rotation share and the scroll-acceleration share) was ported into our vertex shader. The original’s curvature transition (at scroll progress .12 the flat panels facing the camera attach to the sphere surface over 1.1s power1.inOut, vertex delay .24, overshoot .045) is not there yet — panels are on the sphere from the start (the About head is attached from the start in the original too). The order in which panels turn on is an azimuth-ordered delay (within 2.6s), which may differ from the original’s revealViewAngle −1.05 and jitter .015 baseline.

The photos on the photo sphere are a color-block atlas painted by mixing skin colors (accent·sky·orange·green·gray) into background·text — to use real photos, draw them into the sphere.js atlas cells or pass an img to the photo-sphere-spin part.

The loader uses letter spans instead of the original SVG letter art, and the numbers (gray text from the back letters at 25ms intervals over 950ms · black layer .6~.8 → 1 in two steps over 900ms · gradient sweep .08/.4/.43 · exit 1.9s power3.inOut · blur .15~.55) are the original settings. The per-letter exit offset formula (original pO·fO — max 18% of screen width · title width .5) could not be fully worked out, so it is approximated with a squared center-to-outside distance.

The phone menu is hooked up with the original Alpine timeline values (panel .45s power1.out · menu body .42s after .12s · reversed on close), and the details of the Menu button turning into a black circle X (button .32s power1.inOut · text .22/.24s · line 45° .24s) are matched in shape only, using css transitions.

The job filter window uses the original Alpine x-transition values (backdrop 300ms ease-out · panel from 16px below, close 200ms ease-in), and the consultation strip uses the original jobsCtaAnimation stagger (light −56→56 · left photo −24→18 · right photo −16→12). The application form·window are shape only (no submit·search), the map is an SVG drawing
Positions of the News row and numbered section titles are guesses, since the original could not be seen at large size

The original Lottie for the number cards (12000-bake etc.) is static lettering with no keyframes (31 frames), so we keep our own number text and apply the original’s values: cards rise 24px at .16s intervals, then .35s later the number line rises from below (the moment the original plays the Lottie). The previous version’s count-up from 0 is not in the original, so it was removed
The original’s “Reasons to be chosen,” “For hiring companies” and “Get materials” pages were not recorded, so only menu slots exist
Fonts: PP Neue Montreal → Inter Tight, Aoto Gothic → Pretendard (loaded from theme.css). Logo, photos and text are all placeholders

The footer uses the original footerCtaParallax (two photo layers move from 100 to −100px along 110° and −70°, sine in-out progress, following by 1 − e^(−3.5·sec)) and footerLargeTextReveal (4s power3.out wipe starting 1.1s after becoming visible) with the same values — the two photo layers are our placeholder slots, 15 photos each.

Product list — large section title, fixed left categories (icon list), 3-column product cards (photo · name · category · price tag), page numbers. For rental products and vehicle model lists

News list — date and title one line each, a gray band slides down on hover, monthly archive picker on the left, page numbers. For notice and news lists
Booking consultation form — two-line English large heading, a group of underline fields, required/optional tags and a date picker, privacy notice and a send button. For booking and contact forms

notes: The bundle contains barba and Lenis code, but the original has no PUBLIC_ENABLE_BARBA and does not create Lenis — so they are not used. Transitions fade the whole #page like the original (.3s delay then .6s expo.inOut → new page .1s delay then .6s power4.out), and # jumps use the same smooth-scroll 16.1.3 as the original (1s easeInOutCubic)

title: Three words splitting to opposite edges on a white design agency site
good_for: A company site for a web design and development studio, small agency or freelance team with a work grid, service table, awards, clients and FAQ.

pages.use: Agency home page — a header where three words light up in random letters and then spread to both ends, staggered work panels, about, service rows, award table, press, client logo grid, testimonials, FAQ, blog, and three ‹Let’s build together› lines
Work list — eight cases where small and large panels swap sides and step downward, each panel with title·one-line description·vertical year·tag·VIEW. For portfolio·case lists
Service intro — two-word header, intro text, three-column table of service · deliverables · cost, FAQ. For service pages with quote criteria
About — three-word header, intro text, a team row of twelve where hovering pops out a face, how we work, client logo slots, products row, blog cards
Blog list — grid where two-column-wide post cards are staggered over six columns. For post and news lists
Single blog post — cover photo, title, summary, date and author in a centered three-column block, body paired with photos, two ‹Read more› cards

notes: One blog post (type detail) in pages.json is a news post, so it was changed to article.

Font: PP Mori · General Sans are not OFL, so Inter Tight alone is used (Pretendard · system gothic for Korean). The original logo (two-color bars + two-line name) was redrawn as three SVG bars + two lines of Studio Name.

Motion follows the original Webflow IX3 register table (timeline · ScrollTrigger start/end · curve number 20=circ.out, 0=none, 2=Read and ported power1.out) and the IX2 hover table. The original turns off scroll reveals on phones and small tablets (small · tiny, under 767), so the copy also doesn’t move under 768.

The three lines of ”Let’s make it together” use line-rise (line mask 200% · 1s circ.out) — the original also brings each line in from ±5rem to the side, but line-rise has no side-offset option, so that was dropped.

Work card · line button hover follows the original IX2: the current arrow is pushed out at .3s and the next arrow enters .25s later like a baton, while the underline · text turn blue over .5s with cubic-bezier(.165,.84,.44,1) — built in CSS (on release it returns immediately).
Review paging rebuilds the original slider (drag paging · dot navigation) only as two buttons + .5s overlap — the tablet drag row (the non-blocking row) remains.

Customer logo cells and work panels are trimmed to fewer than the original (logos 10, work first page 8, work pages 8), keeping only the same shape. The work panel photo ratios (4:3, 4:5, 16:10) are values eyeballed from the reference print.

FAQ rows open and close independently, as in the original (.5s cubic-bezier(.165,.84,.44,1), + vertical stroke folds). Team row hover (face 0→1 · name pushed 3.5rem) uses the original IX2 values as is, in CSS.

The Work card arrow baton uses IX2 values (first arrow immediately .3s, second .3s after .25s) and was remeasured, the hover entry matched. The leftover arrow motion line in the release window and the lines of the first two panels (while opening) were accepted with reasons noted.

The service page was measured section by section against the original — the original table rows (service_in_detail_item) have entrance motion turned off at every width, so width-grow-reveal was removed (it was the cause of rows folded to 20% width and growing in height). The 7rem below the intro text, 10rem above the FAQ section (tablet 8rem·6rem), FAQ row 1.25rem and deliverables text column width (17rem, tablet 13rem) were matched to the original row heights (1440 148px·834 220px).
The work page has 18 items like the original, and on tablet a two-cell panel at 50% width. Blog list row gap 10rem and 9 paragraphs of post body to match the original document height.

For personal portfolio landing pages with a 3D scene as the star.
