The original home has an editor (hero-framing) that saves room and text positions separately for each screen ratio — here only the laptop (≤1440), desktop, tablet and mobile defaults were carried over

The original orbit loader is an 8.4s GSAP timeline (seven scenes). Here it is drawn with six scenes (orbit · drop · light beam · focus · big circle · small orbit) and the final white flash at the same times as simple lines (the number reaches 100 at 9.2s)

The 3D letter pieces on the About page background (9 letters of the original name) are replaced with yellow bent frame pieces. Curve points, pitch, radius and speed of the sub-page piece spiral are the original values
The original text effect uses Web Animations (not GSAP), so it was built the same way. Instead of gsap.matchMedia it reads prefers-reduced-motion directly and leaves the text in its final state

Work detail keeps only the form of six sections from the original’s long case (map-pin pie chart, emotion curve, journey table etc.) — illustrations and map are replaced by a dot map and circle placeholders

In the home Work section the original furniture pieces flow along fixed paths (furniture-flow editor values) — here it is an approximation where they flow scattered from bottom to top and regroup before the transformation section

Cursor reaction decision (2026-11-12): the Hero room turning toward the cursor by ±13° horizontally and ±3.5° vertically existed only in the copy and is not a reaction in the original, so it was removed (the pointer paths in the original home bundle are only sun parallax, furniture clamps, closing push and eyes). For the sun parallax to look like the original, the sun must be beyond the back window, so the light-theme sun direction and light levels were changed to the original values (direction relative to the room (−.45,−.47,.76), sun 4.6, fill .7, sky .55, floor .25, exposure 1.05, aim position and distance 1.9× the room size). Dark-theme levels stay at the values we set, and only the sun uses the original dark-theme direction (height 10° · azimuth −10°)

title: Black and white pet brand with white vertical panels, spaced headings and diagonal gray wipes
good_for: A brand site for pets, furniture or household goods that speaks through a single photo and wide whitespace, with about, products, news and company pages.

pages.use: Brand home page — white vertical panel over a photo (tagline, wordmark, latest news with a rotating LATEST circle), dark About section, product doors, horizontal News rows, company/Contact band, footprint Footer band

Product list: a horizontal row of page names (drag to scroll), then per row a large photo on the left and a group of small photo + text on the right. For product pages of brands with only a few products.
News (journal) list — a category picker panel, a 3-column grid of vertical photos, and rounded-arrow pagination. Category lists (journal/news) share this same layout, so this one page covers them.
About the company — large centered title, large sticky photo that follows on the left and a company info list on the right (name · CEO · founded · business · clients)

notes: Same libraries as the original: page transition barba.js 1.0.0 (Pjax · only .r-container inside #r-wrapper is swapped), News line·page-name line swiper 4.5.1 (original 4.x — the version where breakpoints means max-width). barba only runs over http — opened via file:// it covers the same curtain and then falls back to a normal navigation.

The original smooth scroll is site code (TweenMax.to(.scrollcontents, .4, {y: −scrollTop, ease: Circ.easeOut})) is not a library — I rewrote the same formula in shared.js with GSAP 3 circ.out (768 and up only, off on phones, as in the original).

Since barba swaps only the body, every page carries the four per-page css files (index·product·news·about), and after the transition shared.js setup() reattaches that page’s motion (reveals·swiper·parallax) by namespace.

The original typeface Neue Helvetica W01 is paid, so the closest free option, Inter, is used (500 for headings, 400 for body), with Noto Sans KR for Korean. The logo, the circular LATEST text, the footprints and the cat silhouette were redrawn instead of using the original SVGs.
journal/news (category News list) has the same shape as the journal list, so it is a single news.html page — choosing in the category board only changes the Category: text (no real filtering).

The original’s js-viewin-each (line-by-line in sequence) stagger for the right list of the company page could not be found in the original, so the whole list appears at once over .8s. The original map (company location) is not visible on the company page, so it was left out.
The two-layer text swap (fade-shift-swap) on logo and menu applies the transition only on enter as in the original, and snaps back immediately on release.

title: Photo cards drifting across a lake for a marina club
good_for: A facility site for a marina, campground, leisure club or activity venue that splits activities into color cards and links to booking and pricing tables.

pages.use: Facility first page — a Hero with straight-flowing photo cards and a rotating text ring Lottie, three News cells and a weather box, a yellow section with a text-and-photo strip, sky-blue and orange activity cards, yacht product cards, an outline-text strip, rental and member photo cards, a Contact card, a flowing photo strip, a blue About section with a facility slider, and a first-time visitor link table.
Company · facility About — white intro panel (text + photo), six-cell facility grid, access card · map slot, company overview table, pill link grid, contact card
News list — row list with title, date and yellow pill arrow, plus a contact card. On hover the text and pill turn blue
News item — white title card, a few lines of body, pill button back to the list. For short notices and event alerts

First-timer guide — white intro panel (text + photo collection), experience cells (photo + text), price table, info box, two rental price cells, yellow pill booking button. For experience, lesson and price guides

notes: The “SCROLL DOWN” text-ring Lottie plays with the same player as the original (@dotlottie/player-component 2.7.12, MIT copy in _vendor), and the artwork keeps the same size (169×169) and duration (60fps 720 frames = 12s, -360° straight) in our JSON (media/scroll-ring.json — 40 rounded bars instead of letters).

The cell width and speed of the photo strip (below the Contact card) were judged as 33.3px per second on 300·470px cells, because only the 9000ms slider was read from the original DOM and the cell width couldn’t be found.

The facility slider is a hand-built one-cell advance of the original STUDIO slider (cell 410 + gap 24, cubic-bezier(.58,.21,.41,.96)) — the transition length is blank in the original (JS fills it), so I judged it as .8s.

The weather widget (external iframe) is a placeholder with the same size and the same cell layout (region label · current temperature · wind · humidity · pressure · five hourly cells · prev/next buttons).

The lake-shaped background of the blue About section is a round lake shape we drew (transparent .12) instead of the original map silhouette, and the round border under the section is approximated with a clip-path ellipse.
The logo is a Rubik bold italic English placeholder (MARINA / CORPORATION) instead of the original image logo.

The subpage ‹First-time visitors› is trimmed from the original 17,590px long page by keeping only one of each section type (experience cell, price table, info box, two rental cells, yellow membership panel) — repeated cells such as SUP, windsurfing and yacht lesson courses were left out.
Fixed the types attached at recording time: /beginners is type page, guide.html. /news/ei5rWu_Y (detail) is a single News item, so type article, article.html.

Interaction was measured on the original and matched. Studio only smooths elements that declare a transition length: pill arrow .5s (exit ease, enter cubic-bezier(.4,.4,0,1)), burger background .5s and line color .3s, nav line and footer link color .5s, facility button border .5s/.4s, photo zoom .7s ease (rental 1.08, activity 1.05). Header pills, small links, contact button, SNS and blog hovers are not in the original, so they are left out.

title: Rotating-word video hero and two-step pill menu for a housing developer

About — big title, an intro where big paragraph lines rise, and a vertical video, team category shortcuts and a grid of staff cards per category (appear in line as they enter the screen). For About of companies with many teams

notes: Video: the hero background, the river in the Philosophy section and the vertical video in the About section are placeholders for the original bunny background video — same spot, ratio and autoplay-loop conditions, and while playing it just shows as a background with flowing light bands

Map: the ”Map” panel on the Work page is a Mapbox globe in the original (external map service, token), so it is a same-size placeholder — the grid/map toggle pill’s slide (--toggle-active) and the panel switch are built the same way

smooothy (slider) is loaded on every page in the original, but none of the six recorded pages use it (no calls in the site script), so it wasn’t included — it seems to be used for the photo slider on the detail page (work-template), which wasn’t recorded

The menu’s ‹What We Do› (what-we-do) and ‹Connect› (connect) pages were not recorded, so they were not built. Menu links point to About or #. The transition on the What We Do page (hero photo 1.1→1) is shown in the same way by the Careers page.
Team cards cut the original several dozen people in five groups down to 3~5 per group, and the staff detail (team-member) transition was not built

The company logo is an English text placeholder 「● Company」 (data-label 「Your brand’s English name here」). The original SVG logo was not used. 「Brand Name」 wrapped onto two lines in the footer logo cell (10rem), so the character count was reduced

Font backfill: the original is an English site, so all Korean placeholder text in the Newsreader (heading font) slots was replaced with English placeholder text — menu and footer menu (Home · About · Works · News · Careers · Contact), the hero ”Word_” + rotating words one~four, large page titles, section names, the name lines for complex, staff, job and team groups (Project Name 01 · Person Name 01 · Job Title 01 · Department 01), and news titles with their aria-labels. Korean kept: 0 (no Chinese-character or kana slots).

Judgment: description sentences set in the heading font (value slide description t-h4, large About paragraph t-h3, article quote t-h3) are also swapped for English placeholder copy, since the original has English sentences in that font. Items in the body font (Inter) stay in Korean per the README: labels t-label (Our Philosophy, About, etc.), body t-main, job titles, dates, filter buttons and footer labels (Inter, then Pretendard, sans-serif ↔ gothic). The About team shortcut (t-main) has the same text as the genre title below, so it was changed to English too

title: Fixed left menu column with side-opening sub panels for a public theater
good_for: A public cultural venue such as a theater, concert hall, community center or museum with heavy content on performance schedules, facilities, calls for entries and columns.

pages.use: Landing — left menu pillar, photo fade slider with an important-notice band, two banners, PICK UP, today’s performances (venue-colored tags) and notices in two columns, three facility cells, partner logos, ink footer. For a theater or cultural facility hero

Column and archive home — a separate magazine-style frame with no columns, a find-by filter for category·genre·series·year, and per-series card rows that overflow horizontally (Swiper). For web magazine and column collections
Participant and performer recruitment — intro text, in-page navigation row, three cards for open and closed recruitment with deadlines. For open call and participant lists
Theater introduction — four underlined tabs (About, Concept, History, Greeting), photo fade, long text, spec table, six facility cells. For facility and institution introductions
In-house program lineup. Big hero image, planning text and a expert window, 75 performance cards filtered by category buttons (status and genre tags). For season programs and project lists
A single news item — date and category tags, bold title under a dotted line, share buttons, body, back to list. For notice and alert posts
Column article — hashtag tags, 800px centered body (photo captions, footnotes), author intro, related program and article cards, two buttons. For critique, interview and report articles

notes: The original photos, banners, posters, logos (theatre logo · online ticket · partner organizations) and the venue name graphic are not used, placeholders state what goes in each spot. The venue name graphic (Main Hall) was replaced with two lines of text.

The in-house business category filter does not use the original MixItUp 3 (commercial licence). The same behaviour (fade scale · 600ms · ease, fade-out kept straight, list height matched) was rebuilt as the flip-filter-grid part, measuring the first, middle and end positions by hand (GSAP Flip’s absolute mode was dropped because cards jump all at once at the end, unlike the original). Because the original measures a list of over 70 cards, motion starts one or two frames after the press, so a delay option was added to the part and set to .04s. The 75 cards are placeholders that carry over only each original card’s status, genre, category, anniversary mark and title length.

On the original About page at phone widths (767 and below) the photo slick doesn’t run, so the two photos stack vertically (650px at 390, no fade while scrolling, from 834 up a 2s fade every 3s) — the copy also attaches slick only at 768 and above.

The pace loader on the column site: the original version (1.0.0) is not on npm, so the closest one, pace-js@1.0.2, was used. For slick, features in the original bundle (focusOnChange etc.) confirmed it is the 1.8 line, so slick-carousel@1.8.1 was used.
The original wide-screen frame has min-width 1230px (column site 1200px) so it overflows horizontally on an 834 tablet — left as in the original.
The original drawer menu’s sub-expansion is bootstrap 3 dropdown adding open to the li, so without loading bootstrap, a short jQuery in shared.js adds the same open.

Cookie consent is shown by an external widget (ulcc, cookieconsent), so only the same position, colors and buttons were carried over as a static version. Mouse devices get a bottom bar, touch devices get a 384px box at the bottom left (the widget switches to floating on mobile, ported as (hover: none)). On click a 1s fade is applied and it is hidden on transitionend like the widget. With a finger tap, the button hover transition’s (.3s) transitionend bubbles up and cuts it off at about .3s (as measured on the original at 390), while column sites without a button hover run the full 1s. The purple was matched to the original #704b92 by converting the accent through oklch. The notice text was written to match the original line counts (two lines on wide screens, five lines in the phone box, six lines on column sites), and the bar sits one layer above the shared wireframe button row (.wf-ui, 9999) at 10000. If it sits beneath, the center of Agree gets covered and can’t be pressed.

On wide screens the original consent widget leaves a 100px-wide element even after it is closed (probably the cc-revoke ‹reopen› tab in ulcc.css, but its shape and position could not be confirmed from the recording) — not included in this copy.

Went past 180 minutes (about 535 minutes, much of it waiting for a browser slot shared with other students). Even after that it got as far as bringing the blocking lines to 0, and the non-blocking lines above stopped where they were.

In the original, links to outside sites (online tickets·SNS·share) are set to https://example.com/ in a new window, and language JP stays on the current page — with a # placeholder the measuring tool counts it as a button to press and presses something different from the original.

Of the original’s project text and business category popups (Magnific Popup) and the column photo zoom popup, only the first two are hooked up. Column photo zoom (doc-photo-list) was not used in the recorded column.
Venue tag colors, business category colors and genre colors are distinction colors set by content, so they are not Skin and keep their original values.

title: Single orange accent architecture office with a paper-flying loader and photos growing between words

Work list — large title and a photo grid with folded corners. For an architecture portfolio list
Services — full-bleed photo header · tiered service list · process linked by a thread · closing invitation. For service introductions
Office About — large title cutting across a photo, sentence over the photo, principles grid, closing invitation, team photo. For small architecture office About pages
Single work detail — photo header, three text sections with photos, full-bleed closing photo. For architecture project case details

notes: Hero: a placeholder video in the same form as the original (desktop 1920×1080, phone 608×1080 portrait, 30fps, 19.67s, media/hero-*.webm — our scene: a person with an orange umbrella walking between glass buildings and wooden pillars on a cloudy day) is laid over the first image slot. As in the original, it loops only while visible on screen and fades in over .8s once it actually starts playing. At 1200px and wider, an ASCII shader rebuilt with the same values (6px cells, glyph sheet ' ·LOGO' · a 400px lens around the mouse · follow .18 · reveal .08) lights up that video. No mp4 version for Safari was included (VP9 webm only)
The wordmark is a newly drawn LO/GO (one O as an orange 3D capsule) instead of the original logo — the same shape in the loader (solid black), header band (horizontal bar) and footer (two lines)

Page transitions match the original: barba 2.10.3 with two sync transitions. First page ‹View project› → detail: caption bar slides out in .35s → photo frame shrinks to the detail’s first photo spot over .9s power3.inOut with the new page at .4s and the cover at .25s. For the rest, the next page stays fixed on screen and opens from the center over .9s power3.inOut. Next-page-only css and scene scripts are loaded and attached on first visit. barba fetches the next page and can’t run on file://, so only then a white curtain opens from the center before navigating, replaced by a multi-page transition where the detail picks up the photo frame

The big numbers in the number band use the placeholder 00+, which is wider than the original 15+ and got cropped heavily on phones, so it was set to 10+ (the original also slightly clips the + end on phones).

Heading typeface NEXT ART (paid) replaced by Lexend — English word widths are nearly the same (4.78 vs 4.62em), but the Korean placeholder shows in Pretendard or a system sans, so the wide-capitals feel of the original is weaker.
Tablet (768–1199) rules: all twenty-five groups of original rules were ported under this copy’s names (1024 width unit --t). Screen checks were done only at 1440 · 390

The team (/team) and terms pages were not recorded so they were not built. Menu 5 (Team) and the View Team button link to the team photo (#team) at the bottom of the About page. Three other detail pages of the same type use a single detail.html
In the photo scene between words, when the center photo covers the screen it scales with transform, so the photo slot label text grows too (no matter once a photo is added)
The contact form doesn’t send like the original — it only validates, then switches to a thank-you message
The sites pull stopped midway because of a name clash (EEXIST) between the work file and the work/ folder, so the sub-page originals were extracted directly from the archive pages.har.zip and read.

Spots set in the body typeface (Google Sans, since the original also uses the body typeface for t-display-sm) stay in Korean: loader corner text, intro scroll sentences, menu panel intro and terms, [ Scroll down ], footer notices and paragraphs. The thumbnail is the loader screen, so this Korean is visible.

Article list — two-line big title, two article cards where the arrow sits as a topic image (laptop check, padlock), with date and summary. For blog or guide article lists

notes: Cursor reaction (cursor-sweep) was also only measured on index (passed)
The original main portrait is dot data extracted from a photo, so it is not used, a head-and-shoulders silhouette was drawn and traced instead (no photo slot)

Original Let'The new-shape dot data for the s talk section (3D bird flock) is not used, replaced with the cover shape (four chevrons) — the original also uses the cover (logo) shape for the contact section

Language toggle (EN/UA) is label only, with no behavior
Lenis settings: could not find the creation options in the bundle so left at default (lerp .1)

good_for: A homepage for an investment firm, family office or consulting company with a portfolio list, investment philosophy and focus areas.

pages.use: Company home page: a wordmark-spreading loader, a Hero with turning stones and dot tiles, an About paragraph where a bar passes over each line, three principle cards (covered as they step back), a partner table, a mission with a turning tick-mark circle, leadership where portraits pin in place, and a closing CTA where the nav drops in. Work and investment case list — accent-color light-beam hero, intro paragraph, large title with category picker, case rows pairing a text and spec cell (status, site link) with an image, load more, focus-area notice. For portfolio and case list pages

title: Hero video filling a rounded panel for a health brand growth agency
good_for: An agency, consulting or B2B service site needing a client name dial, video case cards, a horizontal service strip and testimonial cards, plus blog, case list and team pages.

pages.use: Agency first page — in a fixed Hero a 16:9 video grows to a full rounded panel · three field rows (tilted dark cards on hover) · client name dial · case videos stacking one screen at a time · horizontally pushed service cards · three steps · testimonial cards sweeping sideways · FAQ · wave CTA

Work list — three-column case cards below the title and buttons (photo · name · two metric chips · intro · read more). For client case and portfolio lists
Company About — blue gradient first panel (heading · button · black-and-white group photo) · president message card and portrait card · four-column round team portrait grid

notes: The original moves with the site builder’s IX2·IX3 (a paid runtime, so not used). The same values were rebuilt with GSAP: slideInBottom 100px · growIn .75 · slideInLeft −100px 1s outQuart (cubic-bezier(.165,.84,.44,1)), Hero IX3 load (panel .25s@.2 · title words 1s power4.out at .07 intervals@.44 · video 0→1 1s power1.out@1.45 · header line −50px@1.46 · both sides .5s@2.45, with phones handled separately), expanding panel .4s power3.out / .3s power3.inOut after .1s, cursor pill .2s easeOut.

Photos and videos are gray placeholders (media/loop-16x9.mp4 — 8-second looping ffmpeg gray gradient) with labels. Original client logos, 3D icons and team portraits are left as labeled placeholders.

The original HTML of the blog post detail could not be pulled by sites pull because its name collides with the blog list file (blog file vs blog/ folder), so it was read from the archive pages.har.zip.
The blog list category tabs use seven panels swapped with no-code builder tabs (out .1s · in .3s) — only the number of post cards differs per panel, the content is the same placeholder.

I therefore also screenshotted and replaced heading-sized text painted with the body variable: two rv-h56 section titles, section names (Sectors we serve·Services), sector names (80px) and card h4, thirteen client dial entries (64px), the trust line (dial·phone logo grid), case names (Home 40px·Work list card), service card names, process title (64px)·step number·step name. Body-size text stays Korean: menu·buttons·tags·paragraphs·metric descriptions·partner names (16px)·reviews·question lines·person names (20px)·article card titles (20px, only the featured article 24px — article titles are sentences, so the whole list is kept Korean)·path display. title: Shape-shifting polygon and logo letter wall for an event agency

For event and creative agency landing pages

About the company (manifesto) — polygon header, principles section where nine number blocks orbit in an arc (pause at each slot), big sentence, two sections of differently colored blocks with text, mission and vision. For company philosophy and manifesto pages
Services — polygon header, five services as cards that change color per section and carry on the block shape of the section above as they go down. For service and capability intros
Work list — polygon header, giant title and branch buttons, staggered 12-column work cards (photo opening, parallax), load more. For portfolio lists
News list — photo slider band, giant title and year buttons, news cards cut into chunks in three columns, channel invitation. For blog lists
Single article — wide diagonally cropped header photo with an overlapping title box, one-column body (subheads, questions) and a photo slider. For blog posts and news details

notes: Polygon types: the original SVG paths (artwork) are not carried over. Instead, five shapes of our own (a~e) with the same character (angular 8–10-sided shapes with one or two concave spots), plus dot and menu shapes, were newly drawn and morphed with MorphSVG (type linear, map size) at the same length and curve (1s power4.inOut, first .75s back.inOut(.75)). The logo, clinic icons, transit/phone/mail icons and corporate mark are not copied from the original but redrawn as our own SVGs at the same position and size. The three banners (one corporate, two facility) are image banners, so they are rebuilt with a border color, name text and photo slot.
The About video (embedded) is replaced by a video placeholder of the same size (640×360), and the map-pattern image on the map button by a line-pattern background.

Recruit pages (recruit · detail) set sg-saiyo on body like the original, switching the accent to orange and the background to apricot — the orange, red and apricot shades are all generated from the accent color in shared.css via oklch (within 1/255 of the original values). The original recruit header’s ”Contact Us” and ”Entry!” buttons reuse the shared header, so the mail and phone button text is kept and only the color was changed.

Decision: built the five lower pages in pages.json as they are (about·recruit·news·service·detail). The recruit original is long at 8311px (several join-message cards·doctor messages·training schedule), so cards of the same type were cut to one each. All section types were kept: Hero, photo banner, program chips, three numbers with a circular relationship diagram, video, message cards, two doctor cards.
News·topic list rows share the same type, so shared.js stamps placeholder rows (news panel seven tabs × five rows, news page sixteen rows, topics five cards).
The original hero vertical copy was text baked into an image, so it is re-set as live text at the same position and size (white translucent box with the highlighted word in teal).

Adjusted to match the original length for pairing: one document-button section (hospital annual report) was added to about, and one income-criteria box section to service, and the menu text placeholder lengths were set closer to the original menu widths (109, 125, 76, 76, 76px). Banner colors were moved to data-tone so they are picked as one candidate of the same type, like the original.

title: Black statement panels and a letter-noise footer for a design and tech studio
good_for: A small design or technology studio homepage with a few large case studies and an about page that states philosophy in sentences.

pages.use: Studio home — large centered title and 1.63:1 hero photo (rises for .6s after .2s) · about · three works · three sentences stuck to a 500vh black section that change at each step · four journals · sideways-push testimonials · text-noise footer. For a quiet studio landing
Work list — large title, grid/list toggle button, three-column vertical case cards (5px gap). For portfolios with few cases

Studio About — full-screen photo·549px text column (43px heading·serif subheading)·graphic where two circles overlap every 2s·black section title/text·draggable flowing band of work photos. For philosophy·about text
Journal list — two-line large title · four-column article cards (first cell is video). For article and News lists
Work detail — field pill, large name, intro, visit-site button, full-screen photo, two photos, two-column text, gray panel (screen capture grid, inner photo), large photo. For a single Work page

notes: The original Ask window is an AI chat feature, so only its look (blurred backdrop, chat panel, sample question chips, input field, close) and open/close are built. The chips rise from 6px below with a linear .5s after .1s, like the original ask-rise (the second one .08s later). There are no real questions or answers.

The footer text noise and the about two-circle drawing are new parts (ascii-noise-field · venn-converge) we rewrote in our own code after reading the values of the original Framer code components (density .35 · 9px Geist Mono · 30fps · radius 100/150 · overlap 42 · 2s easeInOutCubic · 153 dots) — the noise hash is ours so the pattern shape is not identical, but density · flow · response are the same

The About section’s flowing work-photo strip was moved from the original Framer ticker (60px/s · gap 8px · drag · hoverModifier 80) to the drag-marquee part (per-px 1/60 · hover-speed .8 newly added). The original drag inertia curve is internal to Framer, so InertiaPlugin’s default inertia stands in

The work list’s ‹List view› just switches to rows of name (27px) and field pills as in the original, devices like a hover photo preview on list rows were not confirmed on the original screen, so they are not included

The journal article detail, contact, and First Serve pages were not recorded, so they were not built — journal cards link to the footer, and the detail is reached from work cards through a single detail.html. Next steps for whoever continues

Font: Helvetica Neue LT Pro 55 Roman (paid) → Arimo (same shape, free). The serif Hedvig Letters Serif and the monospace Geist Mono are free, so they are the same. The original has no smooth scrolling (.lenis in the bundle is just the name of a scrollbar-hiding part) — the copy has none either, only the scrollbar is hidden

As in the original, on subpages only the nav floats up at .6s after a .2s delay (Framer appear), and only the work-list cards float up over .7s with cubic-bezier(.44,0,.56,1). The original has no transition between pages either (it stays as is while the new page loads, then switches)

type backfill — the heading (Arimo t-h1 · t-h2 · t-h43) and serif (Hedvig Letters Serif: testimonials · About subheadings · two footer lines) slots are English placeholders like the original. Work names are the same works as the list view (t-h2), so grid cards and home cards (t-body) use the same English names.

Korean text in the body font slot (Arimo → Pretendard) is left as is — nav, Ask window, intro sentence, black section sentence, journal card titles and intros, review name line, footer columns, © Studio name. The original is also a body-font slot, so these are not Latin headings or serif fonts

The original work detail source was dropped when the archive was unpacked, because the work file and the work/ folder names collided — since the whole site is in English, the detail title and subheads were assumed to be English and rewritten in English

title: Photo strip flowing along an arc for a nursery school
good_for: An intro and recruiting site for a nursery, kindergarten or learning center, including small multi-branch operators, with a warm serif-toned brand home.

pages.use: Institution home — loader, Hero of a photo band flowing along an arc, four About blocks on a large oval background (concept · gallery · daily life · parents · meals), three facilities with photo cards flying in, category-tab News, fan-shaped social feed, admission Contact, recruiting badge · recruiting band, Footer

About (what we cherish) — sub-page Hero (right-side serif title, breadcrumbs, wide photo), two-column intro, large photo flush left with six numbered color-square policies, the way we see children, cells leading to next page, circle list and application

News list — category pills (All · Admission · Hiring · Notices), rows of date · category chip · title, round page numbers. Choosing a category like #admission shows a category header and a Coming soon notice (same shape as the original category page)

Recruiting site home page — circle loader, a hero where four photos in rounded blob windows change every 6 seconds and the ‹Name × ○○› word changes with them, a large flowing English line, three round photo links (a color cover peels away on hover), three stories, a circle-list slider (buttons · filling line), an apply guide with a button-colored band cover rolling in, and the recruiting footer

notes: Fonts: Shippori Mincho·Zen Kaku Gothic New·Quicksand are the same free fonts as the original, with Gowun Batang·Noto Sans KR added as Korean pairs. The handwritten line in the recruiting band (a picture in the original) is set as Nanum Pen Script text

Logo and kangaroo mark were redrawn as a red round mark plus an English name placeholder. The menu cover corner art and between-section stain art (original PNG) are replaced with CSS ellipses and blobs

Three facility settings: the original’s 600vh sticky, the section numbers (every 150vh), and the toss range (first cell height ×2 to ×3 + screen + 300px) were calculated at 1440×900 and converted to vh (pin-toss-stack height 600 · first 105 · every 233 · span 1.4). Unlike the original, where the first cell height changes with the screen ratio, these are fixed to the screen height. The section background color is switched with :has([data-step])

Loader: the original uses cookie load=loaded (30 min) so it is skipped from the second time — the copy works the same way (ss-load). The wave-edge SMIL animation was ported as changing the same three shapes over 1s in sync with the time

News categories: the original has a different address per category (news/category/admission etc.), so the same form is shown by hash like news.html#admission (category header, ‹Coming soon› notice, breadcrumbs)

Recruit (recruit.html): the original is a separate recruit site and only the Hero (900px) was recorded in the archive — following the original HTML, the page was built through Hero, About, three links, story, circle list, application guide and a recruit footer (a different form from the main footer). The SVG clipPath of the round blob photo window was replaced by a circle (circle 48.6vw), and the photo background of the application guide panel is a light pink panel.

Careers cursor circle: the original script has code that opens a colored circle over links, but the circle element (.js-c-mousestalker) isn’t in the page HTML, so nothing actually shows (it wasn’t caught in the original measurement either) — so it wasn’t built
Pages below the recruit header menu (roots, climate, work, story, recruit info, apply) are not in the archive, so they link to inner anchors (#intro etc.)
The Instagram section has seven photo slot placeholders instead of the external feed. Gallery photo count is four, same as the original

title: Black and white architecture studio page with line-cube spaces and layered doors
good_for: A one-page intro for an architecture, interior or design studio, or a monochrome portfolio.

pages.use: A one-page studio introduction — Hero with a full-width wordmark and a cell-header menu, a line-cube 3D space with words attached, three fixed panels (solid · confident · quiet), we see and hear, clock sequence, four steps and layered-door 3D, a Work collection where a center band opens, horizontally flowing services, process spread, team and world, contact — the end loops back to the Hero. For architecture and design studio landing pages.

notes: The original cube·door scene is a metal material painted with three 0.1xx modules, a glTF (Draco) door model, an HDR environment and three lights (Main·Fill·Rim) — the model and environment files are not used, so the same placement and spread order are made with our basic shapes (five line panels and diagonal slats) and a line material. No metal reflections or shadows

The original watch movement scrolls through an image sequence (watch_white.json) and a room sequence (room.json) — we don’t use the sequence images, we drew three gears on a canvas and spin them in the same place over the same scroll range (top bottom → bottom top). The room sequence spot wasn’t built (couldn’t find which section it belongs to in the recording)
The original door section’s step transitions have spots where numbers and shapes change via morphSVG. Only number text swapping and DrawSVG line drawing were done instead of MorphSVG

The original loads swiper and lottie-web, but where they are used in the recorded screens could not be found (guessed to be the phone Work collection swipe), so they are not included — the next person should drag the original Work collection on a phone and match the swiper version
”We see, hear, touch and feel” word highlight on, and the length and spacing of the work strip could not be fully read from the bundle, so they were estimated from the screen (how: guess)

The loop from the end back to the Hero works by a Hero clone attached at the end secretly jumping back to the top when it reaches the top — the original is presumed to use the lenis approach (not measured)

Two accepted: ① loader length·curve — the original with the same code, measured twice, wobbles with first change 2983ms·4383ms·length 3916·6583ms, mixing in blank screens that wait on Nuxt·three·Draco downloads. ② cookie close end value — the original code (y 12 · .3s Out) and the copy are the same, and the original’s first sample is already 20% moved so there is a difference

title: Five colored ribbons streaming from a taxi exhaust in a transport company intro
good_for: A homepage for a taxi, transport or local service company with a friendly profile and recruiting, dividing sections with bright five-color waves.

pages.use: Company home page — opening screen where a taxi rolls in and three exhaust ribbons cover the screen, intro text beside a fixed vertical title, section title where a taxi crosses and a band forms, service·event card slider, three rounded-square About blocks, recruiting video band, News·columns, CONTENTS of five stacked panels

Service list — big header with a color band crossing between a white top and blue bottom, flowing outlined text, two-column rounded cards, six dark icon links on a cream panel. For a business or service category list

Recruiting home — large gold header, big English pledge and in-car photo, message split in two, reverse-flowing band, reasons list·bar chart, two work-life figures, big number circles, interview band, benefit cards, region-by-region hiring rows, four career photos, four yellow icons, phone·apply row
Leader message — small header with a five-color fan flowing at top right, seven blocks of long greeting text, title and handwritten signature. For the leader greeting in a company About
News list — list divided by thin lines with date, arrow and one-line title, plus purple circle page numbers. For notice and press lists

Online survey / application form — intro text, then inside a rounded gray panel a name field, inputs, yes/no and checkbox rows, with a dark pill Send button in the center. For surveys, inquiries and applications

notes: The wave panel·ribbon·section title band·sub-header fan were not ported from the original shaders but rewritten with our own shaders: the noise is our 3D gradient noise (same texture as the original simplex but a different shape), and the phone uses the same noise too (the original phone uses sine multiplication). Instead of the original canvas’s 1.4x height·perspective camera (FOV 3), a screen-sized orthographic camera fits the panel to pixel positions.

Phone hero ribbon: in the original the ribbon bulges up big and covers the top of the screen. The original coordinates (different horizontal and vertical units) couldn’t be carried over as is, so on phone only the thickness is multiplied by 3.2 (uStretch). The shape is similar but the figure is eyeballed.

The band in the large header (Service·Careers) is an approximation: instead of the original’s six lines + angular gradient, it adds a left tint (.35) to the same fan shader. The origin and angle (-0.09π) were matched by eye against the original screen.

After the chapter-title taxi passes, the line → band switch swells from behind the taxi first like the original (the further back, progress +0.75×distance^1.5). The slope of the line stage was simplified with a tan approximation.

Hero slogan 'MAKE IT / COLORFUL.' Seat is an English placeholder 'MAKE IT / BRIGHTER.'(similar character count). The original has two SVG gradient text layers — front (overlay blend) and back (behind canvas) — same structure with two CSS gradient text layers.

Vertical title is a placeholder for Korean vertical writing in place of the original Japanese vertical text (writing-mode: vertical-rl). The three bars are 1px lines instead of the original SVG rects.

The logo is a placeholder in Outfit bold italic letters instead of the original wordmark. Taxi and wheels are our own SVG (body, windows, lights, wheels spin separately). Service logos and channel icons are image placeholders (what to insert is in data-label).
Fonts: Gilroy (paid) → Outfit, Japanese Hiragino → Pretendard.

The original service page’s 12 service cards are cut to 6, and the recruiting page’s work images, interviews and benefits cards are reduced to image placeholders. The recruiting page KV’s 'expandYellow'(the original branch where gold spreads into the band) is not built separately but done with the same fan with the base set to gold.
The original video (recruiting band) is a video placeholder in the same spot and ratio (951:560). Autoplay loop is not set since there is no video file.

Hero taxi slides out (0→-50vw 2s) as in the original 'First scroll after the Hero sequence passes 3.5 seconds'Runs only when — once the sequence is over, scrolling down for the first time leaves a taxi in the original too.

title: Typographic experiments on a graph-paper grid for a musician site
good_for: An experimental personal site for a musician, composer or creator, built only from type and grids for bio, works and track lists.

pages.use: Home page — a vertical name centered in an empty grid, two lyric blocks typed out in mixed fonts in step with scroll (when finished only the song title becomes a link), date-cell news flowing inside a 400vh pinned window, and a ‹Next› band that advances when you keep scrolling at the end. For text and grid focused artist heroes
About — four-character names fitted to the cells and body text 10 columns wide, with a bio that has gradient plus ASCII pattern bands between the lines. For short bio and self-intro pages.

Work list — on the left a beige grid with a column of 5 covers, only the center cover shows its title with previous and next titles floating, and on a white panel a hand drawn with that title’s letters follows the cursor. For entries and work lists that have covers

Song list playground — a board of song titles scattered without overlap that you push endlessly by dragging or wheel, shrinking the farther they are from the center circle. Touching a title turns on its lyrics, and touched titles are joined by curves. Suits discographies and indexes with many song or work titles.

notes: The original locks the body and attaches Lenis anew to an inner box (.default) on every page. Capture and measuring tools only read window scroll, so here the window is scrolled with the same Lenis 1.3.23 and the same settings (0.7s, 1-(1-t)^5, autoRaf). The visible result and the wheel accumulation of the Next strip (2% per tick, 7% on touch) are the same.

The original’s 23 sound effects (recorded files), the line canvas drawn to the sound and the 16-step sequencer, and the color-flip effect (data-burakura) that inverts colors for 0.23s when the sequencer plays the ‹yu› sound were not carried over — the recorded files cannot be copied. With sound on, only short WebAudio-made sounds and a 9-bar bounce near the cursor play.

The hand in the Activities section is the original’s hand video rendered as ASCII with p5 (2.3, LGPL so it can’t go into _vendor) — the video is also an original asset so it isn’t used. Instead, a hand silhouette drawn with shapes is measured by brightness per cell and redrawn at 12fps using the letters of the current hero title. The fingertip follows the cursor (on the left side up to 1/3 of the screen) and the arm reaching in from off-screen at the bottom right were matched via interact capture.

The lyrics’ “reading kana → kanji” swap is a Korean placeholder, so it was changed to “jamo → syllable”. The four fonts (Zen Kurenaido · New Tegomin · Shippori Mincho B1 · Zen Kaku) have no Hangul, so they are backed by Gaegu · Song Myung · Nanum Myeongjo · Noto Sans KR.

The logo was newly drawn as a black blob symbol of the same ratio (218:132) instead of the original artwork, and the menu characters for one-two-three, ask, sound, yes/no and next item were replaced with One·Two·Three·Ask·Sound·Yes/No·Next.

The contact and lab (lab-*) pages weren’t recorded, so they weren’t built — the door cell stays # (the original swup link picker a[href]:not([href*="#"]) stays as is, so it stays put without advancing).
The original reloads when crossing 767px (breakpointReload). It isn’t included because the mixed build would wipe other sections’ state, so only the column count is re-measured.
The original could not be viewed with phone-width interact (inner scroll), so the phone state was checked only against the original CSS values and compare still screens.

Since swup swaps only #swup, every page carries the css and js of all four pages (the original Astro also ships one bundle). .sh-container·.contents·.sh-foot etc., which used to collide between page css files, are scoped with [data-page-name].

On the album → home transition, after the cover lifts, the tail until the home screen is fully up is longer than the original (330ms for .84→1) — it seems to come from swup rebuilding the grid cells and the lyric typing timeline in a single frame right after swapping in the long home document. It can be reduced by building only the visible grid rows first and filling in the rest later (the next person’s job).

title: Scenes revealed like window frames over a water-ring gradient for a lodge
good_for: A homepage for an inn, ryokan, glamping, sauna or nature experience facility where photos lead the place introduction.

pages.use: Lodging first page — rounded cover intro, hero where a half-width photo at the bottom left fills the screen, fading wordmark, five photo scenes revealed like window frames (copy rising one character at a time on green, gray-brown and teal panels with asymmetric photos), stay and sauna bands, and a large booking button.

About (concept) — small title, big copy, panorama photo and centered serif text on a pale forest background, a self-flowing photo strip, five cards of title + text + two photos, and a credits line. For brand philosophy and sustainability About pages

News list — title and categories pinned on the left (click to filter in place), with dotted lines separating the date, tag and title rows on the right. For announcement and media lists (the category URL /news/news-category/media uses the same layout)

Lodging guide: hero with big copy + vertical photo, full-bleed aerial photo, dotted-table usage guide, and a facility guide on a green panel (shortcut buttons · large photo per room · splide photo row · details box). For room and plan guide pages.

notes: Archived subpage 4 (news category /news/news-category/media) has the same type as the News list, so it is not built separately. The category button on news.html filters in place (the original uses a different address per category).
The News item (article) page was not recorded so it was not built — the Hero news row links to news.html

The original photos, logo, video and SVG lettering (the brand name and the tagline Savor the water and wind.) were not used. The wordmark is STIX Two Text letters scaled to the panel width, and the logo is a newly drawn placeholder of a circle and waves
The five videos in the scene use one placeholder video of the same ratio (3:2) and length (5s loop) (media/loop-3x2.mp4), set to play only when visible

The npm browser build of lenis 1.3.8 (dist/lenis.min.js) is not wrapped and uses the globals t·e·r …, so it gets overwritten by the global r in splide.min.js — avoided by loading it at the very end of the libraries

Subpages apply motion .6s late on first open — matched to the measured delay where the original attaches motion after downloading a large bundle script, so photos and headlines turn on that much later
The original English version (/en/) was not built — the header EN is index.html?lang=Reopens the same first page with en (like the original, no intro, only the first screen turns on again)
The original menu’s sauna, dining, activities and access pages were not recorded, so menu items 2, 3, 4 and 6 are # placeholders
The big wordmark in the phone menu panel rises one character at a time like the original, but the menu panel’s gradient type (navi) is made only by switching the type of the background part
Typeface backfill: the only spot switched to English is the index Hero intro text (kv__summary, STIX Two Text) — 40 words in 6 lines to match the original’s 6 English lines and 38 words
All page titles, menu, copy and footer — the original uses a Japanese Mincho title (vdl-v7mincho), Korean kept. --kf-font-display loads Nanum Myeongjo first, so the pairing already matches

The index intro section image can’t be captured by library-shots (at capture time the box measures under 20px and under 200px wide) — it had no image in shots even before the font backfill. The intro text was not changed

title: Text column body melting into a letter grid for a research project
good_for: A text-centered site for a research project, publication, archive or journal that lays out articles as horizontal columns and renders body text with a rippling letter texture.

pages.use: Post list Hero — equal-width columns (new-post label · author · title) lined up horizontally and pushed by wheel·drag, and below the header the entire body is a fixed-width uppercase grid canvas that scatters and ripples further down. A raised column turns red including the header and scattered letters, filtered by type buttons. For post archive·journal lists

Project About — section name pinned on the left, body two columns wide in the middle of a six-column grid (email, two About paragraphs, participant name links, maker, sponsor note), sponsor logos at the end. For research and publishing project About and credits.

notes: Fonts: Century Schoolbook (URW Century Schoolbook L) loads TeX Gyre Schola, the same design, from cdnfonts (PT Serif if blocked), and the paid NEXT Mono Thin becomes IBM Plex Mono 100 — since the glyph width goes 5.88→6px, by the original formula (floor(300/glyph width)×glyph width) the column goes 294→300px

The canvas grid text is fixed-width, one character per cell, so Korean (two cells wide) breaks the grid. The body placeholder is English words (the header author and title are also English placeholders). The About body is Korean.
The sponsor logos at the end of the About page are placeholders at the same spot and size (center four columns wide, 64px tall) instead of the original images

title: Horizontal-flowing selective course recruitment page scanning down a 3D statue
good_for: An education program landing page for a selective class, special lecture, academy or residency recruitment that runs concept, intro, purpose, curriculum, instructors, requirements and application on one page.

pages.use: One-page course recruitment — giant title split around a 3D head, concept manifesto, three About cells flowing horizontally·orbit diagram purpose·3×3 curriculum cards·stippled reviewer panel·recruitment details that go further down vertically, and a final question above a light ring underfoot with an apply button. For academy·selective class landing pages

notes: The original is a single page (pages: [] in pages.json), so there are no subpages.

3D camera: the SECTION_SYNC_SCROLL section table from the original _desktop chunk (position and target for top · concept · about · purpose · curriculum · supervisor, ease none between sections), SPLASH (from a far spot behind the head, 8s expo.out, is-a1 → 1000ms → is-a2), the render position following at .5 per frame, the 30° field of view, and the world sway (yurayura) were carried over as they are. Targets use anatomical positions (original head 75 · chest 37.5 · hip 0 → ours 1.6 · 1.225 · .85), and the distance was scaled by the head-size ratio of the original first scene (.00574). The original actor model (gltf+draco) could not be used and ours is built from basic shape pieces, so the proportions differ.

apply·entry camera: the original views a walking actor (walk 10f·30fps) and a footprint-dot floor from separately placed ground heights, so no basis to carry over into our piece coordinates was found in the bundle. We use the spot looking at our glow ring under the feet. The original’s walk motion, footprint stamp (press .1/2s · effect .3/2.7s) and floor reflection are not there yet

The original 3D textures (scanned face, sheen material, blue spot #00deff, 10s pulse band) and screen post-processing (fluid distortion, RGB split, depth blur, grain) are not carried over — only basic shape pieces with basic lighting

Reviewer version: rebuilt as a WebGL point cloud like the original — on first view, a 4s power4.out reveal (threshold .95→.12 · 1.1x silhouette · 1.35x points · scattered rotation .5 · depth 0→own depth), tint dark→bright (contrast 1.4/1 · gamma 1.2), and two light bands running along the depth over 8 seconds (width .1 · strength 2) are original values. The original photo, depth and light maps (sprite 4×2) can’t be used, so upper-body silhouette brightness is used for color and depth — put data-src on .h-ht to use that photo’s brightness instead. Point size is matched to the cell size because the original absolute value (80 × 260/z) is in original plate units.

Loading: the original opens SPLASH as soon as asset loading finishes. The copy also waits only for fonts and 3D readiness (the fake 0.35/0.8/1.3s waits added earlier were removed), and the number closes the gap to its target by .33 each frame

BigBang narrow ink-trap and Reign are paid fonts, so they were swapped to League Gothic and Inter, and the Japanese body text to Noto Sans KR. League Gothic is slightly wider, so the giant words run a few % longer than the original, and the letter hover distance (110% of letter width) is correspondingly larger.

The logo is a tilted shape + ”Logo wordmark” placeholder instead of the original mark. The original’s external links (application form · course detail · SNS) were changed to same-page section jumps or empty links.
Tablet (768~1024) drops the original’s is-v-m details (such as stacking the header label on two lines) and carries over only the rules common to phone and desktop.

title: Aquarium-themed school intro with floating fish and bubbles
good_for: Schools, cram schools, and education programs, or hands-on facilities like aquariums and zoos, that need a bright water-toned recruitment page.

pages.use: School home page — a hero where fish swim in and a ring pops up, a white oval intro with a feature card slider, four course panels that stick under the title and shrink, a creature-guide card stack, a social grid with link cards, and a water-toned footer with two flowing rows of photos. For the home page of an education and hands-on facility
Application (web) — per-department pastel boxes with enrollment year and application period fields and an apply button, plus in-progress event cards. For student and trainee recruitment schedules
Request materials — two boxes for paper and digital guides plus an apply button, with a contact box below. For the entrance to material requests and inquiries
School About — for an index-style intro that links to sub pages with six photo cards below the intro text (greeting, instructors, facilities, directions, etc.)
News list — year·category filter and a list of date·category tag·title rows, plus an ongoing event card. For notice and news boards
News item — dot title, date, tag, body, schedule list, event button, back to list. For notice detail pages

notes: Cutouts (original photo PNGs) of fish, animals and people are placed as silhouette SVGs and photo placeholders with the same position, size and motion (from 100px right with back.out(2) 4s, up and down 5~8s) — the original hero copy (lettering image) is rebuilt as text in the same spot

The water-colored background (original bg_grad.jpg photo), light ring (kv_bg_circle.png) and bubble art (bubble.svg) are images, so they were redrawn as a CSS gradient, SVG ring and canvas (ring rotates 10s, bubble values from the original)

Swiper build: the original bundle is Swiper 11.0 series (has loopAddBlankSlides, no swiperSlideGridSet), so the closest swiper@11.1.1 in _vendor was used. The keen-slider build has no marker in the bundle, so 6.8.6 in _vendor
In the original creature-guide slider, advancing on touchmove hijacks phone scrolling, so it was left out. Only tap-to-next and 4s autoplay were carried over.
The official SNS photo grid is an Instagram feed plugin (Smash Balloon) in the original, so it is set as twelve square placeholders in the same spot (no lightbox)

Sub pages of the menu such as departments and school life (course detail, greeting, creature guide, events) were not recorded so they were not built — menu links go to our page and the rest to #. The sub header fish was random from five sets in the original but is fixed to one set

title: Monochrome music label with glitch slices and X-tape section dividers
good_for: Music labels, creator agencies, and merch brands that bundle about, releases, roster, and news into one black-and-white site.

pages.use: Music label home page — glitch mark whose horizontal pieces snap together · X-shaped tape boundary · About · wordmark marquee · News · release list · artist cards · Contact. For a label, agency or merch brand home
News list — header with a folding row cover · row list where a white cover fills in on hover · pagination. For label notice lists
Label About — guide-line canvas greeting · hover-photo support list · rainbow keyword cards. For label statements and support details
Release list — release rows with a white pill and spinning disc cover on hover · pagination. For music and merch release lists
News item — group photo body with three other news items and paging. For label notice article detail

notes: The symbol · wordmark do not use the original logo, they are a newly drawn oval S symbol and LABEL WORDMARK lettering fitted to width with textLength. The three stickers (square hologram · globe · band) were also redrawn as SVG in the same position · size · tilt.

The hero glitch carries over the original structure as is (ten overlapping vertical strips stacked in the center, 100%→10% wide, with per-strip horizontal scales 1.4·1.35·1.3·1.25·1.2·1.15·1.05·.95·.8·.45 → reaches 1 at 312px of scroll, a flat plate switches on from 437→561px, and the whole plate drops 160px over 0→1123px). The artwork inside the strips is a dotlottie in the original (460×401, 0.48s loop), but measuring it showed zero animated properties, i.e. a still image, so the static SVG symbol in this copy behaves the same (only the symbol shape is our own).

The two-line wordmark above the hero and below the footer was measured from the original dotlottie (1360×184·60fps, appear) and rebuilt as an SVG+GSAP entrance with the same timing. Bottom line → second piece → top piece rise at .2s intervals from 25.5/184 of the height below over .8s cubic-bezier(0,0,0,1) while fading on at constant speed over .8s. The hero one starts after 3.48s (4.78s plate), the footer one immediately (1.2s plate). The piece shapes cut our wordmark in the original’s proportions.

The X-shaped tape is the original dotlottie (1440×274 · 60fps 300 frames at .5x speed = 10s, text line moves 367 · bold band 1485 units) — instead, a CSS marquee is given the original speed (at 1440 width, text line 36.7px/s · bold band 148.5px/s, proportional to panel width) via JS. ±3.6° · the holographic band at the end of the bottom row stays as is. Tape copy is a placeholder

Menu names are ABOUT·RELEASE·ARTISTS·NEWS·CONTACT instead of the original proprietary words (STATEMENT etc.), and functional labels such as VIEW MORE·CATEGORY·GET IN TOUCH·BACK TO LIST·PREVIOUS/NEXT PAGE·MENU/CLOSE are kept in English as is. Large section titles are placeholders like LIST TITLE·CARD TITLE·SECTION TITLE·KEYWORD ONE.

The artist detail, release detail and contact form pages were not recorded, so they were not built. ARTISTS links to #artists on the home page, and CONTACT and GET IN TOUCH link to #contact on the same page. The music and video icons are # placeholders.
The five category links in the news list were left out because they show at width 0 in the original.

The disc that rises from behind on artist card hover was drawn after measuring the original dotlottie (252×252, constant 360° over 5s): a rainbow conic disc with circular text at the same speed (one turn per 5s). The hover rainbow on the About page keyword cards is a CSS gradient instead of the original image
At 841px and below, as in the original tablet rules, roll, pill and photo-move hovers are turned off, and at 390 the sticker parallax is 0 as in the original.

The original is a STUDIO SPA, so the document stays put when moving between pages. The copy also swaps only #swup with swup 4.8.3 (plus js, head and preload plugins). Going to a subpage, a 13-line curtain covers in .75s, the new page’s loader stays covered (ms measured per page on the original) and then lifts. Going to the first page, it moves straight to the wordmark loader. The loader art is our own, matched to frames captured from the original (first page wordmark flicker at .5–1.6s, subpage 13-line curtain). When opened as a file (file:), it falls back to normal navigation after the curtain covers

Of the Lottie files, the GET IN TOUCH hover dotlottie (1296×270 · 1.4s) is rebuilt as the original measured: one line of letters rolling (.3s) and the dot scaling 1.1x. The first About dotlottie (1296×440 · 1.98s) is rebuilt as ‹HELLO, IT'The ‹S US› letters rise at 1s cubic-bezier(0,0,0,1) with .1s intervals when the curtain starts to lift. The home page loader dotlottie (1360×184·4.21s) is replaced by a wordmark SVG blink, so the pixel distribution differs.

Font backfill: slots changed to English. The first-line release track title (original numeric title) became Track 01, the third-line artist name and the third artist card name (original Latin names) became NAME (index and release alike), and the index hidden h1 label name became LABEL NAME. Large titles, menu, labels and English body text were already English placeholder copy.

Article title in the detail header’s travel path — the original is a Japanese article title, kept in Korean. --kf-font-display calls Noto Sans KR after Montserrat (sans-serif ↔ gothic) so the pair matches
About large body · news titles · Japanese release titles · item titles · card summaries — the original is Japanese (Noto Sans JP), Korean kept (Noto Sans KR via --kf-font-ko)

Small subtitles and two-line contact copy that mix a brand’s English name with Japanese particles (about · what is · support for · uniqueness of · to) keep the Korean placeholder text — the original also uses a Japanese typeface (Noto Sans JP), so it was judged not to be a Latin title font slot

title: Faculty launch site with a fixed 3D wave and a flowing column of cards
good_for: Faculty or department openings, school and institute introductions, and institutional sites that present lots of information as a sequence of cards.

pages.use: School home — a fixed left symbol and tag with a right card column, vision blinking text, and 16 cards: video, about, strengths line art, two courses, career carousel, voices, news, overview, brochure, admissions, data visualization, questions, campus, directions, contact, related links. For information-heavy school or institution homes

School About — video and founding purpose, talent-profile band illustration and 01~03 strength cards, career carousel, six voices, prep office head’s greeting, faculty cards. For school and institution About subpages
News list — ten rows of date and title, numbered paging, back-to-top button. For notice and news lists
Single news item — date, a title with a growing red bar, 16:9 photo, body with red-underlined subheadings and links, list button. For notices and event report posts

notes: Fixed background: the original feeds a white wing-wave video (720 square, .9x speed, 30fps) into a shader and combines it with a clock-minute-hand angle gradient using overlay, hard light, soft light, average and lighten. The composite formula, angle, 30fps, .9x speed and the blend-mode change on ”sdb” input (vivid light·subtract) were carried over the same, and in the video slot we drew our own instance’s plate wave (brightness only). Remaining difference: the wing shape (large feather curved surfaces, camera movement in the video) is the content of the original video asset, so it can’t be copied, and scene values can’t be measured from a video, so a plate wave stands in. A hash grain of the same 11x tile replaces noise.png.

Data visualization card: the original is a rig that draws a baseball stadium glb model and hit data (data/hitting.json) with three (BgyJO_4p.js·BPJsxDXS.js — night lighting, point cloud, camera moves). For now a flat canvas stadium painted with skin variables and player dot trails remain. Blocked: it is an 84KB scene rig, so within the 150-minute cap per place the symbol, vision, three feature items and background composite were matched first and this was left. Next person: measure the bundle’s camera, lighting and point-size values, then build the three scene with our basic shape stadium (fan-shaped field, spectator ring) and placeholder hit trajectories (three is in _vendor).

Symbol: the original logo artwork (animation-file image and track-matte layers) is not used. It is rebuilt in the same composition from placeholder letters A·B·C plus four English lines. Timing and curves (3s after 1s, 6 white-square flashes, piece entrances at 11·14·21·24·27·29f, English wipe 52→64.6f, 2.1s tag) are read as is from the animation layers. The piece shapes were mattes fitted to the original strokes, so our letters use half, pillar and body rectangular cuts instead.

Vision heading: the original is a Lottie drawn in Japanese stroke order, so in our Korean placeholder each character is wiped evenly across the same ranges instead of by stroke (first line 0.3~13.1f · second line 18.8~39.9f, 4f curve .001,0,.999,1). The blue shadow leading by 1f, the first word’s 20px shift with the 20f jump, and the second word’s 90px shift (25→32f) are the same

Photo corner block: the original opens one WebGL context per photo and draws 3D simplex noise from the cell coordinates and time. Inside a cell it is a single value, so the same 3D simplex formula (cell coordinates, (time+seed)×.3) is painted per cell on a canvas to produce the same picture — judged so that more than ten photos do not hit the browser’s WebGL context limit (16)

Talent profile band: 12 window slots · 160×32 · band width (blue 52.8 + gradient 158 + blank, one loop 288px) · speed (289px per 179.2f) were read from Lottie. The gradient plate’s anchor point could not be read because the layer size (w·h) is not in the bundle, so only the initial phase may differ

Page transition: the original is an SPA, so there is no transition curtain and the new page cards rise in 3D .5s late. Ours is multi-page, so we clear the pillars over .3s, navigate, then do the same 3D entrance. When returning home from a subpage, the vision is already fully written and only the panel is wiped in from the right with .7s expo (.2s late) — matched using a flag left on navigation (sessionStorage)
The video window is just a black box and a spinning circle (no YouTube), and the access map is a grayscale placeholder
English section titles (About, Features, News, etc.) are generic English labels so they keep the same typeface, and original copy was swapped for Korean placeholders
Recorded type detail (single news item) was corrected to article per the README and built as article.html
On the news list, pagination only moves the active mark and locks the prev/next buttons, the list content does not change

Section height: the placeholder text is shorter than the original, so features, courses, careers, voices, news and others were up to 1,500px short — the voice cards (6) and news rows (5) are expanded to the original count, and on desktop the rest get the original 1440 measured section height as min-height so the scroll position where the ripple gap between cards arrives matches (phone unchanged)

First-load card entrance: in the original SectionReveal3D the cards stand in place on first load, and only when arriving from another page does the on-screen card rise in .5s late — the copy also raises it only when arriving via our page link. The original’s rise on table-of-contents jumps (.3s) and the neighboring section’s transparent fade-in (.8s) are not there yet
Career and campus carousels were fixed to the original values (career: no loop · start at 1 · gap 8/16 · .3s, campus: no loop · gap 16/24 · .4s, button locks at the end slide)

index overview tuition breakdown (”Breakdown” · admission fee · tuition · facilities fee · lab fee, five lines) — the original sets kanji (breakdown · admission fee…) in the Nippo numeral typeface, so Korean is kept. Pairing is Pretendard (gothic, close to Nippo’s sans-serif feel)

Font backfill: spots where the original used a Latin typeface (section English titles, overview English names, professor English names, Read more, date numerals, four English symbol lines) are already English placeholders, so nothing changed — which is why the hero and section images were not re-captured either.

title: Campus magazine with tilted instant photos and pop-out stickers

For a student magazine home.
Article list — handwritten POSTS + two search buttons, Polaroid bundles and stickers by topic, tag cloud, and two banners for gallery · glossary. For article collections grouped by topic · tag
Gallery — four-column film photos that cover and rise over a fixed cloud-sky head panel, click to enlarge, back-to-top button stuck to the bottom. For photo collections and photo essays

Single article — a vertical video and title card on two tilted sheets of paper, a pinned photo (fades between images) with table of contents and interview body, a next-article card, and a corner statue speech-bubble button. For interview and feature articles.

New SVGs were drawn in the same position and size — the stickers are handwriting-font (Gaegu) text with a white outline, so the original sticker illustrations and shadows are absent. Next person to continue by drawing more art.

The polaroid thumbnail is also an autoplay, loop, muted video in the original (a nearly still 9.6s screen where only a small doodle over a four-photo collage shimmers) — in the same form, a 9.6s placeholder video (media/thumb.mp4, 224×312) where a nearly still panel has only one small band shimmering is attached with the same attributes (a placeholder with the whole screen moving kept the list section from settling for 15 seconds, so it was changed)
