title: Public-interest site with a tunnel intro and eyelid transitions that simulate vision
good_for: Public awareness campaigns, condition-education sites, and experiential learning pages that let visitors experience the issue (entry, choose, experience with explanation).

pages.use: Experiential public-interest hero — tunnel-hole intro that follows the mouse, film-still hero, two eye buttons (Enter · Without sound). For the entrance of a condition-awareness or experience campaign
Symptom picker — a grid of 8 symptom cells that swell like a lens on hover. For list screens where users choose an item to try

One symptom experience — simulator where dragging the dot scale narrows the field of view, explanation card, unfolding Curve panel, fixed explanation, film strip, treatment card, help card wheel. For item details with experience + explanation

notes: The archived pages.json recorded only one page, the first page. Its two buttons lead only to /conditions, and the card’s two key scenes (the aging scale simulator and the symptom ring icon) sit below it, so /conditions and /conditions/tunnel-vision on the original address were captured directly in headless mode and built as list and detail (judgment call). Seven detail pages of the same shape were reduced to one

The code pieces for the detail page are not in the archive, so the curved panel curvature (30vh→6vh)·film strip tilt (6°→2°)·help card wheel rotation (±18°)·pinned card position are estimates measured from scroll captures. The eyelid·intro timetable·eye button·cell bulge shader·dive into the eye are the original code values as they are.

Text dissolve was switched to the original’s WebGL (three) version: text is drawn on a plane and tears from left to right (three noise layers 70, 24, 9px, depth 480px, edge 24px, scroll-in reveal 2s linear). The original uses three r185, but the r185 in _vendor is CJS only, so r186, which has a global build, was loaded.

The depth-map tilt of the first page photo (TILT .012) was reduced to pushing the whole plate 1.2% of the plate width away from the mouse — the depth map is a grayscale image baked separately for each original photo, so placeholder photos have no depth to read. The blur when the eye zooms in (original: 8-tap radial smear from the focus point + color split .35) was approximated with CSS blur 34px×t — the same shader can only be applied once the photo sits on a WebGL plate (same issue as the line above).

The eight symptom ring icons were redrawn as SVG loops in the same place and size instead of the original Rive animations. The Rive runtime (MIT) can be used, but the motion lives inside the original .riv file and cannot be copied, and our own .riv cannot be made without the Rive editor.

Rebuilt the WebGL veil that blocks the simulator’s view from the original tunnel shader values (ellipse stretch .75·1.2 → screen-ratio circle, radius .95→.3, softness .55→.16, .6s power3 following the age ticks). The original detail code isn’t in the archive, so I read it from fragments at the live address. The scene isn’t a video texture as in the original but a backdrop-colored veil laid over the DOM photo slot at (1 − vignette), so the result is the same. The other seven symptom shaders (double vision, ripple, blur, glare, spots, color shift, central loss) are the same kind of detail, so I didn’t build them. The expanded symptom card shape is an estimated .6s horizontal expansion from 9rem→35rem.

The sound (headphone) button only changes its on indicator with no sound — the original audio can’t be copied and there is no placeholder audio file. Original external links (institutions, clinical trials, find a specialist) were changed to in-page anchors.
Font brush-up-too (paid) is replaced with Kirang Haerang plus a -7° slant — the dry-brush texture of the original is missing. The logo is redrawn as a spreading pink ring + name slot.

Detail page interactions were matched using the code and css from the original’s live address — symptom card (9rem→min(44rem, screen−8rem) .7s cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1) · plus fades out .4s · text shifts 2rem), a scrub where the Hero side elements rise 8vh (down button 20vh) and fade out over the first 25% of a screen of scroll, down button moves one screen down in 1.5s, arrow bobbing 2s, sound button .3s ease-out · slash line 33 .35s, symptom picker with eight dots (on hover the current dot turns pink and the rest turn cream at random .07 intervals .2s→pink .4s), next-symptom background 5→10% .5s · arrow .5rem, lens button text horizontal .95. The bottom double underline is overwritten by the tool button in _shared/wire.js, so hover cannot be measured with the measuring tool (the css is the same as the original). The original Hero has an eye blink that closes and opens at random every 3~8s (.28s power2.in · .22s · .24s power2.out), but it can only be applied when the scene is a WebGL version, so it was not built (same issue as the fluid post-processing above)

title: Forest-green nursery site with torn brush edges and hand-drawn art
good_for: Nurseries, kindergartens, schools, and nature-activity facilities that want a warm site mixing illustrations with photos.

pages.use: Original first page — a page that sharpens in from blur, a big torn-edge photo (three slowly zooming in and crossfading on a 21s cycle), a vertical title tag, two tilted feature cards, intro text stepping back like stairs, a green guide card panel, an endlessly flowing photo row, a vertical-writing recruit section, three staggered blog cards, and a footer with a feature card · contact box · torn playground photo

Story (education philosophy) — hand-drawn forest and children around a big English title, wiggling on a 1.5s beat, green heading, mixed-size photo flow, three sections: yard, field and paddy. For institution About and brand story pages

Blog list — white category panel pinned to the screen and staggered two-column text cards (vertical category pills), pagination. For the News/blog list (the category list /blog/category/tweet has the same shape).

Staff recruitment — sub hero (large torn photo + vertical title over a green wave strip), green heading, and below the photo flow an 830px inner scroll panel (pinned vertical title · rotating badge) with four work environments and benefits, then a green recruitment guidelines card. Fits recruitment pages.

notes: Hand drawings: the story page’s hand drawings (dozens of trees, fields, children and animals, original PNGs) were redrawn by placing five of our SVG pieces (round tree, conifer, dotted bush, child, sprout) at the same spots and sizes — fewer prop varieties and less brush texture than the original. The jerky wiggle (1.5s steps(1), delays .15·.25·.4s) uses the step-nudge-loop part (newly made), applied to the same group.

Torn edges: the original masks (PNG · SVG) are not used. Brush-serrated edges are freshly baked from seed-fixed noise (img/*.svg originals → shared.css data URI, because opened via file:// the outside SVG masks are blocked by CORS) and hung in the same places. The paper grain pattern (t-bg texture jpg overlay) is not carried over, leaving a single cream background color

Page transition: as in the original script.js, body comes into focus from blur 30px and .8 opacity, and clicking a link blurs it again and navigates immediately — blur-page-fade part (newly extracted). The Hero photo crossfade is the slow-zoom-cycle part (newly extracted) with the 21s cycle keyframes as-is.

Category blogs (/blog/category/tweet) share the blog list’s layout, so a single news.html covers them. About the Institution, A Day at the Institution, Admission Info, Access, Contact, and post detail were not captured in the archive, so they were not built (menu links are #)

The original deSVG (swapping img for inline svg) and the swap of _sp images at screen width 800 have no image files, so there is nothing to port. The .inview.blur of jquery.inview becomes blur-focus-in (on entering view, blur 5px → 0 · .8s easeOutSine, opacity unchanged) with the same values

Blog category names and menu text match the original’s character count (Story·of·Nature·Tale, 14 characters, etc.) — the letter hop is staggered by .05s × character count, so a different count changes the stagger length

title: Craft brand with photos and vertical text set into a tile grid
good_for: Craft and material brand sites, artisan or workshop introductions, and small shops selling product series and samples.

pages.use: Brand home: a mosaic hero that splits a photo into three cell-mask layers pushed out of sync by scroll, an About with photos and vertical-writing sentences set in 275px grid cells, three products as cream cards on a patterned background, sample invitation, Contact cell. For craft and material brand landing pages.

Brand About — a section with nine photos, three bold lines of copy and in-cell body text placed cell by cell on a dark grid panel, closing with a full-width two-line wordmark. For workshop, artisan and brand story pages
News list — large two-line heading, a tag and archive filter box in the left column, news rows with thumbnails on the right. For news and notice lists
News article — bold title, date and tags, a 3:2 header photo, body mixing subheadings and product photos, arrow links, and a button back to the list. For product launches and announcements.

Shopping guide (terms and notice type) — a sticky table of contents on the left, and a wide right column with guide text made of subheadings, lists and two-column tables. For terms of use, privacy policy and shipping info.

notes: The original photos (clay · workshop · tile), the SC logo artwork and the slogan lettering image (Serious about tiles…) were not carried over — photos are placeholders describing subject, light and composition, the logo is a newly drawn S·C mark with bold strokes, and the slogan image is replaced with text of the same position and size (two lines of bold Mincho + two Latin lines squeezed to 75% width)

The cell masks of the hero mosaic (mosaic-shift) do not carry over the three original SVGs. Cells are split by a seed at the same cell size (276px, left 30 · top 106) and drawn anew, so which cell belongs to which layer differs from the original. Per-layer photo size·position table, shift distance, rise distance and curve are the original values
The product tile background (a wall photo tiled with that pattern) is redrawn with CSS gradients as half-circle, triangle and square patterns at the same tile size — there is no real tile texture

The first-visit panel is decided not by a cookie as in the original but by sessionStorage (one tab) — only the section first opened in the same tab shows the logo panel, and from the next sections the cells just clear away.

Product detail, swatch, and the three legal notices (privacy, terms, seller notice) were not recorded, so they were not built — the menu’s four notice links go to the shopping guide (guide.html) of the same type.

Between 781 and 1439px it stays 1rem like the original = Screen width/144 so it scales proportionally, 1rem at 767px and below = Follows the original phone cell (118px) at width/37.5. News list — category pills on the left, square-photo row list (title shifts and a triangle bobs on hover), pagination. For announcement and notice lists

Town About: cover photo (title runs all the way), vertical lead, video panel, numbered browse list, numbered facility cells, three-column grid, hand-drawn guide map and tour cards, and a dining section. For the menu slot ‹What kind of place is this›.
One facility (art museum) — cover video, vertical lead, endlessly flowing photo band, tour cards, four-cell collection grid, visitor guide. For facility and exhibition hall About pages

notes: Of the four recorded subpages, number 4 (/news/index.html) is the same page as the news list in number 1, so only one (news.html) was built. /museum was captured as page during recording and is kept as page.html (one facility).

Smooth scrolling uses the same ScrollSmoother as the original (smooth 1.5 · effects · normalizeScroll) with the GSAP 3.15 build from _shared (original bundle 3.12.7). Off on touch devices and with reduced motion.

The white curtain (loader) was made to lift after the font loads, as in the original, but measuring shows the original also changes within .3~.6s after first paint and ends (Typekit attaches quickly), so the copy lifts as soon as the font is ready — to make the curtain visible, give open() in shared.js a minimum time.

The weather row omits the original’s call to a weather API and only fills in today’s date — the weather icon and temperature are placeholders. The social strip (newsfeed__insta, 5-second carousel) shows posts from an outside account, so it was not built.

On the About page, the original’s eight spaces for the facility columns and grid (main building, warehouse, forest, outdoors, garden, stone park, garden, gallery) are cut to five, and the columns under the restaurant and café are reduced to one numbered list. The phone grid open/close (about’s grid3 accordion) is not built.

The hand-drawn guide map does not use the original painted map image — hills, fields, trees, roads and roofs are redrawn in SVG. The art colors are content, so they are marked ‘not skin’ in about.css. Dot labels follow the original down to the letter roll (15px).

The gallery photo strip was cut from the original 15 photos (three groups of 5, 429rem·59.58s) to 10 (286rem) with 39.72s, keeping the same speed (7.2rem/s). The collection was reduced from 19 pieces to 8, and the artwork list page and modal were not built.

The original YouTube modal in the video panel is a placeholder player panel at the same position and size (96×54rem), and the forest and gallery videos are 10-second gray placeholders with the same autoplay and loop (media/forest.mp4).
Hero photo swap: the first change is 4.6s as measured from the original (the original runs a 6s timer from DOM ready, and 1.4s passes while the curtain lifts), then every 6s.

The original hero and daily video use the jstream player (paid video hosting), so only a placeholder box + the same fade (1s linear after .5s) is placed — the play/pause sync when the daily video reaches the screen center is not included

Number shuffle (30ms random → real value), speech bubble bounce.out drop, and the about character line wrap exist only in page code and have not been extracted as parts yet — for the next person to pick up
Could not check by swapping theme.css between light and dark skins and capturing — only confirmed library-lint color 0 · font 0

The chronicle and message card rows pin the section and push horizontally. For music or work releases and dark-toned exhibition introductions

notes: The original is a single page (pages: [] in pages.json), so there are no subpages.

Font futura-pt (paid font service) is replaced by Jost, the closest free geometric sans-serif — letters are a bit narrower, so the title shadow is shorter than the original. Korean pairing is Noto Sans KR.

The two noise layers (original noise.png and noise_white.png) are new SVG feTurbulence tiles of the same size (166.5×110.5) instead of image files — the grain is similar but not identical. The jerky position shift (.3s steps(1), ten-column background-position) is the original value.
The six loader images (original band logo variants) are six drawings made by rotating a line-pattern logo mark.

The flashlight circles’ paths are fixed once, measured at the moment of load, just like the original — shapes inside the mask aren’t drawn, so getBoundingClientRect returns 0 and the original calculation receives n.width and n.height as 0, same here. The photo slots are placeholders baked as textures (background color · grid · diagonals), and putting a photo URL in data-src swaps in that photo (same origin only).

The 7-cell photo stack in the tech row (9 layers) keeps the original’s array order, delay (.05s apart) and covering rule (only the center cell is advanced by one cell), with a placeholder in the original photo’s main color laid on lightly instead of photos.

The original Astro view transition css has fade rules of .18s (site-loader) and .35s/.5s (root), but the same explorations css has ::view-transition-*(*) { animation: none !important } wins over all those rules, so the actual screen swaps instantly — that is why the v1 .18s body fade was removed. In the original, Astro ClientRouter fetches the document and swaps it in, so the background WebGL and loader carry over, but this build opens a fresh page (loader only once per session).
The original reloads the page when the width changes by more than 50px and applies an --app-height fix for in-app webviews. Neither was carried over (100lvh is used).
With prefers-reduced-motion, the loader is skipped, the stage follows scroll without scrub delay (scrub:true), and the card bounce and gallery tunnel flow stop.

As in the original, the work detail swaps a background · ink color pair per work onto the body’s --wk-bg · --wk-ink (the original’s three pairs are in the works.css header comment). The 7 other work detail pages of the same type were not built.

Shaders and GSAP can’t read var() or oklch, so they are resolved through SH.rgbOf and SH.vec3. The list page corner gauge color is --kf-ink (#191919) instead of the original #000.

This site’s open source is only lenis (switched to the original 1.3.17)·OGL (convex)·GSAP, and the dot-grid background is hand-written WebGL in the original too, so the hand-written shader is kept as is.

good_for: Hot spring, tourist area, regional guide, inn association, and traditional shop sites that evoke a Japanese mood with vertical writing, ink, and paper grain.

pages.use: Hot spring town front page — centered brush-script logo, vertical verses on the left and right with a vertical menu, crossfade photo strip, ink-line story box riding on the photo with three cards, two vertical text columns (hot spring · lodging), two-column lodging row, gray-green surrounding walk, notice, ink map and access. For the Hero of a regional / tourist-spot flagship site

Town story — wide-tracked title · sub menu, white vertical text over a pinned photo, eight era tabs (panel switches at .5s), sticky large vertical title + interview lines, a coming-soon section, Macy two-column customer-voice masonry. For an About page that bundles history and people stories

Header for article lists (articles, blog) — a big vertical title on the right is pulled up to the sub-menu row, with a vertical intro beside a 60% photo, plus a coming-soon notice for when there are no posts yet. At the top of column and blog lists

The washi paper background (the original bg-sand.jpg photo multiplied onto #f2f2f0) is redrawn as a mask from two feTurbulence noise layers (fine grain · large blotches) — the original’s large wave pattern is missing.
Ink-dot buttons (original sprite hover0~3, six frames) were redrawn as circle bundles + six twisted noise SVGs (same steps(5) .3s, same layering) — the bleed pattern shapes differ

The three original videos were cut off in the archive (no moov), so length could not be measured — 8-second looping placeholder videos (media/) of the same ratios (3:4 · 4:5) were baked in with ffmpeg
The access map (original map.png of a central region) was replaced with an abstract land-shape SVG (ink grain, white borders, pins)

Subpages not captured (interviews, guests, hot springs, trails nearby, four-season notebook, access, news list) were not built — menu links point to the nearest of the four pages (# anchor). The English link goes to the first page

Email address change form — labels, red required marks, four light gray field rows, privacy notice, round blue confirm button. For a single sign-up, change or inquiry form (corrected from detail, as detected during recording)

notes: The hand-drawn character illustrations in Hero·featured events·directions (student on a vehicle·seated student) are redrawn as flat SVG shapes of the same position·size — they lack the original’s line feel and expressions. A slot for the consumer to swap in their own illustration
Map · route from the station · campus layout (originally image files) are drawn simply as SVG maps at the same ratio
Title font Industry (paid font service) replaced by Saira, and the kanji title images (mv-ttl, ttl01) were replaced with Korean text

The mega dropdown on sub-pages (university main site CMS) does not actually open because the original markup has no box — the copy also shows only an underline and a down-triangle on hover. Site search is just an input (no external custom search)

Sub-page panel expansion (per visitor · search) and section link scrolling use jQuery as in the original (slideToggle 400ms · animate 550ms swing), with 1.12.4 from _vendor instead of the original 1.10.2. The pair mismatch (Access↔Contact) caused by the sub-page loader and page-turn lengths and the original’s four header buttons dropping out of the measurement candidates was accepted, with reasons noted
Went past 180 minutes (matching the sub-page CMS frames to the original hover values) — redrawing the hero illustration closer to the original line art is left to the next person

title: Vertical serif library site for a long-established confectionery shop
good_for: Brand archives for old shops, publishers, and workshops that line up books, reading, and products in vertical writing, with about text, book list, book spread, product cards, and photo panels.

pages.use: Book imprint home page — a loader where the logo blinks and a brown curtain sweeps away, fade photo hero, white section with vertical greeting, staggered vertical card book list, volume contents and book-spread Swiper (desktop), snack cards, two-column photo strip and photo board, black footer. For long-established shop · publishing brand intros.

Library (phone only) — pick a volume from a chooser list, read the book with a tab label and spread Swiper per volume, ending with a tea house card and photo strip. Wide screens go to the first-page library section. For pages where reading material and catalogs are flipped through on a phone

notes: sites pull stalled on a long file name from the font service, so the original code was read by extracting only html·css·js separately from the archived HAR.

Original class names (l-nav·c-list·p-home-…) are not used, they were renamed with sk- names. The behavior (jQuery animate 500ms scroll·fadeUp toggle·menu panel·select list) and the Swiper 8.4.7·magnific-popup 1.1.0 settings were rewritten fresh using the original values as they are.

title: Product news page with an oil-painted 3D stage and torn paper panels
good_for: Product update roundups, release notes, annual announcement pages, and long news pages grouping hundreds of features by section.

pages.use: Winter edition first page — 3D oil-painting stage (the camera slips out between painting layers) · title inside a classical construction-line frame · contents move into a fixed left table of contents · per section a stage sentence / giant title / 3D device in a corridor · two or three cards on a torn-paper panel · dense feature list · News signup. For the first page of product news and release pages with many sections
Browse all releases — ten 3D album covers leaning on two wall shelves (lift on hover, come forward and flip on press) with a release list below. For past issues, seasons, albums and collection lists

An autumn edition issue — a pinned mesh graph (zooms toward a big node per section) · color bands that change per section · giant vertical edition names lying on their side · fixed-width number cells · feature cards in translucent panels · 4-column dot list. For a single release note with a data and network feel

Spring issue. On a dark backdrop, a particle stage changes shape at each section head into a light beam, a clump, a stepped pyramid and radial stems. The center column holds big statements, a video card, 3-column cards and a 3-column list, with a pinned section-name pill at bottom center. For a single dark-toned presentation or release.

notes: Post-processing: the original bloom(4.8), zoomBlur swipe transition and light-shaft volume are absent. The torn paper curtain between sections is drawn in the same place with our shader (noise tear above and below the cover + inner rim + shadow), and also extracted as the motion part torn-paper-band.

Sections: the original’s 12 sections (I~XII, about 250 features) were cut down to 7 by section type — stage sentence + video, two cards + flow panel + list, text card over stage + phone, stage sentence + three cards + dense list, 3D device in a corridor (three text sets), giant title + two cards, giant title + two-column list, developer bundle + code + newsletter signup

Rive graphics (flow panel, theme generation, chat window UI and other state-machine animations) are left as placeholders, and only the flow panel uses GSAP so the step cards float up at .3s intervals. The original sidekick-card click-to-open window (.8→1 .25s) and skill-tag bubble hover were not built.

Fonts: NeueMontreal (paid) → Inter Tight, Brand (paid) → Instrument Serif. Inter and Imperial Script are the same as the original. The original header and stage are pure white and pure black, so the skin’s --kf-contrast-ink and --kf-contrast-bg are set to #fff and #000 (made in oklch, color transitions would blend in Oklab and diverge from the original sRGB curve)
sites pull stopped at a long file name (ENAMETOOLONG) from an ad URL, so I unpacked and read the HAR directly in /tmp (long names shortened to a hash)

Font slot text (2026-11-08): since the original is all English, no title spots were left in Korean. Section names are Section 1–7 across the contents, giant titles, pills and hidden h2s, issue names are Issue 01–10 so they don’t wrap in the phone list cell (64px) (the autumn issue’s vertical text is also Issue 01), the hero title is The Sust·ai·nable Edition so that a script ai sits inside the word as in the original, and the legal notice is shortened to Terms·Privacy so the floating button doesn’t cover it in the phone footer. Header-line buttons (issue picker · search), card descriptions and list descriptions that use the body fonts (Inter·Pretendard) stay in Korean

title: Design team intro with dot-bloom titles, scroll-wound clock, and press-and-hold 3D flip
good_for: Design team or studio introductions with a work collection, a single-number statement, interview and article carousels, a locations list, and a 3D device mockup tool page.

pages.use: Team home page — big title blooming from dots, three-tier stone work cards (press for a modal) under the LIVE row, a clock winding over 600vh with 3D objects and declaration text around it, an interview and article carousel (press for an article modal), a city name row, and a 3D pill scroll indicator. Pressing and holding the screen flips it into a black 3D space.

3D device mockup editor — left control panel (upload screen image · fold angle · finish · scene · lighting · PNG export), right a foldable phone you can rotate plus three pose buttons. For product demos, mockup tools and settings screens

notes: The camera look-around uses the original values (mouse follow .15, approach 1/6, pan 500, pitch π/3, field of view 50→75) but replaces the original’s projection matrix blending (spreadT³) and upside-down flip (up 0,0,-1) with a simple tilt and pan.

Clock numerals use SVG instead of the original’s font outline paths <text> ’s stroke-dasharray(720) draws the outline — outline length differs per font, so the drawing speed is slightly different from the original. The needle is an SVG bar + axis (skin accent color gradient) in place of the original DOM needle graphic.
The original ticking sound (clock-tick·tock mp3) was not included.

AntiqueLegacy is paid, so Inter Tight 500 is used, and Pretendard for Korean. Big title sizes and line heights are the original values (Hero hero-fs · .7, elsewhere .85, city line min(160px,11.111vw) · phone 19vw/.9) — the .78~.82x reductions made for Korean placeholder text were removed when switching to English placeholder text.

Card videos and photos are all labeled placeholders (sd-ph). The original work card video (fetched when close, plays at 30% visible, poster fades out on loadeddata over .18s ease, pauses on long press) and autoplay of video inside the window are not built yet. Next step: make a same-ratio placeholder video and give it p0-style play rules.

The first loading tile intro was rebuilt with the numbers from the original rules (20 columns across, 3-cell blocks 15% · 2-cell blocks 45%, tiles pop in later the farther they are from the center: .55 + random .3 + big block .15, density fills up to .9 in the first half of progress and tiles drop out randomly in the second half, then after 1.1s a 2s cubic-out). The white and blue light at the end of the center tunnel is approximated with a radial glow in the composite shader instead of the original electric band pass.

Hide the title before it is split into words (the original also empties the text while loading) — if not hidden, the title showed during the first 200ms paint and then vanished, stretching the loader by 1.4s.

Sub-page entrance: with the original values as they are, over 2400ms the camera swings half a turn around the aim point (1-(1+8f)e^-8f), swelling +4.5% in distance and +.32 in height and then settling, while the canvas blur 72px · opacity .35 clears with smoothstep(.04~.96). Shaders are baked with compileAsync before starting, and the side panel slide-in (.48s expo) runs when inert is released at the end. As in the original, the empty screen is a switched-off black glass with a faint label (the inner screen must sit outside the body’s corner bevel .012 at z .014 to be visible). Going to view 2 hands angle and camera over as in the original and instantly switches to the fully opened pose, hiding the render-only rows (fold angle · export · pose buttons), and Back to start of view goes to the book pose in render mode. Fixed the 3D loop that grabbed a frame twice, from both the control change and the end reservation, which doubled calls during auto-rotate and drag damping and froze the screen. It now grabs once.

The declaration button (”Read more”) works like the original: it locks the 3D, opens, and 420ms later opens the declaration window on top. The 3D canvas goes to blur 10px and brightness .3 over .72s power3.out (enlarged by 30px on all sides), with 40vh dark gradients at top and bottom, and a 580px white-text column starting below 50vh of the screen (200~480px). Paragraphs float up when visible (15%) with opacity 1.8s, up 48px 1.2s and blur 4px .8s (expo), and the first group is staggered by 80ms each. Closing also releases the lock.

On phone (under 768) the work cards use the original code (ResizeObserver width <As the (768 → 2 columns) rule says, it is 2 columns. The original phone capture draws the layout WebGL first settled on as 3 columns, so it looks like 3, but the DOM rule was followed.

Typeface placeholder note (2026-11-08): the original is all English, so there are no Korean title placeholders. Big titles follow the original line and word counts (hero: The title / goes here. — with line height .7 the top line uses words with no descenders), city lines use common neighborhood names matching the original character counts (Midtown·Uptown·Old ▢ Town·Harbor·Bayside — the fourth is cut to six letters because Downtown is clipped at 19vw on phone), and carousel card data-modal goes into the article window’s big title as Article Title 01~09. Monospace labels (live, source, card underline, region, country, footer top line) and the intro sentence (sd-t5) are body-typeface slots, so they stay in Korean.

title: Season announcement where cards roll on a wheel and settle into a grid
good_for: Seasonal product or feature announcements and launch pages that present a collection of feature cards through scroll animation.

pages.use: Season announcement single page — navy wordmark → photo bento → scroll video → emblem zoom → card wheel and grid (picker) → partner accordion → closing form in a card rain, tap a card for a horizontal-swipe detail panel. For feature and product launch intros

notes: The hero’s 83-frame scroll video (webp bundle) is a placeholder drawn to a canvas per frame (a backlit window silhouette turns around while moving 12% closer) — it is tied to the same 83 cells and the same range (timeline 4.0~6.3), so just draw real frames instead of drawFrame.

The 8am mark and Showcase wordmark are our own abstract mark (68×54, drawn so the two zoom target points from the original sit in filled spots) and English placeholder. Original typeface PP Neue Montreal (paid) replaced with Inter Tight.

The loader’s card ring SVG is our own drawing of fourteen rounded rectangles arranged in a circle instead of the original art — the lighting order, 3.2s ring and .5s fold-away are the original values.

The icons on the fourteen cards are our line drawings, partner logos are outlined text placeholders, and product screens are labeled wf-img. Card colors rotate around the color wheel from the accent color to match the original OKLCH lightness and chroma.

The closing form doesn’t actually send, it only switches to a thank-you panel (the original sends via Brand). The original’s cookie consent bar and landscape phone rotate hint (rotate-gate) were left out.

On narrow screens the partners section uses only the integrations--pinned shape (transparent background) as in the original and is not pinned separately (the original has no pinning ScrollTrigger either).

Decision: at 834 width, pressing the original’s select button registers as the button’s own transform and color changing all at once, but the original code has no opening motion (it seems the element changed because React redrew the deck), so it was not copied — it remains as a non-blocking tablet touch-response line.

title: Old-house inn with fixed photos inside paper frames
good_for: Homepages for ryokan, traditional stays, old-house lodgings, and inns with restaurants, with room lists and booking entry.

pages.use: Lodging home page — a rounded photo panel in a paper frame sticks to the screen (4-slide fade) with vertical paragraphs flowing over it, then a news row, two room photo panels, meals, a staggered flowing experience photo band, a photo band that stands in the screen, access directions and a booking band. About — round-top hero photo, vertical title with a photo poking out at the edge, sticky text beside a hand-drawn alley map, row of local culture photos. For lodging and brand history About pages

Stay guide — a horizontal map image, per building a room-type cell (expands on hover) and facility shortcuts, for each room a photo slider, info table and booking button, plus facilities and a collapse. For room lists and product detail bundles
News list — round header photo, category on the left, rows of date · category · title (hover gray), page numbers. For notice and news lists

notes: Background: the original is a paper-grain picture (bg_v4.jpg, 375px repeat) and a screen frame wrapped in the same picture (.waku border-image) — instead of using the picture, a flat frame of one average color (--kf-bg) with the same thickness (2rem top · 4rem bottom) is used

Repeat trimming: lodging room detail 6 cells → 3 cells (same shape), intro photo slider one image per section

title: Manga label site that repaints each page in two swapped colors

Wordmark: the original Brand logo is hand-drawn pill-bar lettering (SVG path) and can’t be carried over, so the English placeholder text BRAND was drawn in Rubik Mono One and sliced into seven horizontal bands to redraw it (pill-row-wordmark, horizontal .72). Bar ends·letter shapes differ from the original, but the wobble (±.4rem every 1 second·.5s ease-in-out) and the signboard border (wine·teal·pink) are the same.

good_for: Brand or product landings built around one item, such as detergent, cosmetics or beverage bottles, especially with scent or flavor variants.

For a brand landing led by a single product
News list — left vertical outlined title and two-column photo cards, floating bead background. For brand news and press release lists

A single News post — white title panel overlapping a big hero photo, long body on a translucent panel (subheads, check lines, product photos, footnotes), outlined button back to the list. For new product press releases and notice posts

notes: Instead of the original model files (three GLB files, 4MB each), the 3D bottle was newly carved from our own surfaces of revolution (body · shoulder · neck · translucent cap · cap band) with a canvas-text label (LOGO/HERE + a strip of small text). Size and position match values measured on the original screen (1440 panel length about 707px · diameter 230px, model scale .28 · phone .18). The scene structure (outer group → fixed tilt −π/8·0·−π/9 → spin on its own axis 1.8rad/s·innerRx → orientation lay-down) and the camera (fov 30, z = screen height/2/tan15°/100), lighting (ambient 1, front directional light 15), and scroll values (blur 4px, z −15, rx −2π, x .5/−.75, rotation 6π, footer, smScale .65/1.8, bottle swap .75s power4.inOut) are exactly as in the original. The original model’s material is unknown, so the gloss was tuned by eye with a background-color reflection map (PMREM) at metalness .86 and roughness .27. Model details such as grooves on the cap and small label text are not included.

The blurred-bead background photo (3000×2250) in the hero and the five bead photos are treated as drawings, not photos, so they were redrawn as SVG beads (one · two joined · three joined, three blurs). Only the bottle cutout photo is a placeholder (1316:910)
The News card row (Embla) has only two cards in the original so it can’t be dragged, four are placed here so dragging can be seen

The FAQ usage table graphic (original SVG table) is an HTML table of the same size (67.8rem × 16rem), and the fragrance pyramid (TOP·MIDDLE·BOTTOM) and the three illustrations in the feature section (wave net, rings, seven-strand spider-web table) are newly drawn as our own line art in the same position and size

For the FAQ only the .3s height animation for opening and closing by clicking the summary row was carried over — the original handling that syncs state when the browser find feature opens details on its own (toggle event) was not built (next step for whoever continues: take the open state from toggle and call the same height animation). The original Contentful preview mode (live editing) is a product feature, so it was not built.

title: Office furniture maker with alternating photo and poster hero and draggable panels
good_for: Furniture and interior manufacturers and B2B companies with large catalogs, delivery cases, columns, company info, recruiting and custom-order pages.

pages.use: Company home — loader, Hero where large photo/poster pairs swap in staggered fashion every 2s, news line, drag-to-swipe horizontal panels of featured products·new products·cases (DRAG cursor), catalog·showroom half-and-half, three columns, contact strip. For a furniture/manufacturing company home
Product list — left panel to filter by type and condition + cutout cards in 3 columns (small view switches to 6 columns), pagination. For catalogs and shopping lists with many products

Custom order product detail — three order steps, a photo slider that cross-fades per picture tab (top) and text tab (legs), specs, color swatches, price table. For product details where you pick options and order
Delivery case list — two-column large photo cards divided by lines, with names and pagination. For construction and delivery record lists
Column list — 3-column cards split by lines (photo, title, subtitle, author, date), pagination. For blog, column and news lists
About — two-column heading, full-bleed cover, overview table, HQ and branch photos with addresses, vertical-line history (diamond dots · photos). For company overview and history pages
Careers — full-bleed video and job list (the hovered row’s photo lights up beside it). For short recruiting pages

notes: Font: the original Neue Haas Grotesk Display (paid) is replaced by the closest free font, Inter Tight, and the Japanese gothic font slot by Noto Sans KR. The logo image is wide-spaced English placeholder letters BRANDNAME.

DRAG cursor: the original CSS wrote a transition that bounces from .5→1x, but the script overrides transform with an inline translate, so in reality only the opacity changes over .15s — this measured behavior was followed (the .92x press survives because of !important).

Product list: the original’s bulk download mode for drawings·photos (card checkboxes·pick 2D/3D/photo·confirm window) was left out, with only the button spot kept. The search field’s two-way pinning (20px from the bottom when scrolling down, 20px below the bar when scrolling up) maps the original’s three states fixed/fixed-top/absolute into a single translateY. On phones, the filter search is a panel that expands downward instead of the original panel

Detail (size-matching table): all 6 top and 8 leg slots are kept, but the value table and fit table have fewer rows (value table 5 rows, the original has more and two tables). Step graphics, top cross-section and leg photos are placeholders.
Case and column lists have fewer cards than the original (16 · 18), now 8 · 9. The company history keeps only 8 of the 16 years.

Recruiting: the original has only one recruiting-site band in the job-type rows and an empty right photo slot — to show the form the original CSS and script accept (tag, two lines, ↗, photo lights up on the hovered row), two job-type rows and three photos were added.
The search field only opens and closes and does not search. Favorites (favorites.min.js), the cookie notice bar and reCAPTCHA are left out.

Some box sizes in the phone About and Detail pages do not carry over all the original phone rules but are scaled in vw from the 1440 ratio (header · first page · list · card · contact · footer use the original phone values).

Time: exceeded the 180-minute cap (about 235 min). The last detailed interaction and phone comparison pass took nearly an hour because the original detail page was slow, and during that phone comparison I found and fixed a closed drawer that enlarged the header bar to 574px and covered the hero. After the fix, only the first page (including drawer open) and the detail page were re-shot on the phone — the phone comparison for the other pages was not rerun.

title: Hilltop wedding venue where a small sky window opens to full screen
good_for: Wedding venues, resorts, scenic restaurants and hotel banquet sites showcasing views, space types, event and plan cards, galleries and news.

pages.use: First page — sky curtain loader (on first visit a tree logo grows over a sky video, then the curtain lifts at 3.2s). Under a sky-blue English wordmark, a small vertical window opens on all four sides over 400lvh into a full-screen chapel photo (sky video inside the window). Recent news line and notice strip, big left label | three flag-style date cards, vertical-writing titles + two large photo blocks, three-branch English cards over a photo, sky photo window opening, Story|People two columns, flag-style plan cards with head count and price, dark panels descending and overlapping (photo service·banquet|cafe), Access|Contact, dark footer with photo pillars rising and falling and a flowing logo band. For a wedding venue or resort Hero where the view is the pride

About (original concept): a full-screen photo cover with a big white English title rising from below, a three-chapter contents box with photos attached, a section cover for each chapter (a photo window widens from 3rem inside to the edges + a big serif heading), blocks of vertical title + large photo + small photo alternating left and right, a gray panel symbol story, and gray panel three-way cards. For telling a day’s flow or a brand philosophy in sections.

Photo album: a dark big English title, a big photo (right), a small photo and an About cover. On the left, each 102rem section has a 3:2 cover photo plus a continuously flowing thumbnail strip (speed · direction follow the mouse). On the right is a fixed index. Clicking a thumbnail opens a full white-screen big-photo window (number · page dots · left/right half-screen navigation). For showing photos grouped by scene.

News list: dark ink large English title cover (big photo at left), left column with title · ALL button · archive accordion | right a strip where two picked posts slide every 5s (a circle draws on the page dot), one-line post list with photos, page numbers. For blog and notice lists

notes: The original English typeface linotype-didot is paid, so it was swapped for GFS Didot, and the body font source-han-serif-japanese for Noto Serif KR 500, the Korean version of the same family. The logo (a wordmark of a growing tree) and the Hero English wordmark are redrawn as SVG and text placeholders instead of the original image files (logo / PLACE NAME WEDDING)

Of the four recorded subpages, number 4 (blog/date/2026) has the same type as number 3, the news list (only the year filter differs), so it is built as one news.html. For number 1, Concept, only three same-type blocks (left · right · left) of the seven scene blocks and three section covers are built, of the six photo gallery pictures, only four
Event·product·news cards are lists the original fills from a server, so they are static cards. The page numbers and archive-year links in News are #

Menu pages that were not captured (Ceremony, Banquet Hall, Dishes, Event Records, People, Events, Products, Benefits, FAQ, Notices) link to #, and Contact links to the footer contact anchor. The two external links are shape only
The first-visit loader runs only once using sessionStorage instead of the original cookie. As in the original, the veil lifts after fonts, document ready, 1.5s and sky video playable are all done
Black-and-white map photo slot instead of an embedded map

title: Designer portfolio with floating metal blobs and horizontal flow on a vertical wheel
good_for: Individual or product designer portfolios with a statement hero, horizontally flowing thoughts, a pinned work list, plus about, case detail and contact pages.

pages.use: First page of a horizontally flowing portfolio — a hero with a statement sentence where the vertical wheel becomes horizontal movement, plus metal drops, a growing vertical photo, a filling quote, a pinned work handoff (phone screen swap), and contact. For a product designer’s personal site
Self-introduction — four photos of varying heights, inverted intro, career timeline, results, email marquee. For designer self-introductions
Single work detail — metal-drop title header, problem, solution sentence, step-by-step screens, results, next work. For app and product design case details
Contact — info bar and big title on one screen. For reaching a personal portfolio

notes: The blob board is rewritten with our shader on the same three build, using the formulas of the original three r182 board (four blobs plus one cursor joined with smin .25, wave 4.2·phone 2 / speed 2.8, accent blob center→edge .58x·soft blob one color, drift·wall bounce .2·cursor push .1·blob-to-blob .05·follow .05, entrance 1.6s sine.inOut·opacity 1.6s sine.out·physics strength .15→1 2.2s). Blob positions and color assignments are random on every open, as in the original. The original draws everything on one board (shared scene), but here there is one canvas per cell, so the original’s 'clip-overlap'(drops spilling over into the neighboring cell) is clipped inside the cell.

The photo panel is built after the original media shader (noise wobble at .25 around the cursor and red/blue split .005, strength .15, settling after 300ms of stillness · six blobs attach at .15 intervals over 2s power3.out as the opening entrance, once when entering within 15% of the edge), but it is applied only to the first-page four and the About one among the photos where the original applies this shader (places where the original also applies an entrance). The four About header photos are built as photo panels (data-media) with only cursor wobble and no entrance, like the original (2026-11-11 cursor backfill, 6 WebGL panels on the About page). Original Work detail·Contact have no photo panels (data-webgl-media 0). Photos use a placeholder image (background·diagonal·label) as the texture.

In the original, html blocks scrolling and an inner box (.app) scrolls with Lenis (1.3.23). Here it was changed to window scroll + the same Lenis build. Horizontal strip values (start center center, length = Strip overflow + screen height, moves for the first W/(W+H) then stops) are the same.
Fonts: residenz (paid) → Inter Tight 500, italic instrument → the same free font Instrument Serif. Korean titles use Pretendard, so strokes are heavier than the original.

The symbol (S monogram graphic at top left) is a placeholder that draws the first letter of the center word in bold Inter Tight 800 (currently ”M”) — the logo melt bakes a distance field between this letter and the first letter of the center word on canvas. The original S is a hand-refined glyph, so its stroke ends are rougher. The logo shown is the wf-logo box

Work detail keeps every section type of the original long page (hero, problem, one-sentence solution, how it works, three-phone steps, results, next work), but the step videos and result figures are placeholders. The five other work detail pages of the same type were not built (all drawer links go to works.html). The three work-header bubble colors (#c9cfd7·#8e8c97·#7e849b) are that work’s content colors, so they live in works.css 'Not Skin'was set as.

The work list’s soft glow is built from the original mesh gradient shader formula (three color points, wave .8·swirl .1, inverse mix of distance^3.5, color follow .05, light mode saturation ×.8·brightness +.1·white .12). Each work’s three colors were picked from original captures, so they live in index.js 'Not Skin'Set to (work content color).

The original first page and subpages scroll inside an inner box, so on the original side of shot and compare only the hero is captured — the layout of the lower sections was matched to the original HTML classes (spacing · text steps), and the horizontal band · work list · bottom CTA were checked against temporary captures made by rolling the mouse wheel directly.

The loader uses original values — progress 5s power1.inOut, when it ends the line folds .55s power2.inOut · number .4s · curtain lifts .7s after .35s, the logo settles to the header spot in 2s power3.inOut and the body appears at 1.2s. As in the original, the header logo itself rises over the curtain and sticks to the vertical center of the screen (pinLogoToViewportCenter), the three name lines enter .2s later sliding x -30→0 in .8s (.18 stagger, power2.out), stay .7s, then the 1.9s ‹symbol → name› morph timeline is rewound at 2.6s to become the symbol. As in the original, the morph is a shader that blends two glyph distance fields (SB.logo · part sdf-glyph-morph) — instead of the original distance field images, the symbol glyph and the first letter of the center word are drawn on a canvas and baked with EDT (height 384, spread .1 of the height, edge .5; ...the last-character baseline is measured from the DOM text range and overlaps the name line). The original curtain is server-rendered and covers the page from the first paint, so a one-line script in each page head adds html.sb-loading, which covers even the first paint, before the script raises the curtain, in the background color.

The original follower is moved to SB.follow. In Contact only the 50rem cell at the lower right of the name is a mail link, and in that cell a pill follows at .55s power3 while the arrow cell opens. The About mail marquee runs two groups of ‹⁑ text →› at 35s, and when the pointer is within the band height the mail pill follows at .55s (proximity). On the Work detail ‹Next work›, a gradient preview card in the work’s color (20rem, 444:944) follows the link hover at 1.25s power3. The ‹Work› drawer uses the original values (.6s power2.out · pill .86→1 .38s · tail .08 · panel .16 · text .4/.61/.07 · 1.5x rewind, mouse devices open and close by hover only). Pill button height is the original arrow cell width (height×.84=Matched to 40.79px). The original header logo (HeaderLogo·AnimatedLogo) has no hover handler — the name unfolding is an automatic cycle (SB.logo).

Header logo auto cycle built to the original values (SB.logo, bundle Vl): noise of stickiness 1.14 · distortion .05 · melt .2 sweeps over the symbol along the diagonal: in 6s, hold .1s, out 6s, overlap -2s (10.1s per cycle, edge .14). After two cycles it goes name (1.9s) → 2s hold → symbol (1.9s rewind) → sweep restarts from the beginning. As in the original, the sweep clock runs during the loader too, and the cycle continues from that spot when the loader ends. From the second page in the same window it stands as the symbol with no loader and runs from clock 0 (the original is a single-page app, so the clock continues across navigation). Panel pixel ratio is 1 as in the original. Text color is --kf-ink, and changes in .3s power3.out when the skin changes.

Type backfill: the original text is entirely Latin (residenz, instrument), so there is nothing to keep in Korean. The 31 Instrument Serif italic spots (section labels, city lines, group titles, credit links, italic words inside sentences) were replaced with English placeholder text. Large sentences containing italic words (hero quote, intro line, thoughts text, uppercase quote, two inspiration texts, achievements line, one-sentence summary of what we made, title line) were switched entirely to English so Korean and English never mix within one sentence. Big names set in the same Inter Tight (t-lg2 name, work title, next work, three contact name lines, three loader name lines), the header menu (About, Projects, Contact, work list Project Name 01~06), the light switch, and the marquee Get in touch were also changed to English. Body paragraphs without italics, small captions, button pills (See About, Let’s talk) and info labels (Product, Year, Role) stay in Korean, since Pretendard pairs well with the same grotesque texture.

title: Household product page linked by gradient pill bands and apricot circles
good_for: Brand landing pages for a single household, medical or cosmetic product covering features, usage, FAQ, retailers and contact on one page.

pages.use: One-page landing for a single product — a gradient pill band that stands up during loading, a pill-window Hero, intro / three features / map where a pinned circle graphic changes, product and store pins where the circle grows, application-spot and how-to-use card pins where the circle opens, Q&A accordion, two companies, contact form and purchase banner. For introducing household goods and medical devices.

notes: The original is a single page (pages: [] in pages.json), so there are no subpages.

The original typefaces (a Japanese gothic from a type foundry and Futura PT) are paid (Typekit), so Korean uses Gothic A1 and English uses Jost, which has a Futura feel — the letter-spacing of the large sentence (12px) is the same but the glyph widths differ, so line lengths differ slightly.

Spots where the original speaks through images (patch cross-section diagram · world map · five feature droplets · attachment-spot line drawing · four-step hand-drawn usage guide · product sheets) were redrawn with SVG · CSS. The map reduces continents to thin line clusters and the pin spots are ”Region 1~5” — redrawing at the same density without copying the original map would require new continent outlines, so it was left as is.

The product section lifestyle photos use the same board as the original’s three large composite images (4652:2684 landscape, collections of photos cut into pills and circles): centered, 167vh tall, low windows 2326×1342 and 2746×1585, phone 200vw, 912px and 812px — with pill and circle placeholders scattered inside at the same proportional positions. Pill positions were measured from a 1440×900 screenshot.

The original contact field is an iframe from a third-party form service with a captcha, so it is rebuilt as a non-submitting form with the same fields, and the security check widget is left as a placeholder.

The original bundle contains the string ScrollSmoother, but it actually uses only Lenis 1.3.25 + ScrollTrigger — the copy uses the same two versions. The original Lenis option smoothTouch is not a name in 1.3.25, so touch is not smoothed (same in the copy).
Because the card was auto, I looked at the sites show printout and the original code and filled in name · kind · layout seven axes · motion.items · signatures (kind is hospital · clinic → product).

Index: three seller spots (sellers 1·2·4, the same three in the menu drawer, the product seller pills and the footer menu). The original uses Japanese store names (official online store, marketplace, shopping site), so they stay Korean. The third name mixes Latin and kana, but it is mostly kana, so it stays Korean. Only the third (a big online marketplace in the original) was changed to Store 3. The Korean pair Gothic A1 was added to the title font stack (--kf-font-display) so Korean after Jost is drawn in the same gothic as the body

The big two-line sentence (s-catch) in the menu drawer and footer — the original is a Japanese sentence (With body and daily life, …) and is kept in Korean here. The body is set in Gothic A1, so the grain matches the original print-company gothic

title: Design studio portfolio with giant single letters and a flame photo strip
good_for: Design studio or solo creative portfolios with a work list, principles, specialties and project detail pages.

pages.use: Design studio home page — 3D hero with a year wordmark resting on the floor · featured work · About with black-and-white video · full-screen-height single letters · name scattering to the four corners · fire photo sales band (date · coordinates). For solo or small creative portfolio homes
Work list — flame photo header and scattered work tiles of varied size and position. For portfolio lists
Studio About — four single characters, portrait photo header, story, principles header, stacked overlapping photo panels, big numbers. For studio principles About
Specialties — dark stage photo header · sticky field tabs · per-field blocks · scattering names. For service area intro
Single work detail — full-bleed photo hero and bold title · a photo collection in several types (centered · full-bleed · two-up · small four). For branding case detail

notes: Fonts: Helvetica Now Display, PP Editorial New and Brand Mono are paid, so they were replaced with Inter Tight (plus Pretendard for Hangul), Instrument Serif and IBM Plex Mono.

Sales band 3D is re-hung with the original values (three r171, camera FOV 10° (−8,−3,15)→origin, scene x .1, ACES·exposure 1·PCFSoft shadows, canvas window width × 16:9/1:1/9:16 attached at −4% below the band, device size .6/.5, rotation −.6 + progress×60°·height −.2 + progress×.6, disc −.005/frame + scroll speed×−.005, orange point light intensity 50·distance 3.5·decay 3.6 (−2,−1.3,2)→(−.5,−.5), metal #EBEFF4·metalness .85·roughness .2·reflection .1→3, black glass transmission 1·refraction 1.3, screen video ×200 as light). The model (GLB·Draco) and the HDR alley reflection are original files so they are not used — we built a rounded-box device and a reflection room of three bright panels, so the silhouette and reflection pattern differ. The original’s OrbitControls (damping) is left out because the canvas takes no input (pointer-events none), so it produces no visible motion

The Hero is a single photo like the original (one dark device render) — the old 3D hero isn’t in the original, so it was removed and replaced with a photo slot plus the original Gu pixel dissolve (width 160→300→400→600→1000 every .1s, .5s after a first visit · 0s on a carried-over page), a 1.05→1 settle and 10% parallax. The photo slot draws the same shapes (faces, diagonals, label) on a canvas and enlarges it at each step. The per-cell dissolve applied to the other photos isn’t in the original, so it was dropped (the original dissolves only the first photo on each page)

Smooth scroll is Lenis 1.1.6 same as the original (1.2s, exponential ease-out, touch ×1.5). Text rise-in, as in the original, splits into words and letters only above 1024 width, firing when the center touches the bottom of the screen, letter scramble uses ”+?84564XERSHKZN” at speed .5 for 1.5s (scroll text also fades opacity 0→1), on hover a Work card’s label scrambles after .5s and reappears

Video slots (first-page recent work · featured work · case, work list slots 1·2·4, first About case card, detail laptop mockup · half-width slot) are placeholder videos that autoplay, loop and stay muted, like the original (media/*.mp4, same ratio and length as the original: 10s 1156:720 · 12.5s 16:9 · 5.5s 16:9 · 5.4s 16:9 · 11s 1080:1364 · 21.7s 1154:720). The third video on the first page, the second and third on the work list, and the third on the detail page have no file in the archive, so they follow the length of another video on the same page. The detail page’s third video (full-width mockup) is left out because the copy has no such slot.
The work list tile placement is an approximation of the original /work moved onto a 12-column grid, and the original’s per-tile parallax speeds (IX2) could not be carried over
Images in the work detail such as brand graphics, T-shirts and newspaper collages are all left as photo slot labels only
On phone, as in the original, menu links stack vertically in the center with no hamburger (the original .mob-nav is off at this width)
Work detail subpages follow the shape of the one recorded page (test-project-2). Every work list card links to this detail.html
sites pull stalled at the /work response (the file name work and the folder work collide), so for subpages the original was read by unpacking the archived pages.har.zip directly

Typeface placeholder text: the original is entirely in English (Helvetica Now Display, PP Editorial New). The body font is also Inter Tight, so latin-slots catches only serif, h2 and h3. After checking screenshots, every spot where the original uses the heading typeface at large size was switched to English: wordmarks (SN.CO, SN’00, Footer SN . CO), giant single letters, the four corner names (Na, me, He, re), large headings (five About lines, two sales-band lines, section names, principles, fields, detail titles), the city band, menu, tabs, name lines (case, work, awarding body, field), buttons, serif lines, and mail and account text

Body and description sentences (body-copy, one-line field descriptions, the principle panel ”One-line pledge here.”), small mono labels (header label, category, city, footer pledge, channel name), and list details (award names, detail items) — the original is English, but Korean is kept per the README ”body and description sentences are Korean”. Pretendard is paired after the body fonts Inter Tight and IBM Plex Mono

title: Digital organization intro with a sinking building photo and two sidenote columns
good_for: Digital or DX units inside large companies, research labs, in-house ventures and innovation departments needing recruiting branding.

pages.use: Organization home page — below a large English wordmark a full-bleed building photo settles from 1.2x and lands late on scroll, a latest-news card in the corner, large thin intro text, a full-bleed photo, two people photos (parallax), a work and voices carousel (one slot every 3 seconds), two groups of team blog posts, a notice line, a recruiting band.

About the organization — large English title, five intro lines, section shortcuts, full-bleed photo, left sticky table of contents + section name column + 794px body (overview figure, structure figure with eight numbered functions and icons, activity area figure overflowing to the right, two sites, history bar), vision band
Notice list — year · category filter on the left, date + title row with arrow on the right, ”More”. Slot for press · event notice lists
Work list — tag filter on the left, on the right a photo (4:3) + eight rows of title · description · tags, and a recruiting band. For service and project work slots

Careers — big title and intro, full-bleed photo, pinned table of contents + five strengths (text and photos staggered), full-bleed photo, vision, mission and six values, two groups of benefits, open FAQ (hiring flow diagram), job rows by category

One notice — small section name, large title, post date, 1000px cover, 600px body offset to the right (announcement title, presenter card), and other notice rows. For press release and event announcement posts (original subpages 5 and 6 are the same post, so one section).

notes: The original is a site built with Studio, so its appear (.appear), scroll parallax (animation-timeline: view()) and carousel (sd-carousel) live in the Studio runtime — we didn’t use the runtime code and rewrote them as parts with the same values (studio-appear · view-range-shift · step-carousel)

The original org chart, structure diagram, activity map and history bars are image files. They were redrawn as SVG graphics at the same position and size (gray panels, white cells, accent bands, bars) with placeholder content.
The logo (group mark + English) and wordmark are images — placed at the same size as an SVG of a rounded accent-color mark + Be Vietnam Pro text

Hiragino Kaku Gothic (paid) was replaced by Noto Sans KR, with the original W3 and W6 mapped to 400 and 600. Most original text is Be Vietnam Pro 300, so Korean falls back to Noto Sans KR 400 (there is no 300 weight for Korean)
Language switch (JP/EN) is only a placeholder — other language versions were not built
Voices in the original header menu has no recorded subpage, so it links to a single notice (article.html)

The full-bleed photo band between careers sections is sized to the original height (about 948px). The original content in that spot (photo, spacing) could not be confirmed from the recording, so it is left as a photo slot

title: Product site flowing like one song: intro, feature pages and documents
good_for: Sites for feature-rich own products or apps, with steps, demo, pricing and questions on the home page, feature detail pages and long legal documents.

pages.use: One-song product intro — a gauge showing scroll as measures·time, bouncing wordmark, pinned version steps, feature pads that demo on press, phone view switch, strikethrough declaration, 4-tier pricing, filtering FAQ, and bouncing, stacking file chips. For a landing page of a feature-rich in-house app
Single feature detail — glow-title hero, version tree, A/B comparison, three-step cards, glow-halo call to action and more links. For per-feature product sub-pages
Long document — type chip, last-updated header, sticky table of contents with read progress, section list. For terms, refund and privacy documents

notes: The original has two feature detail pages (versions, comments) with the same frame, so, following the README note ”Details of the same shape are built one at a time”, only service.html (versions) was built. The demo panel that exists only on the comments page (track name row + COMMENT MODE table + waveform with a painted range + comment rows with bar and time, floating up from 20px below on entry) is missing. It can be assembled in the same spot (version-tree) from the wave-bars and cue-hover parts with fade-up.
Document pages share the same shape for terms, privacy and refunds in the original, so just one page.html

The original uses Next client transitions, so there is no loader or page-transition effect — only the title fading in from faint to sharp (0.42s) on entry and the cookie bar rising up were carried over, pages are linked with ordinary links
No photo slots — the original speaks only through product screens (waveform, pads, phone), so everything was redrawn in HTML · CSS

title: Endless polaroid wall in pastel fog, explored by wheel and drag
good_for: Pet, kids or travel photo albums and photographer portfolio landing pages showing dozens to hundreds of photos on one screen.

pages.use: Endless polaroid photo wall — photos floating by wheel and drag (click to enlarge to center) · corner UI · numeric title · footprint loader. For pet or travel photo albums, or when showing dozens of photos on one screen

notes: The original is a single page (pages: [] in pages.json), so there are no subpages.

All photos are gray placeholder textures with labels (what the photo is · light · ratio). The original photos are mostly vertical phone shots, so many 3:4 and 9:16 slots are used. For that reason the wall looks paler and flatter than the original with photos in it — real photos will bring back the original density. Color grading (warmth .05 → brightness 1.04 → contrast 1 → saturation .94, hover 1.06×) is applied in the photo shader with the original settings.

The grid was ported from the original makeGrid (board = 1.4x screen width, 6 columns (phone 3), cell height 1.1x, photo width .5~.7 of the cell, jitter .5, overlap relaxation 120 steps with margin .15, two sets of panels laid out offset by half a panel, with .382 vertical offset every horizontal lap, edge and depth fade). Three depth layers ±1.2 is how the original depthPattern was read.

Depth of field is redrawn in our own shader because the original uses DepthOfFieldEffect from postprocessing (Zlib license, so it can’t be used). Original settings (focus z 1.68 = Layer gap 1.2 × (2 × DOF_FOCUS 1.2 − 1), focus distance 3, bokeh 2.4, and on zoomed screens focus is 3.2 in front of the camera) are used, the blur circle is smoothstep(0, 3, |distance − focus|), gathering a 32-point golden-angle disc at radius bokeh×8px. The original’s separate front·back blur bake step and bokeh shape differ. For the original hoverFocus (focus shifting to the hovered photo) I couldn’t find its enable condition in the bundle, so focus stays at 1.68. The original also turns off the shadow map (SHADOW_MAP_ENABLED false) — the shadow plate behind the photo (.2) is the same.

Background noise: the original shader (Solar Flare preset, cosine palette formula) is site code, so it was not carried over. Instead it is drawn with our own fbm using the same two colors (BG_NOISE_LOW pale sky blue · HIGH white) plus a pale violet bleeding toward the end color. Like the original, it updates only 20 times per second (BG_UPDATE_FPS 20). The original’s half-resolution (BG_RESOLUTION_SCALE .5) render is not done. The next person can draw the background alone to a half-size target and upload it. The zoomed-screen background (SLIDE_BG_NOISE #ffe5e5↔white) is mixed in the same shader.

Zoomed view passes raw values — target of one wheel tick advance += deltaY×.006, inertia .93, once more than 400ms have passed since release and it is slowing, it snaps to the nearest section by (1−.01^dt), the actual position follows by (1−.0008^dt), during a page turn it shrinks to .92× and stops, then after 200ms returns by (1−.02^dt). The original’s video photos (preview mix 160ms after hover, play 200ms after enlarge) were not built — turning some of the placeholders into same-ratio placeholder videos (VideoTexture) and blending them with uMix is left for the next person.

The 3D star in the middle of the title (star.glb) and the glass icon in the middle of the badge (instagram.glb) cannot use the model files, so we sculpted our own shapes in three (a four-point star extruded thick, a rounded square plate with camera-shaped lines). The material is our own glass shader, using the original icon glass settings (rim 2.5, shine 50, transparency .6→.5, shine strength 1.45, rainbow .4). The motion follows the original formulas exactly: star x .12·sin(.7t), y .8t, z .05·sin(.5t), height .03·sin(1.1t), and pressing spins 4π in 1.1s power3.out. The icon rotates on the y axis at .5rad/s, and hovering the badge makes it 2.2rad/s (1−.01^dt). The badge text ring turns at 20°/s normally and 60°/s on hover (1−e^(−3.5dt)), radius 37, title typeface weight 12.

Six rising glass bubbles from the original were newly added (original values: a band 1.6 times the screen height at .045 screens per second, sideways sway .6rad/s with 5% width, the first two in front of the photo, size screen height ×.075×(.6~1.3), appearing over 1.4s after a .5s entrance delay, popping in .2s when pressed and growing back over 1.2s after .8s). The bubble glass uses the original bubble settings (rim 3.3, sparkle 60, opacity 0→.55, rainbow .85).

The loader is built the way the original is. Eight photo cards (hashed positions, ±29px, ±23px, ±8.5°) drop in at .24s intervals from 28px above at .94 scale (.75s cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.25,1)). The date counts up from the birthday to today over 2.3s with 1−(1−s)³. Paw prints are laid every 58px along a random quadratic curve (400 segments) from outside the panel to outside the panel, alternating left and right by 11px, skipping the card and date areas (±16px). At 2.9s the content fades out over .45s, and .3s later the opening hole expands over 1.2s. The paw shape is a newly drawn paw (pad plus four toes) instead of the original paw.svg, and the card photos are placeholders.

Pinch zoom (two fingers · Ctrl+wheel to move in depth, original PINCH_SPEED .006 · PINCH_WHEEL_SPEED .008, inertia .92) was not built — the next person can add z (target · velocity) to input and subtract it from camera z. The wheel moves by deltaY×.0042 regardless of screen size, as in the original. Following the original rule, the scroll bar is visible only while zoomed in, while dragging, and within 800ms after motion stops (.5s). Dragging moves the grid to that vertical position and the zoomed view to that index’s photo. [ Back ] accepts input even when closed, as in the original, and on hover its letter spacing widens .08→.12em.

On the record page, the night bar is painted in just two segments (navy and gold) as in the original, not split into per-play segments (white gaps) within one night.

Font placeholder text (2026-11-08): since the original is entirely in English, every spot using the heading font (a display serif) and the wordmark font (a wordmark serif) became English placeholder text — large title, featured section title, play names, stat card big values, dates (00 Mon 0000), categories, working method, paragraph inside the frame, large made-at paragraph, menu, spot cards, footer title, contact button. Remaining mismatches (unrelated to text wrapping, left untouched): in the record section at phone width (390) the paging row (← New night · 01 02 … · ‹See past nights here →›) overflows by 46px and causes horizontal scroll.
