title: Restaurant intro with unrolling hanging scroll and ink-line paintings
good_for: Restaurant and traditional shop homepages, brand landings opening with a scroll story, and sites with menus and store info.

pages.use: Shop first page — a rolled scroll bounces down and settles, unrolls with scrolling and grows past the screen, then storm clouds part and an ink-line picture scroll flowing right to left (vertical-text copy · dishes · artisans) follows, after passing a cloud curtain it moves on to a video hero · about · two-column menu · fade slider with horizontal-flow gallery · SNS marquee · black news band · two store locations. For a storytelling restaurant landing page
News list — centered vertical title, one-line list of date, title and diamond arrow, circle page numbers. For shop notice and news lists

Single news item — black category tag, date, bold heading, short gold underline, business information body, pill-shaped back button. For store opening and business notices (two recorded posts share the same form, so merged into one)

notes: Clouds were redrawn in an auspicious-cloud shape layering round lumps and swirls with a seeded random — the original cloud image (fine brush grain, wave bundles) is original artwork so it was not used, and the grain is less dense by that much

For the hanging-scroll roller sprite, instead of the original art we used an 8-frame SVG with a bright grain moving across, with the same steps(7). For the two smoke wisps when the roller lands, we drew new ink smoke at the original kemuri position and keyframes (.8s ease, .24s late, ±15·−20px)

The phone opening switches to one screen where steps 1~6 are on for 2H and rest for 1H, as in the original, but the per-step artwork is kept simple for the same reason as the illustrations above. The phone hero’s big brush-script logo screen (lettering image in the original) is replaced by a video hero
The cloud mask (hero boundary) shares the nine-blob spots of cloud_mask instead of the original hero_mask image, and the exit distance is calculated so it leaves the screen completely

The gallery slider is the same Swiper 11.2.10 with the same options as the original (fade · loop · speed 1200 · autoplay 5000 · clickable pagination) and the pagination look (vertical number circles at top right · current slide light fill · line stretching in 1.2s) also follows the original CSS values

Lenis runs at 1.1.9, the same as the original, and like the original only on PC. It switches on 2.7s after window load (2.2s if the URL has a #hash) with lerp 1, duration 1.2 and easeOutQuart, and is driven by its own rAF. With lerp 1 the original has no inertia either. The menu fade uses WAAPI with the same curve as the original jQuery fadeIn/Out 400ms swing (cubic-bezier(.37,0,.63,1)), so jQuery is not loaded just for this one line.
The news list page numbers are hidden in the original because there are only three posts, but they are kept for when it is reused
The article page’s share button is not visible on the original screen, so it was removed. The store map is a map embed placeholder
Logo and signage lettering (brush-script wordmark, mark, badge) are original artwork, so a roof + circle emblem placeholder mark and vertical 'Your business name here' was used instead
The handwritten SCROLL and SKIP images (original picture text) are replaced with slanted Kaisei Decol text (--kf-font-hand)

Skin: the handmade-paper grain speckle is a faint black-noise SVG instead of the original paper photo, so it follows the background color (--kf-bg) and a slightly darker grain shows through in any skin. Ink-line drawings, diamonds and the menu keep their SVG fills as --kf-* and --site-* (var() does not work in SVG attributes, so TNM.paint moves them to style), and the black band and menu use --kf-contrast-bg and ink

title: AI office product intro with a talking mascot
good_for: Collaboration and AI product landings, character-led service intros, and product sites with pricing, FAQ and blog.

pages.use: Product home page — a title where greeting speech bubbles pop up, an office app window where bubbles are typed out, a grid of 100 AIs, three fixed steps, a wiki app, tool cards, an auto-advancing security card strip, a WebGL globe, three pricing cards (with a Coming soon band), a box-style FAQ, and a mascot CTA lining up in a queue. For SaaS landing pages with characters

About the company — big slab title with cutout illustration, mission·photo, four promises with spinning Lottie rings, achievement strip with rolling number cells, history with a vertical year line. For company and team story sections
Blog list — grid of 1200:630 cover cards with slab titles and type chips (Story · New · Press). For News and blog lists
A single blog post: back button, chips, title, author row, share buttons, cover, 720px body (subheadings, photos), author card, and three related posts. For event report and news detail pages
Contact — slab title and a six-field form (input · select · text box) · send. For sales inquiry and consultation request sections

notes: The card’s tech field (lenis·three) was based on the old version — the 2026-10-29 archive and the current original are the new version (Next.js, no lenis·three, only the About section uses lottie-web 5.13.0), so I built it on the new version. The card has been updated to the new version too.

Mascot art: the original’s 3D-rendered hexagon character art (teras.webp sprite · prop SVGs) is not used. It was redrawn in SVG at the same position, size and five colors as a rounded hexagon body + tilted eyes + side shading. The props (hat · cap · balloon · leaf) are also simple new drawings
The three Office-stage panels (view, record, organize) reduce the original app screen choreography (camera pan, writing, tags) to gray boxes and drawn lines

Of the original 26 blog pages, only the 12 of the same form were kept. The pre-1.0 migration guide page and the download page were not recorded so were not built, and their menu items link to article · contact
About mission, three lines — original titles are in kana, Korean kept
About pledge lead sentence — the original is a kana title, Korean kept
About promises, four lines — original titles are in kana, Korean kept
about history title — the original uses kana for the title (History above stays in English), Korean kept
About history: four section titles — the original uses kana titles, Hangul kept
article other-post card, three titles — the original uses kana titles (only the leading [Why I Joined …] head is English), Hangul kept
Contact big title — original is a kana title, Korean kept
The three header feature names (original English product names) sit in body Gothic rather than the title typeface, so they are kept in Korean

title: App intro site with yellow speech-bubble character and flowing logo band
good_for: Mobile app and community service intros with a download hero, three features, placement results, article list and detail, FAQ and business advertising info.

pages.use: App intro home page — a phone screen collage hero, a vertical-writing title intro box, a flowing logo band, three features with phone slides over a cluster of three circles, a scrolling list of publication results, reading cards, a yellow-pattern product plate, an FAQ, and green and orange guide cards. For mobile app and community service landings.
Reading (blog) list — Swiper band of featured posts on a yellow slanted panel, category picker, three-column post cards, pagination. For service blog and news lists

Single article — date, tag and title in a white rounded box, share button row, rounded image, subheading paragraphs, related list, back-to-list button. For blog article details such as award news or columns
FAQ — logomark bracket title, question rows in three categories inside a white box (they slide open in 400ms). For app and service FAQ pages
Advertising·partnership info — narrow 860px column with a yellow-underlined title · monitor mockup · two hand drawings · square-tag Q&A. For corporate ad placement and sponsorship recruitment notices

notes: AOS 2.3.1 and Swiper 11.2.10 are loaded from _vendor, same as the original, and the settings carry over unchanged (offset 200 · 500ms · ease-out-cubic · once, per-section data-aos-offset/easing, Swiper autoplay 4000 · speed 600 · 743px breakpoint). The original jQuery menu panel fadeIn/Out ('fast') and FAQ slideToggle (400ms swing) are done without loading jQuery, using gsap sine.inOut (= swing)·the height-fold part produces the same curve·length.

The button arrow circle (.c-btnStyle1::after) and the recommended-article arrow button are built with pseudo-elements as in the original, and the arrow is painted with a mask (--site-arrow) so the element’s text color does not change on hover (the original swaps a background image).

Lazy image loading (.u-loadlazy: rest 300ms after loading, then .3s linear) has no images to fetch in the copy, so window load is treated as arrival. To avoid hiding images on a second visit, where the original draws instantly from cache, it is applied only on the home page of a session’s first visit.

The original copy (Japanese), company names and award names are replaced with placeholder text, while the wordmark (brand), the #01 numbering and the App Store/Google Play badge labels are kept as English placeholders. The original ad page was listed as about in pages.json, but since it is ad guidance for businesses it was built as service.html (type service), and the article detail (post1885) as article.html (type article).

title: Mom-and-baby experience event opened by three arch windows
good_for: Events and experience programs for moms, kids and families, schedule finders for events held repeatedly at multiple locations, and soft photo-led brand sites.

pages.use: Event landing page — a hero with a serif wordmark covering half the screen that shrinks into the header logo on scroll, three arch windows opening in turn with photos swapping staggered per window, plus an event search bar. Below: a left pinned arch photo + right cream column (intro text · video, a rounded sage event schedule section with search box · cards, review/column/news sliders, a full-bleed photo, a pill-shaped question list, a rotating text band), and a black arch footer
Brand intro — intro text, four blue feature cards, rounded sage section with three join steps + search box, circular testimonial photos, question pills. For event and program intro pages

Column list — curved English title, one-line intro, tag filter, a vertical chain of cards with photo (NEW circle), tag, bold title, date and ‹Read article› pill, and numbered pagination. For blog, column and news lists
Entry guide — sky-blue box with four icon circles, a pie chart and big-number stats, below a list of pill buttons by entry type. For sponsorship·entry·partnership recruitment pages

Single column article: bold title with underline, tags, hero photo, body mixing subheads, photos and lists, prev/next and list buttons, and two other columns. For blog post detail (the column article captured as detail during recording).

notes: The original the-seasons (Adobe, paid) is replaced by Fraunces, and instead of the original logo image the wordmark uses the three words ‹Brand Name Here› (same width, same rising motion)
The slider is Splide (loop · perPage 1 · speed 800) like the original, but the build could not be read from the original bundle so 4.1.4 from _vendor is used

The original menu panel shape was not seen in the recording (no opened screen), so it is built as a cream panel unfolding from a circle with a two-line English/Korean list. Opening duration, curve and icon sway values are exactly as in the original Header code

In the original, each section has a rounded-top section covering the previous one (exit-lag-scrub), and the pinned arch photo on the left doesn’t change with sections but advances by itself every 6s — the copy does the same. Comparing scroll-effect (--scroll) values wasn’t done because the original is a panel inside #app that the tool can’t measure

title: Monthly video shrinking into a frame, with vertical-text inn pages
good_for: Ryokan, hotel, traditional guesthouse or old-shop sites that quietly show the seasons and the space through a monthly video, essays, news and access info.

pages.use: Home — the month’s full-black-screen video shrinks into a framed picture on paper as you scroll (background night → paper), vertical month name · vertical title and a three-column essay, and a black footer with a moonlit night video. For inn or shop home pages that change video and text each season

About — vertical title header, wide photos per section that bleed out to the center/left/right edge, a vertical section title that sticks to the screen center and follows, and a narrow English column | a wide Korean column with small photos. For introducing history, cooking, rooms, or things you make, split into sections
News list — vertical title header and a three-column grid of date, Korean title, English title and 3:2 photo. For news lists where notices and press coverage appear only occasionally

Access — full-width eaves photo, English|Korean address, bright street map with three panels for train, taxi and car directions (tabs on phone), background turns to night with two affiliated shops (fixed vertical names) and a dark map. For location info of a place where the main building and affiliated shops sit together

notes: The original typefaces (a paid old-style serif and Univers 45 Light) are paid, so they were replaced with Noto Serif KR 300 and Hanken Grotesk 300. The wordmark and seal logo are newly drawn placeholders (LOGOTYPE letters, a line seal in a jar shape).

About is built from only three of the original five sections (history·cooking·rooms·building things·attached restaurant), those whose photo-band types differ (centered·sticking out left·sticking out right) — the rooms and attached restaurant sections repeat the same type
The news detail (a single news item) was not recorded so it was not built, and the list cells link to #

The directions map: the original is a commercial map service (a commercial API·service, not open source that could go in _vendor), so this is a street grid drawn in SVG — no drag·zoom·route drawing. Only the station marker yellow is a map legend color, so it sits outside the skin (/* not skin */). Pressing a transport button fills only the chosen button (on large screens all three guides are always visible), and on phones the guide switches

The page transition veil (cover .6s power2.out + stamp · reveal .5s then 3.75s linear) was not extracted as a part — the nearest page-veil has cover and reveal on one curve and no slot for a center mark, so a reveal curve option (ease-reveal) and a mark (data-fx-part=mark) type remains to be added (capped at 150 minutes per spot, so the next person will pick it up)

title: Illustrated facility guide scrolling sideways on vertical wheel
good_for: Local facility introductions such as converted schools, community hubs, experience farms or multi-shop complexes, and one-page illustration-led festivals or events.

pages.use: Facility single page — hero with logo and school building illustration, concept text, three-color place cards on a sky panel (tap to open a same-color detail modal) and group cards, overview table, map and inside-only-scrolling Q&A on a charcoal panel, checkered-edge footer. Flows sideways with the vertical wheel. For local facility and farm experience About pages

notes: The original is a one-page site (pages: [] in pages.json), so there are no subpages. Place details are built like the original as three modals (same frame #tpl-place, with only color, name and photo label swapped and filled in by index.js) plus group, map, store and SNS modals.

The original illustrations (30-odd characters · school building · map · Q/A · finger icon · strawberry scale board) are image files so they are not ported, but redrawn as an SVG set in illust.js — people are one figure() frame with only skin color, arm pose and held item changed, so unlike the original their poses do not vary much, and the piece counts in the hero and concept stage are lower than the original (30-odd each) at 18~28 each. Position, size, entrance delay and sway timing follow the original CSS values. All fills are --site-* skin variables
The original logo (a soft, bubbly three-line BRAND mark) was drawn as a YOUR/000/LOGO placeholder in Bagel Fat One, which has a similar feel. The Hero sticker is also a LOGO placeholder.
The original fonts are paid (Adobe Fonts square gothic, Neulis Neue, Neulis Cursive), so Noto Sans KR, Outfit and Fredoka were used. The HOW TO ENJOY band text is a SECTION TITLE placeholder.

The original pattern graphics (droplets on the modal color background, faint logo shapes on the charcoal panel, card background pattern) are image files, so they were redrawn as CSS gradient dots and circles. The checkered patterns at the bottom of the menu panel and on the footer’s right band use conic-gradient.

A walking character (fixed to the screen, stops at 2vw, turns rotateY 180 0.3s power1.inOut when going back, flips rotateY 90→-90→0 for 0.2s each at section boundaries 0.4/0.3/0.2, hidden on phones when overlapping a card) and a Lenis 1.3.17 horizontal stage (duration 1.2, body height = horizontal length + screen height), loader (min 3 seconds · black panel .6s 1s · lift .6s 1.6s cubic-bezier(.19,1,.22,1) · sessionStorage first visit only) use the original values as they are. The Swiper and mouse follower (Stalker) in the original bundle have no place to be used in this page DOM (0 swiper classes) so they were not included.

Type backfill: Outfit, Fredoka and Bagel Fat One slots (menu, section titles, place names, band text, logo graphic, Loading, phone number) were English slot text from the start, so latin-slots is 0 and nothing was replaced

Loader two-line intro · concept paragraph · the ”Your section title here” line under chapter titles · Korean place-name line. The original is Japanese (an angular Japanese Gothic typeface), Korean is kept. Body Noto Sans KR Gothic matches the Outfit sans-serif

title: Personal blog with a draggable 3D grass island and typed title
good_for: Personal blogs, writing collections or work notes that open with one touchable 3D scene and then move into quiet paper-like reading panels.

pages.use: Blog hero — a large serif headline is typed one letter at a time (writing and erasing a hidden word), then the intro and buttons appear. A grass island at the bottom of the screen lies down under the cursor (trail 20 seconds) and rotates 15° at a time when dragged, while the central picture changes in waves. Hovering the headline types the hidden word again and nearby letters swell in a variable font. A sun button cycles day → sunset → night. For the entrance of a personal blog or work notes

Post list — after approaching a field, a paper panel rises from 22% below, with a big year stuck to the left for each year + rows of title · one-line summary · category · number · date (on hover the title shifts with an arrow, and the summary is replaced by the first sentence and a sound bar). A grass band at the bottom of the screen overlaps the list. For blog·News lists

A single article — scroll-snap sections step through the title section, body section and closing section (next article). On wide screens the left table-of-contents ticks mark the current section in red, and a listening bar at bottom center holds play · 11-segment progress · section picker · ”Listen from here” per section · reading-paragraph highlight. For one long article or case study

notes: The field (_fx/grass-turntable-gl) is our own shader with the same numbers: 220k grass blades · wind ripple · cursor ball 1.15 · 8 marks for 20 seconds · growth 2.7s · turntable 24 cells 15° · ease 9 · drag 90px · image change .42s ripple. The original’s green floor (light and hill shade baked in), grass shadow capsules, petal atlas, small islands around the island, and the landmark warp of the image panel are missing. The floor is one color, the hills are low sine hills, and the change is a ripple plus mass-conserving blend without warp. The grass shape (ink outline 14% · occasional long grass 4% · red flower clusters) uses values picked by eye to match the original print.

The 24 center illustration panels (original situations png) reuse four of our own canvas-drawn scenes (child reading with a dog · telescope · kite · cat on a box) — baseline .36, 3:2 transparent. The two colors for human skin and fur are part of the illustration, so they are marked as ”not Skin” in shared.js. It does not have the hand-drawn illustration texture of the original.

The original meadow sound (short band-noise via WebAudio when typing and flipping the bar), the voice preview for the post list and posts, and the dialogue audio are absent. The listening bar only runs the 4:05 time, and hovering a list row shows only the first sentence and the bar (after 220ms).

Decisions: the title wordmark (The Sample Blog, hidden words not·?), list titles, post titles and speaker names are Latin Fraunces in the original, so they are English placeholders. The menu (Menu 1) and Subscribe are also English (same button shape as the original, so tools skip the same button). The intro, summaries, body, button text (Go read the post · Back to the field) and the bar hint (Drag to rotate) stay Korean copy. The two social buttons use generic icons (@ · ring) and outside placeholder URLs instead of the original’s two social brand marks.

three is r185 in the original, but three@0.185.0 in this repo has no browser build (min.js), so the r186 IIFE build is used — the APIs we use (InstancedBufferGeometry·ShaderMaterial·OrthographicCamera) are the same in both.

Swapping the whole theme.css for a dark skin (night background) was not tested — the site itself has day, dusk and night transitions, so the night state was checked (side by side with the original night), but with a swapped skin it would cycle to dusk and night again on top of that skin. Left for the next person to follow up.

title: Quiet company home with an animated emblem drawing itself in
good_for: One-screen intros for small companies or studios with a few products, hiring pages, and long essay-style statements of values.

pages.use: Company home — the crest is drawn as lines, then shrinks and rises into place, and an italic sentence, two product links, a menu line and five Lottie symbols below appear. For a one-screen intro of a small company

Careers — centered crest and menu on top, intro text, open positions rows (department · role · location links), six FAQs with only one open at a time, closing box with a two-line divider. For careers and application guides

Values essay — illustrated hero, dark intro, five sections where a differently colored band for each chapter stops at the end and is covered by the next band (line art, numbered paragraphs, bold quotes), closing with a sources list. For company values, manifestos and long reads.

notes: The seven Lottie files (curtain intro, curtain loop, globe, four letter plates, coin, wordmark, copyright line) don’t use the original JSON. We generated new shape-based Lottie with a /tmp generator and put them in lottie-data.js. Frame counts (29.97fps, intro 0→63 · loop 90→140 · symbols 0→150), size, loop range and playback speed (loop .5, 2 on hover) match the original, but the art is simple lines and bars. Color is a single black, which CSS overrides with currentColor so it follows the skin and dark panels. Because fetch is blocked on file://, the data is loaded through JS rather than as JSON files.
The original fonts ABC Diatype Mono and Brand Text are paid, so they are swapped for DM Mono and Source Serif 4. EB Garamond is the same free font.

The values essay shrinks the original 16000px Webflow page (five sections × about twelve numbered paragraphs, a line-illustration column, a pile of 18 film-still photos) to three to five paragraphs and one line illustration per section. The line illustrations (original SVG) are redrawn at the same position, size and red line texture, and the hero illustration is a gray panel with a label.

The cursor pixel trail is matched to the values the original calls (pixelSize 10, fade 500ms linear, internet blue) — it was first built with the component default of 20px, but cursor-sweep showed only the copy reacting widely, so the original call site was reread and fixed.

The strip above the values essay folds into a hamburger even on large screens, like the original, and the original CSS’s color-strip sticky (top −160vh…) is overridden by the very next rule to static, so it is actually off and the copy keeps normal flow too. The values page has no theme button or pixel tail, as in the original (separate app-router version).

title: Morphing droplet window and color-shifting garden stay site
good_for: Resort, lodging, glamping or garden facility homepages that bundle several offerings such as stays, dining, barbecue and activities into one site.

pages.use: Facility landing page — a hero where a looping video inside a droplet window (Snap.svg morph) peels away into a full-bleed video with a single wheel turn, a date search bar, a member bar, a news slider, four facilities whose background color changes (droplet photo · cursor), a flowing photo strip, info · map, and booking. For the landing page of a lodging with several facilities

Concept intro — centered title, white intro text over a photo, three droplet photos in a zigzag, video strip, facility surround illustration around a garden, two cards. For place and brand philosophy intros
News list — text header, dotted category tabs, 4-column square cards, page numbers. For news and event lists

Careers — header with a 4-cell mosaic of photos and color tiles, intro inside a mint droplet, zigzag of droplet photos by department, three mint-background appeal cards, large ink-black button. For service-industry careers pages

Barbecue menu — dark photo header, anchor guide, band title, course blocks (price row + photo on the right) · two-column ingredients · allergy icons, à la carte and drink price list, contact band. For restaurant barbecue menus

Barbecue area guide — photo header, anchor guide, and for each band title a seat layout diagram, price table, photo plus text, facility icons, parking diagram, a contact band, and a Q&A accordion. For the Facility Guide page
Page not found — big 404, one line, mint button. The recorded ”Member service notice” news URL is a 404 on the original, so this screen was built

notes: The droplet window shape does not copy the original path data (five snap shapes) and is drawn instead with the same number of our own seeded droplets. The morphing itself chains the same Snap.svg 0.5.1 animate 10000ms easeInOutQuad each time it ends.

The original facility photos mix pre-cut PNGs and objectBoundingBox clipPath — the cut shapes are image files themselves and can’t be carried over, so all use the same droplet clipPath instead. Photo positions and sizes are vw values measured from the 1440 capture (each original PNG has its own CSS padding, so there is no basis for transferring numbers)

The compare tool (compare.cjs) wheel does not advance the original’s hero steps (original jQuery wheel handling), so the lower part of the original was checked against a separate wheel capture (/tmp/lib-brand-brand-orig-2).

The News Swiper is attached only on wide screens — the original keeps it on phones and shows only three items via CSS, but loop reorders sections so a different three may show, so on phones it is not attached and stays a vertical list of the same three items
The original typefaces Helvetica Neue LT Pro and FONTPLUS Hiragino are paid, so they were swapped for Inter and Pretendard. The logo is a Wordmark/Place letter placeholder.

Menu and usage guide: the original’s six repeating course blocks and facility list are cut to two and one. Seat layout art and parking art are newly drawn SVGs in the same composition (light gray background like the original)
The card composition inside the mega menu panel (3 to 4 photos) was guessed from the original image names (mega_concept01~03 · mega_stay01~04 · mega_bbq01~03)
Review-site widget, map embed and booking-engine search bar are shape-only placeholders

title: Secret-society club site under a CRT overlay with pixel serif type
good_for: Homepages for clubs, communities, meetups or circles with event info, member introductions and a contact form in a playful pixel and CRT tone.

pages.use: Community home page — a loader where the logo opens, a pixel-serif Hero where photos and stickers pop out following the cursor, a navy About where words fly in (fixed), photo cells with three events that switch every 6 seconds, endlessly flowing people cards (photos turn into pixels), and a Footer with draggable window stickers. For organization landing pages centered on events and people

Event list — over a full-bleed photo, the next event (badge, large title, sign-up button) is covered by pixel cells and swapped in, past events are listed as table rows, and hovering a row changes the preview photo stuck to the cursor. For event, talk and performance archives

Group About — group photo header, a pinned panel where sixteen photos recede in depth and scatter upward, big text marquee, highlighter tags, a big sentence with a side column, and a six-photo row. For a group or team About page.

Contact — big text that bends on a navy panel locked to one screen, two draggable window stickers (click to copy the email address), a downward-flowing marquee and a photo strip. For short contact pages

notes: Typefaces: the original heading FK Raster Roman Compact Smooth, label KH Interference and body KH Brand are all paid, so they were swapped for Redaction 35 (a pixel-broken roman, OFL), Geist Pixel Square and Inter Tight. KH Interference is monospaced so its width stays fixed during the letter scramble, but Geist Pixel is proportional, so the footer window links are locked to their initial width (shared.js scramble)

Art: the original stickers (flame, taco, beer, heart, headphones, eye) and sentence (eight-point star + eye) are redrawn as our own pixel art (shared.js ART, the 25-cell sentence is drawn by formula). Some original stickers are lime and orange tiles, so the sticker colors in the trace look flatter than the original

Loader: the original loads the site script after DOMContentLoaded and starts about 1.2s after the first image — the same wait (HOLD 1200ms) is kept. As in the original, it appears only on the first page
The 6s progress bar in the event cell is a plain empty element like the original (the original CSS gives it no shape, so it is invisible). Only the advance timing and order match
Hidden original sections (the display:none browser window mockup, the mwg066 line mask, the mwg094 card strip, two intro cards) are not visible on screen, so they were not built.

Motion parts not yet extracted (for the next person): photo trail (elastic.out(2,.6) per 1/8 width · ×4 slide), word fly-in pinned panel (mwg005), photo depth scatter (mwg082), neon strip walk (each row folds right with .9s power3.inOut), wipe-cover tag, draggable window sticker (magnet + corner pixel handle), event 6s auto-advance, preview follow (±100% .5s power2.inOut), footer −55% rise-up

title: Dark gym product story with 3D court, horizontal tech band and falling pouch
good_for: Sports gear or single-product brand pages that present features scene by scene and route team or bulk orders to a quote form.

pages.use: A single product landing page: number-hole loader, light-beam Hero, 3D court (spiral cards), four horizontally flowing technologies, sawtooth-band transition, name embroidery, two review videos, a pouch falling behind a light haze, dusk, and a video Footer. For a first page that sells one sports item or product as a scene.

Statement and guidance document — large title and lead followed by sections divided with thin lines (list, two-column table, closing). For text-only pages such as transparency notices, accessibility guides and terms
FAQ — each question with a thin line + small uppercase question, answers as paragraphs or numbered lists. For order, shipping and sizing pages

notes: Of the original’s three sub-pages, the AI disclosure (ai-transparency) and accessibility pages are statements of the same form, so they share one page.html, and the FAQ is built as faq.html. The original’s quote room (/kit) was not recorded, so the Quote button is wired to move to faq.html (name slot: Next Page).

Court 3D: the original sock model (a glb made from 47 photos), card photos and video are not used, they are replaced with tube-and-sphere shape socks and canvas-label cards. The reflective floor (Reflector) is reduced to flipping the light pillar below the floor. Card spiral (radius .59 · height 1.31 · 1.5 turns · birth .07+.2·.1) · camera (0.1, .78, 1.3, 42°) · dust 420 · heading panel (5 from camera · width .46 · top .27) values are the original’s.

In the name-embroidery section the background and leg cutouts are photos, so they are placeholders: our silhouette SVG at the same position and ratio (2400×1600, ankle 1493,893) plus photo-slot labels. good_for: Production studio or agency homepages with scroll-driven 3D objects and dark layouts that transition with green light.

pages.use: Agency home page — first loader (000→100%), a title dispersing like smoke with flying 3D ironing boards, five lines turning like a wheel, a manifesto filling with light, a to-do accordion whose striped ring changes circle→square→triangle→pentagon, work ironing boards with falling cloth and a number panel, a horizontally flowing why section with an iron path, and a review slider

Work list — a 3D list with a big title, a featured work (an ironing board under cloth), and 12 work cards sliding along a spiral around an ironing board standing behind a large band of text. For the Hero of portfolio or case lists

About the company — from a dark head, a folded ironing board flies in, spins and leaves while four number panels rise from below spinning, two founders (cutout photo + name card), two story columns, a year ring whose digits roll over each year, six team-role cards sliding in from left and right row by row on a stage where the ironing board spins and flies off, helper card pile. For company and team About pages

Single case — name, subtitle and client table, large featured screen, fixed title on the left with long text, numbers, tags, screens, steps and feature list sections continuing on the right, ending with results and testimonial. For case detail pages

The hero, footer, loader and transition glows are our own shaders (glow-field·glow-veil-page). The original pushes the light away with a flow texture that draws hand traces separately, and four diagonal wave bands (sweeps) pass across the transition veil. The bands were not built

The work card ring (works) passes at eye level around a standing board — in the original it is the same scene produced by the camera rising along a spiral (22 high, 5.6 turns). Card titles and descriptions are not drawn on the board, only placeholder boards.
The 3D on the pinned stage at the end of detail isn’t visible in the original recording, so an iron was used (judgment call)
For Agencies·Let's Talk (Contact) page was not recorded, so it was not built. Menu items 3·4 link to Work and Footer

Each page’s script is registered with TB.page(name, hook), and when the body leaves it clears gsap.context, window listeners (AbortController), WebGL renderers and draw loops. Header, drawer, footer and loader exist once in the document. So every page loads the css and scripts of all four pages

title: Gold particle animal morphing into rings, bracelets and gems
good_for: Immersive intros or launch pages for luxury goods such as jewelry, watches and fragrances that tell a collection story.

pages.use: A single page for a high-end jewelry brand — blink-of-an-eye loader, giant serif name over a particle tiger, declaration that clears from blur, pinned horizontal collection, spinning particle ring and full-screen photo, particle bracelet work section, particle tiger that changes color with three finish buttons, two ruby and diamond particle interludes, editorial and video panel, photo slots between words, shop grid and detail panel, footer over the particle tiger face. For product launches and brand stories

notes: Instead of the original particle images (webp for particle sampling), shaders and post-processing (UnrealBloom, color grading, vignette), points are sampled from shapes freshly drawn on a canvas: a tiger in profile (ruby stripes), a tiger-face silhouette with formula-based rings (a ring and a tilted bracelet), icosahedron edges (ruby), and four beads with gold thread (diamond). Glow comes from additive blending (canvas alpha 0) and large sparkle points (6% of points at 7x size) rather than post-processing. The screen-whitening bloom intensity and the fur-like density of the original are weaker here.
The point count is lower than the original (about 160k) — 2.60k on wide screens and 1.40k on phones. No mechanism that measures the original’s fps and lowers quality was added.

Scene values are the original bundle’s as they are — first Section scatter .1→.64 · ring gather .42→.83 · camera z 6→5.3 · opacity 1−.55, ring Section orbit 2π (.12→.59) · tilt .24 · dive z 6.2−3.2g−4p, bracelet Section gather .01→.22 · rotation .28→.73 · dive .78→1 · text .17→.26/.59→.72 · photo from .65, closing Section m×3.8 hold range · gather .32→.52, photo cover clip .01→.22 · up 105% .72→1 · scrub .65, Hero birth 1.8s power2.out · camera 9.2→6 2.6s power3.out · text 1.1s (+.35), Lenis 1.25s expo out.

The original artwork section code covers five works, but the actual page has only one bracelet section, so only one section was built. The finale section height (240vh · pinned stage) could not be read from the original, so the scene progress was set to fit the screen.
The original’s brand morph, where the particle face in the last section turns into TIGRIS letters, isn’t included. The face scatters and the footer wordmark (DOM) stands on the same stage.

Sound (background music·effects) is not included — Sound on only changes state. The original’s app install (PWA), visit consent window and viewing-reservation form dialog are not built (the detail page reservation button is a placeholder only).
Photo and video entries are placeholders noting what the image shows. The object-position 85%→15% on the collection cell photo shifts a 130%-wide placeholder by −23%, showing the same flow.

Bodoni Moda and Space Grotesk have no Hangul, so Korean falls back to Noto Serif KR and Noto Sans KR. In the font backfill (2026-11-08), the Bodoni slots (four wordmarks, big title, two italic subtitles, manifesto, section titles, piece names) were swapped for Latin placeholder text (STUDIO, Piece 01…) so the stroke contrast stays alive, as in the original. The brand name is set as the six-letter uppercase STUDIO, matching the original’s six-letter wordmark — Studio Name would overflow the screen in the giant title (15.8vw) and footer (19vw) (judgment call). Slots for the body font (Space Grotesk) — menu, header, buttons, body copy and the footer intro panel — stay in Korean (outside latin-slots scope). The loader shows its dot once fonts are ready (3s max), just as the original shows it after assets load.

title: Big capitals with a shrinking showreel and a time-zone globe

Work list — a big uppercase title and a case grid alternating one large cell and two small cells (photo parallax). For portfolio·case collection pages. A button at the bottom of the screen switches to Film strip view (a photo strip per case that flows with the mouse, plus a large preview)
About. Large quoted sentence and hand drawing, pinned line where ”Victory” stacks like stairs, method slides, black partner panel, orange founder and team name panel

notes: Font backfill (2026-11-08): the original is entirely English, so every Korean filler in the heading font (Inter Tight) and the serif (Newsreader) was replaced with English placeholder copy. This covers the logo, loader text and wordmark (Studio Name), the big Hero word, the ”Feeling” heading and band words (Feeling 01–06, including card data-word and sub text), the one-line company statement, service names, field panels and the News band, the About quote and stacking words (step) and team member names, Careers headings, sentences and benefits, Work and News section headings, and Case detail titles, slogans and next case. Each replaced element carries a data-label noting what goes in that slot. Menu, results rows, card sub text and descriptions drawn in the body font (--kf-font-sans) stay Korean, since falling back to a paired Korean font is the intended use. No heading-font slot remains in Korean. Team member names were set to Full Name 01 (about 12 characters, like the original names) so they do not wrap in the two 390 columns. For the next person: in the About section ”stacking words” row, below 767px .tw-stack-row turns vertical and the .tw-stack-words width collapses to 0 (all children are absolute), so the words spill past the left edge. This is a structural issue from an earlier version, unrelated to text length, so it was not fixed in this backfill (text only).

In the ”Feel” section, the floating photos reduce the original image sequence (photos change in turn and the words ”Make them feel radiant/well mastered” swap) to six photos flowing at different speeds. The horizontal case strip carries over 520vh pinned, scrub .6 and the word swap on each card (original HOME_MOTION_PROFILE horizontalSpectrum).

The company statement section (brandStatement 270vh, transitionFraction .28, scrub 1.15) has only a pinned heading plus lines rising one by one, and the services list darkening one line at a time with scroll progress. The selected work follows the original HomeWorkGridMotion: two-card rows (the hovered side grows to 1020:724, Flip .58 power4.out), single-card rows (24% empty and 76% card, hovering shifts the row width 16% to the left and crops the photo by 6px over .5s), and the ”All Work” link. The rotating client logo band was not built.

Recruiting globe: the original R3F + drei setup (OrbitControls, Html pins, land-map texture) is rebuilt with three 0.174. It has a sphere of r1 with 64 segments, semi-transparent. Of 9000 Fibonacci points, only those where our own sine noise passes the threshold become land dots. Dashed arcs use dash .045 and gap .035. The group is scaled .8x at y −.25, camera z 3.2, auto-rotate .052rad per second (autoRotateSpeed .5), and dragging with the mouse rotates it. The ten pins and cities are placeholders (only the clock times are computed from real city time zones). The land shapes are not the real continents.

Recent news carries over the original News dialog: a 20% black blurred backdrop, a close button at top right, a row of 421px cards 60px from the right, and ”See all news”. Opening (backdrop .35 · cards .4 power2.out at .06 intervals after .1 · close button after .15), closing (cards .35 · backdrop .3 power2.in after .1) and the body lock are all carried over. The hamburger menu and showreel button have only their look and opening, and the showreel video curtain was not built. The contact panel is a small panel instead of the original 548px large panel (image, copy address).

The case detail was built with only the representative sections of the original’s long case layout (full-screen hero · growing slogan · blue panel · photo grid · next case). The news list starts from 12 cards as the original does (three columns, n%3), and ”Load more” unfolds the remaining cards and replays the first-line·scroll entrance — category filtering only changes the button state and does not actually filter. The arrow link is built with a CSS d transition for the original BentArrowIcon (on hover the bent arrow lengthens over .5s and shifts .4em) and the right→left underline

Inherited and fixed: the Footer in the original style (top row + margin clamp(80px, 100svh − 232px − 24.8vw, 330px) + a wordmark slot at logo ratio 1844:458 → one screen at 1440×900, columns 84·63 / 103·66px). The previous version was 560px, so the News strip covered the Footer links when the tool pointed at them. On the first page of News, the card photo label is attached to the top so it doesn’t move when the cell grows. Load more is wrapped in a row (mt 80) like the original, and new card photos get FadeInImage (.7s cubic-bezier(0,0,.2,1)). Added the original ‹Jump to open roles› slot (arrow link) to the Careers Hero, with the entrance order following the original code (title line .45 then .85s at .1 stagger · body line .62 then .8s · link .8 then .85s). Removed the branch that skipped in-section entrances on arrival sections (the original re-mounts parts on every section switch, so entrances run again). Body and Footer are wrapped in one cell (.tw-shell) like the original AppShell and fade together. Fading them separately let the Footer behind show through the translucent body during the entrance.

title: Year-ruler loader then a 3D brush-script logo for an anniversary page
good_for: Company anniversary microsites with greeting, events, projects, history, future plans and company overview.

pages.use: Anniversary one-pager — year-ruler loader · 3D brush-calligraphy logo tilting with the mouse and stickers · pixel band lettering · News band · glass greeting · event photo slider · project collection · history filling in navy · company About with physics-dropped pills. For company anniversary specials

notes: The original is a single page (pages: [] in pages.json), so it has no subpages. The external special sites (T-shirt and package contest) that the original stickers point to were changed to same-page anchors.

The 3D logo cannot use the original OBJ (brush calligraphy character with hand-shaped stroke ends), so it is our own shape made of four joined tubes (three is 0.160.0, same as the original). The longest side is set to 23.68, same as the original OBJ, so the entrance formula (size 4% interpolation · sin 0.7x swell · z rotation = remaining size ×2·one turn of y as the start) and mouse tilt (±0.5rad, 0.05 interpolation) · phone auto-sway come out the same values. Material and lighting use the original values (black metalness .7 roughness .2, ambient 1.2·directional 2·point 15), but since our shape lacks the OBJ’s fine curvature the gloss doesn’t reflect, so a white light-panel room was added as a PMREM environment map. Once you have the OBJ, just swap buildModel() for an OBJLoader.

The loader logo repeats a 73×106 · 60fps · 183-frame (3.05s) Lottie via lottie-web 5.12.2 like the original, but the artwork is ours (logo-anime.js — header brush-script mark + 00th). From the original only the moments the eye moves (frames 0·48·96·144, 2 up, 2/3 down-left) and the eye-closing span (frames 159.6~177.6) were measured and carried over. The original uses the canvas renderer, but the lottie-web@5.12.2 in _vendor is only the svg-only build (lottie_svg.min.js), so it draws with the svg renderer — shapes and timing are the same, and it was left as is so as not to add files to someone else’s build folder. The original CSS logo slot is 30rem, but the Lottie draws at about 85px inside it, so the visible size (9rem) was carried over.

The flowing text bands, photo rows, News band, event photo crossfade and thumbnail row use the same Swiper 8.3.0 as the original, with the original settings applied as they are (speed 40000/8000 · 10000/500, autoplay delay 0/5000/2500, fade crossFade, initialSlide -1). Band text width: the original CSS says 133.98cqw (548.8vw on phone), but inside a Swiper slide (flex, width 100%) it shrinks and actually renders at one screen width, so the rendered width (slide 100%) was carried over. The original pixel-text SVG band was rewritten with Pixelify Sans and Instrument Serif letters (the history page uses ink color at 20%). The event photos are 8 instead of the original 17 (the same count as the thumbnails).

The blurred color photo behind the hero (mv_bg) is a radial-gradient blob layout in the same arrangement. The ten stickers, event logo set, foundation mark, CMYK dots and circular text were redrawn as SVG (shape, position, size and tilt values match the original, while the picture content is a placeholder).

Skin: every original color is a --site-* variable in shared.css that produces the same value as an oklch relative color from --kf-accent·--kf-ink·--kf-surface (computed colors across all 557 elements were compared at 1440·390 before and after the skin cleanup, with zero differences). When you switch skins, the sticker, pill and blotch colors rotate at the same intervals following the accent — to keep the original colors, the consumer overrides --site-*. Only the CMYK dots beside the crop marks are print ink, so their values are set as ”not skin”. The navy stage of the timeline·message sections uses --kf-contrast-bg·--kf-contrast-ink.
History has 15 rows and photo slots equal the original count, with years swapped for 2000~2020 placeholders (loader numbers too, data-from/data-to 2000→2020).

For a lifestyle company landing with three product lines.

Concept · Promise — big photo header, pinned contents box, column box, three-type comparison table, pill index of 10 promises with promise text alternating photos and illustrations, big-letter photo band, recommended pages. For company philosophy, promise and service comparison pages
Project list — collapsible left filters (type, region, price range…) and two-column project cards (price, tags), pagination. For lists of projects, works and listings
Blog list — categories on the left and a one-line post list of thumbnail · date · tag · title · arrow. For blog, column and news lists
Event list — three columns of event cards with category on the left and a date range (start↓end). For tour, seminar and campaign listings

notes: The recorded 5th subpage (works/category/factory·office) has the same form as the work case list, so a single works.html stands in for it (type was captured as detail during recording, but it is actually a category list). The event list (recorded type lookbook) has the same form as the News list, so its type was changed to news.
The Japanese body font TsukuOldGothic (paid, FontPlus) was replaced by Gothic A1 800. The handwritten title art (Our homes, all kinds.) was rebuilt as text with letters split by color

Illustrations (people shaking hands, excavator ground, walking family, book stack, floor plan and pencil, map, etc.) were redrawn as simple line drawings of the same position, size and motion — with fewer strokes than the original hand drawings
Of the ten promises on the About page only 01, 02, 03, 06, 07 and 09 are built (cut down since the form repeats, but all added parts — shortcut strip, example card, table, confirm box — are kept)

The wavy underline and the white arrow over photos are repeating images that cannot be painted with a mask, so shared.js reads the skin colors (--kf-accent · --site-sky · --kf-contrast-ink) and bakes the image URL — if you swap in a different theme.css, reopen the page for it to update
Raised the fixed bottom menu bar above the wire.js check bar (z-index 10000), so on phones part of the check bar is covered by the menu bar
Font backfill: the Latin heading font slots (section names, numbers, TYPE, Check it!, LOGO, rotating text circle) were English placeholder text from the start, so there is nothing to change

index three types: If you’re unsure… (.s-script) — the original uses kana picture letters (bold gothic bent into an arc: Custom build? Ready-made?… and If you can’t decide…), Korean copy kept. Yellowtail has no Korean, so bold handwriting Gaegu 700 was paired as --kf-font-script (Nanum Brush Script has a small letter body and nearly hid behind the badge). The slight overlap of the text’s bottom edge on the badge is the build-time margin-bottom -1.5rem as is — in the original the arc-bent text sits above the badge

Category pills in 7 slots in index·news text rows (.s-tag inside .h-row__meta·.l-row__meta) — the original uses a kana category (Other), Korean is kept. The row head is Lato, but Korean is drawn in its paired Gothic A1, so it matches the original body gothic.

title: Draggable isometric town with sticker logo for a spot-the-difference game
good_for: Landing screens for children's or school learning games, quizzes and hands-on campaigns with stage select, how-to and teacher materials.

pages.use: Learning game hero, a single screen — a village illustration larger than the screen (drag to look around) with a sticker logo, start button and credits popping on top, then after start a five-card how-to-play slide and three stage buttons on the map, a stage cover, stage list and material download modal. For educational games and quiz campaign home pages.

notes: The original was recorded as a single page (pages: [] in pages.json). The stage game screens (stage_1~3.html: tap the wrong spot, answer explanation, remaining count, clear modal) were not recorded, so they were not built. ”Start” uses the same barba 2.10.3 transition as the original (leave: after the menu and modal are tucked away and the stage circle closes in .6s, 900ms, enter: new container from opacity 0) to ?stage=Goes to the same first page with n attached, and re-triggers the first draw on the incoming container (TKB.pages.top)

The original village is a single hand-drawn SVG (1380×1090, with hundreds of characters, signs, bicycles and so on). It was redrawn with the same composition, line weight and fill feel using a seeded isometric generator (2-lane road bands, 7×7 blocks, lot splitting, buildings, gabled houses, parking lots, parks, playgrounds, cars, people, traffic lights). It is more geometric than the original, with fewer people and props. To use the original art, replace everything inside #t-art with the single drawing (same viewBox).

Of the original repeating motion inside graphics, only representative ones were ported: steam scale 1.1 · tree scale 1.04 twice · swing -2deg · bird 3deg (all 2–3s steps(1)), traffic light blinking. Pressing the cat or bird makes a 0.8s jump (the original jump), which is included. The original dozens of per-character keyframes are not included.
Stage locks are fixed to the original first-visit state (10k open, 2·3 gray) — unlocking by the original’s clear record (openedstage) is not implemented.
The how-to card width matches the original measurement (327px at 1440, 34rem on phones). Why it differs from the 35.3rem in the original CSS was not found.
The original’s announce and error modals and the ‹Find the differences› title strip at the top of the stage screen are used only on the stage screen, so they are not placed on the first page.

Font: Zen Maru Gothic (the same free font as the original web font service) has no Hangul, so headings come out in Jua and body in Gowun Dodum — headings are less round than the original 900-weight round gothic and the body is thinner.

The logo is a placeholder sticker (two-line title, tag speech bubble, big eyes, three illustration tiles). Per-cluster entrance (1.4x→1, delays .2/.6/1/1.3/1.5s), 3D wobble and eye motion values are as in the original.

title: Left branch panel and fading number plates for a parts trading firm
good_for: Homepages for multi-branch B2B trading, distribution or maintenance companies with business and product lists and a company profile.

pages.use: Company first page — left navy branch panel (click opens a side drawer) · video hero · recent News strip · business list whose photos change on hover · product cards with faint English phrases flowing · number panel whose photos blur while attached · photo strip · education facility · leads into About

Company info — big English header and two photos, INDEX panel pinned on the left, overview table, history, sales bar chart, branch cells, mission, vision photo that spreads to fill the screen, code of conduct. For company overview pages
Products — header with a flowing row of product photos, fixed INDEX panel, per category a 4-column product cell group and a 2-column maker list. For parts·product catalog lists
Business intro — two header photos, INDEX panel and product banner pinned, three feature cards (photo·number·title) and four business rows (text·button·large photo). For business·service guides
News list — 3-column cards (photo·date·two-line title) under a big English heading. For company notice lists

notes: The company info VISION photo spread (left·right 24rem · top·bottom 6rem · corner 1rem → 0 · -10% · 0, scrub 1) is built in about.js with the original values and not extracted as a part — side-inset-open only takes left and right clip, so options for top/bottom, corners and overflow (-10%) must be added, which did not fit in the time

The original menu’s ‹About Brand› (/about/), ‹Training Room› (/trainingroom/) and the business sub-pages were not recorded, so they were not built — menu links connect to about.html#mission · index.html#training · service.html#our

title: Draggable floor plan with scene video tiles on one-screen map
good_for: Campaign or brand pages for airports, stations, campuses, malls or exhibition halls that let people browse scene videos and stories across a map.

pages.use: One-screen map campaign: a center wordmark whose letters bounce up after a loading percent, a floor plan moved by wheel or drag with 20 video tiles (1.3x when near), a small hatched map and zoom buttons, sound on/off/only, an About drawer at top center, and a scene modal that opens when a tile is clicked. For campaigns that invite people to explore scenes around a place.

notes: The original is a single page (pages: [] in pages.json), so there are no subpages. The details of the 20 scenes open in a same-page modal like the original — the content is attached to each tile’s <template data-js=item-detail> Is located at.

Video tiles are drawn, as in the original, by a three r173 orthographic camera in the DOM tile spots (camera = Map slot, half screen, zoom = Map scale, mesh scale = tile scale value). The original video is an asset, so the texture is a 3:2 placeholder plate with its label drawn, and a band of light passes over it every 8 seconds (the peak lasts until 7.1s, hence 8) — put the real video in place of paint() in index.js <video muted loop playsinline> Swap in a THREE.VideoTexture.

Sound uses the same Tone.js 15.0.4 graph as the original (per scene: sound → Panner(±.8) → Gain(cursor distance) → master Gain → Volume 0 → 10 over .5s when switched on, indoor/outdoor ambient CrossFade .5s, and when a scene panel opens only that scene is set to 1·centered). The original scene sounds and ambient mp3s are assets, so scene sounds are short sine tones fired at each peak of the placeholder video, and ambient is brown·pink noise — swap the Synth slots for Tone.Player to get the real sound.

As in the original, the center wordmark plays a lottie-web 5.12.2 Lottie (29.97fps · 150 frames) bounce, then at 3.8s it swaps over 1.6s to a static wordmark in the same spot. The original glyph outlines are assets, so we measured the position, typeface and color of our placeholder letters in the static wordmark and built a text layer, then applied the original’s per-letter start frame and per-frame y curve (as a ratio of letter height) unchanged. The bottom line uses the first 5 of the original 6-letter (Name) curves for Brand.

The loading percentage counts by following the Lottie load at 10% per tick, like the original. The original also counts the first 5 videos (data-first-load) becoming downloaded enough to play, but the placeholder has no video files, so only the one Lottie step is counted. When real videos are added, add their canplay events to steps in shared.js

Mouse following (tile swelling · sound distance) and dragging turn on only after the first entrance finishes, as in the original, and turn off while the About or scene panel is open. The three panel is also built at first entrance (before that the map panel is transparent)

The wordmark placeholder keeps the original structure (a brand-name line overlapping a light-gray greeting line) as Have a Good Day / Brand Good Day. notes: Page transitions use Barba 2.9.7, same as the original (leave and enter each .4s transparent, power1.inOut, not sync), and smooth scroll uses the same Lenis 1.1.16 (lerp .25, wheel 1×). When the page changes, init(page) in shared.js reruns letter splitting, is-v on visible, underline hover, magnet and card stamping. Since Barba only swaps the page, every page type lives in one set of pages.css and pages.js.

The original’s infinite drag strip (js-ifs: an own class where the current position chases the target by .08 per frame, each cell jumps separately to the right end once it passes the left end, and it stops off screen) is site code, so it is not carried over. Instead, three options are added to drag-marquee (1px per frame · boost .25 · drag: lerp) to give the same flow — ramp (first-step catch-up .08, strips inside a panel .15 to match the measured start time) · wrap: item (per-cell wrap, hero·Keywords·Information strips) · inview (stop off screen, all strips). Strips in the closed menu·search panels are lowered below the screen (top 100vh) as in the original so they do not flow, then rise and flow when the panel opens. The feel of drag inertia (lerp constants) uses the part defaults (catch .002 · decay .02), so it differs slightly from the original

Cover card flipping (not endless) uses the same formula as the original (target = (column number × column width, follows .08 per frame / .15 while dragging, snaps to the nearest column on release) newly written in pages.js. Advance with the lime-green circle buttons inside the 25% side columns of the original desktop.

The magnet (-mag) follows the original approach exactly — at the moment the pointer enters it measures the pivot (.-pvt 1px, dead center of the photo frame), half the cell size and the Lenis scroll position, then each frame chases the cursor’s offset (minus scroll movement) by .1, with piece i shifted (i+1)/n × offset × TY px and tilted by X·Y product × 10° (TY = min(.2 of half-height·half-width, .05 of screen width). If the cell is off screen the share is left as is (IS_VIEW). Values are used uncut, like the original. The new-post card is a magnet frame as a whole card, like the original. data-mag-auto (re-measuring the anchor point even while scrolling) was not added.
The information page has no images because the archived copy is an access-blocked screen, so a four-cell list was built in the card type of the first page’s Information section (judgment call).

The original journal/category/feature share the same shape as journal, so they were not built separately. The search panel opens like the original, with a white left column (input field · keyword chips) + a black keyword band on the right while the logo folds, but no real search happens (it sends to journal.html).

Fonts: neue-haas-grotesk-display and a Japanese gothic face are paid, so Inter Tight + Pretendard. Cover colors that differ per article and keyword were made as --site-* by rotating the hue from the accent color.
Logo, social icons, textbook covers and portraits are placeholders. The three-semicircle logo table is redrawn in the same shape with CSS and SVG.

notes: The original is a single-page SvelteKit app, so the new page rises over the old screen in .75s. Here, split across multiple documents, a cross-document View Transition (.75s · power1.inOut curve) produces the same overlap, and the original’s Preload on hover (preload-data=hover) is moved to speculation rules prerender (eagerness moderate) so a click swaps the page instantly. The cross-document view transition opt-in (@view-transition) goes in an inline style in each page’s head. If it lives only in the external css, Chrome (default with RenderDocument on) skips the transition on documents that have body scripts, and the change cuts abruptly (confirmed by adding ingredients one at a time to an empty document and bisecting). Only when going to the first page does the curtain cover the screen as in the original, then lift .75s after a .25s delay from the click. title: Gaming space intro with glitchy 3D button-glyph background and blinking bitmap title
good_for: One-page intros for game cafes, esports spaces, creator lounges and clubs that sell atmosphere with raw colors and huge type.

A 3D button glyph with a glitch effect sits in the background

notes: The original is a single page (pages: [] in pages.json) — there are no subpages. Only the phone hero is a WebGL triangle-shard slide (two images, 1.5s linear, starting after 3s and resting 4.5s), while on PC one large photo carries the slogan over it.

The background 3D is not a copy of the original model (nine gamepad button glyphs in all.glb: ring·A·B·O·+·□·△·X·Y). It is rebuilt with our own extruded Shapes of the same size (base .5~.6, thickness .04) and silhouette. The ten photo textures are striped canvas placeholders painted in clothing colors. Layout, camera (45°, z 200), flow (PC 5000 × progress, phone 4000) and glitch values are the same as the original.

The glitch is the original’s modified GlitchPass (while on, amount rand/10 every frame, PC distortion_x ±10 · seed_x ±.5, phone both axes), reproduced with our own code pushing the same values over the three 0.114 example DigitalGlitch shader + ShaderPass.

Smooth scrolling was rewritten with the same numbers as the original’s own code (page fixed + translate3d, 20% of the remaining distance each frame, normal scroll on phones) — it is not a library. The 1s scroll curve for menu presses is hidden inside the original P.to, so power3.inOut is used (estimate).

Slogan · section titles must blink in Press Start 2P bitmap letters, so they use English uppercase placeholders instead of Korean (WRITE A BOLD / SLOGAN HERE / LINES.). The lead is English for EN and a Korean placeholder for JA · ZH · KO (Skin’s Noto Sans KR instead of Noto Sans JP · SC).

The lock character, stickers and greeting card face icon were redrawn as our own SVG of the same position and size. The frame gradient (original frame_pc.png 50×1946 and phone frame_sp.png repeated vertically) repeats a magenta→purple→navy gradient made from the accent color at the same height — the seam shape of the original image is unknown, so it is symmetric (estimate).

The circular photo band (a ring that flows with scroll direction and acceleration and follows when dragged) and the weight breathing (FOLLOW) exist only in this site’s code. No ready-made part does the same job, so none was extracted (next person’s task).

The copy also moves to the next HTML at that moment, and the arriving page appears right away without a plate. The loader appears only when Home is first opened (once per session) — the original also shows the loader only when the first-page app first appears, and entering a subpage directly shows the entrance without a loader.
