title: Mac app waitlist with sunset desert frame, cursor-smeared logo and rotating 3D app window
good_for: Pre-launch waitlist pages for desktop apps, design tools and developer tools, with a product intro voiced by the maker.

pages.use: Product landing page — sunset desert frame, line logo that smears under the cursor, big marquee, a letter and three numbers, 3D stage where two app windows turn around, clock checklist that spins with scroll, demo where the cursor clicks to choose, feature cards, black manifesto panel, growing scroll film, makers, night desert waitlist footer

A guide article — a 720px single-column article with a short answer box, six numbered methods (the last in a dark panel), a comparison table, a step list, tips, Q&A, and a dark waitlist panel. For product blogs, guides and comparison posts

title: Forest lodging with four-corner orange frame and fixed island photo
good_for: Homepages for private-villa lodgings, guesthouses, inns and small hotels, and photo-led travel or regional introductions.

pages.use: Lodging home page — hero with difference frames at four corners and a single center photo, poem-like intro, endless slider of 3 rooms, staggered sauna and garden, dining, a pinned island photo poem where the frame lifts away, map, FAQ. For lodging and destination landing pages.

Stay intro — large bouncing-letter title and pen-drawn illustrations (sailboat, house, people), two-column intro text, 12 landscape photos stacked vertically, closing words, three-column credits of collaborators. For brand stories and area introductions

Rooms About — 29% cell title + two-photo head, per room type a photo slider and large italic name (staggered left and right), vertical decorative photo, three-cell amenities list. For room and product type About pages.

Facility About (sauna and garden) — title header beside a screen-height vertical photo, a photo pair with short text, two photos of different heights staggered, a garden where a difference-blend title settles onto the photo, two stacked photos and a facility list. For amenities or experience introductions

notes: The section titles in the original are hand-drawn SVG logotypes (serif with a different baseline per letter), so English placeholder letters are set with varied height and size per letter instead — the letterforms are not as hand-crafted as the original
The logo is a placeholder that scatters seven English lowercase letters (example) in the same layout as the original’s scattered seven-letter lowercase monogram

The About page pen drawings were redrawn in the same spots and composition (two sailboats, birds, trees, fence, four people in front of a house, bushes) but have fewer lines than the original, and the people and boats are simpler.
The map is an SVG fake map drawn in the same tone (monochrome + orange color-burn) instead of a map embed — no drag or zoom

The original has no page-transition effect (the page simply reloads and only the header fades in over 2s), and the copy does the same. The loader is an orange curtain present in the first page HTML from the start, and it follows the original’s two clocks. On a first visit the curtain lifts over .8s (swing) 3 seconds after the DOM is ready, and the header and first photo turn on 3 seconds of separate loading + 1 second later. On a return visit the curtain is removed immediately. The logo on the curtain is a graphic (SVG) like the original, so it does not change when the web font arrives late. It is a placeholder drawing the seven scattered letter positions as boxes.
The FAQ, terms of use and reservation pages that weren’t recorded were not built — the menu’s Questions goes to the home Questions section, and terms and reservation are set to #
The 4th scene of the island photos (original bg4) could not be confirmed in the screen recording, so the label was guessed as night village lights to fit the poem
Logo, photos and text are all placeholders

Skin: the photo slot fills (--wf-fill, line, ink), the tones of the four island photos and the fake map fill are built with oklch relative expressions of --kf-bg so that the original values come out unchanged under this skin (shared.css :root, index.css). The Korean body font is --kf-font-kr in theme.css (Gowun Dodum), used as var(--kf-font-kr, var(--kf-font-sans)). Body width is --site-container and --site-container-sm. Before and after the skin cleanup, four pages × 1440 and 390 were captured in full and the pixels were confirmed identical.

Font backfill: every place that was English in the original — frame, menu, booking, burger (menu/CLOSE), phone menu, and the whole footer, the six section titles and page title, small titles, room names, list titles, English subtitles and descriptions, buttons (View more), question categories, the 「」 subheads at the start of meal body copy, the About big title, subtitle, and the credits header — was swapped for an English placeholder. The latin-slots regex can’t see data-letter (titles that JS splits into letters) or the common markup in shared.js, so Korean inside the computed fonts (Sorts Mill Goudy·Instrument Sans·Playfair Display) was swept with a browser to find those too.

Section names are set as Works·Works & Notes·Journal·Place Name·Location·FAQ without carrying over the original words — the room page title matches 01, the facilities page title matches 02, and the large phone menu text is the same as the section title. The booking button must stay on one line in a 140px cell (90px on phone) and fit inside the underline, so it is Book Here (31px to 131px) — Book a Stay (142px) wrapped to two lines and Reservation (145px) ran 5px past the underline

Body copy on index·about·product·service (intro poem, rooms, sauna, garden, meals, facilities text), six poem lines over the island photo, directions address·parking notes, five Q&A pairs, room amenities list, facilities list, seven credit slots, footer postal address — the original is Japanese text, kept in Korean. Sorts Mill Goudy has no Korean glyphs, so it is drawn in Gowun Dodum, which theme.css loads (in the place of the original Zen Kaku Gothic New)

About body three 「」 subheadings · home page sauna body 「」 subheading — the original has Japanese subheadings (in the form of “A sketch of memory drawn by island and garden”), Korean kept. Only the meal body has an English subheading in the original, so it was switched to English

title: Charter flight booking with a white wall opening hero and stair-stacked steps
good_for: Service homes with search or booking at the top, travel and mobility landings, and company sites with blog, about and recruiting.

pages.use: Service home — a 300vh video hero where a white wall opens a vertical gap and slips away, four steps stacking like stairs, a drag-to-flip quote table card, a blank bridge table (brightens in the reasons section), a photo card following the cursor, reviews, subscription, news. For a booking service landing with search attached to the header
News list — big title · category and tag pills · two large posts (photo | text) · small post grid · subscribe card. For blog and magazine lists

About — header, big statement, two-column company intro, serif story over a large rounded photo, and testimonials, where a rounded light panel slides up over a photo pinned to the screen. For an About page
Careers — big serif title with cabin photo, section nav stuck on the left, reason rows, four job cards, hiring steps, application form over a dark band. For careers pages
Single article — long guide text in a narrow centered column (subheads, photos, lists), a guide box linking to search, and three related articles. For blog posts and guide details

notes: The header search row’s departure and arrival cells open only a placeholder list and a calendar shape instead of airport search results · date picking (the original uses an API search). The open and close motion (curtain .35s · panel −6px .05s later cubic-bezier(.25,.1,.25,1)) uses original values.

The search drawer only goes up to the step-1 field shapes — steps 2·3 of the original (aircraft · summary) and the actual submit are product features, so they were not built. Opening is from 28px above, .75s ease as in the original

The Ask window has only the greeting, sample questions and input field shape. The original voice, chat and search filling are product features. The opening motion uses original values (pill-position clip inset(580px 0 0 100px round 30px) · position (92,571) → in place .6s cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1), ring 3.4→1.08x).
The quote table carousel reworks the original framer-motion drag into pointer drag (not the library) — drag inertia is shorter than the original, and switching currency only changes the pill state

The Reason section cursor photo card size (17rem · 3:4 portrait) could not be measured in the original (the original card is not drawn headless), so it is estimated from the screen — follow, tilt and swap values were read from the original bundle

Page transitions open a fresh document rather than swapping only the body, like the original (next-transition-router) — three panels cover (.8s, staggered .1s) and are peeled back in reverse on the arriving page, same as the original. Arriving from within the same site also skips the hero white wall, as in the original (from-internal-nav)
Fonts: neue-haas-grotesk (paid) → Inter Tight, benton-modern-display (paid) → Instrument Serif. Stroke contrast of the large serif titles is weaker than the original
Of the 5 recorded subpages, 4 and 5 (the empty-bridge article and the masters article) share one article frame, so they are built as a single article.html

title: Black web design studio with work screens spiraling upward
good_for: Web design and development studios and small agencies needing a work spiral, service grid, pricing, process, testimonials and FAQ as one set.

pages.use: Home — light-beam header and editor laptop (tilts back, then stands up), about · logos · collage flowing sideways, work screen spiral (WebGL), service grid, band, three prices, six work-method panels (second-hand clock), numbers · reviews · dot globe, questions
About the company — two big words and a glowing table, two intro paragraphs, a row of award badges, thinkers and makers, five values alternating along the branches of a vertical line
Work list — big two-word header, category buttons, three-part card grid of capture · name · category · ”View site”. Slot for portfolio and case lists
Service list — blue-tinted header, three blue panel picture cards (name, description, ”Learn more”). For business or service introductions
Blog list — big two-word header, category buttons, three-column post cards of cover, title, date and reading time. For News and post list spots
Single work case — name, overview · buttons, four-cell info, capture strip, three cells of role · approach · result, work story with side column, three other works. For case detail pages

notes: The coil-helix-cards spiral is rebuilt in our shader, keeping the original cylinder pieces, 14 slots, 1.5 turns, camera and follow values as they are. The slot gap height (.62) could not be read from the bundle, so it was tuned by eye (guess). The gradient shader behind the original (light rays and cursor ripples) started as a CSS radial gradient and was moved into our shader field.js during the cursor backfill (11-10) (see the cursor reaction line below).
Hero light pillars too: instead of the original gradient shader, four blurred CSS pillars breathe 7px over 7s (original vv-breathe 14px period).

The editor inside the laptop copies only the look and the strip flow (60px per second) of the original’s real-editor imitation (properties panel, work strip: hold to preview, drag to flip, marquee speed control) — the press and drag interactions are not reproduced.

/  The original shader where pressing the CTA makes the screen edges glow blue and the walls close inward (u_hover · u_fire) couldn’t be ported. The page transition uses the original five vertical bands (column-rise-page) values as is.

The dotted globe uses the same cobe (MIT) as the original, loaded as a plain script (cobe.global.js) where only the ESM export at the end of the 2.0.1 build was changed to window.createGlobe, so it runs even when opened via file://. The original’s marker and arc settings couldn’t be read, so markers are left out.

Fonts: GT Walsheim is paid, so the closest free geometric sans, Figtree, is used. Italic serif words use Fraunces like the original, and body text uses Geist like the original. Korean uses Pretendard and Gowun Batang. Light panels get a sun/moon button like the original, with theme.css [data-theme=Turn on light].

Subpage card images are all photo slots (data-label), so they are gray placeholders. Blog category buttons only change their selected look (the original post categories are not public), only the work list category actually filters.
FAQ rows open and close with details/summary instead of the original accordion (the + rotates 45° in .3s). The original review card pager (02 / 03) is kept to a single card.

Third fix: fixed a motion-part bug (column-rise-page) where the page-turn curtain strip stayed stuck off-screen because GSAP read the translateY(100%) in fx.css as px. The sun/moon button now swaps its background between a black and a white panel like the original, while the handle stays white. 118→102 lines. Still open: loader length (original photo data-reveal 3.2~6.9s), the 684ms stagger of the sun/moon button children, work card / Visit site hover, decline button delay (60ms), and the soft button background end value.

title: 3D experience of decorating and sealing a glass display case, then scrolling through time
good_for: Experience pages that let people hold a brand keepsake, logo or artwork in 3D, such as product teasers, anniversary campaigns and studio experiments.

pages.use: A one-page experience — loader · entrance door (sound on/off), a refractive glass display case that approaches as fog clears (drag to rotate · zoom · floor ring · reflection), a customizing panel (image upload · blob/particles · engraved text · background color · refraction), close the case → turn a clock dial with the wheel to age a thousand years → pull in → seal · opening date and save. For interactive introductions that make a single object the protagonist

notes: The original is a single page (pages: [] in pages.json) — there are no subpages.

The original inner logo is a logo-3d.glb model. I did not use the model. Instead I drew our own shape, a three-peak tube with two arch holes cut through (thickness .25), onto the same 1024² render target so the box refracts it. The engraved text (original ”Brand”, Faculty Glyphic) is ”BRAND” in the same typeface.

The glass refraction shader was newly written our own way, following only the original’s uBevel and uDispersion names and values (1.5 · .8). It reads the render target using face coordinates, a refraction vector and edge curvature, and splits R and B to make a rainbow edge. Unlike the original, it doesn’t truly refract the scene behind the box (inner panel only).

Aging: following the original AGING table (1 hour to 1000 years, dust, blur, flaws), the number of years is interpolated logarithmically and fed into the box shader (frost, dust specks, flaw lines) and the screen grain. The original flaw drawing (Nt: randomly drawing scratches, hairline cracks and deep cracks on a canvas) is reduced to a single shader stripe — the flaw shape is simple.

Absorb: follows the original ABSORB (.15 per hit, fills .3 per second, after a .5s rest drains .25 per second, 2s power2.in). From the original receive (playReceive) — the hand light (a radius-240 spotlight following the cursor) and floor .2 — only the camera pull (×.78, 4s power2.out) and the floor blur were carried over. There is no hand light.

Sound: WebAudio synthesis with the same values as the original (55, 82.5, 110Hz, low-pass 320Hz Q4, .06Hz breathing, 700Hz band noise, a 2kHz tick every second, filter opening with intensity), rewritten in our own code. The original’s range-adjust tick (rangeTick) is not included.
The original’s ‹Enter› under the entrance door goes in with sound on — headless checks were done only with ‹without audio› (the sound could not be checked by ear).

Customize background color: like the original, if the chosen color is bright (luminance above .5) the text flips dark (the :root[data-bright] mode block in theme.css). The chosen color is overridden inline on --kf-bg — even when the skin is swapped, the user’s chosen background wins.

The stage uses, like the original, a 60 field of view·transparent background (page background shows through)·ACES tone mapping. The time-mode camera is tied to the aspect ratio so the clock face takes .72 of the height on wide screens and .66 of the width on portrait screens (ratios measured on the original 1440·390 screens — the original TIME_POSE calculation was not ported). In time mode the box grows 1.35x (judgment).

title: Production house with work slides that change the screen color per section
good_for: Web and print production houses and design studios where work is the star, and portfolios where each project has its own color.

pages.use: Studio first page — three lines of thin serif uppercase declaration (the background cycles through four colors every 60s), ten one-screen work sections (when a section passes the center the whole screen tints to that work’s color and the title letters pop up at random, each section with a different asymmetric grid), a right-side photo circle dot index and up/down buttons. For a studio landing with few works, each shown large

Work list — black header line, work color cards in 3 columns (2 on phone) that rise .25s later per column, a view more line that flows on card hover, and a FILTER panel at bottom right (branch, genre pick, search). For a list that lays out many works distinguished by color.

Company overview — big COMPANY title, a black-and-white map overlapping a charcoal address box, list of representative, founding and business details, SNS account row divided by a top line. For a small company’s company info page

News list — black cards (photo · date · title · long body) stacked in two columns continuing on the shorter side on wide screens, cards float up from 10% below, appended with more. For news · work logs that feel like reposted social posts

Recruit — big RECRUIT title with a band of flowing job names beneath, a black-and-white office photo that sharpens from blur, a table-style job listing numbered 01·02 (sub-items divided by dotted lines · check heads) and a CONTACT link. For job postings with two or three roles

A single work — the whole panel in that work’s color, a big name overlapping the main photo, an overview box whose two corners are bitten by dark ink climbing up (three cells for category · genre · year, client, role, intro in Japanese · English as two columns), vertical photos and videos with a play triangle drawn on hover, and a black strip at the end with dot-circle other works (300px photo circle on hover). In the portfolio work detail

notes: Blog and Contact pages were not recorded, so they were not built — blog and contact in the menu are # placeholders. The original swiper (swiper@7.2.0) is only used in the blog related-posts panel, so it is not included in these six sections

The original typeface Saol Display (paid) is replaced by Cormorant 300 — similar stroke contrast but narrower letters, so big work-name lines run slightly shorter. Body text uses the system gothic (Apple SD Gothic Neo) in place of the original YuGothic (system) — Korean web fonts download glyph pieces late, so for a few seconds after opening the text would change (loader, transition tail) and cause jitter absent from the original, so it was dropped

The Work list has 111 cards like the original (same type, rotating placeholder colors, categories and names). FILTER filters by each card’s data-cat and data-genre (the original uses the first and second tag text)

News ”more” does not fetch from a social feed like the original, but clones the first four cards and appends them. News · recruiting posts match the original document height (±15%) by their placeholder line counts
Company map is a black-and-white photo placeholder instead of a Google Maps embed (no drag or zoom response)

On the first page work section, the baseline for the background color curtain and the text rise is, in the original, 0.5 × screen.height (not the window height) — the card entrance (data-in) uses the same value, but tone-scroll-swap and char-random-rise use 50% of the window height (on a measuring rig where screen.height and window height differ, the start position goes off, see the scroll line)

Waiting — the Mac mini browser slots (3) were shared with other students, so each measurement meant queueing for tens of minutes, and at 01:18 a session restart killed a running measurement once. Time spent building and fixing is within 180 minutes, but it ran over by wall clock

title: Artist management agency with undulating photo columns
good_for: Agency sites for photographers and directors, production or casting companies, and photo-led studio homepages with a news feed.

pages.use: Agency home — below the wordmark, five photo pillars that sway with mouse and wheel (left alone, they sink one by one and the photo changes), a large sentence that scatters and gathers on scroll, a News brick grid, and a Footer where a photo opens over the name

News list — large serif section title above a 3-column brick layout stacked at the original ratio (photo or video tile plus uppercase title, underline on hover). For campaign news and work-log collections

About the company — two big slanted identity lines and three promise sentences by customer type, a contact person’s info sticking and following on the right (photo peek above the email), three-column service list for prep, shoot and post, a standalone photo that picks a new spot each time it opens

Production work list — a right-aligned section name and a 16-cell, 3-column brick wall of brand campaigns. A collection of shoot cases the company made itself (captured as product during recording, but it is a work list).

One campaign: big serif campaign name, half-width intro paragraph, 4-column photo wall (press to enlarge in place to the screen center, ←·→ to page), and a ”Next story” button with a photo window that opens upward

notes: The original news·production grid uses a packing library (GPL·commercial license), so it is not used. VV.pack in shared.js was written anew with the same placement rule (cell 33.333%−10px · gap 10, each cell goes to the topmost slot, if equal the leftmost empty slot, percentPosition). The .8s on re-layout is a CSS transition (left·top).

Video slots (mux-video — Hero pillar second column, some News columns, Footer Artist Name 05 preview) are still placeholders (wf-video). The original’s autoplay and loop with rewind at 10±2s and pause when offscreen were not applied since there is no video file to put in — next person: <video autoplay muted loop playsinline> Switch to this, and add IntersectionObserver (rootMargin 200px) play/pause and timeupdate rewind to shared.js.

Subpages that were not recorded (artists list, artist/director detail, enlarged all grid) were not built — menu Artists links to the first page, All and Production to works.html, and the pillar press and footer name to about.html and index.html respectively.
The news list keeps the first 18 of the original 49 cells (original ratio kept), production has all 16 (original ratio). Shortened because the same shape repeats.
The standalone photo on the About page randomly picks left·center·right and a width of 40~80% each time it opens, like the original — the position differs on every shot.

Font: Garamond Narrow (paid) → Cormorant Garamond 500. It is a bit wider, so the big About sentence overflowed by a line, and the English placeholder was shortened to match the original line counts (identity 2 lines · promise 10 lines). Helvetica Now Display → Inter Tight.
The original’s 12-column dev grid overlay (.c-grid, turned off) was not built.

title: Mockup goods shop with bouncing wordmark loader and pixel-trail cursor
good_for: Shops selling digital goods such as templates, mockups and fonts, small creator-collab brand malls, and product-heavy showcase homepages.

pages.use: Shop home page — first-visit wordmark loader, video hero, pixel-icon titles (cells light up and flicker as a glitch), two drag-to-scroll product rows, two collection panels that widen on hover, a prize card that bounces, gets pulled and drops, a category list where a photo lights up under the cursor, a fixed community panel (news pill and news window at the bottom), a creator pill marquee, a story strip. For the first screen of a digital product shop
Product list — icon title, filter tabs and search field, four-row product grid (hover on the second scene), category list. For the all-products and category list pages

Brand intro — big uppercase heading, a text paragraph that darkens on scroll, founder slider, pixel icon row and flowing band · two paragraphs darkening in turn (news pill at the bottom), a photo frame cropped and rounded by scroll, join-us video, creator pills and application copy·button. For small studio·brand story pages
Collection list. Header with two overlapping photos, live cards laid at a tilt, white panels stacking upward. For bundled products and series intro pages

notes: Community pinned panel: the original WebGL photo-cell columns (top and bottom halves flow in opposite directions, 6 columns on desktop · 4 tablet · 3 phone, cell 4:5 · corner .03, per frame .003 + scroll speed, sin bend) were rebuilt with our own shaders on _vendor ogl@1.0.11. Cell images use a placeholder panel texture instead of the original JSON photos and videos, and the original version number is not left in the bundle, so ogl 1.0.11 was used.
The keen-slider build is 6.8.6 in _vendor (the build number of keen inside the original bundle does not remain as a string)

CTA icon Lottie (c-cta__lottie): the original cta part only finds and stores .c-cta__lottie and plays nothing, and neither that element nor a lottie library exists anywhere in the four pages’ DOM or the bundle — there is no playback behavior to build, so it is left as is. The cookie settings dialog (tarteaucitron) is a third-party service widget, so it is not built
Roobert (paid) was swapped for Figtree 500

Page transition: the original pixel cover was rebuilt. After an inner link is clicked, .1s later 10px cells cover the screen at random over .4s and the page changes, then on the next page they uncover at random over .5s. In the original film the bottom right seems to be covered late, but the bias in cell order could not be measured (guess). The original transition log was accepted because frames cut off mid-cover.

About founders slide rebuilt to the original structure — a section of photo count × 100lvh with a pinned panel. The scroll share (scrub .5) lifts the right-hand photo strip and lights the buttons in turn. Clicking a button scrolls to that person’s slot in 1.2s expo.out (ScrollToPlugin). On hover, a 118px emoji cursor (placeholder) sits at the cursor spot and follows with a .12 lerp. The original’s pixel reveal on photos (data-pixel-reveal mosaic) is not included.

Product offer panel: on index, as in the original, when the header’s bottom edge rises above the bottom of the screen it leaves the group and stays at the lower right of the header (the cookie panel drops 132px). The product offer and lifetime pass panels live only on index, as in the original.

Download window: in the original, the button just before it opens it on account and product pages that were not recorded — the window (key copy shown 1.5s, row delete collapses in .3s, add domain up to 3) and its open and close were built from the original window frame, and the opening button was placed in ”My downloads” inside the cart drawer (guess)

In collections, the tilted live card panel is a section that does not exist in the original’s below-1023 layout (card list right after the header), so it is hidden at that width — the desktop original also had no such section, so it was left as the previous student built it

title: Product intro with a 3D creature that follows the cursor and page-turn sections
good_for: One-page landings for AI or software products, immersive intros with an entrance gate, and product stories that end in a calculator.

pages.use: A single product intro page: loader number and entrance line, a 3D octopus stuck to the screen (two eyes that watch the cursor, wavy legs), four section text panels flowing at 1/3 of the scroll, a drawer, ability rings, an ROI calculator, and a closing button

notes: Octopus position per section: like the original sceneNorm, progress between section anchors (hero · four sections · skills · calculator · closing) is taken evenly 0→1 and joined across eight keypoints with smoothstep. For the light section (the fourth), when its text panel is within ±1 screen of the screen centre, the background and skin flip to lilac

Text panel: exactly the original useFixedFrame — flows at 1/3 of the scroll (LAG 3), skewY ±4° by speed ÷1000 × 1.2, hidden when off-screen, xPercent 10 when the drawer opens. The ability · calculator sections stay at 0 in pin form until the section ends. The original’s bend reduction while pinned (i/50) is not included

Sound: the original ”Enter with sound” plays background music and effects. There are no sound files, so only the button text (Sound On/Off) changes. Language buttons (US·UK·FR) only have shape and expansion, no text change

title: Airy one-page company intro entered through a pink layered ring tunnel
good_for: Small advertising or branding firms and studios needing a one-page site with a philosophy paragraph, five services, company profile and contact.

pages.use: Whitespace-style company one-pager — a pink layered-ring tunnel canvas you press into · a philosophy text band orbiting on the rings · five attached services · work slots · company overview with map · contact card · wordmark footer. For a small ad and branding company home page

notes: The original is a single page (pages: [] in pages.json) so there are no subpages. The menu moves to a section within the same page in 1.5s power3.inOut like the original.

The original 3D is a GLB model (three 0.180.0 — the copy uses the same build) (4 pink tori, 4 text plates, 13 gray tori with baked animation). It was rebuilt with TorusGeometry and PlaneGeometry using the same node positions, sizes, colors (converted linear → sRGB #e681a2 · #d47795 · #b5647e · #99546a · #e7e7e7), camera path (z -40 scrub .5 → y -28 scrub .3, pitch -20°, scene .75 at the last 1/5.5), entrance (back.out(2.5) 1.2s delay .3~.9, text plate .8→1 1.4s delay 1.2~1.5) and magnet wobble (radius 180px, spring .02, damping .82 and the other original constants as they are)

The gray donut’s path and rotation approximate the GLB keyframes (200) with a smoothstep curve and one rotation axis per box — rise height (-22→-2), sideways bend width, size peak, start time and period match, while the flipping angle change differs slightly.

Text band on the ring instead of the original texture image <ol class="w-hero__words"> … words are drawn on the canvas in a circle. The depth, size, rotation direction and 33-second turn of the four plates match the original, and the word positions (radius·angle) are values fitted to the first-screen photo. The two plates spin in opposite directions, so small keywords sometimes overlap (the original overlaps too).

The service illustrations are our own flat SVGs in the same place and ratio (1000×660), in place of the original Lottie (cow, card and phone, orange character, three walking people, monogram). Playback follows the original. Crossing the line at 20% from the bottom of the screen plays the intro set at the original Lottie lengths (cow 1.668s, media .4s, character 2.035s, people 1.969s, monogram 1.702s) with back.out(2.5). When it ends, it moves to the loop set and sways endlessly, fitted exactly to one lap of the original loop lengths (6.507s, 11.478s, 1.969s, 8.442s, 9.409s). lottie-web (original 5.12.2) is not loaded, because our art is SVG rather than Lottie JSON, so lottie would have nothing to read. The individual motions inside the loop set (original keyframes) are sways fitted to our art parts.
The company map (Google Maps embed, grayscale) is left as a .wf-img placeholder. The mail link in the contact card was changed to a same-page anchor.

Fonts: Gen Interface JP Display has no Hangul, so body text uses Noto Sans KR. English headings and wordmark use Poppins, same as the original. The wordmark and logo art are replaced with Poppins text ‹Name&Co.›.
Typing speed follows the original code values, not the card’s 75ms (normal 40ms, hero copy 20/25ms, philosophy copy 90ms · body 22ms).
The original gasp.js error (undefined serviceItems, a console error) was not carried over.

The per-case glow (data-glow — the client brand color) is a value made by rotating only the hue from the skin’s accent color (oklch(from var(--kf-accent) …)), so it changes along with it when the skin is swapped.

Metallic W 3D logo: we do not use the original Engine’s logo model or pose table (per-section x, y, z and angle mixes such as home-np-b, home-awards, proof-title, studio-behind). Instead our ring-plus-lightning-bolt W shape (three r186, PMREM environment reflection) is eased 9% at a time into the center of whichever empty placeholder box, one per section, is closest to the screen center. Hero video box Flip (scrub .25·−5°·mouse 14° (original data-max-rotate)), badge bounce (back.out 2.6·±40°·wobble ±4°) and letter rise (140%·8°·1.15s expo.out .035) use the original values. The badge is our own SVG stamp instead of the original award image.

Service drum: the line shape follows the original sfr (240svh · 3.2 line-heights between lines · dim .32), but the cylinder rotation angle (24° per line) and the tile bounce curve (back.out(1.7) .7s) are values tuned by eye (exact numbers could not be read from the bundle).

The four subpages were matched using the original HTML and page CSS from the archive pages.har.zip and the Engine module values (the previous version could not see this bundle and was built from screenshots). The unfolded layers in Work detail use the original layers module (attach 48×(3.3+1.2×(layer−1))% · scrub .6 · power2.inOut — lying at 52°·−14°·.86 → lifting to 24°·−7°·.9, each layer moving forward one at a time (z 70 · y −24 · x −10), the others .38 darker, text .28↔1 → stacking back again, scene Interaction tilt X±5° · Y±7°), and under 992 it is not attached, like the original. The previous version’s 220% was a value from a different module (explode) on the Service page. The table-of-contents progress line is left as matched by eye.

Testimonial strip: drag plus inertia (speed × 350ms, .9s power3.out), odd/even ±32px stagger, whole-card links (View cursor label) and a video panel (hover makes it stand right away and the poster lifts over .45s). The original’s in-mask playback and infinite repeat clones are left out and the video is a placeholder. Drag grabs the pointer once it moves more than 5px, otherwise the link opens.

The original first-visit white loader (performance clock 2.8s) appears only when the head script runs within 1.1s and did not appear in the original measurement either, so it is not built. The cookie card follows the original condition: it checks every .25s starting 1.5s after script start (after the entrance ends if there is a Hero, otherwise at 7s) and rises from 24px below with .6s expo.out. On closing, the pressed button dips to .95 and bounces back, and the card slides out 16px·.3s power2.in from the click moment and is hidden 283ms after the click (92.6%) (original measurement). A Settings panel (necessary always on · statistics toggle · save) was built.

Button pull and press (original module as-is): buttons, menu button, header Contact and data-magnetic are pulled .2 toward the hand (.6s elastic.out(1,.4)), pressed to .95 (.12s) on press, and bounce back on release with .45s elastic.out(1,.5).

Highlighter (the original marker module as-is): two SVG lines (thickness height/2×1.42, slope min(.05h,3), 18px margin outside the element) draw segments and tips with gradient stops, and the text cover measures progress including the length the stroke sticks out of the element. The start was advanced by half a frame to match the original measurement (.21~.26 already in the first frame). Strokes already drawn are not redrawn.

Speed text (original module as is): menu words·footer big title move their glyphs onto a WebGL canvas when the pointer first moves (DOM text turns transparent), and pixels near the pointer trail (latest 23 points · radius glyph size ×.6) are smeared by speed over 32 overlapped samples, brightening 14% the faster it moves.

Work list card: as in the original, poster 1.04 (1.2s ease-out), video panel .4s ease, four award stamps (.089s stagger, −140° → 0 .88s, .5s on exit), three tags (.067s stagger .2s, border pure white 35% → pure white). Video and stamps are placeholders and CSS stamps.

Post list and end-of-post ”Read more” (original services module as is): row columns (50%−48px)·remainder·48px·top and bottom 3.33rem·title 2.5rem. The photo panel (24.3rem·16:9 screen panel) attaches to the interaction slot inside the list. It is hidden at 8% right·vertically centred·−3°·.95, moves from the first row into the interaction slot and settles with .5s power3.out, with x·y .7s·tilt .8s (side movement ×.4, ±8°). When the row changes only that photo takes .35s, and on leaving it takes .2s. Like the original module it does not run on touch, and at widths 767 and below or on devices without hover the panel is hidden (to prevent horizontal overflow on phones). Highlighter on the round arrow. The big name rows of the work list are a different module so the earlier version (photo following the cursor .45s) is kept. In the free-check box, like the original, a search-result demo (my-site row enters from 18px left and the rank table turns green, AI answer panel, four lines fill up and the sparkle rotates 50°) repeats while on screen, and hovering the check button lifts the third row from .07→1.

Header and menu: chrome W sits in the header logo slot when there is no nearby section marker (original is-docked). While the 3D logo is on, the header 2D mark is hidden (original logo-dock-on) and turns on in .3s when the menu opens — if the 3D logo is sitting in the header, it disappears first in .3s and the 2D mark turns on .05s later. On menu open, the button text color changes .4s late and the header text color .35s late, and after .34s the button highlighter retracts. Menu line blur clears at .74s on the first page and .55s on subpages, as measured on the original. Footer region expand follows the original module (height .45s power3.inOut, close .36s after a .1s delay, one at a time, plus sign mark .45s).

title: Company intro that goes from a pressable pixel logo into a tilted voxel world

notes: The original is a single page (pages: [] in pages.json), so there are no subpages — the four sections after entering (Statement · Legacy · Philosophy · About) live at the same address, so everything is built in one index.html.

WebGL was rebuilt as world.js instead of using the original engine (hand-written gl-matrix + instanced cubes) — same values: cube face brightness .5+.5·dot(face, light), hero light (-1,-2,-10) · world light (1,-10,-3), focus 200 (1px=1px field of view), logo cube 32px (phone 12), press −1 cell (phone −2 cells), flicker 1% per frame · (10+30r)/strength · press strength 10 · −.2 every frame, 100 rolling cubes · 16px (phone 8) · rest 10~100 frames · probability .1 · 10 frames cubic-bezier(0,0,1,.4), entry acceleration .2/frame · bundle fly-up (5-cell and 6-cell targets, beats at 9 and 31 frames) · camera 2.4s cubic-bezier(.5,0,.5,1) with distance 200→1500→5000 · X 45° · Y −10°→0 · Z atan(2w/h) (phone 3w/h) · focus 200→5000 · handed to the second beat at 1680ms, 3× panel height between sections.

The original’s decorative models (doodles.json 7MB, dozens of kinds such as castle, unicorn, lighthouse, dinosaur, ship, tower) are not carried over. Our five basic shapes (tree, flag, lamp, cloud, house) are scattered in the same spots (section-top flag, English title lamp, both sides of the bottom). To use them, add a cell list to MODELS in world.js.

The original pixel logo (№10) and the Japanese text images (texture png) are not used — the logo is ”LOGO” in pixel letters on the same 24×11 cell frame, and text pixels are placeholder text drawn small on a canvas, with a square placed on every lit cell (section title 16px · body 8px · pledge 4px cells, original data-scale unchanged).

English body text, names and section names use the DOM in CSS 3D (matrix3d, like the original = Same matrix as the WebGL camera, perspective = focal point) laid flat on the floor. Since the DOM layer sits above the canvas, text is not covered when a cube passes in front of it.

Sound: the original mp3s (background music, press sound) aren’t used. Only a WebAudio square-wave blip on hand-lift and a three-note rising tone on entry are played. There is no background loop — the sound on/off button stays in the same place.

The light view (original lite view — a flat panel made of SVG drawings) is built as a version that turns off WebGL and stacks the same DOM sections flat. It also shows on devices with reduced motion or no WebGL.

Judgment: the four cube colors are placed on the standard variables --kf-accent (blue), --kf-danger (red), --kf-success (green), and --kf-warning (yellow) — they change together when the skin is swapped.

Decision: the rolling cells on the Hero are, in the original too, flat cells with no visible side faces at front focal length 200, so they are drawn as flat rectangles, and only after entering are they drawn as 3D cubes rolling around an edge axis.

Clinic About: sub-page Hero (title, photo, line), copy with two photos, director greeting (white name band under the photo) and three career cells, About band, three spaces (big photo breaking out of the frame), three equipment cards, next page card. For the About menu slot of clinics and offices

For first-time visitors: three policy cards, first-consultation steps on a pale wave panel, a step list linked by new footprints (two columns, adult · child), and map · directions · four transport options. For usage guide and care-flow pages of clinics, academies and counseling centers.

A single treatment detail — intro and benefits, a navy-blue band with two treatment types (photo, description, three-column highlights), dotted-line price table and payment, process slider (Splide), FAQ. For a page that introduces one treatment, procedure or product in depth

notes: The original’s Hero copy, the #01~#03 numbers, and the vertical and horizontal large text ”Message” and ”Smile in the making” are image files (SVG·PNG), so we re-set them as live text at the same position and size (Zen Kaku Gothic New for copy, Instrument Serif for numbers and decorative text). The number serif is the closest free typeface to the original (a narrow, high-contrast Didone).

The header wave, wave band above sections, wave under Contact, hand-drawn underline, hand-drawn line, two birds, logo mark, medical icon and transit icon are not copied from the original art. They are redrawn as our own SVG in the same position, size and feel. Like the original, the header wave becomes two wide layered waves above 1280 and two small waves below.

The map (embedded map) and the clinic calendar (embedded calendar, two months) are external embeds so they are not included, shared.js draws a still map picture of the same size (blocks · roads · pin) and a 7-column calendar grid (the clinic-day band is a fixed pattern). The clinic-day band color is the accent color instead of the original’s purple.

The original uses jQuery 3.7.1 fadeIn/fadeOut (300ms swing) for the menu overlay, WAAPI 300ms linear for details height, and Splide 4.1.4 (+auto-scroll 0.5.3 · intersection) for three sliders. We load the same builds from _vendor and apply them with the same options. The original site’s own scripts (the custom code in script.js) are not used, and the same behavior was newly written in shared.js.

Decision: in pages.json, new-patients (type page) is a usage guide, so it is named guide.html (type page), and adult_orthodontics (type page) is the detail of one treatment, so it is named service.html (type service). The three treatments in the original menu (adult · child · whitening) share the same form, so they all link to the single service.html.

Text placeholders: the original titles are Japanese, so they are written in Korean here. The English section names (About us·Menu·Greeting·Equipment·Policy·Flow·Access·Price·FAQ·Contact·Calendar) and the large English names in the menu drawer are kept as English placeholders (Outfit), as in the original. Korean runs wider than Japanese, so the About band titles are written short to match the original line counts (3·3·2 lines).
The original first news post is four paragraphs of 381 characters and grows to 589px when opened — the placeholder body uses the same length and paragraph count so the open-close height matches.

The first News post placeholder shows its last two lines on PC only (yo-pc-only) to match the open height of the original (589 at 1440, 626 at 390) — Korean runs wider than Japanese, so the number of wrapped lines differs at each width.

title: Village media with trembling crayon forest art and newspaper-column articles
good_for: Local or town introduction media, reading sites for municipalities and cooperatives, and local media gathering people interviews.

pages.use: Home — loader that draws the logo outline, trembling crayon forest art and vertical-writing intro, 2·4 staggered newspaper-column reads, village intro opened by tab labels (map·flowing photo band) and four forestry goals (line art), news·contact two columns. For the home of a village·regional outlet.
Reading list — speech-bubble intro and an eleven-cell staggered newspaper grid (2·4·4·4), each cell with photo · category pill · title · author face, page-turn pills. For article and interview lists
News list — English and Japanese header between top and bottom rules, narrow date column in the middle | vertical rule | title row. For notice and press lists
One news item — date | title head, two body paragraphs, six vertical page scans, previous·next pills. For press introductions and notice details

notes: The hero crayon forest drawing and the four goals drawings are drawn as two of our own SVG line drawings (with a crayon-grain wobble filter) at the same position and ratio (4:3, 740:540) instead of the original GIF and PNG — the jitter (two sheets alternating every 1s) matches the original GIF, but the drawing density (people, deer, flowers) is sparser than the original
The original body font, a paid Japanese gothic web font, is replaced with the free Zen Kaku Gothic New of similar feel. Latin letters and digits use Roboto, same as the original.
Logo, tab labels and ridge-line footer are newly drawn instead of the original SVG, in the same forms (house shape of two arches, two-peak tab with a dipped middle, 1400:54 jagged ridge)
The village map is a placeholder SVG of a simple outline, dotted lines and village spots instead of the original regional outline drawing
The reading list has eleven cells like the original, but the pagination (1·2) is only a shape and there is no second page
For a single news item, the two originals (news/415 · news/474) share the same form, so only 474, whose print scan has six pages, was built
The loader is applied only on the first page, like the original (the original also applies it when reopening within the same session — session memory was not implemented)
The original site has no page-transition effect (show_duration 0) — the copy uses plain navigation too

Judgment: at recording time the reading list was set as about and news 415 as works, so I checked the pages and fixed them to news (list) and article (single item). The sites pull stopped at a long font response file name (ENAMETOOLONG), so I extracted html, css and js directly from the archived bundle (desktop·pages.har.zip) and read them.

title: Regional design portal with a floating bottom shortcut dock and crossfading hero
good_for: Portals for local governments and public bodies, award or contest sites, promotion sites bundling several programs, and winner or case galleries.

pages.use: Portal home page — a hero with photo and text crossfading inside a rounded panel (progress bar, one-line news ticker), three program section heads with a symbolic icon per program (grand prize big card + award list / pinned left title + two-column cases / three-column cases), magazine cards flowing in two rows, a four-tab report panel with a footer pill, a news row with a pinned title, and a bordered-card footer with a giant flowing wordmark
Newsletter signup — big title and narrow centered guidance text, registration email address in a bordered box. For email signup · simple inquiry guidance
Award gallery — pinned left side panel (year·category picker under the current menu), search box, year headers and 16 three-column vertical cards. For contest winners·work lists.

Road traveled — a side panel + a timeline linked by big years and thin vertical lines (per year a group of arrow links + three photo cells), ending with two cream cards. For business history · past event records
Paired case list: side panel (category picker) + three-column square photo cards (title, company, designer row). For collaboration and matching case lists

Single report — narrow side panel (category pills · share) + two-line title, category, date, tags, large photo, body with three photos, three other reports, back to list. For event reports and news posts

Single award entry — a side panel (search, filter) + award and year tags with the work name, a large square photo, small photos with intro, three line-headed sections (jury comment, details table, where to buy). For presenting one work or product

notes: Swiper build: the original bundle is Swiper 11.1 or later (it has swiperElementNodeName and loopAddBlankSlides), so swiper@11.2.10 from _vendor was used — the exact version number is not written in the bundle.
The search box selectors (year · category · field) and search button are only for looks — in the original it is a server feature that filters the list with a CMS query (?pyear · work-cat)

Cursor sweep: the original hero reaction cell 18.9% (wobbling twice at 23.9·47.8%) is the 5s auto crossfade landing in the sweep window. The original cursor listeners are only Swiper drag (off) and SimpleBar scrollbar drag, so accept

Waiting for browser slots and memory on a small desktop machine (30–60 minutes at a time) ran long, so a little over half the elapsed time was queueing — hand-building and fixing took under 180 minutes

title: Photo shop that opens on one photo and merges CMYK plates into a single image
good_for: Homepages for photo shops, film labs, studios and small workshops with a few services, news, classes and a price list on quiet white panels.

pages.use: Shop home — a four-line square loader, then a single full-bleed photo inside a 4rem margin, a right vertical menu that switches between white text over the photo and ink outside, and one featured article card. For a one-screen home with no scroll.

Service (class) About — vertical title column on the left, a small fixed photo and text beside it while a large vertical photo scrolls past, two class groups on a gray surface (fixed name text, photo, description, news row) and a large-text link. For About pages of a class, course or single service branch

Studio lookbook — under the same header, a 60rem-tall photo strip flows endlessly over 70s, and for each of two shoot bundles a pill button opens a price table panel plus a square photo strip. For photo studios and shoot packages

News list — category pill row (the + pill opens a small sub-category panel) and a three-column grid divided by thin lines (square photo in the middle · title · date · category below · corner arrow cell), page numbers. For shop news · event lists

Single news item — a ”Back to list” link pinned at bottom left that follows you, large thin title, date · category on the left and 70% body on the right (poster photo · paragraph · subheading). For event announcement · notice posts

About the shop — under a vertical title, four CMYK plates gather while pinned to become a full-color photo, six photos scatter past behind pinned text, then it continues into an opposed-stage strip (three photos and text), a vision block and a service list whose photo changes with the mouse. For pages that state the ideas of a shop or brand

notes: The five recorded subpages (workshop·grafto·news·about·a single news article) are all built. The original menu’s Service 1~3 (Development·Presets·RAW), company info, contact, FAQ and photographer map were not recorded, so those menu links point to the nearest pages of ours (service·lookbook·about·article).
Fixed the types in pages.json — workshop is a class introduction, not a product, so it is service, and a news post is an article, not a detail.

The logo (handwriting-style kanji wordmark), class logo and studio logo are drawn lettering, so they are set as text placeholders of the same position and size (Your Brand / Class Name!! / AB / STUDIO).

Hero menu, logo and photographer credit are white text over the photo like the original — the placeholder is light gray so the white text is hard to see. With a photo in place it looks like the original.

The original top-right button’s black version is in theme.css under :root[data-theme=Moved into the dark] block (session memory). If swapped to another skin that has no dark block, the button changes nothing.

The original intro timeline calls an element that does not exist (.news). Nothing moves, but it takes up time, so an empty .6s slot keeps the timing the same. The featured post card stays visible throughout the intro, as in the original.
The photos in the studio photo strip: the original is 60rem tall with a different portrait ratio per photo, so they are mixed as 2:3·3:4·4:5·3:2·1:1 (strip length differs slightly from the original).

Smooth scrolling is the same Lenis 0.2.28 as the original (only the option smooth: true). The npm version needs tiny-emitter and virtual-scroll supplied externally to run, so the official bundled build of the same version (bundled/lenis.js) is placed in _vendor/lenis@0.2.28 (SOURCE.md). ScrollSmoother and swiper listed on the card are not used by the original (swiper only loads its css).

The original counts boxes as content-box — on top of wire.css’s border-box, only the spots that have both width and padding (drawer text column · vertical title · phone tab bar · article body etc.) were reverted to content-box.
The About page is 151px shorter than the original (15857 vs 16008) because of Korean line-count differences, and one post is slightly shorter because of body paragraph line counts.
smart menu · The external links in the Footer (social · store · privacy) are #.

The phone hamburger button (bottom right) is covered by the shared wire.js ‹List · N notes› bar (z 9999), so the interact tool clicks that bar — pressing it directly and capturing opens a dark full menu like the original. It is a shared file, so it was left untouched.

title: Forest campground site with a lifting green curtain, paired photos and a flowing photo band
good_for: Campgrounds, glamping, inns and small lodgings needing a one-page site with paired hero photos, vertical-text intro, activities, plans, prices, site map, nearby spots, FAQ and access.

pages.use: A one-page facility home — a hero where a light green curtain lifts and two photos left and right fill every 6 seconds, vertical-writing About with a flowing photo strip, three staggered enjoy guides with photo and text, three plan cards·usage guide·price table·illustrated layout map, nearby attractions in two rows of four, FAQ accordion, regional map with directions, a Footer with a giant flowing slogan, and a following reservation circle. For campground·lodging landing pages

notes: The two-line outline wordmark ”PLAY THE CAMP!” (Hero, footer flow strip, About logo underline) is SVG drawn lettering in the original, so it has no typeface. The free font Train One, whose strokes are split into two lines, backs it as SVG text (fitted with textLength to the original widths 1108 and 2205). The letter shapes differ from the original’s round geometric font. The phone Hero keeps a separate three-line panel (157×152), like the original

The About body vertical text is a spot where the original PC version placed the text as an SVG image (665×370), so it was rewritten as real vertical text (vertical-rl, about 16px) in a panel of the same size — it is Korean placeholder copy, so line count and height differ a little from the original.

The campsite layout map and the directions area map stand in for the original illustration PNGs — simple SVGs redrawn in the same spot, size and color tone (earth-colored land, water-blue river, dark zones, white pins, white area silhouette, light green circles, dotted lines). Fine details of the original (numbered zones, building drawings, road names) are fewer. On phones the same art is reused in a portrait version (330×816) like the original (<use>)

The background paper grain uses SVG feTurbulence noise to make the same overlay instead of the original noise.png (soft-light .2). The circular text around the reserve circle (original circle-reserve.svg .1) and the RESERVE graphic lettering are done with textPath and plain text

Swiper version: the original bundle has no version string but contains loopFillGroupWithBlank and maxBackfaceHiddenSlides, so it was judged to be 8.x and 8.4.7 was used. Hero, flowing strip, footer slogan and phone spot row settings are exactly as in the original common.js

Button and booking-circle cursor pull puts transform in directly as in the original, with css transition .3s ease following (motion part magnet-pull uses GSAP quickTo with the same values — pull .2 · label 0 · dur .3 · ease 0.25,0.1,0.25,1 · spring none)

Phone (390) document height is slightly shorter than the original — a difference in line count of the Korean placeholders in the vertical About text and plan cells. Section order and structure are the same

The reservation circle hover swaps two layers, dark and lime, with .4s opacity like the original (text color is not changed). The button text is the original a{color:initial} Because it runs from pure black to lime green, --kf-on-accent is set to #000. The arrow is drawn with a border instead of swapping the original image, so it follows the text color

title: Hand-drawn welfare organization site where the logo becomes a green hill
good_for: Welfare, medical and care organizations, local public bodies, and child or senior services that need a warm, friendly tone.

pages.use: Organization Hero page: a loader where the logo blooms into green ground at the bottom of the screen, an endlessly flowing band of masked photos and hand drawings with a vertical title, an intro text that fills line by line, three promise cards that rise tilted and stack up, a green gallery with a facility and service finder, Contact, News, a recruiting card pop, and an outer banner. For welfare and public institution landing pages

Company About: photo header with flowing English lettering, mission and vision (big sentence painted green), three value cards (expand), a green commendation section with a wavy edge, CEO greeting, company info table, history list, and three link cards below. For company and organization About pages
Service list — short intro, then 18 white cards with hand-drawn icons in a two-row grid, plus ‹Other services›. For finder pages of sites with many business or service types

News list — photo header, category pills (All, Notices, Recruiting news), flowing English lettering, three-row grid of news cards with pagination. For notice and blog lists (category-filtered lists share the same type)

Careers: a header where the center interview card flips every 7s, recruiting messages that fill in line by line, click-to-flip code-of-conduct cards, a CEO message, hiring News, green number cards, benefits, training, job tracks and a fixed apply band. For care and service industry career pages.

notes: The hand drawings do not carry over the original illustrations (two or three webp images flipped through). They are redrawn with the line-art generator in shared.js (human body, limb angles, head shapes, mascot, tree, flower, bus and more, 18 kinds, two each) in the same position, size and flip tempo (800·1500·2500·700ms, including the elastic panel). Unlike the original, expressions and props do not vary from person to person. To add more drawings, add a kind to the ILL table

The logo does not use the original mark — two beans of a similar feel (the top is concave below, the bottom concave above) were drawn in a new shape. The intro’s dot→circle→bean morph lengths and curves (.3s power1.in·.5s power4.out·1.1s elastic.out(.8,1)), the text elastic.out(.3,1), the 1.8s power4.inOut where the lower bean becomes ground at 1820/1440 of screen width (phone 540/390) with its top edge 165/1440 from the bottom, and the random breathing after that of 1~4°·.95~1.1x·2~4% width are the original values as they are

On entering a sub-section the transition is built as in the original (base panel rises over 1.2s power3.in after 600ms, green cover .8s power1.in, top edge morph elastic.out(2,.5) 1.8s, clears after 1100ms over .5s circ.out, bottom wave 10x power4.in). On leaving, a new page loads after a .3s background-color curtain (the original also reloads the document for ordinary links). The original’s swup (4.8.2) is used only for the transition from a recruitment interview card to the interview detail. Since the interview detail section was not recorded, swup is not bundled. When building the interview detail, add _vendor/swup@4.8.2 + swup-js-plugin and the transition where the card flies to the screen center and flips (transition.interviewCardOut/In values)

The Recruiting section header is a port of the original recruitHeader: first-appearance opening (the center card shows its back at 2.77x in the middle of the screen with a 1s text fade → both faces rise with .55s power4.out → .8s power3.inOut into place, elastic.out(1,.5) 1.8s to full size → elastic.inOut(.1,1) 1.5s to the front face → side cards come in with elastic.inOut(.3,.9) 2s → the sections below the header float up in .8s), a 7s (6s on phone) auto-advance, and a cursor that follows at 120px (0.1 lerp, only on the right side of the header, folds over links, shows View over the center card, and on press gives an elastic bounce and Next, with the 7s clock shown as an outline). As in the original, the Recruiting section only clears the transition panel at .3s (skipTransition). Drag-to-advance was not built.

Careers section ‹Workplace Scenes›: the photo slider (original keen-slider), the pie chart inside number cards and the line chart are not built, only the number cards are kept. keen-slider is available at _vendor/keen-slider@6.8.6, so just attach baseSlider (perView auto · origin center, blurred bands at both ends) as is

The bean below the first-section gallery (the original bottomSymbol rises by half its height and scales 2.68x with scroll progress p) is wired the same way, but our shape is flatter than the original, so the curve is shallower when it grows
The small hand-drawn illustrations (96px images between letters) inside the big flowing English text of the original page header are removed, leaving only the flowing text

Font backfill: the heading font is Noto Sans KR, so the only Latin-only font is the English label font Inter. Labels the original set in Helvetica (Menu·Scroll·Space·Fact·Life·Facility·Service·Contact·Form·Q&A·News·Recruit·About·Mission·Vision·Value·My Hospitality is·View·Next) were English placeholder copy from the start, so no spot was changed to English.

Phone block ‹Reception hours› (yt-tel__h) on all sections — the original uses the kana ‹Reception hours› (Japanese gothic semibold) with only the times in Helvetica, and the Korean is kept. Only the Korean that fell back to Inter is split into yt-tel__hk and set in Noto Sans KR 600 (13, desktop 16px), while the times stay in Inter.

title: Publisher site with a window-house graphic whose two colors shift by time of day
good_for: Company homepages for small publishers, design firms and bookshops laying out books, works and articles in a bold-lined grid.

pages.use: Company home — a window house at the center of a two-color panel (every 10s the window opens and a cover is carried off by a bird · current-time clock), a book row (square cover + spread flow line + DETAILS·BUY strip), two-column work cards, three-column reading cards, news rows, a big CONTACT strip
About. Half-and-half square panels of intro text and house illustration, two members with face drawings, company info table. The slot for the ABOUT item in the first page’s header menu
Terms guide — below the heading band, three numbered trading methods followed by a long body panel with lists and links. For trade terms and usage guide pages
Full reading list — an endless article list of 3-column cards (photo, name-line marquee, series pill, DETAILS band). It sits in the first page’s ALL MAGAZINES spot
Single news post — breadcrumb row, title band, date row, body panel. News and notice detail reached from the home page TOPIC row

notes: The original picks one of three two-color combinations by the opening hour (morning 6–12 navy·pink, daytime 12–17 brown·yellow, otherwise green·purple). shared.js attaches html[data-time] and blocks in theme.css change --kf-ink·--kf-accent·--kf-line — when you swap the skin, these three blocks must also be replaced with the new skin’s so the time-of-day colors stay alive.

House, bird, mailbox, signboard and member-face illustrations don’t use the original SVGs — new shapes were drawn in the same place, size and two colors. The open-window state was drawn as two shutters swung outward (the shape differs from the original drawing).

The Hero cover fly-out (after 3s · every 10s · 6s linear · window opens for 3s · phone 3s) is extracted as the fly-out-cycle part, and the overflowing title and author line marquee (10s linear) as the overflow-marquee-line part. The site uses both.

The book-spread flow row uses the same slick 1.8.1 (jQuery 3.4.1) and the same settings as the original (autoplaySpeed 0 · speed 5000 · linear · variableWidth). The original’s init step that clones cells to fill gaps when the row is short is not included, since slick’s infinite cloning is enough.
ScrollMagic 2.0.5, TweenMax and lightbox, which the original loads, are not included, since these pages have no targets for them (js-scroll-anim etc.) and so there is no motion

Books were cut from five in the original to three, work cards to four, and reading cards to six (nine on the list page) — repeats of the same type. The recorded fifth subpage (series category list, magazine_type) is an empty list, so it was treated as the same type as list.html and not built separately.

The Latin title font Helvetica Bold (a paid font the original ships as its own file) is replaced by Inter 700, and the Japanese Noto Sans JP by its family sibling Noto Sans KR. Header and menu icons (Font Awesome) are replaced with our own SVG.
The original Hero dot buttons are display only and do not advance when tapped — fly-out-cycle gets tap: 0 to give the same behavior

title: Multi-discipline artist portfolio with cursor photo trail, work tunnel and dropping menu
good_for: Personal portfolios for artists and creators working across illustration, music and photography, with one subpage per discipline.

pages.use: Versatile artist home page — stacking photo loader · dropping menu · cursor photo-trail hero · paper-curl About · 28-work tunnel · standing DJ card · sine-wave photo strip · ASCII footer. For portfolio homes of artists working across several fields
Single-field (illustration) work list — while ten rows of nine works each pass through the screen, width grows from 125% → 500% (phone is a single-row list). For work lists by field
One field (DJ·Video) — photos that open as 9 cells grow in diagonal groups, a video group that loops silently once visible. For music and video work lists
One field (photo) — mood-switch button, four-cell photo grid that grows when a row enters and shrinks when it leaves. For photo work lists

notes: Fonts: the paid wordmark and footer logotype were replaced with Bagel Fat One (Korean included), which has the same plump rounded weight, and the Coolvetica button font with Manrope 700. Bagel Fat One is wider, so the phone hero wordmark was reduced from 19.5vw to 17.5vw.

The footer dot text follows the original formulas as is (cell 11px, glyph 11×12, 10px monospace A~Z, push radius 10 cells·7, press scatters → falls → returns, speech bubble follows at .18·140ms), but it does not use the logo image the original reads (logo3.png). Instead it draws and reads our wordmark text (Bagel Fat One) fitted to the board width, so the dotted shape follows the letterforms. On phones (under 1000px), like the original, a solid text logo replaces the canvas.

The paper curl on the about photo was rewritten with our own shader on three r185 (original values: 30° axis·cylinder radius 1/2π·progress -0.15→1.25·panel twice the size of the photo·paper back side .82~1x lighting). The original edge-shade formula (a shadow that fades by distance from the corner) is not ported, and only a faint shade (max 20%) is placed on the flat photo in front of the curled area.

The three DJ media video slots are YouTube autoplay in the original (muted, looping, plays at 15% visible, stops when out of view). Reuse the same playback behavior <video> Hooked up as such, and the content is an 8-second placeholder video (media/clip-*.mp4) of the same ratio (5:4 · 16:9) — the original video length sits inside a video platform embed, so it could not be measured.

When a DJ card stands up, the original code has a line that changes word color to #57524f, but its target selector is empty (.undefined) so nothing actually changes on screen — the copy doesn’t include it either (same as the original screen).

Loading appears, like the original, only on the first visit to the home page (once per session). Adding ?enter for previews and thumbnails skips it (not in the original). Page transitions hook only between our own .html links, and the arriving page starts covered by a curtain via a one-line script in head.

title: Neighborhood dental clinic with a shrinking round photo panel and stacking green cards
good_for: Dental, dermatology and veterinary clinics wanting a bright, soft tone with treatment menus as cards and an always-visible booking prompt.

pages.use: Dental home page: intro curtain, rounded photo panel overlapped by a big serif logo, greeting over decorative words, about card and photo slider, treatment concern card grid, banner, doctor slider, green news/blog, recruit card, booking cells, and a footer with an hours panel

Treatment list — a grid of worry-sentence cards (mix of small squares and large two-cell ones) with a guide to referring to other clinics and a four-step flow. For service lists of clinics and counseling centers

Hospital About — slogan and vertical photo · text paragraph curtain, representative message, wide photo strip, purpose · vision · mission triangle, six value cards. For organization About and philosophy pages
News list — category tabs (underline) · title rows with date and category attached · circular page numbers. For notice and blog lists
Recruitment — big photo header · greeting · recruitment cards · environment, career and benefits sections (photo + bullet rows alternating). For clinic and small company recruitment pages
Single treatment — photo header · description · target chips · four consultation types · fee box · three-step flow · four phone screens showing how to book. For service detail and usage guides

notes: Paid fonts are replaced by the closest free font: Neue Haas Unica → Inter 500, FOT-NewCezanne Pro → Gowun Dodum, New Baskerville ITC Bold → Libre Baskerville 700, body Noto Sans JP → Noto Sans KR.

The Brand wordmark (four letters on the hero · header · intro · correction banner) is a placeholder set in Libre Baskerville ”Logo” lettering, and the 12 subject-specific illustrations on the treatment cards are unified into this single SVG — a spot to swap in the per-subject illustrations when reusing.

The swiper version could not be read from the bundle (Vue swiper), so swiper@11.2.10 from _vendor was used. The slide options (speed 1500·autoplay 1500·spaceBetween 4·rewind·slidesPerView auto·curve .65,0,.35,1·button 600/300ms) are kept exactly as in the original.

The inside of the expanding menu (.menu) couldn’t be fully read from the bundle, so it is approximated with large menu rows and an address on a green board (entry values from the original .menu v-enter: opacity 0, 10px → in place over .3s cubic-bezier(0,.55,.45,1)).

Pages not captured in the recording — doctor intro, hours/directions, fees, blog, contact, privacy — were not built and their links are left as #. For treatment detail, only the online consultation page is built (other departments of the same type use the same template).

title: One-page cafe site with folder-like stacking section tabs over snowy mountain video
good_for: Cafes, small shops and lodgings presenting story, menu, location and map on a single page.

pages.use: One-page store — a hero split into a left panel and right video, a story paragraph where blur clears over video with a photo collage, a menu list where photos and cards float up on hover, two places with an ultramarine band that draws in, info and a map, and a final line over video. Stacking folder tabs act as the table of contents. For cafes, dessert shops, and small lodgings

notes: The original is a single page (pages: [] in pages.json), so there are no subpages.

Background video as in the original <video> Two videos (16:9 at 641px and wider, 1:1 below that, measured from the original posters 3840×2160 and 1080×1080) are loaded only for the matching width and held paused. They play when the hero video turns on, and run only from the very top through the end of the story while the last line is visible (exactly the original conceptMov ScrollTrigger onEnter/onLeave). The content is a placeholder video in media/ (a 20-second loop of a bright band flowing over a blue-gray panel with a bar filling below). The original kv.mp4 (36.5MB) survives in the archive only as 206 partial responses with no body, and the server blocks ffprobe and headless Chrome requests with 403, so the length could not be measured. The 20 seconds is a guess

The titles, tabs and labels in the original are lettering outlined as SVG in TT Firs Neue (paid). Real text is used instead, in Archivo (width 100, 600), which has the same uppercase glyph width ratio, and --cap (the original SVG glyph height) is converted to font size so the heights match. The hero title shrinks with cqw so that two lines never overflow the plate width — if you enter a line longer than 13 characters, raise the 7.5 in calc.
Japanese body text (Noto Sans JP and a Japanese gothic face) was replaced with Noto Sans KR. At the same letter spacing (.2em), Korean runs a little wider per line than the original.

The logo (character face bars + vertical pixel letters) was replaced with a bundle of rounded bars + a checker-pattern strip SVG (#y-mark). Same position and size (hero 163px, info 160px, loader 162px). The pixel-letter logo in the phone header is left as two lines of text.

Outside links that opened in a new window in the original (menu PDF pill · neighboring shop · map · SNS · hashtag · screensaver see more · operator logo) are # links with data-ext, so clicking leaves the page where it is.

The menu photo·description card slider was switched to Swiper 11.0.5 (_vendor/swiper@11.0.5), the same as the original — the photo slots slide, the cards use fade crossFade · fraction page numbers (01/02) · prev/next (dimmed at the ends), and the two Swipers are linked to each other with controller, observer·observeParents. As in the original, pressing a card button also bubbles up to a list row press.

Recording type detail (tag list) was fixed to news, and page (course) to service.

Header text color is decided as in the original by tracing the background at the point below the header upward, but where the original picked photo sections by class name, this uses data-tone=Switched to dark display
Tables on course pages (tuition, timetable tablepress) and some related links at the bottom were trimmed
Only in the original Fashion Creator Course, the vertical Step timeline (Fashion Project) was included as one section inside course.html — remove it when using the Top Creator type

Font backfill: the original Oranienbaum spots (logo letters · MENU · section English titles · Hero English slogan · course English names · VIEW MORE · CLOSE · Tags:) are English placeholder text from the start. The 66 lines that latin-slots says remain are spots where shared.css and course.css call the mincho font as var(--kf-font-mincho, var(--kf-font-display)) and the regex read the fallback’s title font name as Latin — by computed font they are all Noto Serif KR and Noto Sans KR, and the original also uses Shippori Mincho and Noto Sans JP Japanese slots, so Korean is kept. The fallback is not removed because it is where text lands when another skin has no mincho. Rechecked 11-09 — by computed fonts (including JS-inserted text and ::before/after) on three pages at 1440 and 390, Korean text in the first font Oranienbaum is 0, and the original main.min.css Oranienbaum selectors (logo, MENU, English titles, VIEW MORE and so on) are all English in the copy so there is nothing to change

index loader · header department name · hero h1 · Japanese slogan · nine section subtitles (yf-h2__jp) · two-line course intros (yf-course__text) · special program intro and name (p.text · h3.title) — the original uses kana and kanji in a Mincho face, Korean kept

course header subtitle (yf-ckv__jp) · section subtitle (yf-h2b__jp) · subheading (yf-h3) · field sentences · special program names (p.t) · learning-flow grades and steps (b·span) · fashion project steps · instructor titles and names (card·modal) · other course names. The original is kana·kanji, Hangul kept
