News section subtitle (yf-h1__jp) · header department name — original is kana, Korean kept

title: Public hospital site with white panels over a blue gradient band
good_for: Hospitals, medical centers and public institutions with many departments, news, recruiting and contacts, including home, lists, articles and job detail pages.

pages.use: Hospital front page — blue gradient hero (70vw photo crossfade on the right, white band copy, flowing curves, quick menu), four-way guide cards, news tab panel straddling a blue band, intro slider and directions, department tabs, recruit card fan, pickup and SNS sliders
Recruit listing: job category anchor buttons, document links, two-column postings by category, and a right sidebar that sticks and follows. For institution recruit lists
News list — category pill filter, date, category badge and title rows, round page numbers, yearly sidebar. For organization notice lists

Hospital features — blue band with a photo attached on the right of the header, feature rows with text and photo side by side, two-column list of designations and accreditations, About sidebar. For organization About and strengths pages
Long-form text such as research disclosures: document pages with a collapsible table of contents and long runs of h2, h3 and link lists. For regulations, disclosures, and notices
Job posting detail — one highlighted line and intro, gray-header requirements table, related links, recruit sidebar. For a single posting or requirement

notes: The original smooth-scroll is 16.1.4, but that version isn’t on npm, so 16.1.3 is used with the same settings (speed 100 · speedAsDuration · top offsets 71/58). Swiper 11.1.4 · sticky-sidebar 3.3.1 are the same versions.

jQuery, magnific-popup (video popup), luminous (photo zoom), simplebar (News list scrollbar) and scroll-hint (horizontal scroll hint) are not included — our placeholders have no spot that uses a video window or photo zoom, and the News list keeps the default scrollbar. If someone adds a video card, put magnific-popup in _vendor and open it as an iframe window like the original.
The original SNS slider fills itself with social posts from a server API — ours uses the same Swiper settings with eight square photo placeholders.

The length values of the three flowing curves (2424·1832·2417px) are kept as in the original while the curve shapes were redrawn. Original erase curve "power4.Out" It is not a name in GSAP, so it actually runs as power1.out — written as power1.out to match the visible motion.
The original hero background is a gradient image (bg_kv.jpg) — replaced with a CSS gradient of the same color flow (deep blue→sky→teal).

The five sub-pages are very long document-style text in the original, so all section types (header, sidebar, list, table, table of contents) are kept but the line count is reduced. The original sidebar’s 2- and 3-level expandable lists are flattened to one level.

In the original the quick menu sits inside the Hero and sticks once you scroll past, but ours is stuck at the bottom right of the screen from the start, and only the open/close rules (open at top · fold below 200px in .8s) follow the original.

The original button text and border are #000, but the rule is to use only skin variables for color, so shared.css derives --site-black: oklch(from var(--kf-ink) 0 0 h). When mixed with white it blends in OKLab, so the fade-out curve differs slightly.

Font backfill: the places where the original used a Latin title font (Roboto) — section names NEWS · ABOUT · DEPARTMENT · RECRUIT, the English line in subpage headers, the English organization name in the header, and the digits for dates · phone · page numbers — were English/numeric placeholders from the start, so 0 places were swapped

Index hero big copy, white banner notice copy, About/Careers subheadings, and large subpage titles — the original uses Japanese headings (Noto Sans JP 700~900), Korean kept. The matching Noto Sans KR 400·500·700·900 is loaded in theme.css so the weights line up.

News tab ALL, footer TEL/FAX and footer menu HOME are Latin in the original too but set in the body type (Noto Sans JP), so the Korean slot text is kept — Korean falls to the same family Noto Sans KR, so the feel does not change

The hero rotation’s kv-rattle isn’t included because all its rotation values are 0 in the original. On phones the original groups some of the entry order differently, but the same timeline as PC is used.

News cards advance every 5s in .6s cubic-bezier(.58,.21,.41,.96). The photo strip (right) and text strip (left) move 60px per second. Menu wave gap 8 to 2px in .3s. Drawer (backdrop .4s, panel opacity plus translate -300px in .3s delayed .2s). The four hero items get their pre-appear state (fx-studio-appear-wait) in the markup up front — if it is added when the part attaches, the first paint is already the end value and there is no transition (confirmed by measuring).

notes: Since the card is auto, the breakdown cells (name, seven layout axes, motion, key scene) are filled with the original code and screens.

All three recorded subpages are built. They were fixed by checking type in pages.json: /work (work intro index) stays about, while /work/hire (job detail) was set to works but is a single page explaining roles rather than a case list, so it uses service.html (type service). The column, interview, company info, guidelines and apply pages were not recorded and were not built. Their links point to in-page spots in our page (#column · #interview · #company · #guidelines · #entry).

Swiper is the same 8.4.3 as the original, newly added to _vendor (npm build, MIT LICENSE). GSAP uses the 3.14 in _shared, since the APIs used (fromTo, timeline, ScrollTrigger) are the same as in the original 3.9.1. The original jQuery is not used, and the same behaviors (header bar 300px, banner, drawer) are written in vanilla JS.

Ribbon · logo · large mark art · icons do not use the original SVGs or art but were redrawn as our own SVG — the ribbon is a gray gradient band + a blue band in two layers, the logo is a diagonal monogram + BRAND. They do not match the original ribbon curve exactly (position · size · opening motion are the same). The ribbon behind the support box is laid as light gray over dark ink, as in the original.

The concave curve images at section corners in the original (work_top_curve etc. png) were carried over only as rounded corners (border-radius 100px) — no concave piece that interlocks with the neighboring section.

Fonts: Special Gothic Expanded One (free, same as the original), and body text Noto Sans JP → Korean edition Noto Sans KR. English titles (News · Work · Column · Interview Movie · Company · Guidelines · Entry · Reservation) are common section names, so they stay in English. The hero English slogan The era of hire cars has arrived. became The age of new rides has arrived. with the same line breaks, and company and logo names were changed to BRAND.
The loading curtain runs only once per tab like the original (sessionStorage key zm-access) — open a new tab to see it again. With reduced motion it skips the curtain.
The play circle on interview cards is a link to the interview page, not a video window, in the original too, so it is kept as a same-place link (no video playback behavior).

The first-page loading overlay part (logo blur → sharp, letters vanish 15x) was not extracted separately — a similar logo-blur-loader exists and adding it as an option there is the right way, but there was no time this session. A task for the next person to pick up.

title: Wordmark curtain reveal for an outdoor brand store
good_for: Product brand homepages and online store front pages, plus careers, usage guides and news article pages.

pages.use: Brand shop home page. A wordmark loader over a black sheet lifts to reveal a full-width wordmark and a large landscape photo. Then a two-column intro, a drag-to-slide new product row (white circle cursor), three feature rows that are half photo and half product, the total product count, a concept sentence filling up over gray, three news rows, and a large footer photo.

Careers first page — big English title, one paragraph of mission, an office photo strip flowing over 68s, a job list beside a sticky JOB label (underline and arrow pill on hover). For a company’s careers entrance
Usage guide: section names pinned on the left, a long terms-style body on the right with titles, subtitles and bullet lists. For shopping guide, shipping, returns and terms pages

Single News post — heading, category, date and share buttons stuck to the left, featured image plus body and inline images on the right, two previous and next post cells below, and a back-to-list link. For event notices and announcements

Single job posting — job title and date pinned on the left, on the right underlined subheadings and body for each item (duties, requirements, how to apply), black apply button at the bottom. For a job detail.

notes: Fonts: original headings Graphik (paid) → closest free Inter Tight, menu/labels Satoshi (free, so the same), body Noto Sans JP → paired Korean Noto Sans KR. The hero and footer wordmarks are SVGs drawn letter by letter in the original, so shared.js draws them with the same cell structure (letter cell height 20.2rem, footer 17.6rem, fitted exactly to line width) using the glyph ink boxes of the skin’s heading font — placeholder WORDMARK and ©WORDMARK (8 and 9 cells in the original)

Loader (wordmark-curtain-loader part): original values as they are (1.2s wait → letters .06s stagger .7s power3.out → two wordmarks 1s power2.inOut · black curtain .25s later .8s · white plate .4s later .9s · first photo 1.7→1 .4s later 1.4s power2.out, skipped from the second time in the same tab, sessionStorage isLoaded)

Two videos (vertical window 360:445 · 8s below the first photo, small concept window 285:350 · 10s) are placeholder videos of the same ratio and length (media/mv.mp4 · concept.mp4, baked with ffmpeg) and, like the original, play when in view, pause when out of view and rewind to the start

The original cart is an e-commerce platform app, so the drawer only has the empty state. The variant picker window, back-in-stock window and product filter window (part of the product list and detail pages) are not in the recorded pages, so they were not built. The PRODUCTS sub-panel of the menu drawer (.5s power2.inOut side slide) was built.

Page transition: same as the original, a plain navigation (on click, is-leaving fades body and footer out in .35s, navigation happens after 15ms, and the new page adds is-visible on DOMContentLoaded with a .1s delay over .7s). Menu links to unrecorded pages such as product list, stores and login are left as #

Next steps for whoever continues: the side-by-side phone (390) comparison and hover capture for the shopping guide, news posts and job detail were done only for the first page because browser slots ran short (the first-page 390 comparison matches the original in order and proportion)

title: Spinning logo ring B2B product site with pill-header mega menu and cover footer
good_for: B2B SaaS product homepages, landing pages comparing three products on fixed panels, industry solution pages and gated guide download articles.

pages.use: Product first page: video header with chips that change every 4.5s, three layers of logo tile rings turning on scroll, a fixed panel of three products whose text changes with role chips, customer stories, a row of number cards, an event band, FAQ, an insight row, role and industry pills, and a closing footer. For the B2B product home page.
Company about — video header, centered intro text, logo ring, four stacking value cards with a left table of contents attached, team quote card row, news row. For company and team about pages

Industry solution — centered headline, wide photo panel, logo wall that swaps one cell at a time, use-case chips, four icon features, stacked cards with a table of contents, story rows, FAQ. For industry or customer-segment solution pages

Resource or News single entry — left-aligned title with download and share buttons, wide cover photo, body next to category chips, download form card, related insights row. For a whitepaper or guide download post, or a single notice

notes: product-overview in the recording list is redirected by the original to the home page and has no separate document, so it was not built — the archived height is also the same as the home page
The two posts (guide and notice) share the same type, so they are built with one article.html — the notice post just lacks the download form card

The art in the three product panels is UI screenshots in the original (video depending on the product), so screen shapes (video call · coaching plan · agent flow) are drawn in HTML in the same spot — if there is a video as in the original, it goes inside the panel <video> Add it and it changes with the same .6s stagger
The Webflow IX3 curve for the footer CTA has no name in the bundle (tt:2), so it is set to the GSAP default (power1.out) .8s
The original pulls ring logo tiles at random each time it opens, but the copy and parts pull them in a fixed order (only so the same image never neighbors itself)
The marketing tool’s cookie window, form submission, bot check and chat are not included. The newsletter and download forms don’t send.
View Transition page change (.4s off → .4s on, header stays in place) only applies on same-origin http — opened via file:// it is usually a plain page change

title: Stickers wrapping a bumpy cylinder in an exhibition site
good_for: Small sites for exhibitions, festivals or design events presenting artists, schedule and venue, with giant lowercase headings and WebGL stickers as the focus.

pages.use: First page — a huge wordmark (pill outline) fixed to the screen, with exhibition slogan stickers wrapped around a cylinder that spin past over 6 screens of scrolling. For an event or exhibition hero

One exhibition detail — big two-line title, intro list, body, participating-artist pill links, then per artist a name sticker and portrait wrap around a cylinder and pass over a section stuck to the screen. For exhibition·project details

Schedule — under a big title, three columns (opening day · closing day · opening hours) with a date sticker passing over, and for each event a small title, two-line list and description. For event schedules and program tables
Place — city name sticker over the big title, address and directions link, and a place abbreviation sticker over the place intro and SNS links. For directions and place info

Organization About — name title, intro body, people accordion, three columns (identity, purpose, audience), and above three columns of sponsor and partner logos, partner name stickers. For group and host intros
Legal notice — address, contact, cookies, limitation of liability and copyright text in one block. For the footer’s legal notice slot

notes: Sticker art (the original artist-name SVG and portrait photos) is redrawn on canvas as color blobs plus placeholder English words, and photos are replaced by gray panels with labels — what each photo is noted in the data-config label and in the slot’s data-label. Photos keep the original ratios (2.162, 1.372, 1.345, 1.028, 1.063).
Exhibition page artist sections were cut from seven originals to two (body→link, link→body types), and the About page people accordion is kept at five.
Font: Clash Display (free) is loaded directly from an https address — the API’s //cdn address does not load on file://. Korean body text uses Pretendard.

title: Dark instrument-panel HUD scroll for a defense drone product page
good_for: Long-scroll product pages for hardware, defense, aerospace or robotics that present specs and scenes, such as launch pages or technology overviews.

pages.use: Product first page: a loader where an orange dot grows into a plate → first sequence screen, a decoding status line and a big title → five gauge stages (circular gauge with counting numbers) → one threat sentence over a backplate that opens as a circle → big rolling numbers → video scrub and feature cards → five numbered cards (HUD over orange monotone photos) → cost bar comparison → a spec photo growing to fill the screen with two big numbers → six auto-advancing system cells → a closing section with a flowing text column → big wordmark footer

Page not found (404) — inside the same four-corner frame as the loader, a big error word offset like tape and a signal band, with a link back to the start. For product site 404 and under-maintenance screens

notes: The original’s image sequences (hero 149 frames · flyby about 340 frames), two scroll videos, and loop video do not use the original assets. With the same frame counts and the same playback behavior (first half auto 2s → progress .09~.17 scroll, loop playback starts at progress .175, scrub 0→8s in .04s steps during .23~.77), our placeholder scene (light beam · pillar · aircraft silhouette) is drawn on a canvas (shared.js zkPaint). To use real sequences or videos, just draw those frames on the same canvas.

The five gauges (original Webflow Lottie ×5, 640×640·300 frames·60fps) were redrawn as SVG gauges in the same position and the same frame ranges (e.g. the number layer changes at frames 45→162) instead of using lottie-web — dotted circle · orange arc · number · unit · tag. The fifth (target tracking) is an aiming square and three drifting dots.

The Webflow IX2 scroll effects (hero step-change spot, threat sentence lines entering, number section opacity, video section card swap, five numbered cards changing, spec photo growing, system panel appearing) were approximated by comparing the original screen at the same scroll positions (jump capture) rather than unpacking the IX2 data. Motion built in inline scripts (loader, sequence, text flicker, decode, bar curtain, number roll, video scrub, system auto-advance, text column speed change, cursor, footer glow) uses the original values as they are.

The number roll has both a scrub version in the original (s12: Section 55%→65%, scrub 1) and an Observer gesture version (s15: advances state with 1.05s expo.out). The gesture version hijacks the wheel and blocks scrolling, so only the scrub version was built.

The text columns on both sides of the closing section (80s marquee + speed scaling with scroll speed) are similar in character to the existing part velocity-reel, but the speed-scaling form (1 + speed×2.5, max 6x, direction flip, follows by .08) differs, so it is kept as site code rather than a part option.

Fonts are the same free ones as the original (Inter opsz 32 in place of Inter Display, Geist Mono). The wordmark uses a three-letter English placeholder ORB instead of the original logo, plus our own drawn three-letter line lettering (footer).

title: Dish photos stacking one by one for a fine dining restaurant site
good_for: Homepages for restaurants, fine dining, omakase or bars that speak through photography, covering course prices, opening info, news and reservations.

pages.use: Restaurant first page — two full-screen dish photos stacking in place with a fixed wordmark, photo plus text bleeding off the edge, staggered chef, a photo group covering in, overlapping shop cards, fixed photo window, hours and map, visit info and news, reservation window. For a restaurant home

Course menu: a round window in the center opens to full screen while pinned, then lunch and dinner course names and prices, a drinks intro, a notice box and seven dish photos cover one after another. For a restaurant’s course and price page
News post — below a wordmark box, the date, title, wide line-spacing body and back link, followed by a gray-cell full News list. For shop notices, closures and event announcements

Job info — blue ENTRY · orange band · tab header and a white box over a hatched background (open role · location · qualifications · hours · pay · benefits · how to apply), apply button. For shop staff recruiting pages

notes: The two News items (news/175 and news/172) are article pages of the same shape, so they were built as one article.html. During recording news/175 was captured as about, but it is actually a News article, so it was fixed to article. The menu page is a course and price list, so it was left as product.

The Careers page uses a different recruiting frame from the restaurant site in the original too (separate CSS, header and footer), so it was built in that frame without the shared menu and Footer. Lenis is not applied, as in the original. Same-page anchors were rewritten with the same steps as the original SmoothScroll V2: every 10ms, 1/20 of the remaining distance + 1px. The grain pattern artwork (bands and backgrounds) was redrawn with repeating gradient hatching.

BRAND (nav and reservation English typeface) is free but has no web font distribution, so it was replaced with Noto Sans KR. Body Noto Serif JP is a Korean slot, so it became Noto Serif KR. Band labels and button text use system Times New Roman like the original.
The logo is replaced with justified ‹L O G O T Y P E› lettering inside a black box. The sister-shop logos in the news cards are wf-logo placeholders.

The original map is a grayscale embedded web map. Here it is redrawn in SVG with slanted roads and pins at the same ratio (2.495:1, phone 750:460), and the colors follow the skin via --site-map-*. To swap in a real map, put an iframe inside .z-map with filter: grayscale(1).

jQuery is not loaded — the header class (scroll threshold) and phone drawer slideToggle (.4s swing) that the original does with jQuery use the same threshold and the same Curve (swing = 0.5 − cos(πp)/2 = GSAP sine.inOut), so it was moved to ScrollTrigger pass-through and GSAP height .4s.

The original’s outside links (reservation site, social media, English page, sister shop) were changed to same-page anchors or #. Nav MENU 2~4 (Chef, Space, Sustainability) are unrecorded pages, so they link to the matching sections on the first page.

For the next person: tablets at 1025px and below switch to a drawer header like the original, but type and spacing were only scaled with --u (1024 basis) without porting the 1024 design values separately (129 in the original style.css max-width:1025px block) — only 1440 and 390 were checked against the original.

The photo group scrub (start 70% 0%·end 100% 90%·scrub 1.75) and the circle window (a clip-path circle crops the position: fixed photo) keep the original values and method — even the end coming before the start, so it flips all at once at the 70% point. Under reduced motion the circle stays at its initial size (46.2vh).

For data and SaaS product landing pages.

About the company — fixed video card (lightbox), mission statement, value fade slider, executives in a four-per-row grid, investor strip, principles paragraph that darkens on scroll, photo invitation. For company About and team About

Recruit — photo header, intro that darkens on scroll, photo strip, department job board (filter), big slogan band, colleague quote slider, life slider, teal benefits grid and application invitation. For recruiting pages

A single post — back · category · author line, two-line title, left cover image, one-column body (key summary · subheadings · lists · quotes), related reading, News strip below. For blog post and press release detail pages.

notes: Hero background: the original dotted-net photo (hero_img) is redrawn as a static canvas image (scattered square dots on the right + short connecting lines)

The big menu panel’s content (the original’s list and recommended card layout) was simplified to four cells (three lists + a recommended card). Open/close and neighbour-item swap values (.35/.4/.25s, 30px, 120·150ms waits) are as in the original. The backdrop blur behind the panel, invisible on the original desktop, was not built

Job board: the original is drawn by an external hiring widget (Brand) — the same shape (three-column cards by department, filter box) is built in static HTML, and only the department filter works. In the News list, the Finsweet filter and pagination also work only for category buttons and search, and pagination is for looks only.
The news list header’s background video is replaced by a teal light flowing slowly in place (CSS 12s loop) — the original video file is not used

The event card posters (original photo · logo posters) were redrawn as text posters on a deep teal panel. One hidden (u-d-none) Lottie on the original first page is not visible on screen, so it was not built. The ScrollSmoother attached to the card is not used by the original page (it uses Lenis 1.0.23 lerp .15, applied the same way)

Header of Careers and News (dark hero): as in the original only the hovered item darkens (button instantly, link .3s), the logo icon fill goes aqua → accent in .3s when hovering the header, and the demo button changes including its border in .3s. The icon is a line drawing instead of the original filled drawing, so the chevron changes to the line color.

Typeface backfill: 63 heading typeface (--kf-font-display) slots, plus js-inserted titles and marquees (news strip title · footer slogan), the wordmark (Logo), client, investor and poster logo text, person name lines (executives · name tags) and the company name in the copyright line were replaced with English placeholder text. The original uses a single typeface through the body text, but in this copy the header menu, buttons, eyebrow text, card titles, value names, quotes and certification badges drawn in the body typeface (--kf-font-sans) were left in Korean per the README body rule. Whether to switch the menu to English too is for the next person to decide.
Home page event poster: the original is a Latin-text poster image, so the four logos, Join us, the event name and the date lines are all set in English
